accūsĭto.opening: v. freq. [accuso], to accuse : nil erit quod deorum ullum accusites, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 23 .

ac-cūso.opening: (also with ss; cf. Cassiod. 2283 P.), , v. a. fr. causa; cf. cludo with claudo , orig. = ad causam provocare, to call one to account , to make complaint against , to reproach , blame. In gen., of persons: si id non me…

Acē.opening: Ἄκη , a town in Galilee , afterwards called Ptolemais or Acca, now St. Jean d'Acre , Nep. Dat. 5 ; Plin. 5, 19, 17, § 75 .

acĕto.opening: v. a. , old form for agito, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 23 Müll.; cf. the letter C.

achlis.opening: a wild beast of the North , which modern naturalists consider to be the same as the alces. — Acc. achlin, Plin. 8, 15, 16, § 39 .

Achrădīna.opening: a part of the city of Syracuse , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 53 ; Liv. 25, 24, 10 .

Acis.opening: one of the Cyclades , i. q. Siphnus, Plin. 4, § 66 .

aclassis.opening: tunica ab humeris non consuta, Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.

aclys.opening: (better than aclis), = ἀγκυλίς (first used by Verg.), a small javelin , Verg. A. 7, 730 ; Sil. 33, 362 al. ; cf. Non. 554, 3 .

Acmōn.opening: A companion of Aeneas : Acmon Lyrnessius, Verg. A. 10, 128 .— A companion of Diomed , Ov. M. 14, 484 ; acc. Acmona, ib. 497 .

Acmŏnensis.opening: adj. , pertaining to Acmonia , a town of Phrygia , Cic. Fl. 15, 34 ; Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 106

Acmŏnĭdes.opening: one of Vulcan's workmen , Ov. F. 4, 288 .

acnŭa.opening: or , , ἄκενα or ἄκαινα , a measure or piece of land , 120 feet square , Varr. R. R. 1, 10 ; Col. 5, 1, 5 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 15, 15, 5 .

ac-quĭesco.opening: ( ), , v. n. , lit., to become physically quiet , to come to physical repose; hence, in gen., to repose or rest (freq. in Cic.). Lit. : sine respirem, quaeso. Pe. Immo adquiesce, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 20 ; id. As. 2, 2, 60 :…

ac-quīro.opening: ( ), , v. a. quaero , to add to , to get or acquire (in addition), with ad or dat. (freq. in Cic.). Lit. : mihi quidem ipsi, quid est quod ad vitae fructum possit acquiri? Cic. Cat. 3, 12 ; 2, 8 : vides quam omnis…

acquīsītĭo.opening: acquiro , acquisition. In abstr. , Dig. 44, 4, 4, § 31 ; Tert. Exh. Cast. 12 .— Concr. , an increase , accession , Frontin. Aquaed. 10; 69 sq.

acra.opening: , also , , = ἄκρα , a promontory or headland , App. de Mundo prooem.: Acra Iapygia, a promontory in Magna Graecia, Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 100 .

Acrae.opening: , = Ἄκραι . A city of Sicily , on a lofty hill near Syracuse , now Palazzolo , Liv. 24, 36 ; Sil. 14, 206 .— A town in the Chersonesus Taurica (Crimea), Plin. 4, 12, 26, § 86 .

Acraephĭa.opening: Ἀκραιφία , a town of Boeotia , now Kardhiza , Liv. 33, 29 ; Plin. 4, 8, 12, § 26 .

Acraeus.opening: adj. , = ἀκραῖος , dwelling on the heights; an epithet of Jupiter and of Juno , whose temples stood on heights , Liv 38, 2; 32, 23.

Acrĭae.opening: Ἀκριαί , a town of Laconia , Liv. 35, 27, 3 .

Acrillae.opening: a town in Sicily , on the road from Syracuse to Agrigentum , Liv. 24, 35, 8 .

acro.opening: or , , , = ἄκρων , the extremity of a thing; so of a member of the body , Veg. 2, 28, 17 ; 5, 65, 2 ; of the stem of a plant , Apic. 4, 4 .

acrŏcōlēfĭum.opening: , = ἀκροκωλήφιον , the upper part of the foot of a swine , Veg. 6, 1, 2 .

acrŏcōlĭon.opening: , = ἀκροκώλιον , i. q. acro, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11 ; cf. Veg. 2, 47, 1 .

acrŏlĭthus.opening: adj. , = ἀκρόλιθος (of stone at the extremity): statuae, statues whose extremities only consisted of marble , the remainder of wood , Treb. Poll. XXX. Tyr. c. 32 (in Vitr. 2, 8, 11 written as Greek); cf. Müll. Arch. §…

Acrōnĭus lacus.opening: a part of Lake Constance , now the Ueberlingen Lake , Mel. 3, 2, 8 .

Acrŏnŏma saxa.opening: an unknown place in Lower Italy , Cic. Att. 13, 40, 2 .

Acrŏta.opening: king of the Albani , brother of Romulus Silvius , Ov. M. 14, 617 .

acrōzȳmus.opening: adj. , = ἀκρόζυμος , slightly leavened , Isid. Or. 20, 2, 15 .

actaea.opening: a strong - smelling plant , herb Christopher , Actaea spicata, Linn., Plin. 27, 7, 26, § 43 .

Actaeōn.opening: Ἀκταίων , a grandson of Cadmus , who , having seen Diana bathing naked with her nymphs , was torn to pieces by his own dogs , Ov. M. 3, 230 sq. ; ib. 720 ; id. Tr. 2, 105 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 9 ; Hyg. F. 181 al.

Actaeus.opening: adj. , Ἀκταῖος , pertaining to Attica , Attic , Athenian : in Actaeo Aracyntho, Verg. E. 2, 24 (as being on the border of Attica): arces, of Athens, Ov. M. 2, 720 ; fratres, i. e. Clytos and Butes, ib. 7, 681 : mel…

actē.opening: , = ἀκτῆ , a plant , perh. = ebulum, Plin. 26, 11, 73, § 120 ; Ap. Herb. 91.

Actē.opening: , = Ἀκτή . Lit. , coastland or maritime country; hence, the earlier name for Attica , the province of Middle Greece, in which Athens was situated, Plin. 4, 7, 11 ; Gell. 14, 6 .— One of the Horae , Hyg. F. 183 .— A…

Actĭăcus.opening: adj. Actium , relating to Actium : victoria, at Actium, Suet. Aug. 18 : ludi, the games which Augustus revived at Actium in honor of his victory, id. Tib. 6 : Phoebus, who had a temple here, Ov. M. 13, 715 : acquor, id.…

Actĭăs.opening: [Acte.] Attic , Athenian , Verg. G. 4, 463 .— [Actium.] Of Actium : Cleopatra, conquered at Actium by Augustus, Stat. S. 3, 2, 120 .

actīnŏphŏroe.opening: adj. (Gr. nom. plur. ), = ἀκτινοφόροι (bearing rays), epithet of the cochloe, Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 147 , v. Jan ad h. l.

actīnōsus.opening: ἀκτίς; pr. full of rays, hence , glorious : ecclesia, Ambros. in Psa. 41 .

actĭo.opening: ago , a doing , performing , acting , action , act. In gen.: non modo deos spoliat motu et actione divina, sed etiam homines inertes efficit, Cic. N. D. 1, 37 ; 2, 16 ; virtutis laus omnis in actione consistit, id. Off.…

actĭto.opening: v. freq. [ago], to act or be employed in , often or much (only of judicial or dramatic action): multas privatas causas, Cic. Brut. 70 : tragoedias, id. Rep. 4, 35 : so Tac. H. 3, 62 ; Suet. Galb. 3 ; cf. Gell. 9, 6 .

actĭuncŭla.opening: dim. actio , a short judicial harangue , Plin. Ep. 9, 15 .

actīve.opening: adv. , v. the foll. art. fin.

actīvus.opening: adj. ago . Active : philosophia, practical (opp. to contemplativa): philosophia et contemplativa est et activa; spectat simul agitque, Sen. Ep. 95, 10 : (opp. to spectativus) thesin a causa sic distinguunt, ut illa sit…

actor.opening: id. . One who drives or moves something : pecoris actor, Ov. H. 1, 95 : habenae, a slinger, Stat. Ach. 2, 419 .— In gen., he who does any thing , a doer or performer (cf. ago, II.). In gen. of every kind of action: ut…

Actor.opening: , m. A companion of Aeneas , Verg. A. 9, 500 .— An Auruncan , ib. 12, 94 ; 96 .—Hence, , , patron. , son or grandson of Actor: his son , Menoetius , Ov. F. 2, 39 ; his grandson , Patroclus , Ov. Tr. 1, 9, 29 ; id. M.…

actōrĭus.opening: adj. , i. q. activus, Tert. An. 14 .

Actōrĭus.opening: a Roman name , Suet. Caes. 9 al.

actrix.opening: actor . A female plaintiff , Cod. Th. 7, 16, 41.— A stewardess , Inscr. Murat. 913, 6 .

actŭālis.opening: adj. id. , active , practical , Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 17 .— Adv. : , actively , Myth. Vatic. vol. 3, p. 181 ed. Bod.

actŭārĭŏlum.opening: dim. actuarius , a small , swift vessel impelled by oars , row-boat , barge , Cic. Att. 10, 11, 4 ; 16, 3, 6 ; 16, 6, 1 .

actŭārĭus.opening: (written by some actarius , to distinguish it from the preceding, Vel. Long. 2234 P., and so found in Inscr. Grut. 260 ; ap. Henzen, 6284), sc. , 2. actus, II. B. 1. . A short-hand writer , Suet. Caes. 55 ; Sen. Ep. 33,…

actŭōse.opening: adv. , see the foll. art. fin.

actūtum.opening: adv. ab actu (as astutus from astu; or with tum as enclitic, in der Handlung da, Corss. Ausspr. II. 849), id est, celeritate, Prisc. 1013 P.; so Hand, s. v. who explains: uno actu, nulla re intercedente; Lindem. de Adv.…

adadūnĕphros.opening: = Ἀδάδου ϝεφρός (Adad's kidney), , Adad , a certain precious stone , Plin. 37, 11, 71, § 186 .

adasia.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 12 Müll.; Gloss. Mai Clas. Auct. viii. p. 52.

ad-bĭbo.opening: v. a. ad, intens. , to drink (not in Cic.). Lit. : quando adbibero, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 58 ; so Ter. Heaut. 2, 1, 8 ; Gell. 2, 22 .— Trop. , of discourse, to drink in , Plaut. Mil. Gl. 3, 3, 10 (cf. devorare dicta, id.…

ad-blătĕro.opening: v. a. ad, intens. , to prattle , to chatter : affanias, App. M. 9, p. 221, 25 Elm.

ad-dĕcet.opening: v. impers. [ad, intens. ], it behooves , it becomes , it is fit or proper that (used only in Enn. and Plaut., in the latter very often), constr. with acc. or with acc. and inf. : sed virum virtute vera vivere animatum…

ad-dĕcĭmo.opening: to take by the tenth part , to tithe (v. decimo): vinearum reditus, Vulg. 1 Reg. 8, 15 : greges vestros, ib. 8, 17 .

ad-disco.opening: , no sup. , , v. a. To learn in addition to , to learn further : Quid? qui etiam addiscunt aliquid? ut Solonem versibus gloriantem videmus, qui se cotidie aliquid addiscentem senem fieri dicit, Cic. de Sen. 8, 26 ; so…

addĭtāmentum.opening: addo , an addition , accession , increase : inimicorum, * Cic. Sest. 31, 68 : vitae, Sen. Ep. 17, 6 : praeter nomen nihil est additamenti, Pseud. Sall. ad Caes. de Rep. Ord. 2 : pretii, App. M. 9, 6 .

addĭtīcĭus.opening: (not -tius), , adj. id. , added , annexed , additional , Tert. de Rebus Carn. 52 ; Dig. 50, 16, 98 .

addĭtĭo.opening: id. , an adding to , addition : figurarum additio et abjectio, Quint. 9, 3, 18 : Sic corpori fit additio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37 ; Prisc. p. 978 P.

addĭtīvus.opening: adj. id. , added , annexed; of the pronoun ipse , Prisc. p. 1095 P.

ad-dīvīno.opening: v. a. ad intens. , to divine , to prognosticate : quemdam ex facie hominum addivinantem, ex his dixisse futurae mortis annos, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 88 dub. (Cod. Bamb. and Sillig: divinantem).

ad-do.opening: v. a. 2. do (addues for addideris, Paul. ex Fest. p. 27 Müll.), to put , place , lay , etc., a person or thing to another. In gen. Lit. , NEVE AVROM ADDITO, let no gold be put into the grave with the dead , Fragm. of…

ad-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. , to teach something in addition to , to teach : ebrietas addocet artes, Hor. Ep. 1, 5, 18 (but in Cic. Clu. 37, 104 , the correct read. is adducti, B. and K.).

ad-dormĭo.opening: v. n. , to begin to sleep , to go to sleep : rursus addormiunt, Cael. Aurel. 1, 11, 38.

ad-dormisco.opening: v. inch. n. , to go to sleep : quoties post cibum addormisceret, Suet. Claud. 8 .

addubānum.opening: = dubium, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 21 Müll.

addŭbĭtātĭo.opening: addubito , a doubting , a rhetor. fig., Mart. Cap. 5, p. 171 ; Cic. Off. 3, 4, 18 , where dubitatio is the better reading (B. and K.).

ad-dŭbĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.

adg.opening: . Words beginning thus, v. under agg.

ad-jăcŭlātus.opening: adj. , thrown or cast at : fulgor, Mart. Cap. 2, p. 41 .

adjectīcĭus.opening: or , adjicio , adj. , added besides (late Lat.): incommoda, Cassiod. Varr. 11, 8 .

adjectĭo.opening: id. , an adding to , addition , annexation. In gen.: Romana res adjectione populi Albani aucta, Liv. 1, 30 : illiberalis, a small addition, id. 38, 14 ext. : caloris, Sen. Ep. 189 : litterarum, Quint. 1, 5, 16 ; also…

adjecto.opening: v. a. , false reading in Apic. 8, 2 .

adjectus.opening: adjicio , an adding or applying to : odoris (ad narīs), Lucr. 4, 673 ; so id. 1, 689 : cuneorum, addition (opp. exemptus), Vitr. 9, 6 .

ad-jŭbĕo.opening: v. a. , false read. in Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 50 , instead of ut jubeat (Ritschl); and in Cat. 32, 4 , inst. of adjuvato.

adjūdĭcātĭo.opening: adjudico , a judicial adjudging of a matter , an adjudication , Dig. 10, 2, 36 ; 28, 5, 78 al.

ad-jūdĭco.opening: v. a. , to grant or award a thing to one, as judge , to adjudge (opp. abjudico).—With acc. and dat. Lit. : me est aequum frui fraternis armis mihique adjudicarier, Poët. ap. Auct. Her. 2, 26, 42 : regnum Ptolemaeo, Cic.…

ad-jŭgo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to yoke or fasten to or together , to unite. Lit. , in the lang. of gardening: palmites, Col. 4, 17, 6 : pampinos adjugatae (vitis), Plin. 17, 22, 35, § 175 .— In gen., to join or add to…

ad-jungo.opening: v. a. , to add , join , annex , or bind to any thing. Lit. , of cattle, to yoke , to harness (cf.: jugo, jugum, jungo, etc.): adjunxere feras (preceded by bijugos agitare leones), Lucr. 2, 604 : tauros aratro, Tib. 1,…

adjūrāmentum.opening: adjuro , a conjuring , entreating (late Lat.), Vulg. Tob. 9, 5 .

adjūrātĭo.opening: id. , a swearing to something by something, swearing , adjuration : adjuratione suae salutis, by swearing by her own safety, App. M. 2, p. 123 fin. : divini nominis, Lact. 2, 17 .

adjūrātor.opening: id. , one who conjures a thing , a conjurer (late Lat.), Alcim. 2, 312 .

adjūrātōrĭus.opening: adj. adjurator , pertaining to swearing : cautio, Cod. 12, 26, 4, § 2; 12, 30, 3, § 3.

ad-jūro.opening: v. a. , to swear to , to confirm by an oath. —With acc. , or acc. and inf. , or ut. Lit. : eam suam esse filiam sancte adjurabat mihi, Plaut. Cist. 2, 3, 27 ; Ter. Hec. 2, 2, 26 : adjurasque id te me invito non esse…

ad-mīror.opening: v. dep. , to wonder at , to be astonished at , to regard with admiration , to admire , to be in a state of mind in which something pleases us by its extraordinary greatness, its sublimity, or perfection; while mirari…

admissārĭus.opening: adj. admitto , sc. equus, asinus, etc., a horse , ass , etc., that is used for breeding , a stallion , etc.: equus, Varr. R. R. 2, 7 : asinus, id. ib. 2, 8 .—Hence, metaph. subst. , Of a sensual, lewd man: scitus…

ad-rōro.opening: v. a. ros , to bedew : herbam vino, Marc. Emp. 34 .

Aeăcĭdēĭus.opening: adj. , pertaining to the Æacidœ (the posterity of Æacus): regna, i. e. Ægina, Ov. M. 7, 472 .

Aebūra.opening: a city of Hispania Tarraconensis , now Cuerva , Liv. 40, 30, 3 .

Aebūtĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens , Cic. Att. 16, 2, 5 ; id. Caecin. 1 ; id. Fl. 37, 93 al. —Hence: , , the tribune Aebutius; enacted A.U.C. 520, Cic. Agr. 2, 8 ; Gell. 16, 10, 8 .

aedĭfacĭo.opening: v. a. , = aedifico: Labeo, Dig. 19, 260 Torrentinus, where others read aedificare.

aedĭfĭcātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. aedificatio , a little building : ecquid de illa aedificatiuncula mandavisses, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2, § 5 .

Aemĭlĭus Măcer.opening: a poet , the friend of Virgil and Ovid , who wrote De Serpentibus et Volucribus (and perh. De Virtutibus Herbarum), of which nothing is extant , Ov. Tr. 4, 10, 43 ; Serv. ad Verg. E. 5, 1 .

aemŭlātĭo.opening: aemulor , an assiduous striving to equal or excel another in any thing , emulation (it denotes rather the mental effort, while imitatio regards more the mode of action; but rivalitas is a jealous rivalry, and therefore…

aemŭlātor.opening: id. , a zealous imitator , emulator (in a good sense), ζηλωτής : ejus (sc. Catonis), * Cic. Att. 2, 1 fin. : animus aemulator Dei, Sen. Ep. 124 fin. : virtutum aemulator fuit, Just. 6, 3 : aemulatores sunt legis, Vulg.…

aemŭlātrix.opening: aemulator , a female emulator (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 7, 5 .

aemŭlātus.opening: Perh. only in Tac. for the class. aemulatio, emulation , rivalry , Hist. 3, 66.—In plur. , Ann. 13, 46. (But in Agr. 46, aemulatu is only a conjecture of Heinsius; Orell. and Halm read similitudine ).

aemŭlo.opening: v. a. An active form for aemulor (q. v.), App. M. 1, p. 112 .

aemŭlor.opening: v. dep. aemulus , to rival , to endeavor to equal or to excel one , to emulate , vie with , in a good and bad sense; hence (as a consequence of this action). to equal one by emulating. In a good sense, constr. with acc.…

aemŭlus.opening: adj. cf. ἁμιλλάομαι and ἅμα, imitor, imago, Germ. ahmen (Eng. aim) in nachahmen = to imitate , striving after another earnestly , emulating , rivalling , emulous (cf. aemulatio and aemulor), in a good and bad sense;…

Aenārĭa.opening: an island on the western coast of Campania , the landing-place of Æneas , now Ischia , Cic. Att. 10, 13 ; Liv. 8, 22 ; Suet. Aug. 92 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.

Aenēa.opening: or , , , = Αἴνεια , a city of Chalcidice , in Macedonia , opposite Pydna , Liv. 40, 4 ; 44, 10 ; 32 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Ænea , Liv. 40, 4, 4 .— , , adj. , belonging to Ænea : abies, Plin. 16, 39, 76, § 197…

Aenĕădēs.opening: ( gen. plur. Aeneadūm, Lucr. 1, 1 ; Ov. Tr. 2, 261 ), patr. m. [Aeneas]. A descendant of Æneas; his son Ascanius , Verg. A. 9, 653 ( Aenides , Rib.).— In gen., those who are related in any manner to Æneas; nence, A…

Aenēae Portus.opening: a harbor near Torone and Mount Athos , Liv. 45, 30, 4 .

Aenēas.opening: (also in the nom. Aenea, Varr. ap. Charis. p. 50 P.; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 61 ; gen. sometimes Aeneā, Apul. Orth. § 23 Osann.; acc. Aenean often, after the Gr. Αινείν , Ov. F. 5, 568 ; id. H. 7, 36 ; voc. Aenēā, Poët. ap…

aenĕātor.opening: aes , one who blows a horn in war , a trumpeter : Aeneatores cornicines dicuntur, id est cornu canentes, Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.; Suet. Caes. 32 .

Aenēis.opening: Aeneas , the Æneid , Virgil's celebrated epic , the hero of which is Æneas , the progenitor of the Romans : Aeneïdos auctor, Ov. Tr. 2, 533 : nec tu divinam Aeneïda tenta, Stat. Th. 12 fin. : morbo oppressus (Vergilius)…

Aenēĭus.opening: (quadrisyl.), adj. id. , of or pertaining to Æneas : nutrix, Verg A. 7, 1: virtus, Ov. M. 14, 581 : pietas, id. F. 4, 799 : fata, his death , Stat S. 5, 3, 37.

Aenēsi.opening: the companions of Æneas , Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.

aēnĕus.opening: (less freq. ), , adj. , of bronze [aes]. Of copper or bronze : equus, Cic. Off. 3, 9 : statua, id. Phil. 9, 6 : candelabra, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 26 : loricae, Nep. Iphicr. 1 ; Hor. C. 3, 3, 65 ; 3, 9, 18 ; 3, 16, 1 ; id.…

Aenĭānes.opening: a people of Thessalia , west of the Sinus Maliacus, Cic. Rep. 2 4; Liv. 28, 5, 15 (the Ἐνιῆνες of Homer, II 2, 749).

Aenīdēs.opening: patr. m. A son of Æneas , Verg. A. 9, 653 .— A descendant of Æneus , king on the Propontis. —In the plur. , the inhabitants of Cyzicus , because a son of Æneus was the founder of that city, Val. Fl. 3, 4 .

aenigmă.opening: , = αἴνιγμα ( dat. and abl. plur. aenigmatis, Charis. p. 38 P.), that which is enigmatical or dark in a figurative representation , an allegory; accto Quintilian's expl.: allegoria, quae est obscurior, Inst. 8, 6, 52 ;…

aenigmăticus.opening: adj. aenigma , like an enigma , obscure , enigmatic : ille clarum esse somnium dixit, et nihil aenigmaticum, nihil dubium continere, Cassiod. H. Eccl. 9, 4 .

aenigmătista.opening: and , , , = αἰνιγματιστης , one that proposes riddles , one that speaks in riddles , an enigmatist , Sid. Ep. 8, 6 ; Aug. Quaest. in Num. 4, 45 .

aenitologium.opening: In metre, a dac tylic verse with an iambic penthemimeris, e. g. Carmina bella magis vellem sonare, Serv. in Centim. 1825 P.

aēnŭlum.opening: dim. aenus , a small bronze vessel , Paul. ex Fest. p. 28 Müll.

Aeŏles.opening: ( , Varr.), , , = Αἰολεῖς , the Æolians , orig. in Thessaly, later in the Peloponnesus, on the coast of Asia Minor, in Lesbos, and other places, Varr. L. L. 5, § 25 ; 102 Müll.; id. R. R. 3, 1, 6 ; 3, 12, 6 ; Cic. Fl.…

Aeŏlĭa.opening: , = Αἰολία . A group of islands near Sicily , so called after Æolus , who is said to have once reigned there , now the Lipari Islands , Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 92 sq. — In mythol., the abode of Æolus , the god of the winds.…

Aeŏlĭcus.opening: adj. , = Αἰολικός , pertaining to the Æolians , Æolian , Æolic : gens, Plin. 6, 2, 2, § 7 : digamma, Quint. 1, 4, 7 : littera, id. 1, 7, 27 : dicta, id. 8, 3, 59 .

Aeŏlĭdes.opening: patr. m. , = Αἰολίδης , a male descendant of Æolus: his son Sisyphus , Ov. M. 13, 26 ; Athamas , id. ib. 4, 511 ; Salmoneus , Ov. Ib. 473 ; his grandson Cephalus , id. ib. 7, 672 ; also Ulysses , whose mother, Anticlea,…

aeŏlĭpĭlae.opening: aeolus-pila , vessels (or instruments ) for investigating the nature of the wind , eolipiles , Vitr. 1, 6 .

Aeŏlis.opening: patr. f. , = Αἰολίς , a female descendant of Æolus; so his daughters: Halcyone , Ov. M. 11, 579 ; Canace , id. H. 11, 34 .

Aeŏlĭus.opening: adj. , = Αἰόλιος , pertaining to Æolus , Æolia , or Æolis , Æolian. Pertaining to Æolus , the god of the winds , or to his posterity; Euri, Ov. Am. 3, 12, 29 : venti, Tib. 4, 1, 58 : aurum, the golden fleece (of the…

Aeŏlus.opening: , = Αἴολος . The god of the winds , son of Jupiter (or Hippotas) and of Menalippa , ruler of the islands between Italy and Sicily , where he kept the winds shut up in caverns , and , at the bidding of Jupiter , let them…

aeōn.opening: , = αἰών (age, eternity). Often used by Tert. adv. Haer. 33 ; 34 ; 49 , and adv. Valentin., who invented much concerning the Thirty Æons, whom he maintained to be gods.

Aepy.opening: , = Αἶπυ , a city of Elis , mentioned by Homer (II. 2, 592), Stat. Th. 4, 180 .

aequābĭlĭs.opening: adj. aequo , that can be made equal , equal , similar , like ( aequalis alterius staturae par; aequabile quod aequari potest, Front. Differ. 2198 P.); class.; in Cic. very freq. (syn.: aequalis, aequus, planus, par,…

aequābĭlĭtas.opening: aequabilis , the quality of aequabilis, equality , uniformity , evenness , equability (in the class. per., perh. only in Cic.; Lact. 5, 14 ). In gen.: motūs, Cic. N. D. 2, 5 : universae vitae, tum singularum actionum,…

aequaevus.opening: adj. aequus-aevum , of equal age , just as old , coeval (in gen. only poet. ; esp. freq. in Claudian): amicus, Verg. A. 5 . 452; so id. ib. 2, 561 : aequaevi gregis, Sen. Agam. 673 : majestas, Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 121…

aequālis.opening: adj. aequo , that can be put on an equality with; conseq., equal , like; constr. with dat. , absol. and as subst. with gen. (syn.: aequus, aequabilis, planus, par, similis). Lit. : partem pedis esse aequalom alteri…

aequālĭtas.opening: aequalis , equality , similarity , uniformity (syn.: similitudo, planities, aequitas). In gen.: similitudo aequalitasque verborum, Cic. Part. Or 6 : fraterna, id. Lig. 12 ; Vulg. 2 Cor. 8, 13 , 14.— In Tac. freq. of…

aequāmen.opening: aequo , an instrument for levelling or smoothing , as explanation of amussis, and syn. to levamentum, Varr. ap. Non. 9, 18 .

aequāmentum.opening: id. , an equalling , requiting , translation of hostimentum, Non. 3, 26

Aequāna.opening: (sc. juga), a mountain range near Sorrentum , Sil. 5, 466 .

aequănĭmis.opening: aequus-animus , adj. in Vet. Onomast. = εὐγνῶμων , kind , mild. —Adv. : , calmly , with equanimity (only in later Lat.), Macr. S. 2, 4 ; Sulp. Dial. 1, 14 ; Amm. 19, 10 ; Tert. Patient. 8 al.

aequănĭmĭtas.opening: aequanimis (rare for aequus animus). Before the class. per., favor , good-will (favor et propitius animus, Don. ad Ter. Ad. prol. 24 ): bonitas vestra atque aequanimitas, Ter. Phorm. prol. 34 ; id. Ad. prol. 24 .— In…

aequănĭmus.opening: aequus-animus , adj. , even-tempered , patient , composed , calm : aequanimus fiam, Aus. Sept. Sap. 3 : nulla fuit res parva umquam aequanimis, id. Idyll. 3, 9

aequātĭo.opening: aequo , an equalizing , equal distribution : gratiae dignitatis suffragiorum, Cic. Mur. 23 ; cf. Liv. 34, 31 : bonorum, community of goods, communism, Cic. Off. 2, 21, 73 : juris, Liv. 8, 4 al.

aequātor mŏnētae.opening: one who , in the coining of money , examines the equality of its weight , an assizer , Inscr. Orell. 3228

Aequi.opening: A warlike people of ancient Italy , in the neighborhood of the Latins and Volsci , on both sides of the Anio , whose cities were Alba, Tibur, Praeneste, Carseoli, etc. They were almost entirely destroyed by the dictator…

aequĭcrūrĭus.opening: adj. aequoscrus = ἰσοσκελής , of equal legs , isosceles , in geom. of the triangle, Mart. Cap. 6, p. 230 .

aequĭdiāle.opening: aequus-dies , old form for aequinoctiale, the equinox : aequidiale apud antiquos dictum est, quod nunc dicimus aequinoctiale, quia nox diei potius quam dies nocti annumerari debet. Graeci quoque in hoc consentiunt,…

aequĭdĭānus.opening: adj. aequidiale , i. q. aequinoctialis, equinoctial : exortus, App. de Mundo, p 62 (270 ed. min. Hildebr.).

aequĭdĭci.opening: (sc. versus) [aequus-dico], verses containing corresponding words or expressions ( ἀντιθέτους ), as ( Verg. E. 2, 18 ): alba ligustra cadunt, vaccinia nigra leguntur: Albis enim nigra opposuit, ligustris autem vaccinia…

aequĭdistans.opening: adj. aequusdisto . In math. parallel , equidistant : circuli, Mart. Cap. 3, p. 276 .

aequĭformis.opening: adj. aequus-forma , uniform : versus, composed of single , unconnected words , as ( Verg. A. 7, 171 ): urbe fuit media Laurentis regia Pici, where no two successive words are connected, Diom. p 498 P.

aequĭlanx.opening: aequus-lanx , with equal scale : trutina aequilance ponderare, Fulg. Cont. Verg.

aequĭlātātĭo.opening: aequus-latus , the equal distance of two parallel lines from each other , Vitr. 9, 8 .

aequĭlătĕrālis.opening: adj. id. , equilateral , Censor. de D. Nat. 8 .

aequĭlătĕrus.opening: adj. id. . In math. equilateral; triangulus, Mart. Cap. 6, p. 229 and 230.

aequĭlătus.opening: adj. id. . In math. equilateral : regula, Aus. Idyll. 11, 50 .

aequĭlăvĭum.opening: aequus-lavo , a half of the whole , said of wool, when half of the weight remains after washing , Paul. ex Fest. p. 24 Müll.

aequĭlībrātus.opening: adj. aequuslibra , = aequilibris, Tert. c. Hermog. 41.

aequĭlībris.opening: adj. id. , in perfect equilibrium or equipoise , level , horizontal , Vitr. 5, 12 .

aequĭlībrĭtas.opening: aequilibris (a word coined by Cic. as a transl. of the Epicurean ισονομία ), the equal distribution of the powers of nature : confugis ad aequilibritatem; sic enim ἰσνομίαν , si placet, appellemus, Cic. N. D. 1, 39, 109…

aequĭlībrĭum.opening: aequilibris , a level or horizontal position , equilibrium : quaedam ligna ad medium submersa ad aequilibrium aquae, Sen. Q. N. 3, 25 ; so Col. Arb. 5, 2 .— Trop. , a perfect equality : rumpendi pariter membri, Gell.…

Aequĭmaelĭum.opening: (better than ), , , the open space in Rome below the Capitol , not far from the Carcer, where had stood the house of the turbulent tribune of the people , Sp. Mœlius , who was slain by Ahala during the dictatorship of…

aequĭmănus.opening: adj. aequusmanus , who can use both hands equally well , ambidextrous , ἀμφιδέξιος , Aus. Idyll. 12 ; Beda Orth. 2329 P.— Trop. , of equal skill in two departments or in two pursuits : περιδέξιος , Symm. Ep. 9, 101…

aequĭnoctĭālis.opening: adj. aequinoctium , pertaining to the equinox , or the time of equal day and night , equinoctial : circulus, the equator, Varr. L. L. 9, § 24 Müll.: aestus, Sen. Q. N. 3, 28 (cf. aequinoctium fin. ). horae, Plin. 2 .…

aequĭnoctĭum.opening: aequus-nox , the time of equal days and nights , the equinox , Cic. Att. 12, 28, 3 ; Caes. B. G. 4, 36 ; cf. id. ib. 5, 23 , Varr. L. L. 6, § 8 Müll.: autumnale, Liv 31, 47: vernum, id. 33, 3 : aestus duobus…

aequĭpar.opening: adj. aequus-par , perfectly alike or equal , only in later writers, e. g. Aus. Idyll. 12 ; App. Flor 3 .

aequĭpărābĭlis.opening: (better, ), , adj. aequiparo , that may be compared , comparable (perh only in Plaut.); with dat. : diis aequiperabile, Curc. 1, 3, 11.—With cum , Trin. 2, 4, 65 (also in Non. 304 ).

aequĭpărantĭa.opening: (better, ), , id. , a comparison (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Val. 16 .

aequĭpărātĭo.opening: (better, ). , id. , an equalizing , a comparison : aequiperatio et parilitas virtutum inter se consimilium, Gell. 14, 3 : rex de aequiperatione aestimanda ( whether his army could be put on an equality with )…

aequĭpăro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
aequĭpăro.opening: (better ; cf. Dietrich in Zeitschr. für vergl. Sprachf. 1, p. 550), , v. a. and n. aequipar . Act. , to put a thing on an equality with another thing , to compare , liken; with ad , cum , or dat. : suas virtutes ad…

aequĭpĕdus.opening: , and , , adj. aequus-pes , having equal feet , isosceles (of a triangle). App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 5 , and Diom. p. 472 P.

aequĭpollens.opening: adj. aequus-polleo , of equal value or significance , equivalent , a dialectic word, used several times in App. de Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 36 and 39.

aequĭpondĭum.opening: aequus-pon dus , an equal weight , a counterpoise , Vitr. 10, 8 .

aequĭtas.opening: aequus , the quality of being aequus (syn.: aequalitas, jus, justitia, fas). The uniform relation of one thing to others , equality , conformity , symmetry; portionum aequitate turbatā, Sen. Q. N. 3, 10 : commoditas et…

aequĭternus.opening: adj. aequeaeternus , equally eternal , coeternal , Claud. Mam. Anim. 2, 4 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 13 .

aequĭ-vălĕo.opening: v. a. aequus , to have equal power , be equivalent , Auct. Carm. de Phil. 6.

aequĭvŏcus.opening: adj. aequus-voco ; in gram.: verba aequivoca, of like significations, ambiguous, equivocal, Isid. Orig. 2, 26 ; so Mart. Cap 4, 97 .

aequo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
aequo.opening: v. a. and n. aequus . Act. , to make one thing equal to another; constr. with cum and (in gen. in the histt.) with dat. , and with cop. conj. (cf. adaequo). With cum : inventum est temperamentum, quo tenuiores cum…

aequor.opening: aequus . In gen., an even , level surface (ante-Aug. poet. ; only once in Cic. and once in Sallust): speculorum aequor, a plane surface , as of a mirror, Lucr. 4, 106 ; 291 : in summo aequore saxi, upon the polished,…

aequŏrĕus.opening: adj. aequor , of or pertaining to the sea (only poet. ): rex, Neptune, Ov. M. 8, 604 : Britanni, the Britons surrounded by the sea, id. ib. 15, 753 : genus, the ocean kind, fish, Verg. G. 3, 243 : aquae, Mart. 10, 51 al.

aequus.opening: ( , Pac. 32 Rib.; Lucr. 5, 1023 Lachm. and Munro; AIQVOS, S. C. de Bacch. 1. 26), , adj. formerly referred to ΕΙΚΩ, ἔοικα, but Pott connects it with Sanscr. ēka = one, as if properly, one and uniform; others consider it…

aera.opening: [from aera, counters; v. aes, 2. E., later Lat. In math., a given number , according to which a reckoning or calculation is to be made , Vitruvius (Vetrubius) Rufus ap. Salmas. Exercc. I. p. 483.— Anitem of an account…

aerāmen.opening: aes , a late form for aes , copper , bronze; aeramen aut marmora, Cod. Th. 15, 1, 37: ferri vel aeraminis purgamenta, Theod. Prisc. 1, 9 .

aerāmentum.opening: id. , that is prepared from copper or bronze; hence, a copper or bronze vessel or utensil , Plin. 33, 5, 30, § 94 ; 35, 15, 51, § 182 .

aerārĭa.opening: and , v. aerarius, under B. and C.

aerārĭus.opening: adj. aes . That pertains to or is made of copper , bronze , etc.: aerarium metallum, a copper-mine, Vitr. 7, 9 ; Plin. 33, 5, 26, § 86 ; fornaces, smelting-furnaces, id. 11, 36, 42, § 119 : fabrica, the preparation of…

aerātus.opening: P. a. from aero, āre, found in no example, and only mentioned in Priscian: a metallorum quoque nominibus solent nasci verba, ut ab auro, auro, as, ab aere, aero, as; unde auratus et aeratus. p. 828 P. . Furnished or…

aerĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. aes . Made of copper : cornua, Verg. A. 7, 615 : clavus, Plin. 16, 10, 20, § 51 : tabulae, Suet. Vesp. 8 : vasa, Vulg. 2 Reg. 8, 10 .— Furnished or covered with copper or bronze : clipeus, Verg. A. 12, 541 ;…

aerĭfer.opening: ( ), , adj. aes-fero , bearing copper or bronze , i. e. bronze cymbals , of the attendants of Bacchus: manus, Ov. F. 3, 740 .

aerĭfĭcē.opening: adv. aes-facio , with the art of the worker in bronze : Musae (i. e. Musarum statuae), quas aerifice duxti, Varr. ap. Non. 69, 30 , and 283, 31.

aerĭfĭcĭum.opening: dictum, quod fit ex aere, Non. 69, 28 .

aerĭfŏdīna.opening: , a false read. in Varr. L. L. 5, § 7 .

aerĭnus.opening: adj. 1. aera , of darnel or cockle , Plin. 22, 25, 58, § 125 ; 24, 11, 59, § 100 .

aerĭ-pes.opening: adj. aes . Bronzefooted ( poet. ): tauri, Ov. H. 12, 93 : cerva, Verg. A. 6, 802 (since, acc. to fable, they had feet of bronze; hence we need not, with Charis. p. 249 ; Diom. p. 437 P., and Pomp. p. 449 Lind., take…

aerĭ-sŏnus.opening: ( ), , adj. aes , sounding with bronze : antra, i. e. in which the Curetes beat their bronze shields, Sil. 2, 93 : mons, Val. Fl. 3, 28 al.

aero.opening: (also written ), , , = αἴρω , a braided or wicker basket , hamper : aerones ex ulva palustri facti, Vitr. 5, 12 : aeronibus harenae plenis, Plin. 36, 14, 21, § 96 ; Dig. 19, 2, 31 ; cf. Don. ad Ter. Phorm. 1, 2, 72 .

aerōsus.opening: adj. aes , full of copper : Cyprus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.: aurum, gold that contains many parts of copper, Plin. 33, 5, 29, § 93 : ferrum, id. 34, 14, 41, § 143 : pecunia, Dig. 46, 3, 102 .

aerūca.opening: aes , a kind of verdigris , Vitr. 7, 12 .

aerūgĭno.opening: v. n. aerugo , to become rusty , cankered (eccl.): aurum et argentum vestrum aeruginavit, Vulg. Jac. 5, 3 .— Trop. : sicut aeramentum, aeruginat nequitia illius, Vulg. Eccli. 12, 10 .

aerūgĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of copper-rust , rusty (perh. only in Seneca): manus, Contr. 1, 2 fin. : lamellae, id. Brut. Vit. 12 .

aerūgo.opening: aes, as ferrugo from ferrum . Rust of copper : aes Corinthium in aeruginem incidit, * Cic. Tusc. 4, 14 ; Plin. 15, 8, 8, § 34 ; 34, 17, 48, § 160 .— Transf. The verdigris prepared from the same : Aeruginis quoque magnus…

aerumna.opening: (pleb. ), contr. from aegrimonia; as to the suppressed g, cf. jumentum from jugum, Doed. Syn. IV. p. 420. Others explain aerumna (with Paul. ex Fest. s. v. aerumnula, p. 24 Müll.) orig. for a frame for carrying burdens…

aerumnābĭlis.opening: adj. aerumna , that may be regarded as wretched or miserable , full of trouble , calamitous , * Lucr. 6, 123 ; App. M. 1, p. 102 ; 8 , p. 205.

aerumnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of trouble or misery , suffering , wretched , miserable : salum, Att. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 28, 67 : inopes, aerumnosae, Plaut. Rud. 1, 4, 39 ; so id. Ep. 4, 1, 32 : miseros, afflictos, aerumnosos,…

aerumnŭla.opening: dim. aerumna, q. v. , a traveller's stick for carrying a bundle , Paul. ex Fest. p. 24 Müll.

aeruscātor.opening: (aerusco], one who roves about the country , and obtains his living by exhibiting sleight-of-hand tricks; an itinerant juggler , Gell. 14, 1, 2 .

aerusco.opening: v. a. aes , to get money by going about and exhibiting tricks of legerdemain , to play the juggler : aeruscare: aera undique, id est pecunias, colligere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 24 Müll.—Esp., of mendicant philosophers, Gell.…

aes.opening: (often used in plur. nom. and acc.; abl. aeribus, Cato ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 27 Müll., and Lucr. 2, 636 ; gen. AERVM, Inscr. Orell. 3551 ), cf. Germ. Eisen = iron, Erz = copper; Goth. aiz = copper, gold; Angl.Sax. ar,…

Aesăcus.opening: , and Gr. , , , = Αἴσακος , a son of Priam , Ov. M. 11, 762 .

aesălōn.opening: , = αἰσάλων , a species of falcon or hawk; acc. to Billerbeck, the rust-kite , moor-buzzard , Falco aeruginosus, Linn., Plin. 10, 74, 95, § 205 .

Aesar.opening: . A name of God among the Etruscans , Suet. Aug. 97 .— , , , a river in Lower Italy , in the neighborhood of Crotona , now Esaro , Ov. M. 15, 23 .—Hence, , , adj. , pertaining to the Æsar , Ov. M. 15, 54 .

Aeschĭnes.opening: , = Αὶσχίνης . A disciple of Socrates , Cic. Inv. 1, 31 ; Quint. 5, 11, 27 .—But more celebrated, The orator Æschines , rival to Demosthenes , Cic. de Or. 2, 23 ; 3, 56 ; Quint. 2, 1, 17 ; 10, 1, 22 . — A physician of…

ancŏrālis.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to an anchor : strophia, App. M. 11, p. 265, 7 .—Hence, , , , a cable , Liv. 37, 30 fin. ; so id. 22, 19 ; Plin. 16, 8, 13, § 34 ; cf. ancorarius.

ancŏrārĭus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to an anchor : funes, cables, Caes. B. C. 2, 9 .

ancŭla.opening: pr. dim. anculus , a maidservant , Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.

ancŭlus.opening: pr. dim. v. 2. Ancus , a man-servant , Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.

ancus.grammar: appellatur, qui aduncum bracchium habet et exporrigi non potest
ancus.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 19 Müll. [v. ango].

Ancus.opening: ( ), , v. ango (prop. a servant , as bending, crouching; hence = ancus Martius = θεράπων Ἄρεως , servant of Mars ), the fourth king of Rome , A.U.C. 116-140, said to have been the grandson of Numa by Pompilia, Cic. Rep.…

Ancȳra.opening: , = Ἄγκυρα . A town in Galatia , now Angora , where was a marble temple of Augustus, built in his lifetime, Liv. 38, 24 ; Curt. 3, 1 ; Plin. 5, 32, 42, § 146 ; Claud. in Eutr. 2, 98 .— A town in Phrygia , Plin. 5, 32,…

andābătă.opening: a kind of Roman gladiator , whose helmet was without openings for the eyes , and who therefore fought blindfolded for the amusement of spectators , * Cic. Fam. 7, 10 Manut.: more andabatarum, Hier. adv. Helv. 3 ; id.…

Andanĭa.opening: , = Ανδανία , a very ancient town of Messenia , now Andorossa , Liv. 36, 31 .

Andes.opening: a village near Mantua , the birthplace of Vergil , now Pietola; hence, , , of or from Andes : Andinus, i. e. Vergil, Sil. 8, 595 .

andrachnē.opening: , = ἀνδράχνη , a plant , purslane : Portulacca oleracea, Linn.; Col. 10, 376 ; Plin. 25, 13, 103, § 162 .

Andraemōn.opening: , = Ἀνδραίμων . The father of Amphissus and husband of Dryope , who was changed into a lotus , Ov. M. 9, 333 ; 9, 363 .— or , , , father of Thoas , a combatant before Troy , Ov. M. 13, 357 ; cf. Hom. Il. 2, 638.

Andrīcus.opening: a servant of Cicero , Cic. Fam. 16, 14, 1 .

Andriscus.opening: , = Ἀνδρίσκος , a slave who claimed to be the son of the Macedonian king Perseus and occasioned the third Macedonian war , Liv. Epit. 49 ; Vell. 1, 11 ; Flor. 2, 14 .

Andrĭus.opening: adj. , born at Andros , one of the Cyclades , Ter. And. 5, 4, 3 .— Hence, , ae. , a woman of Andros; The Maid of Andros , a comedy by Terence.

Andrō^cles.opening: , or , , , = Ἀνδροκλῆς , the well-known slave who cured the foot of a lion and was afterwards recognized by the lion and saved from death , Sen. Ben. 2, 19 ; Gell. 5, 14 .

andrŏdămās.opening: , = ἀνδροδάμας (man-subduing). A species of bloodstone (so called from its great hardness), Plin. 36, 20, 38, § 146 .— A silver-colored , quadrangular , and cubical precious stone (acc. to Bruckmann, a cubical,…

Andrŏgĕōn.opening: , i. q. Androgeos; acc. Gr. Androgeona, Prop. 2, 1, 62 .—Hence, , , adj. , pertaining to Androgeon : caedis, Cat. 64, 77 .

Andrŏgĕōs.opening: , and , , , = Ἀνδρόγεως , son of the Cretan king Minos , whom the Athenians and Megarians slew; on account of which the enraged father made war upon them , Ov. M. 7, 458 ; id. H. 10, 99 ; Verg. A. 6, 20 .

andrŏgўnē.opening: , = ἀνδρογύνη , a masculine , heroic woman , Val. Max. 8, 3, 1 .

andrŏgўnus.opening: , = ἀνδρόγυνος, ἀνδρογύνη , a man-woman , hermaphrodite : imberbus, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 493, 27 ; so * Cic. Div. 1, 43 ; Liv. 27, 11 ; Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 15 ; 7, 3, 3, § 34 al. ; Lucr. 5, 839 .

Andrŏmăchē.opening: , and , (Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 82 Müll., or Trag. v. 100 Vahl.), , = Ἀνδρομάχη , a daughter of king Eëtion , and wife of Hector. After the destruction of Troy, she was carried by Pyrrhus to Greece, and was…

Andrŏmĕda.opening: , and , , , = Ἀνδρομέδη , a daughter of the Ethiopian king Cepheus and Cassiope. On account of the arrogance of her mother she was bound to a rock by the command of the oracle of Jupiter Ammon, in order that she might…

andrōn.opening: , = ἀνδρών ( ἀνήρ , a man). Among the Greeks, the part of the house in which the men resided , the men's apartment; also called andronitis (opp. gynaeceum, q. v.): locus domicilii, in quo viri morabantur, Paul. ex Fest.…

Andrŏnīcus.opening: the cognomen of several Romans , among whom the most distinguished , L. Livius Andronicus, the first dramatic and epic poet of the Romans , lived in the middle of the third century B.C., Cic. Brut. 18 ; Gell. 17, 21 al.…

Andrŏs.opening: and , , , = Ἄνδρος , one of the largest of the Cyclades , in the Ægean Sea , south-east of Eubœa , now Andro , Ter. And. 1, 1, 43 al. ; Ov. M. 7, 469 ; 13, 649 ; cf. Mann. Greece, p. 743.

andrŏsăcĕs.opening: , = ἀνδρόσακες , a plant , now unknown, perh. zoophyte, Plin. 27, 4, 9, § 25 .

andrŏsaemŏn.opening: , = ἀνδρόσαιμον (man's blood), a kind of St. John's-wort , with blood-red juice : Hypericum perforatum, Linn.; Plin. 27, 4, 10, § 26 sq.

andruāre.opening: to run back : a Graeco verbo ἀναδραμεῖν , Paul. ex Fest. p. 9 Müll.

anfractŭōsus.opening: adj. anfractus , roundabout , prolix : locutio, Aug. Serm. 135 .

anfractus.opening: (not ), , id. , pr. a breaking round; hence, a bending , recurving , turning (in the ante-class. per. rare; v. the preced. art.). Lit. : quid pulchrius eā figurā (sc. sphaericā) quae nihil incisum anfractibus, nihil…

angărĭa.opening: , = ἀγγαρία [angarius], the service of the angarius, and, in gen., service to a lord , villanage , Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 29 ; 50, 5, 11 al. ; v. on angaria and angarialis, Gloss. Man. art. clabularis.

angărĭālis.opening: adj. angaria , of or pertaining to service : copia, Cod. Th. 8, 5, 4.

angărĭo.opening: v. a. id. . Lit. , to demand something as angaria, to exact villanage , Dig. 49, 18, 4 ; so Aug. Ep. 5 med. al. — Meton. , to compel , constrain (eccl. Lat.): quicumque te angariaverit mille passus (vadere), vade cum…

angărĭus.opening: , = ἄγγαρος [introd. into the Greek from the Persian], a messenger , a courier , Lucil. ap. Non. p. 21, 21 .

angĕlĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀγγελικός (suitable or pertaining to messengers). Angelicum metrum, a dactylic measure (so called on account of its rapidity of movement), Diom. p. 512 P.; Victor. p. 2531 P. — Belonging to angels , angelic :…

angĕlĭfĭcātus.opening: , qs. part. of angelifico, changed into an angel : caro, Tert. Res. Carn. 25 .

angellus.opening: dim. angulus , a little angle or corner (only ante- and post-class.), * Lucr. 2, 428 ; Arn. 7, p. 253 .

angĕlus.opening: , = ἄγγελος . A messenger , Sen. Ep. 20 med. dub.; Vulg. Matt. 11, 10 .— An angel. In bon. part. very freq. in the Vulg., the Church fathers, Aug., Tertull., Jerome, etc.— In mal. part.: Diabolus et angeli ejus, Vulg.…

Angĕrōna.opening: ( , Macr.), , ango , the goddess of Suffering and Silence , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 65 ; Macr. S. 1, 10 ; Inscr. Orell. 116 . —Hence, , , , her festival , Varr. L. L. 6, § 23 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 17 Müll.

angĭna.opening: (for the quantity of the pen., v. the foll. examples, and cf. Wagner ad Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 139 ), , ἀγχόνη; v. ango . The quinsy , as suffocating: Insperato abiit quam unā angina sustulit horā, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 35, 9…

angĭportus.opening: (and , , ; cf. Prisc. p. 714 P.) [ang- as in angustus, and portus; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 145 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 17 Müll.], a narrow street , lane , or alley , Paul. ex Fest. l. l.; cf. Dig. 16, 59 ; Plaut. Cist. 1,…

Angĭtĭa.opening: sister of Medea and Circe , who received divine honors from the Marsi , Verg. A. 7, 759 (acc. to Serv. ad Verg. A. 7, 750 , Medea herself ); Sil. 8, 498 ; Inscr. Orell. 115 ; 116 ; 1846 .—Hence, Nemus Angitiae, the…

Angli.opening: the Angli , a branch of the Suevi in Lower Germany , Tac. G. 40 ; c. A.D. 450 they united with the Saxons (hence the designation Anglo-Saxons ), conquered Britannia, and gave their name to the country,—Anglia, England.

ango.grammar: xi, ctum, and anxum, 3 v. a.
ango.opening: v. a. ( perf. and sup. rest only on the assertion in Prisc. p. 895 P.; Diom. p. 366 P.; part. anctus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 24 Müll.; acc. to Prisc. l. c., the sup. is sometimes anxum; cf. Struve, 214) [the root of this…

angor.opening: ango , = angina. A compression of the neck , a strangling : occupat fauces earum angor, the quinsy, Plin. 8, 27, 41, § 100 : aestu et angore vexata, i.e. aestu angorem ac prope suffocationem efficiente, Liv. 5, 48 .—Far…

Angrivarii.opening: a German tribe in the neighborhood of the Teutoburg Forest , on both sides of the Weser , Tac. G. 33 Rup.; id. A. 2, 8 ; 2, 19 ; 2, 22 ; 2, 24; 2, 41.

anguĕus.opening: adj. anguis , of or pertaining to a serpent : lapsus, Sol. 24 .

anguĭcŏmus.opening: (four syl.), , adj. anguis-coma , with snaky hair (only in the poets): Gorgon, Ov. M. 4, 699 ; cf. id. ib. 4, 801 ; Stat. Th. 1, 544 .

anguĭcŭlus.opening: dim. anguis , a small serpent , Cic. Fin. 5, 15, 42 .

anguĭfer.opening: ( ), , adj. anguis-fero , serpent-bearing : caput, Ov. M. 4, 741 : Gorgo, Prop. 2, 2, 8 .—Hence, subst. : , , (as transl. of Ὀφιοῦχος ), the serpent-bearer , the constellation Serpentarius or Ophiuchus , Col. 11, 2, 49…

anguĭgĕna.opening: anguis-gigno , engendered of a snake or dragon , an epithet of the Thebans, who sprang from dragons' teeth, Ov. M. 3, 531 ; cf.: draconigena urbs, i. e. Thebes, id. F. 3, 865 .

anguilla.opening: dim. anguis, Varr. L. L. 5, § 77 Müll.; but it may be directly con. with Gr. ἔγχελυς; v. anguis , an eel. Lit. : Muraena anguilla, Linn.; Plin. 9, 21, 38, § 74 al. ; Juv. 5, 103 .— Trop. : anguilla est, elabitur, he is…

anguĭ-mănus.opening: adj. anguismanus , with serpent-hand , an epithet of the elephant, because he makes quick, serpent-like motions with his trunk (manus), perh. only in Lucr. 2, 537 ; 5, 1303 .

anguĭnĕus.opening: adj. anguis , less freq. than the foll. Of or pertaining to the serpent , snaky : Gorgonis comae, Ov. Tr. 4, 7, 12 .— Similar to a serpent in form , serpent-like : cucumis, Col. 2, 9, 10 ; 7, 10, 5 .

anguīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to the serpent , snaky : cervix, Pac. ap. Cic. Div. 2, 64 : capillus Eumenidum, Cat. 64, 193 : pellis, Cato, R. R. 73 : cucumis, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 25 : adeps, Plin. 30, 5, 12, § 37 :…

anguĭ-pēs.opening: ( ), , adj. anguis-pes , serpent - footed , an epithet of giants, Ov. M. 1, 184 ; cf.: serpentipedes Gigantes, id. Tr. 4, 7, 17 .

anguis.opening: ( ), (rare form , , Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 29 Mai.— Abl. angue; but angui, Enn. ap. Cic. Ac. 2, 28 , or Trag. v. 51 Vahl.; Hor. Ep. 1, 17, 30 ; Ov. M. 4, 483 MS.; cf. Prisc. p. 766 P.; in Cic. Div. 2, 31, 66 ,…

anguĭ-tĕnens.opening: adj. anguis-teneo , serpent-holding; hence, subst. , the constellation , = anguifer, transl. of the Gr. Ὀφιοῦχος , Serpent-bearer , Cic. N. D. 2, 42 ; Manil. 5, 384 .

angŭlāris.opening: adj. angulus , having corners or angles , angular : lapis, a square stone, Cato, R. R. 14, 1 ; Col. 5, 3, 2 : lapis, a corner-stone, Vulg. Job, 38, 6 ; and, in trop. sense, ib. Isa. 28, 16 ; ib. Ephes. 2, 20 ; ib. 1…

angŭlātim.opening: adv. id. , from corner to corner , from angle to angle (post-class.): cuncta perlustrari, App. M. 9, p. 237, 26 ; so id. ib. 3 , p. 103; Sid. Ep. 7, 9 .

angŭlo.opening: v. a. id. , to make angular or cornered , Ambros. Ep. 42 .—Hence, * , , P. a. , made angular; with angles , angular : corpuscula, Cic. N. D. 1, 24 .

angŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of corners (post-Aug.; perh. only in Plin.): folia, Plin. 16, 23, 35, § 86 : acini, id. 15, 24, 29, § 100 : recessus, id. 4, 4, 5, § 9 : gemmae, id. 37, 12, 75, § 196 et saep.

angŭlus.opening: cf. ἀγκύλος, crooked, bent, angular, Paul. ex Fest. p. 11 Müll.; v. ango , an angle , a corner. Lit. Math. t. t., an angle : angulus optusus, Lucr. 4, 355 : angulus acutus, Plin. 12, 3, 29, § 50 : meridianus circulus…

angustĭae.opening: (rare in class. Lat. in sing , , Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 61 ; cf. Charis. p. 20 P.; but freq. in eccl. Lat., Vulg. Gen. 42, 21 ; ib. Psa. 118, 143 ; ib. Rom. 2, 9 ; ib. 2 Cor. 2, 4 al.), angustus . Lit. , narrowness ,…

angustĭclāvĭus.opening: adj. angustus-clavus , wearing a narrow ( purple ) stripe; an epithet of a plebeian tribune, who, as a plebeian, could wear only a narrow stripe of purple on his tunic (while the tribune from the nobility had a broad…

angustĭo.opening: v. a. angustus , pr. to make narrow , to straiten; only trop. and in eccl. Lat. to straiten , hamper , distress : angustiatus prae pavore, Vulg. Jud. 13, 29 : qui se angustiaverunt, ib. Sap. 5, 1 : sed non angustiamur,…

angusto.opening: v. a. angustus , to make narrow , to straiten (first used after the Aug. per.): Cujus (Hellesponti) iter caesis angustans corporum acervis, Cat. 64, 359 : (puteus) ore angustatur, Plin. 17, 8, 4, § 45 : servorum turba,…

angustus.opening: , um. adj. v. ango , narrow , strait , esp. of local relations, close , contracted , small , not spacious (syn.: artus, brevis, contractus; opp. latus, Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 92 ). Lit. : fretus, Lucr. 1, 720 : Angustum per…

Anna.opening: (cf. Gesen. Gesch. Hebr. Spr. p. 228), the sister of Dido , Verg. A. 4, 9 et saep.; Ov. H. 7, 191 ; Sil. 8, 55 al.

Anna Perenna.opening: an old Italian goddess , the protector or bestower of the returning year (acc. to Macr. S. 1, 12 , offerings were made to her, ut annare perennareque commode liceat, and hence her name); cf. Inscr. Orell. II. 1847 ; II.…

annālis.opening: adj. annus . Continuing a year , annual : tempus, cursus, Varr. R. R. 1, 27, 1 ; so Dig. 14, 2, 1 ; 38, 17, 6 .— Relating to the year or the age : Lex Villia Annalis, the law passed B. C. 180 by L. Villius, which…

annārĭus.opening: adj. id. , relating to the appointed year : annaria lex dicebatur ab antiquis, quā finiuntur anni magistratus capiendi, Paul. ex Fest. p. 27 Müll.: lex, Lampr. Com. 2 ; Arn. 2, p. 91 .

an-năto.opening: (better ), , v. n. To swim to or toward : ei insulae crocodili non adnatant, Plin. 8, 25, 38, § 93 ; Jan here reads adnant; Sil. 10, 610 .—With ad : ad manum hominis adnatare, Plin. 9, 29, 46, § 87 ; 9, 10, 12, § 38 .—…

an-nāvĭgo.opening: (better ), , v. n. , to sail to or toward , to come to by ship. Absol. : tres (pyramides) sane conspicuae undique adnavigantibus, Plin. 36, 12, 16 , § 76.— With quo : quo cum adnavigāsset, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 11 .

an-necto.opening: (better ), , v. a. , to tie or bind to , to connect , annex. Lit. : (animum) corporibus nostris, * Lucr. 3, 688 : funiculus scapham adnexam trahebat, Cic. Inv. 2, 51 : ad linguam stomachus adnectitur, id. N. D. 2, 54 ;…

annexĭo.opening: ( ), , annecto , a tying or binding to , a connecting , Pall. Mart. 10, 36 .

annexus.opening: ( ), , annecto , a tying or binding to , a connection : Cremona annexu connubiisque gentium floruit, Tac. H. 3, 34 .

Annĭānus.opening: adj. Of or pertaining to Annius or Annia , Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 46 .— The name of a Roman poet under the emperors Antonine and Adrian , Gell. 7, 7 ; 20, 8 ; cf. Bähr, Röm. Gesch. 71 and 194; Teuffel, Rom. Lit. § 349, 3.

Annĭcĕrīi.opening: , = Ἀννικέρειοι , a philosophical sect of Cyrene , so called from its founder Anniceris , Cic. Off. 3, 33, 116 .

an-nicto.opening: (better ), āre. v. n. , to wink with the eyes , to wink or blink to or at : alii adnutat, alii adnictat, Naev. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 29 Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 19 Rib.).

annĭcŭlus.opening: adj. annus , a year old , of a year , or a yearling (not in Cic.; freq. in Vulg.): nuces, Cato, R. R. 17, 2 Schneid.: taurus, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 12 : vituli, Vulg. Micah, 6, 6 : agnus, ib. Ex. 12, 5 : ovis, ib. Lev. 14,…

annĭfer.opening: adj. annus-fero (only in Plin. H. N. ). Bearing fruit the whole year : Citreae et junipirus et ilex anniferae habentur, Plin. 16, 26, 44, § 107 .— Producing annually a new stalk (in Theophrast. ἐπετειόκαυλα ), Plin. 19,…

an-nĭhĭlo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to bring to nothing , to annihilate; introd. by Jerome: nullificāsti seu adnihilāsti vel adnullāsti, Hier Ep. 135 fin.

annīsus.opening: ( ), , annitor , a striving , exertion : ut alieno adjuventur adnisu, Symm. Ep. 5, 74 .

an-nītor.opening: (better ), , v. dep. Lit. , to press upon or against , to lean upon; with ad or dat. (most freq. after the commencement of the Aug. per.): natura ad aliquod tamquam adminiculum adnititur, Cic. Lael. 23, 88 : hasta…

Annĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens, e. g. T. Annius Milo, T. Annius Cimber, P. Annius Asellus al.—Hence, Annianus, v. Annianus, I.

annĭversārĭus.opening: adj. annusverto , that returns , happens , is used , etc., every year , returning or renewed annually , annual , yearly : sacra, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 39 : Ecce solemnitas Domini est in Silo anniversaria, Vulg. Jud. 21, 19 :…

an-no.opening: (better ), , v. n. To swim to , toward , or along; constr. with the dat. , ad , or acc. With dat. : terrae, Verg. A. 6, 358 : ei insulae crocodili non adnant, Plin. 8, 25, 38, § 93 Jan.— With ad : ad litus, Gell. 7, 8,…

anno.opening: v. a. annus , to pass or live through a year , Macr. S. 1, 12 ; cf. Anna.

an-nōdo.opening: (better ), , v. a. , to cut off knots , to cut away suckers or shoots of the vine , in the lang. of gardening and the vintage, Col. 4, 22, 4 Schneid.; for which, as also in id. 4, 24, 10 al. , other edd. have abnodo.

annōna.opening: from annus, as pomona from pomum . In gen., the yearly produce , the annual income of natural products , in the widest sense (cf.: cibaria annua, Cato, R. R. 60 ): vectigal novum ex salariā annonā, Liv. 29, 37 : lactis,…

annōnārĭus.opening: adj. annona , of or pertaining to provisions : frumentum, ceteraeque annonariae species, Veg. Mil. 3, 3 : causa, Dig. 49, 14, 46 .

annōnor.opening: v. dep. id. , to collect provisions , Capitol. Gord. 29 .

annōsĭtas.opening: annosus , fulness of years , old age (post-class.), Cod. Th. 12, 1, 113; Aug. Ep. 251 .

annōsus.opening: adj. annus , of many years , aged , old (a favorite word of the Aug. poets and post-Aug. prose writers): anus, Ov. F. 2, 571 : vetustas, id. Tr. 5, 2, 11 : merum, Tib. 3, 6, 58 : bracchia, Verg. A. 6, 282 : robur, id.…

annŏtāmentum.opening: ( ), , annoto , a remark , annotation (perh. only in Gell.), Gell. 1, 7, 18 ; 1, 17, 2 .

annŏtātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a noting down in writing , a remark , annotation (post-Aug.). In gen.: a te librum meum cum adnotationibus tuis exspecto, Plin. Ep. 7, 20 ; Gell. praef.— Esp. In the jurists, the registering of a person…

annŏtātĭuncŭla.opening: ( ), , dim. annotatio , a brief annotation (only in Gell.), Gell. 19, 7, 12 ; 19, 17, 21 fin.

annŏtātor.opening: ( ), , annoto . An observer , remarker (post-Aug.): Non ante medium diem distentus solitariā cenā spectator adnotatorque convivis tuis immines, Plin. Pan. 49 .— In the jurists, the controller of the annual income , Cod.…

annŏtātus.opening: ( ), , id. , a remark , mention : mortes dignae adnotatu, Val. Max. 9, 12, 1 .

annōtĭnus.opening: adj. from annus, as diutinus from diu , a year old , of last year (only in prose and rare): cum annotinis (navibus), Caes. B. G. 5, 8 (the paraphrast: συν ταῖς τοῦ πρόσθεν ἔτους ): ungues, Col. 4, 24, 8 : novus fructus…

an-nŏto.opening: (better ), , v. a. , to put a note to something, to write down something, to note down , remark , comment on (only in post-Aug. prose, like its derivatives annotatio, annotator, annotamentum, etc.). In gen.: ut…

annŭālis.opening: adj. annus , a year old (post-class. and rare): agni, Paul. Sent. 3, 7 : cum operario annuali, * Vulg. Eccli. 37, 14 .

an-nūbĭlo.opening: (better ), , v. a. , to involve in clouds , to overcast : velis adnubilat aura secundis, Stat. S. 5, 1, 146 .— Trop. , to obscure : virtutem, Amm. 27, 6 .

an-nullo.opening: (better ), , v. a. ad-nullus , to annihilate , annul (eccl. Lat.): adnullabunt substantiam, Vulg. Eccli. 21, 5 : adnullabitur superbia, ib. ib.; v. annihilo.

annŭmĕrātĭo.opening: ( ), , annumero , a numbering , counting : dierum, Dig. 27, 1, 13 .

an-nŭmĕro.opening: (better ), , v. a. Lit. , to count to , to count out to , to put to a person's account : mihi talentum argenti adnumerat, Plaut. Merc. prol. 88 : argentum, * Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 15 : et reddere pecuniam mulieri, Cic. Div. in…

annuntĭātĭo.opening: ( ), not ( ), , annuntio , an announcing , announcement , annunciation (eccl. and late Lat.), Vulg. 1 Joan. 1, 5 ; 3, 11; Lact. 4, 21 ; Aug. Serm. Sanct. 18 ; Arn. 7, p. 248 .

annuntĭātor.opening: ( ), not ( ), , id. , an announcer (eccl. Lat.), * Vulg. Act. 17, 18 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 7 ; Aug. Serm. Sanct. 14 .

an-nuntĭo.opening: (better ), not ( ), , v. a. , to announce , make known , relate , proclaim (post-Aug. and mostly eccl.; very freq. in Vulg.). With acc. and inf. : adnuntiavere exanimatum illum, Plin. 7, 52, 53, § 174 .— With quod :…

annuntĭus.opening: ( ), not ( ), , annuntio , that announces or makes known (late Lat.): signum, App. de Deo Socr. p. 52, 28 ; Ambros. Hexaëm. 5, 9.

an-nŭo.opening: (better ), (ūvi, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 882 P.), , v. n. -nuo, whence nutum; Gr. νεύω; cf. abnuo , to nod to , to nod. In gen.: ne illa ulli homini nutet, nictet, adnuat, Plaut. As. 4, 1, 39 : adnuerunt sociis, Vulg. Luc.…

annus.opening: acc. to some, as Corssen, Beitr. 16, for am-nus, from 2. an- am-; or acc. to others, directly from 2. anus, a ring, and kindred to the form appearing, in ἐνοαυτός, δί-ενος, τρί-ενος . Lit. , a circuit , circular course…

an-nūto.opening: (better ), , v. freq. , to nod often to , to nod to (ante- and postclass.): alii adnutat, alii adnictat, Naev. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 29 Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 19 Rib.); Plaut. Merc. 2, 3, 100 ; App. M. 10 .

an-nūtrĭo.opening: (better ), , v. a. , to nourish or train up at or near to : arboribus vites, Plin. 17, 23, 35, § 202 .

annŭus.opening: adj. annus . That lasts a year or continues through a year , of a year's duration : penus, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 45 : tempus, Cic. Att. 6, 5 : provincia, id. Fam. 15, 14 fin. : magistratus, Caes. B. G. 1, 16 : reges, Nep.…

anquīna.opening: the rope by which the sail-yard is bound to the mast , Cinna ap. Isid. Orig. 19, 4, 7 ; so also Lucil. ap. Non. p. 536, 8 .

an-quīro.opening: v. a. 2. anand quaero , to seek on all sides , to look about for , to search after. Lit. and in gen.: anquirere est circum quaerere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 22 Müll.: anquirere aliquem, apud quem evomet virus, etc., Cic.…

anquīsītĭo.opening: anquiro, II. , a judicial indictment : anquisitionis M. Sergii, Varr. L. L. 6 , §§ 90 and 92 Müll.

ansa.opening: cf. χανδάνω, and pre-hendo, pre-hensum, and λαβή from λαβεῖν , that by which something is taken hold of , a handle , haft; of a vessel, pitcher, vase, and the like. Lit. , Cato, R. R. 113 ; Verg. E. 3, 45 ; 6, 17 ; Ov.…

ansātus.opening: adj. ansa , furnished with or having a handle : capulae a capiendo, quod ansatae, ut prehendi possint, Varr. L. L. 5, 26, 35 : vas, Col. 9, 15 : tela, darts having a thong , Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 1 (Ann. v. 155…

anser.opening: , usu. Sanscr. hasas; Gr. χήν; Germ. Gans; Engl. Gander; Erse, goss = goose ( , Varr. R. R. 3, 10, 3 ; Col. 8, 14, 4 ; cf. Schneid. Gram. II. p. 7; Bentl. ad Hor. S. 2, 8, 88 ; Neue, Formenl. I. p. 612 sq.), a goose;…

Anser.opening: a petulant and obscene poet ( Ov. Tr. 2, 435 ), a friend of the triumvir Antonius , who presented him with an estate at Falernum ( Cic. Phil. 13, 5 ). Acc. to Servius, Virgil makes a sportive allusion to him in Ecl. 9,…

ansercŭlus.opening: dim. anser , a little goose , a gosling , Col. 8, 14, 7 .

ansĕrīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to geese : genus, Col. 8, 5, 10 ; Plin. 10, 22, 29, § 56: pedes, id. 11, 47, 107, § 257 : adeps, goose-grease, id. 30, 8, 22, § 133 al. : lana, down, Dig. 32, 68 .

Ansibarĭi.opening: a Cheruscan tribe on the western shore of the Weser , Tac. A. 13, 55 ; 13, 56 ; cf. Mann. Germ. 156 sq.

ansŭla.opening: dim. ansa , a little handle : cymbii, App. M. 11, p. 258, 37 .— A small ring or hook , App. M. 4, p. 143, 41 .— A small loop at the edge of sandals for the ties , Val. Max. 8, 12 fin.

antăchātēs.opening: , = ἀνταχάτης , a precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 139 , where Jan reads aethachates; others still, autachates.

antae.opening: perh. ante, q. v. , pillars or pilasters on each side of (i.e. opposite sides of) doors or at the corners of buildings , Vitr. 3, 1 ; 4, 4 .—Hence, aedes in antis, a temple with pilasters on the corners , Vitr. 4, 7 .

Antaeŏpŏlītes.opening: ( ), , , a district of Upper Ægypt , Plin. 5, 9, 9, § 49 .

Antaeus.opening: , = Ἀνταῖος , a huge giant in Libya , slain by Hercules , Ov. M. 9, 184 ; Luc. 4, 590 sq.

antăgōnista.opening: , = ἀνταγωνιστής , an adversary , opponent , antagonist , Hier. Vit. Hil. fin.

antămoebaeus.opening: adj. , pes, in verse (opp. amoebaeus, q. v.), composed of two short , two long , and a short syllable , as, e. g. mănĭfēstārĕt; cf. Diom. 3, p. 478 P.

Antandrŏs.opening: ( ), , , = Ἄντανδρος , a maritime town in Mysia , now Antandro (acc. to Thuc. 8, 108, an Æolic colony), Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 123 ; cf. Mann. Asia Min. 3, 418.—Hence, , , adj. , of Antandros , Cic. ad Q. Fr. 1, 2, 2 .

antăpŏcha.opening: , = ἀνταποχή , the writing by which a debtor showed that he had paid a debt , Just. Cod. 4, 21, 18 (opp. apocha).

antăpŏdŏsis.opening: , = ἀνταπόδοσις ; in rhet., the application of a similitude to the object compared, Quint. 8, 3, 77 ; v. apodosis.

Antărădos.opening: ( ), , , a harbor and town in the northern part of Phœnicia and over against the island of Aradus , whence its name , Tab. Peuting. Itin. Ant.; cf. Plin. 5, 20, 17, § 78 .

antarctĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀνταρκτικός , southern , Hyg. Astr. 1, 6 ; App. de Mundo, p. 57 (in Varr. L. L. 9, § 24 Müll., written as a Greek word).

antārium bellum.opening: : quod ante urbem geritur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 8 Müll. [ante].

antārĭus.opening: adj. ἀνταίρω, to raise against , that serves for raising up : funes, the cables for raising a scaffold , stage , mast , and the like, Vitr. 10, 3 .

antĕ.grammar: whence antidea, antideo prep. adv. prep. adv.
antĕ.opening: (old form , , antidhac; v. antea, anteeo, and antehac) [Gr. ἀντί , over against, facing, ἄντα, ἄντην ; Sanscr. anti = over against; Germ. ant- in Ant-wort = Goth. anda-vaurdi, an answer, anda-nahti, the night before],…

antĕā.opening: temp. adv. (old form * or , MS., Liv. 22, 10, 6 ; v. Neue, Formenl. II. p. 680) [ante-eā like antehāc, posteā, posthāc, proptereā, quāpropter, etc., in which Corssen, Ausspr. I. p. 769, regards the pron. as an old acc.…

anteactus.opening: , and ; better written separately, and ; v. ante and ago.

antĕ-ambŭlo.opening: (in poetry four syll.), , ambulo, āre , a forerunner , a servant that went before distinguished personages to clear the way , etc.: anteambulo regis, Mart. 2, 18, 5 ; so id. 10, 74, 3 ; Suet. Vesp. 2 .

Antĕ-cănis.opening: , transl. of Προκύων , a constellation , the Lesser Dog-star , so called as rising before the Dog-star : Antecanis Graio Procyon qui nomine fertur, Cic. N. D. 2, 44, 114 ; id. Arat. 222 ; cf. Plin. 18, 28, 68, § 268 .

antĕ-cantāmentum.opening: cantamen , a prelude , overture , App. M. 11, p. 261, 24 Elm.

antĕ-cantātīvus.opening: adj. canto , of or pertaining to a prelude , Marc. Vict. p. 2500 P.

antĕ-căpĭo.opening: v. a. , to obtain before , to receive before. In gen.: quam appellat πρόληψιν Epicurus, anteceptam animo rei quandam informationem, an inborn , innate idea , Cic. N. D. 1, 16, 43 B. and K. (cf. anticipatio, I.).— Esp.…

antĕ-cēdo.opening: v. n. , to go before , precede (in space), to take the lead , get the start; with dat. , acc. , or absol. Lit. With dat. : ubi ambitionem virtuti videas antecedere, Titin. ap. Non. 499, 8 : si huic rei illa antecedit,…

antĕ-cello.opening: ( perf. and sup. not used), v. n. -cello ; lit., to project; hence, trop., to be prominent , to distinguish one's self; and with dat. or acc. , to distinguish one's self above any one, to surpass , excel , be superior…

antĕ-cēnĭum.opening: cena , a meal taken before the principal meal , a lunch , luncheon , Isid. Orig. 20, 2 ; hence, trop., App. M. 2, p. 121, 29 Elm.

antĕcessĭo.opening: antecedo . A going before , preceding : quae in orbibus conversiones antecessionesque eveniunt, Cic. Tim. 10 .— That which goes before , the antecedent cause , as opp. to the final cause (perh. only in Cic.): homo…

antĕcessor.opening: id. , he that goes before; hence, In milit. lang., antecessores, the forerunners of the army , the advanced guard (cf. antecursor): speculatores et antecessores, Auct. B. Afr. 12: agminis antecessores, * Suet. Vit. 17…

antĕ-curro.opening: v. n. , to run before : stella solem antecurrens, Vitr. 9, 4 .

antĕcursor.opening: antecurro , he that runs before; hence, In milit. lang.: antecursores, the forerunners of the army, the advanced guard, precursors, pioneers, Caes. B. G. 5, 47 ; id. B. C. 1, 16 ; 3, 36 ; so Vulg. Sap. 12, 8 .— In Tert.…

antĕdīco.opening: and , , , etc., v. ante and dico.

antĕ-ĕo.grammar: īvi or ii, īre v. n.
antĕ-ĕo.opening: v. n. (old form = anteeo, like antidea for antea, Plaut. Cist. 2, 1, 3 ; antidit = anteit, id. Trin. 2, 4, 145 Ritschl. In verse the e in ante blends with the foll. e or i , per synaloephen, into one syll.; hence,…

antĕfactus.opening: , um; better written separately, , v. ante and factus.

antĕ-fĕro.opening: v. a. To bear or carry before : ut legum latarum tituli anteferrentur, Tac. A. 1, 8 .—More freq., Trop. , to place before , to prefer , give the preference to , aliquem alicui: longe omnibus unum Demosthenem, Cic. Or. 7…

antĕfixus.opening: Part. , qs. from antefigo, fixed or fastened before , nailed to (rare): truncis arborum antefixa ora, Tac. A. 1, 61 .—Hence, , , ; subst., the little ornaments , images , statues , etc., affixed to the roofs and gutters…

antĕ-gĕnĭtālis.opening: adj. , before birth : experimentum antegenitale, of that which was before our birth, Plin. 7, 55, 56, § 190 .

antĕ-grĕdĭor.opening: v. dep. -gradior , to go before , to precede (perh. only in Cic.): stella Veneris cum antegreditur solem, Cic. N. D. 2, 20, 53 : quicquid est quod deceat, id tum adparet, cum antegressa est honestas, id. Off. 1, 27, 94…

antĕ-hăbĕo.opening: v. a. , to prefer : incredibilia veris, Tac. A. 4, 11 .

antĕ-hāc.grammar: like antidea for antea, and antideo for anteeo
antĕ-hāc.opening: (old form , , Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 79 ; id. Aul. 2, 8, 26 ; id. Cas. prol. 88 ; id. Cist. 1, 1, 1 ; 1, 3, 50 ; id. Ep. 4, 1, 12 ; id. Bacch. 3, 6, 10 ; id. Ps. 1, 1, 14 ; 2, 2, 26 ; id. Poen. 3, 5, 7 .—Antehac, dissyl.,…

Antēlĭi.opening: ( ), , , = Ἀντήλιοι or Ἀνθήλιοι , images of gods that stood before the house door , Tert. Idol. 15 .

antĕlŏgĭum.opening: vox hybrida, from ante-λόγος , a prologue or preamble : Huic argumento antelogium quidem hoc fuit, Plaut. Men. prol. 13 .

antĕ-lŏquĭum.opening: loquor (postclass. and rare). The right of speaking before another , Macr. S. 7, 4 ; 1, 24 .— A proem , preface , Symm. Ep. 8, 23 .

antĕ-lūcānus.opening: adj. lux , before light , before day (class.; only in prose): ex antelucano tempore, Cic. Fam. 15, 4 : gutta roris antelucani, Vulg. Sap. 11, 23 : industria, Cic. Tusc. 4, 19, 44 : cenae, which continue the whole night…

antĕ-lūcĭo.opening: adv. id. , before daybreak (only in App.): aufugere, App. M. 1, p. 107, 8 Elm.: recubare, id. ib. 9 , p. 223, 30.

antĕ-lūcŭlo.opening: adv. id. , before daybreak , App. M. 1, p. 108, 36 Elm.

antĕ-lūdĭum.opening: ludo , a prelude , App. M. 11, p. 260, 31 Elm.

antĕ-mĕrīdĭālis.opening: adj. (a rare form for the foll.), before mid-day or noon : horae, Mart. Cap. 6, p. 195 .

antĕ-mĕrīdĭānus.opening: adj. , before mid-day or noon : sermo, Cic. de Or. 3, 6 : ambulatio, id. ib. 3, 30 : litterae, received before mid-day, id. Att. 13, 23 .

antĕ-mitto.opening: v. a. , to send before , send forwards , send on (rare; for praemittere): equitatum, Caes. B. G. 1, 21 , ubi v. Herz.: antemissis equitibus, id. B. C. 1, 51 ; Sol. 25 .

Antemnae.opening: ( sing. Antemna, Cato. Orig. ap. Prisc. p. 716 P.; Sil. 8, 367 ), , a very ancient town of the Sabines , so called from its situation on the river (ante amnem; cf. Interamna) Anio, where it empties into the Tiber, Varr.…

antĕ-moenĭo.opening: v. a. munio , to furnish with a front or protecting wall , to provide with a rampart : antemoeni aliquā, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 68 dub. (Ritschl, anteveni; v. Ritschl ad h. l.).

antĕ-mūrāle.opening: a protecting wall , an outwork , breastwork (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Hom. 2 : murus et antemurale, Vulg. Isa. 26, 1 : luxitque antemurale, ib. Thren. 2, 8 .

antĕ-mūrānus.opening: adj. murus , that is before the wall : vallum, Amm. 22 (12).

antenna.opening: (also ), , akin to ἀνατείνω, acc. to Doed. , a sail-yard : funes, qui antemnas ad malos destinabant, Caes. B. G. 3, 14 : malis antemnisque de nave in navem trajectis, Liv. 30, 10 Weissenb.: antemnae gemunt, * Hor. C. 1,…

Antēnor.opening: , = Ἀντήνωρ . A noble Trojan , who was in favor of restoring Helen and making peace with the Greeks; after the fall of Troy , he went to Italy and founded Patavium (Padua), Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 247 ; Ov. M. 13, 201 ;…

antĕ-nuptĭālis.opening: adj. , before marriage (only in late Lat.), Justin. Novell. 2, 1 al.

antĕ-paenultĭmus.opening: (less correctly written ), , adj. ; in gram., pertaining to the third syllable from the end, antepenultimate, Diom. p. 425 P.; Mart. Cap. 3, p. 60 al.

antĕ-pagmentum.opening: or , , pango ; in archit., every thing that is used for garnishing the exterior of a house , as the ornaments about the doors , windows , etc., Cato, R. R. 14 ; cf. Vitr. 4, 6 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 8 Müll.; Müll.…

antĕ-passĭo.opening: , a transl. of the Gr. προπάθεια , a presentiment of pain , suffering , etc., Hier. Ep. 97 ad Salv. 9 .

antĕ-pendŭlus.opening: adj. , hanging before (only late Lat.): crines, App. M. 2, p. 125, 4 Elm.; 5, p. 168, 23 Elm.

antĕ-pēs.opening: * The forefoot Cic. Arat. 454 .— = anteambulo, a forerunner , etc., Agroet. Orthogr. p. 2274 P. (in Juv. 7, 143 , the correct read. is ante pedes , Jahn).

antĕ-pīlānus.opening: In milit. lang. The soldiers who fought before the pilani, i. e. the hastati and the principes , Liv. 8, 8 .— In Ammianus, = antesignanus, one who fought before the standards , 16, 12, 20. — Trop. , a competitor , a…

antĕ-pollĕo.opening: v. n. , to be more powerful , to excel , surpass (late Lat.): alicui, App. M. 1, p. 104, 20 Elm.: toto vertice cunctos, id. ib. 7 , p. 189, 35 Elm.

antĕ-pōno.opening: v. a. , to set or place before. Lit. In gen.: equitum locos sedilibus plebis, Tac. A. 15, 32 : propugnacula anteposita, id. ib. 12, 56 . — Esp., to set ( food ) before one (com., pono, as Hor. S. 1, 3, 92 ; Juv. 1, 141…

antĕ-pŏtens.opening: adj. , superior in power or fortune : voluptatibus gaudiisque antepotens, Plaut. Trin. 5, 1, 2 .

antērĭdes.opening: , = ἀντηρίδες ; in archit., counter-props set against a wall to support it, a buttress, Vitr. 10, 1 .

antērĭdĭon.opening: dim. n. , = ἀντηρίδιον , a little prop or support , Vitr. 10, 17 fin. (dub.).

antĕrĭor.opening: adj. comp. [ante] (only in late Lat.), that is before , foremost : pars. Amm. 16, 8 ; 25, 3 .—Of time, previous , former , anterior : litterae tuae, Symm. Ep. 6, 59: reges, Sulp. Sev. Hist. Sacr. 1, 52 al. — * Adv. : ,…

Antĕrōs.opening: , = Ἀντέρως (an opponent of Eros) An avenger of slighted love , Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 60 .— A kind of amethyst , Plin. 37, 9, 40, § 123 .— A slave of Atticus , Cic. Att. 9, 14, 3 ; 11, 1, 1 .

antes.opening: etym. unc., perh. from ante, as before, over against, one another , rows , e. g. of vines, Verg. G. 2, 417 , cf. Paul. ex. Fest. p. 16 Müll.—Also of plants, Col. 10, 376 .—Of ranks of soldiers, Cato ap. Philarg. ad…

antĕ-schŏlānus.opening: , i. schola , a kind of teacher , Petr. 81 .

antescŏlārius.opening: , same as foregoing: ANTE SCOLARIS VIRGINVM (Vestalium), Inscr. Orell. 1175 .

antĕ-signānus.opening: signum , that is before the standard; hence, Lit. : antesignant (sc. milites), a chosen band of Roman soldiers who fought before the standards, and served for their defence, Caes. B. C. 1, 43 ; 1, 57 ; Liv. 22, 5 ; 9,…

ante-sto.opening: or , , v. n. , to stand before , only in a trop. signif., to excel , be superior to; with dat. or acc.; also absol. , to distinguish one's self , to be distinguished : brassica, quae omnibus holeribus antistat, Cato, R.…

antestor.opening: v. dep [acc. to Corssen, Ausspr. II. p. 564, from an-, the Gr. ἀνά , as in anhelo, q. v. fin. , and testor; acc. to others, from ante and testor], a word peculiar to judicial proceedings, to call up as a witness before…

antĕurbāna.opening: : anteurbana: praedia urbi propinqua, Paul. ex Fest. p. 8 Müll.

antē-vĕnĭo.opening: v. n. , to come before , get the start of , anticipate. Lit. , with dat. or acc. (cf. Rudd. II. p. 137): temport, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 66 (tempus, Claud. 23, 152 ): exercitum, Sall. J. 48, 2 ; so id. ib. 56, 2 : consilia…

antĕ-ventŭlus.opening: adj. venio , coming before , hanging before , = antependulus (perh. only in App.): comae, App. M. 9, 231, 5 : crines, id. Flor. 3, p. 342, 2 Elm.

antĕversĭo.opening: anteverto , an anticipating , preventing : anteversio et praegressus, Amm. 21, 5 fin.

antĕ-verto.opening: (archaic ), , v. a. (as dep antevortar, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 5, 1 ), to place one's self before , to go or come before , to precede. Lit. : maerores antevortunt gaudiis, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 60 : stella tum antevertens, tum…

antĕ-vĭo.opening: v. n. via , to go before , Ven. Fort. 4, 26.

antĕ-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly before; with acc. (only post-Aug.; in Verg. A. 9, 47 , and 12, 455 Rib., it is written apart, ante volo): currum, Stat. Th. 3, 427 : agmen, Sil. 12, 600 : Zephyros, Claud. Phoen. 21 .

Antĕ-vorta.opening: verto , the name of a goddess who reminds men of things past (opp. Postvorta), Macr. S. 1, 7 (in Ov. F. 1, 633 , and Serv. ad Verg. A. 8, 336 , called Porrima).

anthălĭum.opening: , = ἀνθάλιον , a kind of bulbous esculent root : Cyperus esculentus, Linn.; Plin. 21, 15, 52, § 88 .

anthēdon.opening: , = ἀνθηδών , a species of the medlar-tree , the Greek medlar : Mespilus tanacetifolia, Linn.; Plin. 15, 20, 22, § 84 .

Anthēdon.opening: , = Ἀνθηδών , A town and harbor in Bœotia , opposite the island Eubœa (hence called Euboica), the birthplace of Glaucus , and noted for its great traffic in sponges , now Paleo-kastro , Ov. M. 13, 905 ; 7, 232 ; cf.…

anthĕmis.opening: , = ἀνθεμίς , the herb chamomile : Anthemis, Linn.; Plin. 22, 21, 26, § 53 .

anthĕmum.opening: , = ἄνθεμον , an herb good for calculi , Plin. 26, 8, 55, § 9 .

Anthĕmūs.opening: , = Ἀνθεμοῦς . A region in Macedonia , Plin. 4, 10, 17, § 36 . — A town in Mesopotamia , Plin. 6, 26, 30, § 118 ; called also , (sc. urbs), Tac. A. 6, 41 .— A river of Colchis , Plin. 6, 5, 5, § 15 .—Hence, , , adj. ,…

Anthĕmūsia.opening: a town in Macedonia , Plin. 5, 24, 21, § 86 ; also called , q. v.

Anthĕmūsa.opening: an old name of the island of Samos , Plin. 5, 31, 37, § 135 .

anthēra.opening: , = ἀνθηρά (blooming), a medicine composed of flowers , Cels. 6, 11 med. ; Plin. 24, 9, 42, § 69 .

anthĕrĭcos.opening: , = ἀνθέρικος , the stalk of the asphodel , Plin. 21, 17, 68, § 109 ; 22, 22, 32, § 67 .

anthĭas.opening: , = ἀνθίας , a sea-fish unknown to us , which was difficult to catch , Plin. 9, 59, 85, § 180 ; Ov. Hal. 45 .

anthĭnus.opening: adj. , = ἀνθινός , gathered from flowers : mel, Plin. 11, 14, 14, § 34 .

anthŏlŏgĭca.opening: , = ἀνθολογικά , anthology , a work consisting of choice thoughts , proverbs , poems , etc., Plin. 21, 3, 9, § 13 .

anthrăcĭnus.opening: adj. , = ἀνθρἀκινος , coal-black , Varr. ap. Non. p. 550, 5 .

anthrăcītes.opening: , = ἀνθρακίτης , a kind of blood-stone , Plin. 36, 20, 38, § 148 .

anthrăcītis.opening: , = ἀνθρακῖτις , a kind of carbuncle , the coal-carbuncle , Plin. 37, 7, 27, § 99 ; in Sol. 37 fin. called , , , = ἀνθρακίας .

anthrax.opening: , = ἄνθραξ (coal). Natural cinnabar (the color of which is like a burning coal), Vitr. 7, 8 .— In medic., a virulent ulcer (in pure Lat., carbunculus), Aem. Macr. de Herb. c. de Sabina.

Anthrax.opening: . , , = Ἄνθραξ , name of a slave , Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 8 .

anthriscus.opening: , or , , , = ἄνθρισκον , the southern chervil : Scandix australis, Linn.; Plin. 22, 22, 38, § 81 ; 21, 15, 52, § 89 .

anthrōpō^grăphŏs.opening: , = ἀνθρωπογράφος , portrait-painter , an epithet of the painter Dionysius, Plin. 35, 10, 37, § 113 .

anthrōpŏmorphītae.opening: , = ἀνθρωπομορφῖται , heretics that attributed to God a human form , Aug. Haeres. ad Quod vult Deum.—Hence, , , adj. , professing the error of such heretics : haeresis, Isid. Orig. 8, 5 .

anthrōpŏphăgus.opening: , = ἀνθρωποφάγος , a man-eater , a cannibal , Plin. 4, 12, 26, § 88 ; 6, 17, 20, § 53 ; 6, 30, 35, § 195 .

anthus.opening: , = ἄνθος (cf. τὸ ἄνθος = blossom, brilliancy), a small bird , prob. the yellow wagtail : Motacilla flava, Linn.; Plin. 10, 42, 57, § 116 ; 10, 74, 95, § 206 .

anthyllĭon.opening: , = ἀνθύλλιον , a plant , acc. to Sprengel, the Cretan pitchplant : Cressa Cretica, Linn.; Plin. 26, 8, 51, § 84 (called in Plin. 21, 99, 103, § 175 , also anthyllum).

anthyllis.opening: , ïdis, , = ἀνθυλλίς , a plant , acc. to Sprengel, the musk-ivy : Teucrium iva, Linn.; Plin. 26, 15, 90, § 160 .

antiae.opening: (cf. Charis. p. 20 P.) [ante], the hair growing upon the forehead , forelock; of Apollo, App. Flor. 3, p. 342, 1 ; of lions, Tert. Pall. 4 ; of the hair of women, Paul. ex Fest. s. h. v. p. 15 Müll.

antĭbăsis.opening: ( ), , , = ἀντίβασις (counter-basis), the hindmost small pillar at the pedestal of the ballista , Vitr. 10, 17 ; cf. id. 10, 15 .

antĭbŏrēus.opening: adj. , = ἀντιβόρειος , turned toward the north : horologium, Vitr. 9, 9 .

antĭcătēgŏrĭa.opening: , = ἀντικατηγορία , a recrimination , counter-plea , Aug. 3 : contra Cresc. 26; 74 fin. (in Quint. 3, 10, 4 , and 7, 2, 9, written as Greek, Halm).

Antĭcăto.opening: the title of Cœsar's reply to Cicero's panegyric of Cato Uticensis , the title of which was , Quint. 1, 5, 68 ; Juv. 6, 337 ; Gell. 4, 16 ; cf. Bähr, Lit. Gesch. 267 and 462; Teuffel, Rom. Lit. § 182, 7.

Antī^christus.opening: , = Ἀντίχριστος , the Antichrist (eccl. Lat.); Vulg. 1 Joan. 2, 18 ; 2, 22; 4, 3; ib. 2 Joan. 7 ; very freq. in the Church fathers.

antichthŏnes.opening: , = ἀντίχθονες , = antipodes ( ἀντίπόδες ), the antipodes Plin. 6, 22, 24, § 81 ; Mel. 1, 1 ; 1, 9 .

antĭcĭpātĭo.opening: anticipo . A preconception , the innate notion of a thing formed before receiving instruction concerning it , Gr. πρόληψις (only in Cic.): deorum, Cic. N. D. 1, 16, 43 : sive anticipatio sive praenotio deorum, id. ib.…

antĭ-cĭpo.opening: v. a. ante-capio . To take before one or before the time, to anticipate something. With acc. : vigilias, Vulg. Psa. 76, 5 : nos, ib. ib. 78, 8 : ita est informatum anticipatumque mentibus nostris, etc., already known,…

Anticlēa.opening: or , , , = Ἀντικλεία , the mother of Ulysses , Hyg. Fab. 201 ; App. de Deo Socr. 24, p. 55 ; Serv. ad Verg. A. 6, 529 ; in Cicero , erroneously put for the nurse of Ulysses , Euryclea , Cic. Tusc. 5, 16, 46 .

antīcus.opening: adj. ante , that is in front , foremost , Paul. ex Fest. p. 220 Müll.: antica (pars) ad meridiem, postica ad septentrionem, Varr. L. L. 7, § 7 Müll.: pars, * Cic. Tim. 10 .

Antĭcўra.opening: , = Ἀντίκιρρα , Dicaearch. and Strabo; Ἀντίκυρρα , Eustath.; and Ἀντίκυρα , which the Romans followed. A town in Phocis , on a peninsula (which Pliny and Gellius erroneously call an island), on a bay of the Corinthian…

antĭdactўlus.opening: adj. , = ἀντιδάκτυλος : pes, a reversed dactyl , ˘˘¯ (e. g. lĕgĕrēnt), Mar. Vict. p. 2488 P.

antĭdŏtum.opening: , and or , , (cf. Scrib. Larg. Comp. 99, 106 , and passages cited there), = ἀντίδοτον ( -ος ), a counterpoison. Lit. : antidota raro, sed interdum necessaria sunt, Cels. 5, 23 ; Phaedr. 1, 14, 3 : se antidotum daturum,…

antigerio.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 8 Müll. [perh. antegero]; cf. Quint. 1, 6, 40 ; 8, 3, 25 .

Antignōtus.opening: , = Ἀντίγνωτος , an artist that cast statues , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 86 .

Antĭgŏnē.opening: , or , , , = Ἀντιγονη . A daughter of the Theban king Œdipus , Hyg. Fab. 72 : Antigones, Juv. 8, 228 .— A daughter of the Trojan king Laomedon : Antigonen, Ov. M. 6, 93 ; Serv. ad Verg. G. 2, 320 .

Antĭgŏnēa.opening: , = Ἀντιγόνεια or Ἀντιγονία , the name of several towns. In Epirus , Liv. 32, 5 ; 43, 23 .—Hence, : ager, Liv. 43, 23 ; and , , , its inhabitants , Plin. 4 , praef. 1, 1.— In Macedonia , Liv. 44, 10 .— In Arcadia ,…
