Antĭlĭbănus.opening: , = Ἀντιλίβανος , a mountain range in Phœnicia , opposite to Libanus , now Jebel esh-Shurky , Cic. Att. 2, 16 ; cf. Mann. Phoen. 270 sq.

Antĭlŏchus.opening: , = Ἀντίλοχος , a son of Nestor , slain by Hector before Troy , Hor. C. 2, 9, 14 ; Ov. H. 1, 15 ; Juv. 10, 253 .

Antĭmăchus.opening: , = Ἀντίμαχος . A Greek poet of Colophon , a contemporary of Socrates and Plato , and author of a Thebaid , Cic. Brut. 51, 191 ; Cat. 95, 10 ; Prop. 3, 32, 45 .— A centaur slain by Cœneus in the contest with the Lapithœ…

antĭmĕtăbŏlē.opening: , = ἀντιμεταβολή , a rhet. fig., a reciprocal interchange , in Auct. ad Her. 4, 28, 39 , called commutatio, e. g.: non ut edam vivo, sed ut vivam edo, Isid. Orig. 2, 21, p. 81 Lind. (in Quint. 9, 3, 85 , written as…

antĭnŏmĭa.opening: , = ἀντινομία , a contradiction between laws , Quint. 7, 7, 1 ; so id. 7, 10, 2 ; 3, 6, 45 .

Antĭŏchēa.opening: or (like Alexandrēa, Alexandrīa, q. v.; cf. Prisc. p. 588 P., and Ochsn. Eclog. 143), , , = Ἀντιόχεια , Antioch. The name of several cities. The most distinguished is that founded by Seleucus Nicator , and named after…

Antĭŏchēnus.opening: adj. Antiochus , of or belonging to King Antiochus : pecunia, received from him, Gell. 4, 18 ; 7, 19 fin. (cf. 2. Antiochensis).

Antĭŏchēus.opening: or , , adj. , = Ἀντιόχειος , of or pertaining to the philosopher Antiochus : ista Antiochea contemnit, Cic. Ac. 2, 36, 115 ; id. Att. 13, 19 .

Antĭŏchus.opening: , = Ἀντίοχος . The name of several Syrian kings , among whom Antiochus Magnus was most distinguished , on account of his war with the Romans , Liv. 31, 14 ; 33, 13 sq. al.; Nep. Hann. 2, 7 ; Cic. de Or. 2, 18, 75 ; Cic.…

Antĭpăter.opening: (later form, ANTIPATRVS, Inscr. Orell. 4727 ), , = Ἀντίπατρος . One of the generals and successors of Alexander the Great , the father of Cassander , Just. 11, 7 ; 11, 12 ; 13, 5 al. ; Cic. Off. 2, 14, 48 .— His…

antĭpăthēs.opening: , = ἀντιπαθής (serving as remedy for suffering), a black kind of coral used as a preventive of witchcraft , Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 145 .

antĭpăthĕs.opening: , = ἀντιπαθές , a charm against pain , Lael. ap. App. Mag. 30 .

antĭpăthīa.opening: , = ἀντιπάθεια , the natural aversion of two things to each other , antipathy (opp. concordia), Plin. 37, 4, 15, § 59 ; so id. 20, 4, 13, § 28 ; 24, 9, 41, § 67 al.

Antĭpā^trĭa.opening: , = Ἀντιπατρία , a town in Macedonia , on the borders of Illyria , Liv. 31, 27 .

Antĭphătes.opening: , = Ἀντιφάτης . A king of the Lœstrygones , who sunk the fleet of the Greeks returning from Troy with Ulysses , and devoured one of his companions , Ov. M. 14, 234 sq. ; Juv. 14, 20 ; Sil. 8, 531 .— A son of Sarpedon ,…

antĭpherna.opening: , = ἀντίφερνα , the return-present which the bridegroom brought to the bride , Cod. Just. 5, 3, 20 .

antĭphrăsis.opening: (better written as Gr.), , , = αντίφρασις , the use of a word in a sense opposite to its proper meaning; as, lucus , quod minime luceat, Diom. p. 458 P.; cf. Charis. p. 247 P. al.

antĭpŏdes.opening: , = ἀντίποδες , the antipodes , Lact. 3, 23 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 16, 9; Serv. ad Verg. A. 6, 532 ; hence ironic. of banqueters who turn night to day, Sen. Ep. 122 (in Cic. Ac. 2, 39, 123 , written as Greek).

antiptōsis.opening: , = ἀντίπτωσις , a gram. fig., the putting of one case for another , Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 577 ; 2, 283 ; 6, 727 ; 10, 653; 11, 56 al.

antīquārĭus.opening: adj. antiquus , pertaining to antiquity. Adj. : ars, the art of reading and copying ancient MSS., Hier. Ep. ad Flor. 5, 1 .—Hence, Subst. : , , One that is fond of or employs himself about antiquities , an antiquarian ,…

antīquātĭo.opening: antiquo ; in judicial lang., an abrogating , annulling , repealing : poenarum, Cod. Th. 6, 55, 4.

antīquo.opening: v. a. antiquus; cf.: veto, vetus . In class. Lat. only a t. t. of civil life, to leave it in its ancient state , to restore a thing to its former condition (antiquare est in modum pristinum reducere, Paul. ex Fest. p.…

antirrhīnon.opening: ( ), , , = ἀντίρρινον ; also , , , = ἀνἀρρινον , a plant , wild lion's-mouth : Antirrhinum Orontium, Linn.: antirrhinum, Plin. 25, 10, 80, § 129 Jan; cf. App. Herb. 86 .

antīsăgōgē.opening: , = ἀντεισαγωγή , a figure of speech by which one thing adduced is opposed to another , a counter-assertion , Mart. Cap. 5, p. 172 .

antiscĭi.opening: , = ἀντίσκιο . (counter-shadows), people on the other side of the equator , whose shadows are cast in the opposite direction from ours , Amm. 22, 15 fin.

antĭsŏphista.opening: , = ἀντισοφιστής , a counter-sophist , i. e. a grammarian who takes the opposite side of a question (only post-Aug.), Quint. 11, 3, 127 ; Suet. Tib. 11 ; so id. Gram. 9 .

antispŏdos.opening: , = ἀντίσποδος , ashes used instead of spodium , Plin. 34, 13, 35, § 133 .

Antissa.opening: , = Ἄντισσα , a town in the southern part of the island of Lesbos , now Kalas Limneonas , Liv. 45, 31 ; Ov. M. 15, 287 ; Plin. 5, 31, 39, § 89 .—Hence, , , , inhabitants of Antissa , Liv. 45, 31 .

antistātus.opening: v. antesto , superiority in rank : angelorum, Tert. adv. Val. 13 .

Antisthĕnes.opening: , = Ἀντισθένης , a pupil of Socrates , teacher of Diogenes , and founder of the Cynic philosophy : Antisthenes, Cic. N. D. 1, 13, 32 ; so id. de Or. 3, 17, 62 .—In plur. : Antisthenae multi, Gell. 14, 1, 29 .

antĭthĕus.opening: , = ἀντίθεος (a counter-deity), one who pretends to be God , Arn. 4, p. 134 .—Hence, the devil , Lact. 2, 9 .

Antĭum.opening: , = Ἄντιον . An ancient town in Latium distinguished for the temple of Fortune ( Hor. C. 1, 35, 1 ), not far from the sea-coast , now Porto d'Anzio , the birthplace of Nero, Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 27 ; Inscr. Orell. 1738 ;…

Antĭus.opening: adj. , name of a Roman gens; hence, Antia lex (by Antius Restio), against prodigality, Gell. 2, 24 ; Macr. S. 2, 13 .

antizeugmĕnon.opening: , = ἀντιζεύγμενον , a grammatical figure , by which several clauses are referred to one verb , Mart. Cap. 5, p. 176 .

antlĭa.opening: , = ἀντία , a machine for drawing water , worked with the foot , a pump , Mart. 9, 14, 3 ; * Suet. Tib. 51 .

Antŏdĭcē.opening: one of the Danaids , Hyg. Fab. 170 .

Antōnĭaster.opening: dim. from Antonius, as surdaster from surdus, parasitaster from parasitus; cf. Prisc. p. 628 P. , a servile imitator of the orator Antonius , a petty Antony : hic noster Antoniaster, Cic. Varen. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 617…

antŏnŏmăsĭa.opening: , = ἀντονομασία , a rhetorical figure , by which , instead of the name , an epithet of a person is employed (e. g. instead of Scipio, Eversor Carthaginis; instead of Achilles, Pelides; instead of Juno, Saturnia, etc.),…

antŏnŏmăsīvus.opening: adj. antonomasia , pertaining to or forming an antonomasia , Serv. ad Verg. A. 2, 171 ; 2, 615 .

antroare.opening: : gratias referre, to requite , Paul. ex Fest. p. 9 Müll.; cf. Kuhn in Zeitschr. für Vergl. Sprachf. 7, p. 64 sq.; Vanicek, Etym. p. 291.

Antrōn.opening: , = Ἀντρών (Hom. Il. 2, 697), a town in Thessaly (Phthiotis), now Fano , Liv. 42, 42 ; 42, 67 .

antrum.opening: , = ἄντρον , a cave , cavern , grotto (almost entirely confined to the poets). Lit. : succedere antro, Verg. E. 5, 19 : subire antra, Ov. M. 1, 121 : occulere se antro, Val. Fl. 8, 315 : ingens, Verg. A. 6, 42 : gratum,…

anxĭo.opening: v. a. anxius , to make uneasy or anxious (only in late Lat.): anxiatum iri, App. M. 4, p. 155, 14 : dum anxiaretur cor meum, Vulg. Psa. 60, 3 : anxiatus est super me spiritus, ib. ib. 142, 4 .

anxĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of anxiety; act. , causing anxiety , pain , uneasiness , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2 .

anxĭtūdo.opening: (mostly ante-class.), and , , (post-class. for the class. anxietas) [id.], anxiety , trouble , anguish : animi, Pac. ap. Non. p. 72, 33 ; Att. ib. 28 ; 29 .—Once also in Cic.: anxitudo prona ad luctum, Rep. 2, 41:…

aphthae.opening: , = ἄφθαι , an eruption in the mouth , the thrush , Marc. Emp. 11 (in Cels. 6, 11 , written as Greek).

aplănēs.opening: adj. , = ἀπλανής , not moving about , standing firm , Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, 9 and 11.

aplysĭae.opening: , = ἀπλυσίαι , an inferior kind of sponge , Plin. 9, 45, 69, § 150 .

ap-pango.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to fasten to , Paul. ex Fest. p. 8 Müll.

appărāmentum.opening: ( ), , apparo , a preparing , preparation; concr., that which is prepared , Inscr. Orell. 2332 ; cf. apparator.

appărātē.opening: ( ), adv. , v. apparo, P a. fin.

appărātĭo.opening: ( ), , f [apparo], a preparing , preparation (rare) adparatio popularium munerum, Cic. Off. 2, 16, 56 ; Vitr. 2, 10 .— Trop. apparatio atque artificiosa diligentia, preparation , Cic. Inv. 1, 18 , so Auct. ad Her. 1, 8…

appărātor.opening: ( ), , id. , one that prepares , Inscr. Orell. 2325 ; cf. apparamentum.

appărātrix.opening: ( ), , apparator , she that prepares , Hier. Ep. 18 .

appārĭtūra.opening: ( ), , id. , a serving , service , Suet. Gram. 9 .

arcĕra.opening: arca, Curt. , a covered carriage for sick persons : quod ex tabulis vehiculum erat factum ut arca, arcera dictum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 140 Müll.; Gell. 20, 1, 29 ; Non. p. 55, 26 . So in the laws of the XII. Tables, Fragm.…

Arcĕsĭlas.opening: ( , , Gell. 3, 5 ), ( acc. Arcesilam, Cic. Ac. 2, 24, 76 : Arcesilan, Mel. 1, 18, 1 ), = Ἀρκεσίλας (- αος ). Arcesilas (mostly in this form), a Greek philosopher of Pitane , a pupil of Polemon , and founder of the…

Arcēsĭus.opening: , = Ἀρκείσιος , son of Jupiter , father of Laertes , and grandfather of Ulysses , Ov. M. 13, 144 .

arcessītĭo.opening: arcesso , a calling , summons : dies propriae arcessitionis, i. e. the day of death , Cypr. de Mortal. extr.

arcessītor.opening: id. , one that calls or fetches another (perh. only in the two foll. exs.): nemo arcessitor ex proximo, Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 45 .—Hence, in judic. lang., an accuser , Amm. 29, 1, 44 .

arcessītus.opening: arcesso , a calling , summons (very rare; only in abl. sing. ): tuo arcessitu venio huc, Plaut. Stich. 2, 3, 3 : cum ad eum ipsius rogatu arcessituque venissem, * Cic. N. D. 1, 6, 15 ; Amm. 31, 10 .

arcesso.opening: (and ), , v. a. ( inf. arcessire and arcessiri, like lacessiri instead of lacessi, freq. and in the best class. writers, though the MSS. and editt. vary very much; cf. Struve, p. 198.—The form accerso, used freq. by…

arceuthĭnus.opening: adj. , = ἀρκεύθινος , of the juniper-tree : ligna, Vulg. Par. 2, 2, 8 .

Archaeŏpŏlis.opening: , = Ἀρχαιόπολις , a town in Lydia , Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 117 .

archangĕlus.opening: , = ἀρχάγγελος , an archangel (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. 1 Thess. 4, 15 ; ib. Judas, 9; Hier. Ruf. 1, 6 ; Tert. adv. Val. 19 .

archē.opening: , = ἀρχή (beginning). One of the Æons of Valentinus , Tert. adv. Val. 35 .— , one of the four muses; a daughter of the younger Jupiter , Cic. N. D. 3, 21, 54 .

Archĕlāus.opening: , = Ἀρχέλαος . A philosopher of Miletus , pupil of Anaxagoras , and teacher of Socrates , Cic. Tusc. 5, 4, 10 .— A king of Macedonia , son of Perdiccas , and friend of Euripides , Cic. Tusc. 5, 12, 34 ; Just. 7, 4 ;…

archēōta.opening: , = ἀρχειώτης , a keeper of the archives , a recorder , Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 10 .

archĕtўpus.opening: adj. , = ἀρχέτυπος , that was first made , original (very rare): archetypos servare Cleanthas, i. e. the original statues of Cleanthes, Juv. 2, 7 . So Martial calls the original MSS. of his epigrams, archetypae nugae,…

archēzōstis.opening: the bryony , also called ampeloleuce: Bryonia alba, Linn.; Plin. 23, 1, 16, § 21 .

Archĭas.opening: , = Ἀρχίας . Aulus Licinius, a Greek poet of Antiochia , who became distinguished by Cicero's defence of him; v. Cic. Or. pro Archia.— A cabinet-maker; hence, , , um: lecti, a couch made by Archias , and from the…

archĭā^trĭa.opening: , = ΑΡΧΙΑΤΡΙΑ , the rank of chief physician , Cod. Th. 13, 3, 8.

archĭā^trus.opening: ( ), , , = ἀρχίατρος ; in the time of the emperors, the chief physician , who was at the same time physician in ordinary to the emperor , Cod. Th. 12, 13; Inscr. Orell. 3994 ; 4017 ; 4226 al.

archĭbūcŭlus.opening: ( ), , , = ἀρχι-βούκολος , a chief priest of Bacchus , Inscr. Orell. 2335 ; 2351 ; 2352 .

archĭdĭācŏnus.opening: , = ἀρχιδιάκονος , an archdeacon , Hier. ad Pamm. Ep. 61, 4 ; Sid. Ep. 4, 25 .

archĭĕreus.opening: , = ἀρχιερεύς , a chief priest , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 28 fin. ; so Inscr. Orell. 2160 ; 2543 ; 2627 .

archĭĕrōsўna.opening: , = ἀρχιεπωσύνη , the chief priest's office , Cod. Th. 12, 1, 112.

archĭgallus.opening: , = ΑΡΧΙΓΑΛΛΟΣ (cf. Gallus), a chief priest of Cybele , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 70 ; Tert. Apol. 25 ; Inscr. Orell. 2320 sq. al.

archĭgĕron.opening: , = ΑΡΧΙΓΕΡΩΝ , chief of the old men , a title under the emperors, Cod. Th. 14, 27, 1.

archĭgŭbernus.opening: , = ΑΡΧΙΚΥΒΕΡΝΟΣ , chief pilot or helmsman , Dig. 36, 1, 46 ; Inscr. Orell. 3634 .

Archĭlŏchus.opening: , = Ἀρχίλοχος , a Greek poet of Paros , who, acc. to Cic. Tusc. 1, 1, 3 , lived in the age of Romulus; but, acc. to Nep. ap. Gell. 17, 21, 8 , was a contemporary of Tullus Hostilius; he was the originator of iambic…

archĭmandrīta.opening: , = ἀρχιμανδρίτης , a chief or principal of monks , an abbot , Sid. Ep. 8, 14 .

Archĭmēdes.opening: ( gen. Archimedi, Cic. Rep. 1, 14, 21 ; 1, 14, 22 ; cf. Schne id. Gr. II. 163 sq. ; Rudd. I. p. 58, n. 71; Neue, Formenl. I. p. 333; acc. Archimeden, Cic. Verr. 4, 58, 131 ; Liv. 25, 31, 9 : Archimedem, Cic. Tusc. 5,…

archĭmīmus.opening: , = ἀρχίμιμος , chief mimic actor or pantomime , * Suet. Vesp. 19 ; so Inscr. Orell. 2625 .—Hence, fem. ARCHIMIMA, ae, chief mimic actress , Inscr. Orell. 4760 .

archĭpīrāta.opening: , = ἀρχιπειρατής , a leader of pirates , Cic. Off. 2, 11, 40 ; so Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 25 ; 2, 5, 29 ; Liv. 37, 11 .

archĭpresbўter.opening: , = ἀρχιπρεσβύτερος , the chief of the presbyteri, arch-priest , Hier. Ep. 4 ad Rustic.

archĭ-săcerdos.opening: vox hybrida , chief priest , Ven. Carm. 3, 13, 1.

archĭsўnăgōgus.opening: , = ἀρχισυνάγωγος , the priest that was chief ruler of the synagogue , Vulg. Marc. 5, 22 ; ib. Luc. 13, 14 ; ib. Act. 18, 8 al. ; Lampr. Alex. Sev. 28 fin. ; Cod. Th. 16, 8, 13 al.

archĭtectŏnĭcē.opening: , = ἀρχιτεκτονική (sc. τέχνη ), the art of building , architecture , Quint. 2, 21, 8 .

archĭtectŏnĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀρχιτεκτονικός , relating to architecture : rationes, Vitr. 9, 4 .

archĭtector.opening: v. dep. architectus . Lit. , to build , construct , make (rare): situm loci cujusdam ad suum arbitrium fabricari et architectari, Auct. ad Her. 3, 19, 32 : Olympium, Vitr. 7 , praef. 17: cardines, id. 9, 4 .— Trop. , to…

archĭtectūra.opening: id. , the art of building , architecture , = ἀρχιτεκτονία . Lit. , * Cic. Off. 1, 42, 151 ; Vitr. 1, 1 ; 1, 3 .— Trop. , of historical representation: Specus ipsa quā concameratur architecturā! Plin. 11, 24, 28, § 82 .

archĭtectus.opening: , = ἀρχιτέκτων (the usual form, while † , , is rare). Form architectus. A master-builder , architect : fabri architectique, Plaut. Mil. 3, 3, 45 : Philo architectus, Cic. de Or. 1, 14, 62 ; so id. Fam. 9, 2 ; Vitr. 1, 1…

Archītis.opening: the name of Venus among the Assyrians , acc. to Macr. S. 1, 21 .

archĭ-triclīnus.opening: vox hybrida; triclinium , = tricliniarcha, one that presides at the table , the master of a feast , Vulg. Joan. 2, 8 ; 2, 9 bis.

archīum.opening: or , , , = ἀρχεῖον , the archives (post-class.), Dig. 48, 19, 9, § 6 ; Mel. 3, 8 fin. : antiquissimarum gentium archiva, Tert. Apol. 19 ; so id. adv. Marc. 4, 7 .

archōn.opening: , = ἄρχων (a ruler), the highest magistrate at Athens after the abrogation of royal authority , an archon , * Cic. Fat. 9, 19 ; cf. Vell. 1, 2 and 8.

Archȳtas.opening: ( nom. Archўtă, Sid. Carm. 2, 176 ), = Ἀρχύτας , a Pythagorean philosopher of Tarentum , and friend of Plato , Cic. Tusc. 4, 36, 78 ; 5, 23, 64 ; id. Sen. 12, 41 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 1, 8 ; Vitr. 7 , praef. 14 and 9; Hor.…

arcĭfīnālis.opening: , or , , , adj. arceo - finis ; among surveyors, agri, lands received in possession and built upon by victors after expelling the previous owners (whence the term), Sic. Fl. p. 3; Front. p. 38 ; Hyg Lim. p. 160. Defined…

arcīon.opening: , = ἀρκεῖον , a plant (in pure Lat., persollata), Plin. 25, 9, 66, § 113 .

Arcĭ-pŏtens.opening: adj. arcus , skilful with the bow , a skilful archer , an epithet of Apollo, Val. Fl. 5, 17 .

arcirma.opening: (this is the correct read., not ), , arcera , a kind of small carriage , Paul. ex Fest. p. 15 Müll.; v. Müll. ad h. l.

Arcĭ-tĕnens.grammar: like arquus for arcus, quur for cur entis adj.
Arcĭ-tĕnens.opening: (in MSS. also , , etc.), , adj. arcus-teneo , carrying a bow , bow-bearing , in imitation of the Gr. Τοζοφόρος . A poet. epithet of Apollo and of Diana; of Apollo, Naev. Bell. Pun. ap. Macr. S. 6, 5 (p. 14 Vahl.); Ov.…

arctĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀρκτικός (pertaining to the constellation of the Bear, ἄρκτος ; hence), northern , arctic : circulus, Hyg. Astr. 1, 6 .

arctĭon.opening: , = ἄρκτιον , a plant , also called arcturus, Plin. 27, 5, 16, § 33 .

Arctŏphўlax.opening: , = Ἀρκτοφύλαξ , the Bear-keeper , a constellation , usu. called Bootes, Cic. Arat. Phaen. 394 B. and K.; id. N. D. 2, 42, 109 (as transl. from Arat. 92); so Luc. 8, 180 .

arctŏs.opening: ( nom. arctos, Verg. G. 1, 246 ; acc. arcton, Ov. M. 2, 132 ; 13, 293 ; id. F. 2, 192 ; Verg. G. 1, 138 : arctum, Cic. N. D. 2, 42, 109 (in verse); nom. plur. arctoe (as in Ter. Adelphoe for Adelphi), Cic. N. D. 2, 41,…

arctōus.opening: adj. , = ἀρκτῷος , prop., pertaining to arctos (q. v.); hence, poet. , northern (syn.: arcticus, aquilonius, Borealis), Mart. 5, 68 ; 10, 6, 2 ; Luc. 1, 53 ; 10, 250 ; Sen. Oedip. 604 ; id. Herc. Oet. 1566 .

arctūrus.opening: , = ἀρκτοῦρος . As a star. The brightest star in Bootes ,, whose rising and setting was supposed to portend tempestuous weather ( Plaut. Rud. prol. 71 ): stella micans radiis, Arcturus, Cic. Arat. 99 ; id. N. D. 2, 42,…

arcŭārĭus.opening: adj. arcus , pertaining to the bow : fabricae, Veg. Mil. 2, 11 . —Hence, subst. : , , , a maker of bows , Dig. 50, 6, 6 .

arcŭātĭlis.opening: adj. arcuo , bow-formed : caminus, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 ; cf. arcuatim.

arcŭātim.opening: adv. id. , in the form of a bow (perh. only in the foll. exs.): millepeda animal multis pedibus arcuatim repens, Plin. 29, 6, 39, § 136 : sanguis arcuatim fluens, Fest. s. v. Tullios, p. 352 Müll.

arcŭātĭo.opening: id. , an arch (only in Front.), Aquaed. 18; 121.

arcŭātus.opening: , um. Part. of arcuo.— = arquatus, q. v.

arcŭ-ballista.opening: (better than ), , arcus , a ballista furnished with a bow; only Veg. Mil. 2, 15 ; 4, 22 .

arcŭballistārĭus.opening: ( ), , arcuballista , he that shoots with an arcuballista, Veg. Mil. 4, 21 .

arcubii.opening: : qui excubabant in arce [ar, = ad, and cubo], Paul. ex Fest. p. 25 Müll.; cf. Doed. Syn. II. p. 162.

arcŭla.opening: dim. arca , a small chest or box , a casket , etc. For unguents, ornaments, etc. A small perfume - box , a jewel-casket , Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 91 : arculae muliebres, Cic. Off. 2, 7, 25 .—Hence, trop. of rhetor. ornament:…

arcŭlārĭus.opening: arcula one that makes little boxes or jewel - caskets , Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 45 .

arcŭlāta.opening: Arculus , sacrificial cakes made of flour , Paul. ex Fest. p. 16 Müll.

arcŭlum.opening: dim. arcus , a roll or hoop placed upon the head for the purpose of carrying the vessels at public sacrifices , Paul. ex Fest. p. 16 Müll.

Arcŭlus.opening: arca , the god of chests , coffers , etc., Paul. ex Fest. p. 16 Müll.

arcŭo.opening: v. a. arcus , to make in the form of a bow , to bend or curve like a bow (not before the Aug. per.): curru arcuato vehi, i. e. covered, Liv. 1, 21 : opus, Plin. Ep. 10, 46, 2 : (millepeda) quae non arcuatur, does not…

arcus.opening: (the orthography, arquus (cf. arquatus), is freq. in MSS., like quum for cum, quur for cur, etc.; cf. Freund ad Cic. Mil. p. 31 sq. Thus Charis. p. 92 P. upon Cic. N. D. 3, 20, 51 , reads arcuis; Prisc. p. 712 P. arci;…

ardĕa.opening: kindred with the Gr. ἐρωδιός and ῥωδιός; cf. the Sanscr. rud = sonare , a heron (in Pliny usu. ardeola, q. v.), Verg. G. 1, 364 .

Ardĕa.opening: v. arduus , = Ἀρδέα , the capital of the Rutuli , six leagues south of Rome; acc. to the myth, it was burned by Æneas, and from its ashes the heron ( ardea ) was produced, Ov. M. 14, 573 ; Verg A. 7, 411; cf. Serv. ad…

ardĕlĭo.opening: ardeo , prop. a zealous person; hence, in a bad sense, a busybody , a meddler , = πολυπράγμων , Phaedr. 2, 5, 1 sq. ; cf. the epigrams of Mart. 2, 7 ; 4, 79 .

ardĕo.opening: v. n. ( perf. subj. ARDVERINT, Inscr. Fratr. Arval., of the time of the emperor Alexander Severus, in Inscr. Orell. 961 ) [cf. Sanscr. ghar = to shine. Sonne foll. by Curt.], to take fire , to kindle; hence, Lit. , to…

ardĕŏla.opening: dim. ardea , a little heron , Plin. 10, 60, 79, § 164 ; 11, 37, 52, § 140 .

ardesco.opening: v. inch. [ardeo], to take fire , to kindle , to be inflamed (mostly poet. or in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic.; while exardesco is very freq.), lit. and trop. Lit. : ut omnia motu Percalefacta vides ardescere, Lucr. 6,…

ardĭfētus.opening: adj. ardeo-fetus , pregnant with flame; poet. of a torch: lampas, Varr. ap. Non. p. 243, 25 ; cf. id. ib. p. 312, 6.

ardor.opening: ardeo , a flame , fire , heat , burning heat , lit. and trop. Lit. : solis ardor, Lucr. 2, 212 : exortus est sol cum ardore, Vulg. Jac. 1, 11 : ignium, Lucr. 5, 587 : ignis, Vulg. 2 Pet. 3, 12: flammarum, Lucr. 5, 1093…

Ardŭenna.opening: ( , Ven. Fort. Carm. 7, 4), v. arduus; cf. Welsh ardh, to raise up , the forest-covered mountains in Gaul , now Ardennes , Caes. B. G. 5, 3 ; 6, 29 Herz.; Tac. A. 3, 42 ; cf. Mann. Gall. p. 203.

ardŭĭtas.opening: arduus , steepness : montium arduitas, Varr. R. R. 2, 10, 3 .

arduus.opening: adj. akin to ΑΡΔΩ, ἄρσω = to water, to cherish; ἀλδαίνω = to make grow; ἀλδήεις = growing; alo, altus, q. v.; 1. ad-oleo, ad-olesco; related to arbor, arbutus as ἐρυθρός, Germ. roth, Engl. red, is related to ruber;…

Arĕātae.opening: a Sarmatian tribe , also called Arraei, Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 41 .

arepennis.opening: Gallic; in mod. Fr. arpent = an acre ; syn. with semijugerum, a half acre of ground, Col. 5, 1, 6 : arapennis, Isid. Orig. 15, 15, p. 485 Lind.

arferia.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 11 Müll. [ar, = ad, and fero].

Arganthōnĭus.opening: , = Ἀργανθώνιος , a Tartessian king who lived to a great age , Cic. Sen. 19, 69 ; Val. Max. 8, 13 , ext. 4 (cf. Herod. 1, 163); Plin. 7, 48, 49, § 154 ; Censor. 17 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or pertaining to Arganthonius ,…

Arganthus.opening: a mountain in Mysia , near Bithynia , Gr. Ἀργανθώνιον ὄρος : Arganthi Pegae sub vertice montis, Prop. 1, 20, 33 .

Argēi.opening: A part of the city of Rome : Argeorum sacraria in septem et XX. partes urbis sunt disposita, Varr. L. L. 5, § 45 sq. : Argea loca Romae appellantur, quod in his sepulti essent quidam Argivorum illustres viri, Paul. ex…

argĕma.opening: , = ἄργεμα [ ἀργήεις , white; cf. albugo], a small ulcer in the eye, Plin. 20, 5, 20, § 40 ; 25, 13, 92, § 144 .

argĕmon.opening: , = ἄργεμον , an herb; in pure Lat., lappa canaria, Plin. 24, 19, 116, § 176 .

argĕmōnē.opening: , = ἀργεμώνη , an herb; in pure Lat., inguinalis, Plin. 26, 9, 59, § 92 .

argĕmōnĭa.opening: a plant similar to the preceding, Plin. 25, 9, 56, § 102 ; Cels. 5, 27, 10 .

argennon.opening: ἀργεννός, white , brilliant , white silver , Paul. ex Fest. p. 14 Müll.

Argentānum.opening: a town of the Bruttii , Liv. 30, 19 .

argentārĭus.opening: adj. argentum . Of or pertaining to silver (cf. argentum, I. A.): metalla, silver-mines, Plin. 33, 5, 26, § 86 : plumbum, a mixture of tin and lead, id. 34, 9, 20, § 95 , and 34, 17, 48, § 160: creta, for polishing…

Argentārĭus.opening: mons. A promontory on the coast of Etruria , now Monte Argentaro , Rutil. Itin. I. pp. 315-324.— The part of Mons Orospeda , in which the Bœtis took its rise , so called from its silvermines, Avien. Or. Marit. 291 .

argentātus.opening: adj. argentum (cf. aeratus and auratus, and Prisc. p. 828 P.). Plated or ornamented with silver (cf. argentum, I. A.): sandalia, Albin. 2, 65 : sella, Lampr. Elag, 4 fin. : milites, whose shields were covered or plated…

argentĕŏlus.opening: ( , Fronto de Or. 1), a, um, adj. dim. [argenteus], of silver : sicilicula, Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 125 .

argentĕus.opening: adj. argentum . Of or from silver , made of silver (cf. argentum, I. A.): polubrum, Liv. And. ap. Non. p. 544, 23 : aquila, Cic. Cat. 1, 9, 24 : brattea, Plin. 37, 7, 31, § 105 : phalerae, id. 8, 5, 5, § 12 : vasa, Hor.…

Argentĕus.opening: adj. , a standing epithet of a river in Gallia Narbonensis, now Argents : flumen Argenteum, Lepidus ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 34, 1 : amnis Argenteus, Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 35 ; with a tēte du pont and castle: Pons Argenteus,…

Argentĭa.opening: a place in upper Italy , between Milan and Bergamo, Itin. Hieros.

Argentiextĕrĕbrŏnĭdes.opening: a word formed by Plautus in jest , as the name of one who is skilled in extorting money [argentum-exterebro], a sponger , Plaut. Pers. 4, 6, 21 (cf. id. Capt. 2, 2, 35 ).

argentī-fŏdīna.opening: (also written separately, ), , argentum , a silver - mine , Varr. L. L. 8, § 62 ; Vitr. 7, 7 al. : Odor ex argenti fodinis inimicus omnibus animalibus, sed maxume canibus, Plin. 33, 6, 31, § 98 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 22 .

Argentīnus.opening: id. , the god of silver money , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 21; cf. Aesculanus.

Argentŏrātus.opening: the name of a city , now Strasburg in Alsace , Amm. 15, 11 ; cf. Mann. Gall. 270.—Hence, , , adj. , of or pertaining to Argentoratus : campi, Aur. Vict. Ep. 42 : pugna, Amm. 17, 1 .

argentōsus.opening: adj. argentum , abounding in silver : aurum, Plin. 33, 5, 29, § 93 .

argentum.opening: ἀργήεις, ἀργής, Dor. ἀργᾶς, white, like Tarentum, from Τάρας, Doed. Syn. III. p. 193; prop. white metal; cf. Sanscr. arǵunas = bright; raǵatam = silver; hence , silver , whose mineralogical description is found in Plin.…

argestes.opening: , = ἀργέστης , acc. to Vitr. 1, 6 , the west-southwest wind; acc. to Plin. 2, 47, 46, § 120 , the west-northwest wind.

Argestes.opening: , = Ἀργέστης , son of Astrœus and Aurora , Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 136 .

Argīa.opening: , = Ἀργεία . Daughter of Adrastus , and wife of Polynices , Stat. Th. 2, 266 ; 12, 113 .— Wife of Inachus and mother of Io , Hyg. Fab 145 .

Argīlētum.opening: Argiletum sunt qui scripserunt ab Argolā, seu quod is huc venerit ibique sit sepultus; alii ab argillā, quod ibi id genus terrae, Varr. L. L. 5, § 157 Müll.: sane Argiletum quasi Argilletum multi volunt a pingui terrā,…

argilla.opening: , = ἄργιλλος ( ἀργής , white), white clay , potter's earth , argil; cf. Col. 3, 11, 9 ; Pall. 1, 34, 3 : homulus ex argillā et luto fictus, * Cic. Pis. 25 : glandes ferventes ex argillā fusili, * Caes. B. G. 5, 53 ( ἐξ…

argillācĕus.opening: adj. argilla , clayey , of clay , argillaceous : terra, Plin. 17, 7, 4, § 43 .

argillōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of clay , abounding in clay : terra, Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 2 ; so Plin. 12, 14, 30, § 31 , and Vulg. 3 Reg. 7, 46 ; ib. 2 Par. 4, 17 : collis, Col. Arb. 17 .

Arginūsae.opening: or , , , = Ἀργινοῦσαι or Ἀργινοῦσσαι , three small islands in the Ægean Sea , near Lesbos : classem ab Arginusis removere, Cic. Off. 1, 24, 84 B. and K.: Arginussae ab Aege IIII. M. passuum distant, Plin. 5, 31, 39, §…

Argīphontes.opening: , = Ἀργειφόντης (Hom. Il. 2, 103), the Argus-slayer , an epithet of Mercury, who slew the hundredeyed Argus, Arn. 6, p. 209 ; cf. Macr. S, 1, 19 .

Argĭthĕa.opening: a town in Athamania , now Knisovo , Liv. 38, 1 .

argītis.opening: ἀργής = white , a kind of vine with white clusters of grapes , Col. 3, 2, 21 and 27; cf. Isid. Orig. 17, 5, 23 .

Argo.opening: ( gen. Argūs, Prop. 3, 22, 19 ; acc. Argo, Varr. ap. Charis. p. 94 P.; Argon, Prop 1, 20, 17 Müll.; dat. and abl. prob. not used), = Ἀργώ , the name of the ship in which the Greek heroes , under the guidance of Jason ,…

Argŏnautae.opening: , = Ἀργοναῦται (the sailors of the Argo), the Argonauts , Val. Fl. 1, 353 ; Hyg. Fab. 14 ; Plin. 36, 15, 23, § 99 : vehiculum Argonautarum, Cic. N. D. 2, 35, 89 : navis, id. de Or. 1, 38, 174 : princeps, i. e. Jason,…

Argŏs.opening: (only nom. and acc. ), more freq. in the plur. , , ( Varr. L. L. 9, § 89 Müll.: Graecanice hoc Argos, cum Latine Argei; cf. Prob. p. 1447 P.; Phocae Ars, p. 1707 P.), = Ἄργος . Argos , the capital of Argolis , in the…

argūmentābĭlis.opening: adj. argumentum , that may be proved : propositio difficile argumentabilis, Boëth. Arist. Anal. 1, 27.

argūmentālis.opening: adj. id. , containing proof : narratio, Ascon. ap. Cic. Div. in Caecil. 1 .— Adv. : , by way of proof , Aggen. Urb. Com. ap. Front. p. 64 Goes.

argūmentātĭo.opening: argumentor (a rhet. t. t., most freq. in Cic.). An adducing of proof , an argumentation : argumentatio nomine uno res duas significat, ideo, quod et inventum aliquam in rem probabile aut necessarium, argumentatio…

argūmentātor.opening: id. , he that adduces proof , an arguer; only in Tert. Anim. 38 ; id. Res. Carn. 24 .

argūmentātrix.opening: argumentator , she that adduces proof , a female arguer , Tert. Spect. 2 .

argūmentor.opening: v. dep. argumentum . To adduce proof of a thing , to prove : ego neque in causis, si quid est evidens, de quo inter omnes conveniat, argumentari soleo, Cic. N. D. 3, 4, 9 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 57 ; id. Att. 3, 12 : cum…

argūmentōsus.opening: adj. id. . Rich in proof (v. argumentum, I. A.), Sid. Ep. 9, 9 ; Acron. ad Hor. S. 2, 3, 70 .— Rich in matter or material (v. argumentum, II. A. a.): opus, Quint. 5, 10, 10 .

argūmentum.opening: arguo . The means by which an assertion or assumption may be made clear , proved , an argument , evidence , proof (and in particular, that which rests upon facts, while ratio is that which depends upon reasoning):…

argŭo.opening: (ŭĭtum, hence arguiturus, Sall. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 882 P.), , v. a. cf. ἀργής, white; ἀργός, bright; Sanscr. árgunas, bright; ragatas, white; and rag, to shine (v. argentum and argilla); after the same analogy we have…

Argus.opening: , = Ἄργος . The hundred-eyed keeper of Io , after she was changed into a heifer by Jupiter; slain by Mercury at the bidding of Jupiter. His hundred eyes were placed by Juno in the tail of the peacock, Ov. M. 1, 625 sq.…

argūtātĭo.opening: argutor , a rustling , creaking : lecti, Cat. 6, 11 .

argūtātrix.opening: argutator , a prattling female , Paul. ex Fest. s. v. lingulaca, p. 117 Müll.; v. Müll. a. h. l.

argūtē.opening: adv. , v. arguo, P. a. fin.

argūtĭae.opening: (the sing. argutia, ae, is rare and only among later writers; cf. Charis. p. 20 , and Phocae Ars, p. 1708 P.), argutus . That which is clear to the senses , vigor of expression , liveliness , animation; of works of art:…

argūtĭŏla.opening: dim. argutiae, q. v. fin. , a piece of slyness or subtlety , a cavil , quirk , or quibble (only in Gell.), Gell. 9, 14 fin. ; 2, 7, 9 ; 18, 1, 12 .

argūtor.opening: v. dep. (archaic inf. argutarier, Titin.; v. infra ) [argutus] (except in Prop. only ante-class.), to make a noise. With the voice, to prattle , prate : argutari dicitur loquacium proloqui, Non. p. 245, 26 : exerce…

argūtŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.]. * A little noisy , talkative , or loquacious (v. argutus, A. 2. a.): famula, App. M. 1, p. 117, 20 .— Somewhat subtle , acute , keen (v. argutus, B. 1.): libri, Cic. Att. 13, 18 .

Argynnus.opening: , = Ἄργυννος , a boy from Bœotia , loved by Agamemnon; he was drowned in the river Cephisus, Prop. 4, 6, 22 .

argўranchē.opening: , = ἀργυράγχη , a sarcastic word formed in imitation of συνάγχη (inflammation of the throat), the silver quinsy , Gell. 9, 9 ; cf. Pollux Onomast. 7, 24, and synanche.

argўraspis.opening: adj. , = ἀργύρασπις , having a silver shield , armed with a silver shield , Liv. 37, 40 ; Curt. 4, 13, 15 ; cf. id. 8, 5, 4 ; Just. 12, 7 .

Argўrippa.opening: or , , , = Ἀργυρίππα (acc. to Serv. ad Verg. A. 11, 246 , compounded of Argos Hippion), a town in Apulia , afterwards called Arpi , now Arpa : Argyripa, Verg. l. c. Rib.; cf. Mann. Ital. II. 83; Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 104…

Argўrippus.opening: , = Ἀργύριππος , the name of a man , Plaut. As. 1, 1, 59 .

argўrītis.opening: , = ἀργυρῖτις (containing silver), a kind of silver dross , litharge of silver , Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 106 .† † , , adj. , made of Corinthian brass (which was similar in lustre to silver; cf. Plin. 34, 2, 3 ): CRATERA,…

argўrŏdămas.opening: , = ἀργυροδάμας , a silver-colored stone , similar to the diamond , Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 144 .

argўros.opening: a plant , otherwise called mercurialis, App. Herb. 82 .

arhythmus.opening: or , , adj. ἀ-ῥυθμός , of unequal measure , inharmonious , only in Mart. Cap. 9 , pp. 327, 328.

arilātor.opening: or , , , a haggler , chafferer , = cocio, Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.; Gell. 16, 7, 12 .

arinca.opening: Gallic , a kind of grain , otherwise called olyra, Plin. 18, 8, 19, § 81 ; 18, 10, 20, § 92 ; 22, 25, 27, § 121 .— Acc. to Harduin, rye (in Dauphiné, now riguet ); acc. to others, the one-grained wheat : Triticum…

Ariovistus.opening: the king of a German tribe in the time of Cœsar , Caes. B. G. 1, 31 al.

aristē.opening: the name of a precious stone , = encardia, Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 159 .

arma.opening: ( gen. plur. armūm, Pac. ap. Cic. Or. 46, 155 ; Att. ap. Non. p. 495, 23 , considered by Cic. in the connection armūm judicium as less correct than armorum) [cf. ΑΡΩ, ἀραρίσκω = to fit; ἄρθρον = joint; ἁρμός = armus =…

armămaxa.opening: , = ἁρμάμαξα , a covered Persian chariot , especially for women and children , Curt. 3, 3 .

armāmenta.opening: arma, III. , implements or utensils for any purpose. In gen.: armamenta vinearum, props, Plin. 17, 21, 35, § 152 : armamenta ad inclusos cantus, reeds, pipes, id. 16, 36, 66, § 170 : Excussis inde tunicis iterum iisdem…

armāmentārĭum.opening: armamenta , an arsenal , armory : ex aedibus sacris armamentariisque publicis arma populo Romano dantur, Cic. Rab. Perd. 7 : qui (Philo) Atheniensibus armamentarium fecit, id. de Or. 1, 14, 62 ; Plin. 7, 37, 38, § 125 ;…

armāriŏlum.opening: dim. armarium , a little chest , or casket (ante- and post-class.): armariola Graeca, Plaut. Truc. 1, 1, 35 .— A small cabinet , a bookcase , Sid. Ep. 8, 16 ; Hier. ad Matth. 3, 21 .

armārĭum.opening: arma , a closet , chest , or safe , for food , clothing , money , etc.: armarium promptuarium, Cato, R. R. 11, 3 : reclusit armarium, Plaut. Capt. 4, 4, 10 ; id. Men. 3, 3, 8 ; id. Ep. 2, 3, 3 : cum esset in aedibus…

armātūra.opening: armo , armor , equipment. Lit. : armatura varia peditatūs et equitatūs, Cic. Fam. 7, 1 : cohortes nostrā armaturā, id. Att. 6, 1 : Numidae levis armaturae, of light armor, Caes. B. G. 2, 10 : universi generis armatura,…

armātus.opening: armo , armor (only in the abl. ). Lit. : haud dispari, Liv. 33, 3 : Cretico, id. 42, 55 fin. : armatu sustinendo assueti milites, Fronto, Prim. Hist. Fragm. 2, p. 341 .— Meton. , armed soldiers (cf. armatura, I. B.):…

Armĕnĭa.opening: , = Ἀρμενία . A country of Asia , divided into Armenia Major (eastern, now Turcomania and Kurdistan) and Minor (western, now Anatolia), Plin. 6, 9, 9, § 25 : utraque, Luc. 2, 638 : utraeque, Flor. 3, 5, 21 .— Absol.…

armentālis.opening: adj. armentum , pertaining to a herd of cattle (except once in Verg., only post-class.): equa, * Verg. A. 11, 571 : lac, Symm. Ep. 6, 17 ; 2, 2 : viri, Prud. Cath. 7, 166 al.

armentārĭus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to a herd of cattle : morbi, Sol. 11 : equiso, App. M. 7 .—Hence, Subst. : , , A herdsman , neat-herd , * Lucr. 6, 1252 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 18 : omnia secum Armentarius Afer agit, Verg. G. 3, 344 :…

armentīcĭus.opening: (better, ), , adj. id. , of or relating to a herd of cattle (perh. only in Varr.): pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 16 : greges, id. ib. 2, 10, 3 (Schneid. in Veg. 1, 18 reads armentiva ).

armentīvus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to a herd , Plin. 28, 17, 68, § 232 Hard.; besides, only Veg. 1, 18 Schneid. var. lect.; v. armenticius fin.

armentōsus.opening: adj. id. , abounding in herds : Italia armentosissima, Gell. 11, 1 .

armentum.opening: (old form , , , Liv. Andron. and Enn. ap. Non. p. 190, 20 ; Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 4 Müll.) [contr. for arimentum from aro, Varr. L. L. 5, § 96 Müll.; cf. Isid. Orig. 12, 2 ]. Cattle for ploughing; and collectively,…

armĭfer.opening: adj. arma-fero , bearing weapons , armed , warlike (perh. first used by Ov.; for the distinction between it and armiger, v. armiger, II.). Lit. , as an epithet of Mars and Minerva: armifer armiferae correptus amore…

armĭger.opening: (ARMIGERVS in a late inscr., Orell. 3631), , adj. arma-gero , bearing weapons , armed , warlike (in this last sense rare, instead of armifer). Pennigero non armigero in corpore, Att. ap. Cic. Fam. 7, 33 : cum paucis…

armĭlausa.opening: acc. to Isid. Orig. 19, 22 fin., contr. from armiclausa , a military upper garment (post-class.), Paul. Nol. Ep. 22 ; id. Ep. 17 ; Schol. ad Juv. 5, 143 .

armilla.opening: acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 25 Müll., from armus; acc. to Prisc. p. 1220 P., from arma . A circular ornament for the arm , a bracelet , armlet , for men and women: armillae, quae bracchialia vocantur, Cic. ap. Prisc. l.…

armillātus.opening: Part. [armilla], ornamented with a bracelet : armillatum in publicum procedere, Suet. Calig. 52 : armillata et phalerata turba, id. Ner. 30 ; so, armillati colla Molossa canes, i. e. wearing on their necks the bracelets…

armillum.opening: acc. to Paul. ex Fest., from armus; v. infra , a vessel for wine (ante- and post-class.): armillum, quod est urceoli genus vinarii, Varr. ap. Non. p. 547, 15 : armillum vas vinarium in sacris dictum, quod armo, id est…

Armĭlustrium.opening: the Roman festival of the consecration of arms; v. Armilustrum.

Armĭlustrum.opening: a place in Rome (in the 13th district), where was celebrated the festival Armilustrium, consecration of arms, ὁπλοκαθαρμός (19th Oct.; v. Inscr. Orell. II. p. 411 ): Armilustrum ab ambitu lustri, Varr. L. L. 5, § 153…

Armĭnĭus.opening: a distinguished Cheruscan prince , who defeated Varus in the Teutoburg forest , A.D. 9, and thus freed Germany from the dominion of the Romans , Vell. 2, 118 ; Flor. 4, 12, 32 ; Tac. A. 1, 55 ; 1, 60 ; 1, 63 ; 2, 9; 2,…

armĭ-pŏtens.opening: adj. arma-potens , powerful in arms , valiant , warlike; a poet. epithet of Mars, Diana, etc.: Mavors, Lucr. 1, 32 sq. : Mars, Verg. A. 9, 717 : diva, id. ib. 2, 425 : Deiphobus, id. ib. 6, 500 : genitor, Claud. VI.…

armĭpŏtentĭa.opening: armipotens , power in arms , valor , Amm. 18, 5 .

armĭ-sŏnus.opening: adj. arma-sono , resounding with arms ( poet. ): numina Palladis armisonae, Verg. A. 3, 544 : antrum, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 67 .

armīta.opening: armus , a virgin sacrificing , with the lappet of her toga thrown back over her shoulder , Paul. ex Fest. p. 4 Müll.

armītes.opening: ὁπλῖται οἱ ἐν ἐσχάτῃ τάξει , soldiers of the rear-rank , Philox. Gloss.

armo.opening: v. a. arma . Lit. , to furnish with weapons , to arm , equip , aliquem or aliquem aliquā re: cum in pace multitudinem hominum coëgerit, armārit, instruxerit, Cic. Caecin. 12 : milites armari jubet, Caes. B. C. 1, 28 :…

armon.opening: or = armoracia in the language of Pontus, Plin. 19, 5, 26, § 82 .

armŏrăcĭa.opening: ( , Col. 6, 17, 8 ; Pall. 4, 9, 5 ; 11, 11, 4 : , , , Col. 12, 9 fin. ), = ἀρμορακία , horseradish : Cochlearia armoracia, Linn.; Col. 9, 4, 5 ; 20, 4, 12 ; cf. Dioscor. 2, 138.

Armŏrĭcae.opening: (later form , Aus. Ep. 9, 35 ; id. Prof. 10, 15 ), , , = Ἀρμορικαί [ar, Celt. and old Lat., = ar, on, and mor, Celt., = mare], some of the northern provinces of Gaul , Bretagne , with a part of Normandy , Caes. B. G. 5,…

Armŏsăta.opening: ( , Tac. A. 15, 10 ; Plin. l. l.), , , = Ἀρμόσατα Polyb., Ἀρσαμόσατα Ptol., a fortress in Armenia , Plin. 6, 9, 10, § 26 .

armus.opening: , = ἁρμός [ ἄρω ; v. arma inct. ], pr., a joining together; the shoulder where it is fitted to the shoulder-blade , the fore quarter (opp. suffrago), and, with few exceptions, of the shoulder of an animal , while umerus…

Arna.opening: a town in Umbria , a mile east of Perusia , now Civitella d'Arno , Sil. 8, 458 ; Inscr. Orell. 91 ; cf. Mann. Ital. I. 483.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Arna , Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 113 ; Inscr. Orell. 90 and 5005.

arna.opening: a lamb , Paul. ex Fest. p. 17 Müll. (v. aries init. ).

arnăcis.opening: , = ἀρνακίς , a garment for maidens , a coat of sheepskin , Varr. ap. Non. p. 543, 1 .

Arnē.opening: , = Ἄρνη , a woman who betrayed her country ( the island Siphnos ), and was changed into a jackdaw , Ov. M. 7, 465 .

Arnŏbĭus.opening: An African Church father in the time of Diocletian , c. A. D. 295. His work, Adversus Gentes, is distinguished by strength and purity of diction; cf. Teuffel, Rom. Lit. § 639, 2.— ( ), , , a theological author , c. A.…

arnoglossa.opening: , = ἀρνόγλωσσον , a plant , sheep's-tongue or plantain : Plantago major, Linn.; App. Herb. 1 (also called arnion; Isid., Orig. 17, 9, 50, calls it arnoglossos).

Arnus.opening: , = Ἄρνος , a river of Etruria , now the Arno , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 50 ; Tac. A. 1, 79 al. ; cf. Mann. Ital. I. 328.—Hence, , , adj. , of or pertaining to the Arnus : tribus, situated on the Arnus , acc. to Liv. 6, 5 ,…

Arpi.opening: a city in Apulia , earlier called Argyripa (q. v.), now Arpa , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 104 ; cf. Mann. Ital. II. 82 sq.— Hence, Derivv.: , , adj. , of or from Arpi : Dasius Altinius Arpinus, Liv. 24, 45 ; , , , the…

Arpīnum.opening: a town in Latium , the birthplace of Cicero and Marius , now Arpino , Cic. Att. 2, 8 ; cf. Mann. Ital. I. 676.— Hence, Derivv.: , ( nom. Arpinatis, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 629 P.; cf. Ardeatis), adj. , of or pertaining to…

Arpīnus.opening: adj. Of or from Arpi , v. Arpi.— Of Arpinum , v. Arpinum, II. B.

arquātus.opening: adj. arquus = arcus = rainbow; v. arcus init. : morbus, the jaundice (a disease in which the skin turns to the yellow color of the rainbow), Cels. 3, 24 .—Hence, subst. : , , , one that has the jaundice , Non. p. 425, 3…

arquītes.opening: = sagittarii, bowmen , archers , Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll. [arquus = ar cus].

arrectārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. arrectus , in an erect position , erect , perpendicular; hence, arrectaria, the upright posts of a wall (opp. transversarii, cross-beams), only Vitr. 2, 8 , and 7, 3.

arrĕnĭcum.opening: ( , ), , , = ἀρσενικόν ( ἀρρενικόν ), arsenic , orpiment. vitia cum chartā et arrhenico sanant, Plin. 28, 15, 60, § 214 ; 34, 18, 56, § 178 ( Vitr. 7, 7, 7 fin. uses for it auripigmentum).

ar-rēpo.opening: (better, ), , v. n. , to creep or move slowly to or toward something, to steal softly to , lit. and trop.; constr. with ad; post-Aug. with dat. Lit. : mus aut lacerta ad columbaria, Varr. R. R. 3, 7, 3 ; so Plin. 35,…

arreptīcĭus.opening: ( ) or ( ), , adj. arreptus , seized in mind, inspired (in eccl. Lat.). In bon. part.: ut sis dux in domo Domini super omnem virum arreptitium et prophetantem, Vulg. Jer. 29, 26 .— In mal. part., raving , delirious ,…

arrepto.opening: , a false read. in Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 109 , instead of obreptantibus, v. Sillig ad h. l.

arrha.opening: , and (also without aspiration and ), , (the latter form ante-class.; cf. Gell. 17, 2, 21 ; in Cic. the word is never used), = ἀρραβών [from the Heb. from , to give security], the money given to ratify a contract ,…

arrhālis.opening: ( ), , adj. arrha , of a pledge : pactum, Diocl. Cod. 4, 49, 3.

arrhĕnŏgŏnon.opening: , = ἀρρενόγονον , a species of the plant satyrion, Plin. 26, 10, 63, § 99 .

arrhētos.opening: , = ἄρρητος (unutterable), one of the Æons of Valentinus , Tert. adv. Val. 35 .

Arrĭa.opening: the wife of Pœtus , distinguished for her magnanimity , Mart. 1, 14 ; Plin. Ep. 3, 16 ; Tac. A. 16, 34 .

ar-rīdĕo.opening: ( , Lachm., B. and K., Halm, K. and H.; , Fleck., Merk., Weissenb.), , v. n. , to laugh at or with , to smile at or upon , especially approvingly. Lit. , constr. absol. or with dat. , more rarely with acc.; also pass. —…

ar-rĭgo.opening: ( , , Halm; , Fleck., Rib., Weissenb.), , v. a. rego , to set up , raise , erect (not used by Cic., but for it he employs erigere). Lit. : leo comas arrexit, Verg. A. 10, 726 ; so id. ib. 4, 280 : aurīs, Plaut. Rud. 5,…

ar-rĭpĭo.opening: ( , B. and K.; , Lachm., Ritschl, Fleck., Merk., Rib., K. and H., Weissenb., Halm), , v. a. rapio , to seize , snatch , lay hold of , draw a person or thing to one's self (esp. with haste). In gen. Lit. : ut eum…

arrīsĭo.opening: ( ), , arrideo , a smiling upon with approbation : alicujus adrisio, Auct. ad Her. 1, 6, 10 .

arrīsor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who smiles on another , a flatterer , fawner : stultorum divitum arrosor, et (quod sequitur) adrisor, et, quod duobus his adjunctum est, derisor, Sen. Ep. 27 .

ar-rōdo.opening: ( , , Jan), , v. a. , to gnaw or nibble at , to gnaw (cf.: aduro, accendo, accīdo, adedo al.). Lit. : spartum, quod asellus adrodit, Plin. 35, 11, 40, § 137 : mures adrosis clipeis, etc., id. 8, 57, 82, § 221 : semina…

arrŏganter.opening: ( ), adv. , v. arrogo, P. a. fin.

arrŏgantia.opening: ( ), , arrogans . An assuming , presumption , arrogance , conceitedness (syn.: superbia, insolentia, fastus): cum omnis adrogantia odiosa est, tum illa ingenii atque eloquentiae multo molestissima, Cic. Div. in Caecil.…

arrŏgātĭo.opening: ( ), , arrogo , a taking to one's self; hence, as jurid. t. t., the full adoption , in the comitia curiata in the presence of the pontifices, later of the emperor himself , of a homo sui juris in the place of a child…

arrŏgātor.opening: ( ), , id. , he that adopts one in the place of a child (cf. arrogatio), Dig. 1, 7, 2 ; 1, 7, 19 ; 1, 7, 22 ; 1, 7, 40.

ar-rŏgo.opening: ( , Fleck., B. and K., Dietsch, Halm, Weissenb.; , , Dinter; Keller uses both forms), , v. a. Jurid. and polit. t. t. To ask or inquire of one , to question : Venus haec volo adroget te, * Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 45 ; cf.…

ar-rōro.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to moisten , bedew : herbam vino, Marc. Emp. 34 .

arrōsor.opening: ( ), , arrodo , one who gnaws at or consumes a thing, a nibbler , consumer : stultorum divitum, Sen. Ep. 27 .

ar-rŏtans.opening: ( ), , adj. qs. Part. of arroto, āre; rota , in a winding , circular motion , turning , trop. wavering : arrotanti tactu, Sid. Ep. 6, 1 .

Arrŭbĭum.opening: a town on the Danubius in Scythia Minor, Tab. Peut. Itin.

arrūgĭa.opening: akin to runco, runcina, ὀρύσσω, ὀρύξω, to dig; cf. Corssen, Ausspr. I. p. 543; v. corrugus , a shaft and pit in a gold-mine , Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 70 .

Arruntĭus.opening: a Roman nomen. L. Arruntius, consul A.U.C. 759, Tac. A. 1, 13 ; 3, 11 ; 6, 5 ; prob. the same as the historian L. Arruntius, who composed a work on the Punic Wars, Sen. Ep. 114, 17 sqq.— Arruntius, a celebrated artist…

ars.opening: v. arma , skill in joining something , combining , working it , etc., with the advancement of Roman culture, carried entirely beyond the sphere of the common pursuits of life, into that of artistic and scientific…

Arsăces.opening: , is , = Ἀρσάκης , the first king of the Parthians , Just. 41, 5 .— Derivv. , , ( gen. plur. Arsacidūm, Luc. 10, 51 ), successors of Arsaces , Tac. H. 1, 40 ; Luc. 1, 108 ; 8, 217 ; 8, 306 al. — , , adj. , Arsacian ,…

arse verse.opening: a Tuscan-Latin incantation against fire : ARSE VERSE averte ignem significat, Paul. ex Fest. p. 18 Müll. (cf. Plin. 28, 2, 4, § 20 ). A pure Tuscan inscr. found at Cortona with this formula reads: ARSES. VVRSES.…

arsella.opening: a plant , also called argemonia, q. v., App. Herb. 31 .

Arsēnārĭa.opening: a Roman colony in Mauretania Caesariensis, now Arzew , Plin. 5, 2, 1, § 19 ; it is called Arsinna in Mel. 1, 6, 1 .

Arsĭa.opening: a small river of Istria , which became the boundary between Italy and Illyricum under Augustus; the present Arsa , Plin. 3, 26, 29, § 150 ; Flor. 2, 5 ; cf. Mann. Thrace, p. 325.

Arsĭa Silva.opening: a forestin Etruria , celebrated for a battle between the Tarquinii and the Romans , Liv. 2, 7 ; Val. Max. 1, 8 ; cf. Nieb. Röm. Gesch. 1, 553.

arsinĕum.opening: a woman's headdress , Paul. ex Fest. p. 20 Müll.; Cato ap. Fest. p. 265 Müll.

Arsĭnŏē.opening: , and , , , = Ἀρσινόη . Arsinoa, mother of the third Mercury , Cic. N. D. 3, 22, 57 .— Arsinoë, daughter of Ptolemy Lagus and Berenice , wife of king Lysimachus , afterwards of her brother Ptolemy Philadelphus , Just.…

arsis.opening: , = ἄρσις , in metre, the elevation of the voice; opp. thesis, depression (in pure Lat., sublatio, Diom. p. 471 P.), Mart. Cap. 9, p. 328 ; Don. p. 1738 P.; cf. Ter. Maur. p. 2412 P., and Mar. Vict. p. 2482 P.

artăba.opening: an Egyptian dry measure = 3 1/3 Rom. modii, Rhem. Fan. Pond. 89 .

Artăbānus.opening: A Parthian king of the family of the Arsacidœ , Just. 42, 2 ; Tac. A. 2, 3 ; 2, 58 ; 6, 31 sq.; 11, 8.— A general of Xerxes , Nep. Reg. 1, 5 ; Just. 3, 1 .

Artăcĭē.opening: , = Ἀρτακίη (Hom. Od. 10, 108), a fountain in the country of the Lœstrygones , Tib. 4, 1, 60 .

Artaxăta.opening: ( , , , Tac. A. 2, 56 ), = Ἀρτάξατα , the capital of Armenia Major , on the Araxes , now Ardaschad , Juv. 2, 170 .

Artaxerxes.opening: , = Ἀρταξέρξης , the name of several Persian kings , Nep. Reg. 1, 3 ; Just. 3, 1 ; 10, 3 al.

camur.opening: adj. acc. to Macr. S. 6, 4 fin., peregrinum verbum; prob. root of κάμπτω; cf.: camera, καμάρα, Non. p. 30, 8; Paul. ex Fest. p. 43 Müll.; Serv. ad Verg. G. 3, 55; nom. camur, Isid. Orig. 12, 1, 35; 15, 8, 5 , crooked ,…

cāmus.opening: , = κημός (Dor. καμός ). A muzzle for horses (only in eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Psa. 31, 9 ; Ambros. Hex. 6, 3 .—* Perh. a kind of collar for the neck , Non. p. 200, 16 (Trag. Rel. v. 302 Rib.).

cana.opening: , Gr. (* κάνεον , plur. κάνεα κάνη , a wicker basket) for canistra, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 45 Müll.

cānăba.opening: (or ), , kindr. with κάναβος and κάννα; acc. to others, with καλύβη , a hovel , hut , Aug. Serm. 61 , de Temp.; Inscr. Orell. 39 ; 4077 .

cānăbŭla.opening: dim. canaba , a small hovel , Auct. Limit. p. 257 Goes.

Cănăcē.opening: , = Κανάκη . Daughter of Æolus , who , living in incest with her brother Macareus , bore a son to him , and was forced by her father to kill herself , Ov. H. 11 ; id. Tr. 2, 384 .— The name of a dog , Ov. M. 3, 217 ;…

cănăchēni.opening: a class of thieves , Arn. 6, p. 207 dub.; cf. Öhler ad h. l.

Cănăchus.opening: , = Κάναχος , the name of two artists of Sicyon , Cic. Brut. 18, 70 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 50 .

Canae.opening: , = Κάναι , a town on the coast of Æolis , opposite Mytilene , now Kanot-Koli , Liv. 36, 45, 8 ; cf. Mel. 1, 18 ; Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 122 .

Cănālĭcŏlae.opening: poor or lazy people who used to lounge near the Forum , at a place called the Canalis , Paul. ex Fest. p. 45 Müll.

cănālĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. canaliculus , like a channel or pipe , channelled , Plin. 19, 7, 36, § 119 ; 27, 9, 55, § 78 .

cănālĭcŭlus.opening: ( , , (ante- and post-class.), Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 14 ; Lucil. ap. Non. p. 198, 7 ; Gell. 17, 11, 2 ; cf. canalis), dim. canalis , a small channel , pipe , or gutter. A water-channel , Vitr. 10, 14 fin. ; Col. 8, 15, 6 .—…

cănālĭensis.opening: , and , , adj. id. , dug out of shafts or pits : aurum, quod puteis foditur canalicium vocant, alii canaliense, Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 68 ; absol. (sc. aurum), id. 33, 4, 23, § 80 .

cănālis.opening: (rarely ante- and postclass., , Cato, R. R. 18, 6 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 2 ; 3, 7, 8 ; 3, 11, 2 ; Auct. Aetn. 127 and 149; cf. the dim. canaliculus, etc., Rudd. I. p. 25, n. 35) [kindr. with Sanscr. root khan, fodere,…

cănārĭus.opening: adj. canis , of or pertaining to dogs , dog- : augurium, i. e. in which dogs were offered , Auct. ap. Plin. 18, 3, 3, § 14 ; Fest. s. v. rutilae, p. 285 Müll. (cf. Ov. F. 4, 936 ; Col. 10, 342 sq. ; Paul. ex Fest. s. v.…

cānaster.opening: μιξοπόλιος , half-gray , grizzled , Gloss. Gr. Lat. [canus].

cănātim.opening: adv. canis , in the manner of a dog , like a dog , κυνηδόν , Nigid. ap. Non. p. 40, 26 .

cancămum.opening: , = κάγκαμον , an Arabian gum used for incense : Amyris Kataf, Forsk.; Plin. 12, 20, 44, § 98 .

cancellārĭus.opening: adj. cancelli , living or kept behind bars : turdus, Schol. Pers. 6, 24 .

cancellātim.opening: adv. cancellatus, cancello , lattice-formed , trellis-like (post-Aug.; most freq. in Plin. the elder), Plin. 7, 20, 19, § 81 ; 9, 33, 52, § 103 ; 11, 37, 79, § 201 ; Sid. Ep. 5, 17 .

cancellātĭo.opening: cancello , in the agrimensores, the fixing of boundaries , the measuring of land , Front. Col. p. 109 Goes.; Sicul. Flacc. p. 16.

cancelli.opening: ( sing. cancellus, Dig. 43, 24, 9, § 1 ), dim. 2. cancer , a lattice , enclosure , grating , grate , balustrade , bars , railings : ( = κιγκλίδες ; Latini tamen cancellos non tantum fores τοῦ δικαστηρίου , sed etiam…

cancello.opening: v. a. cancelli (post-Aug.). In gen., to make like a lattice , to lattice : solum, i. e. with vines, Col. 4, 2, 2 : cancellata cutis (elephanti), Plin. 8, 10, 10, § 30 ; cf. cancelli: cancellato bracchiorum implexu, id.…

cancellōsus.opening: adj. cancelli , covered with bars or a railing : postes, Cassiod. Var. 5, 42 .

cancer.opening: root kar-, to bend, twist; whence corona, circus , a lattice , the radical form of cancelli, q. v., Paul. ex Fest. p. 46 ; cf.: inter Orci cancros, App. M. 6, p. 176, 25 .

cancĕrasco.opening: v. inch. n. [cancer, III.], to become cancerous , be afflicted with a cancer , to suppurate like a cancer (post-class.; only in perf. ), Plin. Val. 1, 10 ; App. Horb. 36 ; Marc. Emp. 9 .—Hence, , , cancerous : vulnera,…

cancĕrātĭcus.opening: adj. canceratus, v. cancero , like a cancer , cancerous : foetor, Veg. 3, 43, 1 .

cancĕrōma.opening: (contr. , Veg. 6, 19, 2 ; Salv. adv. Avarit. 1, p. 232 , and corrupted , Veg. 3, 22, 15 ), , , = καρκίνωμα , a cancer , App. Herb. 19 ; 31 .

Candăcē.opening: a queen of Meroë , Plin. 6, 29, 35, § 186 ; gen. is, Vulg. Act. 8, 27 .

candacus.opening: or ,) a false read. in Varr. L. L. 7, § 107 Müll. ad h. l.

Candāvĭa.opening: , = Κανδαουία , a mountainous district in Illyria , Caes. B. C. 3, 11 ; 3, 79 ; Sen. Ep. 31, 8 ; Plin. 3, 23, 26, § 145 ; Cic. Att. 3, 7, 3 ; Luc. 6, 331 .

candĕ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. candeo . (Cf. candeo. I., and candidus.) To make dazzlingly white (ante- and postclass.): argentum, Gell. 6, 5, 9 ; and jestingly: ebur atramento candefacere, of an impossibility, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 102 ; cf.…

candēla.opening: candeo; Fr. chandelle, Engl. candle; hence , a light made of wax or tallow , a wax-light , tallow-candle , taper. Lit. , Varr. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 727 ; Col. 2, 22, 3 ; as a light of the poor, diff. from lucerna,…

candēlābrārius.opening: candelabrum , a maker of candlesticks or chandeliers , Inscr. Orell. 4157 .

candēlābrum.opening: (old form , , like arater for aratrum, acc. to Arn. 1, p. 36 : , Petr. 75 . 10.— Acc. : candelabrum ardentem, Caecil. Com. Fragm. 111 , ap. Non. p. 202, 16 ) [candela]: in quo figunt candelam candelabrum appellant,…

Candēlĭfĕra.opening: candela- fero , Taper-bearer , a goddess supposed to assist at childbirth , for whom a symbolical candle or torch was lighted , Tert. ad Nat. 2, 11 .

candens.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. candeo.

candentia.opening: candens , a white , clear lustre , whiteness : lunae, Vitr. 9, 2, 2 .

candeo.opening: v. n. Sanscr candami, to be light; candra, the moon; connected with caneo as ardeo with areo , to be brilliant , glittering , to shine , glitter , glisten (cf. candidus and albus; mostly poet. ). Lit. Verb finit. :…

candesco.opening: v. inch. n. [candeo], to become of a bright , glittering white , to begin to glisten or radiate (rare; mostly poet. ): ut solet aër candescere solis ab ortu, Ov. M. 6, 49 ; Tib. 1, 10, 43 .— To begin to glow , to grow…

candētum.opening: , a Gallic word signifying a space of 100 or 150 square feet , Col. 5, 1, 6 ; cf. Auct. Limit. p. 292 Goes.; Isid. Orig. 15, 15, 6 .

candicantia.opening: , a false reading in Plin. 37, 13, 76, § 200 ; v. Sillig ad h. l.

candĭco.opening: v. n. candeo, like albico, from albeo , to be whitish or white (first used by Plin. the elder), Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 189 ; 34, 12, 32, § 127 ; App. M. 5, p. 168 ; Scrib. Comp. 237 ; Mart. Cap. 1, § 70 ; 7, § 728 ; Plin.…

candĭdārius.opening: a baker of white bread , Inscr. Murat. 304, 3 [candidus].

candĭdātōrĭus.opening: adj. candidatus , of or pertaining to a candidate for office : munus, Cic. Att. 1, 1, 2 .

candĭdo.opening: v. a. candidus , to make glittering or bright , to make white (eccl. Lat.): vestimenta sua, Tert. adv. Gnost. 12 : albis vestibus candidari, Aug. Ep. 168 .— P. a. : , , brilliantly white , Isid. Orig. 14, 8, 21 ; cf. 1.…

candĭdŭlus.opening: adj dim. [candidus], shining white' dentes, * Cic. Tusc. 5, 16, 46 : grex, Prud. Cath. 3, 157 .—* Adv. : , in trop. signif. (cf. candidus fin. ), candidly , sincerely , Arn. 2, p. 50 .

candĭdus.opening: adj. candeo , of a shining , dazzling white , white , clear , bright (opp. niger, a glistening black; while albus is a lustreless white, opp. ater, a lustreless black; cf. Serv. ad Verg. G. 3, 82 ; ls id. Orig. 12, 1,…

candĭfĭco.opening: v. a. candeo-facio , to make dazzlingly white , Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 7.

candĭfĭcus.opening: adj. candifico , that makes dazzlingly white : pulvisculus, tooth-powder, App. Mag. p. 277 .

candor.opening: candeo, as algor from algeo, etc. . A dazzling , glossy whiteness , a clear lustre , clearness , radiance , brightness , brilliancy , splendor , glitter , etc. (class.): aetherius sol irrigat adsidue caelum candore…

candosoccus.opening: Gallic ; in husbandry, a layer of a plant; pure Lat. mergus, Col. 5, 5, 16 .

Cănens.opening: daughter of Janus , and wife of Picus , Ov. M. 14, 333 sq.

canentas.opening: (Cod. Mon. ), an ornament for the head , Paul ex Fest. p. 46 Müll.

cānĕo.opening: v. n. canus , to be gray or hoary , be white ( poet. or in post-Aug. prose); P. a. : , , gray , grayish , hoary , white : temporibus geminis canebat sparsa senectus, Verg. A. 5, 416 ; cf. Tac. G. 31 : canens senecta,…

Cănēphŏrŏs.opening: ( , , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 70 ), , = Κανηφόρος, ἡ (she that bears a basket, v. κανηφόρος , and cf. Hor. S. 1, 3, 10 ; Ov. M. 2, 711 sq. ), paintings or statues of Greek artists , representing Athenian maidens , who , in…

cānesco.opening: . ĕre, v. inch. n. [caneo]. to grow white , whiten. Lit. , to become gray or hoary : pabula canescunt (sc. calore), Ov. M. 2, 212 ; Plin. 31, 10, 46, § 106 : canescant aequora remis, Ov. H. 3, 65 : canescunt tecta, id.…

Cangi.opening: , = Καγγανοί , a people in the western part of Britain , Tac. A. 12, 32 .

canĭa.opening: a kind of wild nettle , Plin. 21, 15, 55, § 92 .

canĭcae.opening: a kind of bran : canicae furfures de farre a cibo canum vocatae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 46 Müll.; Lucil. ap. Non. p. 88, 16 sq.

cănīcŭla.opening: dim. canis . A small dog or bitch , Plin. 32, 7, 26, § 79 .—Hence, Trop. , of a passionate, quarrelsome woman, Plaut. Curc. 5, 1, 8 ; Gell. 4, 20, 3 .— Transf. Canis Minor, the lesser dogstar , in the mouth of the…

cănīcŭlāris.opening: adj. canicula, II. A. , of or pertaining to the dog-star (post-class.): dies, dog-days, Pall. Jul. 1 and 7; Sol. Veg. 5, 35 : inclementia, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 .

Cānĭdĭa.opening: a sorceress , often mentioned by Horace , Hor. Epod. 3, 8 ; id. S. 1, 8, 24 ; 2, 1, 48 ; 2, 8, 95 ; to whom Epod. 5 and 17 are addressed.

Canĭdĭus.opening: a Roman name; esp., P. Canidius Crassus, a general under Lepidus and Antony , put to death by Octavius , Cic. Fam. 10, 21, 4 ; Vell. 2, 85, 2 ; 2, 87, 3 .

cānĭfĕra.opening: : mulier, quae fert canuam, id est qualum, quod est cistae genus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 65 Müll.; v. Canephoros.

cănĭformis.opening: adj. canis-forma , having the form of a dog , dog-shaped : Anubis, Prud. Apoth. 263 .

Caninĕfātes.opening: ( ), , , a people dwelling upon the Batavian peninsula , Vell. 2, 105 ; Tac. H. 4, 15 ; 4, 32 ; 4, 56 ; 4, 79; 4, 85; also called , Plin. 4, 15, 29, § 101 ; and , Inscr. Orell. 96 .—In sing. : dux natione Caninefas,…

Cănīnĭus.opening: the name of a plebeian gens at Rome. C. Caninius Rebilus, lieutenant of Cœ sar in Gaul , consul for a few hours at the end of December , A. U. C. 709; hence the jest of Cicero: Caninio consule scito neminem prandisse,…

cănīnus.opening: adj. canis , of or pertaining to a dog , canine , dog-. Lit. : lac, Ov. Ib. 227 ; Plin. 29, 6, 39, § 133 : pellis, Scrib. Comp. 161 : stercus, Juv. 14, 64 : rictus, id. 10, 271 : far, spelt-bread for dogs, id. 5, 11 :…

cānĭpa.opening: , = canistrum, a fruitbasket for religious uses , Frat. Arv. Marin. 3.

cănis.opening: ( , Plaut. Men. 5, 1, 18 ; id. Trin. 1, 2, 133 ; 1, 2, 135 ; Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 32 Müll., or Ann. v. 518 Vahl.; Lucil. ap. Varr. ib.; cf. Charis. 1, 17, p. 118 P.; abl. always cane; gen. plur. canum; v. Neue,…

Cănis.opening: a small river tributary to the Po , Plin. 3, 16, 20, § 117 .

cănistellum.opening: dim. canistrum, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. cana, p. 45, 19 Müll. , a bread-basket , a fruit-basket : argentea, Symm. Ep. 2, 81 ; 7, 76 .

cănistrum.opening: cănistri, ōrum, m., Pall. Nov. 17, 1 , = κάναστρα , a basket woven from reeds ( κάννα ), a bread- , fruit- , flower- , etc., basket (esp. for religious use in sacrifices), Cic. Att. 6, 1, 13 ; Tib. 1, 10, 27 ; Prop. 3…

cānĭtĭes.opening: ( , Plin. 31, 7, 42, § 91 ; 11, 37, 64, § 169 ; cf. Charis. p. 41 P.), em, ē (other cases not in use), canus , a gray or grayish-white color , hoariness ( poet. or in post-Aug. prose): lupi, Ov. M. 1, 238 ; folia…

cānĭtūdo.opening: id. (ante-class. access. form of the preced.), a gray color , hoariness : capitis, Plaut. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 62 Müll.— Absol. , Varr. ap. Non. p. 82, 24 .

Canius.opening: a Roman proper name. C. Canius. a Roman of learning , Cic. Off. 3, 14, 58 sq. ; id. de Or. 2, 69, 280 .— Canius Rufus, a poet , Mart. 1, 61, 9 ; 8, 20, 1 .

canna.opening: , = κάννα , a reed , cane (less freq. than harundo), Col. 7, 9, 7 ; 4, 32, 3 : palustris, Ov. M. 4, 298 : tremulae, id. ib. 6, 326 al.— Transf. , any thing made of reed. A reed-pipe , flute , Ov. M. 2, 682 ; 11, 171 ;…

cannăbĭnus.opening: adj. , = καννάβινος , of hemp , hempen : retis, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 11 : tegeticulae, id. ib. 2, 8, 2 : funes, Col. 6, 2, 3 ; 12, 50, 8 .

cannăbis.opening: , and , , kindr. with Sanscr. sana, the same, Bopp, Gloss. p. 343, a , = κάνναβις and κάνναβος , hemp; nom. cannabis, Col. 2, 10, 21 ; Plin. 19, 4, 22, § 63 ; 19, 9, 56, § 173 ; acc. cannabim, Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 6 ;…

cannăbĭus.opening: adj. cannabis , of hemp : silvae, Grat. Cyn. 47 .

Cannae.opening: , = Κάνναι ( Κάννα , Polyb.), a village in Apulia , north of Canusium , famous for the victory of Hannibal over the Romans; it lay on the east side of the Aufidus (which is hence called Amnis Canna by Marcius vates ap.…

cannētum.opening: canna , a thicket of reeds , Pall. Febr. 23, 2 ; 24, 13 ; Cassiod. Var. 2, 40 .

cannĕus.opening: adj. id. , made of reeds , reed- : tegetes, Col. 12, 50, 8 dub.

cannŭla.opening: dim. canna . A small , low reed , App. M. 4, p. 145 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 224 .—* (Cf. canna, II. C.) Pulmonis, the windpipe , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 152 .

Cannutĭus.opening: ( ), , , a Roman proper name. P. Cannutius, an orator in Cicero ' s time , Cic. Brut. 56, 205 ; id. Clu. 10, 29 ; 18, 50 ; Tac. Or. 21 .— Ti. Cannutius, tribune of the people A. U. C. 710, Cic. Fam. 12, 3, 2 ; 12, 23, 3…

căno.opening: (ancient imp. cante = canite, Carm. Sal. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 37 Müll.; fut. perf. canerit = cecinerit, Lib. Augur. ap. Fest. s. v. rumentum, p. 270 ib.; perf. canui = cecini, acc. to Serv. ad Verg. G. 2, 384 ,…

cănon.opening: ( acc. canona, Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 55 ; acc. plur. canonas, Aus. Ep. 136 ; in Cic. Fam. 16, 17, 1 , used as a Greek word), = κανών [κάννα, κάνη , a reed, cane]. A marking or measuring line; hence, a rule , canon , model…

cănŏnĭcārĭus.opening: canon, II. B. , the collector of an annual tribute , Just. Nov. Const. 30 ; Cassiod. Var. 6, 8 ; 12, 13 .

cănŏnĭcus.opening: adj. , = κανονικός , according to rule or measure. In music: ratio, the theory of harmony, Vitr. 1, 1 ; 5, 3 ; cf. Gell. 16, 18, 5 .— In astronomy: defectiones solis, as following at regular intervals , Aug. Civ. Dei ,…

cănŏnizo.opening: v. a. canon, II. C. , to put into the list or catalogue of saints , to canonize , Alex. III. P.P. Ep. 3.

Cănōpus.opening: ( ), , , = Κάνωπος , the brightest star in the constellation Argo (visible in Southern Europe), Manil. 1, 215 ; Vitr. 9, 4 (7); Plin. 2, 70, 71, § 178 ; Luc. 8, 181 (scanned Cănŏpŭs, Mart. Cap. 7, § 808 ).

cănor.opening: cano , tune , sound , song , melody ( poet. or in post-Aug. prose; rare). Lit. Of living beings, Quint. 1, 10, 22 : cygni, Lucr. 4, 182 ; 4, 911 : res est blanda canor; discant cantare puellae, Ov. A. A. 3, 315 :…

cănōrus.opening: adj. canor , of or pertaining to melody , melodious , harmonious , euphonious; neutr. or act. (of sound, men, animals, instruments, etc.; class. in prose and poetry). Neutr. : profluens quiddam habuit Carbo et canorum,…

cantābĭlis.opening: adj. canto , worthy to be sung , Cassiod. Var. 2, 40 ; id. 8, 9 ; Vulg. Psa. 118, 54 .

cantăbrārĭus.opening: cantabrum , a standard-bearer on festive occasions , Cod. Th. 14, 7, 2.

Cantā^bras.opening: a tributary of the Indus , now Tschandrabagha , Plin. 6, 20, 23, § 71 (Cantabas, Sillig).

Cantăbrĭa.opening: , = Κανταβρία , a province in Hispania Tarraconensis, east of Asturia , in the region of the present Biscaya , Plin. 34, 14, 42, § 148 ; 34, 16, 47, § 158 ; Suet. Aug. 20 ; 81 ; id. Galb. 8 ; Flor. 4, 12, 48 .— Derivv.…

Cantā^brĭcus.opening: , v. Cantabria, II. B. and cantabrum, I.

cantăbrum.opening: etym. unknown; the connection with Cantabria is a mere conjecture . A kind of bran (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2 ; 4, 3 ; Apic. 7, 1 ; Schol. Juv. 5, 11 (as an explanation of far caninum); hence, cantabricus sucus,…

cantābundus.opening: adj. canto , singing (rare: sedeo ego cantabundus et stellas numero, Petr. 62, 4 : Gallus suā disciplinā scuto projecto cantabundus (constitit), Quadrig. ap. Gell. 9, 13, 16 dub. (Hertz, cunctabundus).

cantāmen.opening: canto, III.; cf. cano, II.; cantus, II. B., and carmen; lit. a charming with words; hence, abstr. pro concr. , a spell , charm , magic sentence , incantation (very rare), Prop. 4 (5), 4, 51 ; App. M. 2, p. 114 ; id.…

cantātĭo.opening: canto; lit. a singing, a playing; hence, abstr. pro concr. . Music , song , mentioned by Varr. L. L. 6, 7, § 75 Müll.: animum cantationibus permulcere, App. M. 2, p. 125 ; Vulg. Psa. 70, 6 (but in Plaut. Stich. 5, 5, 19…

cantātor.opening: id. , a musician , singer , minstrel (mentioned by Varr. L. L. 8, § 57 Müll.): vetus et nobilior Ario cantator fidibus fuit, Gell. 16, 19 (transl. of the Gr. κιθαρὡδός , Herod. 1, 23 Bähr): cantator cygnus funeris ipse…

cantātrix.opening: adj. cantator (postclass.). Musical , singing : choreae, Claud. B. Gild. 448 .— Subst. : , , , a female singer , Vulg. 2 Reg. 19, 35 ; cf. Prisc. p. 1225 P.— Using enchantments : anus, App. M. 2, p. 128, 1 : aniculae,…

Canteci.opening: a people in Sarmatia Asiatica, near Palus Maeotis, Plin. 6, 7, 7, § 22 .

cantērĭātus.opening: ( ), , adj. canterius , supporied by props , underpropped : vineae, Col. 5, 4, 1 .

cantērīnus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or pertaining to a horse , horse- : ritus, like a horse, Plaut. Men. 2, 3, 44 : hordeum, i. e. winter barley, Col. 2, 9, 14 ; 2, 10, 31 ; Pall. Oct. 1, 2 : lapathum = rumex, Plin. 20, 21, 85, § 231 .

cantērĭŏlus.opening: dim. id. , a small trellis for supporting plants , Col. 11, 3, 58 .

Canthăra.opening: the name of a woman , Ter. And. 4, 4, 30 ; Plaut. Ep. 4, 1, 40 .

canthărĭas.opening: κανθαρίς , a precious stone having in it the figure of a Spanish fly , Plin. 37, 11, 72, § 187 .

canthăris.opening: , = κανθαρίς . A genus of beetle , of several species; in pure Lat. scarabaeus parvus, Plin. 29, 4, 30, § 94 ; freq. used in medicine, id. 11, 35, 41, § 118 ; 29, 4, 30, § 93 .—Esp. the (very poisonous) Spanish fly ,…

canthărītes vīnum.opening: = κανθαρίτης οἶνος , a kind of wine , Plin. 14, 7, 9, § 75 .

Canthărŏlĕthros.opening: , = κανθαρόλεθρος (death to beetles), a place in Thrace near Olynthus : in quo unum hoc animal exanimatur, Plin. 11, 28, 84, § 99 .

canthărŭlus.opening: dim. cantharus , a small drinking-vessel , Arn. 6, p. 209 .— A small candlestick , Paul. Nol. Carm. 22, 462 .

canthărus.opening: , = κάνθαρος . Lit. , a large , wide-bellied drinking-vessel with handles , a tankard , pot (very frequent in Plaut.), Plaut. As. 5, 2, 56 ; id. Bacch. 1, 1, 36 ; id. Men. 1, 2, 64 ; 1, 3, 5 ; id. Most. 1, 4, 33 ; id.…

canthērĭus.opening: or , , perh. κανθήλιος, a beast of burden . A gelding , Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 15 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 46 Müll.; Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 21 ; id. Capt. 4, 2, 34 ; Cic. N. D. 3, 5, 11 ; id. Fam. 9, 18, 4 ; Sen. Ep. 87, 9 .— An…
