Cē^brēn.opening: , = Κεβρήν , a river in Troas; also, a river god , father of Œnone , Sabin. Ep. 89, and of Hesperie , who is thence called ; gen. Cebrenĭdos, Stat. S. 1, 5, 21 ; acc. Cebrenida, Ov. M. 11, 769 .

Cĕcaumĕna.opening: , = κεκαυμένα , prop., the burnt regions , i. e. the torrid zone , Mart. Cap. 1, § 17 .

Cēcrops.opening: , = Κέκροψ , the most ancient king of Attica , who went there from the Egyptian Sais , and was founder of the citadel of Athens (which is hence called Cecropia; v. infra ), Hyg. Fab. 48 and 158; Cic. Leg. 2, 25, 63 ;…

cēdo.grammar: cessi, cessum, 3 v. n. and a.
cēdo.opening: v. n. and a. [perh. for cecado, redupl. from cado], to go , i. e. to be in motion , move , walk , go along. In gen. Lit. (rare, and only poet. : for which, in the common lang., incedo); candidatus cedit hic mastigia,…

cĕdo.opening: , old imperat. form, whose contr. plur. is cette (cf. Prob. II. p. 1486 P.; Non. p. 84, 31 sq. ) [compounded of the particle -ce and the root da-; v. 1. do], hither with it! here! give! tell , say (implying great haste,…

cē^drĕlătē.opening: , = κεδρελἀτη , the cedar , fir-tree , a large kind of cedar , Plin. 13, 5, 11, § 53 ; 24, 5, 11, § 17 .

cē^drĕus.opening: adj. cedrus , of cedar : oleum, Vitr. 2, 9 .

cē^drĭa.opening: , = κεδρία , the pitch or resin from cedar , Col. 6, 32, 1 ; Plin. 29, 3, 11, § 47 ; 32, 7, 24, § 70 al.

cē^drĭnus.opening: adj. , = κἐδρινος , of cedar-wood , cedar- : trabes, Plin. 16, 40, 79, § 213 : Apollo, id. 13, 5, 11, § 53 : oleum, id. 32, 7, 24, § 76 .

cē^dris.opening: , = κεδρίς , the fruit or berry of the cedar , Plin. 24, 5, 12, § 20 .

cedrostis.opening: acc. , , = κέδρωστις , one of the names of the white vine , Plin. 23, 1, 16, § 21 .

cē^drus.opening: , = κέδρος , the cedar , juniper-tree : Juniperus oxycedrus, Linn., which has a very fragrant wood, and furnishes an oil that protects from decay, Plin. 13, 5, 11, § 52 ; 16, 40, 76, § 203 ; Col. 9, 4, 3 ; Vitr. 2, 9,…

Cĕlădon.opening: , = Κελαδών . An Egyptian companion of Phineus , Ov. M. 5, 144 .— One of the Lapithœ , Ov. M. 12, 250 .

Cĕlaenae.opening: , = Κελαιναί , a town of Phrygia , on the Mœander , where, acc. to the fable, occurred the contest of Marsyas with Apollo, Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 106 ; Liv. 38, 13, 5 sq. ; Curt. 3, 1, 1 ; Luc. 3, 206 ; Stat. Th. 4, 186…

Cĕlaeno.opening: , = Κελαινώ . A daughter of Atlas and Pleione , and one of the Pleiades , Ov. H. 19, 135 .— One of the Harpies : dira, Verg. A. 3, 211 ; 3, 365 .— Hence, appel. for an avaricious woman , Juv. 8, 130 .

cēlātim.opening: adv. id. , secretly , privately (very rare), Sisenn. ap. Gell. 12, 15, 2 ; App. M. 4, p. 151, 39 .

cĕlĕber.opening: adj. ( masc. celebris, Auct. Her. 2, 4, 7 ; Tac. A. 2, 88 fin. ; 13, 47 ; 14, 19 ; Curt. 5, 1, 18 ; Gell. 17, 21, 10 ; comp. very rare, but sup. freq.) [perh. Sanscr. çru-, audire; Gr. κλέος ; v. Corss. Beitr. p. 368],…

cĕlē^brābĭlis.opening: adj. celebro , commendable (late Lat.): favor, Amm. 29, 5, 56 ; Ambros. de Cain et Abel, 2, 3, 12 al.

cĕlē^brātĭo.opening: id. . A numerous assemblage , concourse : hominum coetus et celebrationes, Cic. Off. 1, 4, 12 : quae domus? quae celebratio cottidiana? id. Sull. 26, 73 .— The celebrating of a festival in great numbers , a festal…

cĕlē^brātor.opening: id. , he who extols , a celebrator : triumphi, Mart. 8, 78 .

cĕlē^bresco.opening: v. inch. n. [celeber], to become renowned , Att. ap. Non. p. 89, 15 .

cĕlē^brĭtas.opening: id. . A great number , a multitude , a large assembly , a numerous concourse or gathering , a crowd (syn. frequentia; opp. solitudo; in good prose): in multitudine et celebritate judiciorum, Cic. Fam. 7, 2, 4 ; cf. Tac.…

cĕlē^brĭter.opening: adv. id. , frequently; only in sup. : per noctes celeberrime acclamatum est, Suet. Tib. 52 Oud. (Roth, creberrime).

cĕlē^bro.opening: v. a. id. . To go to a place or person in great numbers or often , to frequent , to fill (syn. frequento; class.): deūm delubra festis diebus, Lucr. 5, 1167 : viam, Cic. Cael. 14, 34 ; id. Sest. 63, 131 : domum…

Celēja.opening: or , , , a town in Noricum, now Cilly , in Stiria , Plin. 3, 24, 17, § 146 ; Inscr. Orell. 501 ; 1982 .

Celelātes.opening: a Ligurian tribe , mentioned only by Liv. 32, 29, 7 .

Cĕlemna.opening: or , , , a city of Campania , mentioned only by Verg. A. 7, 739 .

Cĕlendĕris.opening: ( ), , , = Κελένδερις , a fortified harbor in Cilicia, now Kelenderi , the Turkish Gulnar , Mel. 1, 13, 4 ; Tac. A. 2, 80 .—Hence, adj. : , , of Celenderis : regio, Plin. 5, 27, 22, § 92 .

cĕler.opening: ( masc. , Cato ap. Prisc. p. 760 P.; fem. celer, Liv. Andron. ap. Prisc. l. l.; cf. acer; sup. celerissimus, Enn. and Manlius ap. Prisc. l. l.) [cello; cf. Doed. Syn. 2, pp. 123 and 93, urging, pressing forward; cf.…

cĕlĕranter.opening: adv. celero , with speed , in haste , Att. ap. Non. p. 513, 25 (Trag. Rel. v. 123 Rib.).

cĕlĕrātim.opening: adv. id. , quickly , Sisenn. ap. Non. p. 87, 2 ( Gell. 12, 15, 2 , has celatim).

cĕlĕrĕ.opening: adv. , v. 1. celer, II. B. a.

Cĕlĕres.opening: , = Κέλερες [cello, those who are prominent in position, = celsi; acc. to some from κελης , eques], the orig. general name for patricians or knights , Plin. 33, 2, 9, § 35 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 42 (cf. Nieb. Röm. Gesch.…

cĕlĕrĭpēs.opening: adj. celer-pes , swiftfooted (very rare), * Cic. Att. 9, 7, 1 ; besides only in Aus. Epigr. 141 ; id. Parent. 27, 4 .

cĕlĕrĭtas.opening: celer , swiftness , quickness , speed , celerity (in good prose; syn.: velocitas, pernicitas; opp. tarditas): velocitas corporis celeritas appellatur, quae eadem ingenii laus habetur, etc., Cic. Tusc. 4, 13, 31 :…

cĕlĕrĭtūdo.opening: celer , = celeritas, swiftness , Varr. R. R. 3, 12, 6 (considered by Schneid. as a gloss).

cĕlĕrĭuscŭlē.opening: adv. dim. [id.], somewhat quickly : celeriuscule dicere, Auct. Her. 3, 14, 24 ; cf. Prisc. 5, p. 611 P.

cĕlĕro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
cĕlĕro.opening: v. a. and n. id. (mostly poet. , or in post-Aug. prose). Act. , to quicken , hasten , accelerate; syn.: festinare, properare): casus, Lucr. 2, 231 : fugam in silvas, Verg. A. 9, 378 : gradum, id. ib. 4, 641 : iter…

cĕlēs.opening: , = κέλης . A racer , race-horse , Plin. 34, 5, 10, § 19 ; v. Serv. ad Verg. A. 8, 635 .— A swift-sailing vessel , a yacht , pure Lat. celox, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 208 ; cf. Gell. 10, 25, 5 .

Cĕlētīzontes.opening: , = κελητιζοντες , riders upon race-horses , a piece of statuary by Canachus and Hegias, Plin. 34, 8, 19 , §§ 75 and 78.

Celetrum.opening: a town of Macedonia , now Castoria , Liv. 31, 40, 1 .

Cĕlĕus.opening: , = Κελεός , a king in Eleusis , father of Triptolemus. He or his son was taught agriculture by Ceres , whom he entertained as a guest , Hyg. Fab. 147 ; Ov. F. 4, 508 ; Verg. G. 1, 165 Serv. et Philarg.

cĕleusma.opening: (also ), , ( , , , Ven. Vita S. Mart. 4, 423 ), = κέλευσμα ( κέλευμα ), a command or call given by the chief oarsman , which gave the time to the rowers , Mart. 3, 67, 4 ; Rutil. 1, 370 ; cf. Ascon. Cic. Div. in Caecil.…

cēlĭa.opening: ( ), , Celtic , a kind of beer made in Spain , Plin. 22, 25, 82, § 164 ; Flor. 2, 18, 12 ; Oros. 5, 7 ; Isid. Orig. 20, 3, 18 .

cella.opening: cf. celo, oc-cul-o, clam, v. Varr. L. L. 5, 33, 45; Fest. p. 50 , a storeroom , chamber. In agricult. lang., a place for depositing grain or fruits , or for the abode of animals , a granary , stall , etc.: olearia,…

cellārārĭus.opening: , = cellarius, a steward , butler , Paul. Sent. 3, 6, 72 .

cellārĭensĭs.opening: adj. cella , belonging to a store-room : species, Cod. Th. 7, 4, 32; 11, 28, 16.

cellārĭŏlum.opening: dim. cellarium , a little chamber , Hier. adv. Jovin. 2, 16 .

cellārĭum.opening: cellarius (post-class. access. form to cella), a receptacle for food , a pantry , Dig. 32, 41, 1 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11, 93 ; 3, 21, 204 .— Meton. , food , provisions , Cod. Th. 1, 10, 3.

cellārĭus.opening: (access. form acc. plur. cellares, perh. for the purpose of avoiding the os four times repeated, Col. 8, 8, 1 ), adj. cella , of or pertaining to a storeroom : sagina, Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 31 .—Hence, Subst. : , , , one…

cellātĭo.opening: id. , a series of store-rooms or chambers , Petr. 77, 4 .

cello.opening: v. n. , found only in the compounds antecello, excello, praecello; v. celsus init.

cellŭla.opening: dim. cella , a small store-room or apartment , Ter. Eun. 2, 3, 19 ; Col. 8, 9, 3 ; and acc. to cella, II. D., Petr. 11, 1 .

cellŭlānus.opening: cellula , a hermit , recluse , Sid. Ep. 9, 3 .

Celmis.opening: , = Κέλμις , one of the Dactyli or Corybantes , priests of Cybele; for despising Jupiter, changed by him to adamas, Ov. M. 4, 282 .

cēlo.opening: v. a. (contract. form of the gen. plur. part. pass. celatum = celatorum, Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 15 Ritschl N. cr. ) [cf. caligo], to hide something from one , to keep secret , to conceal; constr., With a double acc. , as in…

celostrata antepagmenta.opening: Vitr. 4, 6, 6 ; of unknown signif. and various readings (others propose cerostrota, inlaid with horn; and others, clathrata, furnished with a trellis; v. Schneid. ad h. l.).

cĕlox.opening: celer, cello (orig. adj. , related to celer, as atrox to ater, ferox to ferus, etc.; cf. Doed. Syn. 2, p. 123; later subst. , sc. navis, ratis, etc.), a swift-sailing ship , a cutter , yacht , κέλης , Enn. ap. Isid.…

celsĭtūdo.opening: celsus . A lofty carriage of the body : corporis, Vell. 2, 94 . — In late Lat., a title; your Highness , Cod. Th. 1, 6, 6; 9, 1, 15 al.

celsus.opening: adj. P. a., of obsolete 2. cello, found in antecello, excello, etc., to rise high, tower; root kar-, in κάρη, κάρηνον, κόρυς; cerebrum, crista, pro-ceres; calamus, culmus, columna, etc. , raised high , extending upward…

Celsus.opening: a Roman cognomen; esp., A. Cornelius Celsus, the greatest of the Roman writers on medicine. — C. Albinovanus, a friend of Horace , Hor. Ep. 1, 3, 15 ; 1, 8, 1 .

Celtae.opening: , = Κελταί , a great parent - stock of people in the north of Europe , the Celts; among the Romans, in a more restricted sense, the inhabitants of Middle Gaul , Caes. B. G. 1, 1 ; Liv. 5, 34, 1 ; Mel. 3, 2, 4 ; cf.…

Celtĭbēri.opening: , = Κελτίβηρες , Celtiberians , a people in Middle Spain, which originated (cf. Luc. 4, 10 ) by a mingling of the Celts with the native-born Iberians, Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 19 sq. ; Cic. Tusc. 2, 27, 65 ; Caes. B. C. 1, 38 ;…

celtis.opening: an African species of lotus , Plin. 13, 17, 32, § 104 .

cēna.opening: (not , ; old form ; cf. Casmena for Camena, Fest. p. 205, 15 Müll.), , Sanscr. khad-, eat; Umbr. çes-na; cf. Gr. κνίζω , the principal meal of the Romans in the early period , taken about midday , dinner , supper (Paul.…

cēnācŭlārĭus.opening: ( and ), , adj. cenaculum , pertaining to a garret; only twice subst. , , , , a tenant of a garret , Dig. 13, 7, 11, § 5 .— , , , a leasing of a garret : exercere, Dig. 9, 3, 5, § 1 .

cēnācŭlātus.opening: adj. id. , with garrets : domus, Marin. Papir. Dipl. 123, § 2.

cēnācŭlum.opening: ( and ), , cena , orig., a dining-room , usu. in an upper story; hence, an upper story , an upper room , a garret , attic (later, the dwelling of the poorer class of people): ubi cubabant cubiculum, ubi cenabant…

Cēnaeum.opening: , = Κηναῖον ἄκρον , the north-western point of the island of Eubœa , now Cape Litar , Liv. 36, 20, 5 ; Mel. 2, 7, 9 ; Plin. 4, 12, 21, § 63 .—Hence, , , of Cenœum : Juppiter, Ov. M. 9, 136 .

cēnātĭcus.opening: ( and ), , adj. cena , pertaining to a dinner (very rare): est illic mi una spes cenatica (i. e. cenandi), * Plaut. Capt. 3, 1, 36 .—In late Lat. subst. : , , , the money given instead of food (to soldiers, priests,…

cēnātĭo.opening: ( and ), , id. (lit. an eating, dining), meton. (like cena, II. C.), a dining-room , a dining-hall (post-Aug. prose), Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 10 and 12; Plin. 36, 7, 12, § 60 ; Sen. Prov. 4, 9 ; id. Cons. ad Helv. 9, 2 ; id.…

cēnātĭuncŭla.opening: ( and ), , dim. id. , a small dining-room , Plin. Ep. 4, 30, 2 .

cēnātor.opening: ( ) [ceno], a diner , guest , δειπνητής , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

cēnātōrĭus.opening: ( and ), , adj. id. , of or pertaining to dinner , or to the table (only post-Aug.): fames, Sid. Ep. 2, 9 fin. : vestis, Capitol. Max. Jun. 4 .— Subst. : , , , dinner dress , Petr. 21, 5 ; Mart. 10, 87, 12 ; 14, 135…

cēnātŭrĭo.opening: ( and ), v. desid. [id.], to have an appetite for dinner , Mart. 11, 77, 3 .

Cenchrĕae.opening: , = Κεγχρέαι , one of the three harbors of Corinth , on the Saronic Gulf , now Kenkri , Liv. 32, 17, 3 ; Ov. Tr. 1, 10, 9 ; cf. Mel. 2, 3, 7 ; Plin. 4, 4, 5, § 10 . —Hence, Adj. : or , , of Cenchreœ : manus, Stat. Th.…

Cenchrēĭs.opening: The wife of Cinyras and mother of Myrrha , Ov. M. 10, 435 ; Hyg. Fab. 58 .— An island in the Ægean Sea , Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 57 .

cenchris.opening: , = κεγχρίς . Fem. , a kind of hawk , Plin. 10, 52, 73, § 143 sq. ; 29, 6, 38, § 127 .— Masc. (cf. Passow under κεγχρίας ), a kind of spotted serpent , Plin. 20, 22, 90, § 245 ( acc. cenchrim); Luc. 9, 712 .

cenchrltis.opening: , = κεγχρῖτις , a millet stone , a kind of precious stone now unknown, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 188 Sillig N. cr.

Cenchrĭus.opening: ( ), , , = Κέγχριος , a river of Ionia near Ephesus , Tac. A. 3, 61 .

cenchrŏs.opening: , = κέγχρος (millet), an unknown kind of precious stone , Plin. 37, 4, 15, § 57 .

Cenīmagni.opening: a British tribe in Norfolk , Suffolk , and Cambridge , Caes. B. G. 5, 21 .

cēnĭto.opening: ( and ), , v. freq. [ceno], to dine often or much , to be accustomed to dine , to dine (rare but class.). Absol. : si foris cenitarem, Cic. Fam. 7, 16, 2 : apud aliquem, id. ib. 7, 9, 7 ; 9, 16, 7; Plin. 33, 11, 50, §…

cēno.opening: ( and ), (e. g. Lucil. ap. Cic. Fin. 2, 8, 24 : Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 154 ; Cic. Fam. 1, 2, 3 ; Suet. Aug. 64 ; id. Calig. 24 al. ; acc. to Varr. ap. Gell. 2, 25, 7 , also cenatus sum, but of that only the part. cenatus is…

Cĕnŏmāni.opening: , = Κενομανοί , a Celtic people in Gallia Cisalpina, Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 130 ; Liv. 5, 35, 1 ; Caes. B. G. 7, 75 ; v. Dict. of Geog.

cĕnŏtăphĭum.opening: , = κενοτάφιον , an empty tomb , the monument of one whose body is elsewhere , a cenotaph , Dig. 11, 7, 2 and 6; Lampr. Alex. Sev. 63, 3 ; Vop. Flav. 15, 1 ; Hyg. Fab. 273 (pure Lat.: tumulus inanis, Verg. A. 3, 304 ;…

cēnseo.opening: (on the long e , v. Corss. Ausspr. 1, p. 257 sq.), ui, cēnsum (late Lat. censitum, Cod. Just. 11, 47 tit.; 11, 49 tit.; 11, 47, 4 al.; but not in Monum. Ancyr.; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, 557), , v. a. etym. dub.; often…

censeo.opening: , = succenseo, to be angry : ne vobis censeam, si, etc., Varr. ap. Non. p. 267, 24 .

cēnsĭo.opening: 1. censeo (only anteand post-class.). An estimating , taxing , esp. censor ' s estimating , rating , appraising : capitis, Gell. 16, 10, 13 : Servi Tulli, id. 10, 28, 2 ; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 81 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 65,…

censītĭo.opening: 1. censeo, censītus . * A taxing , tax , tribute : levare, Spart. Pescenn. Nigr. 7 fin. — A declaration of the will , a command : Vespasiani censitione et jussu, Front. Colon. p. 146 Goes.

censītor.opening: id. , in the provinces, the magistrate presiding over the rating of citizens ( = censor), Dig. 41, 1, 30 ; 50, 15, 4 ; Cod. Th. 6, 3, 2; Inscr. Orell. 208 al.

censor.opening: 1. censeo; cf. also Umbr. censtur; Sanscr. canster, leader, governor , a censor , a Roman magistrate , of whom there were two, chosen orig. every five, and afterwards every one and a half years, who at first only had…

Censōrīnus.opening: A cognomen in the gens Marcia, Cic. Brut. 90, 311 al. — A grammarian of the third century , whose work, De Die Natali, is extant.

censōrĭus.opening: adj. censor , of or pertaining to the censor , censorial : tabulae, the lists of the censor, Cic. Agr. 1, 2, 4 : lex, a contract for leasing buildings, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 55, § 143 ; public revenues , id. Prov. Cons. 5,…

censŭālis.opening: adj. census , of or pertaining to a census (in late and jurid. Lat.): forma, Dig. 50, 15, 4 : vincula, ib.: professiones, ib. 50, 4, 18 .— Subst. : , , Those who make out the censor ' s lists , Capitol. Gord. 12 ; Cod.…

censum.opening: 1. censeo , = 2. census, II. c., wealth , riches , Cic. ap. Non. p. 202, 23 (IV. 2, p. 456 Orell.).

censūra.opening: censor . The office of censor , censorship , Liv. 4, 8, 2 ; 4, 24, 3 sq.; 9, 34, 16 sq.; 9, 46, 10 et saep.; Cic. Inv. 1, 30, 48 ; Plin. 14, 4, 5, § 44 ; Ov. F. 6, 647 et saep.—Prov.: dat veniam corvis, vexat censura…

census.opening: 1. censeo . A registering and rating of Roman citizens , property , etc., a census; cf. Liv. 1, 42, 5 ; Dig. 50, 15 , and the compendiums referred to under censor: habere, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 53, § 131 : agere, Liv. 3, 22,…

centaurēum.opening: or , , (access. form , , , App. Herb. 34 and 35), = κενταύρειον and κενταύριον , centaury , a plant of two kinds : majus, Centaurea centaurium, Linn.; and minus, Gentiana centaurium, id.; Plin. 25, 6, 30, § 66 : ferum,…

Centaurēus.opening: adj. Centaurus , pertaining to a Centaur , of the Centaurs : rixa, Hor. C. 1, 18, 8 .

Centaurĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to a Centaur : lustra, Stat. Achill. 1, 266 .

centauris.opening: , = κενταυρίς , a species of centaureum, Plin. 25, 6, 32, § 69 .

Centaurŏmăchĭa.opening: a fictitious name of a part of Thessaly , Plaut. Curc. 3, 75 .

Centaurus.opening: , = Κένταυρος , a Centaur; the Centaurs were wild people in the mountains of Thessaly , who fought on horseback; acc. to the fable, monsters in Thessaly of a double form (the upper parts human, the lower those of a…

centēnārĭus.opening: adj. centeni , consisting of a hundred , relating to a hundred : numerus, Varr. L. L. 5, § 86 Müll., p. 26 Bip.: grex, id. R. R. 2, 4, 22 ; 3, 6, 6 : pondera, Plin. 7, 20, 19, § 83 : ballistae, throwing stones weighing…

centēni.opening: (among the poets and in post-class. prose also in sing. ; cf.: bini, terni, etc.; gen. plur. centenūm, like binūm, etc., Plin. 7, 49, 50, § 163 sq. al.), num. distrib. [centum], a hundred each , a hundred : illos…

centēnĭōnālis nummus.opening: a small coin , Cod. Th. 9, 23, 1 and 2.

centēsĭmo.opening: v. a. centesimus , to take out every hundredth for punishment, to centesimate : milites, Capitol. Macr. 12 .

centēsĭmus.opening: num. ordin. [centum], the hundredth : pars, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 166 : lux ab interitu Clodii, Cic. Mil. 35, 98 al. — Subst. : , , (sc. pars), the hundredth part of a thing , as a revenue, tax, a percentage: rerum…

centĭceps.opening: adj. centum-caput , hundred-headed : belua, i. e. Cerberus, Hor. C. 2, 13, 34 .

centiens.opening: or , adv. centum , a hundred times : eadem imperare, Plaut. As. 2, 4, 16 : dictum, Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 8 : sestertium centiens et octogiens (sc. milia), Cic. Pis. 35, 86 : circiter centies sestertium, Nep. Att. 5, 2 .

centĭfĭdus.opening: adj. centum-findo , divided into a hundred parts , or, in gen., into a great many parts : iter, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 888 .

centĭfŏlĭa.opening: centum-folium rosa, the hundred-leaved rose , Plin. 21, 4, 10 , §§ 17 and 18.

centĭgrānĭum.opening: centum-granum triticum, wheat that has a hundred grains , Plin. 18, 10, 21, § 95 .

centĭmālis.opening: κέντημα fistula, a surgical instrument , a trocar; Fr. trois quarts, Veg. 2, 15, 4 ; 2, 5, 24 .

centĭmănus.opening: (cf. Prisc. p 718 P.; Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 107 ), adj. centum-manus , having a hundred hands , an epithet of Gyges, Hor. C. 2, 17, 14 ; of Typhoeus, Ov. M. 3, 303 : infantes centimanos, Arn. 2, p. 97 , acc. to Lachm.…

centĭmĕter.opening: centum-metrum , he who employs a hundred , or, in gen., very many metres : Terentianus, Sid. Carm. 9, 265 .

centĭmetrum.opening: centum-metrum , the title of a metrical writing of Servius in Putsch. p. 1817 sq.

certātus.opening: 2. certo , a contention , fight , Stat. S. 3, 1, 152 .

cervārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to deer : lupus, a lynx, Plin. 8, 22, 34, § 84 ; 11, 37, 79, § 202 : venenum, an herb with which arrows were smeared, Plin. 27, 11, 76, § 101 ; Fest. s. v. toxicum, p. 355: cervaria ovis,…

cervīcātus.opening: adj. id. , stiffnecked , obstinate , Vulg. Ecclus. 16, 11 .

chordapsus.opening: , = χόρδαψος , a disease of the intestines , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 144 ; Theod. Prisc. 4, 8 (in Cels. 4, 14 written as Greek).

chordus.opening: ( , v. the letter C ), , adj. a very ancient word relating to husbandry, of unknown etym. , lateborn , or produced late in the season : dicuntur agni chordi, qui post tempus nascuntur, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 29 ; cf. Plin.…

chōrĕpiscŏpus.opening: , = χωρεπίσκοπος , a deputy of a bishop for a village , a suffragan bishop , Cod. Just. 1, 3, 42 .

chŏrĭcus.opening: adj. , = χορικός , pertaining to the chorus : tibiae, Diom. 3, p. 489 . —In metre: metrum, a kind of anapœstic verse , consisting of a hypercatalectic dipody, e. g. animus male fortis, Serv. Centim. p. 1821 P.

chōrŏbătes.opening: , = χωροβάτης . an instrument for finding the level of water , a ground-level , Vitr. 8, 5, 1 Schneid.

chŏrŏcĭthărista.opening: , = χοροκιθαριστής , he who accompanied the chorus on the cithara , Suet. Dom. 4 .

Chōrŏgrăphĭa.opening: , = χωρογραφία , the description of countries , geography , Lact. ad Stat. Th. 2, 44 .—Esp., the title of a book of Cicero , Prisc. p. 717 P.; and of a poem of P. Terentius Varro Atacinus.

chōrŏgrăphus.opening: , = χωρογράφος , one who describes countries , a geographer , Vitr. 8, 2, 6 Schneid. (others read, instead of chorographis, chorographiis, from chorographia, q. v.).

chortĭnus.opening: adj. , = χόρτινος , of or from grass : oleum, Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 30 .

chŏrus.opening: , = χορός [cf. Lidd. and Scott under χορός ]. A dance in a ring , a choral dance , a dance , = chorea: chorus et cantus, Tib. 1, 7, 44 ; cf. Prop. 4 (5), 6, 70 . Nympharum leves chori, Hor. C. 1, 1, 31 : ferre pedem…

Chrĕmes.opening: , = Χρέμης , the name of an old miser in the Andria , Heaut. , and Phormio of Terence , Cic. Fin. 1, 1, 3 ; id. Off. 1, 9, 30 ; Hor. Epod. 1, 33 ; gen. Chremi, Ter. And. 2, 2, 31 ; acc. Gr. Chremeta, Hor. S. 1, 10, 40 ;…

Chrestŏlŏgus.opening: , = χρηστολόγος (well speaking, but ill working), a nickname of the emperor Pertinax , Capit. Pert. 13; Aur. Vict. Epit. 18 .

chreston.opening: , = χρηστόν (useful), a name by which the plant cichorium was sometimes called , Plin. 20, 8, 30, § 74 .

chrīa.opening: , = χρεία , in rhetoric, a sentence proposed as a theme for rhetorical exercise , with its logical development , Quint. 1, 9, 3 sq. ; 1, 9, 4 sq.; 2, 4, 26 Spald.; Sen. Ep. 33, 6 ; Diom. p. 289 P.

chrisma.opening: , = χρίσμα , in eccl. Lat., an anointing , unction , Tert. Bapt. 7 ; id. adv. Jud. 13 ; Prud. Cath. 6, 128 ; Psych. 361 al.

Christĭānismus.opening: , = Χριστιανισμός , Christianity , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 33 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 19, 23, 1; Hier. in Gal. 6, 4 .

Christĭānĭtas.opening: Christus . Christianity , = Christianismus, Cod. Th. 16, 7, 7; 12, 1, 112.— Meton. , the Christian clergy , Cod. Th. 12, 1, 123.

Christĭānīzo.opening: v. n. , = Χριστιανίζω , to profess Christianity , Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 21 .

Christus.opening: , = Χριστός (the Anointed, Heb. ; cf. Lact. 4, 7, 7 ), Christ , Tac. A. 15, 44 Rupert. ad loc.; Plin. Ep. 10, 97 ; and in the Church fathers very freq.

chrōma.opening: (ătŏs, Vitr. 5, 5 ), , = χρῶμα (a color), in music, a chromatic scale (a species of harmony in which the tones of the tetrachord measure two and a half tones, as a half, again a semitone, and then a tone and a half…

chrŏmis.opening: or , = χρόμις , a seafish : immunda, Ov. Hal. 121 ; Plin. 10, 70, 89, § 193 : chromin, qui, etc., id. 32, 11, 54, § 153 ; 9, 16, 24, § 57 .— , nom. propr. m. , of a satyr, Verg. E. 6, 13 ; of a Trojan, acc. Chromim, id.…

chrŏnĭcus.opening: adj. , = χρονικός , pertaining to time : libri, chronicles, Gell. 17, 21, 1 ; so also absol. : , , , = τὰ χρονικά , Plin. 35, 9, 35, § 58 ; Gell. 17, 4, 5 ; 17, 15, 1 ; and in sing. : in primo chronico, id. 17, 21, 3 :…

chrŏnĭus.opening: adj. , = χρόνιος , chronic , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 28, 148 ; 3, 16, 135 .

chrŏnŏgrăphus.opening: , = χρονογράφος , a chronographer , annalist , Sid. Ep. 8, 6 fin.

Chrȳsa.opening: , or , , , = Χρύση . A town on the coast of Troas sacred to Apollo , Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 122 ; Mel. 1, 18 ; Ov. M. 13, 174 (cf. Hom. Il. 1, 390; 1, 452).— , Plin. 4, 12, 20, § 61 .— An island of India , Mel. 3, 7, 7 .

chrȳsallis.opening: , = χρυσαλλίς , the gold-colored chrysalis , aurelia , or pupa of the butterfly , Plin. 11, 32, 37, § 112 ; 11, 35, 41, § 117 .

chrȳsēlectrum.opening: , = χρυσήλεκτρον . Gold-colored amber , a precious stone , Plin. 37, 3, 12, § 51 .— , , , a dark-yellow precious stone , perh. amber-colored hyacinth , Plin. 37, 9, 43, § 127 .

chrȳsendĕtus.opening: adj. , = χρυσένδετος , set in gold , inlaid with gold : lances, Mart. 14, 97 inscr.—Also absol. : , , (sc. vasa), vessels inlaid with gold , Mart. 2, 43, 11 ; 6, 94, 2 ; 14, 97, 1 .

chrȳsĕus.opening: adj. , = χρύσεος , golden : basiliscus, i. e. gold - colored, App. Herb. 128 .— Subst. : , , , golden vessels , Mart. 9, 95, 4 .

Chrȳsis.opening: a comic person in Terence and Trabea, Cic. de Or. 2, 80, 327 ; id. Tusc. 4, 31, 67 ; Ter. And. 1, 1, 58 al.

chrȳsītes.opening: , = χρυσίτης . A precious stone , also called phloginos, Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 179 .— Another gold-colored precious stone , Plin. 36, 22, 43, § 157 .

chrȳsŏaspĭdes.opening: , = χρυσοάσπιδες (bearing golden shields), a kind of soldiers under Alexander Severus , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 50 .

chrȳsŏcĕphălŏs.opening: , = χρυσοκέφαλος , a golden basilisk , App. Herb. 128 .

chūs.opening: , = χοῦς , a measure for liquids , = congius, Rhemn. Fann. Pond. 7, 70.
