cĭlĭcĭārĭus.opening: cilicium; v. Cilicia, II. B. β , a maker of hair coverings , Inscr. Orell. 4162 .

cĭlĭcīnus.opening: adj. id. , made of hair-cloth : tentoria, Sol. 33 : tunica, Hier. Vit. Hil. fin. : saga, Vulg. Exod. 26, 7 .

cĭlĭcĭŏlum.opening: dim. cilicium , a small garment or coverlet of goats ' hair , Hier. Ep. 71, 7 ; 108, 15 .

cīlĭo.opening: (a vulgar collat. form of caelum), a chisel , graver , Isid. Orig. 20, 4, 7 .

cĭlĭum.opening: kindr. with Gr. κυλίς, κύλα . An eyelid , Paul. ex Fest. p. 43, 3 Müll.; Plin. 11, 39, 93, § 227 ; App. M. 10, p. 247, 10 ; Lact. Opif. Dei, 10 init. — Transf. , the lower eyelid (opp. supercilium): extremum ambitum…

Cilla.opening: , = Κίλλα , a town in Troas , distinguished for the worship of Apollo , Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 122 ; Sen. Troad. 227 ; acc. Cillan. Ov. M. 13, 174 (cf. Hom. Il. 1, 38).

cillĭba.opening: , = κιλλίβας , a round dining-table , Varr. L. L. 5, § 118 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 43, 9 ib.

cillo.opening: 1. cillo , = cinaedus, Pseudo ic. in Sall. 6, 18 .

Cilnĭus.opening: adj. pure Etrusc. Cfelne or Cfenle , a designation of a very distinguished Etruscan gens, from which Mœcenas originated; Cilnian , Liv. 10, 3, 2 ; 10, 5, 13 ; Sil. 7, 29 ; Tac. A. 6, 11 ; Macr. S. 2, 4, 12 .

cilo.opening: having a prominent forehead pressed in upon the sides , Fest. p. 43, 10 ; cf. Charis. 1, p. 78 P.; a dim. of it, cilunculus, Arn. 3, 14 .

Cim.opening: n. : nomen vici, Cels. ap. Prisc. pp. 644 and 688 P.

Cimbri.opening: , = Κίμβροι [Cimbri linguā Gallicā latrones dicuntur, Fest. p. 43, 7 ], a people of Northern Germany (in Holstein, Silesia, and Jutland); on their irruption into Italy conquered by Marius, Mel. 3, 3 fin. ; Plin. 2, 67,…

cīmēlĭarcha.opening: , = κειμηλιάρχης , a treasurer , keeper of treasure , Cod. Just. 7, 72, 10 .

cīmēlĭarchĭum.opening: , = κειμηλιάρχιον , a place where jewels are deposited , a treasury , Cod. Just. 7, 72, 10, § 2 ; 11, 47, 19 .

cīmex.opening: (so always acc. to Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 619 sq.; but fem. , Plin. 32, 10, 47 § 136 Sillig and Jan.), a bug , Liv. Andron. ap. Fest. p. 210, 17 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 2 fin. ; Col. 6, 18, 2 ; Plin. 30, 14, 45, § 131 ; 29, 4,…

cīmĭco.opening: , = κορίζω , to purify from bugs , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

Cĭmĭnus.opening: a lake in Etruria , near Sutrium , now Lago di Vico , or di Ronciglione , with a mountain forest lying near it , Verg. A. 7, 697 .—Hence, , , adj. , Ciminian : lacus, i.e. Ciminus, Col. 8, 16, 2 : silva, Liv. 9, 36, 1…

Cimmĕrii.opening: ( gen. Cimmeriūm, Val. Fl. 3, 399 ; Cimmeriōn, Tib. 4, 1, 64 ), , = Κιμμέριοι . A Thracian people in the present Crimea , on both sides of the Dnieper , whose chief town was Cimmerium, Mel. 1, 19, 15 ; Plin. 6, 6, 5, §…

Cĭmōlus.opening: , = Κίμωλος , an island of the Cyclades , distinguished for its chalky soil , now Kimolo or Argentiera , Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 70 ; Ov. M. 7, 463 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or from Cimolus : creta (freq. used in medicine),…

Cīmon.opening: ( , Val. Max. 5, 4 , ext. 2), , , = Κίμων . Father of Miltiades , Nep. Milt. 1 .— A son of Miltiades , a distinguished general of the Athenians , whose life is written by Nepos , Nep. Cim. 1 sqq.; cf. also Cic. Off. 2,…

cĭnaedĭas.opening: , = κιναιδίας , a precious stone , unknown to us, said to be found in the brain of the fish cinaedus, Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 153 .

cĭnaedĭcus.opening: adj. cinaedus, 1. , pertaining to one who is unchaste; immodest , lewd (ante-class.): cantio, Plaut. Stich. 5, 5, 19 .— Subst. = cinaedus, Plaut. Stich. 5, 7, 1 (769); Varr. ap. Non. p. 176, 19 .

cĭnaedŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a male wanton , Scip. Afric. ap. Macr. S. 2, 10 .

cĭnăra.opening: , = κινάρα , a kind of artichoke (Cinara scolymus, Linn.), a native of the island of Cinara , Col. 10, 235 ; 11, 3, 14 and 28; Sen. Herc. Fur. 206 .

Cĭnăra.opening: , = Κινάρα . A Greek proper name , Hor. C. 4, 1, 4 al. — An island in the Ægean Sea , now Zinara , Mel. 2, 7, 11 ; Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 69 .

cincinnālis.opening: adj. cincinnus , curled : herba, a plant , also called polytrichon, App. Herb. 51 .

cincinnātŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [cincinnatus], with curled hair : pueri, Hier. Ep. 130 , n. 19.

cincinnātus.opening: adj. cincinnus , with curled hair , having locks or ringlets of hair (as an indication of luxurious effeminacy), Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 115 : moechus, id. Mil. 3, 3, 49 ; id. Truc. 2, 7, 48 : consul, Cic. Sest. 11, 26 :…

Cincinnātus.opening: a cognomen of the renowned L. Qumctius, taken from the plough to the dictatorship , Liv. 3, 26, 6 ; 4, 13, 14 sq.; Cic. Fin. 2, 4, 12 ; id. Sen. 16, 56 ; Col. 1 , praef. § 13; Plin. 18, 3, 4, § 20 ; Val. Max. 4, 4 al.

cincinnus.opening: , i. kindr. with Gr. κίκιννος and Lat. cirrus; Sanscr. cicura, crinis, Bopp, Gloss. 124 a , curled hair , a lock or curl of hair , Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 32 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 31, 4 ; Cic. Pis. 11, 25 .— Trop. , too…

Cincĭŏlus.opening: dim. Cincius , a pet name for Cincius , Cic. de Or. 2, 71, 286 .

Cincĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; hence, M. Cincius Alimentus, a tribune of the people , A.U.C. 549, whose legal enactment was called Lex Cincia De donis et muneribus (quā cavetur antiquitus, ne quis ob causam orandam pecuniam…

cinctĭcŭlus.opening: dim. 2. cinctus , a little girdle , Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 28 .

cinctōrĭum.opening: 2. cinctus , a swordbelt , = balteus, Mel. 2, 1, 13 .— In gen., a girdle (late Lat.); trop.: et erit... fides cinctorium renum ejus, Vulg. Isa. 11, 5 .

cinctūra.opening: 2. cinctus, cingo , a nncture , a girdle (very rare), * Suet. Caes. 45 ; * Quint 11, 3, 139.

cinctus.opening: (post-class. access. form , , , Scrib. Comp. 163 , Isid. Orig. 19, 33 , Pophyr. ad Hor. A. P. 50 ) [cingo]. Abstr., a girding (rare): cottidiani cinctus, Plin. 28, 6, 17, § 64 ; cinctus Gabinus, a manner of girding , in…

cinctūtus.opening: adj. a lengthened form from cinctus, like astutus, actutum, versutus, etc., from astus, actus, versus, etc. , girded , girt (rare; perh. only in the foll. exs.): Luperci, * Ov F 5, 101 Cethegi, i. e. the ancients (who…

Cīnĕas.opening: , = Κινέας , the friend of king Pyrrhus of Epirus , who counselled him to make peace with the Romans , he is said to have had a remarkably retentive memory, Cic. Tusc. 1, 24, 59 ; id. Sen. 13, 43 ; id. Fam 9, 25, 1 ;…

cĭnĕfactus.opening: adj. cinis-facio : at nos horrifico cinefactum te prope busto ... deflevimus, i. e. turned to ashes, Lucr. 3, 906 , cf. Non. p. 93, 33 (Lachm. ad loc. makes the word = qui jam prope cineris colorem et adspectum nanctus…

cĭnĕrācĕus.opening: adj. cinis , similar to ashes , ashy terra, Plin. 17, 5, 4, § 33 : color, ash-colored, id. 27, 7, 27, § 44 .

cĭnĕrārĭus.opening: adj. cinis , pertaining to ashes. As adj. very rare: fines, boundaries of land bordering upon graves , Auct. Limit. p 296 Goes.— More freq. subst. , , , a servant who heated in glowing ashes the iron used in curling…

cĭnĕresco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to turn to ashes (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 40 , Fulg. Myth. 2, 18 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 20 .

cĭnĕrĕus.opening: adj. cinis , similar to ashes , ash-colored : color, Col. 2, 2, 16 ; Scrib. 23 ; Plin. 37, 10, 68, § 183 sq. : terra, id. 35, 16, 54, § 192 uva, id. 14, 3, 4, § 42 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a kind of salve , Scrib. Comp.…

cinĕrĭcĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , similar to ashes , like ashes : terra, Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 7 .

cĭnĕrōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of ashes : mortui, App. M. 4, p. 150, 27 : canities, id. ib. 7 , p. 299, 41.

Cinga.opening: a small river in Hispania Tarraconensis, in the territory of the Ilergetes, now Cinca , Caes B C. 1, 48; Luc. 4, 21

Cingetŏrix.opening: A Gaul , rival of his father-in-law Indutiomarus , in respect to dominion over the Treviri, Caes B. G. 5, 3; 5, 56 al— A king of the region about Cantium , in Britain , Caes. B. G. 5, 22 .

Cingilia.opening: a town of the Vestini on the Adriatic Sea , Liv 8, 29, 13.

cingillum.opening: dim. cingulum , a small girdle , Petr 67, 4; Not. Tir. p 158 Grut.; cf.: cingillus, στρόφιον, ζώνιον , Gloss.

cingo.opening: v. a. cf. Gr κυλλός, κυρτός; Lat. curvus, and clingo, Georg Curtius Griech. Etym. p. 545 sq. , to go round in a circle , to surround , encompass , environ , gird , wreathe , crown , etc. (class. in prose and poetry).…

cingŭlum.opening: (access. form , , m , and , , ; v. infra , cf cingulum hominum generis neutri est, nam animailum feminino genere dicimus has cingulas, Isid. Orig 20, 16, 4 ; Serv. ad Verg A. 9, 360 ) [cingo, cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 114…

Cingŭlum.opening: a small town in Picenum , now Cingulo , Caes. B. C. 1, 15 ; Cic. Att. 7, 11, 1 ; also , Sil. 10, 34 , its inhabitants were called , Plin. 3, 13, 18, § 111 .—Also adj. : , Front. Colon. p. 121 Goes.

cinifes.opening: or ( ), , , = σκνιπες or κνίπες , a kind of stinging insect (eccl. Lat.), Aug Trin. 3, 7; Hier. in Joel, 2, 25; cf. Isid. Orig. 12, 8, 14 .

cĭnīflo.opening: cinis-flo, or instead of cinilio , = cinerarius, a hair-curler , Hor S. 1, 2, 98; Tert. Uxor 2, 8 ; cf. Becker, Gallus, 2, p. 115 alt.

cĭnis.opening: (in sing. fem. , Lucr. 4, 926 ; Cat. 68, 90 ; 101, 4 ; Caesar, acc. to Non. p. 198, 11 ; Calvus ap. Non. l. l. and ap. Charis; p. 78 p; App. M. 9, 12, p. 222 ; Scrib. c. 226; 230; 232; 245, Ser. c. 44; Aus. Parent 27, 3…

cĭniscŭlus.opening: dim. cinis , a little ashes : arens, Prud. Cath. 10, 149 .

Cinithii.opening: a people of Africa , Tac. A. 2, 52 .

Cinium.opening: ( ), , , a town of the island of Majorca , now Sinau , Plin. 3, 5, 11, § 77 .

Cinna.opening: a family name of the gentes Cornelia and Helvia. L. Cornelius Cinna, consul A.U.C. 667-670; a confederate of C. Marius in the Roman civil war with Sylla , Vell. 2, 20 sq. ; Flor. 3, 21 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 19, 54 and…

cinnăbăris.opening: ( , , , Sol. 25, 14 dub., and in some MSS. and edd. Plin. 33, 7, 38, § 115 ; cf. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 555), = κιννάβαρι . A pigment obtained from the gum of the dragon ' s-blood tree , dragon ' s-blood , Plin. 33, 7,…

cĭnnămĕus.opening: adj. cinnamum , of or from cinnamon , smelling of cinnamon : nidus, Aus. Idyll. 11, 17 : odor, App. M. 8, p. 205 : crines, smelling of cinnamon, id. ib. 5 , p. 164.

cinnămolgos.opening: a bird in Arabia (prob. = κινναμολόγος ), Plin. 10, 33, 50, § 97 ; Sol. 33, 15 .

cinnămōmĭnus.opening: adj. , = κινναμώμινος , of or from cinnamon : unguentum, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 15 .

cinnămōmum.opening: , or , , (post-class. access. form , , , Sol. 33 , in the signif. of ll.), = κινναμωμον or κίνναμον [ ], cinnamon : Laurus cinnamomum, Linn. Cinnamomum, Plin. 12, 19, 42 , §§ 85 and 86. —As a term of endearment: tu mihi…

cinnus.opening: kindr. with κυκεών, κόγχος , a mixed drink of spelt-grain and wine , Arn. 5, 174 ; cf. Non. p. 59, 30 .

Cinxia.opening: , ae. cingo , an appellation of Juno , as tutelary goddess of marriage , because, acc. to Paul. ex Fest., initio conjugii solutio erat cinguli, quo nova nupta erat cincta, Fest. p. 63, 9 ; and Arn. 3, p. 115 . —Access.…

cĭnўphes.opening: corrupted from κνῖπες, σκνῖπες , very small flies , gnats , Isid. Orig. 12, 8, 14 .

Cīnyps.opening: , = Κίνυψ or Κίνυφος , a river flowing through a very fruitful region in Libya , between the two Syrtes , now Cinifo or Wady Khahan , Mel. 1, 7, 5 ; Plin. 5, 4, 4, § 27 ; Claud. Laud. Stil. 1, 251 .— Hence, , , adj. ,…

cĭnўra.opening: , = ; Gr. κινύρα , the lyre , an instrument of ten strings , Vulg. 1 Macc. 4, 54 ; 13, 51.

Cĭnўras.opening: ( , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 195 ), , , = Κινύρας . A king in Assyria , afterwards in Cyprus; father of Myrrha , and , by her , of Adonis , Ov. M. 10, 299 sq. ; cf. Hyg. Fab. 58 ; 242 ; 270 ; acc. Gr. Cinyran, Ov. M. 6, 98 ;…

Cĭŏs.opening: A river in Bithynia , Plin. 5, 32, 40, § 144 .— A town at the mouth of the river Cios , now Ghio or Ghemlio , Liv. 32, 34, 4 ; Mel. 1, 19, 4 ; Plin. l. c. v. Ciani.

cippus.opening: ( ), , kindr. with scipio; cf. σκήπτω , a pale , stake , post , pillar , Lucil. ap. Fest. p. 258 ; and specif., A gravestone , tombstone , * Hor. S. 1, 8, 12 ; Pers. 1, 37 ; Prud. Apoth. 361 ; Inscr. Orell. 4524 al. —…

Cīpus.opening: ( ), , , a fabled Roman prœtor , upon whose head horns grew suddenly , Ov. M. 15, 565 ; Plin. 11, 37, 45, § 123 ; Val. Max. 5, 6, 3 .

circā.opening: , a later access. form for circum; not freq. before the Aug. per., esp. in Livy and Quintilian [acc. to Klotz, circa = circum ea; cf: antea, interea, postea, praeterea, etc.]. Adv. ( = circum, I. B.) Around , round…

circaea.opening: , = κιρκαία , a plant used as a charm , Plin. 27, 8, 38, § 60 .

circaeum.opening: ( ), , , = κιρκαῖον , the plant also called mandragoras, Plin. 25, 13, 94, § 147 .

Circaeus.opening: pertaining to Circe; v. Circe, II.

circāmoerĭum.opening: circa-moerus, for murus; cf. pomerium , the space about a wall , on both sides of a wall : pomerium, verbi vim solam intuentes, postmoerium interpretantur esse; est autem magis circamoerium, Liv. 1, 44, 4 .

circānĕa.opening: circa , a bird so named from its circular flight , Paul. ex Fest. p. 43, 1 Müll.

Circē.opening: ( gen. Circae, Liv. And. ap. Fest. s. v. topper, p. 270; Verg. A. 3, 386 : Circes, Prop. 3 (4), 12, 27. acc Circam, Plaut. Ep. 4, 2, 34 Ritschl; Cic. N D. 3, 21, 54 ; together with Circen, id. ib. 3, 19, 48 ; v. Inscr.…

Circēii.opening: ( abl. Circēis, Hor. S. 2, 4, 33 K. and H.), , = Κιρκαῖον , the town of Circeii , near the promontory of the same name , in Latium; acc to the fable, named after Circe, who fled hither from Colchis (cf. the preced.…

circellus.opening: dim. circulus , a small ring , Apic. 2, 5 , Schol Juv. 6, 379 .

circen.opening: circinus , a circle , a circular course : solis, a year , Poët. in Anth. Lat. 4, 274 (Meyer, n. 1373).

circĕs.opening: circum-ire , a circle (ante- and post-class.): ut parvi circuli Anuli, sic magni dicebantur circites Ani, Varr L. L. 6, § 8 Müll.; Sid. Carm. 22, 222 . —So of the circumference of the circus , Sid. Carm. 23, 381 .

circĭnātĭo.opening: circino (lit. the describing of a circle; hence, concrete), the circumference of a circle , a circle (a word of Vitr.): linea circinationis, Vitr. 1, 6, 6 : circuli, id. 9, 7, 2 ; 3, 3 ; 10, 10 al. —Of the circular path…

circĭno.opening: v. a. circinus , to make round , to round (perh. not anteAug.): arbores, quae in orbem ramos circinant, Plin. 17, 12, 17, § 88 ; 16, 38, 73, § 185 : circinatum tympanum, id. 18, 34, 77, § 332 : folia circinatae…

circĭnus.opening: m.. = κίρκινος , a pair of compasses ' flumen Dubis. ut circino circumductum, paene totum oppidum cingit, Caes. B. G. 1, 38 : diducere, Vitr. 9, 7, 2 : circino spatia dimetiri, id ib.; id. 10, 4, 1 : ratio circini,…

circĭter.opening: adv. and prep. circus . Adv. Of place, round about , on every side : lapidem fuisse quadratum circiter (i. e. cubical ) in mediā arcā vinctum candelis quaquaversum, Cass. Hem. ap. Plin. 13, 13, 27, § 85 (cf. the passage…

circĭto.opening: v freq. a. [for circuito, from circueo for circumeo], to frequent , make busy : omnes istae artes, quibus aut circitatur civitas aut strepit. Sen. Ep. 90, 19 ; cf.: circito, περινοστῶ : circitat et circat, κυκλεύει ,…

circĭtor.opening: (or , Petr. 53, 10 ), , for circumitor, from circumeo, lit. one who goes around, hence , A watchman (of gardens. buildings, etc.; postclass.), Auct. Priap. 16, 1 , Front. Aquaed. 117 ; Petr. 1 1.— In milit. lang., plur.…

circĭtōrĭus.opening: circitor, II. , pertaining to patrols : dignitas, Cod. Th. 7, 22, 2, § 2.

circĭus.opening: ( , Cato ap. Gell. 2, 22, 28 sq. ), , perh. from circus, on account of its circular motion, but said to be a Gallic word , a violent wind blowing in Gallia Narbonensis; to the Romans, a west-northwest wind, Plin. 2, 47,…

circo.opening: v. a. circus . = circumeo. To go about , traverse : montem, Gromat. Vet. p. 326, 17; v. also circito fin. — To wander through : TOTAM REGIONEM, Inscr. ap. Hermes, 1, 343.

circŏs.opening: , = κιρκος (a top), a precious stone unknown to us, Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 153 .

circŭĭtĭo.opening: ( , Cic. Div. 2, 17, 40 ; 2, 61, 127 ; Liv. 3, 6, 9 ; Front. de Or. 3 ; Amm. 24, 2, 2 ), , circumeo . A going round; in milit. lang., the rounds : circuitio ac cura (vigiliarum) aedilium plebei erat. Liv. 3, 6, 9 .— A…

circŭĭtus.opening: ( , Cic. N. D. 1, 12, 29 ; 2, 62, 155 ; 2, 19, 49 ; id. Rep. 1, 29, 45 ; Quint. 1, 10, 42 al. ; cf. circumeo, and v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 737), , circumeo (class. in prose and poetry). A going round , a circling ,…

circŭlāris.opening: adj. circulus , circular , round (post-class.): flexus, Mart. Cap. 6, § 579 ; 8, § 814 init.

circŭlātim.opening: adv. circulor , circularly , in a circle (post-Aug. and rare). Prop.: pectori circulatim cerotaria apponere, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 29, 153 ; id. Tard. 1, 4, 91 ; Petr. 67 Gronov. (Büch circumlatum).— Fig., in circles ,…

circŭlātĭo.opening: id. , a circular course , revolution : Mercurii, Vitr. 9, 1, 8 .

circŭlātor.opening: id. . A pedler : auctionum, Asin. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 32, 3 .— A mountebank , quack , Cels. 5, 27, 3 ; Petr 68, 6; Dig. 47, 11, 11 ; Sen. Ben. 6, 11, 2 ; App. M. 1, p. 103, 38 .—Of noisy philosophers, Sen. Ep. 29, 5

circŭlātōrĭus.opening: adj. circulator , of a mountebank , quackish (post-Aug.): jactatio, Quint. 2, 4, 15 : volubilitas, id. 10, 1, 8 : praestigiae, Tert. Apol. 23 .

circŭlātrix.opening: id. , a female mountebank or stroller , Auct. Priap. 18, 1 . — Adj. : lingua, of a mountebank, Mart. 10, 3, 2 .

circŭlo.opening: v. a. (post - class. collat. form of circulor) [circulus], to make circu lar or round , App. flor. 9, p. 346, 21. circulatus gressus, Cael. Aur Tard. 1, 1: digitos. bent in , App. Mag. 89, p. 330 .— Esp., to encircle ,…

circŭlor.opening: v. dep. id. . To form a circle (of men) about one ' s self , or to gather in a company or circle for conversation , * Cic. Brut. 54, 200 : totis vero castris milites circulari et dolere, etc., Caes. B. C. 1, 64 .—Hence,…

circŭlus.opening: (contr. , like vinclum = vinculum, Verg. G. 3, 166 ) [kindred with κίρκος, κύκλος , circinus], a circular figure , a circle : circulus aut orbis, qui κύκλος Graece dicitur, Cic. N. D. 2, 18, 47 : muri exterior, Liv. 36,…

circum.opening: properly acc. from circus = κίρκος , adv. and prep. , designates either an entire encompassing or surrounding of an object, or a proximity only partially em. bracing or comprehending it, around , about , all around ,…

circumactĭo.opening: circumago . Lit. , a turning around , revolving (very rare): solis, Vitr. 9, 9, 15 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 885 .—* Trop. , of discourse, a turning , turn , compass , Gell. 17, 20, 4 .

circumactus.opening: circumago , a moving or turning round (post-Aug.): assiduus caeli, Sen. Q. N. 7, 2, 2 ; Censor. de Die Nat. 23 : corporis, Plin. 8, 30, 44, § 105 ; 8, 50, 76, § 201 : rotarum, id. 28, 9, 37, § 141 .

circum-aggĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to heap up around (very rare): terram, Col. 5, 12, 3 : fimo radices, Plin. 19, 5, 23, § 68 .

circum-ăgo.opening: v. a. To drive or turn in a circle , turn round (most freq. since the Aug. per.; not in Cic. or Quint.): impera suovetaurilia circumagi, Cato, R. R. 141, 1 .—And with two acc. (on account of circum): terram fundumque…

circum-ambŭlo.opening: v. a. , to walk around : omnes glebas, Dig. 41, 2, 3, § 1 .

circum-ămictus.opening: adj. amicio , enveloped , invested (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Apoc. 4, 4 .

circum-ăro.opening: v. a. , to plough around , Liv. 2, 10, 12 ; Plin. 18, 3, 3, § 9 .

circum-caesūra.opening: the external contour or outline ( = circumscriptio), Lucr. 3, 220 ; 4, 645 ; Arn. 3, p. 107 .

circum-calco.opening: (in MSS. also ), , v. a. , to tread or trample upon all around : codicem, Col. 5, 6, 21 ; id. 5, 6, 21, § 8 : terminos, Sicul. Flac. p. 6.

Circumcellĭo.opening: cella . A class of monks , who , without fixed abode , wandered about from cell to cell , Aug. in Psa. 132 .— A class of heretics , Hier. Ep. 22, 15 ; Isid. Orig. 8, 5, 53 .

circumcīdānĕus.opening: adj. circumcīdo , prop., of or from cutting or paring around : mustum, wine pressed out after the ordinary pressing, when the husks and stems remaining in the press had been cut around, Cato, R. R. 23, 4 ; cf. Plin. 14,…

circum-cīdo.opening: v. a. caedo , to cut around , cut , clip , trim (orig. in agriculture; syn.: amputo, reseco): ars agricolarum, quae circumcidat, amputet, erigat, etc., Cic. Fin. 5, 14, 39 : gemmam acuto scalpello circumcidito...…

circum-cingo.opening: v. a. , to enclose around , surround : quā Mons Apenninus regiones Italiae Etruriaeque circumcingit, Vitr. 2, 6, 5 : eum zonā gloriae, Vulg. Ecclus. 45, 9 : PORTICVS, Inscr. Orell. 4043 .—In part. pres. , Cels. 7, 15 :…

circum-circā.opening: adv. , a strengthened circum or circa, all around (cf. the Heb. , Vulg. Ezech. 40, 5 ; the Gr. ἀμφὶ τερί ; and our round about —very rare, perh. only in the foll. exs.; and acc. to Serg. ap. Don. p. 1855 P. also in…

circumcirco.opening: v. n. , = circumeo, to go round : regiones, Amm. 31, 2, 23 Eyssenh.; dub. (al. circumcurrunt).

circumcīsē.opening: adv. , v. circumcido, P. a. fin.

circumcīsĭo.opening: circumcido , a cutting around , circumcision , physical and moral (only in eccl. Lat.): carnis, cordis, spiritūs, Lact. 4, 17, 1 sqq.; Tert. adv. Jud. 2 ; 3 et saep.

circumcīsōrĭum.opening: id. , an instrument for cutting around , Veg. Vet. 1, 26, 2 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 28, 31 .

circumcīsūra.opening: id. , a cutting around : arborum, Plin. 16, 40, 79, § 219 .

circum-clāmo.opening: v. a. , to roar around , poet. of the raging waves: ora circumclamata procellis, Sid. Carm. 2, 506 .

circum-claudo.opening: v. a. (postclass. collat. form of circumcludo), to shut in : farinā circumclaudendus locus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 7, 103 .

circum-clūdo.opening: v. a. claudo , to shut in , enclose on every side (in good class. prose): ne duobus circumcluderetur exercitibus, Caes. B. C. 3, 30 ; cf. * Suet. Tib. 20 ; Auct. B. Hisp. 6: cornua ab labris argento, to surround with a…

circumcŏla.opening: circumcolo , dwelling around : gentes, Tert. adv. Gnost. 3 fin.

circum-cŏlo.opening: v. a. , to dwell round about or near : sinum maris, Liv. 5, 33, 10 : paludem, id. 31, 41, 4 ; absol. , Dig. 43, 12, 1 ; cf. ib. 43, 13, 1 : Amazones circumcolunt Tanain, Amm. 22, 8, 27 : insulam, id. 22, 8, 43 .

circum-cordĭālis.opening: adj. , around the heart (post-class.): calor, Tert. Anim. 43 : sanguis, id. ib. 15 .

circum-cŭmŭlo.opening: v. a. , to heap or pile up around : exanimes circumcumulantur acervi, Stat. Th. 10, 655 .

circum-curro.opening: v. n. , to run round or about (not ante-Aug.), Vitr. 4, 6 : circumcurrens linea, the periphery, Quint. 1, 10, 41 .—* Trop. : eam artem (rhetoricen) circumcurrentem vocaverunt. quod in omni materiā diceret, universal,…

circumcursĭo.opening: circumcurro , a running around (late Lat.), App. M. 9, p. 222, 41 .

circum-curso.grammar: āre v. freq. a. and n.
circum-curso.opening: v. freq. a. and n. , to run round about , to run about in , at , or near something (ante- and post-class.; in Cic. Fam. 7, 1, 5 , more recent editt. read concursare); act. : omnia, * Plaut. Rud. 1, 4, 4 : aliquam hinc…

circumdătĭo.opening: circumdo , the putting around : auri, Vulg. 1 Pet. 3, 3.

circum-do.opening: v. a. , lit. to put , set , or place around , i. e. both to wrap around (e. g. a mantle). and also to enclose (e. g. a town with a wall; syn.: cingo, vestio, saepio, circumvallo al.), with a twofold construction (cf.…

circum-dŏlĕo.opening: v. n. , to suffer on every side : spiratio circumdolens; acc. to Forcellini: circum, seu undique, vel ab omni parte angens, i.e. very painful, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 14, 92 .

circum-dŏlo.opening: v. a. , to hew off around , Plin. 16, 32, 57, § 133 .— Trop. : qui, tamquam bonus animi faber, vitia nostra circumdolat, Ambros. in Luc. 3, 2 .

circum-dūco.opening: v. a. ( imper. circumduce, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 83 ; id. Most. 3, 2, 159 ; id. Mil. 2, 2, 66 ), to lead or draw around (class.; esp. freq. in milit. lang.; in Cic. perh. only once). Prop.: circumduce exercitum, Plaut. Mil.…

circumductĭo.opening: circumduco . A leading or conducting around : aquarum, Vitr. 8, 6, 5 sq. : sphaerae, the circumference, Hyg. Astr. 1, 2 ; of a person, Cod. Th. 4, 8, 1.— Trop. * A cheating , defrauding : argenti, Plaut. Capt. 5 . — The…

circumductor.opening: id. , one who leads about , converts another, Tert. adv. Val. 10 .

circumductum.opening: circumduco, II. B. ; in rhet., a period, Quint. 9, 4, 22 .

circumductus.opening: circumduco . The circumference of a figure , Quint. 1, 10, 43 .—* Motion in a circle , a revolution : orbium, Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 1, 5 .

circŭm-ĕo.opening: or (v. circum, III.; Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 736 sq.), īvi or ii, circuĭtum, īre ( inf. pass. circumirier, Plaut. Curc. 3, 81 ), v. n. and a. Prop., to go around , travel or march around , etc. (class.): sparsis Medea…

circŭm-ĕquĭto.opening: v. a. , to ride round : moenia, Liv. 10, 34, 7 .

circŭm-erro.opening: v. n. , to wander round , stroll about : neque turba lateri circumerrat, Sen. Contr. 2, 9, 7 : tempora (of the revolution of Saturn in his orbit), to pass through , App. de Mundo, p. 71, 11.

circum-farcĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to fill up all around , to stuff , Plin. 17, 13, 21, § 98 .

circumfĕrentĭa.opening: circumfero , a circumference (post-class.): sedilium, App. Flor. 18, p. 359 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 817 ; Front. Expos. Form. p. 33 Goes.

circum-fĕro.opening: v. a. to bear round , or, in gen., to move or carry round or about (class. in prose and poetry). Prop.: age circumfer mulsum, pass around, Plaut. Pers. 5, 2, 45 : satiatis vino ciboque poculum... circumferetur, Liv. 26,…

circum-fīgo.opening: v. a. , to fix or fasten round (very rare): columellam cuneis, Cato, R. R. 20, 1 : duo scelesti circumfiguntur Christo, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 42 .

circum-fingo.opening: v. a. , to form around : carnem alicui, Tert. Anim. 23 .

circum-fīnĭo.opening: v. a. , to complete a circle , to bring to an end : annum, Sol. 3 .

circum-fīrmo.opening: v. a. , to fasten round : vitem, Col. 4, 17, 7 .

circum-flagro.opening: v. n. , to blaze or scorch all around : per immensum circumflagrantibus Austris, Avien. Arat. 274 .

circum-flecto.opening: v. a. , to bend or turn about (Verg. and post-class. writers); prop. of the charioteer in the circus; hence, transf.' longos cursus, Verg. A. 5, 131 ; 3, 430 .— Trop. : circumflexa saecula, returning upon themselves,…

circumflexĭbĭlis.opening: adj. circumflecto , provided with a circumflex accent (late Lat.), Excerpt. ex Macr. Diff. p. 235 Jan.

circumflexĭo.opening: id. , a bending or winding round : obliqua circuli, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 12, 1 .

circumflexus.opening: circumflecto , a bending round , a vault , arch : mundi, Plin. 2, 1, 1, § 1 : caeli, id. 6, 34, 39, § 212 .— A winding , circuit : qui (Tanais) per sinuosos labitur circumflexus, Amm. 22, 8, 27 .

circum-flo.opening: v. n. , to blow round about; of the wind (very rare; in the class. per. only in the foll. exs.): circumflantibus Austris, Stat. Th. 11, 42 .— Trop. : ab omnibus ventis invidiae circumflari, to be assailed by every…

circum-flŭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to flow round (class. in prose and poetry). Neutr. : in poculis repletis circumfluere quod supersit, flows over all around, Plin. 2, 65, 68, § 163 ; cf. Curt. 8, 8, 12 .— Act. : utrumque latus circumfluit…

circumflŭus.opening: adj. circumfluo ( poet. or in post-Aug. prose). Act. , flowing around , circumfluent : umor, Ov. M. 1, 30 : amnis, id. ib. 15, 739 : mare, Plin. 2, 66, 66, § 166 .—More freq., Pass. , flowed around , surrounded with…

circum-fŏdĭo.opening: , no perf. , fossum, ĕre ( inf. pass. : circumfodiri, Col. 5, 9, 12 ; cf. fodio), v. n. and a. , to dig around something , dig about (agricultural t. t.). Neutr. , Cato, R. R. 161 . 4.— Act. : truncum, Col. 5, 6, 17 :…

circum-fŏrānĕus.opening: adj. forum . * Of or around the forum or market-place : aes, debts due in the forum (because the bankers' shops were at the forum), Cic. Att. 2, 1, 11 .—More freq., Strolling about from market to market , that attends…

circum-fŏrātus.opening: Part. [foro], bored or pierced round ' stipes, Plin. 17, 27, 43, § 252 .

circumfossor.opening: circumfodio , one who digs around something , Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 227 .

circum-fractus.opening: Part. [frango], broken off around : turbo, broken around (sc. scopulos), Amm. 22, 8, 15 : colles, precipitous, id. 29, 4, 5 .

circum-frĕmo.opening: v. n. and a. , to make a noise around something (post-Aug. and rare): nidos, of birds, Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 7, 2 ; Prud. Cath. 479 .

circum-frĭco.opening: v. a. , to rub around , to scour , Cato, R. R. 26 .

circum-fulcĭo.opening: v. a. , to support , hold up around : togam, Tert. Pall. 5 .

circum-fulgĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine around , Plin. 2, 37, 37, § 101 .

circum-fundo.opening: v. a. , lit. to pour out around , i.e. as in circumdo, either with the acc. of that which is poured, to pour around; or, with the acc. of that around which something is poured, to surround with a liquid (class. in prose…

circumfūsĭo.opening: circumfundo , a pouring around (post-class.) spiritus ignei, Firm. Math. 1, 4: Oceani, id. ib. praef.

circum-garrĭens.opening: Part. [garrio], blabbing or babbling about. falsiloquia, Claud Mam. Stat. An. 2, 9 .

circum-gĕlo.opening: v. a. , to freeze all around corpus, Tert. Anim. 23 : cortex circumgelatus, Plin. 13, 22, 40, § 120 .

circum-gĕmo.opening: v. n. , to roar around something : circumgemit ursus ovile, Hor. Epod. 16, 51 .

circum-gesto.opening: v. freq. a. , to bear or carry around ' epistulam, * Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 2, § 6 ; deam, App. M. 8, 213, 37 .

circum-glŏbātus.opening: Part. [globo], rolled together , conglobated : animalia escae circumglobata, small insects, Plin. 9, 47, 71, § 154 .

circum-grĕdĭor.opening: v dep [gradior], to go or walk around , travel about (esp. in a hostile manner; post-Aug., several times in Tac, elsewhere rare). Absol. , Tac. A. 1, 64; 2, 17 ; 12, 28 .— With acc. : exercitum, * Sall. H. 4, 61, 21…

circumgressus.opening: circumgredior (perh. only in Amm.). * Abstr., a going about ' rapidi, Amm. 22, 2, 3 .— * Concr., the compass , circuit of a thing ' amplissimi palus Maeotis, Amm. 22, 8, 30 .

circum-hisco.opening: v. n , to stare about with open mouth , Arn. 5 , p 175 dub. (al. circumsciscere)

circum-ĭcĭo.opening: or (access. form , , 18, 17, where more recent editt. read circumagere), , v. a. To cast , throw , or place around (in good class. prose)' amic tum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 132 : vallum, Liv 35, 4, 6: fossam quoque et alia…

circŭm-īnĭcĭo.opening: v. a. , to throw up all around , = circumicio: vallum, Liv. 25, 36, 5 .

circŭm-involvo.opening: v. a. , to involve all around , to enclose , envelop : singula puncta, Vitr. 10, 11 (al. circumvolvo).

circum-jăcĕo.opening: v. n. , to lie round about , border upon (rare; not in Cic.). Absol. , * Cael. ap. Quint. 4, 2, 123 : populi circumjacentes, surrounding, Tac. A. 2, 72 . — With dat. : Lycaonia et Phrygia circumjacent Europae, Liv. 37,…

circumjectĭo.opening: circumicio . A throwing around , casting about (postclass.) manuum, Cael. Aur Acut. 1, 2, 31. —* A putting on clothing , dressing : corporis, Arn. 2 , p 73

circumjectus.opening: circumicio , a casting around , a surrounding , encompassing (rare but class.): (aether) qui terram tenero circumjectu amplectitur, with soft embrace , Cic. poet N. D. 2, 25, 65 (as transl. from Euripides Καὶ γῆν πέριξ…

circum-lambo.opening: v. a. , to lick around ora, Plin. 11, 37, 65, § 171

circum-lăquĕo.opening: v. a. , to wind around , in tmesis cassem, Grat. Cyn 29 .

circumlātĭcĭus.opening: or , , adj. circumlatus , that may be carried around , portable carcer, Sid. Ep 2, 2 fin.

circumlātĭo.opening: f [id.], a carrying around (post-class.): arcae, Tert adv Marc. 4, 12; victimae, Serv ad Verg. A. 6, 229 .

circumlātor.opening: id. , one who carries about (post-class.), Tert. adv Marc. 1, 19; 1, 21 fin

circum-lā^tro.opening: v. a. Prop., to bark around hominem, Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 22, 3 leonem, Amm 22, 16, 16.— Meton. , of the sea (post-class.): totum hoc circumlatrat aestus, roars around, Avien. Perieg 48 .— Trop. , in pass. : domus…

circum-lăvo.opening: v a. , lit. to wash around , hence, of waters, to overflow all around (only in the foll. exs.): Aegyptus, quam Nilus circumlavat, Hyg. Fab 275 : insula superjactis fluctibus circumlavitur, Sall. ap Non. p. 504, 1 ( id.…

circum-lĕvo.opening: v a. , to raise up all around tegmina, Cael Aur Acut. 2, 37, 194.

circum-lĭgo.opening: v. a. Aliquid alicui rei, to bind something to something ' natam mediae circumligat hastae, * Verg. A. 11, 555 ' spongias hydropicis, Plin 31, 11, 47, § 128.—More freq., Aliquid aliquā re, to bind something with…

circum-lĭno.opening: ( perf. late Lat. circumlinisti, Vulg. Ezech. 23, 40 ), v. a. (access. form , īre; cf. lino; so, circumliniunt, Quint. 12, 9, 8 Spald. N. er. : circumliniri, id. 1, 11, 6 : circumliniendus, Col. 6, 16, 3 ; 6, 17, 9 ).…

circumlĭtĭo.opening: circumlino . A smearing or spreading over , anointing : oris, Plin. 24, 7, 24, § 40 .— In painting, an overlaying of color , the tint or hue given to marble by rubbing it with a mixture of oil and wax , Plin. 35, 11,…

circumlŏcūtĭo.opening: circumloquor , circumlocution , periphrasis , = περίφρασις , * Quint. 8, 6, 61 ; Gell. 3, 1, 5 ; Arn. 6, p. 210 .

circum-lŏquor.opening: v. n. , to make use of circumlocution or periphrasis (post-class.), Aus. Ep. 6, 7 , and 146, 15.

circum-lūcens.opening: Part. [luceo], shining or glittering around; trop.: fortuna, Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 2, 5 .

circum-lŭo.opening: v. a. , to flow around or wash upon (rare): Rhenus tergum ac latera circumluit, Tac. H. 4, 12 : pars arcis circumluitur mari, Liv. 25, 11, 1 : litora subit et circumluit pelagus, Mel. prooem. 2: (Aegeum) mare laevā…

circum-lustro.opening: v. a. , to light all around; in tmesis: mundi templum, Lucr 5, 1437.— Trop. , to travel over or through : populos provinciae, Cod. Th. 4, 8, 5.

circum-lŭvĭo.opening: ; and , , luo , the accumulation of land by alluvion around a piece of land , alluvial land : jura circumluvionum, the right of using such land, Cic. de Or 1, 38, 173 .—Form circumluvium, Paul. ex Fest. p. 64, 14 Müll.,…

circum-mĕo.grammar: āvi, āre v. a. and n.
circum-mĕo.opening: v. a. and n. , to go around : circum eam (sc. Taprobanen) isse, for circummeasse, Mel. 3, 7 ; Tert. Pall. 1 .

circum-mētĭor.opening: v. pass. , to be measured around. columnae, Vitr. 4, 4, 3 .

circum-mingo.opening: v. a. , to make water around something; aliquem, Petr. 57, 3 : vestimenta, id. 62, 6 .

circum-mitto.opening: v. a. , to send around : legationes in omnes partes, Caes. B. G. 7, 63 ; id. B. C. 3, 55 : praecones, id B. G. 5, 51; id. B. C. 1, 12 : jugo circummissus Veiens, Liv. 2, 50, 10 : post montes, id. 4, 18, 4 : milites, id.…

circum-mulcens.opening: Part. [mulceo], licking gently around : linguae (serpentium), Plin. 28, 3, 6, § 30 .

circum-mūnĭo.opening: (old orthog. , Plaut. Capt. 2, 2, 4 ), , v. a. , to wall up around , to fortify , secure (freq. in the histt., elsewhere rare; but in MSS. constantly confounded with circumvenire; cf. Oud. ad Caes. B. C. 1, 18 ; 1, 81 ;…

circummūnītĭo.opening: circummunio ; in milit. lang., an investing of a town, circumvallation, Caes. B. C. 1, 19 fin. ; Auct. B. Hisp. 38 fin.

circum-mūrānus.opening: adj. murus , around (but beyond) the walls (perh. only in Amm.): bella, with the neighboring nations, Amm. 14, 6, 4 : pericula, id. 21, 13, 2 .

circum-nascens.opening: Part. [nascor], growing up around : absinthium, Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 232 .

circum-nāvĭgo.opening: v. a. , to sail around , circumnavigate : sinus Oceani, Vell. 2, 106, 3 .

circum-necto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to wrap or bind around , surround , envelop (late Lat.): elephanti flammis conjectis undique circumnexi, Amm. 19, 7, 7 : tenuis membrana illa perlucens, quā circumnectitur alvus, ac tegitur, Lact.…

circum-nŏto.opening: v. a. , to paint or portray around : animalia vario colore, App. M. 11, p. 279, 12, p. 273 Bip.

circum-ob-rŭo.opening: v. a. , to cover around with , wrap around , Plin. 19, 5, 26, § 83 .

circum-ornātus.opening: adj. , ornamented round about , Vulg. Psa. 143, 12 .

circum-pădānus.opening: adj. , found or situate around the Po : campi, Liv. 21, 35, 8 : lanae, Plin. 8, 48, 73, § 190 : musta, id. 14, 20, 25, § 125 .

circum-păvītus.opening: Part. [pavio], beaten or trodden close around : area, Plin. 12, 14, 32, § 58 .

circum-pendeo.opening: (better written as two words), , v. n. , to hang around : margaritis circum pendentibus, Curt. 8, 9, 24 ; Ov. F. 2, 529 .

circum-pēs.opening: (that is round the feet). A kind of parasites (cf. antepes), Agroet. Orth. p. 2274 P.— A covering of the foot , περισκελίς , Vulg. Ecclus. 45, 10 .

circum-plaudo.opening: v. a. , to applaud or greet on all sides by clapping the hands , Ov. Tr. 4, 2, 49 .

circumplecto.opening: ( act. collat. form of circumplector; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 312), to embrace , clasp around : meum collum circumplecte, Plaut. As. 3, 3, 106 : circumplectito foramina laminis, Cato, R. R. 21, 2 .— Part. pass.…

circum-plector.opening: v. dep. a. , to clasp around , embrace , to surround , encompass (class. in prose and poetry): conjunctiones motu undique, Cic. Univ. 7 fin. : domini patrimonium quasi thesaurum draco, id. Phil. 13, 5, 12 : arborem,…

circumplexus.opening: circumplector , an encompassing , embracing , or folding around; only in abl. sing. , Plin. 8, 11, 11, § 32 ; 10, 63, 83, § 174 : caeli, id. 6, 34, 39, § 212 .

circum-plĭco.opening: v. a. To wind , fold , or twine around : tum esset ostentum, si anguem vectis circumplicavisset, Cic. Div. 2, 28, 62 : locum surculo, Gell. 17, 9, 14 (cf. id. 17, 9, 14, § 9 ): belua circumplicata serpentibus, Cic. Div.…

circum-plumbo.opening: a. , to pour in lead around : modiolos, Cato, R. R. 20, 2 .

circum-pōno.opening: v. a. , to set , put , or place around (perh. not before the Aug. per.): ferulas, Cels. 8, 10, 1 : stramenta, Plin. 17, 28, 47, § 263 : armatos, * Suet. Caes. 30 : piper catillis, * Hor. S. 2, 4, 75 : nemus stagno, Tac.…

circumpŏsĭtĭo.opening: circumpono , a setting or placing around (eccl. Lat.): auri, Aug. Ep. 199 ; Ambros. Ep. 38, 1 .

circumpōtātĭo.opening: poto , a drinking around in a funeral meal , Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. Cic. Leg. 2, 24, 60 Orell. N. cr.

circum-pulso.opening: v. a. , to strike or beat around; of sounds: aures, to din, Stat. Th. 6, 228 .

circum-pungo.opening: v. a. , to prick or puncture around : clavum pedis, Cels. 5, 28, 14 (cf.: clavi circum scarificati, Plin. 22, 23, 49, § 101 ).

circum-purgo.opening: v. a. , to cleanse or purify around : dentem, Cels. 7, 12, 1 ; Ambros. Spir. Sanct. 1, 10, 113 init.

circum-pŭto.opening: v. a. , to measure all round : computato Oceano, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 114.

circum-quāque.opening: adv. , on every side , all round , Auct. Orig. Gent. Rom. 17, 6.

circum-rādo.opening: v. a. , to scrape , shave , or pare around : tonsillas digito, Cels. 7, 12 , n. 2: dentem, id. ib. : sarmentum circumrasum, Col. 4, 29, 14 .

circumrāsĭo.opening: circumrado , a scraping or paring around : corticis, Plin. 17, 26, 39 . § 246.

circum-rētĭo.opening: v. a. , to enclose with a net , insnare. Prop.: Martem et Venerem Vulcani esse circumretitos arte, Arn. 5, p. 186 ; cf. id. 4, p. 181 ; cf. circumnecto fin. — Trop. : aliquem, Lucr. 5, 1152 : aliquem fraude, Sid. Ep. 5,…

circum-rōdo.opening: v. a. , to gnaw or nibble all round. Prop.: escam, Plin. 32, 2, 5, § 12 .— Trop. : dudum enim circumrodo, quod devorandum est, i. e. I have long hesitated to speak out , * Cic. Att. 4, 5, 1 : qui Dente Theonino cum…

circum-rōrans.opening: Part. [roro], sprinkling all round : aliquem, App. M. 11, p. 268, 21 .

circum-rŏto.opening: v. a. , to turn round in a circle : caeli orbem, C. German. Fragm. 3, 9 : machinas, App. M. 9, p. 222, 7 .

circum-saepĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to hedge or fence round with something , to surround , enclose (not anteAug.): circumsepta loca parietibus, Col. 1, 6, 4 ; Dig. 41, 2, 3, § 14 : stagnum aedificiis, * Suet. Ner. 31 : solium circumsaeptum…

circum-saltans.opening: Part. [salto], dancing around : chorus, Prud. adv. Symm. 1, 135 .

circum-scărĭphĭcātus.opening: ( , Plin. 30, 3, 8, § 21 ), a, um, Part. [scarifico], scarified around : clavi pedum, Plin. 22, 23, 49, § 101 : dens, id. 30, 3, 8, § 21 .

circum-scindo.opening: v. a. , to rend , strip , or tear off around : aliquem et spoliare, Liv. 2, 55, 5 .

circum-scrībo.opening: v. a. Prop., to draw a line around , to circumscribe , enclose in a circle (in good prose; very freq. in Cic.): orbem, Cic. Fin. 5, 8, 23 : lineas extremas umbrae, Quint. 10, 2, 7 : virgulā stantem, Cic. Phil. 8, 8, 23…

circumscriptĭo.opening: circumscribo . * Prop. (acc. to circumscribo, I.), an encircling , and (concrete) a circle : ex circumscriptione excedere, Cic. Phil. 8, 8, 23 .— (Acc. to circumscribo, II. A.) A boundary , limit , outline , contour ,…

circumscriptor.opening: circumscribo . * (Acc. to circumscribo, II. C.) A defrauder , deceiver , cheat , * Cic. Cat. 2, 4, 7 ; * Juv. 15, 136 ; Sen. Exc. Contr. 6, 3 ; Cod. Th. 10, 10, 27, § 4.—* (Acc. to circumscribo, II. D.) He who makes…

circumscriptōrĭē.opening: adv. , by fraud , deceit : agere aliquid, Lex Rom. Burg. tit. 36.

circumscriptus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from circumscribo, q. v. fin.

circum-sĕco.opening: , no perf. , sectum , v. a. , to cut or pare around : radices vitium, Cato, R. R. 114, 1 : ungulas, Col. 6, 6, 4 : tuberculum ferro, id. 7, 5, 13 : aliquid serrulā, to saw around , * Cic. Clu. 64, 180 : circumsecta…

circum-sĕcus.opening: adv. , round , round about , in the region around (only in App.): astantes, App. M. 2, p. 121, 11 ; 5 , p. 166, 23; 11, p. 264, 33; cf. Hand, Turs. II. p. 74.

circum-sĕdĕo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to sit around a person or thing , to surround. In gen., absol. : inter tot milia populi circumsedentis, App. M. 3, p. 130, 2 ; Sid. Ep. 3, 13 .—With acc. : florentes amicorum turba circumsedet: circa…

circum-sēpăro.opening: to separate around : gingivas a dentibus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4, 74 .

circum-sĕro.opening: v. a. , to sow , set , or plant around something : genistas alveariis, Plin. 21, 12, 42, § 72 .

circumsessĭo.opening: circumsedeo, II. , a hoslile encompassing , a besieging , Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 33, § 83 .

circum-sīdo.opening: v. a. , to set or place one ' s self around in a hostile manner, to besiege (several times in Livy; elsewhere rare): Plistiam, Liv. 9, 21, 6 ; 36, 13, 7 ; 41, 19, 10 ; 42, 56, 5: regem urbemque Philippopolim, Tac. A. 3,…

circum-signo.opening: v. a. , to mark around : gemmam, Col. 5, 11, 19 ; id. Arb. 26, 8 ; Pall. Jun. 5, 3 .

circum-sĭlĭo.opening: v. n. salio , to spring , leap , or hop around (rare): (passer) circumsiliens modo huc, modo illuc, * Cat. 3, 9 .— Trop. , to leap about , surround : morborum omne genus, * Juv. 10, 218 .

circum-sisto.opening: ( Caes. B. G. 3, 15 Oud. N. cr.; 4, 37; Curt. 15, 9, 10 ; Verg. A. 2, 559 ; Tac. A. 15, 15 ; id. H. 4, 79 ; cf. circumsto; rarely circumstiti, Tac. H. 3, 31 ), , v. a. , to place one ' s self or take one ' s stand…

circum-sĭtus.opening: adj. sino , lying or situate around , neighboring : populi, Amm. 23, 6, 17, p. 358 Bip. al.

circum-sŏcĭus.opening: adj. , neighborly , in friendly neighborhood : nationes, Sext. Aur. Vict. Epit. 41 .

circum-sŏno.opening: v. n. and a. (rare but class.). Neutr. , to sound , resound ( with something ) on every side , to be filled with any sound : locus, qui circumsonat ululatibus cantuque symphoniae, Liv. 39, 10, 7 ; 27, 18, 16 ; Vitr. 5,…

circum-sŏnus.opening: adj. , sounding all around. * Act. , filling with sounds : turba canum, barking around, Ov. M. 4, 723 .—* Pass. , filled with sounds , resounding around : Thisbe avibus, Stat. Th. 7, 261 .

circum-spectātrix.opening: spectator , she who looks or spies around , a spy , Plaut. Aul. 1, 1, 2 : juvenum, App. Mag. 76, p. 323, 10 .

circumspectē.opening: adv. , v. circumspicio, P. a. fin.

circumspectĭo.opening: circumspicio . * Prop., a looking on all sides , a looking about : singulorum, sibi horizontem facit, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 15, 17 .— Trop. , foresight , circumspection , caution (v. circumspicio, I. B.): circumspectio…

circum-specto.grammar: āvi, ātum, āre v. freq. a.
circum-specto.opening: v. freq. a. , to look about with attention , precaution , desire , etc.; to cast a look around , to search around; and with acc. , to look about one ' s self ( attentively , anxiously , etc.) after something , to look…

circumspector.opening: circumspicio , a watcher , watchman , spy (late Lat.): septem circumspectores sedentes in excelso ad speculandum, Vulg. Ecclus. 37, 18 : Deus, i. e. all-seeing, id. ib. 7, 12 .

circumspectus.opening: circumspicio . Prop., a looking around eagerly , cautiously; a spying , searching around (rare but class.): cervix flexilis ad circumspectum, Plin. 11, 37, 67, § 177 : (natura) circumspectum omnium nobis dedit, Sen. Ot.…

circum-spergo.opening: ( , Apic. 8, 8, § 406 ; cf. aspergo), , v. a. To sprinkle , strew , or scatter something around : quaternos modios stercoris caprini, Col. 11, 2, 87 : impensam talem, Apic. l. l.— To sprinkle with something all around :…

circumspĭcĭentĭa.opening: circumspicio, II. B. , consideration , deliberation , Gell. 14, 2, 13 .

circum-spĭcĭo.opening: ( perf. sync. circumspexti, Ter. Ad. 4, 5, 55 ; inf. sync. circumspexe, Varr. ap. Non. p. 106, 16 , or Sat. Men. 82), v. n. and a. (class.). Neutr. , to look about one ' s self , to cast a look around; or, with an…

circum-stagno.opening: v. n. , to be poured forth all around : lacrimae, Tert. Pud. 22 .

circumstantĭa.opening: circumsto (post-Aug. and rare). A standing round , a surrounding : hostium, Gell. 3, 7, 5 : aquae, aëris, Sen. Q. N. 2, 7, 2 (as transl. of the Gr. ἀντιπερίστασις ).—* Concr., a surrounding circle , a band , troop :…

circumstătĭo.opening: circumsto , a standing around; concr., a circle : militum, Gell. 7, 4, 4 .

circum-stīpo.opening: or , , v. a. , to surround , accompany , attend (in post-Aug. poetry and rare).— Absol. : magnā circumstipante catervā, Sil. 10, 453 .— Pass. , Claud. Laud. Stil. 2, 356 ; id. VI. Cons. Hon. 595 .

circum-sto.opening: v. n. and a. (the perf. and pluperf. having the same form with those of circumsisto, and a similar meaning, it is sometimes doubtful to which verb a form belongs), to stand around in a circle , to take a station round;…

circum-strĕpo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To make a noise around , to din with clamor , to cause to echo around (post-Aug.), (legatus) clamore seditiosorum circumstrepitur, Tac. H. 2, 44 : fenestrae canticis circumstrepitae, App. Mag. 75,…

circum-strīdens.opening: Part. [strido], shrieking or gibbering around : larvae, Amm. 14, 11, 17 .

circum-stringo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. (post-class.). * To bind about , to put on : aliquid alicui rei: habitus cervicibus circumstrictus, Tert. Pall. 1 .— To tie around , to surround , clothe with : aliquid aliquā re: pallium, Tert.…

circum-strŭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to build round about , surround with buildings (post-Aug. and mostly in part. pass. ). Aliquid aliquā re: lacrimis arborum fores alveorum, Plin. 11, 6, 5, § 15 ; Col. 9, 6, 4 : ripis undique…

circum-stŭpĕo.opening: v. a. , to look around with amazement , to stand amazed , Auct. Aetn. 336 dub. (al. circumstrepit).

circum-sūdans.opening: Part. [sudo], sweating on all sides : vinacea, Plin. 14, 1, 3, § 16 .

circum-surgens.opening: Part. [surgo], rising all around (post-Aug.): juga, Tac. A. 1, 64 : mora, Cels. 7, 15, 6 .

circum-sūtus.opening: Part. [suo], sewed together all around (post-Aug.): linamenta, Cels. 8, 5 : navigia corio, Plin. 4, 16, 30, § 104 ; 34, 16, 47, § 156 .

circum-tĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cover round about (post-class.): corpus veste, Dict. Cret. 3, 11 : arca testamenti circumtecta ex omni parte auro, Vulg. Heb. 9, 4 ; v. also the spurious line, Lucr. 1, 1094 Lachm. and Munro ad loc.

circum-tĕnĕo.opening: to keep around , to possess , Vulg. 4 Esdr. 16, 40.

circum-tentus.opening: Part. [tendo], bound or covered with something that is stretched or drawn around , begirt (anteand post-class.): elephanti corio, * Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 80 : vasculum linteolis, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 174 .

circum-tergeo.opening: v. a. , to wipe around , Cato, R. R. 76, 2 .

circum-termĭno.opening: v. a. , to bound or limit round about , Isid. Orig. 7, 8, 39 .

circum-tĕro.opening: v. a. , to rub around , poet. for, to stand close around , crowd around : aliquem, Tib. 1, 2, 95 .

circum-textus.opening: Part. [texo], woven all around : velamen, Verg. A. 1, 649 . — Subst. : , , , a garment inwoven with purple : et quod amictui habet purpuram circum, vocant circumtextum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 132 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 24, 10 .

circum-tinnĭo.opening: v. a. , to ring or tinkle around , Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 30 .

circum-tollo.opening: v. a. , to remove on every side : corticem, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 42 .

circum-tŏno.opening: v. a. , to thunder around; or, poet. , to make a noise or clamor around : virum armis, Sil. 4, 254 : aulam strepitu, id. 6, 216 : montem undā, Claud. in Rufin. 1, 274 .— Trop. : hunc circumtonuit gaudens Bellona…

circum-tonsus.opening: Part. [tondeo], shorn all around (rare). Prop., Varr. ap. Non. p. 179, 8 ; * Suet. Aug. 45 : pinus, Petr. 131, 8, 3 .—* Trop. , of discourse: oratio circumtonsa et fucata et manu facta, elaborate, artificial, Sen. Ep.…

circum-torquĕo.opening: v. a. , to twist or turn around : me retrorsum, App. M. 6, p. 186, 14 .

circum-trăho.opening: v. a. , to draw or drag around (post-class.), Dict. Cret. 3, 15 fin; Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 .

circum-tuèŏr.opening: v. dep. n. , to look around , App. Flor. p. 341, 5 .

circum-ustus.opening: uro , burnt around , Paul. ex Fest. p. 5, 3 , Müll.

circum-vādo.opening: v. a. , to assail or attack on every side , to encompass , beset (not ante-Aug.). Prop.: naves, Liv. 10, 2, 12 : aliquem clamoribus turbidis, * Tac. A. 12, 43 : redeuntem noctu, Plin. 9, 30, 48, § 92 . — Pass. , Amm.…

circum-văgor.opening: v. dep. n. , to wander about , Vitr. 5, 8, 2 .

circum-văgus.opening: adj. , wandering about , flowing around (very rare): oceanus, * Hor. Epod. 16, 41 ; cf. Auct. Pan. ad Pis. 19; Prud. Psych. 814 .

circum-vallo.opening: v. a. , to surround with a wall , to circumvallate; in milit. lang., to blockade , invest , encompass in a hostile manner (class., esp. in the histt.): circumvallare loci natura prohibebat, Caes. B. G. 7, 17 ; 7, 11 ;…

circumvectĭo.opening: circumveho (only twice in Cic.). A carrying around (of merchandise), Cic. Att. 2, 16, 4 .— Solis, the circuit , revolution , Cic. Univ. 9, 26 .

circumvectĭtor.opening: dep. a. [circum-vectito], to travel about , visit in succession : oppida circumvectitabor, Plaut. Rud. 4, 2, 28 Fleck.

circum-vecto.opening: v. freq. a. , to carry around : Penates, Sil. 3, 291 .—Hence, Esp., mid., to ride or sail around (rare): Ligurum oram, Liv. 41, 17, 7 ; cf. circumvectitor.— Poet. , to go through , describe : +ugit irreparabile tempus,…

circum-vĕhor.opening: v. dep. , to ride around (in a carriage or on horseback), to sail around (class., but not in Cic.); constr. absol. or with acc. dependent on circum: in terras orasque ultimas, Plaut. Most. 4, 3, 4 : mare superum omne…

circum-vēlo.opening: v. a. , to cover around , envelop : aurato circumvelatur amictu, Ov. M. 14, 263 .

circum-vĕnĭo.opening: v. a. , lit., to come around something; hence (the coming being considered as accomplished; cf. advenio and adventus, II.). Lit. In gen., to be around (a thing), to encircle , encompass , surround (rare): quibus…

circumventĭo.opening: circumvenio, II. B. 2. , a circumventing , defrauding (postclass. and rare): adversarii, Dig. 4, 4, 17 ; Cod. Just. 2, 43, 3 : innocentium, Aug. Civ. Dei , 22, 22.

circumventor.opening: id. , a deceiver , defrauder , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 66 .

circumventōrĭus.opening: adj. circumventor , deceitful , fraudulent : obsequia, Aug. Conf. 3, 3 .

circumversĭo.opening: circumverto , a turning round , moving around , revolving (post-Aug. and rare): manus (in gesturing), * Quint. 11, 3, 105 Spald.: cursus annui, Amm. 26, 1, 11 .

circum-verso.opening: or ( ), , v. freq. a. , to turn around (rare and only pass. in mid. sense): quaerentesque viam circumversantur, Lucr. 5, 520 ; 6, 200 ; Avien. Arat. 1528 .

circum-versus.opening: Part. [verro], brushed or swept around : locus purus, circumversus, Cato, R. R. 143, 2 .

circum-verto.opening: or ( ), , v. a. , to turn around (rare; not in Cic.): citius quam rotula circumvortitur, Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 39 ; cf.: rota circumvertitur axem, turns or is turned around on its axis , Ov. M. 15, 522 (Merkel,…

circum-vestĭo.opening: v. a. To clothe or cover over (very rare): arborem, Plin. 17, 23, 35, § 208 .—In a figure: aliquem amictu prudentiae, Ambros. Virg. 12, 48 .—* Poet. , of one who uses language to conceal his thoughts: se circumvestire…

circum-vincĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to bind around : juncis murteta, aliquem virgis, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 27 ; Avien. Perieg. 331 .

circum-vīso.opening: v. a. , to look around at , glare round upon : set angues oculis omnis circumvisere, Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 58 .

circumvŏlĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. circumvolito , flying round : aër, Mart. Cap. 6, § 584 .

circum-vŏlĭto.opening: or , , v. a. and n. (mostly post-Aug.). Prop., to fly around something : lacus circumvolitavit hirundo, * Verg. G. 1, 377 : thyma, * Hor. Ep. 1, 3, 21 .— Absol. : circumvolitantium alitum, Tac. H. 2, 50 .— In gen., of…

circum-vŏlo.opening: v. a. (not ante-Aug.). Prop., to fly around : turba (Harpyiae) praedam circumvolat, Verg. A. 3, 233 : seu (me) mors atris circumvolat alis, Hor. S. 2, 1, 58 ; so Verg. A. 2, 360 : caput, id. ib. 6, 866 ; Ov. M. 2, 719 ;…

circum-vŏlūto.opening: v. a. , to roll around , pass. in mid. force, Plin. 8, 17, 21, § 59 .

circum-volvo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , only with se or mid., to roll one ' s self around , to roll round , revolve , wind , or twine around (prob. not ante-Aug.): aliquid or alicui rei: magnum sol circumvolvitur annum, Verg. A. 3, 284…

circus.opening: , = κίρκος [kindr. with κρίκος ; Dor. κίρκος , and κορώνη ; cf.: κυλινδέω, κυλλός , cirrus, curvus]. A circular line , circle , in astronomy (less freq. than circulus): quot luna circos annuo in cursu institit, Att. ap.…

cīris.opening: , = κεῖρις , a bird (acc. to Hyg. Fab. 198 , a fish = κίρρις , Etym. M.), into which Scylla , the daughter of Nisus , was changed , Ov. M. 8, 151 ; Verg. Cir. 488 sq.

cirrātus.opening: adj. cirrus . Curled , having ringlets (post-Aug.), Mart. 9, 30 : feminae, Amm. 14, 6, 20 .— Subst. : , Pers. 1, 29 .— Vestes, fringed , Capitol. Pert. 8 .

Cirrha.opening: ( ), , , = Κίρρα , a very ancient town in Phocis , near Delphi , devoted to Apollo, Liv. 42, 15, 5 ; Stat. Th. 3, 474 ; Luc. 3, 172 ; Mart, 1, 77; cf. Mel. 2, 3, 10 ; Plin. 4, 3, 4, § 7 .—Hence, ( ), , adj. , of or…

cirrītus.opening: adj. cirrus , having filaments : pirum, a kind of pear , Cloat. ap. Macr. S. 2, 15, 16 ; cf. Not. Tir. p. 155 .

cirrus.opening: (used mostly in plur. ), a (natural) lock , curl , ringlet , or tuft of hair (rare): cirri, Varr. ap. Non. p. 94, 21 ; Mart. 10, 83 .— Sing. : cirrus, Juv. 13, 165 .—Also, the hair on the forehead of a horse , Veg. 2,…

cirsĭon.opening: , = κίρσιον , a kind of thistle , Plin. 27, 8, 39, § 61 .

Cirta.opening: , = Κίρτα , an important town in Numidia , now Constantine , Mel. 1, 6, 1 ; Plin. 5, 3, 2, § 22 ; Sall. J. 21, 2 ; 26, 1 ; 101, 1 ; 102, 1; Liv. 29, 32, 14 al. — , , , its inhabitants , Liv. 30, 12, 8 ; Tac. A. 3, 74 ;…

cis.opening: prep. pronom. stem ki-, whence -ce; Gr. ἐ-κεῖ; cf.: hic, sic, etc. (far more rare than the kindr. citra), on this side (opp. uls, ultra, and trans; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 83 Müll.; Liv. 5, 35, 4 ; 5, 33, 9 al. ); with…

Cis-alpīnus.opening: adj. , lying on this side of the Alps , Cisalpine (very freq.): Gallia, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 12, 35 ; Caes. B. G. 6, 1 : Galli, Liv. 27, 38, 6 : provincia, Suet. Caes. 29 .

cĭsĭārĭus.opening: cisium . The driver of a cabriolet , Dig. 19, 2, 13 .— Plur. : CISIARIEI, C. I. L. 1, 1165.— The maker of a cabriolet , Inscr. Orell. 4109 ; 4163 .

cĭsĭum.opening: a light two-wheeled vehicle , a cabriolet (vehiculi biroti genus, Non. p. 86, 30 ), Cic. Phil. 2, 31, 77 ; id. Rosc. Am. 7, 19 ; Vitr. 10, 1, 6 ; Aus. Ep. 8, 6 ; gen. cisi, Verg. Cat. 8, 3 Burm.; cf. Becker, Gall. 3, p.…

cis-montānus.opening: adj. , situate on this side of the mountain : Aufinates, Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 106 .

cīsōrĭum.opening: caedo , a cutting instrument : ossis, Veg. 3, 22, 1 .

cispellam.opening: , a false read. for aspellam, Plaut. Am. 3, 4, 17 .

Cispĭus.opening: (also , old form in Varr. L. L. 5, § 50 Müll.): mons, one of the peaks of the Mons Esquilinus, now the church S. Maria Maggiore , Varr. L. L. l. l.; Gell. 15, 1, 2 ; Fest. p. 348, 28 ; p. 351, 1; Paul. ex Fest. p. 42,…

Cis-rhēnānus.opening: adj. , situate on this side of the Rhine : Germani, Caes. B. G. 6, 2 .

cissanthĕmŏs.opening: , = κισσάνθεμος , a plant similar to ivy , a species of cyclaminos, Plin. 25, 9, 68, § 116 ; 26, 15, 90, § 156 .

cissărŏs.opening: , or , , , the plant also called chrysanthemon, App. Herb. 17 .

Cisseus.opening: , = Κισσεύς . A king of Thrace; acc. to a later myth, father of Hecuba , Verg. A. 5, 537 ; Hyg. Fab. 91 ; 911 ; who is on this account called , Verg. A. 7, 320 Serv.; 10, 705.— A companion of Turnus , acc. Cissea, Verg.…

Cissis.opening: a town in Hispania Tarraconensis, Liv. 21, 60, 7 sq. Alschefski ad loc.

cissītis.opening: , = κισσῖτις , a precious stone of the color of ivy-leaves , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 188 .

cissŏs.opening: , = κισσός . Ivy , Plin. 16, 34, 62, § 152 .— Cissos erythranos, an ivylike plant , Plin. 24, 10, 49, § 82 .* † , , , = κισσύβιον , a cup of ivy-wood , Macr. S. 5, 21, 11 .

cista.opening: , = κίστη , a wooden box or basket , often woven of slips or twigs , used for keeping money , clothes , books , fruit , etc. In gen., Plin. 15, 17, 18, § 60 ; 16, 40, 77, § 209 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 85, § 197 ; * Hor. Ep.…

cistella.opening: dim. cista , a small chest or box , Plaut. Cist. 3, 7 ; 4, 1, 3 sq.; id. Rud. 4, 4, 65 sq. ; Ter. Eun. 4, 6, 15 ; Auct. Her. 1, 12, 21 dub. (al. sitella).

Cistellārĭa.opening: cistella , the title of a comedy of Plautus; cf. Varr. L. L. 7, § 64 ; Non. p. 63, 33 .

cistellātrix.opening: id. , she who has charge of the money-box (a kind of female slave), Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 25 (253 Ritschl).

cistellŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little box or chest , Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 141 Ussing (Fleck. cistula); id. Rud. 2, 3, 60 ; 4, 4, 34 .

cisterna.opening: cista , a subterranean reservoir for water , a cistern , Varr. R. R. 1, 11, 2 ; Col. 1, 5, 2 ; Sen. Ep. 86, 3 ; Plin. 31, 3, 21, § 31 ; 36, 23, 52, § 173 ; Mart. 3, 56, 1 ; Tac. H. 5, 12 al. —For preserving wine, Dig.…

cisternīnus.opening: adj. cisterna , of or pertaining to cisterns , cistern- : aqua, Col. 12, 43, 6 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 10 ; Veg. 2, 28, 18 ; 6, 8, 3 .

Cisthēna.opening: , = Κισθήνη , a town of Æolis , Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 122 ; Mel. 1, 18, 2 .

cisthos.opening: , = κίσθος (usu. κίστος ), a shrubby plant with red blossoms , Plin. 24, 10, 48, § 81 .

Cis-tĭbĕris.opening: adj. , = cis Tiberim, on this side of the Tiber : quinqueviri, Dig. 1, 2, 2, § 33 : magistratus, Pomp. Orig. Jus. § 33 Osann.

cistĭfer.opening: cista-fero , the bearer of a box or chest , Mart. 5, 17, 4 .

cistŏphŏrus.opening: or , , , = κιστοφόρος . The bearer of the sacred box , Inscr. Orell. 2318 .— An Asiatic coin of the value of about four drachms , on which a cista was stamped , Cic. Att. 2, 6, 2 ; 2, 16, 4 ; 11, 1, 2 ; id. Dom. 20, 52…

cistŭla.opening: dim. cista , a little box , chest , or basket , Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 264 ; id. Rud. 2, 3, 58 ; 4, 4, 38 sq.; Mart. 4, 46, 13 ; App. M. 9, p. 236, 40 .

cĭtātē.opening: adv. , v. 2. cito, P. a. fin.

cĭtātim.opening: adv. citatus, cito , quickly , speedily , hastily (very rare), Auct. B. Afr. 80; comp. and sup. , v. 2. cito fin.

cĭtātĭo.opening: 2. cito . In law, the calling , proclaiming : edictorum sollemnium, Cod. Just. 1, 12, 6, § 4 .— Milit. t. t. , the command , Hyg. Grom. § 43, p. 91.

cĭtātōrĭum.opening: 2. cito , a summoning before a tribunal , Cod. Th. 6, 28, 5.

cĭtē.opening: adv. , v. cieo, P. a. fin.

cĭter.opening: ( comp. citerior; sup. citimus; most freq. in comp.; in posit. only Cato ap. Prisc. pp. 589 and 999 P.; and Afran. ap. Prisc. p. 607 ib.), adj. cis . On this side : citer agnus (ager) alligatus ad sacra erit, Cato ap.…

cĭtĕrĭa.opening: an effigy or caricature carried in procession at the games , Paul. ex Fest. p. 59, 20 Müll.; Cato ib.

Cĭthaeron.opening: ( , Aus. Idyll. 11, 32 ), , , = Κιθαιρών , a mountain of Bœotia , now Elatia , sacred to Bacchus and the Muses , and famous for the death of Pentheus and Actœon , Mel. 2, 3, 4 ; Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 25 ; Verg. G. 3, 43 ;…

cĭthăra.opening: , = κιθάρα , the cithara , cithern , guitar , or lute (very freq. in the poets, esp. in Hor.), Lucr. 2, 28 ; 4, 981 ; Tib. 2, 3, 12 ; 2, 5, 2 ; Verg. A. 6, 120 ; 9, 776 ; Hor. C. 1, 15, 15 ; 2, 12, 4 ; Varr. L. L. S, §…

cĭthărĭcen.opening: cithara-cano; cf. tubicen , the player on the cithara (unused); cf. Varr. L. L. 8, § 61 Müll.

cĭthărista.opening: , = κιθαριστής , a player on the cithara (mostly in Cic.), Cic. Phil. 5, 6, 15 ; id. Div. 2, 64, 133 .—Esp., a statue of a player on the cithara : etiam illum Aspendium citharistam, de quo saepe audistis id quod est…

cĭthăristrĭa.opening: , = κιθαρίστρια , she who plays on the cithara , Ter. Phorm. 1, 2, 32 ; 1, 2, 94 ; Sid. Ep. 9, 13, 2 ; Porphyr. ad Hor. C. 1, 1 .

cĭthărīzo.opening: v n. , = κιθαρίζω , to play on or strike the cithara , Nep. Epam. 2, 1 ; Vulg. Apoc. 14, 2 .

cĭthăroedĭcus.opening: adj. , = κιθαρῳδικός , of or pertaining to the citharœdi : ars, Plin. 9, 8, 8, § 28 ; Suet. Ner. 40 : habitus, id. ib. 25 ; Eutr. 7, 14 : vestis, Dig. 50, 16, 127 .

cŏactor.opening: id. . Prop. A collector of money (from auctions, of revenues, etc.), Cato, R. R. 150, 2 ; Cic. Clu. 64, 180 ; id. Rab. Post. 11, 30 ; * Hor. S. 1, 6, 86 ; cf. Acron. and Porphyr. in h. l. and Auct. Vit. Hor. 1 ; Sen.…

cŏactus.opening: cogo , a forcing , constraint , compulsion (rare and only in abl. sing. ): alterius magno coactu, * Lucr. 2, 273 : coactu atque efflagitatu meo, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 29, § 75 ; 2, 2, 13, § 34 : civitatis, Caes. B. G. 5, 27 .

cŏ-addo.opening: v. a. , to add with , add also , Cato, R. R. 40, 2 ; Plaut. Cas. 3, 1, 4 .

cŏ-ădōro.opening: v. a. , to worship or adore along with (late Lat.), Ambros. Spir. Sanct. 3, 12 ; Cod. Just. 1, 1, 4 .

cŏ-ădŭlesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow up along with (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 19 ; 16 .

cŏădūnātĭo.opening: coaduno , a uniting into one , a summing up : totius calculi, Cod. Just. 5, 12, 31 fin.

cŏ-ădūno.opening: v. a. , to unite , add , or join together , to collect into one (postclass.), Dig. 10, 4, 7 ; 2, 14, 9 ; Aur. Vict. Vit. 1 ; Dict. Cret. 4, 13 .

cŏ-aedĭfĭco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to build up together , build upon (only in Cic.): Campum Martium, Cic. Att. 13, 33, 4 : loci coaedificati an vasti, id. Part. Or. 10, 36 : quarta pars (urbis), Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 53, § 119 Zumpt N.…

cŏ-aegresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become sick at the same time with , Tert. Anim. 5 dub. (al. cohaerescit).

cŏ-aegrōto.opening: v. n. , to be sick at the same time with , Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 47 .

cŏ-aequālis.opening: adj. , of equal age , coeval (post-Aug.): sinciput, Petr. 136, 1 .— Subst. , a comrade , companion in age , Just. 23, 4, 9 ; Inscr. Orell. 4407 al. — Transf. , of geese, Col. 8, 14, 8 .

cŏ-aequo.opening: v. a. , to make one thing equal or even with another , to even , level (rare but in good prose). Prop.: aream, Cato, R. R. 91 and 129: montes, Sall. C. 20, 11 : pastinatum, Col. 3, 16, 1 : sulcum, id. 11, 3, 48 :…

cŏ-aestĭmo.opening: v. a. , to estimate together with : aliquid, Dig. 47, 2, 69 .

cŏaetānĕo.opening: v. n. coaetaneus , to be of the same age , Tert. Res Carn. 45 .

cŏ-aetānĕus.opening: aetas , one of the same age; a contemporary (post-class.), App M. 8, p. 204, 5; Tert. adv. Herm. 6 ; Vulg. Gal. 1, 14 .

cŏ-aeternus.opening: adj. , coeternal (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Herm. 11 ; Hier. Ep. 16 , n. 4 al.

cŏ-aevus.opening: adj. aevum , of the same age , coeval (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Serm. 38 ; id. Verb. Dom. 7 ; Prud. Cath. 12, 137 ; Vulg. Dan. 1, 10 .

cŏ-aggĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. * To heap together : lapides, Serv. ad Verg. A. 5, 273 .—* Aliquid aliquā re, to cover by heaping upon , Col. 8, 6, 1 .

cŏ-ăgĭto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to shake together (in late medic. lang.), Apic. 2, 1 ; 4, 3 ; Marc. Emp. 8 .

cŏagmentārĭus.opening: coagmentum , joining together , ἁρμολόγος , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

cŏagmentātĭo.opening: coagmento , a joining or connecting together; a connection , combination , union (several times in Cic.; elsewh. rare): corporis, Cic. Univ. 5 fin. : non dissolubilis, id. N. D. 1, 8, 20 : naturae, id. ib. 2, 46, 119 .—…

cŏagmento.opening: v. a. coagmentum , t. t., to join , stick , glue , cement , etc., together , to connect (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.). Prop.: opus ipsa suum eadem, quae coagmentavit, naturā dissolvit, Cic. Sen. 20, 72 : nihil…

cŏagmentum.opening: cogo , a joining together; in concr., a joint (in good prose; not in Cic.; mostly in plur. ). Prop., Non. p. 42, 20 sq. ; Cato, R. R. 18, 9 ; Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 143 ; Caes. B. C. 3, 105 fin. ; Vitr. 2, 3, 4 ; 2, 8, 3 ;…

cŏāgŭlāre.opening: coagulo (sc. intestinum), the colon , Veg. 8, 16, 1 al.

cŏāgŭlātĭo.opening: id. , a curdling , coagulating , of a liquid (in the elder Pliny): lactis, Plin. 23, 1, 18, § 30 ; 28, 10, 45, § 158 .

cŏāgŭlo.opening: (contr. COAGLAVI, Inscr. ap. Anthol. Lat. 1177 Meyer), , v. a. coagulum , to cause a fluid to curdle or coagulate (mostly in the elder Pliny): lac, Plin. 12, 25, 54, § 123 ; 20, 14, 53, § 147 : picem, id. 16, 11, 22, §…

cŏāgŭlum.opening: cogo , a means of coagulation , a coagulum or coagulator (the curdled milk in the stomach of a sucking animal, the stomach itself, etc.), rennet or runnet , Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 4 ; Col. 7, 8, 1 ; Plin. 11, 41, 96, § 237…

cŏ-ălesco.opening: ( part. perf. only in Tac. and subseq. writers; contr. form colescat, Varr. R. R. 1, 41, 2 : colescere, Lucr. 6, 1068 : coluerunt, id. 2, 1061 Lachm. N. cr. ), v. inch. n. (most freq. since the Aug. per.; never in…

cŏălĭtus.opening: coalesco , communion , fellowship : humani generis, Arn. 4, p. 150 .

cŏ-ălo.opening: v. a. , to sustain or nourish together with : fetus, Hier. in Jovin. 1, 36 .

cŏ-ambŭlo.opening: v. n. , to go with , Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 3 .

cŏ-angusto.opening: v. a. , to bring into a narrow compass , to confine , compress , contract , enclose , hem in (rare and mostly post-Aug.). Prop.: alvos, * Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 15 : quo facilius fistula claudatur vel certe coangustetur,…

cŏaptātĭo.opening: coapto , an accurate joining together (a word coined by Augustine for translating the Gr. ἁρμονία ), Aug. Trin. 4, 2 ; id. Civ. Dei, 22, 24.

cŏ-apto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to fit , join , adjust together with something (eccl. Lat.; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2 , pp. 135 and 248), Aug. Doctr. Christ. 1, 14 ; Prud. Psych. 557 .

cŏ-āresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to dry or become dry together , Vitr. 7, 11 (al. coaluerint).

cŏ-argŭo.opening: v. a. , orig., to assail a person or thing in different directions (cf. arguo init. ); hence, jurid. t. t. Aliquem, to overwhelm with reasoning , refute , silence , expose; convict of guilt or crime , prove guilty…

cŏargūtĭo.opening: coarguo , a convicting , refutation , Hier. Ep. 41, 4 .

cŏarmĭo.opening: co-arma , a comrade in arms , Inscr. Orell. 2571 .

cŏ-armo.opening: to arm together , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 5, 45 al.

cŏartātĭo.opening: ( ), , coarto , a drawing or crowding together (rare): laxatio aut coartatio, Vitr. 9, 9 : plurium in angusto tendentium, Liv. 27, 46, 2 ; so, militum eo loco, Auct. B. Alex. 74 fin.

cŏ-artĭcŭlo.opening: v. a. , to cause to articulate : ora mutorum, Arn. 1, p. 31 .

cŏ-arto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to press together , compress , contract , confine (opp. laxo, dilato, etc.; class.). Prop.: faenum in struem, Col. 2, 19, 2 ; 8, 7, 2 : alveum Tiberis (opp. laxo), Suet. Aug. 30 : angustae fauces coartant…

cŏassātio.opening: ( ), , coasso , a joining of timber ( boards or planks ) together; hence in concr., a boarded floor , Vitr. 6, 3, 9 ; 7, 1, 1 sq.—In plur. , Plin. 36, 25, 62, § 186 .

cŏasso.opening: ( ), co-axis , to join boards or planks together , Vitr. 7, 1, 5 .

cŏ-assūmo.opening: to assume together , Boëth. Arist. top. 6, 8.

cŏauctĭo.opening: coaugeo , a joint increase , Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 82, § 189 ; dub. al. leg. conjectio or conjunctio.

cŏaxo.opening: v. n. the natural sound of frogs; cf. κοάξ , to croak , Suet. Aug. 94 ; Auct. Phil. 62; Spart. Get. 6 .

Cobiamăchus.opening: ( ), , , a village in Gallia Narbonensis, between Tolosa and Narbo , Cic. Font. 5, 9 .

cōbĭon.opening: , = κώβιον , a species of the plant tithymalus ( wolf ' s-milk ), called also dendroides and leptophyllon, Plin. 26, 8, 45, § 71 .

Coccēius.opening: the name of an Italic gens. Cocceius Nerva, Hor. S. 1, 5, 28 . — M. Cocceius Nerva, a celebrated lawyer under Tiberius , Tac. A. 4, 58 al. — M. Cocceius Nerva, grandson of the preceding , Inscr Orell. 1634; emperor ,…

coccum.opening: , = κὀκκος (a berry, and specif.), The berry that grows upon the scarlet oak (Quercus coccifera, Linn.; acc. to modern botany a kind of insect, cochineal kermes ), with which scarlet was colored , Plin. 16, 8, 12, § 32…

coccȳgĭa.opening: f , = κοκκυγία , a kind of sumach used in coloring , perh. Rhus cotinus, Linn.; Plin. 13, 22, 41, § 121 .

coccȳmēlum.opening: , = κοκκύμηλον , a plum , Cloat. ap. Macr. S. 2, 15 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 17, 7, 10 .

cocētum.opening: perh. from κυκεών , a kind of food prepared from honey and poppies , Tert. adv. Val. 12 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 39, 8 Müll.

cochlacae.opening: ( ), , , = κόχλακες , round stones from a river , resembling snails ' shells , Paul. ex Fest. p. 39, 7 Müll.

cochlis.opening: , = κοχλίς , a precious stone like a snail-shell in form , Plin. 37, 12, 74, § 194 .

cochloe.opening: , = κόχλοι , a kind of shell-fishes with spiral shells , Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 147 Sillig N. cr.

cocĭātor.opening: , = μεταβόλος , cocio, a broker , Gloss. Vet. (prob. for cocĭōnātor).

cōcĭōnātūra.opening: cocio , μετάπρασις , brokery , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

cōcĭōnor.opening: v. dep. id. , to be a broker , Quint. Decl. 12, 21 dub.

coclĕārĭum.opening: ( ), , coclea . An enclosure or pen in which snails were kept and fed , Varr. R. R. 3, 12, 2 ; 3, 14, 1 .— A spoon; v. cochlear.

coclĕātim.opening: ( ), adv. id. , spirally , Sid. Ep. 4, 15 fin.

coclĕātus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , spiral or screw-formed : equuleus, Pomp. ap. Non. p. 105, 15 , and 182, 14: aures, Cassiod. Anim. 9 .

coclĕŏla.opening: ( ), , dim. id. , a small snail , Hier. Ep. 64 , n. 19; id. in Jov. 2, 6 .

cō^cles.opening: for scoculus; root ska-; cf. σκιά, σκότος, and oculus (cf. Fleck. in Rhein. Mus. 8, p. 231) , cognomen of a person blind with one eye , Plin. 11, 37, 55, § 150 ; so Enn. ap. Varr L. L. 7, § 71; Plaut. Curc. 3, 1, 23 .

coco.opening: , acc. to others , the sound naturally made by the hen , clucking , Petr. 59, 2 .

cŏcŏlŏbis.opening: or , , , a Spanish name for a kind of grape. —Form -ŭbis, Col. 3, 2, 19 .—Form -ŏbis, Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 30 .

Cocosātes.opening: a tribe in Aquitania , Caes. B. G. 3, 27 ; Plin. 4, 19, 33, § 108 .

coctūra.opening: id. , a cooking; a melting; a manner or style of cooking , Col. 11, 3, 23, p. 453 Bip.: Apiciana, Plin. 19, 8, 41, § 143 ; 34, 8, 20, § 96 ; Apic. 6, 2 al. ; Pall. Nov. 1, 3 .— Meton. A temperature of the air adapted to…

cŏcŭla.opening: (also ), , dim. coquus , a female cook , Varr. ap. Non. p. 531, 32 .

cŏcŭlum.opening: coquo . * A vessel for cooking , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Isid. Orig. 20, 8, 1 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 39, 2 Müll.— Acc. to some, small wood for cooking , Paul. ex Fest. l. l.; cf. Gloss. Isid. Plac. p. 448 Mai.

Cōcȳtus.opening: ( ), , , = Κωκυτὀς [river of lamentation, from κωκὐω , to howl, weep], a mythic river in the Lower World , Cic. Tusc. 1, 5, 10 ; id. N. D. 3, 17, 43 ; Verg. G. 3, 38 ; 4, 479 ; id. A. 6, 132 ; 6, 297 ; 6, 323 ; Hor. C.…

Cōdēta.opening: coda = cauda , a place in which grew plants resembling the tails of horses. Codeta Major, a place beyond the Tiber , Paul. ex Fest. p. 58, 4 ; cf. ib. p. 38, 17 Müll.—Hence, , , um: campus, Reg. Urb. Rom. 14.— Codeta…

cōdĭcŭla.opening: dim. coda = cauda , a little tail , Apic. 7, 1 dub.

Codomannus.opening: cognomen of the last Persian king Darius , Just. 10, 3 ; 11, 6 sq.

Codrio.opening: or , , , a town in Greek Illyria , Liv. 31, 27, 5 .

Cōdrus.opening: , = Κόδρος . The last Athenian king , who voluntarily devoted himself to death in order to obtain for his people victory over the Spartans , Cic. Tusc. 1, 48, 116 ; id. Fin. 5, 22, 62 ; id. N. D. 3, 19, 49 ; Hor. C. 3,…

Coela.opening: (ōrum, ), Euboeae, Κοῖλα τῆς Εὐβοίας , a deeply-indented maritime region in Eubœa , Liv. 31, 47, 1 ; Val. Max. 1, 8, 10 ; hence this part of Eubœa is also called Coela Euboea, Val. Max. l. l.

Coelē Sўrĭa.opening: , or in one word , , , = Κοίλη Συρἰα (lit. Hollow Syria ), Cœlesyria , between Libanus and Antilibanus , Plin. 5, 20, 17, § 77 ; Liv. 33, 19, 8 ; 42, 29, 9 ; Curt. 4, 1, 4 ; cf. id. 4, 5, 9 . —Called simply Coele, Mel.…

cŏ-ĕlĕmentātus.opening: adj. elementum , composed of elements , Tert. adv. Val. 23 .

coelĭăcus.opening: adj. , = κοιλιακός . Relating to the abdomen or to the stomach : dolor, pain in the stomach, Cato, R. R. 125 (in Cels. 4, 12 , written as Greek).— Subst. : , , (sc. medicina), stomach remedy , Plin. 20, 18, 76, § 201 .—…

coelĭōtĭcus.opening: adj. , = κοιλιωτικός , cleansing the stomach or bowels , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5 .

cŏ-ēmendātus.opening: Part. [emendo], amended at the same time , Arn. 2, 18 fin.

coemēsis.opening: , = κοίμησις , a somniferous song , Mart. Cap. 9, p. 335 (by Kopp, § 996, written as Greek).

coemētērĭum.opening: , = κοιμητήριον (a sleeping - chamber; hence), a churchyard , cemetery , burying-ground (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 51 al.

cŏ-ĕmo.opening: v. a. (cf. the contracted form, 1. como), to purchase together , to buy up (class.): aliquid, Ter. Ad. 2, 2, 17 ; Caes. B. G. 1, 3 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 59, § 133 ; Cassius ap. Cic. Fam. 15, 19, 3 ; Hor. S. 1, 2, 9 ;…

cŏëmptiōnālis.opening: (in MSS. also contracted ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. p. 135 ), , adj. coëmptio , pertaining to a sham sale or a sham marriage : senex, who was made use of in such a performance (cf. Cic. Mur. 12, 27 ); accordingly, poor,…

cŏëmptĭōnātor.opening: id. ; jurid. t. t., one who enters into the coemptio, Gai Inst. 1, 115 sq. ; 2, 98 ; Ulp. Sent. 11, 5 al.

cŏëmptor.opening: coëmo , one who purchases many things , buys up; trop.: testium, App. Mag. p. 321, 31 .

coenŏbīta.opening: coenobium , a cloister-brother , a monk , Hier. Ep. 22 , n. 34 al.

coenŏbĭum.opening: , = κοινόβιον , a cloister , convent , Hier. Ep. 22 , n. 36 al.

coenŏmyia.opening: , = κοινόμυια , the common fly , Vulg. Psa. 104, 31 al. ; cf. Hier. Ep. 106 fin.

coenon.opening: , = κοινόν , a kind of eyesalve , Inscr. Orell. 4234 .

cŏ-ĕo.opening: (e. g. coierunt, Caes. B. G. 6, 22 : coiere, Lucr. 6, 452 ; Prop. 3 (4), 24, 18 ; Ov. M. 4, 83 al. : cŏĭisse, Verg. A. 12, 709 : coisse, Prop. 3 (4), 15, 8. Ov. F. 6, 94 ; Quint. 5, 9, 5 ; 5, 11, 35 ; pedants preferred…

coepĭo.opening: (the tempp. press. only a few times in the ante-class. period, and coepturus, Liv. 30, 5, 6 ; 42, 47, 3 ; Quint. 10, 1, 46 ; Plin. 16, 25, 41, § 98 ; Suet. Calig. 46 ; the tempp. perff. , both in act. and pass. form,…

cŏ-ĕpiscŏpus.opening: an associate bishop , Hier. adv. Lucif. 9 ; Sid. Ep. 4, 25 et saep.

cŏ-ĕpŭlōnus.opening: epulo , a fellowbanqueter or companion at a feast , Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 20 .

cŏ-ĕpŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to feast together (late Lat.), Ambros. Ep. 19, 15 .

Coerănus.opening: , = Κοίρανος , a Greek Stoic philosopher , Tac. A. 14, 59 .

cŏ-ercĕo.opening: v. a. arceo , to enclose something on all sides or wholly , to hold together , to surround , encompass : qui (mundus) omnia complexu suo coërcet et continet, Cic. N. D. 2, 22, 58 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 40, 101 ; Ov. M. 1, 31…

cŏërcĭtĭo.opening: (in MSS. also , , ), , coërceo, II. , a restraining , coercing; coercion , restraint , compulsion , chastisement , punishment (not ante-Aug.). Prop.: coërcitionem inhibere, Liv. 4, 53, 7 : sine coërcitione magistratus,…

cŏërcĭtor.opening: coërceo , one who restrains : disciplinae militaris, an enforcer, Eutr. 7, 20 ; 7, 18 Bip.

cŏ-erro.opening: v. n. , to go or wander about together , Dig. 1, 15, 3, § 3 .

cŏ-exercĭtātus.opening: exercised together or at the same time : artem constare ex perceptionibus consentientibus et coexercitatis ad finem vitae, Quint. 2, 17, 41 (as a transl. of the Gr. ἐγγεγυμνασμέναι καταλήψεις ).

cofānus.opening: a pelican , App. Fragm. p. 609 Oud.

cōgĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. cogito , conceivable , imaginable (post-Aug. and very rare), Sen. Ep. 58, 13 : Deus, App. Mag. p. 315, 4 .

cōgĭtābundus.opening: adj. id. , thinking , thoughtful : Socrates, Gell. 2, 1, 2 .

cōgĭtāmentum.opening: id. , a thought (late Lat.), Vulg. 4 Esdr. 7, 22; cf. cogitamentum, ἐνθύμημα , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

cōgĭtātim.opening: adv. , pro cogitate, Paul. ex Fest. p. 61, 9 Müll.

com-porto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to bear , carry , or bring together , to collect (class.): nobis opus est rebus exquisitis, undique collectis, arcessitis, comportatis, Cic. de Or. 3, 24, 92 : eo frumentum ex Asiā, Caes. B. C. 3, 42 :…

com-pŏs.opening: ( ), , adj. potis , having the mastery , control , or power over a thing , master of , partaking of , possessing , participating or sharing in , guilty of , etc. (very freq. and class.); constr. usu. with gen. , more…

com-poscens.opening: Part. [posco], demanding at the same time , Mart. Cap. 5, p. 136 Grot. dub. (Kopp, § 425, Deliacos poscens artus); Not. Tir. p. 58 .

compŏsĭtē.opening: adv. , v. compono, P. a. fin.

compŏsĭtĭcĭus.opening: or , , adj. compositus , compound , Tert. Anim. 9 .

compŏsĭtĭo.opening: ( ), , compono . A putting together , compounding , connecting , arranging , composition , adjustment , etc. Prop.: unguentorum, Cic. N. D. 2, 58, 146 : membrorum, id. ib. 1, 18, 47 .—Fig.: varia sonorum, Cic. Tusc. 1,…

compŏsĭtīvus.opening: adj. compositus, compono , suitable for uniting , compositive , Mart. Cap. 9, § 945 .

compŏsĭtor.opening: ( ), , compono , an orderer , arranger , disposer , maker (rare): inventor aut compositor aut actor, Cic. Or. 19, 61 : anni, id. Leg. 2, 12, 29 (al. compositio): operum, Ov. Tr. 2, 356 : juris, Cod. Just. 6, 28, 4 :…

compŏsĭtūra.opening: (contr. , Cato, R. R. 22, 3 ). , id. , a joining together , connection (very rare, and only anteclass.). Prop.: olei, Cato, l. l.: oculorum, a connection, commissure, Lucr. 4, 327 . — Trop. , of discourse, conneclion ,…

compŏsĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from compono.

com-pōtātĭo.opening: a drinking together , as transl. of the Gr. συμπόσιον (perh. only in Cic.), Cic. Sen. 13, 45 ; id. Fam. 9, 24, 3 .

compōtātor.opening: , collat. form of compotor, a drinking-companion (late Lat.), Ambros. de Job et Dav. 3, 5, 17.

compŏtens.opening: adj. , having power with one , an epithet of Diana, Inscr. Grut. 41, 2 .

compŏtĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. compos , to make partaker of (only anteand post- class.); constr. with acc. pers. and abl. or gen. rei. Act. : me piscatu novo, Plaut. Rud. 4, 2, 6 : aliquem praedae, App. de Deo Socr. prol. p. 366, 20 :…
