com-pōtrix.opening: ( ), , compotor , a female drinking - companion , Ter. And. 1, 4, 5 ; Sid. Ep. 2, 9 .

com-praecīdo.opening: v. a. , to cut off at the same time : alteram lineam (altera), Hyg. Limit. p. 177 Goes. dub.

com-praes.opening: a joint-surety , Paul. ex Fest. p. 39, 10 Müll.

com-pransor.opening: a companion in a banquet, a boon companion , Cic. Phil. 2, 39, 101 .

comprĕcātĭo.opening: comprecor , a common or public imploring of a deity : sollennis deorum, Liv. 39, 15, 2 ; plur. : deūm inmortalium, Gell. 13, 22, 1 .

com-prĕcor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. (lit. to worship a deity with all the usages belonging thereto; hence, in gen.), to pray to, supplicate, implore (mostly ante-class. and rare; not in Cic.); constr. alicui, aliquem, aliquid , or absol. :…

com-prĕhendo.opening: ( ; also , very freq. in MSS. and edd.; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 21 . In MSS. also and , v. prehendo), di, sum, 3, v. a. , to lay hold of something on all sides; to take or catch hold of, seize, grasp, apprehend; to comprehend,…

comprĕhensĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. comprehendo , that can be seized or laid hold of (very rare; prob. first used by Cic.). Prop.: comprehensibile et solidum corpus, Lact. 7, 12, 2 .—As subst. : , , (opp. incomprehensibile), Tert. Apol. 48 .—…

comprĕhensĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a seizing or laying hold of with the hands . Prop. In gen. (very rare): ingressus, cursus, sessio, comprehensio, Cic. N. D. 1, 34, 94 ; cf. id. Ac. 2, 47, 145 .— Esp., a hostile seizure, arresting,…

comprĕhensīvus.opening: adj. comprehendo , comprehensible, conceivable (late Lat.): definitione, Boëth. Defin. p. 660.

comprĕhenso.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to embrace : suos, Claud. Quadrig. ap. Prisc. p. 797 P.

compressē.opening: adv. ; v. comprimo, P. a. fin.

compressĭo.opening: ( ), , com primo , a pressing together, compression . Prop. In gen.: aurum compressione coactum, Vitr. 7, 8, 4 ; Oros. 7, 6 .— With gen. : ventris, Gell. 16, 3 : musculorum, Scrib. Comp. 84 .— Esp., An embracing : artae…

compresso.opening: , no perf. , , v. freq. a. id. , to press, oppress (late Lat.), Tert. contr. Gnost. 3; Porphyr. ad Hor. S. 2, 3, 173 .

compressor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who compresses (in mal. part.), Mythogr. Vatic. 1, 18; Plaut. Argum. Aul. 2, 7 .

compressus.opening: comprimo , a pressing together, compression (only in abl. sing. ). In gen.: semen tepefactum vapore et compressu suo diffindit (terra), * Cic. Sen. 15, 51 : pennarum, Plin. 11, 28, 34, § 98 . — Esp., an embracing,…

com-prĭmo.opening: ( ), , v. a. premo , to press or squeeze together, compress (very freq and class.). In gen.: (corpora) inter se compressa teneri, Lucr. 6, 454 : dentis, Plaut. Ps. 3, 1, 21 : cum plane (digitos) compresserat pugnumque…

com-prŏbo.opening: ( ), , v. a. Subject., to approve wholly of something, to assent to, sanction, acknowledge (class and very freq., esp in prose): istam tuam sentent. am laudo vehementissimeque comprobo, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 24, 69 : decretum…

comprōmissārĭus.opening: adj. compromissum , pertaining to arbitration : judex, an arbitrator, umpire, referee chosen by contending parties (jurid. Lat.), Dig. 4, 8, 41 ; 26, 5, 4 .

comprōmissum.opening: a mutual promise to abide by the award of an arbiter , Cic. Rosc. Com. 4, 12 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 27, § 66 ; id. Fam. 12, 30 ; Dig. 4, 8, 1 sq. —From

com-prōmitto.opening: ( ), (contr. form conpromesise = conpromisisse, S. C. Bacch. v. 14), v. a. , jurid. t. t. in lawsuits, to promise mutually to abide by the decision of an arbiter : tribunicii candidati conpromiserunt, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 14…

com-prōvincĭālis.opening: adj., born in the same province , Sid. Ep. 7, 7 .

Compsa.opening: a town of the Hirpini in Samnium , now Conza , Liv. 23, 1, 1 ; Vell. 2, 63, 3 .—Hence, ( ), , adj., of or pertaining to Compsa : ager, Liv. 24, 44, 8 : Trebius, id. 23, 1, 1 ; cf. Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 61 , §§ 160 and…

comptē.opening: adv. , v. 1. como, P. a. fin.

comptor.opening: 1. como , one who adorns; only trop.: fabricarum, Cassiod. Var. 4, 51 .

comptŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [comptus, 1. como], luxuriously decked : juvenes, Hier. Ep. 128 , n. 4.

comptus.opening: 1. como , an ornament for the hair or head, a head-dress , Lucr. 1, 88 ; Afran. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 40, 9 Müll.; cf. ib. p. 63, 13 .

compugnantĭa.opening: compugno , a fighting together (late Lat.): inter se contrariorum aërum, Isid. Orig. 5, 35, 8 .

com-pugno.opening: v. n. To fight or contend together (post-class.), Gell. 12, 5, 3 ; 14, 5, 4 ; 14, 5 fin. ; Sulp. Sev. de Vita S. Mart. 14 .— To combat together : amaritudinem, Veg. Art. Vet. 1, 13, 6 .

compulsāmentum.opening: compulso , an impelling; trop., an exhortation , Fulg. Myth. 3, 6 .

compulsātĭo.opening: id. , a (hostile) pressing together, a contest, contention (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 21 ; 38 ; Fulg. Myth. praef. fin.

compulsĭo.opening: compello . An urging, constraint, compulsion , Dig. 36, 1, 14, § 1 sqq.— A dunning , Cassiod. Var. 12, 10 .

compulso.opening: v. freq. [id.]. To press or strike violently (post-class. and rare), App. M. 7, p. 197, 16 .— To contend or fight together , Tert. Apol. 20 ; cf. compulsatio.

compulsor.opening: id. (late Lat.). Lit. , a driver (of cattle), Pall. Jun. 2, 3 . — Transf. , one who asks or forces to a payment, an exacter of money , Amm. 22, 6, 1 ; Cod. Th. 8, 10, 3 and 4; 11, 7, 15.

compulsus.opening: compello , a (hostile) striking together , App. M. 8, p. 203, 6 .

Compulterĭa.opening: a little town in Samnium , Liv. 23, 39, 6, 24, 20, 5 .

compunctĭo.opening: compungo . Lit. , a puncture : ligni, Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 3, § 8.— Trop. , the sting of conscience, remorse (eccl. Lat.), Salv. adv. Avar. 4, 8 al.

compunctōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , admonitory, hortatory (eccl. Lat.): sermo, Sid. Ep. 6, 6 .

com-pungo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to prick or puncture severely, to sting . Prop. (rare but class.): collum dolone, Phaedr. 3, 6, 3 : aculeis urticae, Col. 8, 14, 8 : acu, Cels. 6, 18, 9 : barbarus compunctus notis Threïciis, branded,…

compurgātĭo.opening: a complete purification (late Lat.): tres compurgationes, i. e. by fire, air, and water, Mythogr. Lat. 3, 6, 18.

com-purgo.opening: v. a. , to purify completely : visum, Plin. 20, 13, 50, § 127 .

compŭtābĭlis.opening: adj. computo , that may be computed, computable : impendium, Plin. 19, 8, 41, § 139 .

compŭtātĭo.opening: id. , a computing, reckoning; a computation (post-Aug.). In gen., Sen. Ep. 84, 7 ; id. Ben. 7, 10, 4 ; Plin. 2, 108, 112, § 247 ; 6, 33, 38, § 206 ; Plin. Pan. 38, 3 ; * Quint. 1, 10, 35 al. — Specif., the reckoning of…

compŭtātor.opening: id. , a computer, reckoner (post-Aug.): diligentissimi, Sen. Ep. 87, 5 al.

com-pŭto.opening: ( ), , v. a. To sum up, reckon, compute. Prop. (mostly post-Aug.): id si computare quem piget, brevioribus numeris idem discat, Quint. 1, 10, 43 : digitis rationem, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 51 ; cf. Suet. Dom. 4 : annos,…

com-pū^tresco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. , to become wholly putrid, to putrefy, rot (very rare; not in Cic.): Cass. Hem. ap. Plin. 13, 13, 27, § 86 ; Col. 5, 10, 7 ; Plin. 32, 7, 23, § 67 (Sillig, conputuere).—Per tmesin: artus pereunt…

compŭtus.opening: computo , a computation (late Lat.), Firm. Math. 1, 12 fin. ; Auct. ap. Goes. Agrim. p. 236 .

comtē.opening: = compte, v. 1. como, P. a. fin.

cŏmŭla.opening: dim. coma , pretty hair bessalis, Petr. 58, 5 ; Commod. 60, 11 .

Cōmum.opening: , = Κῶμον , a considerable town in Gallia Transpadana, the birthplace of the younger Pliny , now Como , Liv. 33, 36, 14 ; Plin. Ep. 1, 3, 1 ; Just. 20, 5, 8 ; Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 124 ; rebuilt by Caesar; hence also…

cōnābĭlis.opening: adj. conor , laborious, difficult (late Lat.): conabiles atque laboriosi vomitus, Cael. Aur Acut. 3, 1, 4.

cōnāmen.opening: id. , an effort, exertion, struggle ( poet. ): alarum, Lucr. 6, 836 : eundi, id. 6, 326 : magno conamine, Ov. M. 3, 60 ; cf. id. ib. 8, 366 ; id. F. 4, 325 ; Luc. 4, 287 .—In plur. : conamina mortis, Ov. M. 10, 390 ;…

cōnāmentum.opening: conamen , an instrument for uprooting a plant , Plin. 19, 2, 7, § 27 .

cōnātĭo.opening: conor , an undertaking, endeavoring, an effort, endeavor, attempt (post-Aug. and rare), Sen. Q. N. 2, 12, 1 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 9 .

cōnātus.opening: conor . Abstr., an effort, exertion, struggle, endeavor : ue ista hercle magno jam conatu magnas nugas dixerit, Ter. Heaut. 4, 1, 8 : quo majore conatu studioque aguntur, Cic. Quint. 14, 47 : omnem sui tribunatus…

con-căco.opening: v. a. , to defile with ordure, to fill with defilement : totam regiam, Phaedr. 4, 17, 11 : se, Sen. Apoc. 4 fin. : catillus concacatus, Petr. 66 .

con-caedes.opening: ( sing. abl. concaede, Amm. 16, 12, 15 ), , an abattis, barricade of felled trees (post-Aug.), Amm. 16, 12, 15 ; 17, 10, 6 .— Plur. , Veg. Mil. 3, 22 ; Tac. A. 1, 50 ; Amm. 16, 11, 8 .

con-călĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to warm thoroughly (rare but class.). Act. : bracchium, Cic. de Or. 2, 78, 316 .— Pass. : , , factus sum: vertat ova, uti aequabiliter concalefiant, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 11 : trabes concalefaciuntur, are heated,…

con-călĕo.opening: v. n. , to be thoroughly warm (rare), Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 8 .

con-călesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become or grow thoroughly warm, to glow . Prop. (rare but class.): corpora nostra ardore animi concalescunt, * Cic. Tusc. 1, 18, 42 : frumenta non poterunt cito concalescere, Vitr. 6, 9 ; cf. Plin. 18,…

con-calfactōrĭus.opening: adj. concalefacio , suitable for warming, warming : vis herbae, Plin. 21, 20, 83, § 141 .

con-callesco.opening: v. inch. [calleo]; lit., to become hard or callous; hence, trop., * Of the intellect, to become shrewd, practised (cf. calleo, I.): callidos eos appello, quorum, tamquam manus opere, sic animus usu concalluit, Cic. N.…

concămĕrātĭo.opening: concamero , a vaulting; a vault , Vitr. 2, 4 ; 5, 10 ; Plin. 11, 10, 10, § 22 ; Dig. 32, 31 al.

con-cămĕro.opening: v. a. , to vault or arch over : templum, Plin. 34, 14, 42, § 148 .—In part. pass. : sudatio, Vitr. 5, 11, 2 ; Suet. Aug. 90 ; Inscr. Orell. 3033 : uvae pensili concameratae nodo, suspended from a vault or arch , Plin.…

con-candesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to glow, be inflamed , Manil. 1, 874 ex conj. (Codd. excanduit).

Concăni.opening: , = Κωγκανοί , a savage people of Cantabria in Hispania Tarraconensis; sing. collect.: Concanus, Hor. C. 3, 4, 34 ; Sil. 3, 361 .

concapit.opening: , and difficult of explanation; in the XII. Tab. in a passage in Fest. p. 365 Müll.; cf. Dirks. Uebersicht, etc., p. 433 sq.

con-captīvus.opening: a fellow-captive , Hier. Ep. 119 ; Vulg. Rom. 16, 7 .

concarnātĭo.opening: concarno , a uniting with flesh, incarnation , Tert. Mon. 9 fin.

con-carno.opening: v. a. , to unite or clothe with flesh, to incarnate (post-class. and very rare), Tert. Carn. Christ. 20 ; Veg. Art. Vet. 2, 22, 3 .

con-castīgo.opening: v. a. , to chastise severely, to punish (ante- and post-class.): hominem probe, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 94 ; 5, 2, 56 ; id. Trin. 1, 1, 4 ; M. Aur. ap. Fronto Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 9 .

concătēnātĭo.opening: concateno , a connecting, joining (late Lat.). Lit. , Cassiod. Var. 12, 19 .— Trop. A concatenation, sequence : temporum, Tert. Apol. 19 : causarum, Aug. Civ. Dei , 3, 30.— Mentis (i. e. constrictio), fettering, binding…

con-cătēno.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to link or bind together, to connect (late Lat.), Lact. 3, 17 ; Min. Fel. 17, 2 .

con-cătervātus.opening: adj. caterva , heaped or crowded together : copiae, Amm. 29, 5, 38 : manipuli, id. 31, 13, 2 .

concăvĭtas.opening: concavus , a hollow, cavity (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 14 .

concăvo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. id. , to make hollow, to hollow out, make round (very rare): bracchia in arcus, to curve, bend, Ov. M. 2, 195 ; cf. manus, Nemes. Ecl. 3, 49 : concavati nidi, Col. 8, 5, 11 .

con-căvus.opening: adj., hollow, concave; arched, vaulted; bent, curved : cymbala, Lucr. 2, 619 ; cf.: concava aera, Ov. M. 4, 30 : loca terrae, Lucr. 5, 1255 : altitudines speluncarum, Cic. N. D. 2, 39, 98 : saxa, Verg. G. 4, 49 :…

con-cēdo.grammar: cessi, cessum, 3 v. n. and a.
con-cēdo.opening: v. n. and a. (a strengthened cedo, and corresp. with it in most of its signiff.); lit., to go, walk; hence, Neutr. , with reference to the terminus a quo, to go or walk away from a place, to depart, retire, withdraw,…

con-cĕlē^bro.opening: v..a. (a strengthened celebro; rare but class.). To resort to in multitudes or frequently, to frequent : variae volucres loca aquarum Concelebrant, Lucr. 2, 345 : convivia et passim et tributim, Q. Cic. Pet. Cons. 11,…

con-cellīta.opening: cella , he who dwells with one in a cell, a cell-mate , Sid. Ep. 8, 14 .

con-cēlo.opening: v. a. , to conceal carefully (perh. only in Gell.): errores, Gell. 15, 2, 5 ; 11, 9, 2 .

con-cēnātĭo.opening: ( ), , , a supping together, companionship at table; transl. of σύνδειπνον (like compotatio of συμπόσιον ), Cic. Sen. 13, 45 ; id. Fam. 9, 24, 3 .

concentĭo.opening: concino , a singing together, harmony (very rare): clarissima (catervae), Cic. Sest. 55, 118 ; id. Tim. 8, 24 ; App. de Mundo, p. 71, 20.

concentor.opening: id. , one who sings with others in a chorus (late Lat.), συνῳδός , Gloss. Isid. 7, 12, 28 .

con-centŭrĭo.opening: v. a. ; lit., to assemble by centuries; hence, humorously, in Plaut., to collect, bring together, to prepare in gen.: dum concenturio in corde sycophantias, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 159 : epistulae illae mihi concenturiant…

concentus.opening: concino , sounds blending harmoniously together, symphony, harmony, harmonious music (class.). Prop. In gen.: ille sonus...qui acuta cum gravibus temperans varios aequabiliter concentus efficit, Cic. Rep. 6, 18, 18 :…

conceptācŭlum.opening: concipio , that which receives something, a receptacle (post-Aug. and rare). Prop., Plin. 2, 45, 44, § 115 : sanguinis, Gell. 18, 10, 9 ; Front. Aquaed. 22 al. —* Trop. : superbia aliubi conceptaculum, sed hic (sc. in…

conceptĭo.opening: id. . Prop. A comprehending; hence, concr., a circuit, compass : summa omnium naturae rerum (mundus), the system of the universe, Vitr. 9, 4, 2 : tota mundi, id. 6, 1, 6 .— Aquae, a collection, reservoir , Front.…

conceptĭōnālis.opening: adj. conceptio , pertaining to conception : fatum, Fulg. Myth. 2, 8 ; sol, Firm. Math. 7, 1.

conceptīvus.opening: adj. concipio . * That is conceived : fides et dilectio non substantiva animae sed conceptiva, Tert. Res Carn. 40 .— That is ordered, directed; so only feriae, in the Roman ritual, those festivals that were not fixed…

concepto.opening: v. freq. a. id. (late Lat.). To conceive, become pregnant , Arn. 4, p. 141 .— To conceive in mind : majora, Amm. 31, 10, 5 .

conceptum.opening: , v. concipio, I. B. fin. , and II. B. fin.

conceptus.opening: concipio . A collecting, gathering : (Tiberis) novenorum conceptu dierum navigabilis, after the water had been stopped nine days, Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 53 .— Concr., a collection, conflux : conceptus aquarum inertium vasti,…

con-cerno.opening: v. a. , to mix, mingle together (as in a sieve, in order to separate by sifting): carni, Aug. Conf. 5, 10 fin.

con-cerpo.opening: v. a. carpo , to pluck, pull , or tear in pieces, to rend (rare). Prop.: epistulas, Cic. Att. 10, 12, 3 : librum, Liv. 38, 55, 11 ; cf. Gell. 4, 18, 12 ; cf. litteras, Suet. Ner. 47 : folia coronae concerpta, Plin. 21,…

concertātĭo.opening: concerto , a strife of words, a disputation, dispute, controversy (several times in Cic.; elsewhere rare): contentiones concertationesque in disputando pertinaces, Cic. Fin. 1, 8, 27 ; cf.: concertationum plenae…

concertātīvus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to controversy : concertativa accusatio ( = mutua accusatio), a recrimination, countercharge , Gr. ἀντικατηγορία , Auct. ap. Quint. 7, 2, 9 .

concertātor.opening: concerto , one who contends or vies with another, a rival : concertator Corbulonis: scientiā militiae (corresp. with aemulus), Tac. A. 14, 29 .

concertātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to controversy or disputation, controversial : genus (dicendi), Cic. Brut. 83, 287 .

con-certo.opening: v. a. , to contend with any one zealously or warmly (rare but class.; cf. aemulor). In gen.: te audio nescio quid concertasse cum ero, Ter. Ad. 2, 2, 3 : pro explorato habebat, Ambiorigem proelio non esse concertaturum,…

concertor.opening: v. dep.; collat. form of concerto, q. v. (late Lat.), Vulg. Sap. 15, 9 ; id. Ecclus. 38, 29 .

concessĭo.opening: concedo, I. B. 3. , an allowing, granting, conceding, permission, leave (rare, but in good prose). In gen.: agrorum, Cic. Agr. 3, 3, 11 ; Tac. A. 3, 73 : praemiorum, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 8, 3 : concessio, ut…

concessīvus.opening: adj. concedo , pertaining to concession, concessive (late Lat.), Serv. ad Verg. A. 10, 33 ; Diom. p. 390 P.

con-cesso.opening: v. a. , to cease, leave off, desist (ante- and post-class., and very rare): lavari aut fricari, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 9 : quid ego hic properans concesso pedibus, linguā largior? id. As. 2, 2, 24 ; Front. Ep. ad M.…

concessus.opening: concedo , a permitting, conceding, concession, permission, leave (in good prose, but used only in abl. sing. ): Caesaris concessu, Caes. B. G. 7, 20 : datur concessu omnium huic aliquis ludus aetati, Cic. Cael. 12, 28 :…

concha.opening: , = κόγχη . A bivālve shell-fish, mussel , Plaut. Rud. 2, 1, 8 ; 2, 1, 15 ; Lucr. 2, 374 ; Verg. G. 2, 348 ; Plin. 9, 33, 52, § 102 : legere, Cic. de Or. 2, 6, 22 ; Suet. Calig. 46 : cavae, Ov. M. 4, 725 : marinae, id.…

conchātus.opening: adj. concha , shellformed : cauda, Plin. 10, 20, 22, § 43 : parietum spatium, id. 11, 51, 112, § 270 .

conchĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to a shell-fish : baca, a pearl, Verg. Cul. 67 dub. (prob. a gloss; v. Sillig N. cr. ).

conchī^cla.opening: dim. contr. from conchicula, from conchis , the boiled bean , Apic. 5, 4 ; cf. Petr. 66, 7 .—Hence, , , adj., prepared with beans : pullus, Apic. 5, 4 .

conchis.opening: , = κόγχος , a kind of bean boiled with the pods , Mart. 13, 7 ; Juv. 3, 293 ; 14, 131 ; cf. Apic. 5, 4 .

conchīta.opening: , = κογχίτης [κόγχη] , a catcher of shell-fish , Plaut. Rud. 2, 2, 5 .

conchŭla.opening: dim. concha , a small shell-fish (very rare), Cels. 2, 29 ; Val. Max. 8, 8, 1 al.

conchȳlĭārĭus.opening: conchylium , a purple dyer , Inscr. Donat. 315, 8 .

conchȳlĭātus.opening: adj. id. . Of a purple color : peristromata, Cic. Phil. 2, 27, 67 : vestis, Plin. 9, 39, 64, § 138 ; Suet. Caes. 43 : lana, Petr. 54, 4 ; Marc. Emp. 9 .— Clothed in purple : relictis conchyliatis cum illo seminudo…

conchȳlĭ-lĕgŭlus.opening: id. , a collector of shell-fish , Cod. Th. 11, 7, 15; 13, 1, 9.

conchȳlĭum.opening: , = κογχύλιον . A shell-fish, a testaceous animal , in gen., Plin. 9, 29, 46, § 86 ; Cic. Div. 2, 14, 33 .— Specif. An oyster , Cic. Pis. 27, 67 ; Hor. Epod. 2, 49 ; id. S. 2, 2, 74 ; 2, 4, 30 ; 2, 8, 27 ; Cels. 2, 18…

con-cĭdo.opening: v. n. cado , to fall together, to fall down, to tumble to the ground (class. in prose and poetry). In gen., of buildings: conclave illud concidit, Cic. de Or. 2, 86, 353 : navis veluti terrestre machinamentum, Tac. A.…

con-cīdo.opening: v. a. caedo , to cut up, cut through, cut away, cut to pieces, to bring to ruin, destroy , etc. (class. in prose and poetry). Prop. In gen.: nervos, Cic. Fl. 30, 73 : corpus in partes, Petr. 141, 2 : vitulum Ajax, id.…

concĭens.opening: adj. cf. inciens , pregnant, full : terra aquarum, App. de Mundo, 23, p. 67.

con-cĭĕo.opening: (from the access. form , īre: concit, Lucr. 6, 410 : concibant, Tac. H. 5, 19 : conciret, id. A. 11, 19 : concirent, id. ib. 3, 38 fin. : concire, id. ib. 3, 40 ; 12, 15: conciri, Liv. 25, 27, 9 : concīta, Lucr. 2, 267…

concĭlĭābŭlum.opening: concilium , a place of assembly, a public place , esp. for public intercourse or traffic; a marketplace, an exchange, a place for courts , etc.: conciliabulum dicitur locus, ubi in conciliam convenitur, Paul. ex Fest.…

concĭlĭātĭo.opening: concilio (in Cic. and Quint.). A connection, union . Prop.: totius generis hominum, Cic. Off. 1, 41, 149 ; so, quasi civili conciliatione et societate conjunctos (deos), id. N. D. 2, 31, 78 .— Trop. A uniting in…

concĭlĭātor.opening: id. . He who provides, prepares , or causes a thing; an author, founder, promoter , etc. (in good prose, but not in Cic.; cf. however: conciliatrix and conciliatricula): suillae carnis, who prepares it savorily, makes…

concĭlĭātrīcŭla.opening: dim. conciliatrix , that which concitiates, unites : nobilitate ipsā, blandā conciliatriculā, commendatus, Cic. Sest. 9, 21 ; Ambros. in. Psa. 15, 48.

concĭlĭātrix.opening: conciliator . In gen., that which occasions, produces, procures : (omitto) orationis vim, quae conciliatrix est humanae maxime societatis, Cic. Leg. 1, 9, 27 : conciliatrix amicitiae virtutis opinio, id. Lael. 11, 37 .—…

concĭlĭātūra.opening: concilio , the trade of procurer, pimping, pandering : exercere, Sen. Ep. 97, 9 .

concĭlĭātus.opening: concilio , a union of atoms, a connection of bodies (only in abl. sing. , and in Lucr.): condenso conciliatu artari, Lucr. 1, 576 ; so id. 2, 100 : parvo (i. e. parvā mole), id. 2, 133 : principiūm, id. 2, 936 .

con-cĭlĭcĭātus.opening: adj. Cilicium , clothed in a garment of hair (of a penitent), Tert. Pud. 13 .

concĭlĭo.opening: v. a. concilium . To bring together several objects into one whole, to unite, connect (class. in prose and poetry, not in Hor.). Prop. (thus several times in Lucr. of the union of atoms): primordia Non ex illarum…

concĭlĭum.opening: con- and root cal- of calo; Gr. καλέω; cf. clamo , a collection of people, an association, gathering, union, meeting, assembly , = coetus (class.). In gen.: videre ambas in uno concilio, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 96 ; id. Clst.…

concĭnentĭa.opening: concino (postclass. for concentus), musical harmony, concord , Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 2 fin. ; 2, 3 .— Trop. , in archit., symmetry : architectonica, Sid. Ep. 8, 4 ; Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 21 .

con-cĭnĕrātus.opening: adj. cinis , sprinkled with ashes , Tert. Pud. 13 .

con-cingo.opening: v. a. , to gird, surround completely , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

concinnātĭcĭus.opening: or , , adj. concinno , skilfully prepared : mensula, App. M. 2, p. 119 .

concinnātĭo.opening: id. (post-class.). In economics, an adjusting, preparing : aquae marinae, Auct. Lemmat. ap. Cato, R. R. 106 .— Transf. , a making, composing : epistulae, Aus. Ep. 17 ; cf. id. ib. 7 and 15: metrorum, Mar. Vict. p. 2547…

concinnātor.opening: id. (post-Aug.). An arranger, disposer : capitum et capillorum, a hair-dresser, Col. 1, prooem. § 5 . — A maker, contriver, author, inventor : causarum, an advocate, Dig. 1, 16, 9 : concinnatores atque inventores…

concinnĭtas.opening: concinnus , a neat, elegant , or skilful joining of several things (in good prose, but rare). In gen.: concinnitates colorum, Gell. 2, 26, 4 : non est ornamentum virile concinnitas, a too carefully arranged dress, Sen.…

concinnĭtūdo.opening: concinnus , = concinnitas, II., beauty of style , Cic. Inv. 1, 18, 25 .

concinno.opening: v. a. id. , to join fitly together, to order, arrange appropriately, to set right, adjust : concinnare est apte componere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 38, 1 Müll. (cf. compono, II. B.; mostly anteclass. and post-Aug.; most. freq.…

con-cinnus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; acc. to Non. p. 43, 21, and p. 59, 30, from cinnus , fitly, skilfully put together or joined, well adjusted, beautiful (class.; esp. freq. in Cic. of discourse). Object. Prop.: sat edepol concinna est…

con-cĭno.opening: , no sup. , , v. n. and a. [cano]. Neutr., to sing, play , or sound together, in concert or harmoniously (class.). Prop.: ubi (chorus) certis numeris ac pedibus velut facta conspiratione consensit atque concinuit, Col.…

concĭo.opening: , and its derivv., , , etc., v. under contio, contionabundus, contionalis, etc.

concĭpĭlo.opening: v. a. concipio , to seize, take, catch (only in the foll. exs.): concipilavisti dictum a Naevio pro corripuisti et involasti, Paul. ex Fest. p. 62, 6 : quem ego offatim jam jam concipilabo, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 61 .

con-cĭpĭo.opening: v. a. capio , to take or lay hold of, to take to one's self, to take in, take, receive , etc. (class. in prose and poetry). Prop. In gen.: nuces si fregeris, vix sesquimodio concipere possis, Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 3 :…

concīsē.opening: adv. , v. 2. concido, P. a. fin .

concīsĭo.opening: 2. concido , prop., a cutting; hence, Lit. , a cutting to pieces, destruction , Vulg. Joel, 3, 14 .— Transf. A mutilation , Vulg. Phil. 3, 2 .— In rhet., a separating of a sentence into short divisions or clauses , Cic.…

concīsor.opening: id. , one who cuts down or fells : nemorum, Coripp. 4, 22.

concīsōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , suitable for cutting : ferramentum, Veg. Art. Vet. 1, 56, 31 .

concīsūra.opening: id. . * A dividing, distributing : aquaram, Sen. Ep. 100, 6 .—* A hollow, chink, cleft , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 63 .

concĭtātē.opening: adv. , v. concito, P. a. fin .

concĭtātĭo.opening: concito , lit., a hastening, quick movement : remorum, Liv. 44, 28, 10 .— Trop. In gen., an exciting or rousing up; esp., of the passions, an emotion of mind, affection, passion (in good prose; most freq. in Cic. and…

concĭtātor.opening: id. , one who excites or rouses, a mover, exciter (rare): belli, Hirt. B. G. 8, 38 ; Tac. H. 3, 2 : turbae ac tumultūs, Liv. 25, 4, 10 : concitator et instimulator seditionis, Cic. Dom. 5, 11 : tabernariorum, id. ib. §…

concĭtātrix.opening: concitator , that which excites or stirs up (very rare): Veneris (eruca), Plin. 19, 8, 44, § 154 ; and adj. : concitatricem vim habet satyrion, id. 26, 10, 62, § 96 .

concĭto.opening: v. freq. a. concieo , to move violently, to put in violent or quick motion, to stir up, rouse up, excite, incite, shake . Prop. (thus most freq. in the poets and histt.): artus, Lucr. 3, 292 ; 3, 301 : equum calcaribus,…

concĭtor.opening: concieo , he who rouses or excites, an exciter (rare; not in Cic.; in MSS. freq. interchanged with concitator): belli, Liv. 23, 41, 1 ; 29, 3, 3 ; 37, 45, 17 ; Tac. A. 4, 28 ; id. H. 1, 68 ; 4, 56 ; Just. 2, 9, 21 :…

concĭtus.opening: , üs, concieo , = concitatio, an inciting, spurring on; impetuosity, haste : equi, Claud. Mam. Genethl. Maxim. 8 .

con-cīvis.opening: a fellow-citizen , transl. of συμπολίτης (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 17 ; id. Res Carn. 41 .

conclāmans.opening: P. and P. a. of conclamo.

conclāmātĭo.opening: conclamo , a loud shouting or calling of many persons together, a shout (rare; not in Cic.): universi exercitūs, Caes. B. C. 2, 26 : tot milium sub gladio gementium, Sen. Clem. 1, 12, 2 ; in plur. , Tac. A. 3, 2 ; id.…

conclāmātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from conclamo.

conclāmĭto.opening: v. freq. [conclamo], to call, cry out loudly : totā urbe, Plaut. Merc. 1, 1, 51 .

con-clāmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
con-clāmo.opening: v. n. and a. , to cry or call out together . (Con subject.) To call or cry out together or in a body (hence often joined with omnes, universi, pariter, omnes pariter, Liv. 34, 61, 8 ; Curt. 5, 13, 5 ; 8, 11, 22 ; 10,…

conclāvātae.grammar: dicebantur, quae sub eādem erant clave

conclāve.opening: ( gen. plur. heterocl. conclaviorum, Vitr. 6, 3, 8 : conclavium, id. 7, 9 ), clavis: conclavia dicuntur loca, quae unā clave clauduntur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 39, 9 Müll.; cf. Don. ad Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 35 , a room, chamber,…

conclāvo.opening: to nail together , συνηλῶ , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

con-clērĭcus.opening: a fellow-clergyman , Jul. Epit. Nov. c. 115, § 475.

con-clūdo.opening: ( part. perf. solecist. conclausa semina, Col. 3, 12, 2 ), v. a. , to shut up closely, to close up, enclose, confine . Prop. (class. in prose and poetry), constr. with in and acc. , with adv. and absol . (not with in…

conclūsĭo.opening: concludo . A shutting up, closing (rare, not in Cic.). Abstr.: palpebrarum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 3 and 10.— In milit. lang., a hostile shutting in, a siege, blockade : diutina, Caes. B. C. 2, 22 ; so Nep. Eum. 5, 7 .—In…

conclūsĭuncŭla.opening: dim. conclusio, II. D. , a trifling or captious conclusion, a sophism : fallaces ( = σοφίσματα ), Cic. Ac. 2, 24, 75 : contortulae quaedam et minutulae conclusiunculae, id. Tusc. 2, 18, 42 .

conclūsīvē.opening: adv. concludo, II. D. , in form of a conclusion, conclusively , Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 1 med.

conclūsūra.opening: concludo , a joining, connection : fornicationis, Vitr. 6, 8, 3 .

conclūsus.opening: concludo , a shutting up : corporis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 77 .

con-cŏlōna.opening: colonus , she who inhabits the same town or house with one, a female fellow-citizen or fellow-inhabitant , Aug. Ep. 169 .

con-cŏlor.opening: adj. gen. omn. (postclass. access. form of the fem. concolora, Carystos, Mart. Cap. 6, § 659 fin. ; cf. id. 1, § 80 ), of the same color ( poet. and in postAug. prose; most freq. in Ov.; perh. first used by him). With…

con-cŏlōrans.opening: adj. color , of the same color , Tert. Pud. 8 .

con-cŏmĭtor.opening: v. dep. , to attend, accompany (late Lat., except in part. perf. , v. infra ): concomitando tuos, Ven. Carm. 8, 7, 183: Astris Caesario concomitante suo, id. ib. 8, 6, 157 .— Part. perf. in pass. sense: * , ,…

con-cōpŭlo.opening: v. a. , to join, unite : argentum auro, Lucr. 6, 1077 (al.: auro aurum).

con-cŏquo.opening: v. a. To boil or seethe together (very rare): sal et nitrum sulphuri concoctum in lapidem vertitur, Plin. 31, 10, 46, § 122 : odores, Lucr. 2, 853 : (spondyli) perturbati concoctique, Sen. Ep. 95, 28 : remedia, Macr. S.…

concordābĭlis.opening: adj. concordo , easily according, harmonizing , Censor. de Die Nat. 10, 4 .

concordātĭo.opening: id. , = concordia, concord, unanimity (late Lat.), Vulg. Ecclus. 22, 27 ; 27, 23 .

concordē.opening: adv. from an obsol. concordus = concors , concordantly, in harmony , Inscr. Orell. 4517 .

concordĭa.opening: concors , an agreeing together, union, harmony, concord (opp. discordia, Sall. J. 10, 6 ; Sen. Ep. 94, 46 ; opp. bellum, Lucr. 1, 457 ; opp. repugnantia, Plin. 29, 4, 17, § 61 ; freq. and class. in prose and poetry). Of…

Concordĭa.opening: nom. propr. The goddess of Concord , Gr. Ὁμόνοια , to whom several temples were dedicated at Rome, usually after civil strife; the oldest was founded by Camillus , A. U. C. 386, and renewed by Tiberius and Livia , A. U.…

concordĭālis.opening: adj. concordia , of or pertaining to concord or union (late Lat.): vincla, Firm. Math. 6, 32.

Concordĭālis.opening: a priest of Concordia , Inscr. Orell. 1165 ; 2384 .

concordĭtas.opening: concors , = concordia, concord , Pac. ap. Non. 88, 20 (Trag. Rel. v. 188 Rib.).

concordo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
concordo.opening: v. n. and a. [concors]. Neutr., to agree together, to be united, be of one mind, to harmonize (rare but class.). Of persons: concordare cum aliquo, * Ter. Phorm. 2, 3, 86 .— Absol. : ne tunc quidem fratres concordare…

con-corpŏrālis.opening: adj., of or belonging to the same body or company (late Lat.): gentes, Vulg. Eph. 3, 6 .— Subst. : , , a comrade , Amm. 21, 12, 15 ; 28, 5, 7 .

concorpŏrātĭo.opening: concorporo , a union, harmony (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 4 ; id. Baptism. 8 .

concorpŏrĭfĭcātus.opening: adj. concorporo-facio , united in one body, incorporated , Tert. adv. Val. 23 .

con-corpŏro.opening: v. a. , to unite in one body, to incorporate (except in Pliny the elder, only in late Lat.): aliquid cum melle, Plin. 22, 24, 53, § 113 : vitiligines, id. 27, 12, 90, § 112 : scopuli concorporati, Amm. 22, 8, 15 :…

con-cors.opening: (ante-class. , , Caecil. Stat. ap. Prisc. p. 726 P.; cf. Prisc. p. 764 ib.), cordis ( abl. usu. concordi, Cic. Univ. 5 med. ; Prop. 4 (5), 5, 6 ; Ov. M. 1, 25 ; 5, 664 ; Sil. 16, 381 ; Suet. Caes. 19 ; Sen. Agam. 781…

con-crasso.opening: v. a. , to thicken, make thick : liquida, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 62 .

con-crĕātus.opening: adj., created together (eccl. Lat.): diabolus sanctis angelis, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 3, 7 ; cf. Vulg. Eccl. 1, 16 .

con-crē^bresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become frequent, increase, gather strength : cum levis alterno Zephyrus concrebruit Euro, Verg. Cir. 24 .

con-crēdo.opening: v. a. (anteclass. form, pres. , Plaut. Aul. 3, 6, 49 ; hence perf. concredui, id. Cas. 2, 8, 43 ; cf. credo), to intrust, consign, commit to , = commendo (class.; very freq. in Plaut.; in Cic. perh. only twice; never in…

concrĕmātĭo.opening: concremo , a burning up, conflagration , Fulg. Myth. 1, 15 .

concrēmentum.opening: concresco , a mixture , App. Mag. p. 306, 6 .

con-crĕmo.opening: v. a. , to burn up, consume (perh. not before the Aug. per.): vivos igni, Liv. 3, 53, 5 ; cf. id. 9, 12, 8 : hostilia arma subdito igne, id. 8, 30, 8 : urbem igni, id. 6, 33, 4 : omnia tecta, id. 5, 42, 2 : domos, id.…

concrĕpātĭo.opening: concrepo , a noise, rattling : scabillorum, Arn. 2, 73 .

concrĕpĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to rattle or sound much or loudly : virgarum concrepitat fragor, Prud. στεφ . 11, 56.

con-crĕpo.grammar: pŭi, pĭtum, 1 v. n. and a.
con-crĕpo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr., to rattle, creak, grate, sound, resound, clash, make a noise , etc. (class.): foris concrepuit hinc a vicino sene, Plaut. Mil. 2, 1, 76 : foris, id. Bacch. 2, 2, 56 ; 4, 2, 28 : ostium, id. Men. 2,…

con-cresco.opening: ( inf. perf. sync. concresse, Ov. M. 7, 416 ), v. n. , to grow together; hence with the prevailing idea of uniting, and generally of soft or liquid substances which thicken; to harden, condense, curdle, stiffen, congeal…

concrētĭo.opening: concresco . Abstr., compacting, uniting, condensing, congealing (opp. liquor), Cic. Univ. 14 init. : individuorum corporum concretio, id. N. D. 1, 25, 71 : prava corporis, Firm. Math. 1, 3: substantiarum, Tert. Anim. 52…

concrētus.opening: concresco , condensation : albicantis suci, Plin. 12, 16, 35, § 70 .—Also Verg. G. 2, 318 Voss, Wunderl. ad loc.; but cf. concresco, P. a. fin.

con-crīmĭnor.opening: v. dep. n. , to make bitter accusations, to complain : advorsum aliquem, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 87 .

con-crispo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. (very rare, and only in part. pres. and perf. ). To curl, to give a curling, undulatory motion to : concrispati cincinni, Vitr. 4, 1, 7 : umores (se) concrispantes, id. 8, 1, 1 .—* To brandish , of…

con-crŭcĭfīgo.opening: v. a. , to crucify together : aliquem alicui, Sid. Ep. 6, 1 ; Ambros. Sacram. 6, 2, 8 .

con-crŭcĭo.opening: v. a. , to torment, rack, torture severely , Lucr. 3, 148 .

con-crustātus.opening: adj., entirely covered with a crust, incrusted (late Lat.), Amm. 17, 7, 11 ; 30, 6, 5 .

concŭbātĭo.opening: concubo , a lying or reclining upon : dura lecti, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 193 .

concŭbīnālis.opening: adj [concubinus], lascivious : illecebrae, Sid. Ep. 9, 6 fin.

concŭbīnātus.opening: id. . Union of a man with an unmarried woman (usu. of a lower social grade than himself), concubinage (opp. matrimonium on the one hand, and adulterium or stuprum on the other; not in Cic.): emere aliquam in…

concŭbīnus.opening: , and , , concubo , one who lives in concubinage (cf. concubinatus), a concubine (male or female), a less reproachful designation than paelex (cf. Dig. 5, 16, 144 ). Masc. (not in Cic.), Cat. 61, 130 sq. ; * Quint. 1,…

concŭbĭtālis.opening: adj. concubitus , pertaining to coition , Tert. ad Nat. 2, 11 .

concŭbĭtor.opening: id. , a bed-fellow ( = concubinus; concubitor, συγκοιμητής , Gloss.; eccl. Lat.), Salv. 7, p. 251 ; Vulg. 1 . Cor. 6, 10.

concŭbĭtus.opening: id. . A lying together; in gen. (very rare), for sleeping. Varr. L. L. 7, § 78 Müll.; at dinner, reclining, Prop. 4 (5), 8, 36. (cf. concubo, I.): dentium, a firm, close shutting together of the teeth, Cael. Aur. Acut.…

concŭbĭus.opening: adj. concubo , of or belonging to lying in sleep , or to the time of sleep. As adj. only in the connection concubiā nocte (rarely: nocte concubiā, nocte in concubiā, noctu concubiā; v. the foll. ), at the time of the…

con-cŭbo.opening: , needlessly assumed by some as present for the perf. tenses of concumbo, q. v.

conculcātĭo.opening: conculco , a treading under foot, stamping upon , Plin. 8, 18, 26, § 68 : fructuum in areā, Dig. 3, 34, 14, § 1 .

conculcātus.opening: conculco, II. B. , prop., a trampling upon; hence trop., an object of contempt : conculcatui esse alicui, Tert. Res Carn. 22 .

con-culco.opening: v. a. calco , to tread under foot, to crush or bruise by treading. * Prop.: vinaceos in dolia picata, Cato, R. R. 25 .—More freq., Trop. (cf. calco, I. B.). To tread down, trample upon in a hostile manner, to abuse :…

con-cumbo.opening: v. n. Lit. , to lie together, lie in numbers (very rare): Evandri profugae concubuere boves, Prop. 4 (5), 1, 4. — To lie with (for sexual intercourse). In tempp. pres. (rare). With dat. : Cinyrae. Ov. M. 10, 338 .—…

con-cŭmŭlātus.opening: Part. [cumulo], heaped up, accumulated : cena in verticem, Tert. Virg. Vel. 7 fin.

concŭpĭo.opening: v. n. , to be very desirous, to long much for; as verb finit. (late Lat.), Commod. 64, 4 .—Hence, . entis, P. a., very desirous, warmly desiring, coveting (only in the foll. exs.); with gen. : regni, Enn. ap. Cic. Div.…

concŭpiscentĭa.opening: concupisco , an eager desire, longing, concupiscence (late Lat.), Tert. Res Carn. 45 , id. Anim. 16 al. ; Hier. Ep. 63, 1 ; Paul. Nol. Ep. 30, 3 .

concŭpiscentĭālis.opening: adj. concupiscentia , full of desire (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 1, 25 fin. —Hence, adv. : , lustfully , Aug. Peccat. Mer. 2, 9 ; 2, 28 .

concŭpiscentīvus.opening: adj. concupisco , passionately desiring , transl. of ἐπιθυμητικός , Tert. Anim. 16 .

concŭpiscĭbĭlis.opening: adj., worthy to be longed for, very desirable (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Quaest. in Paral. 1, 1 .

concŭpiscĭtīvus.opening: adj. , = concupiscentivus, passionately desiring , Hier. in Ezech. 1, 1, 7 .

con-cŭpisco.opening: v. inch. a. [cupio], to long much for a thing, to be very desirous of, to covet, to aspire to, strive after (class. in prose and poetry). With acc. : quid concupiscas tu videris: quod concupiveris certe habebis, Ant.…

concŭpītor.opening: concupisco , one who longs eagerly for or covets something (late Lat.), Firm. Math. 8, 22 fin.

con-cūrĭālis.opening: one of the same curia , Inscr. Fea Fast. Cons. p. 23, n. 46.

con-cūro.opening: v. a. , to care for suitably, attend to , Plaut. Bacch. 1, 2, 23 .

con-curro.opening: ( perf. redupl. concucurrit, Flor. 4, 2, 33 Duker N. cr. : concucurrisse, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 901 P., and Suet. Caes. 15 ; cf. Liv. 1, 12 Oud., and Ind. Flor. s. h. v. Duker), v. n. To run together (of several persons),…

concursātĭo.opening: concurso . A running together, a disorderly meeting : cum multā concursatione (populi), Cic. Brut. 69, 242 ; Tac. A. 6, 17 .— Trop. : inventus est ordo in stellis ... cedo tandem qui sit ordo aut quae concursatio…

concursātor.opening: id. , one who runs hither and thither; in milit. lang., a skirmisher (opp. statarius; rare, perh. only in Livy): concursator et vagus pedes, Liv. 31, 35, 6 : levis et concursator hostis, id. 27, 18, 14 .

concursātōrĭus.opening: adj. concursator , of or pertaining to skirmishing : pugna, a skirmish, Amm. 16, 9, 1 .

concursĭo.opening: concurro, II. , a running or meeting together, a concurrence, concourse (several times in Cic.; elsewhere rare). In gen.: atomorum, Cic. Ac. 1, 2, 6 : ut (corpora) concursionibus inter se cohaerescant, id. Fin. 1, 6, 17…

con-curso.opening: v. freq. n. and a. To come violently together, to rush together, clash : concursare, coire et dissultare vicissim (semina), Lucr. 3, 396 .—Far more freq. and class., To go to and fro, run about, rush hither and thither,…

concursus.opening: concurro . A running or flocking together, a concourse, assembly : fit concursus per vias, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 27 ; cf. in plur. : incredibilem in modum concursus fiunt ex agris, Cic. Att. 5, 16, 3 : magni domum concursus…

con-curvo.opening: v. a. , to curve, bend , Laber. ap. Macr. S. 2, 7 (Com. Rel. v. 118 Rib.).

concussĭbĭlis.opening: adj. concutio , that can be shaken , Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 25 .

concussĭo.opening: id. (post-Aug.), a shaking, concussion. In gen.: vasorum, Col. 9, 14 fin. : assidua facium, Plin. Ep. 4, 9, 11 : vasta concussio quae duas suppressit urbes, an earthquake, Sen. Q. N. 6, 25, 4 .— In jurid. Lat., an…

concussor.opening: id. , one who extorts money by threats (late Lat.), Tert. Fuga in Persec. 12 sq.

concussūra.opening: id. , = concussio, II., the extorting of money by threats (late Lat.), Tert. ad Scap. 13 .

concussus.opening: concutio , a shaking, concussion; only in abl. sing. in Lucr. 6, 290 ; 6, 547 (in Plin. 35, 16, 55, § 193 , the better read. is concussis; v. Sillig ad h. l.).

con-custōdĭo.opening: v. a. , to guard, watch carefully : NATOS, Inscr. Orell. 2486 .

con-cŭtĭo.opening: v. a. quatio, as cur = quāre . To strike one upon another, to strike together (rare): utrum cavae manus concutiantur, an planae, Sen. Q. N. 2, 28, 1: concussā manu dare signa, Ov. M. 11, 465 : frameas, Tac. G. 11 .— To…

condălĭum.opening: (access. form more nearly related to the Greek: CONDULUS anulus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 38, 14 Müll.; cf. condylus) [ κονδύλιον, κόνδυλος ; cf. calix = κύλιξ , etc.], a little ring for slaves , Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 7 ; 4, 3,…

Condāte.opening: a town of Aquitania , now Condat , Aus. Ep. 5, 32 .

con-dător.opening: joint contributor , συντελεστής , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

con-dēcerno.opening: v. a. , to decide, determine together , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 2, 12 med.

con-dĕcet.opening: v. impers. , it becomes or it is becoming, meet, seemly (ante-class.): capies quod te condecet, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 90 : haud Atticam disciplinam, id. Cas. 3, 5, 24 : in se capessere, id. Aul. 4, 1, 4 : magis meretricem…

con-dēclīno.opening: v. a. , to decline in the same manner : casus, Prisc. p. 1065 P.

con-dĕcŏro.opening: v. a. , to ornament, decorate, adorn excessively or carefully (rare): ova parire solet genus pinnis condecoratum, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 5, § 59 Müll. (Ann. v. 10 Vahl.): ludos scenicos, * Ter. Hec. alt. prol. 37: loca…

con-dĕcŭriālis.opening: he who has been a decurion with one , Fragm. Jur. Civ. Antejust. p. 39 Mai.

con-dēlector.opening: v. pass., to be delighted with something (eccl. Lat.): lege Dei, Vulg. Rom. 7, 22 al.

con-dēlĭquesco.opening: v. n. , to melt wholly or completely, to dissolve : resina, Cato, R. R. 23, 3 .

condemnābĭlis.opening: adj. condemno , worthy of condemnation , Pall. Insit. 11 .

condemnātĭo.opening: id. , a condemning, condemnation (post-Aug.): pecuniaria, Dig. 2, 10, 5 : condemnationem facere, to condemn, ib. 42, 1, 59 ; or, to bring about the condemnation of one, Cod. Just. 8, 14, 8 : pati, to be condemned, Dig.…

condemnātor.opening: id. . * One who gives sentence, a condemner : delicti, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 9 .—* One who causes a condemnation, an accuser : Claudiae, Tac. A. 4, 66 ; cf. condemno, II.

con-demno.opening: v. a. damno . To sentence, condemn, convict (in good prose; rare in the poets). In judicial proceedings (opp. absolvo); constr. aliquem , with gen., abl., de aliquā re , later with ad or in aliquid , or with ut. Aliquem…

condensātĭo.opening: condenso , a condensing, condensation , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 18, 187 .

condenso.opening: (access form * , ēre: quia se condenseat aër, Lucr. 1, 392 ; cf. denseo = denso), v. a. condensus , to make very dense, to condense, to press close together (rare; not in Cic.): oves se congregant ac condensant in locum…

con-densus.opening: adj., very dense, close, thick (mostly poet. ; most freq. in Lucr.; not in Cic.): condensa contextaque magis (corpora), Lucr. 4, 57 : condensa atque arta nubila, id. 6, 466 ; cf. id. 6, 102 : conciliatu, id. 1, 575 ; 2,…

con-depso.opening: v. a. , to knead together (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 40, 2 ; so id. ib. 76, 2 ; Pompon. ap. Non. p. 39, 13 (Com. Rel. v. 86 Rib.).

con-dēscendo.opening: , no perf. , 3, v. n. , to stoop, let one's self down, to condescend (eccl. Lat.): alicui, Cassiod. Var. 11, 16 ; id. Amic. 8, 4 : ad alicujus inscitiam, Ambros. Cant. Cantic. 6, 9 .

con-dēscensĭo.opening: condescension (late Lat.): seu demissio Jesu Christi, Cod. Just. 6 , c. de S. Trinit.

condĭcĭo.opening: (in many MSS. and edd. incorrectly , and hence falsely derived from condo; cf. 2. conditio), , condico , an agreement, stipulation, condition, compact, proposition, terms, demand. Prop. Absol. : alicui condicionem…

condĭcĭōnābĭlis.opening: adj. condicio , conditional : persecutio, Tert. adv. Gnost. 9 .

condĭcĭōnālis.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , with a condition attached, conditional, with conditions (freq. in the jurists): datio, Dig. 34, 4, 9 : creditores, ib. 50, 16, 54 : servi, Cod. Just. 10, 1, 7 et saep.: criminatio, Tert. adv. Jud. 13…

con-dīco.opening: v. a. To talk a thing over together, to agree upon, to concert, to promise (most freq. as publicists' t. t.): condixit pater patratus populi Romani Quiritium patri patrato priscorum Latinorum, etc., old form ap. Liv. 1,…

condictīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. condictio , of or pertaining to a demand of restitution : actio, Dig. 12, 1, 24 ; 12, 2, 13, § 2 al.

condictĭo.opening: condico . In the lang. of religion, the proclamation of a festival , acc. to Serv. ad Verg. A. 3, 117 (without voucher); cf.: condictio, in diem certum ejus rei quae agitur denuntiatio, Paul. ex Fest. p. 66 Müll.— In…

con-dignus.opening: adj., wholly deserving, very worthy (very rare; mostly anteand post-class.). Absol. : condignum donum, quali'st qui donum dedit, Plaut. Am. 1, 3, 39 sq. — With abl. : dum condignam te sectaris simiam, Plaut. Mil. 2, 6,…

condīmentārĭus.opening: adj. condimentum , of or pertaining to spices or seasoning : caepae, Plin. 19, 6, 32, § 105 : genus, id. 19, 8, 50, § 165 .— Subst. : , , , one who prepares or sells spices; trop.: omnium haereticorum (Platonem), Tert.…

condīmentum.opening: condio (rare; most freq. in Plaut. and Cic.), spice, seasoning, Plaut. Cas. 2, 3, 3 sq. ; id. Ps. 3, 2, 31 sq. : cibi, Cic. Fin. 2, 28, 90 : arida, Col. 12, 51, 2 : viridia, green herbs used in seasoning, id. 12, 8, 1…

condĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
condĭo.opening: v. a. an access. form from condo, q. v. II., and cf. compono, II. B. 2. (orig. belonging to econ. lang.). To put fruit in vinegar, wine, spices, etc., to preserve, pickle : oleas albas, Cato, R. R. 117 : lactucam…

condiscĭpŭla.opening: condiscipulus , a female school-fellow , Mart. 10, 35, 15 ; App. M. 9, p. 224 al.

condiscĭpŭlātus.opening: id. , companionship in school (very rare), Nep. Att. 5, 3 ; and Just. 12, 6, 17 fin. ; Inscr. Orell. 7392 .

con-discĭpŭlus.opening: a school-mate, companion at school , Cic. Tusc. 1, 18, 41 ; id. Att. 5, 19, 3 ; Nep. Att. 1, 3 ; Sen. Ep. 66 ; Quint. 1, 2, 26 ; 2, 2, 12 ; Suet. Ner. 22 ; id. Vit. 14 ; Plin. Ep. 1, 19, 1 .

con-disco.opening: v. a. * To learn with or in company with one : ex his, qui mihi Athenis condidicere, App. Flor. 3 , n. 18, p. 362, 8.— To learn carefully, eagerly , or well, to learn thoroughly (rare but class. in prose and poetry).…

condītānĕus.opening: adj. condio , of fruits, etc., suitable for pickling or preserving, pickled : olea, Varr. R. R. 1, 24, 1 (quoted in Non. p. 94, 9 sq. ): ostreae, Apic. 9, 6 : pisces, id. 9 fin.

condĭtĭcĭus.opening: or , , adj. condo , laid up, preserved : cibaria, Col. 8, 8, 2 (Schneid. conditiva).

condĭtĭo.opening: condo , a making, creating; and, meton., a thing made, a work (eccl. Lat.), Prud. Ham. 19 ; Tert. Habit. Mul. 8 ; id. Spect. 2 al.

condītĭo.opening: condio . A preserving of fruits , etc.: amurcae, Varr. R. R. 1, 61 .—In plur. , Varr. R. R. 1, 61 (for Cic. Div. 1, 51, 116 , v. condicio, II. B.).— A spicing, seasoning, flavoring : suci, Varr. L. L. 5, § 109 : vini,…

condĭtīvus.opening: adj. condo , suitable for laying up or preserving, laid up, preserved (rare; not in Cic.): olea, Cato, R. R. 6, 1 ; Macr. S. 2, 16 : mala, Cato, R. R. 7, 3 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 59, 1 : cibi, Col. 7, 9, 9 ; cf. also…

condĭtor.opening: id. , a maker, builder, framer, establisher, founder, author, compiler , etc. Prop. (class.; most freq. in the poets and prose writers after the Aug. per.). With gen. : Romanae arcis, Verg. A. 8, 313 : oppidum magnum,…

condītor.opening: condio , one who prepares a thing in a savory manner, a seasoner (very rare): ciconiarum, Poët. ap. Schol. Hor. S. 2, 2, 49 .

condĭtōrĭum.opening: condo , a place where any thing is laid up, a repository (post-Aug.). In gen.: tormentorum muralium, Amm. 18, 9, 1 .— Specif. A place for preserving a dead body or the ashes of the dead, a coffin , Suet. Aug. 18 ; id.…

condī^trix.opening: 1. conditor . She who lays to rest (late Lat.): luna mortalium corporum et auctor et conditrix, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 11.— A female builder, founder , etc. (post-class.): Romae, Poët. ap. Philarg. Verg. E. 1, 20 ; Tert.…

condĭtūra.opening: condo , a preparing, making : vitreorum (vasorum), Petr. 51, 5 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 16, 16, 6 .

condītūra.opening: condio . A preserving of fruits , Col. 12, 48, 1 ; 12, 49, 3 : olivarum, id. 12, 11, 2 .— A seasoning , Sen. Ira, 3, 15, 1 ; Col. 12, 19, 1 .— In concr., a condiment, spice , Dig. 33, 6, 9 pr.

condĭtus.opening: condo , a preparing, founding, establishment (post-class.): Thebarum, Censor. de Die Nat. 4 fin. ; so App. Mag. 24, p. 289 .— A concealing, hiding : consilia altiore conditu texit, Aus. Prof. 15, 17 .

condītus.opening: condio , a preserving of fruits , Col. 2, 22, 4 .

con-do.opening: v. a. con- = cum, and 2. do , lit., to bring, lay or put together (very freq. in all periods and species of composition). With the access. idea of uniting, to put or join together into a whole, to form, fashion,…

condŏcĕ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. condoceo , to train, teach, instruct, discipline (rare): beluas, Cic. N. D. 2, 64, 161 ; cf. elephantos, Auct. B. Afr. 27: tirones gladiatores, id. 71 : animum, ut, etc., Cic. Tusc. 5, 31, 87 .

con-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. , to exercise, train, instruct (very rare; perh. only in the foll. exs.): (milites) equo uti frenato, Auct. B. Afr. 19 dub. (al. condocefecerat or constituerat): Mi. Fac modo, ut condocta tibi sint dicta ad hanc…

con-doctor.opening: a fellow-teacher (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Conf. 1, 9 fin.

condoctus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. condoceo.

con-dŏlĕo.opening: v. n. , to feel severe pain, to suffer greatly (eccl. Lat.). Universum corpus, Tert. Poen. 10 .— Trop. : animo, Hier. Ep. 112 , n. 12.— To suffer with another, to feel another's pain; with dat. : qui non condolent…

con-dŏlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [doleo], to feel severe pain, to suffer much, to be in pain or distress, to ache . Prop. (rare, but class. in prose and poetry; most freq. in temp. perf. ): mihi de vento miserae condoluit caput, Plaut.…

con-dŏmo.opening: v. a. , to tame completely, to curb, check; trop., Prud. Cath. 7, 98 .

condōnātĭo.opening: condono , a giving away : bonorum possessionumque, Cic. Verr. 1, 4, 12 .

con-dōno.opening: v. a. Aliquid (aliquem) alicui, to give something to one, to present, deliver up (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.; not in Quint.). In gen. Prop.: pallam, Plaut. Men. 4, 2, 94 : pateram tibi, id. Am. 1, 3, 38 :…

con-dormĭo.opening: v. n. , to fall quite asleep (very rare), * Suet. Aug. 78 ; Curt. 6, 10, 14 (acc. to Madv. ad Cic. Fin. 5, 4, 11 ); Hyg. Fab. 125 ; Capitol. Ver. 4 .

con-dormisco.opening: v. inch. [dormio], to go entirely to sleep, to fall asleep; only in Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 81 ; id. Rud. 2, 7, 13 ; id. Mil. 3, 2, 13 ; in perf. , id. Most. 2, 2, 55 .

Condrūsi.opening: , = Κονδροῦσοι , a people in Gallia Belgica, on the right bank of the Meuse, in the region of Lüttich and Namur , near the modern Condroz , Caes. B. G. 2, 4 ; 4, 6 ; 6, 32 .

condūcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. conduco, II. , advantageous, profitable, expedient (several times in Plaut., elsewhere rare): (consilium) ad eam rem, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 76 : reperiamus aliquid calidi conducibilis consili, id. ib. 2, 2, 71 : istuc…

con-dūco.grammar: xi, ctum, 3 v. a. and n.
con-dūco.opening: v. a. and n. Act., to draw, bring , or lead together, to assemble, collect (class. in prose and poetry). In gen. Of persons (esp. freq. of the collecting, assembling of troops in any place): milites de castellis ad…

conductīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. conduco , of or pertaining to hire, hired, rented (rare): fidicina, Plaut. Ep. 2, 3, 8 ; 5, 2, 41 : alia, id. ib. arg. 2: exercitus, Nep. Iphicr. 2, 4 ; cf. catervae, id. Chabr. 1, 2 : domus, Porcius, poët.…

conductĭo.opening: id. . A bringing together, uniting . In gen. (very rare), Cic. Inv. 1, 40, 74 ; cf. id. ib. § 73.— Hence, Esp., in later medic. writers, a spasm, convulsion , σπασμός : musculorum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 10 : nervorum, id.…

conductor.opening: conduco , one who hires a thing, a lessee, farmer, tenant, a contractor (rare, and mostly absol. ): (histrionum), Plaut. As. prol. 3 : (pecoris), Cato, R. R. 150, 2 : (agri), Caes. B. C. 3, 21 ; Col. 3, 13, 12 ; cf.…

conductrix.opening: conductor , she who hires or rents a thing , Cod. Just. 3, 3, 10 ; 4, 65, 24 ; 5, 12, 18 .

conductus.opening: conduco , a contraction : oculorum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 15, 95 .

con-dulco.opening: v. a. , to sweeten , Vulg. Ecclus. 27, 26 ; 40, 18 .

condū^plĭcātĭo.opening: conduplico , a doubling (very rare); humorously, for embracing , * Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 18 (cf. id. Ps. 5, 1, 16 ).—As a figure of speech, a repetition of the same word , = ἐπαναδίπλωσις , Auct. Her. 4, 28, 38 .

con-dū^plĭco.opening: v. a. , to double (ante-class.): cibum, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 15 : divitias, Lucr. 3, 71 : primordia rerum, id. 1, 712 : quod boni promeritus fueris, conduplicaverit, * Ter. Phorm. 3, 2, 31 : tenebrae conduplicantur, Pac.…

condurdum.opening: a plant : Saponaria vaccaria, Linn.; Plin. 26, 5, 14, § 26 .

con-dūro.opening: v. a. , to harden, to make very hard : ferrum, Lucr. 6, 969 .

condus.opening: condo , one who lays up (provisions), opp. promus, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 14 .

condўlōma.opening: , = κονδύλωμα , a swelling in the parts about the anus , Cels. 6, 18, 8 ; 7, 30, 2 ; Scrib. Comp. 224 and 225 al.; Plin. 21, 20, 83, § 143 al.

condўlus.opening: († , Paul. ex Fest. p. 38, 14 Müll.), , , = κόνδυλος . * The knob or knuckle of a joint; esp. plur., the fist : complicatis in condylos digitis, Mart. Cap. 1, § 88 .—* ( A joint of a reed; hence meton.) A reed , Mart.…

cōnecto.opening: (less correctly, , v. Ritschl, Opusc. II. 448 sq.; Gell. 2, 17, 8 ), , v. a. necto , to tie, bind, fasten , or join together, to connect, entwine, link together (class.; most freq. in part. pass. and the trop. signif.);…

cōnexĭo.opening: ( ), , conecto , t. t. A binding together, close union , etc.: scutorum, armorum (in a testudo), Isid. Orig. 18, 12, 6 ; Serv. ad Verg. A. 9, 517 . — Esp. An organic union; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 35, 13 Müll.: animae et…

cōnexīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , serving to unite, copulative : conjunctio (atque), Gell. 10, 29, 1 .

cōnexus.opening: ( ), , conecto , a joining together, combination, connection (several times in Lucr., elsewh. rare), Lucr. 3, 556 ; Vitr. 10, 1, 5 .—In plur. , Lucr. 1, 634 ; 2, 726 ; 2, 1020 ; 5, 443.

con-fā^brĭcor.opening: v. dep. , to compose, make : originem vocabuli, Gell. 3, 19, 3 .

confābŭlātĭo.opening: confabulor , a conversation, a discoursing together (eccl. Lat.), Symm. Ep. 9, 84 ; Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 3 al.

confābŭlātor.opening: id. , one who converses (late Lat.): Dei, with God, Ambros. in Cant. Cantic. 4, 39 ; Hier. in Ep. 2 , ad Gal. 4, 8.

con-fābŭlātus.opening: id. , a conversation (cf. confabulatio), Sid. Ep. 9, 11 fin.

con-fābŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. and a., to converse together, to discuss something with one (ante-class. and colloq. for colloquor): cum aliquā, Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 76 ; cf. absol. , id. ib. 3, 3, 10 ; so, ad aliquam accedere Confabulatum,…

con-făcĭo.opening: to make together : confecerunt = unā fecerunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 59, 2 Müll.

confarrĕātĭo.opening: confarreo , an ancient solemn manner of marrying among the Romans , in which was an offering of bread [far] in the presence of the Pontifex Maximus, or Flamen Dialis, and ten witnesses (opp. diffarreatio), Gai. Inst. 1,…

con-farrĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. farreus , to connect in marriage (by making an offering of bread; cf. confarreatio; very rare): confarreandi adsuetudo, Tac. A. 4, 16 : dum confarreatur, Serv. ad Verg. A. 4, 374 : confarreatis…

con-fātālis.opening: adj., jointly dependent on fate, decided by fate; the Gr. συνειμαρμένος : copulata res est et confatalis, Cic. Fat. 13, 30 .

confectĭo.opening: conficio (several times in Cic.; elsewh. rare). A making, preparing, producing, arranging, composing, completing : hujus libri, Cic. Sen. 1, 2 ; cf. annalium, id. de Or. 2, 12, 52 : materiae, id. Div. 1, 51, 116 dub.…

confector.opening: id. . A maker, preparer, finisher (rare): coriorum, i. e. a tanner , Firm. Math. 3, 9, 7: purpurae, i. e. a dyer, Vop. Aur. 29 : negotiorum, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 44, § 108 : totius belli, id. Fam. 10, 20, 3 : dux et…

confectōrārĭus.opening: or , , confector , he who slaughters, a butcher , Inscr. Orell. 3672 ; 4167 .

confectōrĭum.opening: , = χοιροσφαγεῖον , a place where swine are slaughtered , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

confectrix.opening: confector, II. , that which destroys, a destroyer : vetustas, Lact. 7, 11, 5 (after a passage of Cicero).

confectūra.opening: conficio , a making, preparing (post-Aug. and rare): mellis, Col. 9, 14, 5 : chartae, Plin. 13, 12, 23, § 75 : caerulei, id. 33, 13, 57, § 162 .

con-fercĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. farcio , to stuff or cram together, to press close together (in verb. finit. very rare; in part. perf. and P. a. class.). Verb. finit. : ventus cum confercit, franguntur montes nimborum, Lucr. 6,…

con-fermento.opening: v. a. , to leaven, ferment through and through , Tert. adv. Val. 31 .

confĕro.opening: (conl-), , v. a. To bring, bear , or carry together, to collect, gather (freq. and class.). In gen.: ligna circa casam, Nep. Alcib. 10, 4 : arma, Vell. 2, 114, 4 : cibos ore suo (aves), Quint. 2, 6, 7 : undique collatis…

con-ferrūmĭno.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to cement, to solder together , Plin. 27, 8, 45, § 69 .

confertē.opening: adv. , v. confercio, P. a. fin.

confertim.opening: adv. confertus, A. 2. , in a compact body, closely; in milit. lang., of marches, battles, etc. (very rare): sese recipere, Sall. J. 50, 5 : et pugnant et cedunt, Liv. 31, 43, 3 ; 21, 8, 9 Weissenb. ad loc.

confertus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from confercio, q. v.

conferva.opening: conferveo , a kind of water plant (so called on account of its healing power), Plin. 27, 8, 45, § 69 (in App. Herb. 59 called consolida).

confervē-făcĭo.opening: v. a. id. , to make glowing or melting : aes aurumque, Lucr. 6, 353 (Lachm. conferve facit).

con-fervĕo.opening: v. n. , to seethe, boil together (very rare). In gen., Pall. 1, 35, 13 .— In medic. lang., of broken limbs, to heal, grow together , Cels. 8, 10, 1 al.

confervesco.opening: (cf. ferveo, and Prisc. p. 866 P.), 3, v. inch. n. [conferveo], to begin to boil, to become heated, grow hot (perh. not ante-Aug.). In gen. Prop.: aër conclusus versando confervescit, Vitr. 5, 3 ; 2, 6, 4 : granum, si…

confessĭo.opening: confiteor , a confession, acknowledgment . In gen. (in good prose; esp. freq. in Cic. and Quint.), with gen. obj. : errati sui, Cic. Div. 1, 17, 33 : ignorationis, id. Ac. 1, 12, 44 ; cf.: inscitiae suae, Quint. 2, 11,…

confessor.opening: confiteor (only in eccl. Lat.; opp. negator), a confessor of Christianity, a martyr, Lact. Mort. Pers. 35 ; Sid. Ep. 7, 17 al.

confessōrĭus.opening: adj. confessor ; in the jurists, of or pertaining to confession or acknowledgment : actio, Dig. 8, 5, 2 ; 8, 5, 4 ; 9, 2, 23 ; 9, 2, 25 al.

con-festim.opening: adv. kindr. with festinus, festino, from fero , immediately, speedily, without delay, forthwith (class. in prose and poetry): abi ad thensaurum jam confestim clanculum, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 69 : rem administrandam…

con-festīnātĭo.opening: , a false read. for cum festinatione, App. M. 10, p. 233 .

confēta sus.opening: a sow offered in sacrifice with all her young , Paul. ex Fest. p. 57, 21 Müll. (cf. Verg. A. 8, 43 ).

con-fībŭla.opening: a wooden double cramp, clincher : ligneae, Cato, R. R. 12 .

confĭcĭo.opening: ( perf. subj. confexim, Plaut. Truc. 4, 4, 39 ; in pass. , besides the regular form conficior, freq., but not in Cic., in acc. with fīo, fieri: confit, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 7 ; Lucr. 4, 291 ; Col. 2, 15, 1 ; Plin. 6, 23,…

confictĭo.opening: confingo , an inventing, fabricating : criminis, Cic. Rosc. Am. 13, 35 .— Absol. : confictionis argumentatio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11, 81 .

conficto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to counterfeit, feign , Naev. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 107 Müll.

confictor.opening: id. , he who fabricates a thing, a fabricator (late Lat.): falsi, Paul. Nol. 21, 4 .

confictus.opening: Part. , from confingo, and from configo.

con-fĭdēlis.opening: a fellow-believer (eccl. Lat.), Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 9, 3 .

confīdenter.opening: adv. , v. confido, P. a. fin.

confīdentĭa.opening: confidens . A firm trust in a thing, confidence (thus very rare): scapularum. Plaut. As. 3, 2, 3 .—With acc. and inf. : confidentia'st inimicos meos me posse perdere, Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 73 .— Absol. : occidit spes nostra:…

confīdentĭlŏquus.opening: adj. confidens-loquor , speaking confidently or audaciously; in comp. : nihil est confidentiloquius quam urbani adsidui cives, quos scurras vocant, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 164 .

con-fīdo.opening: v. n. , to trust confidently in something, confide in, rely firmly upon, to believe, be assured of (as an enhancing of sperare, Cic. Att. 6, 9, 1 ; Nep. Milt. 1, 1 ; freq. and class. in prose and poetry); constr. with…

con-fīgo.opening: ( part. perf. : confictus sagittis, Scaur. ap. Diom. p. 373 ; Veg. Art. Vet. 2, 11, 4 ; cf. figo init. ), v. a. To join (by pressing), to fasten together (rare): sublaminas inter sese, Cato, R. R. 21, 3 : transtra…

confĭgūrātĭo.opening: configuro , a similar formation, configuration , Tert. Pud. 8 .

con-fĭgūro.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to form from or after something, to fashion accordingly (post-Aug. and rare): vitem ad similitudinem sui, Col. 4, 20, 1 : natura lactis, quae ... ex matris etiam corpore et animo recentem…

confīnālis.opening: adj. confinis , pertaining to boundaries, boundary- : lineae, Auct. Limit. p. 310 Goes.: populi, bordering, Cassiod. Var. 7, 4 .

con-findo.opening: v. a. , to cleave asunder, divide : tellurem ferro, Tib. 4, 1, 173 .

con-fingo.opening: v. a. , to form, fashion, fabricate (class., esp. in a trop. signif.). Prop.: nidos, Plin. 10, 32, 47, § 91 : favos et ceras, id. 11, 5, 4, § 11 : verbum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 7 Müll.; cf. Plin. 37, 12, 74, § 195 .— Trop. ,…

con-fīnis.opening: (access. form , , Auct. Her. 4, 11, 16 B. and K.; Schol. Juv. 14, 151 ; Front. Pol. p. 144 Goes.), e, adj., bordering one upon another, bordering on, adjoining, contiguous (class. in prose and poetry, but not in Cic.).…

confīnĭum.opening: confinis , a confine, common boundary, limit, border (of lands; on the contr., vicinitas, of houses, Dig. 10, 1, 4 ; class. in prose and poetry; most freq. after the Aug. per.; in Cic. perh. only once; not in Quint.).…

confirmātē.opening: adv. , v. confirmo, P. a. fin.

confirmātĭo.opening: confirmo , a securing, establishing, confirming (in good prose, but only in trop. signif.; most freq. in Cic., Caes., and Quint.). * In gen.: perpetuae libertatis, Cic. Fam. 12, 8, 1 .— Esp. A confirming, fortifying,…

confirmātīvus.opening: adj. confirmo , serving for confirmation, confirmative : adverbia (profecto, scilicet, quippe, etc.), Prisc. pp. 1020 and 1056 P: conjunctio, Diom. 411 ib.; Prisc. p. 1032 ib.: verbum, Ambros. Abrah. 2, 11, 89 .— Subst.…

confirmātor.opening: id. , he who confirms or establishes a thing; hence, Pecuniae, a surety, security , Cic. Clu. 26, 72 : venditionis, Jul. Epit. Nov. c. 3, § 10.— Trop. : sententiae, Lact. 1, 2 init. : erroris, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 36 .

confirmātrix.opening: confirmator, II. , she who establishes or confirms a thing (late Lat.), Tert. Cor. Mil. 4 ; Jul. Vict. Art. Rhet. 4, 2 MSS.

con-firmĭtas.opening: firmness of will; in a bad sense, obstinacy , Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 34 Brix. (the verse is rejected by Lorenz).

con-firmo.opening: v. a. , to make firm, establish, strengthen, confirm (class., esp. in prose). In gen. (prop. and trop.): stipites confirmare et stabilire, Caes. B. G. 7, 73 : ali hōc vires nervosque confirmari putant, id. ib. 6, 21 :…

confiscātĭo.opening: confisco , a forfeiting, confiscation : regis, Flor. 3, 9, 3 ; cf. confisco, II. B.

confiscātor.opening: a treasurer, master of the exchequer , ταμιοῦχος , Vet. Gloss.

confisco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. fiscus (post-Aug.). To lay up in a chest : quam (summam) et confiscatam semper repositamque habuerat, Suet. Aug. 101 .— Trop. : felices pauperes, qui totam animam in confiscato habent, i. e. in…

confīsĭo.opening: confido , confidence, assurance : confisio firma animi (est fidentia), Cic. Tusc. 4, 37, 80 .

confĭtĕor.opening: (arch. inf. confiterier, Plaut. Cist. 1, 3, 22 ), v. dep. fateor , to acknowledge, confess, own, avow (an error, mistake, or a fact previously denied or doubted, etc., implying a sacrifice of will or a change of…

confixĭlis.opening: adj. configo , that can be joined together : machina, App. M. 4, p. 148, 28 .

confixĭo.opening: id. , a firm joining together (late Lat.): dentium, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 3 ; 3, 6 .

con-flābello.opening: v. a. , to fan violently; trop.: scintillas libidinum, to kindle, Tert. Spect. 25 .

con-flaccesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow quite languid : fluctus conflaccescunt, subside, Gell. 2, 30, 2 .

conflāges.opening: ( , ), places exposed on all sides to the winds , Paul. ex Fest. p. 40, 10 Muuml;ll.; the same in the access. form: † confrages loca, Isid. Orig. 14, 8, 27 .

conflā^grātĭo.opening: conflagro , a burning, conflagration (post-Aug. and rare), Sen. Q. N. 3 , praef. 5; 3, 28, 7; 3, 29, 1 sq.; Suet. Tit. 8 ; Lact. 2, 9, 16 .

con-flā^gro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
con-flā^gro.opening: v. n. and a. , to burn up (rare; mostly in Cic.). Neutr., to burn, be consumed . Prop.: conflagrare terras necesse sit a tantis ardoribus, Cic. N. D. 2, 36, 92 : classis populi Romani praedonum incendio conflagrabat,…

con-flammo.opening: v. a. , to inflame , Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 7, 98 .

conflātĭlis.opening: adj. conflo, II. , cast, molten (late Lat.): Juppiter, Prud. στεφ . 10, 295; cf. Hier. Ep. 130 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a molten image , Vulg. Deut. 27, 15 .

conflātĭo.opening: conflo . A fanning, kindling, stirring up (late Lat.). Prop.: fornacis, Hier. adv. Jov. 1 , n. 1.— Esp., a casting, moulding in metal, Vulg. Jer. 51, 17 .— Trop. : fidei, Tert. Fug. Pers. 3 .—* = inflatio, Cael. Aur.…

conflātor.opening: id. , a metal-caster , χωνευτής , Cod. Th. 11, 21, 1; Vulg. Jer. 6, 29 ; 51, 17 .

conflātōrĭum.opening: id. , a melting. furnace , Vulg. Prov. 27, 21 ; cf.: fornax, conflatorium, χωνευτήριον , Gloss.

conflātūra.opening: id. , a melting of metals by fire (late Lat. and very rare), Firm. Math. 6, 31.

conflictātĭo.opening: conflicto (postAug.), a striking together, a collision, conflict, struggle : exercituum duorum, Gell 15, 18, 3; for a place in the theatre, Quint. 3, 8, 29 Halm: improbissimae, Cod. Just. 1, 3, 33, § 8 .—In plur. :…

conflictātrix.opening: † conflictator, from conflicto , she who afflicts : Aegyptus, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 14 .

conflictĭo.opening: confligo (mostly in Cic. and Quint.), a striking together, a collision. Prop.: duorum inter se corporum, Quint. 3, 6, 6 .—Esp., a conflict, combat : totius exercitus, Gell. 7 (6), 3, 1. — Trop. , a contest, conflict :…

conflicto.opening: v. freq. a. id. . In gen., to strike together violently; hence, trop., mid., to fight with, contend or struggle with (rare): qui cum ingeniis conflictatur ejusmodi, Ter. And. 1, 1, 66 ; so, cum adversā fortunā, Nep.…

conflictus.opening: confligo , a striking together (rare, and mostly in the abl. sing. ). In gen. Prop.: conflictu atque tritu lapidum elici ignem, Cic. N. D. 2, 9, 25 : nubium, id. Div. 2, 19, 44 : corporum (in conflict), id. Caecin. 15,…

conflīgātus.opening: access. form of conflictus, Part. of confligo , struck together : cornibus, Front. Strat. 2, 3, 5 dub. (al. conflictatus).

conflīgĭum.opening: confligo , a striking or dashing together : fluctuum, Sol. 9, 9 .— Absol. : strepente confligio (of the waves), Jul. Firm. Math. praef. p. 1 Pruckn.

con-flīgo.grammar: xi, ctum, 3 v. a. and n.
con-flīgo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. (rare), to strike one thing against or on another, to strike, bring , or join together, to unite. Prop.: semina, Lucr. 4, 1216 (but in id. 2, 98 , the read. is confulta; v. confultus).— Trop. , to…

con-flo.opening: v. a. , to blow together, to blow up, stir up. Of fire, to kindle, light. Prop.: ignem, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 59 ; Plin. 35, 11, 40 , §§ 138 and 143: incendium, Liv. 26, 27, 6 .—In medic. lang.: intestina conflata,…

con-flōrens.opening: Part. [floreo], blooming or flourishing together , Aug. Conf. 4, 4 .

con-fluctŭo.opening: v. n. , to wave on all sides : palla, App. M. 11, p. 258, 27 .

conflŭentĭa.opening: confluo , a flowing together, conflux , Macr. S. 7, 4, 25 .

conflūges.opening: id. , places into which several streams flow : confluges ubi conventu campum totum inhumigant, Liv. And. ap. Non. p. 62, 20 sq. (v. 16 Rib.).

con-flŭo.opening: (confluxet = confluxisset, Lucr. 1, 987 ), v. n. , to flow or run together (class. in prose and poetry). Prop.: materies umoris, Lucr. 6, 637 : in imum, id. 5, 498 : copia materiai Undique confluxet ad imum, id. 1, 987…

conflŭus.opening: adj. confluo , flowing together (post-class.): gurges, Prud. Cath. 5, 76 ; Paul. Nol. 18, 114 .

conflŭvĭum.opening: id. , a conflux, confluence (very rare), Varr. ap. Nou. p. 544, 20; Auct. Aetnae, 119 and 326 dub.

con-fŏdĭo.opening: to dig thoroughly, dig round about, to prepare by digging (orig. pertaining to agriculture). Prop.: terram minute, Cato, R. R. 129 : jugera, Varr. R. R. 1, 18, 2 : hortum, Plaut. Aul. 2, 2, 66 : loca palustria, Sisenn.…

confoedĕrātĭo.opening: a covenant, agreement , Hier. Ep. 22 , n. 35.—From

con-foedĕro.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to unite or join by a league (mostly in eccl. Lat.). Prop.: Sabinae impiis nuptiis confoederatae, Oros. 2, 4 .— Trop. : membra, Prud. στεφ . 2, 437: amicitiam nascentem, Hier. Ep. 4 , n. 1…

con-foedo.opening: to pollute, defile , App. M. 7, p. 200 fin.

confoedustus.opening: adj. con-foedus; cf. onustus, vetustus, from onus, vetus , joined in alliance , Paul. ex Fest. p. 41, 2 Müll.

confŏrānĕus.opening: working or selling at the same market-place , Gloss.

confŏrĭo.opening: 2. foria , to pollute, defile , Pompon. ap. Non. p. 114, 12 (Com. Rel. v. 64 Rib.).

conformālis.opening: adj. conformo , conformable, like, similar (eccl. Lat.): corpus, Tert. Res Carn. 47 ; so id. adv. Marc. 5, 10 .

conformātĭo.opening: id. , a symmetrical forming or fashioning, conformation, shape, form (freq. in the philos. and rhet. writings of Cic.; elsewhere rare). Prop.: lineamentorum, Cic. N. D. 1, 18, 47 : qualis sit (animus) in ipso corpore,…

conformātor.opening: id. , a framer, former : omnium, App. Trism. p. 80, 32 .

conformis.opening: adj. forma , similar, like (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 4, 12 .—With gen. : conformes fieri imaginis Filii sui, Vulg. Rom. 8, 29 .

con-formo.opening: v. a. , to form, fashion, shape symmetrically or skilfully (several times in Cic.; elsewhere very rare). Prop.: si mundum aedificatum esse, non a naturā conformatum putarem, Cic. N. D. 3, 10, 26 : ad majora quaedam nos…

con-fornĭco.opening: v. a. , to over-arch, vault over (Vitr.): cellas, Vitr. 5, 5 ; 8, 7 .

conforto.opening: v. a. fortis , to strengthen much (late Lat.; esp. freq. in the Vulg. of the Vet. Test.): stomachum, Macer. Carm. 71: manus, Lact. 4, 15 : domum Juda, Vulg. Zach. 10, 6 : confortamini, filii Benjamin, id. Jer. 6, 1 et…

confossus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from confodio.

con-fŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to warm, foster, cherish assiduously (ante- and post-class.): hominem, Afran. ap. Non. p. 523, 17 : membra cibo, App. M. 8, p. 204, 20 : semina gremio suo (terra), Hier. adv. Rufin. 8 .

confractĭo.opening: confringo , a breach, rupture , Vulg. Isa. 24, 19 ; id. Psa. 105, 23 (al. confractura).

confractus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from confringo.

con-frăgōsus.opening: adj., broken, rough, uneven (in good prose; cf. confragus; not in Cic.). Prop.: ager, Varr. R. R. 1, 18, 4 : fundus, id. ib. 1, 20, 5 : locus lapidibus, Col. 2, 2, 8 ; cf. id. 6, 17, 2 ; and Liv. 28, 2, 1 ; 32, 4, 4 :…

confrăgus.opening: adj. confringo (post-Aug.; poet. for confragosus), rough, rugged, uneven : dumeta densis arboribus, Luc. 6, 126 ; Val. Fl. 3, 581 .— Subst. : , , , a rough place, thicket : silvae, Stat. Th. 4, 494 .— Comp., sup. , and…

con-frĕmo.opening: v. n. , to sound aloud, resound, to murmur loudly , etc. ( poet. and rare): confremuere omnes, Ov. M. 1, 199 ; Stat. S. 1, 6, 72 : confremit et caelum et ... circus, Sil. 16, 398 : collis, Stat. S. 1, 4, 14 .

con-frĕquento.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to visit frequently or in great numbers, to frequent (post-Aug. and rare), Col. 9, 13, 13 ; Inscr. Orell. 2417 ; 4414 : harenas, Prud. στεφ . 1, 7.

confrĭcāmentum.opening: confrico , something for rubbing : dentium, a dentifrice, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4, 78 .

confrĭcātĭo.opening: id. , a vigorous rubbing. friction; trop., Aug. Conf. 4, 8 .

con-frĭco.opening: v. a. , to rub vigorously, to rub in (belonging to econom. and medic. lang.). Prop.: caput atque os suum unguento, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 25, § 62 : os sale trito, Col. 7, 10, 3 : boves, id. 2, 3, 1 : confricatis dentibus…

confringo.opening: v. a. frango , to break in pieces (class. in prose and poetry). Prop.: hirneam, Cato, R. R. 81 : pultando pedibus paene confregi hasce ambas (fores), Plaut. Most. 2, 2, 25 : fores caedendo, Liv. 26, 46, 6 : portarum…

con-frĭo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, āre, v. a. , to rub in : aliquid sale, Cato, R. R. 7, 5 ; cf. Varr. R. R. 1, 60 .

confrixo.opening: v. a. frigo , to roast or fry with something : aliquid cum oleo, Theod. Prisc. 1, 6 .

confŭga.opening: confugio , one who takes refuge somewhere, a refugee (late Lat.), Cod. Just. 1, 12, 6 al.

confŭgēla.opening: , an old word for confugium, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 39, 9 Müll.

con-fŭgĭo.opening: v. n. , to flee to for refuge or succor, take refuge in or with (class. in prose and poetry). Prop.: ad me nocte primā domum, Ter. Hec. 5, 3, 25 ; cf.: ad aliquem, Cic. Off. 2, 12, 41 ; id. Tusc. 5, 2, 5 ; Verg. A. 1,…

confŭgĭum.opening: confugio , a place of refuge, a refuge, shelter ( poet. and rare), Ov. Tr. 4, 5, 6 ; 5, 6, 2 ; Stat. Th. 12, 504 .

con-fulgĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine brightly, to glitter, glisten (very rare; perh. only in the foll. exs.): aedes confulgebant, Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 15 ; 5, 1, 44 : lucida confulgent alti carchesia mali, Cinna ap. Isid. Orig. 19, 2, 10 .

con-fultus.opening: adj. fulcio , pressed together ( = confertus, conglomeratus): corpora, Lucr. 2, 98 Lachm. N. cr.

con-fundo.opening: v. a. To pour, mingle , or mix together (class. in prose and poetry). Prop.: unā multa jura (cocos), Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 120 ; cf.: jus confusum sectis herbis, Hor. S. 2, 4, 67 : (venenum) in poculo, cum ita confusum…

con-fūnĕro.opening: v. a. , to bury, inter; trop., to ruin, destroy : orbem, Juvenc. 4, 96 (acc. to Barth. Adv. 13, 19).

confūsānĕus.opening: adj. confusus , mingled, miscellaneous : doctrina, Gell. prooem. § 5.

confūsē.opening: adv. , v. confundo, P. a. fin .

confūsim.opening: adv. confusus , in a confused, perplexed manner , = confuse, Varr. L. L. 9, § 4 Müll.

confūsĭo.opening: confundo . A mingling . Prop.: si duorum materiae ex voluntate dominorum confusae sint, totum id corpus quod ex confusione fit, etc., Just. Inst. 2, 1, 27 ; Dig. 6, 1, 23, § 5 : colorum, App. de Mundo, p. 66, 24, 2.—…

confūtātĭo.opening: confuto , a confutation , Gr. λύσις , Auct. Her. 1, 3, 4 .

confūtātor.opening: id. , a refuter, opponent : Valentini, Hier. Script. Eccl.

con-fūto.opening: v. a. futo, v. intens. from foveo , to check or repress a boiling liquid, to suppress, restrain, check . Prop.: cocus magnum ahenum quando fervit, paulā confutat truā, Titin. ap. Non. p. 87, 13 (Com. Rel. v. 128 Rib.);…

con-garrĭo.opening: v. a. , to gabble much, to prattle , Antonin. ap. Fronto, Ep. 1, 15 Mai.

con-gaudeo.opening: v. n. , to rejoice with one (eccl. Lat.): alicui, Tert. adv. Gnost. c. 13; so Cypr. Ep. 50 al.

Congĕdus.opening: a river in Spain, tributary to the Iberus , Mart. 1, 49, 9 .

con-gĕlasco.opening: (no perf. or sup. ), v. inch. n. , to freeze, congeal (late Lat.): oleum, vina, Gell. 17, 8, 10 ; Macr. S. 7, 12, 32 ; Ambros. in Luc. 10, § 135 .

congĕlātĭo.opening: congelo , a freezing, congealing (very rare; not ante-Aug.): liquoris, Plin. 31, 3, 21, § 33 .—In plur. : brumae, Col. 4, 8, 2 .

con-gĕlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
con-gĕlo.opening: v. a. and n. Act., to cause to freeze up, to congeal . Lit. : sal, Vitr. 8, 3 : oleum, Col. 1, 6, 18 ; 12, 50, 12 : pruinas, Plin. 18, 28, 68, § 277 : radices, Col. 3, 12, 1 : mare congelatum, the sea being frozen,…

congĕmĭnātĭo.opening: congemino , a doubling; connected with conduplicatio, in com. lang., for embracing , Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 18 .

con-gĕmĭno.opening: v. a. , to double, redouble, repeat, reduplicate ( poet. ): nunc si pateram patera peperit, omnes congeminavimus, i. e. have produced our like, doubled ourselves, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 154 : L (litteram), Lucil. S. 9, 9 :…

con-gĕmisco.opening: v. inch. n. , to sigh deeply (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Spect. 30 ; Prud. στεφ . 2, 411 al.

con-gĕmo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr., to sigh or groan deeply or loudly, to heave a sigh . Prop. (rare but class.): congemuit senatus frequens, * Cic. Mur. 25, 51 ; * Suet. Tib. 23 .— Transf. , poet. , of trees cut down: supremum…

con-gĕner.opening: a joint son-inlaw , Symm. Ep. 8, 40 dub. (al. generi).

con-gĕnĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To beget or produce at the same time (very rare; perh. only in the foll. exs., and only in the perf. part. ): porci congenerati, of the same litter, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 19 ; so in part. : senium…

con-gĕnĭtus.opening: Part. [gigno], born or produced together with (very rare; not ante-Aug.): pili, congenital, Plin. 11, 39, 94, § 230 .—With dat. : vastitas roborum mundo, coëval with, Plin. 16, 2, 2, § 6 ; Tert. Test. Anim. c. 5.

con-gentīles.opening: kindred, of the same stock , Inscr. Orell. 2491 ; cf. congentilis, ὁμόεθνος , Gloss. Philox.

con-gĕnū^clo.opening: v. n. geniculo , to fall upon the knees , Cael. ap. Non. p. 89, 6 .

con-gĕnŭlātus.opening: Part. [genu], fallen upon the knees : multi congenulati, etc., Sisenn. ap. Non. p. 57, 32 (perh. congenuclati should be the reading; cf. congenuclo).

conger.opening: (access. form , acc. to Charis. p. 12 P.; also gonger, Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 148 ), , , = γόγγρος a sea-eel, conger-eel , Plaut. Aul. 2, 9, 2 ; id. Mil. 3, 1, 165 ; id. Pers. 1, 3, 30 ; Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 23 ; Ov. Hal. 115 ;…

congĕrĭes.opening: ( , , Front. Colon. p. 11, 119 and 125 Goes.; Innoc. Cas. Litt. p. 224 ib.), congero , that which is brought together; hence, a heap, pile, mass (not ante-Aug.; while the syn. acervus is prevalent through all periods).…

con-germānesco.opening: v. inch. n. [germanus], to grow together with one, grow up with : coalescere, conjungi vel consociari, Non. p. 90, 16 sq. (ante- and post-class., and very rare): cum illis, Quadrig. ap. Non. l. l.; so, mecum, App. M. 2,…

con-germānus.opening: adj., grown together with, united with , Varr. ap. Non. p. 90, 20 .

con-germĭnālis.opening: adj. germen , from the same stalk or stock : spicae ceteris congerminales, Aug. Civ. Dei , 5, 7.
