con-germĭno.opening: v. n. , to shoot forth at the same time , Gell. 20, 8, 7 .

con-gĕro.opening: 1. congero , a thief , Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 6 ; cf. Fulg. p. 566, 13 : congerones qui aliena ad se congregant; so also 2. gero.

congerro.opening: ( , Fest. p. 356 Lindem.), , congero; prop. one who contributes to a common feast; cf. Lorenz ad Plaut. Most. v. 919 , a jolly companion, a playfellow (ante-class.), Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 9 ; id. Most. 3, 3, 27 (931…

congestē.opening: adv. , v. 1. congero, P. a. fin.

congestīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. 1. congero , brought together, heaped or piled up (rare; mostly post-Aug.): agger ex materiā, Caes. B. C. 2, 15 ; cf. materia, Col. 2, 16, 5 : humus, id. 2, 10, 18 : terra, Pall. Sept. 7 ; id. Oct. 11, 2 :…

congestim.opening: adv. id. , heaped together, in heaps : congestim et acervatim jacere, App. Mag. p. 296, 40 .

congestĭo.opening: id. , lit. a bringing together; hence, a heaping up, accumulation (rare and not ante-Aug.). In abstr. Prop.: terrae, Vitr. 6, 8, 5 ; Pall. Mart. 1, 4 : stercorum, Pall. 1, 33, 1 .— Trop. : enumerationis, Macr. S. 5, 15…

con-gesto.opening: v. a. , to bring or carry together , Aug. de Pecc. Merit. 1, 28 ; Commod. 64, 15 .

congestus.opening: 1. congero , a bearing or bringing together, an accumulation (rare; mostly post-Aug.). Prop. In abstr.: herbam asperam credo (exstitisse) avium congestu, non humano satu, * Cic. Div. 2, 32, 68 : copiarum, Tac. H. 2, 87…

congĭālis.opening: adj. congius , holding a congius (very rare): fidelia, * Plaut. Aul. 4, 2, 15 : situli, Vitr. 10, 4, 4 .

congĭārĭus.opening: adj. congius , pertaining to a congius, holding a congius. As adj. rare: vinum, given by measure , Cato ap. Fronto Ep. ad Antonin. 1, 2, p. 149 Mai: cadi, Varr. ap. Plin. 14, 14, 17, § 96 .—But very freq. subst. , , ,…

congĭus.opening: a Roman measure for liquids, containing the eighth part of an amphora, six sextarii, or twelve heminae; = about 206 cubic inches or nearly six pints English, Cato, R. R. 57 ; Liv. 25, 2, 8 ; Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 85 ; 14,…

conglŏbātim.opening: adv. conglobo , in heaps, in a mass (late Lat.), Aug. Conf. 7, 7 fin.

con-glōrĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to glorify together with (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. c. 40 al.

conglūtĭnōsus.opening: adj. conglutino , glutinous, viscous : pars umoris, Veg. Art. Vet. 2, 12, 2 .

con-grădus.opening: adj., keeping pace with : sidera soli, Avien. Arat. 1239 .

con-graeco.opening: v. a. graecor, āri , to lavish on banquets like the Greeks, to squander in luxury : aurum, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 91 .

congrātŭlātĭo.opening: congratulor , a wishing of joy; congratulation , Val. Max. 9, 3, 5 ; Don. Vit. Verg. 24 .

con-grātŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to wish joy, to congratulate (very rare; not in Cic.); absol. : dona quid cessant mihi Conferre omnes congratulantes, qui pugnavi fortiter, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 21 Brix; Gell. 12, 1, 4 ; Vulg. 2 Reg. 8, 10 .—With…

con-grĕdĭor.opening: v. dep. gradior , to go, come , or meet with one , esp. with the access. idea of intention, in a friendly or hostile sense (class. in prose and poetry); constr. with cum ( contra , etc.), the acc., dat. , or absol . In…

congrĕgābĭlis.opening: adj. congrego , easily brought together, social : examina apium, Cic. Off. 1, 44, 157 .

congrĕgālis.opening: adj. id. uniting together : vinculum, Ter. Maur. p. 2411 P.

congrĕgātim.opening: adv. id. , together, in crowds : cursant per ampla moenia, Prud. Cath. 7, 143 .

congrĕgātĭo.opening: id. , an assembling together; union, society, association (in good prose). Lit. : nos ad conjunctionem congregationemque hominum et ad naturalem communitatem esse natos, Cic. Fin. 3, 20, 65 ; 4, 2, 4 ; cf. Sen. Ep. 5, 3…

congrĕgātīvus.opening: adj. id. , suitable for uniting or congregating, copulative : adverbia (simul, una, pariter, etc.), Prisc. p. 1021 P.

congrĕgātor.opening: id. , one who brings together, an assembler : horum omnium, Arn. 6, p. 199 ; Ambros. in Psa. 39, § 22 .

congrĕgātus.opening: id. , a union, association : hominum, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 2, 37 .

con-grĕgo.opening: v. a. , to collect into a flock or herd, to assemble. Prop. (rare; mostly in Pliny the elder): oves, Plin. 8, 47, 72, § 188 .—Mid.: apium examina congregantur, collect in swarms, Cic. Off. 1, 44, 157 ; cf. id. N. D. 2,…

congrĕgus.opening: adj. con-grex , united in flocks , etc. (opp. solivagus): aves, Isid. 12, 7, 1 .

congressĭo.opening: congredior , a coming together , in a friendly or hostile manner. A friendly meeting, interview, conference (almost confined to Cic.), Cic. Clu. 14, 41 ; id. Phil. 2, 18, 46 ; id. Top. 15, 59 ; id. Fam. 7, 10, 4 ; opp.…

congressor.opening: id. , one who meets or assembles with , Ambros. Ep. 27, 16 .

congressus.opening: congredior , a coming or going together , in a friendly or hostile manner (class. in prose and poetry). A friendly meeting, a social assembly, conference, conversation , etc.: omnes congressum tuum fugiunt, Cic. Sest.…

con-grex.opening: adj. (post-class.). Of the same herd or flock : equinis armentis, App. M. 7, p. 194, 41 : aves, Sol. 2 dub. (al. congregatae).—Hence, In gen., collected in flocks or multitudes : catervas, Auct. Pervig. Ven. 43: vulgo,…

Congrĭo.opening: conger , the name of a cook in Plaut. Aul. 2, 5, 2 ; 2, 9, 5 .

congrŭenter.opening: adv. , v. congruo, P. a. fin.

congrŭentĭa.opening: congruo , agreement, harmony, congruity, symmetry (postAug. and very rare): morum, * Suet. Oth. 2 : (corporis), with aequalitas, Plin. Ep. 2, 5, 11 : pronuntiandi, App. Mag. p. 283, 15 al.

congrŭo.opening: ( inf. pres. congruēre, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 102 ), v. n. etym. dub.; cf. Corss. Beitr. 457 , to run, come , or meet together with something. Prop. (rare; mostly post-Aug.): guttae inter se congruunt et confunduntur, Vitr.…

congrŭus.opening: adj. congruo, II. , agreeing, fit, suitable; harmonious, concordant (ante-, and more freq. post-class., for the class. congruens): sermo cum illā, * Plaut. Mil. 4, 3, 23 : sententia verecundiae maternae, Dig. 39, 5, 31,…

con-gȳro.opening: v. n. , to make a circle about a person : circa aliquam, Vulg. Judith, 13, 16 .

cōnĭcĭo.opening: (also and ; cf. Munro ad Lucr. 2, 1061 ; Laber. ap. Gell. 16, 7, 5 ), , v. a. (arch. temp. perf. conjexi, Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 99 ) [jacio]. To throw or bring together, to unite , = cogo, colligo. Lit. (very rare): cum…

cōnĭfer.opening: adj. conus-fero , bearing fruit of a conical form : cyparissi, Verg. A. 3, 680 Serv.; cf. coniger and co nus.

cōnĭger.opening: adj. conusgero , bearing fruit of a conical form : pinus, Cat. 64, 106 ; cf. conifer and conus.

cŏnīla.opening: , = κονίλη , a plant, also called cunila and origanum, App. Herb. 123 .

coniptum.opening: or , an oblation made by sprinkling flour , Paul. ex Fest. p. 40, 8 Müll.

cŏnistērĭum.opening: , = κονιστἠριον , a place in the palæstra where the athletæ, after anointing, sprinkled themselves with dust , Vitr. 5, 11, 2 .

cō-nītor.opening: (less correctly ; cf. Ritschl, Opusc. II. 448 sq.), nisus or nix us (conisus, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 29 ; Liv. 1, 33, 5 ; 3, 63, 4 et saep.; Val. Max. 2, 7, 2 ; Ser. Ep. 94, 31; Val. Fl. 3, 193 ; Sil. 2, 629 ; Tac. A. 11, 31…

cōnīum.opening: , = κώνειον , hemlock (pure Lat. cicuta), Ambros. Hexaem. 3, 9 .

con-jăcĕo.opening: to lie together , Myth. Vat. 2, 30, tom. 3, p. 94 Mai.

conjectānĕa.opening: conicio , a memorandum- or commonplace-book, a title of works of miscellaneous contents , Gell. praef. § 9; 6, 5, 1; 14, 7, 13.

conjectārĭus.opening: of or pertaining to conjecture, conjectural : argumenta, Gell. 14, 3, 1 Hertz (al. conjectatoria).

conjectātor.opening: id. , a conjecturer, soothsayer (late Lat. and rare): portenti, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 49 Mai; so Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Al. M. 1, 57 .

conjecto.opening: v. freq. a. conicio (ante-class.; and then not until the time of Liv.), to throw, cast , or bring together. Prop.: hostium duces in carcerem, Decret. Ti. Gracch. ap. Gell. 7, 19, 7 : ad cenulam non cupedias ciborum, sed…

conjector.opening: conicio, I. B. 1. , he who interprets, explains , or divines something, an interpreter . In gen.: conjectore Oedipo orationi opus est, Plaut. Poen. 1, 3, 34 .— In partic., a diviner, interpreter of dreams, a seer,…

conjectrix.opening: conjector , a female soothsayer or interpreter of dreams , Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 99 .

conjectūra.opening: conicio, I. B. 2. , a putting together of facts or indications; hence an opinion founded on a comparison of facts, a conjecture, guess, conjectural inference . In gen. (very freq., and class.): quod ad exemplum'st?…

conjectūrālis.opening: adj. conjectura , belonging to conjecture or guessing, conjectural : ars medicina, Cels. 1 praef. ; 2, 6 fin. —Esp. freq. in rhet. lang.: causa, Cic. Top. 24, 92: causae, id. ib. 11, 50 ; Quint. 2, 4, 26 : status, id.…

con-jŭbĕo.opening: v. a. , to command together with , Edict. Diocl. prooem.

con-jūcundor.opening: v. dep. , to rejoice with one (late Lat.); with dat. : amico, Vulg. Ecclus. 37, 4 .

conjŭgālis.opening: adj. conjunx , relating to marriage, conjugal (prob. not ante-Aug.). Prop.: amor, Tac. A. 11, 4 : licentia, id. ib. 11, 27 : di, who preside over marriage, id. G. 18 ; Sen. Thyest. 1103 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9, 3.— Esp.,…

con-jungo.opening: v. a. , to bind together, connect, join, unite (very freq. in all perr. and species of composition); constr. with cum, inter se , the dat. , or the acc. only; trop. also with ad. Lit. With cum : eam epistulam cum hac,…

con-nŭmĕro.opening: v. a. , to number with something, to reckon among (post-class. and rare): aliquem inter liberos, Dig. 1, 5, 14 : virum heroicis ingeniis, Amm. 25, 4, 1 .— Absol. : quemadmodum connumeratis et dicitis, Arn. 2, 187 ; Gai…

con-sălūto.opening: v. a. , to greet, salute cordially , in gen. (in good prose; esp. freq. in the histt. after the Aug. per.). With acc. : utrumque regem (sua multitudo), Liv. 1, 7, 1 : eum, Petr. 7 ; 131 ; Curt. 7, 8, 5 ; 10, 7, 7 :…

con-sōpĭo.opening: , no perf. , ītum, 4, v. a. , to bring into an unconscious state, to put fast asleep, lull to sleep, to stupefy (rare but class.). Lit. : somno consopiri sempiterno, Cic. Tusc. 1, 49, 117 : Endymion a Lunā consopitus…

con-sors.opening: adj. m. and Sharing property with one (as brother, sister, relative), living in community of goods, partaking of in common : consortes, ad quos eadem sors, Varr. L. L. 6, § 65 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 296, 7 ib.:…

consortālis.opening: adj. consortium , pertaining to property held in common : lineae, Front. Colon. p. 111 Goes.

consortĭo.opening: consors, II. , fellowship, community, partnership, association (rare, but in good prose): omnis humana dissolvetur, Cic. Off. 3, 6, 26 : sociabilis inter binos Lacedaemoniorum reges, Liv. 40, 8, 12 ; cf.: tribuniciae…

consortĭum.opening: consors (not anteAug.). Community of goods , Suet. Claud. 28 : voluntarium inter fratres, Dig. 17, 2, 52, § 8 .— Fellowship, participation, society , Liv. 4, 5, 5 ; Quint. 12, 1, 4 ; Col. 4, 16, 1 ; Tac. A. 4, 3 ; Plin.…

con-spătĭans.opening: Part. [spatior], walking together : inter meretrices, Petr. 7, 3 .

conspectĭo.opening: conspicio , a look, sight, view (late Lat. and rare for conspectus), Jul. Epit. Nov. 57, § 201 .

conspector.opening: id. , he who sees or beholds; an inspector, beholder (eccl. Lat.): cordis Deus, Tert. Or. 13 ; id. Cult. Fem. 2, 13 .

conspectus.opening: conspicio , a seeing, looking at, a look, sight, view, the range or reach of sight, the power of seeing (freq., and class. in prose and poetry). Lit. : casurusne in conspectum videatur animus, an tanta sit ejus…

conspergo.opening: (in MSS. also ; cf. 1. aspergo), , v. a. spargo . To sprinkle, moisten, besprinkle, bespatter, strew (very freq. and class.). Lit. With acc. and abl. : fores vino, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 80 : aras multo sanguine, Lucr. 4,…

conspersĭo.opening: ( ), , conspergo (late Lat.). Abstr., a scattering, strewing, sprinkling : crebra salis, Pall. Nov. 13, 3 .— Concr., paste, dough , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 24 al.

conspĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. conspicor (eccl. Lat.). Visible : ore, Prud. στεφ . 10, 631. — Remarkable, notable : thermae, Sid. Ep. 8, 4 al.

conspĭcābundus.opening: adj. conspicor , considering attentively : Pallas virginem, Mart. Cap. 8, § 803 .

conspĭcĭendus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from conspicio.

conspĭcĭentĭa.opening: conspicio , the faculty of considering : rerum conspicien tiam habere, Cassiod. An. 3 .

conspĭcillum.opening: ( , Plaut. Fragm ap. Non. p. 84, 7 ), , id. , a place to look from , and, transf., a watching : conspicillo consecutu'st me, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 92 ; cf. unde conspici possis, Plaut. ap. Non. 1 . 1.

con-spĭcĭo.grammar: spexi, spectum, 3 v. a. and n.
con-spĭcĭo.opening: v. a. and n. , to look at attentively, to get sight of, to descry, perceive, observe (class. in prose and poetry). Lit. In gen. Absol. : inter eas regiones, quā oculi conspiciant, Varr. L. L. 7, § 9 Müll.: in tabernam,…

conspĭcĭo.opening: 1. conspicio , the survey taken by the augur in fixing the limits of the templum, Varr. L. L. 7, § 9 Müll.

conspĭcor.opening: v. dep. a. [id.], to get sight of, to descry, see, perceive (very freq. in Plaut. and Caes.; several times in Ter.; elsewh. rare; never in Lucr., Cic., Virg., or Hor.). With acc. : nec quemquam conspicor alium in viā,…

conspĭcŭus.opening: adj. 1. conspicio ( poet. or in post-Aug. prose, esp. in Tac.; not in Quint.). Lit. , that is or comes in view, visible; opp. occultus: quot inter Occultum stellae conspicuumque polum, Ov. Tr. 4, 10, 108 : rebus ab…

conspīrātĭo.opening: 1. conspiro , prop. a blowing or breathing together . * Lit. , of unison in wind instruments: canentium, Col. 12, 2, 4 .—Far more freq., Trop. , an agreement in feeling or opinion, union, unanimity, concord, harmony .…

conspīrātus.opening: 1. conspiro , an agreement, harmony; only in abl. sing. : conspiratu tacito mentium animorumque, Gell. 1, 11, 8 .

con-spīro.opening: v. a. spira , to coil up (very rare): anguis se conspiravit, Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 22 .

conspissātĭo.opening: spisso , a pressing together, a thickening : sordium, an accumulation, Theod. Prisc. 1, 18 .

con-spissātus.opening: Part. [id.], pressed together, thickened, condensed, dense (very rare): solum conspissatum et herbis colligatum, Col. 2, 18, 5 : vinacea, id. 12, 45, 3 : creta, Plin. 35, 6, 18, § 36 .

con-splendesco.opening: v. n. , to shine very much : tecta, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 3, 66 .

con-spŏlĭo.opening: v. a. , to rob (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 98, 21 fin.

conspŏlĭum.opening: a kind of sacrificial cake , acc. to Arn. 7, 230 .

con-spondĕo.grammar: ndi, nsum 2 v. a. and n.
con-spondĕo.opening: (old orthog. consposum, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 41, 14 Müll.), , v. a. and n. , to engage or promise something mutually (ante- and postclass. and very rare): NEVE. CONSPONDISE. NEVE. CONPROMESISE. VELET., S. C.…

consponsāta.opening: sponso , the betrothed, the bride (late Lat.), Ambros. in Luc. 3, 3 .

con-sponsor.opening: A joint surety , Cic. Fam. 6, 18, 2 ; id. Att. 12, 17 .— One who binds or obligates himself to something ( = conjurator), acc. to Fest. p. 59, 7 Müll.

con-spŭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. and n. Act., to spit upon (rare; most freq. in Petr.): me immundissimo basio, Petr. 23, 4 .—Esp., to spit upon in contempt , Plaut. Curc. 4, 2, 17 ; Petr. 132, 3 ; Hier. Ep. 50 , n. 4; cf. Barth.…

con-spurco.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to defile, pollute (rare): omnia taetro sapore, * Lucr. 6, 22 : (juvenem) per vim, Suet. Ner. 35 ; Col. 8, 3 fin. ; Tert. Idol. 1 .

con-spūto.opening: , no perf. , , v. freq. a. conspuo , to spit upon in contempt (very rare): nostros coeperunt Clodiana, * Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 3, 2 : maledictus et consputatus, etc., Tert. adv. Jud. 14 ; id. Idol. 1 .

con-stăbĭlĭo.opening: v. a. , to confirm, establish, make firm (ante- and post-class. for stabilio, 2. fundo, and rare); only trop.: rem meam, * Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 93 ; so * Ter. Ad. 5, 1, 9 ; Tert. adv. Valent. 39 .

con-stagno.opening: v. n. , of fluids, = congelo, to cause to stand, to congeal , Fronto, p. 2198 P.

constans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from consto.

Constans.opening: a Roman proper name , Aur. Vict. Epit. 41 ; Eutr. 10, 9 .

constanter.opening: adv. , v. consto, P. a. fin.

constantĭa.opening: 1. constans . A firm standing, steadiness, firmness, immutability, unchangeableness, constancy, perseverance (in good prose; esp. freq. in Cic.): (stellarum) perennes cursus atque perpetui cum admirabili incredibilique…

Constantia.opening: a Roman proper name , Lact. Mort. Pers. 15, 1, 6 ; Amm. 21, 15, 6 .

Constantīna.opening: A daughter of Constantine the Great , Amm. 14, 7, 4 .— The name of several cities, esp., A town of Mesopotamia , Amm. 18, 7, 9 .— A later name of Cirta in Numidia , now Constantine , Aur. Vict. Caes. 40, 28 .— Hence, ,…

Constantīnŏpŏlis.opening: , = Κωνσταντίνου πολις , the city Constantinople , previously called Byzantium; Turkish Stamboul , Amm. 22, 8, 8 ; 31, 16, 4 ; Eutr. 6, 6 ; Aur. Vict. Epit. 35 ; Aus. Urb. 2 ; id. Parent. 3, 11 al. —Hence, , , adj., of…

Constantīnus.opening: , C. Flavius Vaferius Claudius Constantinus, Constantine, a well-known Roman emperor , born A. D. 274, died A. D. 323, Eutr. 10, 2 sqq.; Lact. Mort. Pers. 18 sqq.; Amm. 21, 10, 8 .—Hence, , , adj., of or pertaining to…

Constantĭus.opening: the name of a Roman emperor who reigned from 292 A. D. to 306 A. D., Eutr. 10, 6 sqq.; Lact. Mort. Pers. 15, 6 ; Aur. Vict. Caes. 40 .—Hence, the adjj. : , , um: legiones, Amm. 21, 11, 2 : , , um: thalamus, id. 22, 3,…

con-stellātĭo.opening: stella , a collection of stars supposed to exert an influence upon human affairs, a constellation (late Lat.), Amm. 29, 2, 27 ; Capitol. Gord. 20 ; Spart. Ver. 4 al.

con-stellātus.opening: adj., starred, studded with stars : baltei, Treb. Gall. 2.

consternātĭo.opening: 2. consterno (not ante-Aug.; mostly in histt.), confusion, dismay, consternation, alarm, disquietude, disturbance . In gen.: pavor et consternatio mentis, Tac. A. 13, 16 : quae causa irae consternationisque subitae…

con-sterno.opening: v. a. To strew over, cover by strewing, bestrew, to thatch, floor, pave, spread, cover (class. in prose and poetry). With abl. : tabernacula caespitibus, Caes. B. C. 3, 96 : cubilia gallinarum paleis, Col. 8, 5, 3 :…

consterno.opening: v. a. strengthened collat. form of 1. consterno, acc. to II. . To stretch upon the ground, to overcome : pecorum in modum consternatos (Gallos) caedunt fugantque, Liv. 38, 17, 7 .—Far more freq., esp. after the Aug.…

constīpātĭo.opening: constipo (postclass.), a crowding together; in concr., a dense crowd : exercitūs, Vop. Aur. 21 : militum, Amm. 26, 6, 14 .

con-stīpo.opening: v. a. , to press or crowd closely together (very rare): tantum numerum hominum in agrum Campanum, * Cic. Agr. 2, 29, 79 : se (hostes) sub ipso vallo, Caes. B. G. 5, 42 ; Prud. στεφ . 11.

constĭtĭo.opening: consisto , an abiding, abode, stay : loci, in the same place, Gell. 16, 5, 10 ; cf. Macr. S. 6, 8 .

con-stĭtŭo.opening: v. a. statuo , to cause to stand, put or lay down, to set, put, place, fix, station, deposit a person or thing somewhere (esp. firmly or immovably ), etc. (the act. corresponding to consistere; class.). In gen. Prop.:…

constĭtūtĭo.opening: constituo . In gen., a constitution, disposition, nature : firma corporis, Cic. Off. 3, 33, 117 (as transl. of the Gr. εὐστάθεια τῆς σαρκός ); so Sen. Ep. 121, 10 and 14: prima naturae, Cic. Fin. 4, 6, 15 .— In partic.…

constĭtūtĭōnārĭus.opening: constitutio , he who presides over the copying of the imperial constitutions , Gest. ap. Sen. Recip. Th. Cod.

constĭtūtor.opening: constituo , an orderer, arranger (mostly post-class.): legis, Quint. 3, 6, 43 : rerum omnium Deus, Lact. 3, 9, 10 : Deus machinator constitutorque rerum, id. 4, 6, 1 : moderatorque cunctorum, Arn. 3, p. 101 : SACRI…

constĭtūtōrĭus.opening: adj. constituo, D. 1. b. ; in the jurists, pertaining to agreement : actio, Dig. 13, 5, 20 sq. ; 46, 3, 59 .

constĭtūtus.opening: a meeting of persons : a consistentium multitudine appellatur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 42, 5 Müll.

con-sto.opening: (constātūrus, Sen. Clem. 1, 19, 3 ; Plin. 18, 5, 6, § 30 ; Luc. 2, 17 ; Mart. 10, 41, 5 ; Lact. Opif. Dei, 7, 11), , v. n. To stand together, stand with some person or thing. Lit. (very rare): constant, conserunt…

con-strātor.opening: sterno , a leveller, quieter, calmer : maris, Aus. Technop. 12 .

con-strĕpo.opening: v. n. , to resound, sound loudly or boisterously, to make a noise (post-class.). Lit. : domus tota constrepebat hymenaeum, App. M. 4, p. 154, 23 ; cf. id. ib. 11 , p. 261, 34.— Trop. , of a vivid speech: horum omnium et…

constrictē.opening: adv. , v. constringo, P. a. fin .

constrictĭo.opening: constringo (postclass.), a binding or drawing together , Pall. Mart. 1 ; Scrib. Comp. 84 .— Esp., a binding, stopping of the bowels , Macr. S. 7, 6 al.

constrictīvus.opening: adj. id. , drawing together, contracting, astringent (in later medic. writers): cibi, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 3 fin. : virtutis esse, id. Acut. 2, 18 al. — Adv. : , astringently : tractare aliquid, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 38…

constricto.opening: v. freq. [id.], to draw together; of a physician (with inurere, amputare, etc.), Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 16 .

constrictūra.opening: id. , a drawing together , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 9, 69 .

constrictus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from constringo.

con-stringo.opening: v. a. , to draw together, bind together, to bind, tie up (class. in prose and poetry). Lit. In gen.: vineam alligato recte, dum ne nimium constringas, Cato, R. R. 33, 1 : sarcinam, Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 96 : galeam, Val.…

constructĭo.opening: construo , a putting or placing together, a joining together (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.; not in Quint.). Lit. (rare): lapidum, Sen. Cons. Polyb. 18 (37), 2.— Transf. , an erecting, building, construction :…

con-strŭo.opening: ( part. fut. constrŭĭtūra, Ven. Carm. 2, 10 fin. ), v. a. To heap, bring , or gather together, to heap or pile up (class.): acervos nummorum apud aliquem, Cic. Phil. 2, 38, 97 ; cf.: omnibus rebus et modis constructā et…

con-stŭpĕo.opening: v. n. , to be very much astonished , Juvenc. 1, 179 .

constū^prātor.opening: constupro , a defiler, debaucher : stuprati et constupratores, Liv 39, 15, 9.

con-stū^pro.opening: v. a. , to violate, ravisn, debauch, defile (rare, but in good prose). Prop.: matronas, virgines, ingenuos, raptos, etc., Liv. 29, 17, 15 : virginem, Curt. 10, 1, 5 : praetextatos liberos, Q. Cic. Pet. Cons. 3, 10 ;…

con-sŭādĕo.opening: v. a. , to advise or counsel strongly (Plautin.; cf. however, consuasor): id consuadeo, Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 32 : consuadet homini, id. Trin. 2, 4, 126 : qui consuadet, vetat, id. ib. 3, 2, 46 .—Of favorable auspices:…

consŭāsor.opening: consuadeo , he who strenuously counsels to something, a counsellor, adviser : auctore et consuasore Naevio, Cic. Quint. 5, 18 .

con-sŭāvĭo.opening: ( ), āre; or ( ), , v. a. , to kiss much or affectionately (only in App.), App. M. 6, p. 182, 18 ; 2 , p. 120, 31.

con-sŭbĭgo.opening: to work, knead , or mix together (late Lat.): cineres, lixiva, etc., Garg. Mart. de Cura Boum med.

con-substantĭālis.opening: adj., of like essence, nature , or substance, consubstantial (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Herm. 44 al. —Hence,

consubstantĭālĭtas.opening: consubstantialis , a like quality (late Lat.), Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 2, 7 med.

con-substantīvus.opening: adj. ( = consubstantialis), of like essence, nature , etc. (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Val. 12 fin. and 18.

consūdasco.opening: (in a few MSS. ), , v. inch. [consudo], to sweat much; of olives packed up, Col. 12, 48, 2 .

con-sūdo.opening: v. n. , to sweat much or profusely (very rare), Cato, R. R. 96, 1 ; Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 71 ; Col. 12, 7, 2 .

consŭē-făcĭo.opening: (in Ter. Ad. 1, 1, 29 ; 1, 1, 49 , and 3, 3, 60, consue feci, consue facere, consue facio, acc. to Lachm. ad Lucr. p. 409 ), v. a. consueo , to accustom one to a thing, to inure, habituale (rare, and mostly ante-class.…

con-sŭĕo.opening: v. a. , to be accustomed, be wont , acc. to Charis. p. 224 P.; Prisc. p. 885 ib. (for consuemus in Prop.; v. consuesco init. ).

consŭesco.opening: (in the tempp. perff. the sync. forms prevail: consuesti, consuestis, consuerunt; consueram, etc.; consuero, etc.; consuerim, etc.; consuessem, etc.; consuesse. Thus also consuēmus = consuevimus, Prop. 1, 7, 5 ), v. a.…

consŭētĭo.opening: consuesco, II. B. , carnal intercourse : clandestina, Plaut. Am. 1, 2, 28 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 61, 4 Müll.; Don. ad Ter. Ad. 4, 5, 32 .

consŭētūdĭnārĭus.opening: adj. consuetudo , customary, ordinary, usual (late Lat.): portitor. Sid. Ep. 7, 11 : carnes, Salv. Gub. Dei. 6, p. 219 al. — Adv. : , in the usual manner , Cassiod. Var. 12, 2 fin.

consŭētūdo.opening: consuesco . A being accustomed, custom, habit, use, usage . In gen. (very freq. in all periods, esp. in prose): exercitatio ex quā consuetudo gignitur, Cic. de Or. 2, 87, 358 : dicunt ... consuetudine quasi alteram…

consŭētus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. consuesco fin.

consul.opening: (in the oldest inscrr. CONSOL, COSOL; abbrev. COS., also in plur. COSS., not before the time of the emperors), , prob. from root sal- of salio; Sanscr. sar-, go; hence also exsul, praesul, v. Corss. Ausspr. II. p. 71 ,…

consŭlāris.opening: adj. consul , of or pertaining to a consul, consular (very freq.): aetas, the age required by law for the consular office , viz. the 43d year, Cic. Phil. 5, 17, 48 ; cf. annus, II.: comitia, for the choice of consul,…

consŭlārĭtas.opening: consularis, II. B. , the dignity or office of consul or imperial governor (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 6, 19, 1; 6, 27, 10; 9, 26, 4 al.

consŭlārĭus.opening: adj. , = consularis (late Lat.): dignitas, Jul. Epit. c. 98, § 359.

consŭlātus.opening: consul , the office of consul, the consulate or consulship (very frq. in all periods): honorum populi finis est consulatus, Cic. Planc. 25, 60 : consulatus ille antiquus, id. Tusc. 2, 17, 41 : quo pluris est universa…

consŭlo.grammar: lŭi, ltum, 3 v. n. and a.
consŭlo.opening: v. n. and a. [from con and root sal-; cf. consul and consilium]. To consider, reflect, deliberate, take counsel, reflect upon, consult . Neutr . In gen. Absol. : quid nunc? etiam consulis? do you still deliberate , i.…

consultātĭo.opening: 2. consulto . A mature deliberation, consideration, consultation . In gen. (rare but class.). Abstr., * Ter. Hec. 4, 4, 28 ; Cic. de Or. 2, 33, 142 ; id. Inv. 2, 25, 76 fin. ; id. Off. 3, 12, 50 ; Suet. Ner. 41 al.…

consultātor.opening: id. , one who asks advice, consults (post-Aug. and rare, for the class. consultor, III.), Quint. 6, 3, 87 ; Dig. 1, 2, 2, § 35 .

consultātōrĭus.opening: adj. consultator , of or pertaining to consultation : hostiae (hostiarum genus, in quo voluntas dei per exta disquiritur), opp. animales, Macr. S. 3, 5 .

consultē.opening: adv. , v. consulo, P. a. fin.

consultō.opening: adv. , v. consulo, P. a. fin.

consulto.opening: v. freq. a. consulo . To reflect, consider maturely, to consult, take counsel, deliberate. In gen. (class.). With acc. : quid illaec illic in consilio duae secreto consultant? Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 38 : ad haec…

consultrix.opening: 1. consultor , she who has a care for, provides : consultrix et provida utilitatum opportunitatumque omnium natura, Cic. N. D. 2, 22, 58 .

consultus.opening: , for consultum, only in Isid. Orig. 9, 4, 9 : senatusconsultus a consulendo est dictus.

con-sum.opening: (found only in the foll. exs.). To be together with or at the same time, to coexist : si neque alia quaelibet passio lumbricis confuerit, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 8, 122 .— To be, to happen : confido confuturum, Plaut. Mil.…

consummābĭlis.opening: adj. consummo , that may be perfected, susceptible of completion (post-Aug. and very rare): ratio in nobis (opp. consummata), Sen. Ep. 92, 27 : aevum, Prud. Psych. 846 .

consummātĭo.opening: id. (postAug.). A casting up or reckoning together, a summing up, a summary view . Prop.: operarum, Col. 12, 13, 7 : ambitus Europae, Plin. 4, 23, 37, § 121 : singulorum mancipiorum, Dig. 21, 1, 36 .— Transf. A union,…

consummātor.opening: consummo , a completer, finisher (eccl. Lat.): novi testamenti (opp. initiator veteris), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 22 al.

consummātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from consummo.

con-summo.opening: v. a. summa (not in use before the Aug. per.; most freq. in Quint.). To cast or sum up. Prop.: sumptus aedificiorum per arithmeticen, Vitr. 1, 1 : numerum, Col. 5, 3, 4 : pretium in assem, id. 3, 3, 8 ; 5, 2, 10 .—…

con-sūmo.opening: ( perf. sync. consumpsti, Prop. 1, 3, 37 ; inf. consumpse, Lucr. 1, 234 ), v. a. , to take wholly or completely , i. e., Lit. In gen. (post-Aug. and rare): vasti surgunt immensis torquibus orbes, tergaque consumunt…

consumptĭbĭlis.opening: adj. consumo , that can be consumed or destroyed, transient (late Lat.): vigor, Cassiod. An. 3 .

consumptĭo.opening: id. . * A consuming, wasting, consumption , Cic. Univ. 6 .—* An employing, bestowing, application, use : operae, Auct. Her. 4, 22, 32 (al. sumptione).

consumptor.opening: id. , a consumer, destroyer (very rare): omnium ignis (connected with confector), * Cic. N. D. 2, 15, 41 .—Of fire, Ambros. in Luc. 7, § 132 .—Of the wasters of their property, spendthrifts , Sen. Exc. Controv. 3, 1, §…

consumptrix.opening: consumptor , she who wastes, consumes (late Lat.): terra omnium corporum, Serv. ad Verg. A. 6, 395 .

con-sŭo.opening: v. a. To sew, stitch , or join together (very rare; mostly ante- and post-class.). Prop.: tunicam, Varr. L. L. 9, § 79 Müll.: lumbulos, Apic. 7, 8 ; 7, 2 ; 8, 7 .— Trop. : consuere dolos, to devise, plan, plot :…

con-supplĭcātrix.opening: supplico , she who supplicates with (rare), Claud. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 66 Müll.; Inscr. Orell. 1501 .

con-surgo.opening: v. n. , to raise one's self, to rise (esp. of a multitude), to rise up together, stand up, arise (class. in prose and poetry). Lit. Of living beings: cum Athenis ludis quidam in theatrum grandis natu venisset ...…

consurrectĭo.opening: consurgo , a standing up (as a sign of assent in public transactions) (rare; perh. only in the foll. exs.): judicum, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 4 : omnium vestrum, id. Har. Resp. 1, 2 .

Consus.opening: perh. from condo , a very ancient deity of Italy, a god of the earth and of agriculture, giver of fertility, presiding over counsels and secret plans : CONSVS. CONSILIO. MARS. DVELLO. LARES. COMITIO. POTENTES., old.…

con-sŭsurro.opening: v. n. , to whisper together : cum aliquo, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 64 .

consūtĭlis.opening: adj. consuo , sewed together : crate praecinctus, Cassiod. Var. 5, 42 .

con-tābĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to waste away, to wear out, consume : aliquem (curā), Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 19 .

con-tābesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to waste away gradually, to be consumed, pine away (very rare). Lit. : cor guttatim contabescit, * Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 92 : Artemisia luctu confecta contabuit, * Cic. Tusc. 3, 31, 75 .—* Trop. : o…

contăbŭlātĭo.opening: contabulo , a joining of boards together, a flooring, planking; a floor or story, a covering of boards (very rare), Caes. B. C. 2, 9 (four times); Vitr. 10, 15, 3 : proscenii, App. Flor. 4, 18 .— Transf. , of garments,…

con-tăbŭlo.opening: v. a. , to furnish or cover with boards (several times in the histt.; elsewh. rare): turres, Caes. B. G. 5, 40 : turres contabulatas machimentaque alia quatiendis muris portabant, i. e. built in stories, Liv. 24, 34, 7…

contactus.opening: 1. contingo (except once in Sall., perh. not ante-Aug.), a touching, touch, contact . In gen., Verg. A. 3, 227 ; Ov. M. 4, 52 ; 11, 111 ; Col. 11, 3, 50 ; Plin. 8, 15, 16, § 40 ; 33, 7, 40, § 122 ; in plur. : viriles,…

contāges.opening: id. , contact, touch (Lucretian), Lucr. 3, 734 ; 4, 337 ; in plur. , id. 6, 280 and 1242.

contāgĭo.grammar: ōnis ii ĭnis f. n. n.
contāgĭo.opening: , and , , (contagium only in poets—and in plur. —and in postAug. prose writers; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 59, 12 ; Non. p. 199, 2 ; Marc. Vict. 1, p. 2469 P.; cf. also colluvio: contamen only in late Lat.) [id.], a…

contāgĭōsus.opening: adj. contagio, II. , contagious (perh. only in Veg.): passio, Veg. Art. Vet. 1, 14, 2 : scabies, id. ib. 5, 70, 1 .

contāmĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. contamen , that may be polluted or defiled : propheta, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 20 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 9, 16.

contāmĭnātĭo.opening: contamino (post-class.). A polluting, contamination, defilement : mulieris, Dig. 48, 5, 2 : expositionis, Arn. 5, 168 .—* Corruption, disease : ventris, Jul. Obseq. Prodig. 89 .

contāmĭnātor.opening: id. , a defiler, polluter (late Lat.): honorum, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 6 : paterni tori, Tert. Pudic. 13 .

contāmĭnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. contamino.

con-tāmĭno.opening: v. a. from stem tag, tango . Orig., to bring into contact, touch . In gen. (very rare): manus quibus contaminatur, Tert. Apol. 17 ; cf.: contaminare, contingere, Gloss. ap. Mai, Auct. Class. VI. p. 518 a.— To bring into…

contārĭi.opening: contus , a kind of soldiers armed with pikes, pike-bearers , κοντοφόροι , Inscr. Grut. 40, 2 and 3.

contātus.opening: contus , a soldier armed with a pike or pole , κοντοφόρος , a kind of troops = contarii, Veg. Mil. 3, 6 fin.

con-technor.opening: v. dep. techna , to devise plots, contrive tricks : vide modo ne illic sit contechnatus quipiam, Plaut. Ps. 4, 6, 34 .

con-tĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cover, to cover up or over (freq. and class.). In gen. Lit. , aliquem or aliquid aliquā re : coria centonibus, Caes. B. C. 2, 10 ; so, locum linteis, Liv. 10, 38, 5 : capita scutis, Auct. B. Afr. 47 fin. ;…

con-tĕmĕro.opening: v. a. , to stain, pollute, defile (very rare): torum dominae, Ov. Am. 2, 7, 18 : manus, Mart. Spect. 10, 2 .

contemnenter.opening: adv., in a contemptuous manner , Non. p. 515, 33 .

contemnĭ-fĭcus.opening: adj. contemno-facio , despising, contemptuous, scornful , Lucil. ap. Non. p. 88, 29 .

con-temno.opening: (also ; cf. Ritschl Prol. ad Plaut. p. 103 ), tempsi (-temsi), temptum (-temtum), 3, v. a. , to consider a person or thing as unimportant or of small value, to value little, esteem lightly, contemn, despise, disdain,…

contempĕrātĭo.opening: contempero , a proper or suitable mixture , Aug. Doctr. Chr. 2, 30 .

con-tempĕro.opening: v. a. , to moderate or temper by mixing (very rare; perh. not ante-Aug.): cantharum mulso, App. M. 10, p. 246, 34 ; so Veg. Art. Vet. 6, 9, 7 ; Marc. Emp. 16 ; Apic. 4, 2 .

contemplābĭlis.opening: adj. contemplor , aiming, taking aim (only in Amm.): dextera, Amm. 30, 5, 16 : artifex, id. 23, 4, 2 .— * Adv. : : ferire aliquid, taking aim, Amm. 20, 7, 9 .

contemplābundus.opening: adj. contemplor , considering or contemplating attentively , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 40 .

contemplātĭo.opening: id. , an attentive considering, a viewing, surveying, contemplation (in good prose). Physical. In gen.: caeli, Cic. Div. 1, 42, 93 : injecit contemplationem super umeros, cast a look over, Petr. 12, 4 .— In partic., an…

contemplātīvus.opening: adj. id. , contemplative, speculative : philosophia (opp. activa), theoretical (formed after the Gr. θεωρητικός ), Sen. Ep. 95, 10 : sapientiae pars, Aug. Civ. Dei, 8, 4: vita, Fulg. Myth. 2, 1 .

contemplātor.opening: id. . * An observer, surveyor : peritissimus, a marksman, Amm. 19, 1, 7 .— A contemplator, an observer (very rare): caeli ac deorum, * Cic. Tusc. 1, 28, 69 : mundi animus, Sen. Cons. ad Helv. 8, 4 : astrorum, App. Flor.…

contemplātrix.opening: contemplator , she who observes or contemplates (very rare): medicina, Cels. praef. 1, prooem. § 91; App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 16, 25 .

contemplātus.opening: contemplor . A consideration, contemplation, observance (very rare, and only in abl. sing. ): mali, Ov. Tr. 5, 7, 66 .—* Regard, respect , Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 1, 5 .

contemplo.opening: v. a. (anteand post-class.; collat. form of contemplor), to survey, behold, observe, consider, contemplate , etc.; freq. in imper. : adspecta et contempla, Epidice, Plaut. Ep. 5, 1, 16 : contempla et templum Cereris ad…

con-templor.opening: (arch. inf. contemplarier, Plaut. Poen. 5, 3, 10 ), v. dep. templum, I. A. (orig. pertaining to the lang. of augury; cf. Varr. L. L. 7, § 9 Müll.), to look at, view attentively, to survey, behold, gaze upon, give…

con-tempŏrālis.opening: adj., contemporary; subst., a contemporary (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Herm. 6 sq. al.

con-tempŏrānĕus.opening: adj. tempus , contemporary; subst., a contemporary : M. Varro et Nigidius Caesari et Ciceroni, Gell. 19, 14 inscr.

con-tempŏro.opening: v. n. id. , to be at the same time, to be contemporary , Tert. Res. Carn. 45 .

contemptē.opening: ( ), adv. , v. contemno, P. a. fin .

contemptĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. contemno , contemptible (post-class.), Dig. 1, 16, 9 ; 21, 2, 37 ; Arn. 4, p. 155 .— Comp. , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 20 .

contemptim.opening: ( ), adv. contemno , contemptuously, with contempt, scornfully (a favorite word of Livy; elsewhere rare): superbiter contemptim conterit legiones, Naev. ap. Non. p. 516, 1 ; imitated: ne nos tam contemptim conteras,…

contemptĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a despising; disregard, contempt, scorn, disdain (in good prose): omnium rerum humanarum contemptio ac despicientia, Cic. Tusc. 1, 40, 95 : fortitudo est dolorum laborumque contemptio, id. Off. 3, 33, 117 ;…

contemptor.opening: ( ), , id. , he who puts small value upon or makes light of a thing, a contemner, despiser (freq. after the Aug. per.; not in Cic. or Hor.): divum Mezentius, Verg. A. 7, 648 ; cf. superūm, Ov. M. 3, 514 : magni Olympi…

contemptrix.opening: ( ), , contemptor , she who puts small value upon a thing, a despiser, contemner (rare; not in Cic.): mea, * Plaut. Bacch. 3, 6, 2 : superūm propago, * Ov. M. 1, 161 .— Of inanimate and abstract subjects: contemptrix…

contemptus.opening: ( ), , contemno , a despising, contemning; contempt, scorn (first freq. since the Aug. per., but esp. so in Quint.; perh. never in Cic., for in Sen. Tranq. 11, 4 , prob. the thought only is Ciceronian). Act., a…

con-tendo.grammar: di, tum, 3 v. a. and n.
con-tendo.opening: v. a. and n. , to stretch, stretch out vigorously, to draw tight, strain . Lit. (rare and mostly poet. ): arcum, Verg. A. 12, 815 ; Ov. M. 6, 286 ; id. R. Am. 435 : tormenta, Sisen. ap. Non. p. 258, 27 ; Cic. Tusc. 2,…

con-tĕnē^brasco.opening: v. inch. [tenebrae; cf. vesperasco], to become or grow very dark , Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 11 .

con-tĕnē^bresco.opening: v. inch. [tenebrae], to grow dark (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Jer. 13, 16 .

con-tĕnē^bro.opening: v. a. id. , to make very dark, to darken (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Haer. 12 ; id. Jejun. 10 ; id. Apol. 2 .

contentē.opening: adv. , v. contineo, P. a. fin .

contentĭo.opening: contendo (acc. to contendo, II.), an eager stretching, a straining, exertion of the powers of body or mind, tension, effort, a vigorous struggling or striving for something, a struggle after (very freq. and in good…

contentĭōsus.opening: adj. contentio , pertaining to contention, contentious, disputatious, headstrong, obstinate, pertinacious (mostly post-class.): contentiosa et pugnax oratio, Plin. Ep. 2, 19, 4 : jurisdictio, Dig. 1, 16, 2 .— Comp. :…

con-tĕrē^bro.opening: v. a. , to pierce or bore through (late Lat.): ossa, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 3 .

Contĕrĕbrŏmĭus.opening: conteroBromius , a humorously-coined epithet for Libya, which Bacchus traversed , i. e. where much wine is pressed , Plaut. Curc. 3, 1, 76 .

contermĭno.opening: v. n. conterminus : alicui, to be a borderer, to border upon; perh. only Amm. 14, 2, 5 ; 23, 6, 45 .

con-termĭnus.opening: adj., bordering upon, neighboring, having a common border (not ante-Aug.; perh. first used by Ovid). Prop. In gen. With dat. : morus fonti, Ov. M. 4, 90 ; 1, 774 ; 15, 315 : stabula ripae, id. ib. 8, 553 : quercus…

conternātĭo.opening: conterno , a placing of three things together (late Lat.), Hyg. Lim. p. 191 Goes.

con-terno.opening: v. a. terni , to put three things together, to make threefold (late Lat.), Hyg. Lim. p. 191 Goes.—Hence, P. a. : , , three years old : vitula conternans, Hier. in Isa. 5, 15, 5 .

con-tĕro.opening: (rarely conterui, App. M. 8, p. 212, 12 ; Ven. Fort. C. 6, 4, 33), trītum, 3, v. a. , to grind, bruise, pound, to crumble, separate into small pieces . Prop. (so freq. in medic. lang.): medium scillae cum aquā ad mellis…

con-terrānĕus.opening: terra , a fellow-countryman (castrense verbum), Plin. praef. § 1 (Codd. Barb. concerraneum = congerronem, which is perh. better; cf. Sillig ad h. l.).

con-terrĕo.opening: v. a. , to terrify greatly, to frighten (not freq. before the Aug. per.; esp. freq. in Livy); constr. with abl. or absol. With abl. : pectora vulgi metu, * Lucr. 2, 623 : loquacitatem nostram vultu ipso aspectuque, *…

conterrĭto.opening: v. freq. a. conterreo , to frighten much or greatly , Coripp. 2, Joann. 54; 88.

contessĕrātĭo.opening: contessero , the contracting of friendship , Tert. adv. Haeret. 20 .

con-tessĕro.opening: v. n. tessera , to contract friendsnip by means of the tesserae, Tert. adv. Haeret. 36 .

contestātĭo.opening: contestor . A jurid. t. t., an attesting, proving by witness, testimony : suprema testamenti, Dig. 28, 1, 20, § 8 ; cf.: verbum (testamentum) compositum a mentis contestatione, Gell. 6, 12, 2 : litis, a formal entering…

contestātĭuncŭla.opening: contestatio , a short speech , Sid. Ep. 7, 3 .

con-testĭfĭcans.opening: Part. [testificor], attesting at the same time , Tert. Testim. Anim. 1 .

con-testor.opening: v. dep. , to take or call to witness . Prop. In gen.: deos hominesque, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 29, § 67 ; cf. deos, Caes. B. G. 4, 25 : caelum noctemque, Cic. Fl. 40, 102 .—Far more freq., In pass. signif.: contestari, to be…

con-texo.grammar: xŭi, xtum, 3 v. a. and n.
con-texo.opening: v. a. and n. Act., to weave, entwine, braid, join together; to interweave, unite, connect (class. in prose and poetry). In gen. Prop.: ut earum (ovium) villis confectis atque contextis homines vestiantur? Cic. N. D. 2,…

contextim.opening: adv. contexo , in a connected manner, connectedly (very rare): luto nidificantes paene contextim, * Plin. 10, 53, 74, § 147 ; Aug. Ep. 112, 15 .

contextĭo.opening: contexo (postclass.). A joining, putting together (opp. resolutio), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 5, 18 .— A preparing, composing : classis, Aus. prooem. Per. lliad: libri, Aug. Civ. Dei, 7, 2: narrationis, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1,…

contextor.opening: id. , one who puts a writing together, a composer, author : codicis, Cod. Th. 1, 1, 6, § 2.

contextus.opening: contexo , a joining or putting together, a connection (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif., and in Quint.). Lit. : corporum, * Lucr. 1, 243 : aedificiorum, the building of, Dig. 39, 2, 15 : ratis, Aus. Per. Odyss. 5…

con-thērŏlĕta.opening: vox hybr., θηρολέτης , a fellow-destroyer of wild beasts , Fulg. Myth. 3, 2 .

con-tĭcĕo.opening: v. n. a strengthened form for taceo , to be silent, be still (late Lat.), Calp. Ecl. 4, 98 ; Lact. 5, 2, 9 ; Hier. in Isa. 1, 1 ; 17, 64 ; cf.: conticeo, σιωπῶ , Gloss. Lab.; v. also conticesco.

contĭcesco.opening: ( , Plaut. Bacch. 4, 5, 28 ; id. Mil. 2, 4, 56 ; Arn. 5 init. ), tĭcŭi, 3, v. inch. , to become still, to cease speaking or sounding (class. in prose and poetry). Lit. : sed conticiscam: nam audio aperiri foris, Plaut.…

contĭcĭnĭum.opening: conticesco, the time when all becomes still; cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 7, and 7, § 79 Müll.; also contĭcĭum, Macr. S. 1, 3, 12 , the first part of the night, the evening , Plaut. As. 3, 3, 95 (quoted in Varr. l. l.); cf.…

contĭger.opening: contus-gero , a spear-bearer, a lancer , Paul. Nol. Carm. 20, 188 .

contignātĭo.opening: contigno, a joining together of beams; hence, concrete , a floor composed of joists and boards; a story, floor , Caes. B. C. 2, 9 ; 2, 15 ; Auct. B. Alex. 1; Vitr. 2, 9 ; Liv. 21, 62, 3 ; Pall. 1, 9, 2 al.

con-tigno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. tignum , to join together with beams, to furnish with beams, joists , or rafters (rare), Caes. B. C. 2, 15 ; Vitr. 1, 5 ; Plin. 9, 3, 2, § 7 .

contignum.opening: contigno , a structure of beams; meton., a piece of flesh with seven ribs , Paul. ex Fest. p. 65, 7 Müll.

contĭgŭus.opening: adj. contingo (not ante-Aug.). Act. (lit. touching; hence), bordering upon, neighboring, contiguous, near; absol. or with dat. : (Pyramus et Thisbe) contiguas tenuere domos, Ov. M. 4, 57 : Cappadoces, Tac. A. 2, 60 :…

con-tĭnĕo.grammar: tĭnŭi, tentum, 2 v. a. and n.
con-tĭnĕo.opening: v. a. and n. teneo . Act., to hold or keep together . In gen. (rare). Lit. (syn.: coërceo, conjungo): contine quaeso caput, Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 26 : quod omnem continet amplexu terram, Lucr. 5, 319 ; cf.: mundus omnia…

con-tingo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to wet, moisten (perh. only in Lucr. and Verg.). Lit. : oras, pocula circum mellis liquore, Lucr. 1, 938 : semina rerum colore, id. 2, 755 : lac parco sale, to sprinkle, Verg. G. 3, 403 : tonsum corpus…

contĭnŭanter.opening: and , advv. , v. 2. continuo fin. , 1. and 2.

contĭnŭātim.opening: adv. 2. continuo , continuously , συνημμένως, συνεχῶς , Vet. Gloss.; Aug. Ep. 112, 20 .

contĭnŭātĭo.opening: id. , a following of one thing after another, an unbroken series, a connection, continuation, succession (in good prose). In gen., with gen. : continuatio seriesque rerum, Cic. N. D. 1, 4, 9 : continuatio immutabilis…

contĭnŭātivus.opening: adj. continuo , serving to connect the discourse, copulative : conjunctiones, Prisc. 16, p. 1027 P.

contĭnŭĭtas.opening: continuus , a connected series, continuation (very rare), Varr. L. L. 8, § 107 Müll.: spinae, Plin. 8, 30, 44, § 105 .

contĭnŭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
contĭnŭo.opening: v. a. and n. continuus . Act., to join together in uninterrupted succession, to make continuous . In space, to join one with another, to connect, unite (class. in prose and poetry; most freq. in pass. ); constr. with…

contĭnŭor.opening: dep. collat. form of continuo (rare and mostly post-class.), to unite one's self to, to join : Marius ostio Liris evehitur, adque Aenariam suos continuatur, Sisenn. ap. Non. p. 93 : inde me commodum egredientem…

contĭnŭus.opening: adj. contineo, II. , joining, connecting with something , or hanging together , in space or time, uninterrupted, continuous . Of space (so mostly Aug. and post-Aug.; cf., however, continue); with dat. or absol . Lit. :…

contĭo.opening: (less correctly ), , contr. from conventio, for which COVENTIO is written in S. C. Bacch.; v. conventio, and cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 43 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 38, 4, and p. 113, 10 Müll. , a meeting, assembly that is…

contĭōnābundus.opening: adj. contionor , proposing something or haranguing in a public assembly (several times in Livy; elsewh. very rare). In a bad sense; with acc. : haec prope contionabundus circumibat homines, Liv. 3, 47, 3 ; 5, 29, 10 .—…

contĭōnālis.opening: adj. contio , belonging to or suitable for an assembly of the people : contionalis prope clamor senatūs, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 5, 1 : genus dicendi, Quint. 8, 4, 1 : officium, id. 3, 8, 14 : hirudo aerarii, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 11…

contĭōnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or suited to an assembly of the people (very rare): populus, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 3, 4 : oratio, Amm. 27, 6, 5 : tibia, Gell. 1, 11, 10 : fistula, id. 1, 11, 10 in lemm .

contĭōnātor.opening: contionor , a haranguer of the people; in a bad sense, a demagogue, a political agitator , Cic. Cat. 4, 5, 9 (opp. animus vere popularis); Front. Ep. ad Ver. 1, p. 171 ; cf.: contionator, allocutor multitudinis, Isid.…

contĭōnor.opening: v. dep. contio . * To be convened or united in an assembly, to form an assembly : nunc illi vos, singuli universos contionantes timent, Liv. 39, 16, 4 .— Far more freq., (Acc. to contio, II.) To deliver an oration…

contĭuncŭla.opening: dim. contio , a short harangue, a trifling speech (only in the foll. passages): oratorem excludi ab omni doctrina, ac tantum in judicia et contiunculas tamquam in aliquod pistrinum detrudi, Cic. de Or. 1, 11, 46 ; id.…

con-tollo.opening: v. a. , to bring together : contollam gradum, will go to meet him ( = contra tollam, Wagn. ad loc.), Plaut. Aul. 5, 6 (ap. Non. p. 82, 1 ).

con-tŏnat.opening: v. impers. , it thunders heavily : ibi continuo contonat Sonitu maximo, Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 45 .

con-torquĕo.opening: (also -torsum, acc. to Prisc. 9, p. 871 P.), 2, v. a. , to turn, twist, twirl, swing, whirl or brandish , etc. (class. in prose and poetry). Lit. Of weapons, arms, etc. (mostly poet. ): telum contortum validis viribus,…

con-torrĕo.opening: v. a. , to dry up entirely, to parch, scorch : herbas, Amm. 18, 7, 4 .

contortē.opening: adv. , v. contorqueo, P. a. fin.

contortĭo.opening: contorqueo . * A whirling round : dexterae, Auct. Her. 4 , 19, 26 fin. — An intertwining, involving; intricacy, complication; of discourse, in the plur. : contortiones orationis, * Cic. Fat. 9, 17 ; Aug. Retract. 1, 50 .

contortor.opening: contorqueo , a wrester, perverter : legum, Ter. Phorm. 2, 3, 27 .

contortŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [contortus], somewhat complicated or intricate : contortulis quibusdam ac minutis conclusiunculis, Cic. Tusc. 2, 18, 42 .

contortŭplĭcātus.opening: ( ), , adj. contortus-plico , entangled, complicated : longa nomina, compounded in a complicated manner, Plaut. Pers. 4, 6, 26 .

contortus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from contorqueo.

contrā.opening: adv. and prep. stem con, i. e. cum, through a comparative form conter; cf.: alter, uter, inter, praeter, etc.; in abl. fem. form like the locative adverbs eā, quā, etc.; cf.: ultrā, intrā, extrā, citrā , orig., in…

contrăbĭum.opening: con-trabs , a framework of beams, a flooring , Cassiod. Var. 12, 18 .

contractē.opening: adv. , v. contraho, P. a. fin.

contractĭo.opening: contraho , a drawing together, contraction (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.). Lit. : contractio et porrectio digitorum, Cic. N. D. 2, 60, 150 : bracchii (opp. projectio), id. Or. 18, 59 : superciliorum (opp.…

contractĭuncŭla.opening: dim. contractio ; trop.: animi, dejection, sadness, Cic. Tusc. 3, 34, 83 .

contractor.opening: contraho, I. B. 2. , one who makes a contract, a contractor , Cod. Just. 5, 5, 8 ; cf. Cod. Th. 10, 6, 3.

contractōrĭum.opening: contraho , a lace, string , σφιγκτήρ , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

contractūra.opening: id.; lit. a drawing together; hence , t. t. in architecture, a lessening, contracting (of pillars), Vitr. 3, 3, 12 ; 5, 1, 3 al.

contractus.opening: contraho . * A drawing together : acinorum, a shrinking, wrinkling, Varr. R. R. 1, 68 .— Trop. An entering upon or transacting of an affair : rei, * Quint. 4, 2, 49 .— Jurid. t. t. (not in Cic.), a contract, agreement :…

contrādīcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. contradico , that may be contradicted or spoken against : signum, Tert. de Carn. Christ. 23 .

contrā-dīco.opening: v. n. , until the post-Aug. per. always written as two words, v. contra, I. B. 9.

contrādictĭo.opening: contradico , a reply, answer, objection, counter-argument (post-Aug.; most freq. in Quint. of judicial replications): ubi contradictioni locus non erit, Quint. 3, 8, 34 ; so id. 3, 8, 27 ; 5, 13, 48 sq.; 7, 3, 20; Sen.…

contrādictor.opening: id. ; in jurid. Lat., one who objects or replies, an opponent , Dig. 40, 11, 27, § 2 ; 40, 16, 3 ; Amm. 31, 14, 3 .

contrādictōrĭus.opening: adj. contradictio , containing an objection or contradiction (late Lat.), Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 8, 1 .

con-trādo.opening: v. a. , to deliver together or wholly (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 8, 23 ; Jornand. 11 al.

contră-ĕo.opening: v. n. , to go against, to oppose, make resistance (late Lat.; earlier written as two words); with dat. : invidiae, Arn. 1 init. : auctoritati, Hier. Ep. 84 ad Magnum.

contrā-factĭo.opening: a setting in opposition, contrast (late Lat. and rare), Cassiod. Complex. Apoc. 3 .

con-trăho.opening: v. a. , to draw or bring several objects together, to collect, assemble (freq. and class.). In gen. Lit. (syn. colligo; opp. dissipo): quae in rerum naturā constarent quaeque moverentur, ea contrahere amicitiam,…

contrā-jūris.opening: adj. 2. jus , contrary to law, unlawful , παράνομος , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

contrā-pōno.opening: no perf. , pŏsĭtum, 3, v. a. , to place opposite, to oppose to (several times in Quint.; elsewh. only in late Lat., and rare): non semper quod adversum est contraponitur, Quint. 9, 3, 84 ; Tert. ad Mart. 4 .— P. a. as…

contrārĭĕtas.opening: contrarius , opposition, contrariety (late Lat.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 14, 26 ; 2, 15, 30 ; Sid. Ep. 4, 12 .

contrārĭus.opening: adj. contra , lying or being over against, opposite . In gen. Prop., of places (syn. adversus): collis adversus huic et contrarius, Caes. B. G. 2, 18 ; cf.: contraria tigna iis (tignis), id. ib. 4, 17, 5 ; and: gemma…

contrascrība.opening: a countersigner, comptroller , = ἀντιγραφεύς , Inscr. Orell. 3208 .

contra-scrībo.opening: v. a. , to countersign , App. Mag. p. 324, 10 .

contrascriptor.opening: contrascribo , a comptroller , = ἀντιγραφεύς : RATIONIS SVMMI CHORAGI, Inscr. Grut. 579, 10 ; Inscr. Orell. 3209 .

contrā-vĕnĭo.opening: v. n. , to oppose (late Lat.); with dat. : humanis ratiunculis falsis, Aug. Civ. Dei , 20, 1, 1.

contrā-versus.opening: Part. [verto] (post-class.), turned opposite, lying over against; with dat. : Africa promontorio Apollinis Sardiniae, Sol. 27 : spiranti Zephy. ro contraversa (urbs) Gumathenam contingit, Amm. 18, 9, 2 .— Adv. : , on…

Contrĕbĭa.opening: a fortified town in Hispania Tarraconensis, in the province of the Carpetani, Liv. 40, 33, 1 sq. ; Flor. 2, 17, 10 ; Val. Max. 2, 7, 10 ; 7, 4, 5 .— , , , its inhabitants , Liv. Epit. 91 .

contrectābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. contrecto , that may be felt or handled (except in Lucr., only in late Lat.): contractabile et solidum corpus, Lact. 2, 8 al. —* Adv. : ( ), so as to be felt , Lucr. 4, 660 .

contrectātĭo.opening: ( ), ōnis. id. , a touching, touch, contact (very rare). Prop.: equae, vaccae, Cic. N. D. 1, 27, 77 : quam contrectationes et amores soluti et liberi, id. Rep. 4, 4, 4 ; cf. Dig. 41, 2, 3, § 18 .— In the jurists, an…

contrectātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a thief (in the jurists), Dig. 47, 2, 36 . § 2.

con-trecto.opening: ( ), , v. a. tracto , to touch, handle, come in contact with, feel (class.; most freq. after the Aug. per.). Lit. In gen.: nudum corpus aquaï, Lucr. 6, 854 : pectora, Ov. M. 8, 607 : omnes partes corporis inspectare et…

con-trĕmisco.opening: v. inch. n. and a. Neutr., to tremble all over, to shake, quake (rare but class.): totā mente atque omnibus artubus, Cic. de Or. 1, 26, 121 ; cf.: toto corpore contremisco, Caecin. ap. Cic. Fam. 6, 7, 4 : contremuere,…

con-trĕmo.opening: v. n. , to tremble greatly, to quake (rare): caelum tonitru contremit, Pac. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 39, 157 (Trag. Rel. v. 413 Rib.): fulminis horribili cum plagā torrida tellus Contremit, Lucr. 5, 1220 .

con-trĕmŭlus.opening: adj., trembling violently : (luna), Varr. ap. Non. p. 351, 27 .

contrībŭlātĭo.opening: contribulo , anguish : spiritus, Tert. adv. Jud. 13 ex Isa. 65, 14.

con-trĭbūlis.opening: Of the same tribus (very rare), Inscr. Fratr. Arv. Marin. p. 43; Inscr. Grut. 873, 4 ; Hier. in Gal. 2, 10 ; Ambros. Ep. 6, 14 fin. —* Transf. , of the same religion , Sid. Ep. 8, 13 .

con-trībŭlo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to crush, bruise (eccl. Lat.): capita draconum, Vulg. Psa. 73, 13 : dorsum ipsorum, id. Ecclus. 35, 22 sq. — Trop. , to afflict much, to crush : sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus,…

con-trĭbŭo.opening: v. a. , to throw together, bring together, unite, incorporate, impart. Of a part added to or united with a whole. In gen. With acc. alone: nec non Penëus, nec non Spercheïdes undae Contribuere aliquid, Ov. M. 7, 231 .—…

contrĭbūtĭo.opening: contribuo (postclass.). A dividing, distributing : debiti et crediti, Dig. 16, 2, 1 : in contributionem venire, ib. 24, 3, 7, § 4 ; 35, 2, 30, § 8 .— A contribution : omnium, Dig. 14, 2, 1 .

contristātĭo.opening: contristo , an afflicting, affliction, grief (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 11 ; id. Pud. 7 al.

con-tristo.opening: v. a. tristis , to make sad or sorrowful, to sadden, afflict (except in Caelius, perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : contristavit haec sententia Balbum, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 9, 5 : prudens ... non perturbatur nec…

contrītĭo.opening: contero , a grinding. Prop., Ennod. 3 med. — Trop. , contrition, grief , = θλίψις (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 7, 18 ; Aug. Conf. 7, 7 ; Vulg. Jer. 30, 15 ; id. Psa. 13, 3 ; 59, 2 al.

contrītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from contero.

contrōversĭa.opening: ( dat. plur. CONTROVORSEIS, C. I. L. 1, 199, 1), controversus , lit., a turning against. * Lit. : si controversia aquae insulam subverterit, the turning of the water against it, Dig. 39, 2, 24, § 5 .— Trop. ,…

contrōversĭālis.opening: adj. controversia , pertaining to controversy or dispute, controversial (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 7, 9 al.

contrōversĭŏla.opening: dim. id. , a little controversy , Hier. in Rufin. 1, 30 ; cf. Diom. p. 313 P.

contrōversĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , very much controverted (very rare): res, Liv. 3, 72, 5 ; Sen. Ep. 85, 24 .

contrōversor.opening: v. dep. controversus , to be at variance one with another, to dispute (very rare): ut inter vos de hujuscemodi rebus controversemini, Cic. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 803 P. (IV. 2, p. 477 Orell.): nihil invicem, Sid. Ep. 4, 1…

contrō-versus.opening: adj. from the same root with contra; q. v. init. . * Lit. , turned against, in an opposite direction (cf. controversia, I.; very rare): perticae, Cato, R. R. 43, 1 : litora Isauriae scopulis, lying opposite, Amm. 14, 2,…

con-trŭcīdo.opening: v. a. , to hew or cut to pieces, to cut down, to put to the sword, slay (rare, but in good prose). Prop.: debilitato corpore et contrucidato se abjecit exanimatus (cf., shortly after, concisum vulneribus), Cic. Sest.…

con-trūdo.opening: v. a. To thrust or crowd together (mostly anteclass.): nubes (vis venti), Lucr. 6, 510 ; cf. id. 6, 211 and 734: penitusque casa contrusa jacebant Corpora, crowded together, id. 6, 1254 .— To press, thrust, push , or…

con-trunco.opening: v. a. , to cut down or to pieces (ante- and post-class. and very rare): filios, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 9, 51 ; cf.: inermes et obsistentes, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 61.—Facete: cibum, Plaut. Stich. 4, 1, 48 : offulam grandiorem,…

contŭbernālis.opening: ( abl. contubernale. Pomp. ap. Charis. p. 99 P., or Com. Rel. v. 73, where Rib. reads contubernaleio; usu. -nali, Macr. S. 2, 4, 29 ; Dig. 40, 7, 31, § 1 ; 50, 16, 220, § 1 ) [contubernium]. Milit. t. t. A…

con-tŭbernĭum.opening: taberna . Abstr. In milit. lang. (cf. contubernalis, I.). Tent-companionship, a dwelling together in a tent : legionum, with the legions, Tac. A. 1, 41 ; id. H. 2, 80 .— Concr., a body of soldiers occupying a tent…

con-tŭĕor.opening: (ante-class. and poet. ; access. form pres. , Plaut. As. 2, 3, 23 ; Stat. Achill. 1, 131 : contuimur, Lucr. 4, 35 ; inf. contui, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 111 ; 3, 1, 20 ; id. Most. 3, 2, 152 ; Pompon. ap. Non. p. 470, 31 ; cf.…

contŭĭtus.opening: or , , contueor , an attentive looking at, a view, sight (rare, and only in abl. sing. ): fugat te ipsum a tuo contutu, * Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 27 ; Curt. 5, 12, 19 ; Plin. 11, 37, 54, § 145 ; 37, 5, 16, § 63 : contuitu…

contŭmācĭa.opening: contumax , perseverance in one's purpose or opinion , generally in a bad sense, arrogance, inflexibility, contumacy, obstinacy, stubbornness . Prop. In gen. (in good prose, and very freq.): illa tua singularis…

con-tŭmax.opening: adj. from the root tem, whence also temno; cf. contemno, and contumelia , insolent, unyielding, obstinate, stiff-necked, stubborn, contumacious. Prop. In gen. (freq. and in good prose): quis contum acior? quis…

con-tŭmēlĭa.opening: (post-class. access. form , Mart. Cap. 4, § 424 ; cf.: contumia contumelia, Gloss. Isid.), , from a root tem, whence also temno, contemno, and contumax; cf. Dig. 47, 10, 1 , abuse, insult, affront, reproach, invective,…

contŭmēlĭōsus.opening: adj. contumelia , full of abuse, reproachful, insolent, abusive (in good prose): partim te superbum esse dicunt, quod nihil respondeas, partim contumeliosum, quod male respondeas, Cic. Fam. 1, 10 : uti beneficio Antonii…

con-tŭmesco.opening: v. n. , to swell greatly : gingivae, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4, 71 .

con-tŭmŭlo.opening: v. a. * To heap up like a mound : ovis stragulum molle pulvere, Plin. 10, 33, 51, § 100 .— To furnish with a mound, to inter, bury : saucium ingestā humo, Ov. Ib. 460 ; cf. id. Tr. 3, 3, 33 ; Mart. 8, 57, 4 .

con-tundo.opening: (tunsum, Plin. 21, 27, 101, § 174 ; 28, 16, 62, § 221 al. ), 3 ( perf. contūdit, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 891 P., or Ann. v. 482 Vahl.; but contŭdit, id. ap. Prisc. l. l., or Ann. v. 387 Vahl.), v. a. , to beat, bruise,…

contŭŏli ŏcŭli.grammar: sunt in angustum coacti conniventibus palpebris
contŭŏli ŏcŭli.opening: , i. e. eyes narrowed by a partial closing of the eyelid , Paul. ex Fest. p. 42, 1 Müll. [contueor].

conturbātĭo.opening: conturbo , disorder, confusion. * Lit. : oculorum, confused, indistinct vision , as a disease, Scrib. Comp. 19 .— Trop. , confusion, disquiet, perturbation of mind (rare): conturbatio metus excutiens cogitata, a fear…

conturbātor.opening: id. , that brings disorder or ruin (cf. conturbo, II.), poet. for ruinous, expensive , or costly (very rare): aper, Mart. 7, 27, 10 : macellus, id. 10, 96, 9 .

conturbātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from conturbo.

con-turbo.opening: v. a. , to throw into disorder or confusion, to confuse, derange, disorder, confound (rare, but class. in prose and poetry; most freq. in Lucr. and Cic.; not in Verg., Hor., or Quint.). In gen. Lit. : posituras…

con-turmālis.opening: one of the same squadron (turma) (late Lat.), Amm. 16, 12, 45 al. — Transf. : omnis operae, a companion, Amm. 17, 1, 2 .

con-turmo.opening: v. a. , to arrange in squadrons (turmae). se, Amm. 16, 12, 37 .

contus.opening: , = κοντός , a pole, pike (perh. not ante-Aug.), as an implement of a boat or ship, Verg. A. 5, 208 ; 6, 302 ; Tac. A. 14, 5 ; Suet. Calig. 32 ; as a weapon, Verg. A. 9, 510 ; Tac. A. 6, 35 ; id. H. 1, 44 .—Prov.: non…

contūsĭo.opening: contundo , a crushing, breaking, battering, bruising (rare). In gen.: olivae, Col. 12, 47, 3 : falcis hebetioris, Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 227 .— In medic. language, a bruise, contusion , Scrib. Comp. 101 ; 165 et saep.

con-tūtor.opening: v. dep. , to place in safety (late Lat.), Vulg. 2 Macc. 1, 19 .

cōnūbĭālis.opening: (less correctly ; in the poets gen. to be read as four syll.; cf. conubium; only in Claud. Ep. 2, 18 , cōnŭbiālis), , adj. conubium , pertaining to wedlock, connubial, conjugal ( poet. ; perh. first used by Ov.): jura,…

cōnūbĭum.opening: (less correctly ; cf. Rib. prol. Verg. p. 393 ), ii (m the poets often trisyl., thus: conubio, Verg. A. 1, 73 ; 4, 126 ; 7, 253 ; Ov. M. 6, 428 : conubia, Lucr. 3, 777 : conubiis, Verg. A. 3, 136 ; 4, 168 ; v. Wagn. and…

cōnus.opening: , = κῶνος , a cone. In gen., Lucr. 4, 430 and 432; Cic. N. D. 1, 10, 24 ; 2, 18, 47 al. — Esp., of conical bodies, The apex of a helmet , Verg. A. 3, 468 ; Ov. M. 3, 108 ; Plin. 10, 1, 1, § 2 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 18, 14, 2…

con-vādor.opening: v. dep. , to bind one to appear in court by giving surely; facete: ubi tu es, qui me convadatus Veneriis vadimoniis, cited me to the court of Venus , i. e. made an appointment with me , Plaut. Curc. 1, 3, 5 .

convălescens.opening: P. a. and subst. , v. convalesco, I. fin.

convălescentĭa.opening: convalesco , convalescence, a regaining of health , Symm. Ep. 3, 11 fin.

con-vălesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to recover from a disease, to regain health, to grow strong, gain strength , etc. (very freq., and class.). Lit. , with ex, de, ab , or absol. : ex morbo, Cic. Fat. 12, 28 sq. ; so id. Fam. 13, 29, 4 ;…

convallātĭo.opening: convallo , an intrenchment , Tert. adv. Jud. 8 .

con-vallis.opening: ( abl. regularly convalle, e. g. Caes. B. G. 3, 20 fin. ; Liv. 1, 12, 10 ; Verg. G. 2, 186 ; id. A. 6, 679 al. : convalli, Varr. R. R. 1, 12, 3 ; gen. plur. convallium, Plin. 36, 15, 23, § 100 ). ( plur. post-class.…

con-vallo.opening: v. a. ; lit., to surround with an intrenchment; hence, in gen., to surround, encircle (late Lat.): terras omnes Oceani ambitu, Gell. 12, 13, 20 . — Trop. , Tert. Carm. de Judicio Dom. 6 .

con-vărĭo.opening: v. a. and n. (post-class.). Act., to variegate : cutim maculationibus, App. Mag. p. 306, 14 .— Neutr., to be different, to vary , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 7 .

con-vāso.opening: v. a. vasa , to pack vessels or implements together, to pack up (the figure taken from milit. lang.; anteand post-class. and very rare). Lit. : aliquid convasassem, * Ter. Phorm. 1, 4, 13 ; so Sid. Ep. 7, 2 .— Trop. :…

convectĭo.opening: conveho , a carrying or bringing together : annonae, Amm. 14, 10, 4 .

convecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to bear, carry , or bring together in abundance (very rare): recentes praedas, Verg. A. 7, 749 ; cf. praedam, id. ib. 4, 405 : ligones, dolabras, etc., e proximis agris, Tac. H. 3, 27 : paleas, ligna,…

convector.opening: conveho , one who carries or brings together; hence, Convector, the deity who presided over the gathering in of grain , Fab. Pict. ap. Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 21 .

con-vector.opening: he who goes with one (on board ship, etc.), a fellow-passenger (very rare), * Cic. Att. 10, 17, 1 ; App. M. 1, p. 109 .

con-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to carry, bear , or bring together (in good prose). In gen.: frumentum ex finitimis regionibus in urbem, Caes. B. C. 1, 34 fin. ; cf. Liv. 25, 13, 2 ; 24, 39, 11 al. : lintribus in eam insulam materiem, calcem,…

con-vello.opening: (convulsi, Sen. Q. N. 2, 6, 4 ), vulsum (volsum), , v. a. To draw violently hither and thither something that is firm or quiet (esp. a tree, house, and the like); hence, to tear up, wrest from its position, to tear…

con-vēlo.opening: v. a. , to veil, to cover over (very rare). Lit. : caput, Gell. 19, 9, 10 .— Trop. : ἐπαγωγήν multis argumentis, Gell. 7, 3, 44 .

convĕna.opening: adj. comm. [convenio], coming together, meeting : ego, qui amantis unā inter se facerem convenas, Plaut. Mil. 2, 1, 61 : aquae, Amm. 23, 3, 8 ; 23, 6, 57 ; Sol. 37 : serpentes, id. 47 : convenā undique multitudine, Amm.…

convĕnĭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from convenio.

convĕnĭenter.opening: adv. , v. convenio, P. a. fin.

convĕnĭentĭa.opening: convenio, II. A. 2. , a meeting together, agreement, accord, harmony, symmetry, conformity, suitableness, fitness (a Ciceronian philosoph. word). With gen. : convenientia naturae cum extis, Cic. Div. 2, 15, 34 ; cf.:…

con-vĕnĭo.opening: ( fut. convenibo, Plaut. Cas. 3, 2, 18 ), v. n. and a. To come together, meet together, assemble (class. and freq.). In gen.: milites, qui ex provinciā convenerant, Caes. B. G. 1, 8 : omnes ... eo convenerant, id. ib.…

conventīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. convenio , pertaining to coming together , or intercourse . * Adj. : patres conventicii, coming from various quarters, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 42 .—* Subst. : , , (sc. aes), = τὸ ἐκκλησιαστικόν , money paid to…

conventĭcŭlum.opening: dim. conventus (rare). An assembly, meeting, association : conventicula hominum, quae postea civitates nominatae sunt, Cic. Sest. 42, 91 : plebei urbanae, id. Dom. 28, 74 .— A place of assembly , Tac. A. 14, 15 : ritus…

conventĭo.opening: convenio , a meeting, assembling . In gen. (very rare), Cod. Th. 8, 8, 3; 16, 2, 14 al.— Esp. = contio, an assembly, meeting (very rare), Varr. L. L. 6, § 87 sq. Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 113, 10 : in conventione =…

conventĭōnālis.opening: adj. conventio, II. B. , of or pertaining to an agreement or compact, conventional : stipulationes, Dig. 45, 1, 5, § 52 .

conventĭuncŭla.opening: dim. conventio, I. , a small assembly , Aug. Ep. 56 fin.

convento.opening: v. freq. n. [convenio], to meet often , Sol. 27, § 7 .

conventus.opening: (CONVENTVVS, C. I. L. II. p. 2416), convenio . (Acc. to convenio, I.) A meeting; in concr., an assembly (syn: coetus, contio, corona). Of persons. In gen. (for social intercourse, counsel, religious celebration,…

con-vĕnusto.opening: v. a. , to ornament, adorn (late Lat.): ecclesiam cultu, Sid. Ep. 7, 12 : aliquid oratione, id. ib. 8, 6 : Aurora primo convenustans habitu fenestras, Mart. Cap. poët. 2, § 219 al.

con-verbĕro.opening: v. a. , to strike severely, to beat, bruise (post-Aug.). Lit. : faciem, Plin. 13, 22, 43, § 126 : os, Curt. 7, 2, 5 .— Trop. : vitia, to chastise, Sen. Ep. 121, 4 ; cf. id. Ira, 3, 20, 1.

con-vergo.opening: v. n. , to incline together (late Lat.): punctus quo cuncta convergunt, Isid. Orig. 3, 12, 1 .

converrĭtor.opening: converro , one who sweeps together , Cat. ap. App. Mag. p. 277, 13 .

con-verro.opening: (or ), , v. a. , to sweep or brush together, to sweep, clear away (mostly ante- and post-class.). Lit. , Cato, R. R. 143, 2 : hoc egomet, tu hoc convorre, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 27 : capiam scopas atque hoc convorram, id.…

conversātĭo.opening: converso (not ante-Aug.). * Frequent use , Sen. Ben. 3, 2, 2 ; cf. Cod. Th. 11, 21, 1 al.— Frequent abode in a place , Plin. 10, 33, 51, § 100 ; Dig. 11, 7, 12, § 1 .— Intercourse, conversation (so most freq.):…

conversātor.opening: a companion , ὁμοδίαιτος , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

conversim.opening: adv. converto , conversely (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 5, § 491 ; Firm. Math. 2, 32.

conversĭo.opening: id. , a turning round, revolving, revolution (class.). Lit. In gen.: caeli, Cic. Div. 2, 42, 89 ; id. Univ. 6 med. ; id. Rep. 6, 18, 18 : astrorum omnesque motus, id. Tusc. 1, 25, 62 ; cf. id. N. D. 2, 19, 49 :…

conversĭuncŭla.opening: conversio , a slight change or alteration (eccl. Lat.), Salv. Ep. 4, p. 320 .

con-verso.opening: v. freq. * Act., to turn round : animus se ipse conversans, * Cic. Univ. 8 med. —More freq., In medial form , (post-Aug.; a favorite word of Seneca; not in Quint.), To abide, live , or dwell somewhere : in montibus…

conversus.opening: converto , a turning or twisting round , Macr. S. 7, 9, § 4 .

convertĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , changeable (post-class.): propositiones, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 33, 1 and 2 (al. conversibilis): deus convertibilis et demutabilis, Prud. Apoth. 344 .—Hence, , adv., changeably (late Lat.), Aug. Music.…

con-verto.grammar: ti, sum, 3 v. a. and n.
con-verto.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n. Act., to turn or whirl round, to wheel about, to cause to turn, to turn back, reverse; and with the designation of the terminus in quem, to turn or direct somewhere, to direct to or towards, to move…

con-vertor.opening: or , , acc. to Non. p. 480 , dep. collat. form of converto; only in the line: sed fugam in se tamen nemo convortitur, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 83 ; but the explanation is not satisfactory, and Fleck. reads: in fugam set tamen…

con-vescor.opening: v. dep. , to eat with one (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 18 al.

con-vestĭo.opening: (arch. inf. pass . convestirier, Poët. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 28, 69 ), v. a. , to clothe, cover with clothing (rare, and mostly in ante-class. poetry). * Lit. : cruenta corpora, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 2 .— Transf. : prata…

con-vĕtĕrānus.opening: a fellow-veteran , Cod. Just. 5, 65, 2 ; Inscr. Orell. 3580 .

convexĭo.opening: convexus , a vaulting, convexity , also concavity (post-class.; cf. convexitas): mundi, Gell. 14, 1, 8 : rotunditatis solidae, Arn. 4, 129 .

convexĭtas.opening: id. , a vaulting, convex roundness, convexity, concavity (postAug.; perh. only in Plin. the elder): circuli, Plin. 18, 25, 57, § 217 : mundi, id. 18, 25, 57, § 210 : cava in caelo, id. 2, 64, 64, § 160 : terrae, id. 18,…

con-vexo.opening: v. a. , to press or squeeze together (post-class., and perh. only in the foll. exs.): (multitudo) me male miseram convexavit, Soror Appii Caeci in Gell. 10, 6, 2 : animal, Veg. Art. Vet. 3, 18, 6 : membra, id. ib. 4,…

con-vī^bro.opening: v. n. and a. * Neutr., to move one's self rapidly : pedibus, Poët. ap. Fest. p. 206, 11 .— Act., to move a thing quickly, set in rapid motion (late Lat.): linguam, App. Flor. 2 , n. 12, p. 348, 40; Amm. 17, 7, 15 .

con-vīcānus.opening: ( , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 11 ), , , one who is of the same village, a fellow-villager , Inscr. Fratr. Arv. p. 436 Marin.; Cod. Th. 11, 24, 6, § 1.

convīcĭātor.opening: ( ), , convicior , a railer, reviler (very rare), * Cic. Mur. 6, 13 ; Sen. Ira, 3, 24, 1 ; Suet. Tib. 11 al.

convīcĭŏlum.opening: dim. convicium , a slight reproach, a taunt , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 28 .

convīcĭor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. id. . to revile, reproach, taunt, rail at (rare; most freq. in Quint.; not in Cic.; cf., however, conviciator). Absol. : cum alius eum salutasset, alius conviciatus esset, * Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 1 : ut…

con-vīcĭum.opening: (less correctly, acc. to Brambach, , but preferred by B. and K., and by recent editors of Plaut. and Ter.), , most prob. kindr. with vox; cf. Dig. 47, 10, 15, § 4; Paul. ex Fest. p. 41, 20 , a loud noise, a cry, clamor,…

convictĭo.opening: convivo , companionship, intercourse, intimacy with one ( = 2. convictus): jucundissima, Cic. Fil. ap. Cic. Fam. 16, 21, 4 .— Transf. , = convictor: convictiones domesticae, Cic. ad Q. Fr. 1, 1, 4, § 12 .

convictor.opening: id. , he who lives with one, a table companion, messmate, familiar friend , Cic. Fil. ap. Cic. Fam. 16, 21, 5 ; Hor. S. 1, 4, 96 ; 1, 6, 47 ; Plin. Ep. 2, 6, 4 ; Sen. Ep. 7, 5 ; id. Ira, 3, 8, 2; id. Lud. Mort. Claud.…

convictus.opening: convivo , a living together, intimacy, social intercourse . In gen. (syn.: societas, consuetudo): convictus humanus et societas, Cic. Off. 3, 5, 21 ; Lucceius ap. Cic. Fam. 5, 14, 3 ; Col. 1, 8, 5 ; Sen. Helv. 15, 2 ;…

con-vinco.opening: v. a. , to overcome, conquer; always beyond the circle of milit. lang. With personal objects, to convict of crime or error, refute (very freq. and class.). With simple acc. : quem ego jam hic convincam palam, Plaut. Am.…

con-vinctĭo.opening: vincio , gram. t. t., a connective particle, conjunction : veteres verba modo et nomina et convinctiones tradiderunt ... in convinctionibus complexus eorum esse judicaverunt; quas conjunctiones a plerisque dici scio,…

con-vĭŏlo.opening: v. a. , to violate, desecrate (eccl. Lat.), Prud. Psych. 398 al.

con-vĭresco.opening: v. inch. , to grow green, become verdant (late Lat.): litus insertis arboribus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 3, 58 .

con-viscĕro.opening: v. a. , to incorporate, unite , Tert. Carn. Chr. 20 .

con-vīso.opening: v. a. (rare and mostly ante-class.), to consider attentively, look at, examine thoroughly : omnia loca oculis, Lucr. 2, 357 : penitus res occultas, id. 1, 146 : omnes saucios, Att. ap. Non. p. 398, 4 (Trag. Rel. v. 598…

con-vĭtĭo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to attack or injure at the same time (late Lat.): si sternutamento fuerint convitiati (of epileptics), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 22 .

con-vīva.opening: vivo (lit., one who lives with another; hence), one who feasts with another, a table companion, guest (freq. and class.). Masc. , Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 50 ; Ter. Eun. 3, 1, 17 ; id. Heaut. 1, 1, 120 ; Afran. ap. Non. p.…

convīvālis.opening: (access. form , Curt. 6, 2, 6 Zumpt N. cr.; as var. lect. in Liv. 39, 6, 8 , and Macr. S. 2, 1 ), , adj. convivium , of or pertaining to a feast, festal, convivial (rare; not ante-Aug.): oblectamenta ludionum, Liv. 39,…

convīvātor.opening: convivor , he who gives an entertainment, the master of a feast (rare), * Hor. S. 2, 8, 73 ; Liv. 35, 49, 6 ; Sen. Ira, 3, 37, 3 .

convīvĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to quicken together , Vulg. Eph. 2, 5 ; id. Col. 2, 13 .

con-vīvĭum.opening: vivo ; lit., a living together; hence, a meal in company, a social feast, entertainment, banquet (freq. and class.): bene majores nostri accubitionem epularem amicorum, quia vitae conjunctionem haberet, convivium…

con-vīvo.opening: v. n. (post-Aug.). To live with : avaro, Sen. Ep. 104, 20 : gladiatoribus, Lampr. Comm. 2 : MECVM, Inscr. Marm. Pisaur. p. 42, n. 94; cf. Inscr. Marini Atti, p. 38.— For convivor, to eat, feast , or banquet together ,…

convīvor.opening: v. dep. ( act. access. form convivas, Titin. ap. Non. p. 314, 17 (Com. Rel. v. 89 Rib.): convivat, Enn. ib. p. 474, 23 : convivant, Pompon. ib. p. 21 (Com. Rel. v. 85 Rib.): convivare, Petr. 57, 2 ) [convivium], to…

convŏcātĭo.opening: convoco , a convoking, calling , or assembling together : populi Romani, Cic. Red. in Sen. 15, 38 .

convōcĭum.opening: , a supposed form to explain the etym. of convicium, Dig. 47, 10, 15, § 4 , and Paul. ex Fest. p. 41, 26 .

con-vŏco.opening: v. a. , to call together, to convoke, assemble; to call (esp. for consultation, to arms, etc.; class.; freq. in Cic. and the histt.). Lit. : qui dissipatos homines congregavit et ad societatem vitae convocavit, Cic.…

con-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly or flock together; hence, to come hastily together, to run together . Lit. (rare but class.): populus convolat, * Ter. Hec. prol. alt. 32: statim, Cic. Tusc. 3, 21, 50 : causa, in quā furiae concitate…

convŏlūto.opening: , no perf. , , v. freq. a. convolvo , to whirl or roll round rapidly (very rare): cum omni exoletorum turbā, Sen. Ep. 114, 24 ( id. Q. N. 7, 9, 2 , the true read. is conluctatus, Haase, Fickert).

con-volvo.opening: v. a. , to roll together, roll up, roll round (first freq. in the post-Aug. per., esp. in Pliny the elder). Lit. : ignis semina convolvunt venti, Lucr. 6, 200 sq. : se sol, Cic. Div. 1, 23, 46 : lubrica terga coluber,…

convolvŭlus.opening: convolvo . A caterpillar that wraps itself up in a leaf , Gr. ἴψ , Cato, R. R. 95, 1 ; Plin. 17, 28, 47, § 264 .— A plant, bind-weed , Plin. 21, 5, 11, § 24 .

con-vŏmo.opening: v. a. , to bespew, vomit upon (perh. only in the foll. exs.): mensas hospitum, * Cic. Phil. 2, 30, 76 : maritum, * Juv. 6, 101 .

con-vŏro.opening: v. a. , to eat up, devour : cadavera, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 1 .

con-vŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to devour together : NEVE COMVOVISE, S. C. Bacch. 13 (v. Wordsworth, Fragm. and Spec. p. 172).—Here belongs also: convoti iisdem votis obligati, Paul. ex Fest. p. 42, 8 .

con-vulnĕro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to wound severety (post-Aug.). Lit. : eo magis convolneraberis et confodieris, quia nescis praebere jugulum, Sen. Tranq. 11, 5 ; Plin. Pan. 35, 3 : jumenta, Curt. 5, 13, 17 : os (apes), Plin. 8, 36, 54, §…

con-vulsĭo.opening: ( ), , convello , in medic. lang., cramp, convulsion , Scrib. Comp. 165 ; Plin. 20, 15, 60, § 168 ; 29, 3, 13, § 55 .

cŏnȳza.opening: , = κόνυζα , a plant , of two kinds: the male, the viscous elecampane : Inula viscosa, Linn.; called also cunila bubula, Plin. 19, 8, 50, § 165 ; the female, fleabane : Inula pulicaria, Linn.; Plin. 21, 10, 32, § 58 ;…

cŏ-ŏdĭbĭlis.opening: adj., exceedingly hateful, detestable (eccl. Lat.): haeretici, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 9 ; 4, 36 .

cŏ-ŏpĕrātĭo.opening: co-operation , Quint. Decl. 16 fin. ; Cassiod. Complex. Tit. 1 .

cŏ-ŏpĕrātor.opening: a joint-laborer, co-operator (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Ep. 143, 1 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 16, 5 fin. ; Vulg. Phil. 2, 25 ; id. 3 Joan. 8 .

cŏ-ŏpercūlum.opening: a cover, lid (very rare), Plin. 23, 6, 58, § 109 ; App. M. 6, p. 181, 39 ; Pall. Jun. 7, 9 .

cŏ-ŏpĕrĭmentum.opening: a covering : personae, Bassus ap. Gell. 5, 7, 2 .

cŏ-ŏpĕrĭo.opening: (contr. form coperiunt, Lucr. 6, 491 ; cf. Lachm. ap. Lucr. 2, p. 134 sq. ), v. a. , to cover wholly, to cover, cover over, overwhelm (class.; most freq. in part. perf. ). Lit. Verb finit. : Cyrsilum quendam lapidibus…

cŏ-ŏpĕror.opening: v. dep. , to work with or together, combine, unite (late Lat.): praedicaverunt ubique, Domino coöperante, Vulg. Marc. 16, 20 ; Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 9, 19 .— Transf. , of things: quoniam fides coöperabatur operibus ejus,…

cŏŏpertōrĭum.opening: a cover , Dig. 34, 2, 38 ; Veg. Art. Vet. 3, 77, 5 .
