cŏoptātĭo.opening: co-opto , an election, choice : collegiorum, Cic. Lael. 25, 96 : censoria, id. Leg. 3, 12, 27 : in Patres, i. e. a confirmation by the Senate of Senators nominated by the king, Liv. 4, 4, 7 Weissenb. ad loc.; Flor. 4, 4…

cŏ-opto.opening: ( perf. subj. coop tassint, old formula in Liv. 3, 64, 10 ; contr. form , Cic. Fam. 3, 10, 9 ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 135 ), v. a. ; publicists' t. t., to choose or elect to something, to admit or re ceive into some…

cŏ-ŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. , to come forth, stand up, arise, appear, rise, break forth (class. in prose and poetry; most freq. in Lucr. and the hist., esp. Liv.; in Cic. rare, perh. only once). In gen.: ubi materiaï Ex infinito sunt…

cŏortus.opening: coorior , a rising, originating : maris et terrae solisque, Lucr. 2, 1106 : graviore coortu, id. 6, 672 .

cōpa.opening: ( ), , copo = caupo , a female tavern-keeper and castanet-dancer , who exhibited her arts in her ale-house (cf. crotalum), Verg. Cop. 1 Heyne and Wagner: matronae copas imitantes, Suet. Ner. 27 .

Cōpae.opening: , = Κῶπαι , an ancient town in Bœotia , now Topolia , Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 26 ; on the Copais palus, the large Copais lake, which was named after it, Liv. 33, 29, 6 .

Cŏphes.opening: , or , ( acc. Copheta or Cophen), , a river, a tributary of the Indus . Form Cophes, Plin. 6, 17, 21, § 62 ; 6, 20, 23, § 78 .— Form Cophen, Mel. 3, 7, 1 .

cŏphĭnus.opening: , = κόφινος , a basket , Col. 11, 3, 51 ; Juv. 3, 14 ; 6, 542 al. ; cf. Isid Orig. 20, 9, 9.

cōpĭa.opening: co-ops , abundant power, wealth, riches, abundance (very freq. in all periods and species of composition). Of material objects. Of possessions, resources, wealth, supplies, riches, prosperity (syn.: divitiae, opes; opp.…

Cōpĭa.opening: The goddess of abundance , Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 46 : bona, Ov. M. 9, 88 : opulenta, Hor. C. 1, 17, 16 ; id. C. S. 60 al. — An appellation of the town Lugdunum (Lyons), in Gaul, Inscr. Orell. 194 ; 2325 .— Hence, COPIENSIS,…

cōpĭārĭus.opening: 1. copia , a purveyor , = parochus (late Lat.), Schol. ad Hor. S. 1, 5, 46 .

cŏpĭāta.opening: or , , , = κοπιάτης , a grave-digger, sexton (eccl. Lat.), Cod. Th. 7, 20, 12, § 2; 13, 1, 1; 16, 2, 15, § 1.

cōpĭŏlae.opening: dim. 1. copia, I. B. 2. , a small number of troops , Brut. ap. Cic. Fam. 11, 13, 2 .

cōpĭor.opening: v. dep. 1. copia ; milit. t. t. (cf. Gell. 17, 2, 9 ), to furnish or provide one's self abundantly with something: Romani multis armis et magno commeatu praedāque ingenti copiantur, Quadrig. ap. Gell. l. l., and Cael.…

cōpĭōsus.opening: adj. 1. copia . Furnished abundantly with a thing, well supplied, having abundance, rich, copious, plentiful, abounding (in wealth, means of living, etc.) (very freq. and class., esp. in prose). In gen.; constr. with…

cōpis.opening: (acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, § 92 Müll. N. cr. , more prob. than cops, assumed by Prisc. p. 752 P. The nominative in neither form is found in use), , adj. contr. from coops; cf. inops (ante-class. for the class. copiosus),…

cŏpis.opening: , = κοπίς , a short sword , Curt. 8, 14, 29 ; App. M. 11, p. 260, 33 dub. (MSS. crepides).

Cōpōnĭus.opening: the name of a plebeian family at Rome , e. g. the two brothers, T. and C. Coponii, Cic. Cael. 10, 24 ; id. Balb. 23, 53 .—Hence, , , adj., of or pertaining to Coponius , Cic. Att. 12, 31, 2 .

coprĕa.opening: , = κοπρίας , a low buffoon, a filthy jester (post-Aug.), Suet. Tib. 61 ; id. Claud. 8 ; cf. Dio Cass. 50, 28.

copta.opening: , = κόπτη , a kind of cake made of pounded materials , Mart. 14, 68 .— The same, or a similar kind, called , Petr. 40, 4 ; Vesp. Judic. 46 (ap. Wernsd. Poët. Lat. Min. II. p. 234).

Coptŏs.opening: , = Κοπτός, Κοπτώ , a trading town in the Thebaid, on the eastern side of the Nile , afterwards Justinianopolis , now Coft , Plin. 5, 9, 11, § 60 ; Juv. 15, 28 ; Amm. 22, 16, 2 ; Itin. Ant. p. 165, 6 al.—Hence, , , adj.…

cōpŭla.opening: (contr. form , in Wernsd. Poët. Lat. Min. IV. p. 535), coapio , that which binds together or binds fast, a band, rope, thong, tie (rare; not in Cic.). Lit. : tortae, ship's rigging , Att. ap. Non. p. 200, 33 (Trag. Rel.…

cōpŭlābĭlis.opening: adj. copulo , that can be connected (eccl. Lat.): pedes, Aug. Music. 4, 16 med.

cōpŭlātē.opening: adv. , v. copulo, P. a. fin.

cōpŭlātim.opening: adv. copulo , in union , Diom. p. 402 P.

cōpŭlātĭo.opening: id. , a coupling, joining, connecting, uniting (several times in Cic. and Quint.). Prop.: atomorum inter se (with complexiones and adhaesiones), Cic. Fin. 1, 6, 19 ; cf.: copulatio rerum et coagmentatio naturae, id. N.…

cōpŭlātīvus.opening: adj. copulo , of or pertaining to connecting, copulative (late Lat.): modus, Cod. Just. 6, 38, 4 : conjunctiones, Mart. Cap. 3, § 286 , and other gramm. —* Adv. : , connectedly : dicere (diequinti), Macr. S. 1, 4 med.

cōpŭlātor.opening: id. , a connecter, binder (late Lat.), Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 7 .

cōpŭlātrix.opening: copulator , she who couples, connects (late Lat.): amorum, Auct. Perv. Ven. 5; Aug. Trin. 11, 9 fin.

cōpŭlātus.opening: copulo (only in abl. sing.), a connecting or joining together : rationum consequentium, Arn. 1, p. 2 .

cōpŭlo.opening: ( part. perf. , contr. cōplata, Lucr. 6, 1088 ; dep. collat. form , , v. I. A. b. infra), v. a. copula , to couple, bind , or tie together, to join, connect, unite (class.; most freq. in Cic.). Lit. In gen. With cum :…

cōpŭlor.opening: v. dep. , v. copulo, I. A. b.

cŏqua.opening: coquus , a female cook , Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 38 .

cŏquĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. coquo , that can be easily cooked : caro, Plin. 16, 6, 8, § 25 .

cŏquīnārĭus.opening: adj. coquina , of or pertaining to the kitchen, culinary (rare): vasa, Plin. 33, 11, 49, § 140 .—As the title of a work of Apicius, De arte coquinaria.— Access. form , , adj. : culter, a kitchen-knife , Varr. ap. Non.…

cŏquīnātōrĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or pertaining to the kitchen (late Lat.): instrumentum, Dig. 34, 2, 19, § 12 : vasa, ib. 33, 9, 6 .—Hence, subst. : COCINATORIVM, a kitchen, Inscr. Orell. 1359 .

cŏquīno.opening: v. a. coquinus , to perform the office of a cook , perh. only Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 64 ; 3, 2 ; 85 Lorenz with MSS. (Fleck. in both passages coquitare, ex conj.; cf. coquito); id. Aul. 3, 1, 3 Wagn., Ussing; cf. Non. p. 85,…

cŏquīnus.opening: adj. coquo , of or pertaining to cooking (rare): forum, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 1 and 2.— Subst. : , , A kitchen , Pall. 1, 37, 4 ; Arn. 4, p. 130 ; Non. p. 55, 18 .— The art of cooking, cookery , App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 17, 4…

cŏquĭtāre.opening: , used by Plaut. acc to Paul. ex Fest. p. 61, 18 Müll.: pro coctitare id est frequenter coquere: an tu coquitatum te ire quoquam postulas? Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 64 Fleck.; 3, 2, 85; v. coquino.

cŏquĭtātĭo.opening: coquito , a continuous cooking : diutina, App. M. 4, p. 152 .

cŏquo.opening: v. a. kindr. with Sanscr. pak; Gr. πεπ in πέπτω or πέσσω; Germ. backen; Engl. bake , to cook, to prepare by cooking, to bake, boil, roast, parch, steep, melt, heat (very freq. and class.). Lit. : cenam, Plaut. Aul. 3,…

cŏquus.opening: (ante-class. ; in many MSS. and inscrr. also ), , , a cook (very freq., esp. in Plaut., in whose comedies the cook takes a conspicuous place), Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 11 ; Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 26 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 14, 3 ; Cic. Rosc.…

cor.opening: (ŏ, e. g. Ov. Tr. 5, 8, 28 ; id. P. 1, 3, 32 ), cordis ( gen. plur. cordium, Vulg. Jer. 4, 4 , and 1 Cor. 4, 5; acc. to Fragm. Bob. Nom. et Pron. p. 132, also cordum, but without example), kindr. with Sanscr. hrid; Gr.…

cŏra.opening: , = κόρη (v. Lidd. and Scott in h. v. III.), the pupil of the eye , Aus. Ep. 16, 59 .

Cŏra.opening: , = Κόρα , an ancient town of Latium, in the territory of the Volsci , now the village Cori , in the Campagna di Roma , Liv. 2, 16, 8 ; 2, 22, 2 ; Verg. A. 6, 775 ; Luc. 7, 392 .— , its inhabitants , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 63…

cŏrăcēsĭa.opening: κόραξ , a magical herb said to make water freeze , Plin. 24, 17, 99, § 156 .

cŏrăcĭcus.opening: adj. κόραξ , of or belonging to the raven; only as subst. : , , (sc. sacra), the mysteries of Mithras , Inscr. Orell. 2343 .

cŏrăcĭno.opening: v. n. id. , to caw, croak , κρίιζειν , Isid. Orig. 12, 7, 43 .

cŏrăcĭnus.opening: , a. , adj. , = κοράκῖνος , raven-black : color, Vitr. 8, 3, 14 ; so absol. , coracinum, Dig. 32, 1, 78, § 5 (al. croconum).

cŏrăcīnus.opening: , = κορακῖνος , a species of river fish , esp. in the Nile, Plin. 9, 16, 24, § 57 ; 9, 18, 32, § 68 ; Mart. 13, 85 al.

cō^rā^lĭum.opening: or ( , Sid. Carm. 11, 110 ), , , = κοράλλιον ; Ion. κουράλιον , coral , esp. red coral , Plin. 32, 2, 11, § 21 sq. : curalium, id. 32, 2, 11 , §§ 21 and 22: coralium, Ov. M. 4, 750 ; 15, 416 ; plur. : coralia, Claud.…

Cŏralli.opening: a people of Lower Mœsia, on the Danube, on the coast of the Black Sea , Ov. P. 4, 2, 37 ; 4, 8, 83 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the Coralli : pelagus, Cassiod. Var. 6 .

cŏrallĭnus.opening: adj. κοράλλιον , coral-red : labra, Poëta in Anth. Lat. 1, p. 651 Burm.

cŏrallis.opening: , = κοραλλίς , a precious stone , unknown to us, Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 154 .

cō^rallītĭcus.opening: adj. : lapis, a kind of white marble found in Asia Minor, Plin. 36, 8, 13, § 62 ; Isid. Orig. 16, 5, 9 .

cōram.opening: adv. and prep. prob. kindred with ōs, ōris . Object., in the presence of, before the eyes of, in the face of, before (freq. and class.). Adv. : vereor coram in os te laudare amplius, Ter. Ad. 2, 4, 5 : omnia quae tute…

cŏramblē.opening: , = κοράμβλη , a kind of cabbage injurious to the eyes , Col. 10, 178 .

cŏrax.opening: , = κόραξ , a raven , Sol. 40 ; ls id. Orig. 12, 7, 43 .— Meton. , in milit. lang., a hooked engine of war, a battering-ram (called in pure Latin corvus), Vitr. 10, 13, 7 .

corbĭcŭla.opening: dim. corbis , a little basket , Pall. Febr. 10, 6 .

Corbĭo.opening: Masc., a Roman surname : Hortensius Corbio, Val. Max. 3, 5, 4 . — Fem., a town of the Æqui, in Italy , Liv. 2, 39, 4 ; 3, 28, 10 .— A town of Spain, in the territory of the Suessetani, near the modern Berga , Liv. 39,…

corbis.opening: ( abl. regularly corbe: corbi, Cato, R. R. 136 twice), corbes dicti quod curvatis virgis contexuntur, Isid. l. l.; but more prob. kindr. with κόλπος , a basket (esp. for use in gathering fruits, etc.). Masc. , Auct. B.…

corbītus.opening: adj. corbis , with a scuttle, bower : navis, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 533, 18 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a slowsailing ship of burden : corbitae dicuntur naves onerariae, quod in malo earum summo pro signo corbes solerent…

corbōna.opening: Syrian , a treasurechamber , Hier. Ep. 27, 14 ; Vulg. Matt. 27, 6 .

corbŭla.opening: dim. corbis , a little basket , Cato, R. R. 11, 5 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 15 ; id. L. L. 5, § 139 ; Col. 12, 50, 8 ; Plaut. Aul. 2, 7, 4 ; Caecil. ap. Non. p. 197, 29 ; Suet. Ner. 19 al.

corcholopis.opening: a kind of ape having a tuft of hair at the end of its tail , Fest. p. 54 (where Lindem. reads cercolips, contr. to all MSS.; Müll. cercolopis).

corchŏros.opening: or , , , = κόρχορος , a poor kind of pulse, growing wild : Corchorus olitorius, Linn.; Plin. 21, 32, 106, § 183 ; 25, 13, 92, § 144 .

corcillum.opening: dim. corculum , a little heart : corcillum est quod homines facit, cetera quisquilia omnia, Petr. 75 .

Corcŭlum.opening: dim. cor , a little heart , Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 70 ; as a term of endearment, id. Cas. 4, 4, 14 .—As a surname of Scipio Nasica, on account of his sagacity , Cic. Tusc. 1, 9, 18 ; id. Brut. 20, 70 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill.…

corcus.opening: , i. , a disease of the chest , Marc. Emp. 21 dub.

Corcȳra.opening: (ў, Avien. Perieg. 663 ), , , = Κέρκυρα . An island in the Ionian Sea, opposite Epirus; in fable, Scheria, the abode of Alcinous , now Corfu , Mel. 2, 7, 10 ; 4, 12, 19 ; Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 52 sq. ; Cic. Fam. 16, 7…

cordātus.opening: adj. cor, II. B. , wise, prudent, judicious, sagacious (mostly anteand post-class.): egregie cordatus homo, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 9, 18 (Ann. v. 335 Vahl.); cf. Cic. Rep. 1, 18, 30 ; Sen. Lud. Mort. Claud. 12, 2, v. 7…

cordax.opening: , = κόρδαξ , the extravagant dance of Grecian comedy, distinguished by lively movement and wanton gesture, and by the rope which was kept passing through the hands of the dancers; the imitation of this dance was…

cordĭcĭtus.opening: adv. cor , from the heart, deep in the heart , Sid. Ep. 4, 6 .

cor-dŏlĭum.opening: dolor , sorrow at heart, grief (ante- and post-class.), Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 67 ; id. Poen. 1, 2, 86 ; App. M. 9, p. 226, 28 .

Cordŭba.opening: , = Κορδύβη , a town in Hispania Baetica, on the river Bætis , now Caes. B. C. 2, 19 al. — , , adj., of Corduba , Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 7 ; 34, 2, 2, § 4 ; Auct. B. Alex. 57.—Hence. , , , the inhabitants of Corduba , Auct.…

Cordŭēna.opening: , = Γορδυηνή , a district of Greater Armenia , now Kurdistan , Amm. 16, 8, 20 al. —Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Corduena , now the Kurds , Sall. H. 4, 60 Dietsch; Plin. 6, 15, 17, § 44 ; Sext. Ruf. Brev. 20 .—Called…

cordȳla.opening: , = κορδύλη , the fry of the tunny-fish , Plin. 9, 15, 18, § 47 ; Mart. 3, 2, 4 .

Corfīdĭus.opening: a Roman proper name , Cic. Lig. 11, 33 .

Corfīnĭum.opening: , = Κορφίνιον , a very strongly fortified town of the Peligni, north of Sulmo , now Pelino , Cic. Att. 8, 3, 7 ; Caes. B. C. 1, 15 sq. ; Luc. 2, 478 al. — Hence, , , adj., of or pertaining to Corfinium : clementia, i.…

corgo.grammar: apud antiquos pro adverbio, quod est profecto, ponebatur

Cŏrĭa.opening: , = Κορία , a name of the fourth Minerva, among the Arcadians , Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 59 .

cŏrĭăcĕus.opening: adj. corium , of leather : naves, made of leather, Amm. 24, 3, 11 .

cŏrĭāgĭnōsus.opening: adj. coriago , afflicted with the coriago (late Lat.; perh. only in Veg.): equi, Veg. Art. Vet. 2, 10, 2 ; 2, 16, 1 .

cŏrĭāgo.opening: corium , a disease of the skin of animals , Col. 6, 13, 2 ; Veg. Art. Vet. 4, 12, 1 ; 5, 3, 1 .

cŏrĭandrum.opening: or , , ; also , , κορίαννον , coriander : Coriandrum sativum, Linn.; Cato, R. R. 157, 6 sq. ; Col. 6, 33, 2 ; 11, 3, 29 ; Plin. 19, 7, 35, § 117 sq. ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 103 Müll.; Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 25 ; Apic. 4, 3, § 174…

cŏrĭārĭus.opening: adj. corium , of or pertaining to leather frutex, i. e. useful for tanning leather , Plin. 24, 11, 54, § 91 .— Hence, Subst. : , , , a tanner, currier , Plin. 17, 9, 6, § 51 ; Inscr. Orell. 4074 al.

corruptrix.opening: ( ), , corruptor , she that corrupts or seduces; or adj., corrupting (very rare): tam depravatis moribus, tam corruptrice provinciā, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 1, 6, § 19 : licentia, rerum corruptrix et morum, Amm. 25, 3, 18 .

corruptus.opening: ( ), , Part. and P. a. , from corrumpo.

cor-ruspor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. , to search carefully after , = conquiro, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 62 Müll.

corsae.opening: , = κόρσαι ; in arch., the outer strip in the moulding about a door, a girder, Vitr. 4, 6, 3 sq.

Corsĭca.opening: ( , , Prisc. Perieg. 470 ), (among the Greeks, Κύρνος, Κορσίς ), the island Corsica, in the Mediterranean Sea, renowned in ancient times for the honey and wax of wild bees; the place of banishment of Seneca the…

corsŏīdes.opening: , = κορσοειδής (hairlike), an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 153 .

cortex.opening: and rar. (cf. Quint. 1, 5, 35 ) [Sanscr. kart, to cut, split; Gr. κείρω ; cf. culter], the bark, rind, shell, hull. Prop., of plants: obducuntur libro aut cortice trunci, Cic. N. D. 2, 47, 120 . In gen. Masc. , Varr.…

cortĭcātus.opening: adj. cortex , covered with a bark (very rare): pars (sarmenti), Pall. Mart. 1, 2 : pix, resin taken from a tree with a portion of the bark, Col. 12, 23, 1 .

cortĭcĕus.opening: adj. id. , of bark or cork , Varr. R. R. 1, 40 ; 3, 16 ; Plin. 11, 21, 24, § 71 (cortice, Sillig); Aus. Mos. 246 al.

cortĭcōsus.opening: adj. id. , abounding in bark : radix, Plin. 20, 19, 78, § 205 : tus, id. 12, 14, 32, § 59 .

cortĭcŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a small or thin rind, bark , or shell , Col. 12, 47, 10 ; 12, 50, 10 .

cortīna.opening: a round vessel, a kettle, caldron (for cooking, liquids, etc.), Cato, R. R. 66, 1 ; Plin. 15, 6, 6, § 22 al. ; 36, 26, 65, § 191 ; Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 12 .— In partic., the tripod of Apollo, in the form of a caldron ,…

cortīnāle.opening: cortina , the caldron-room, the place where new wine was boiled down in the cortina, Col. 1, 6, 19 .

Cortīnĭ-pŏtens.opening: adj. id. , powerful on the tripod , an epithet of Apollo, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 258, 33 .

cortīnŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small kettle , Amm. 29, 1, 31 dub. (v. Wagner ad h. l.).

Cortōna.opening: a very ancient town in Etruria, northwest of Lake Trasimenus , Liv. 9, 37, 12 ; 22, 4, 1 .—Hence, , , adj., of Cortona : montes, Liv. 22, 4, 2 .— , its inhabitants , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 52 .

cortumio.opening: , an old word of the augurial lang., perh. equiv. to contumio, from contueor, Varr. L. L. 7, § 9 Müll.

Cortȳnia.opening: ( ), , , a town of Crete , Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 6 ; cf. Gortyna.

Cŏruncānĭus.opening: name of a Roman plebeian gens, Cic. Planc. 8, 20 ; id. Brut. 14, 55 ; Liv. 1, 38 ; Tac. A. 11, 24 ; Sen. Vit. Beat. 21, 3 ; id. Ep. 114, 13 .

cŏruscāmen.opening: corusco , a glittering, a flash (post-class.), App. de Deo Socr. p. 226 Bip.

cŏruscātĭo.opening: id. , a glittering, a flash, coruscation (post-class.): (margaritarum), Sol. 53 fin. : immanis, Vop. Car. 8 .

cŏruscĭfer.opening: adj. coruscusfero , lightning-bearing (post-class.): caelum, Mart. Cap. 8, § 808 .

cŏrusco.opening: v. a. and n. (the access. form conisco is found in some copies of Lucr. 2, 320 , and Cic. Fragm. ap. Quint. 8, 3, 21 ) [root scar-, to leap; Gr. σκαίρω ; cf. also κορύσσω ; v. Lidd. and Scott, s. v.]. To thrust or push…

cŏruscus.opening: adj. corusco, II. ( poet. ). In waving motion, waving, vibrating, tremulous : silvae, Verg. A. 1, 164 : ilices, id. ib. 12, 701 .—Humorously: omnia corusca prae tremore fabulor, i. e. trembling, Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 42 .—…

corvīnus.opening: adj. corvus , of or pertaining to the raven, raven- : ovum, Plin. 10, 12, 15, § 32 : nigredo, App. M. 2, p. 118, 31 .— , , , a surname in the gens Valeria; cf. Gell. 9, 11 ; Flor. 1, 13, 20 Duker.

corvus.opening: root kar-, kal-, to sound; cf.: καλέω, κόραξ, etc. , a raven , Plin. 10, 43, 60, § 121 sq. ; acc. to the fable, orig. white, changed to a black bird in punishment for treachery, Ov. M. 2, 541 sq. ; on account of its…

Cŏrўbas.opening: , = Κορύβας . Plur. : , , ( sing. Corybas, Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 148 al. ), = Κορύβαντες , the priests of Cybele, whose religious service consisted in noisy music and wild armed dances , later interchanged with Curetes…

cōrўcēum.opening: , = κωρυκεῖον , the place in the palæstra where the athletae exercised themselves by striking a suspended sack filled with fig-grains, flour, sand , etc. (v. Lidd. and Scott, s. v. κώρυκος , II.), Vitr. 5, 11, 2 ; cf.…

Cōrўcĭus.opening: adj. , = Κωρύκιος , Corycian . Of or belonging to the Corycian mountain cave ( Κωρύκιον ἄντρον ) on Parnassus, famous in ancient fable : Co rycium nemus, i. e. Parnassian, Stat. Th. 7, 347 : umbra, id. S. 5, 3, 5…

cōrўcŏmăchĭa.opening: , = κωρυκομαχία , the exercise of the athletae with the corycus (v. 1. corycus), Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 11, 134 .

cōrўcus.opening: ( ), , , = κώρυκος , a leathern sack filled with sand, flour , etc., by means of which the athletae exercised in the palæstra; only fig.: corycus laterum et vocis meae Bestia, Cic. Phil. 13, 12, 26 B. and K., Halm; cf.…

Cōrўcus.opening: or , , , = Κώρυκος , a promontory in Cilicia, with a town and harbor of the same name, and a cave, very celebrated in ancient times; also famous for its production of saffron; now Khorgos , Mel 1, 13, 2; Plin. 5, 27,…

cŏrўdălus.opening: , = κορυδαλός , the crested lark , Serv. ad Verg. E. 2, 1 .

Cŏrўdon.opening: , = Κορυδών , Greek proper name; of a shepherd, Verg. E. 2, 1 sq. ; Prop. 2 (3), 34, 73 .al.

Cŏrўlēnus.opening: , = Κορυληνός , a city of Æolis , Liv. 37, 21, 5 .

cŏrўlētum.opening: or , , corylus , a hazel-thicket, a copse of hazeltrees , Ov. F. 2, 587 .

cŏrўlus.opening: or , , , = κόρυλος , a hazel or filbert shrub , Cato, R. R. 18, 9 ; Verg. E. 1, 14 ; id. G. 2, 65 ; Ov. M. 10, 93 al.

cŏrўmbĭa.opening: , = κορυμβία , a species of the plant ferula , Plin. 19, 9, 56, § 175 .

cŏrymbĭātus.opening: adj. corymbus , set round with clusters of ivy-berries, corymbiated : discus, Gall. ap. Treb. Claud. 17, § 5 .

Cŏrymbĭfer.opening: adj. m. [corymbusfero], bearing clusters of ivy-berries , an epithet of Bacchus, Ov. F. 1, 393 .

cŏrymbĭon.opening: , = κορύμβιον , hair curled in the form of clusters of ivy-berries , Petr. 110, 1 and 5.

cŏrymbītes.opening: , = κορυμβίτης , a species of the plant tithymalus, Plin. 26, 8, 44, § 70 .

cŏrymbus.opening: , = κόρυμβος , a cluster of fruit, a cluster of flowers of different plants; so esp. freq. of a cluster of ivyberries , Verg. E. 3, 39 ; Ov. M. 3, 665 ; Juv. 6, 52 ; for the crowning of Bacchus, Prop. 2, 30 (3, 28), 39;…

Cŏrўnaeus.opening: name of two Trojans, companions of Æneas , Verg. A. 6, 228 ; 9, 571 ; 12, 298 .

cŏrўphaeus.opening: , = κορυφαῖος , a leader, chief, head : Epicureorum Zeno, Cic. N. D. 1, 21, 59 .

Cŏrўphāsĭa.opening: , = κορυφασία (v. Anthol. Gr. 1, p. 226), a title of Minerva (from her worship at , , Plin. 4, 5, 9, § 18 ), Arn. 4, p. 137 .

Cŏrўphē.opening: , or , , , daughter of Oceanus, mother of the fourth Minerva , Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 59 ; Arn. 4, p. 137 .

coryphĭa.opening: a kind of murex or snail, yielding a purple dye , Plin. 32, 7, 27, § 84 ; 32, 11, 53, § 147 .

corysidia.opening: another name of the plant Minyas , Plin. 24, 17, 100, § 157 (corinthia, Sillig).

Cŏrўthus.opening: , = Κόρυθος . An ancient town in Etruria , so named from its mythical founder, later called Cortona , Verg. A. 7, 209 ; 10, 719 .— Poet. , in gen., for Etruria , Verg. A. 9, 10 ; and for Italia , id. ib. 3, 170 Forbig.…

cōrȳtŏs.opening: or (˘˘ Sid. Carm. 11, 56 ), , , = κωρυτός , a quiver , Verg. A. 10, 169 Serv.; Ov. Tr. 5, 7, 15 ; Sil. 7, 443 ; Stat. Th. 4, 269 .— Poet. : velox corytus et arcus, Stat. Th. 7, 660 .

cŏrȳza.opening: , = κόρυζα , a catarrh , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 17, 101 .

cōs.opening: Sanscr. ça, to whet, sharpen; cf. cautes , any hard stone, flintstone , Cic. Div. 1, 17, 33 ; Liv. 1, 36, 4 and 5; Curt. 4, 6, 8 ; 5, 3, 8 ; 8, 11, 23 ; Verg. E. 8, 43 . — In partic., a whetstone, hone, grindstone ,…

Cōs.opening: or ( ), , , = Κῶς or Κόως , one of the Sporadic Islands in the Myrtoan Sea, on the coast of Caria, celebrated for the cultivation of the vine and for weaving; the birthplace of Hippocrates, Apelles, and Philetas , now…

Cŏsa.opening: (on coins also ; access. form , , Verg. A. 10, 168 ), , = Κόσσα and Κόσσαι . An ancient town in Etruria, not far from the coast , now Ansedonia , above Orbitello , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Liv. Ep. 14 ; id. 22, 11, 6 ; Plin. 3,…

coscĭnŏmantīa.opening: , = κοσκινομαντεία , a divination by the sieve , Aug. 5, p. 426 .

Coscōnĭus.opening: name of a Roman plebeian gens; esp., C. Cosconius, prætor during Cicero's consulate, also known as a writer on antiquities , Varr. L. L. 6, § 39 , and § 89 Müll.; Cic. Sull. 14, 42 ; id. Brut. 69, 242 .— C. Cosconius…

cosmēta.opening: , = κοσμήτης , he who ornaments one, an adorner; a designation of a slave who had charge of the wardrobe and decoration of his mistress, Juv. 6, 477 .

cosmĭcŏs.opening: adj. , = κοσμικός (syn. mundanus), of or belonging to the world; as subst. , , , a citizen of the world, a cosmopolite , Mart. 7, 41, 1 .— , , , worldly things , Mart. 7, 41, 2 .

cosmittere.opening: , acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 67, 8 Müll.

Cosmoe.opening: , = Κόσμοι , a high council of the Cretans , answering to the Lacedaemonian Ephori, Cic. Rep. 2, 33, 58 fin. Moser N. cr.

cosmō^grăphĭa.opening: , = κοσμογραφία , a description of the universe , Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 25 .

cosmŏgrăphus.opening: , = κοσμογράφος , one who describes the world, a cosmographer , Auct. Progen. Aug. 2; Mythogr. Lat. 3, 6, 35.

Cosmus.opening: a celebrated maker of, and dealer in unguents at Rome , Juv. 8, 86 ; Mart. 11, 8, 9 ; 1, 89, 2 ; 14, 110, 1 .—Hence, , , adj., named or derived from Cosmus : ampullae, Mart. 3, 82, 26 ; and subst. : , , (sc. unguentum),…

cossĭgĕrāre.opening: (perh. corrupted), word of unknown meaning, Att. ap. Non. p. 61, 24 .

Cossinius.opening: a Roman gentile name , Cic. Balb. 23, 53 al.

cossus.opening: a kind of larva under the bark of trees , Plin. 11, 33, 38, § 113 ; 17, 24, 37, § 220 ; 30, 13, 39, § 115 .

Cossus.opening: a surname in the gens Cornelia (cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 41, 9 Müll.); so esp. the military tribune in the war with the Veientes, A. Cornelius Cossus, Liv. 4, 19, 1 sq. ; and id. 4, 30, 4 sqq.; Verg. A. 6, 841 ; Juv. 8, 21…

Cossŭtĭānae.opening: a place near Cæsena in Gallia Cispadana, Q. Cic. ap. Cic. Fam. 16, 27, 2 .

Cossŭtĭānus.opening: a Roman proper name; esp. Cossutianus Capito, Tac. A. 11, 6 ; 16, 33 .

Cossŭtĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens, Suet. Caes. 1 ; Vitr. 7 , pr. 15 al.

costa.opening: a rib , Cels. 8, 1 ; Plin. 11, 37, 82, § 207 ; Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 4 ; Lucr. 5, 1297 ; Verg. G. 1, 273 ; id. A. 1, 211 ; Ov. H. 9, 111 ; Stat. Th. 2, 9 ; Mart. 9, 48, 10 .— Transf. , a side, a wall : aheni, Verg. A. 7, 463…

costābĭlis.opening: adj. costa , riblike (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 3, 48 .

costămōmum.opening: costum - amomum , an aromatic plant, similar to the costum and amomum, Dig. 39, 4, 16, § 7 .

costātus.opening: adj. costa , having ribs, ribbed : bene costati boves, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 8 .

costum.opening: (access. form, like the Greek, , , , Luc. 9, 917 ), = κόστος , an Oriental aromatic plant : Costus Arabicus, Linn.; Plin. 12, 12, 25, § 41 ; Ov. M. 10, 308 ; Hor. C. 3, 1, 44 al. ; freq. used in the preparation of…

Cŏsȳra.opening: ( ) or , , , a small island between Sicily and Africa , now Pantellaria , Ov. F. 3, 567 ; Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 92 ; Sil. 14, 272 ; Mel. 2, 7, 18 .

Cōthōn.opening: orig. a Semitic word, but identified by the Greeks with κώθων . In gen., a name given to any artificial harbor , Paul. ex Fest. p. 37, 9 Müll.— Esp. The artificial inner harbor of Carthage , Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 427 .—…

cŏthurnātĭo.opening: cothurnatus , a tragic representation , Tert. adv. Val. 13 .

cŏthurnātus.opening: adj. cothurnus , of or pertaining to the cothurnus, lit. buskined; hence, elevated, lofty, tragic (opp. excalceatus, comic, Sen. Ep. 8, 8 ; 76, 31 ; not ante-Aug.): Maronis grande opus, Mart. 5, 5, 8 : Lycophron, Ov.…

cŏthurnus.opening: , = κόθορνος , a high Grecian shoe. In gen., Cic. Fin. 3, 14, 46 ; id. Phil. 3, 6, 16 ; Vell. 2, 82, 4 al. — Esp. A high Grecian hunting-boot, laced up in front, and covering the whole foot , Verg. E. 7, 32 ; id. A. 1,…

cōtĭcŭla.opening: dim. cos . A small touchstone, a test , βάσανος , Plin. 33, 8, 43, § 126 .— A small stone mortar for medical use, Plin. 31, 9, 45, § 100 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 4, 11, 7 .

cŏtĭnus.opening: a shrub that furnishes a purple color : Rhus cotinus, Linn.; Plin. 16, 18, 30, § 73 .

Cŏtĭso.opening: a king of the Getæ , Suet. Aug. 63 ; called also king of the Dacians , Hor. C. 3, 8, 18 .

cŏtōnĕa.opening: a plant, wallwort, comfrey, black briony , Plin. 26, 7, 26, § 42 .

cottăbus.opening: , = κότταβος (a social sport consisting in dashing a liquid upon a brazen vessel; v. Lidd. and Scott under κότταβος ; hence humorously transf.), a clap, stroke : ne bubuli in te cottabi crebri crepent, Plaut. Trin. 4,…

cottăna.opening: (also , , and ), , Syrian; Gr. κόττανα , a kind of small Syrian fig , Plin. 13, 5, 10, § 51 ; Mart. 7, 52 ; Juv. 3, 83 ; Stat. S. 4, 9, 28 al.

cottīdĭānus.opening: and (less correctly ), (cŏtīd-, Mart. 11, 1, 2 ; but cōtĭd-, Cat. 68, 139 ), adj. cottidie . Prop. In gen., of every day, daily : febris, Ter. Hec. 3, 2, 22 : labor, Caes. B. G. 3, 17 : consuetudo, id. B. C. 3, 85 :…

cottī-dĭē.opening: or (v. Osann ad Cic. Rep. p. 475 ; less correctly , v. Neue, Formenl. I. p. 676 sq.), adv. quotdies , daily (class.; cf. in dies): ibatne ad Bacchidem? Pa. Cotidie, Ter. Hec. 1, 2, 82 : minari, Cic. Phil. 1, 2, 5 :…

cottīdĭō.opening: ( ), adv. , for cottidie, daily , Q. Caepio ap. Charis. p. 174 P.

Cottĭus.opening: the name of two kings of northern Italy, the father, who was a contemporary and friend of Augustus , Amm. 15, 10, 2 and 7, and the son (cf. Dio Cass. 60, 14), after whose death Nero made the country a Roman province ,…

Cotton.opening: a town of Æolis, in Asia Minor , Liv. 37, 21, 5 .

cŏtŭla.opening: ( ), , , = κοτύλη , a small vessel, as a measure, equal to a hemina or half a sextarius, Fann. Pond. 12; Mart. 8, 71, 8 ; Veg. Art. Vet. 3, 6, 8 al.

cō^turnix.opening: (ō, * Lucr. 4, 641 ; ŏ, Ov. Am. 2, 6, 27 ; Juv. 12, 97 ), , a sono vocis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 37, 4 Müll. , a quail , Plin. 10, 23, 33, § 64 sq. ; Plaut. Capt. 5, 4, 6 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 7 al. —As a term of endearment,…

cŏtўlēdon.opening: , = κοτυληδών , a plant, navelwort : Cotyledon umbilicus, Linn.; Plin. 25, 13, 101, § 159 .

Cŏtўs.opening: ( acc. -tȳn, rarely -tym; abl. -tye), and , , , = Κότυς , the name of several Thracian princes . A ruler of the coast of Thrace B. C. 382-356, son-in-law of Iphicrates , Nep. Iphicr. 3, 4 ; id. Timoth. 1, 2 ; Val. Max.…

Cŏtytto.opening: , = Κοτυττώ , the goddess of lewdness, who was originally worshipped in Thrace, later in Athens also , Juv. 2, 92 . — , , , = Κοτύττια , her festival , Hor. Epod. 17, 56 ; Verg. Cat. 5, 19 .

cŏ-ūtor.opening: v. n. : aliquo, to associate with, have dealings with , = συγχρῆσθαι , Vulg. Joan. 4, 9 .

cŏvīnārĭus.opening: ( ), , covinus , a soldier who fought from a chariot , Tac. Agr. 35 and 36.

cŏvīnus.opening: ( ), , Celtic , a war-chariot of the Britons and Belgæ , Mel. 3, 6, 5 ; Luc. 1, 426 ; Sil. 17, 422 .—Also a travelling chariot, a kind of tilbury , Mart. 12, 24, 1 .

coxa.opening: the hip . Prop, Cels. 4, 22, 1 ; 8, 1 fin. ; 8, 10, 5; Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 38 ; cf. also coxendix.—Hence, The hip-bone , Plin. Ep. 2, 1, 5 .— Transf. , in the Agrimensores: agrorum, a bend inwards (with angulus),…

coxendix.opening: (ī, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 40 ; Lucil. ap. Non. p. 94, 6 ; I, Ser. Samm. 702 ; 968 ), kindr. with coxa , the hip . Prop., Varr. R. R. 1, 20 ; Lucil. ap. Non. p. 94, 6 ; Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 40 ; Suet. Aug. 8 .— The hip-bone…

coxim.opening: adv. coxa; cf.: cessim, cossim , on the hips (late Lat.): insidens, App. M. 3, p. 129, 19 .

Crabra.opening: ( ) , an aqueduct or water conduit that extended from Tusculum to the Tiber , Cic. Agr. 3, 2, 9 ; id. Fam. 16, 18, 3 ; Front. Aquaed. 9 .

crābro.opening: a hornet : Vespa crabro, Linn.; Plin. 11, 21, 24, § 71 sq. ; Ov. M. 11, 335 ; Verg. G. 4, 245 al. —Prov.: irritare crabrones, to stir up a hornet's nest, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 84 .

cracca.opening: a kind of pulse , perh. wild vetch , Plin. 18, 16, 41, § 142 .

crăcens.opening: kindr. with gracilis; v. the letter C , slender, neat, graceful : cracentes = graciles, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 53, 7 Müll. (Ann. v. 497 Vahl.).

Crăgŏs.opening: or , , , = Κράγος , a promontory and chain of mountains in Lycia, the abode of the Chimæra , Mel. 1, 15, 3 ; Plin. 5, 27, 27, § 98 ; 5, 27, 28, § 101 ; Hor. C. 1, 21, 8 ; Ov. M. 9, 646 .

crambē.opening: , = κράμβη , a kind of cabbage , Plin. 20, 9, 33, § 79 .—Prov.: crambe repetita, warmed over , for something repeated, an old story , Juv. 7, 154 .

Cranĭi.opening: , = Κράνιοι , the inhabitants of a town on the island of Cephallenia , now Granea , Liv. 38, 28, 6 .

Crānon.opening: ( ), , , = Κράνων , a town of Thessaly, in the Vale of Tempe , Cic. de Or. 2, 86, 352 ; Liv. 36, 10, 1 ; 42, 64, 7 ; Val. Max. 1, 8 , ext. 7.—Hence, , , adj., of Cranon : ager, Liv. 42, 64, 7 .

Crantor.opening: , = Κράντωρ . In fable, the armor-bearer of Peleus, slain by the centaur Demoleon , Ov. M. 12, 367 .— A distinguished Grecian philosopher of the old Academic school , Cic. Ac. 1, 9, 34 ; 2, 44, 135 ; id. Fin. 5, 3, 7 ;…

crāpŭla.opening: , = κραιπάλη , excessive wine-drinking, intoxication, inebriation , Plaut. Most. 5, 2, 1 ; id. Ps. 5, 1, 46 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 11, § 28 ; id. Phil. 2, 12, 30 ; Liv. 9, 30, 9 ; Plin. 21, 20, 83, § 142 et saep.— Meton. ,…

crāpŭlārĭus.opening: adj. crapula , pertaining to intoxication : unctio, preventive of inebriation, Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 74 .

crāpŭlātĭo.opening: id. , an intoxicating (late Lat.), Cassiod. An. 11 .

crāpŭlātus.opening: adj. id. , drunken with wine, inebriated , Vulg. Psa. 77, 65 .

crāpŭlentus.opening: adj. id. , very much intoxicated , Amm. 29, 5, 54 .

crāpŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , inclined to drunkenness (late Lat.): libidines, Firm. Math. 8, 20.

crās.opening: adv. root ka-, ku-, to lighten, burn; Gr. καίω; cf. Sanscr. cvas, the same , to-morrow , αὔριον (freq. and class.). With tempp. fut. : rus cras cum filio Cum primo luci ibo hinc, Ter. Ad. 5, 3, 54 : scies fortasse cras,…

crassāmen.opening: crasso , the thick sediment of a liquid, the dregs (cf. crassamentum, II.), Col. 12, 25, 2 ; 12, 42, 2 .

crassāmentum.opening: id. (post-Aug.), the thickness of an object. In gen.: portarum, Plin. 16, 40, 77, § 210 : surculi, Gell. 17, 9, 7 .— Esp., the thick sediment of a liquid, the dregs, grounds , Col. 12, 12, 1 .

crassēdo.opening: crassus , thickness , fig.: ingenii, stupidity , Fulg. cont. Verg.

crassesco.opening: v. inch. , to grow thick, to thicken, grow dense or hard, grow large or fat (post-Aug.; most freq. in Pliny the elder): turtures milio, etc., Col. 8, 9, 2 : sues, Plin. 13, 18, 32, § 110 : ceparum capita, id. 19, 6, 32,…

Crassĭcĭus.opening: ( ), , , a grammarian of Rome , Cic. Phil. 13, 2, 3 ; Suet. Gram. 18 .

crassĭfĭcātĭo.opening: crassifico , a making thick or fat; hence, thickness : viscosa, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 3, 56 ; id. Acut. 1, 14, 115 .

crassĭfĭco.opening: v. a. crassusfacio , to make thick, thicken, make fat, fatten , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 208 ; 5, 2, 39 al. — Pass., to thicken, become dense , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 180 .

Crassĭpēs.opening: crassus-pes, thickfoot , a surname of the gens Furia, Liv. 38, 42, 4 ; the most celebrated is Furius Crassipes, Cicero's son-in-law , Cic. Fam. 1, 7, 11 al.

crassĭtas.opening: crassus , thickness, density , App. de Mundo, p. 65, 15.

crassĭtĭes.opening: id. , thickness, density , App. M. 7, p. 189, 38 .

crassĭtūdo.opening: crassus , thickness, density . Abstr. (in good prose): postes ...Quantā firmitate facti et quantā crassitudine, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 135 : parietum, Caes. B. C. 2, 8 : libramentum, in quo nulla omnino crassitudo sit, Cic.…

crassĭvēnĭus.opening: adj. crassusvena , having thick veins : acer, Plin. 16, 15, 26, § 66 .

crasso.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. crassus , to make thick, thicken, condense (postclass.): pili crassantur in setas, App. M. 3, p. 139, 39 : crassatus aër, Amm. 19, 4, 6 ; 19, 4, 8 ; 20, 3, 5 .

crassundĭa.opening: id. , the thick intestines , Varr. L. L. 5, § 111 Müll. N. cr.

crassus.opening: adj. Sanscr. kart-, to spin; cf.: crates, cartilago, etc. ; as opp. to flowing, thin, lean, delicate, etc., solid, thick, dense, fat, gross , etc. (freq. and class. in prose and poetry). Lit. : semina (opp. liquida),…

Crassus.opening: a family name in the gens Licinia. The most distinguished were, L. Licinius Crassus, a celebrated orator, a contemporary of Cicero , Cic. Brut. 38, 143 ; id. Off. 1, 30, 108 et saep.; cf. id. Brut. prol. pp. 68-77…

crastĭnus.opening: adj. cras . Of to-morrow; to-morrow's (freq. and class. in prose and poetry): dies, Plaut. Stich. 4, 2, 55 ; Cic. Att. 15, 8, 2 ; Prop. 2 (3), 15, 54 .al.: Titan, Verg. A. 4, 118 : Cynthius, Ov. F. 3, 345 : Aurora,…

Crastĭnus.opening: a Roman surname , Caes. B. C. 3, 91 ; 3, 99 ; Luc. 7, 471 ; Flor. 4, 2, 46 al.

crătaegis.opening: another name of the plant satyrion, Plin. 26, 10, 63, § 99 .

crătaegon.opening: , or , , , = κραταιγών or κράταιγος , a plant , called in pure Lat. aquifolia, Plin. 27, 8, 40, § 63 .

crătaegum.opening: , = κραταιγόν , the kernel of the fruit of the box-tree , Plin. 16, 30, 52, § 120 .

Crătaeis.opening: , = Κραταιίς , the mother of Scylla , Ov. M. 13, 749 ; Verg. Cir. 65 ; cf. Plin. 3, 5, 10, § 73 .

crătaeŏgŏnon.opening: , and ,, , , = κραταιόγονον , the common fleawort , Plin. 27, 8, 40, § 62 sq.

crātēra.opening: (acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 53, 10 , and Non. p. 547, 25 sq. , sometimes ; cf. Naev. Trag. Rel. v. 45 Rib.), , , and (mostly poet. ) , , , = κρατήρ , Ion. κρητήρ , a vessel in which wine was mingled with water, a…

crătĕrītes.opening: κρατερός , a very hard unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 154 .

Crătĕrus.opening: ( ), , , = Κρατερός , A general of Alexander the Great , Nep. Eum. 2, 2 ; 3, 3 ; 4, 1 ; Curt. 4, 3, 1 al. — A famous physician at Rome in the time of Cicero , Cic. Att. 12, 13, 1 ; 12, 14, 4 ; Hor. S. 2, 3, 161 ; Pers.…

Crătes.opening: , = Κράτης , a Greek proper name . A Theban philosopher , App. Mag. p. 26 Bip.; id. Flor. p. 126 sq. — Crates Mallotes, a grammarian , Suet. Gram. 2 ; Varr. L. L. 8, § 64 .— Crates, an Academic philosopher of Athens ,…

crătes.opening: , falsely assumed as nom. instead of cratis, q. v.

Crāthis.opening: , = Κρᾶθις , a river in Magna Graecia, whose water was said to redden the hair , now Crati or Gratti , Plin. 3, 11, 15, § 97 ; 31, 2, 9, § 13 ; 31, 2, 10, § 14 ; Ov. M. 15, 315 ; id. F. 3, 581 .

crātĭcĭus.opening: or , , adj. cratis , composed of wicker-work, wattled : parietes, lattice-work, Vitr. 2, 8 fin. ; Dig. 17, 2, 15 ; Pall. 1, 19, 2 .

crātĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , prop., fine hurdle - work; hence, a small gridiron , Mart. 14, 221, 1 ; Cato, R. R. 13, 1 ; Petr. 31, 11 ; 70, 7 .

craticulum.opening: a Graeco κρατεῦται deducitur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 53, 11 Müll. [more prob. immediately from crates].

crātĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [cratis], composed of lattice-work, wattled : lucernae, Cato, R. R. 13, 1 : aliter alii.

Crătīnus.opening: , = Κρατῖνος a celebrated Grecian comic poet of the old comedy, a contemporary of Eupolis and Aristophanes , Hor. Ep. 1, 19, 1 ; id. S. 1, 4, 1 ; Pers. 1, 123 ; Quint. 10, 1, 65 .

crātĭo.opening: v. a. cratis , to harrow (rare): herbam, Plin. 18, 28, 67, § 258 .

Crătippus.opening: , = Κράτιππος , a distinguished peripatetic philosopher at Athens, a teacher of Cicero's son , Cic. Off. 1, 1, 1 ; 2, 2, 8 ; id. Div. 1, 3, 5 ; Cic. Fil. ap. Cic. Fam. 16, 21, 3 .

crātis.opening: ( nom. sing. only Veg. Art. Vet. 1, 56, 5 ; acc. sing. cratim, Plaut. Poen. 5, 2, 65 ), Sanscr. kart, to spin; cf. crassus , wicker-work, a hurdle . Lit. In gen. Sing. (rare): flexilis, Plin. 16, 40, 77, § 209 ; 10, 44,…

crĕābĭlis.opening: adj. creo , that can be made or created (post-class. and rare): materia, App. Trism. 85, 12 ; Aug. Conf. 12, 19 al.

crĕāgra.opening: , = κρεάγρα , a fleshhook (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 9, § 997 ; Vulg. 2 Par. 4, 11 al.

crĕāmen.opening: creo , the elements of which created things consist (late Lat.), Prud. Ham. 505 .

crĕātĭo.opening: id. (very rare). A creating, producing, begetting : liberorum, Dig. 1, 7, 15, § 2 .— Absol. : non hujus creationis, i. e. not of man's building, Vulg. Heb. 9, 11 .— An electing to an office, a choice : magistratuum,…

crĕātor.opening: id. . A creator, author, begetter, founder . In gen. (very rare): ipse deūm, Cic. poët. Div. 2, 30, 64; cf. thus of a father , Ov. M. 8, 309 : creator atque opifex rerum, Luc. 10, 266 : hujus urbis, Romulus, Cic. Balb.…

crĕātrix.opening: creator , she who brings forth or produces, a mother ( poet. ): natura rerum, Lucr. 1, 630 al. : mea, patria (with genetrix), Cat. 63, 50 : diva (of a mother), Verg. A. 8, 534 ; cf.: Alexandri Magni, Olympias, Aur.…

crĕātūra.opening: creo , only concr., a creature, thing created (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 30 ; Prud. Ham. 508 : omnes creaturae tuae, Vulg. Tob. 8, 7 .— The creation : Deus caelorum et Dominus totius creaturae, Vulg. Jud. 9, 17 : Dei, id.…

crēber.opening: ( sup. creberrimus; but crebrissimus, Gell. 2, 30, 2 ; cf. Rudd. I. p. 170; and CEREBERRIMVS, Inscr. Orell. 68 ), adj. from cre-, root of cresco, Corn. Beitr. p. 356 , that exists or takes place in a continuous…

crēbrātus.opening: adj. creber , thick, close : telae pexitas, Plin. 11, 24, 28, § 81 .

crēbresco.opening: (in MSS. and edd. sometimes euphon. , , from ruber), brŭi, 3, v. inch. [creber], to become frequent, to increase, grow strong; of a rumor, report, to spread abroad (perh. not ante-Aug.; most freq. in Tac.): crebrescunt…

crēbrĭsūro.grammar: apud Ennium significat vallum crebris suris id est palis munitum

crēbrĭtas.opening: creber , thickness, closeness, frequency : spissae venarum, Vitr. 2, 10, 2 : caeli, id. 9, 8, 3 : fluctuum, Sall. H. Fragm. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 116 (3, 42 Dietsch): litterarum, Cic. Att. 13, 18 init. : crebritas et…

crēbrĭtūdo.opening: creber , for crebritas, Sisenn. ap. Non. p. 91, 30 dub.

crēdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. credo , worthy of belief, credible : credibile est quod sine ullo teste auditoris opinione firmatur, Cic. Inv. 1, 30, 48 (class. in prose and poetry): tametsi verissimum esse intellegebam, tamen credibile fore non…

crēdĭto.opening: v. freq. a. credo , to believe firmly , Fulg. Myth. 1, p. 6 .

crēdĭtor.opening: credo, I. , a creditor . Prop., Dig. 50, 16, 10 sq. ; Cic. Phil. 6, 4, 11 ; id. Quint. 23, 74 ; Liv. 6, 14, 5 ; Sen. Ep. 87, 6; 119, 1; Quint. 3, 6, 84 ; * Hor. S. 2, 3, 65 et saep.— Trop. , of the belly, Plin. 26, 8,…

crēdĭtrix.opening: creditor , a female creditor , Dig. 20, 5, 16 ; 42, 6, 38 al.

crēdo.opening: ( pres. subj. creduam, Plaut. Poen. 3, 5, 2 : creduas, id. Bacch. 3, 3, 72 ; id. Trin. 3, 1, 5 : creduat, id. Bacch. 3, 4, 5 ; 4, 7, 6 : creduis, id. Am. 2, 2, 49 ; id. Capt. 3, 4, 73 : creduit, id. Truc. 2, 2, 52 ;…

crēdŭlĭtas.opening: credulus , easiness of belief, credulity (first freq. after the Aug. per.; never in Cic.): credulitas error est magis quam culpa, Plancus ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 23, 1 ; Quint. 5, 3, 7 ; Tac. A. 2, 40 ; Curt. 7, 7, 8 ; Ov. M.…

crēdŭlus.opening: adj. credo, II. C. 2. , that easily believes a thing, credulous, easy of belief, confiding . Prop. (freq. and class.). Absol. : in fabulis stultissima persona est improvidorum et credulorum senum, Cic. Lael. 26, 100 :…

crĕmātĭo.opening: cremo , a burning, consuming by fire, cremation (post-Aug. and rare), Plin. 23, 2, 31, § 64 ; Prud. στεφ . 6, 88.

crĕmātor.opening: id. , a burner, consumer by fire (eccl. Lat.): Deus, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 16 .

crēmentum.opening: cresco . Growth, increase (very rare): corporum, Varr. ap. Non. p. 169, 14 : lunae, Plin. 11, 37, 55, § 149 (incrementum, Sillig).— Crementum est semen masculi, Isid. Orig. 9, 5, 5 ; 11, 1, 15 .

Crĕmĕra.opening: a small river in Etruria, near Veii, made famous by the heroic death of the Fabii , now La Varca or Valca , Liv. 2, 49 fin. ; Ov. F. 2, 205 ; Gell. 17, 21, 13 .— Poet. : Cremerae legio, i. e. the Fabii, Juv. 2, 155…

crĕmĭa.opening: ( sing. cremium, i, Vulg. Psa. 101, 4 ), cremo , dry fire-wood, brushwood , Col. 12, 19, 3 ; Dig. 32, 55, § 4 .

crĕmo.opening: v. a. Sanscr. çar, çri, to boil, roast; cf. carbo , to burn, consume by fire (freq. and class.; cf. comburo). In gen.: ignis silvas cremarat, Lucr. 5, 1242 ; cf.: poëtam igni, Suet. Calig. 27 fin. : omnes collegas suos…

Crĕmōna.opening: , = Κρεμώνη , the town Cremona in Gallia Cisalpina, on the Po , Liv. 21, 25, 2 ; 31, 10, 3 ; Verg. E. 9, 28 ; Tac. H. 2, 17 ; 2, 22 sq.; Suet. Vesp. 7 et saep.— Hence, , , adj., of Cremona : ager, Tac. H. 3, 15 :…

Cremōnis jŭgum.opening: a part of the Pennine Alps , now Grimsel , Liv. 21, 38, 7 .

crĕmor.opening: kindr. with cremo , the thick juice obtained from animal or vegetable substances, thick broth, pap , etc., Cato, R. R. 86 ; Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 15 ; Cels. 3, 7, 2 ; 6, 6, 26 ; Ov. M. Fac. 95 .

Crĕmūtĭus.opening: a Roman proper name : A. Cremutius Cordus, a Roman historian under Tiberius, distinguished by his frankness, Tac. A. 4, 34 ; Sen. Suas. 7, p. 44 ; Quint. 10, 1, 104 ; Sen. Cons. Marc. 1, 2 .

crena.opening: , corrupted word, Plin. 11, 37, 68, § 180 ; Sillig ad h. 1.; Jan. taeniis.

crĕo.opening: (old form , in Varr. L. L. 6, § 81 Müll.), , v. a. kindred with Sanscr. kar, kri, to make , to bring forth, produce, make, create, beget (very freq. in every period and species of composition). Lit. In gen.: rerum…

Crĕo.opening: , anal. to the Gr., , , , = Κρέων . A king of Corinth, who betrothed his daughter Creusa to Jason , Hyg. Fab. 25 ; Sen. Med. 526 ; Hor. Epod. 5, 64 .— A brother of Jocaste, at Thebes , Hyg. Fab. 72 ; Stat. Th. 12, 477 ;…

crepae.opening: , i. q. caprae, she-goats , acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 48, 16 Müll.

crĕpātūra.opening: crepo , a fissure, crack (late Lat.): parietum, Schol. Juv. 3, 196 .

crĕpax.opening: adj. id. , sounding, creaking : mola, Maecen. ap. Sen. Ep. 114, 6 .

crĕper.opening: adj. Sabine; kindr. with Sanscr. kshapā, night, and Gr. κνέφας , dusky, dark; hence, trop., uncertain, obscure, doubtful, wavering (ante- and post-class.), Varr. L. L. 6, § 5 ; 7, § 77 ; cf. Non. p. 13, 15 sq. ; Paul.…

crĕpĭda.opening: , = κρηπίς , the sole which served the Greeks, and the Romans who adopted Grecian habits, as a shoe, a sandal (pure Lat. solea; cf. Gell. 13, 21, 5 sq. ), Cic. Rab. Post. 10, 27 ; Liv. 29, 19, 12 ; Suet. Tib. 13 ; id.…

crĕpĭdārĭus.opening: adj. crepida , of or pertaining to the sole or sandal : sutor, a sandal-maker, shoemaker , Sempr. Asell. ap. Gell. 13, 21, 8 : culter, Gell. ib.

crĕpĭdātus.opening: adj. id. , wearing sandals , Cic. Pis. 38, 92 and 93; Suet. Dom. 4: fabula, a kind of Græco-Roman tragedy , Don. Ter. Ad. prol. 7 ; cf. Neukirch. Fab. Tog. pp. 15 and 57.

crĕpīdo.opening: κρηπίς . Prop., a ground, basis, foundation, a socle, pedestal, base , Plin. 36, 9, 14, § 66 ; Stat. S. 1, 1, 58 : altaris, Vulg. Lev. 1, 15 .— Transf. , an elevated enclosure, a high projection, an edge, brim, brink,…

crĕpĭdŭla.opening: dim. crepida , a small sandal , Plaut. Pers. 4, 2, 3 ; cf. Gell. 13, 21, 5 .

crĕpĭtācillum.opening: dim. crepitaculum , a small rattle , Lucr. 5, 229 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 8 .

crĕpĭtācŭlum.opening: crepito , a rattle , Quint. 9, 4, 66 ; Mart. 14, 54 ; Mart. Cap. 1, § 7 ; 9 , §§ 909, 927.

crĕpĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [crepo], to rattle much, to creak, crackle, clatter, rustle, rumble, chatter, murmur , etc. ( poet. or in post-Aug. prose): dentibus, Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 52 ; Lucr. 5, 746 : tenui rostro, Ov. M. 11, 735 ; cf.…

crĕpĭtŭlum.opening: ( ; , ) ornamentum capitis, idem enim in capitis motu crepitum facit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 52, 19 Müll. —Form , Tert. Pall. 4 .

crĕpĭtus.opening: crepo , a rattling, creaking, clattering, clashing, rustling, a noise , etc. (in good prose). In gen.: cardinum, Plaut. Curc. 1, 3, 1 ; cf. claustrorum (with sonitus), id. ib. 1, 3, 47 : carbasi, Lucr. 6, 110 : e motu…

crĕpo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, 1 v. n. and a.
crĕpo.opening: v. n. and a. [Sanscr. krap, to lament; cf. crabro] (mostly poet. or in post-Aug. prose; in class. prose, concrepo). Neutr., to rattle, crack, creak, rustle, clatter, tinkle, jingle, chink , etc. In gen.: foris, Plaut.…

crĕpŭlus.opening: adj. crepo , rattling, resounding, crashing (late Lat.): buccae, Sid. Ep. 9, 13, 2 : fragor, id. ib. 4, 15 .

crĕpundĭa.opening: id. , a rattle; and specif., Most freq., a child's rattle (cf. Ruhnk. ad Ter. Eun. 4, 6, 15 ), Plaut. Mil. 5, 6 ; id. Rud. 4, 4, 37 ; 5, 3, 7 ; id. Cist. 3, 5 ; 3, 4 ; 1, 4 ; Cic. Brut. 91, 313 Jahn ad loc.; Plin. 11,…

crĕpuscŭlascens.opening: Part. [crepusculum], growing dusk, dusky : hora, Sid. Ep. 8, 3 .

crĕpuscŭlum.opening: creper , twilight, dusk (cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 5 Müll.); and in partic., evening twilight, the dusk of the evening (opp. diluculum, the morning twilight, dawn; poet. or in post-Aug. prose). Prop., Plaut. Cas. prol. 40 ;…

crescentĭa.opening: cresco , an increase, augmentation : dierum (opp. brevitates), Vitr. 9, 9, 7 .

cresco.opening: ( inf. perf. sync. cresse, Lucr. 3, 683 ), v. inch. n. [1. creo]. Orig., of things not previously in existence, to come forth, grow, to arise, spring, be born, become visible, appear (so mostly poet. ) Lit. : cetera,…

Crēta.opening: ( nom. Crētē, Mel. 2, 7, 12 ; Ov. M. 8, 118 ; 9, 668 ; 9, 735 ; acc. Creten, id. ib. 8, 99 ; Hor. C. 3, 27, 34 al. ; on the contrary, Cretam, Verg. A. 3, 129 al. ), , = Κρήτη , Crete, an island in the Mediterranean Sea,…

crēta.opening: orig. adj., from 1. Creta , Cretan earth , i. e. chalk, white earth or clay. Prop., Plin. 35, 17, 57, § 195 sq. ; Cato, R. R. 39, 2 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 8 al. ; esp. used for cleansing garments, Plaut. Aul. 4, 9, 6…

crētācĕus.opening: adj. 2. creta , chalk-like, cretaceous : siligo, Plin. 18, 9, 20, § 86 .

crētārĭus.opening: adj. 2. creta , of or pertaining to chalk : ARS, Inscr. Grut. 641, 3 .— Subst. : , , (sc. taberna), a shop for Cretan earth , Varr. L. L. 8, § 55 Müll.

crētātus.opening: adj. id. , marked with chalk . Prop.: fasciae, Cic. Att. 2, 3, 1 : pedes, Plin. 35, 18, 58, § 201 : bos (decorated as an offering), Juv. 10, 66 : Fabulla, whitened, Mart. 2, 41, 11 .— Transf. : ambitio, i. e. of the…

crētĕus.opening: adj. 2. creta , made of chalk or clay : persona, Lucr. 4, 298 .

crēthmŏs.opening: , = κρῆθμος , sea-fennel : Crithmum maritimum, Linn.; Plin. 25, 13, 96, § 155 ; 26, 8, 50, § 82 .

crētĭca.opening: , and , , v. 1. Creta, II. F. 2. b.

crētĭ-fŏdīna.opening: 2. creta , a chalk- or clay-pit , Dig. 7, 1, 13, § 5 al.

crētĭo.opening: cerno, II. ; jurid. t. t., the format declaration by the heir of his intention to enter upon his inheritance. Prop., Gai Inst. 2, § 7 ; 2, 164 sqq.; 2, 171 sqq.; Ulp. Fragm. 22, 25 sqq.; Varr. L. L. 6, § 81 Müll.:…

crētōsus.opening: adj. 2. creta , abounding in chalk or clay : locus, Cato, R. R. 8, 1 ; Plin. 15, 18, 19, § 72 : terra, Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 3 ; Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 175 : rura Cimoli, Ov. M. 7, 463 .

crētŭla.opening: dim. id. , white clay, used for sealing , = terra sigillata, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 26, § 58 ; Plin. 35, 7, 31, § 49 .

crētūra.opening: cerno ; concr., the siftings of corn, bran, chaff (late Lat.), Pall. 1, 24, 3 .

crētus.opening: Part. , from cresco. q. v. I. A. fin.

Crĕūsa.opening: , = Κρέουσα . A daughter of king Creon, of Corinth, married to Jason, and on that account put to death by Medea by means of a charmed offering (a garment, acc. to Hor. Epod. 5, 65 ; a garment and a golden chain, acc. to…

crībello.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. cribellum , to pass through a sieve, to sift (late Lat.), Pall. 1, 41, 3 ; Theod. Prisc. 1, 17 al.

crībellum.opening: dim. cribrum , a small sieve (late Lat.), Pall. Febr. 24 ; id. Jun. 11 .

crībrārĭus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to a sieve : cribrarius alica, sifted, Plin. 18, 11, 29 , §115.— Subst. : † , a sieve-maker , κοσκινοποιός , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

crībro.opening: v. a. id. , to pass through a sieve, to sift (perh. not anteAug.), Col. 12, 51, 1 ; Plin. 17, 11, 15, § 76 al.

crībrum.opening: from root cer, whence cerno , a sieve, searce, riddle , Cato, R. R. 25, 76, 3 ; Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 14 ; Cic. Div. 2, 27, 59 ; Col. 8, 5, 16 ; Plin. 18, 11, 28, § 108 sq. ; Ov. M. 12, 437 ; Pers. 3, 112 et saep.— Facete,…

crīmen.opening: contr. for cernimen, from cerno, II. C. ; lit., a judicial decision, verdict, judgment; hence, transf., like the Gr. κρῖμα , of the subject of such a decision, and with partieular reference either to the accuser or to…

crīmĭnālis.opening: adj. crimen , of or pertaining to crime, criminal (jurid. Lat.): causa, Cod. Just. 9, 41, 15 : accusatio, ib. 3, 35, 3 .— Adv. : , criminally : agi furti, Dig. 47, 2 fin.

crīmĭnātĭo.opening: criminor , an accusation, complaint, calumny (in good prose): criminatione in me absentem uti, Cic. Agr. 3, 1, 3 : criminatio tua quae est? Roscium cum Flavio pro societate decidisse, id. Rosc. Com. 13, 37 ; id. de Or.…

crīmĭnātor.opening: id. , an accuser, a calumniator (very rare): meus, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 28 : in alios (opp. sui obtegens), Tac. A. 4, 1 .—Of the devil, Lact. 2, 8, 6 ; 6, 4, 2 .

crīmĭnātrix.opening: criminator , a female accuser, calumniator , Vulg. Paul. ad Tit. 2, 3 .

crīmĭno.opening: v. a. ; collat. form of criminor, to accuse, make an accusation : aliquem apud aliquem, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 78 .— Absol. : apud aliquem, Enn. ap. Non. p. 470, 16 (Sat. v. 9 Vahl.).— Pass. : Sullanas res defendere criminor,…

crīmĭnor.opening: v. dep. crimen, I. . With a personal object, to accuse one of crime, to complain of, impeach, calumniate (rare but class.): hanc metui ne me criminaretur tibi, Ter. Eun. 5, 2, 16 ; so, aliquem alicui, Tac. Or. 42 ;…

crīmĭnōsus.opening: adj. crimen, I. , full of reproaches, reproachful, accusalory, calumniating, slanderous (class.): ne cum me nimium gratum illi esse dicant, id mihi criminosum esse possit, Cic. Planc. 2, 4 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 67, § 162 ;…

Crīmīsus.opening: (in MSS. and edd. also , , , and ), , , = Κριμῖσός ( Κριμισσός ), a river on the south-west coast of Sicily , Nep. Timol. 2, 4 ; Verg. A. 5, 38 ; Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 57 ; Hyg. Fab. 273 .

crīnālis.opening: adj. crinis , of or pertaining to the hair, hair- ( poet. , or in post-Aug. prose): vitta, Verg. A. 7, 403 ; Ov. M. 4, 6 ; 5, 617 : aurum, Verg. A. 11, 576 ; Stat. Achill. 2, 97 : acus, a hair-pin, App. M. 8, p. 207, 4…

crīnĭger.opening: adj. crinis-gero , having long hair , Luc. 1, 458 dub. (al. cirrigeros, with long curls).

crĭnĭnus.opening: adj. , = κρίνινος , made of lilies, lily- : unguentum, Dig. 34, 2, 21 ; cf. crinon.

crystallŏīdes.opening: adj. , = κρυσταλλοειδής , crystal-like , Theod. Prisc. p. 4, 2 med.

crystallum.opening: (analog. to the Gr. , , Sol. 15 fin. ), = κρύσταλλος . Ice , Auct. Priap. 63, 6 .— A crystal, mountain- or rock-crystal , Plin. 37, 2, 9, § 23 ; Sen. Q. N. 3, 25, 12 ; Plin. 36, 26, 66, § 192 ; Curt. 3, 3, 8 ; Stat. S.…

Ctēsĭās.opening: , = Κτησίας , a famous physician of Cnidus in Caria, author of a history of the East , Plin. 2, 106, 110, § 238 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 2.

Ctēsĭbĭus.opening: a mechanic of Alexandria, distinguished for his inventions in hydraulics , Vitr. 9, 6 (al. 9), p. 280 Bip.—Hence, , , adj., of Ctesibius : machina, Vitr. 10, 12 .

Ctēsĭphōn.opening: , = Κτεσιφῶν , a town in Assyria, residence of the Parthian kings , Plin. 6, 26, 30, § 122 ; Tac. A. 6, 42 ; Amm. 23, 6, 23 ; Eutr. 8, 3 ; Spart. Sev. 16, 1 .

Cŭba.opening: cubo , the goddess who protects the lying down of children , Varr. ap. Don. Ter. Phorm. 1, 1, 15 .

cŭbātĭo.opening: cubo , a lying down , Varr. L. L. 8, § 54 Müll.

cŭbātor.opening: cubo , he who lies down , Paul. Nol. Ep. 21, 4 .

cŭbĭcŭlārĭus.opening: ( , e; gen. , Cic. Div. 2, 65, 134 ; dat. , id. Tusc. 5, 20, 59 ; but ap. Suet. Aug. 7 , the better read. is cubiculi Lares; v. cubiculum, I.), adj. cubiculum , of or pertaining to a sleepingchamber . Adj. : lucerna,…

cŭbĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. id. , furnished with bedchambers or state-rooms : naves, Sen. Ben. 7, 20, 3 .

cŭbĭcŭlum.opening: ( , per sync., Mart. 10, 30, 17 dub.), , cubo , an apartment for reclining or (more freq.) for sleeping (cf. cubo), a resting- or sleepingchamber, a bedchamber . Prop., Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 7 ; Serv. Galba ap. Cic. de Or.…

cŭbĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = κυβικός , cubic, cubical : rationes, Vitr. 5 , praef. 3: soliditas, Mart. Cap. 2, § 102 .

cŭbīle.opening: cubo , a place of rest, a couch, bed . Lit. Of men, Lucr. 5, 814 ; 5, 985 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 32, 90 ; 2, 17, 39 ; Liv. 30, 5, 10 ; Hor. S. 1, 3, 100 ; Curt. 5, 2, 15 : salutatorium, an audience - chamber, Plin. 15, 11, 10,…

cŭbĭtal.opening: id. , a cushion for leaning on, an elbow-cushion , Hor. S. 2, 3, 255 (quoted in Fronto Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 1 ).

cŭbĭtālis.opening: adj. cubitum , pertaining to the elbow; hence, as a measure, a cubit long , Liv. 24, 34, 9 ; Plin. 12, 12, 26, § 45 ; Pall. Febr. 18, 6 al. : simulacrum cubitali majus, Suet. Galb. 4 .

cŭbĭtĭo.opening: 1. cubitus , a lying down , Aug. Ep. 151 .

cŭbĭtissim.opening: , a corrupt word in Plaut. Cas. 5, 2, 42 ; acc. to some, adv., lying down.

cŭbĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [cubo], to lie down often, to be accustomed to lie down (rare): anus hic solet cubitare, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 76 ; Cic. Cael. 15, 36 : humi (pavones), Col. 8, 11 fin. : super pedes cubitantis reclinis, Tac. A.…

cŭbĭtor.opening: id. , he who lies down : bos, that often lies down in ploughing, Col. 6, 2, 11 .

cŭbĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a reclining posture : vestimenta, clothing worn at table, Petr. 30, 11 .

cŭbĭtum.opening: ( , , , Cels. 8, 1 ; 8, 16 ; Non. p. 201, 16 ) [id.], the elbow (serving for leaning upon). Prop., Cels. 1 . 1.; Plin. 11, 45, 102, § 249 ; Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 13 ; Verg. A. 4, 690 ; Ov. M. 7, 343 ; Hor. C. 1, 27, 8 ;…

cŭbĭtūra.opening: cubo , a lying down , Plaut. ap. Non. p. 198, 25 .

cŭbo.opening: , ìtúm, 1 ( perf. subj. cubaris, Prop. 2 (3), 15, 17 ; perf. inf. cubasse, Quint. 8, 2, 20 ; cf. also Neue, Formenl. II. p. 478), v. n. cf. κύπτω , to lie down . Of persons. In gen., to be in a recumbent posture, to…

cŭbus.opening: , = κύβος , a die, cube , Vitr. 5 , praef. 4.— As a measure, Rhem. Fann. 61.— A cubic number , Gell. 1, 20, 6 .

cuccuru.opening: ( ), a word of unknown signif.: Afranius in Cinerario: id me celabat cuccuru. An nomen est ut veru, genu? Charis. p. 214 P. ( Afran. Com. Rel. v. 22 Rib.); cf. cucurio.

cūci.opening: Pers.; Gr. κοῦκι , a tree similar to the palm; acc. to Sprengel, Hyphaene coriacea, Plin. 13, 9, 18, § 62 .

cucubălus.opening: the plant called also strychnos and strumus, Plin. 27, 8, 44, § 68 ; Marc. Emp. p. 250 .

cūcŭbo.opening: v. n. cf. κωκύω , of the screech-owl, to hoot , Auct. Carm. Philom. 14 dub.

cŭcullātus.opening: adj. cucullus , hooded, having a hood (late Lat.): vestis, Isid. Orig. 19, 24, 17 .

cŭcullĭo.opening: ( , Cato, R. R. 2, 3 ), , id. , a covering for the head, a cap , Cato, 1 . 1.; Lampr. Elag. 32 ; Capitol. Ver. 4 .

cŭcullus.opening: ( , , , in eccl. Lat., Paul. Nol. 21, 389 ; Hier. Vit. Hil. 46 ; Ennod. Ep. 9, 14 ) [root kal-, of cella, clam, καλύπτω ; cf. culleus], a covering . Of the head, a cap, hood, fastened to a garment , Col. 1, 8, 9 ; Mart.…

cŭcŭlo.opening: v. n. cuculus , onomatop. of the cuckoo, to cry cuckoo , Auct. Carm. Philom. 35.

cŭcūlus.opening: (cŭcŭlus, Auct. Carm. Philom. 35), , Sanscr. ku-, to cry; cf. κωκύω , a cuckoo , Plin. 18, 26, 66, § 249 ; as a term of reproach, Plaut. As. 5, 2, 73 ; id. Ps. 1, 1, 94 ; esp. of foolish men, id. Trin. 2, 1, 18 ; and of…

cŭcŭma.opening: coquo . A cookingvessel, a kettle , Petr. 135, 4 ; Dig. 48, 8, 1 .— Perh., a small private bath (opp. thermae), Mart. 10, 79, 4 .

cŭcŭmella.opening: dim. cucuma , a little kettle , Dig. 8, 5, 17 .

cŭcŭmĕrācĕus.opening: adj., cucumber-like, of cucumber , Theod. Prisc. p. 2, 3 .

cŭcŭmĕrārĭum.opening: cucumis , a cucumber-field (eccl. Lat., transl. of the Heb. , Isa. 1, 8), Tert. adv. Jud. 3 ; Hier. in Isa. 1, 1, 8 .

cŭcŭmis.opening: (is, sometimes in the Nat. Hist. of Pliny; e. g. acc. cucumim, Plin. 9, 2, 1, § 3 ; 20, 1, 2, § 3 ; abl. cucumi, id. 20, 9, 40, § 103 al. ; together with cucumeris, id. 19, 5, 23, § 68 ; 19, 12, 61, § 186 : cucumeres,…

cŭcurbĭta.opening: a gourd . Prop., Col. 11, 3, 48 sq. ; Plin. 19, 5, 24, § 69 sq. ; Pall. Mart. 9, 16 .— Transf. , in medic. lang., a cup, cupping-glass (of similar form), Scrib. Comp. 46 ; 67 ; Juv. 14, 58 : cucurbitae medicinales,…

cŭcurbĭtārĭus.opening: cucurbita , a gourd planter , Hier. Ep. 112 , n. 22.

cŭcurbĭtātĭo.opening: cucurbita, II. , a cupping , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 32 .

cŭcurbĭtīnus.opening: adj. cucurbita , like or similar to a gourd : pira, the gourdpear, Cato, R. R. 7, 4 ; Plin. 15, 15, 16, § 56 : ficus, Cloatius ap. Macr. S. 2, 16, 1 ; 2, 15, 6 .

cŭcurbĭtŭla.opening: dim. id. . Silvestris, the bitter gourd , Scrib. Comp. 106 . — A cupping-glass , Cels. 2, 11 ; 3, 18 .

cŭcurbĭtŭlāris.opening: cucurbitula , the field cypress , = chamaepitys, Isid. Orig. 17, 9, 86 .

cūcūrĭo.opening: v. n. root kar-, to sound; cf. Gr. κρέκω, κραυγή , to crow , Auct. Carm. Philom. 25.

cucus.opening: a daw : interea Cucus, si in ludum iret, potuisset fieri ut probe litteras sciret, Plaut. Pers. 2, 1, 6 .

cucutĭum.opening: cf. cucullus , a kind of hood , Treb. Poll. Claud. 17, 6 .

cūdo.opening: a helmet made of raw skin; abl. cudone, Sil. 8, 495 ; 16, 59 ; cf.: cudon, περικεφαλαίας εἶδος , Gloss. Philox.

cuferion.opening: the nose-bleed , a disease of horses, Veg. Art. Vet. 3, 37 .

cuicuimŏdi.opening: (ante-class. ) [quisquis-modus], euphon. form for cujuscujusmodi (very rare in MSS., but vouched for by the ancient grammarians; v. Kuhner, Gram. I. p. 398; 405 sq.), of what sort, kind , or nature soever : sisne necne…

cuimŏdi.opening: quis-modus for cujusmodi = qualis, of what kind or nature soever : cuimodi esset, Gell. 9, 13, 4 ; 12, 2, 2 ; 12, 15, 1 ; 13, 29, 1 al.

cūjas.opening: (archaic ), (anteand post-class.) uncontr. , , pron. interrog . [pronom. stem quo-; cf.: quis, qui], whence originating? of what country, family , or town? whence? from what place? = ποδαπός ; nom. cujatis (quoj-), Enn.…

cūjus.opening: (archaic ), , pron. rel. [from cujus, gen. of qui], pertaining to whom, of whom, whose (rare): cujum id censebis esse reddes, ancient form of an oath in Gell. 16, 4, 2 ; cf.: argentum ego pro istisce ambabus, quojae…

cūjuscĕmŏdi.opening: ( ) or quisce-modus , of what kind or nature soever (late Lat.): voces, App. M. 8, p. 209, 9 .

cūjuscumquĕmŏdi.opening: , a false read. for cujusque modi, Sall. C. 39, 6 .

cūjusdammŏdi.opening: , better , of some sort , Cic. Fin. 5, 12, 36 ; id. Div. 2, 14, 34 .

cūjusmŏdi.opening: ( ), also quis-modus = qualis, of what kind : cupio cognoscere iter tuum cujusmodi sit, Cic. Fam. 15, 20, 3 ; Auct. B. Afr. 31; Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 132 .— Of whatever kind , Cic. Fam. 4, 7, 4 (al. leg. cuicuimodi); id.…

cūjusmŏdicumquē.opening: adv. quicumque-modus , of whatever kind : cujusmodicumque mater sit, Cic. Clu. 6, 17 Ramsey (where B. and K. read cujuscumque modi).

cūjusquĕmŏdi.opening: ( ) or quisque modus , of whatever kind , Cic. Fin. 2, 1, 3 ; 2, 7, 22 ; Lucr. 4, 135 .

cūjusvis.opening: from cujus-vis, gen. of quivis , to whomever pertaining, whosesoever, of any one : cujavis oratio insimulari potest, si, etc., App. Mag. p. 326, 13 .

Culăro.opening: a town in Gallia Narbonensis, afterwards Gratianopolis, now Grenoble , Cic. Fam. 10, 23, 7 .

culcĭta.opening: (in MSS. also ), , etym. dub.; acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, § 167 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 50, 8, from calco , a sack filled with feathers, wool, hair , etc., for lying upon, warming , etc.; a bed, cushion, mattress, pillow ,…

culcĭtārĭus.opening: culcita , a cushion-maker , acc. to Diom. p. 313 P.

culcĭtella.opening: dim. id. , a little cushion or mattress , transf. in mal. part., Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 14 ; cf.: sponda interior regiae lecticae, Suet. Caes. 49 .

culcĭtŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small cushion or mattress , Lucil. ap. Non. p. 35, 20 ; cf. Diom. p. 326, 20 K.

cŭlex.opening: ( , Plaut. Cas. 2, 3, 22 ), a gnat, midge (comprising very many species), Plin. 11, 2, 1, § 2 sq. ; 11, 35, 41, § 118 ; 17, 27, 44, § 255 ; Plaut. Curc. 4, 2, 14 ; Lucr. 3, 391 ; Hor. S. 1, 5, 14 ; Col. 11, 3, 60 ;…

cŭlĭcellus.opening: dim. 1. culex , a little gnat : amasio Tullae, i. e. buzzing round her , Ser. ap. Diom. p. 513 P.

cŭlĭcŭlārĕ.opening: id. , a fly-net (late Lat.; cf. conopeum), Schol. Juv. 6, 80 .

cŭlĭcŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a little gnat , κωυώπιον , Gloss. Cyrill.

cŭligna.opening: , = κυλίχνη , a small drinking-vessel, a cup , Cato, R. R. 132, 1 ; Fragm. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 55, 2 Müll.

cŭlīna.opening: (old orthogr. , acc. to Non. p. 55, 18 sq. ), , Sanscr. çar, çri, to cook, mix , a kitchen . Prop., Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 1 ; id. Truc. 2, 7, 53 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 13, 2 ; Cic. Fam. 15, 18, 1 ; Sen. Ep. 114, 26 ; Petr. 2 ;…

cŭlīnārĭus.opening: adj. culina , pertaining to the kitchen, culinary, kitchen- . Adj. : operae, Fronto, B. Parth. p. 201 .— Subst. : , , , a kitchen servant , Scrib. Comp. 230 .

cūlĭŏla.grammar: cortices nucum viridium, dicta a similitudine culeorum, quibus vinum sive oleum continetur

culix.opening: an unknown plant , Plin. 19, 5, 23, § 68 .—Also , Pall. Mart. 9, 8 .

cullĕāris.opening: ( ), , adj. culleus, II. A. , of the measure of a culleus: labrum, Cato, R. R. 154 : dolia, Vitr. 6, 9 .

cullĕus.opening: ( , and in the signif. II. B., ), ( nom. plur. cullea, neutr. , Cato ap. Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 7 ; Non. p. 197 ; gen. plur. culleūm, Cato, R. R. 11, 1 ), , = κολεός , Ion. κουλεός (a sheath; hence), a leather bag, a sack…

culmen.opening: , contr. form of columen, q. v.

culmĕus.opening: adj. culmus , of siraw : tecti culmina, Paul. Nol. Carm. 13, 387 .

culmōsus.opening: adj. culmus , stalklike , poet. : fratres, sprung from the dragonteeth, Sid. Carm. 6, 72 .

culmus.opening: kindr. with culmen , a stalk, stem , esp. of grain, straw , Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 3 (Cod. Vindob. culmen); Cic. Sen. 15, 51 ; Verg. G. 1, 111 ; 1, 317 al. —Of other plants: milii, panici, Plin. 18, 7, 10, § 52 : holci, id.…

culpa.opening: kindr. in root with scelus; cf. Sanscr. skhal-, errare , crime, fault, blame, failure, defect (as a state worthy of punishment; on the contr. delictum, peccatum, etc., as punishable acts; diff. from scelus, which…

culpābĭlis.opening: adj. culpa , worthy of blame, culpable, criminal (post-class.): aliquid (opp. laudabile), App. Mag. p. 223 : opinio de diis (opp. digna), Arn. 7, p. 222 . — Comp. : tanto culpabilius est, non observare quod possis,…

culpātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from culpo.

culpĭto.opening: v. freq. a. culpo , to blame or reproach severely or harshly : jusjurandum, Plaut. Cist. 2, 1, 28 .

culpo.opening: v. a. culpa . To reproach or blame a person or thing as wrong or faulty, to censure, reprove, disapprove, condemn (syn.: reprehendo, vitupero; opp. laudo, probo, etc.; rare; mostly post-Aug.; never in the Cic. per.).…

cultē.opening: adv. , v. colo, P. a. fin.

cultello.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. cultellus . To make in the shape of a knife : spinam dorsi, Plin. 8, 25, 38, § 91 ; 32, 2, 5, § 13 Sillig N. cr. — To level land by the coulter , Front. Limit. p. 43 Goes.

cultellŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a little knife , Sol. 38 .

cultellus.opening: dim. culter , a small knife . Prop., Varr. R. R. 1, 69, 2 ; id. Fragm. ap. Non. p. 195, 18 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 51 ; Plin. 12, 25, 54, § 115 al. — Lignei, wooden pegs or pins , Vitr. 7, 3 .

culter.opening: kindr. with Sanscr. kar, to wound, kill; cf. per-cello, clades . Orig. a plough-coulter, ploughshare , Plin. 18, 18, 48, § 171 sq. — In gen., a knife; so a vintner's knife , Col. 4, 25, 2 ; 12, 45, 4 ; a butcher's knife…

cultĭcŭla.grammar: fusticulus quidam ligneus in sacris dicebatur
cultĭcŭla.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 50, 9 Müll., where Lind. reads culcitula.

cultĭo.opening: 1. colo . Agri, a cultivation, preparation of ground, agriculture , Cic. Sen. 16, 57 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 97, § 226 (others, less correctly, agricultio in one word; v. agricultio): cultionis labor, Ambros. Fug. Saec. 8,…

cultor.opening: id. . Prop., one who bestows care or labor upon a thing, an elaborator, cultivator , etc.: agrorum, Liv. 2, 34, 11 ; 4, 25, 4 : agri, id. 40, 29, 3 ; cf. agricultor: virentis agelli, Hor. A. P. 117 : terrae, Cic. N. D.…

cultrārĭus.opening: culter , a slayer of the victim (for sacrifice), Suet. Calig. 32 ; Inscr. Orell. 4175 .

cultrix.opening: cultor . Prop., she who labors at or cares for a thing : earum rerum quas terra gignit ... augendarum et alendarum quandam cultricem esse, quae sit scientia atque ars agricolarum, Cic. Fin. 5, 14, 39 .— A female…

cultūra.opening: 1. colo . A cultivating, care, cultivation : agri, Varr. R. R. 2 , praef. § 4; Cic. Sen. 15, 54 ; Suet. Aug. 42 al. : agelli, Lucr. 5, 1366 ; cf. Cic. Agr. 2, 30, 83 ; 2, 35, 94 ; id. Fl. 29, 71 , and agricultura:…

cultus.opening: 1. colo . Prop., a laboring at, labor, care, cultivation, culture (rare): quod est tam asperum saxetum, in quo agricolarum cultus non elaboret? Cic. Agr. 2, 25, 66 : agricolae, id. Leg. 1, 1, 1 : agrorum, Liv. 4, 12, 7…

cŭlullus.opening: (acc. to Acro upon Hor. C. 1, 31, 11 , orig. a sacrificial vessel for liquids; later, in gen.), a drinking-vessel, beaker, goblet, cup, bowl , Hor. l. l.; id. A. P. 434 .

cūlus.opening: perh. kindr. with κοῖλος, of a curving form; cf. 1. anus , the posteriors, fundament , Cat. 23, 19 ; 33, 4 ; 97, 2 ; Mart. 3, 98, 1 .

cum.opening: (ante-class. ; freq. in MSS. of Cicero; the post-class. form is incorrectly given in many MSS. and edd.), conj. [pronom. stem ka- or kva- with acc. case ending]. Of time, when, as, while , sometimes = after, since . In…

Cūmae.opening: ( , Stat. S. 4, 3, 65 ; gen. Cymes, Sil. 13, 494 ), , = Κύμη , an ancient colony of the Chalcidians, in Campania, on the sea-coast, renowned on account of its Sibyl , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 61 ; Lucr. 6, 748 ;…

cumalter.grammar: significat cum altero, dictum ab antiquis ita brevitatis causā, ut sodes pro si audes, scilicet pro scias licet, sis pro si vis

cūmātĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. from κῦμα, with the Lat. ending ilis . Adj., of the waves : deus, i. e. Neptune, Commod. 10, 1 .— Esp., sea-colored, water-colored, blue : colos, Titin. ap. Non. p. 548, 11 (Com. Rel. v. 114 Rib.).— Subst. :…

cŭmĕra.opening: ( , , , Varr. L. L. 7, § 34 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 50, 7 ib.) [cf. Gr. καμάρα , Lat. camera], a chest, box , or basket , to keep grain in, Hor. S. 1, 1, 53 Acro; id. Ep. 1, 7, 30 ; for the utensils of a bride, Paul.…

cŭmīnātus.opening: ( ), , adj. cuminum , seasoned or mixed with cumin , Pall. Nov. 22, 5 .— Subst. : , , , cumin-spice , Apic. 1, 29 .

cŭmīnīnus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of cumin : oleum, App. Herb. 74 .

cŭmīnum.opening: ( ), , , = κύμῖνον , cumin, a plant : Cuminum (Cyminum), Linn.; said to produce paleness, Plin. 20, 14, 57, § 159 sq. ; Pall. Mart. 9, 17 : exsangue, Hor. Ep. 1, 19, 18 : pallens, Pers. 5, 55 .

cumprīmē.opening: adv., especially, particularly , Quadrig. ap. Gell. 17, 2, 14 : adprime crebrius est, cumprime rarius, traductumque ex eo est, quod cumprimis dicebant pro eo, quod est imprimis, Gell. ib.

cumquĕ.opening: ( or ), adv. cum-que , serves for the generalizing of any action, event, time, etc., however, whenever, howsoever, whensoever, -ever, -soever . Usu. with pronn. and pronom. advv.: quicumque, qualiscumque, etc.,…

cŭmŭlāre.opening: , = commissura renum, Veg. Art. Vet. 6, 1, 2 ; 6, 2, 2 Schneid. N. cr.

cŭmŭlātē.opening: adv. , v. cumulo, P. a. fin.

cŭmŭlātim.opening: adv. cumulatus , abundantly, in heaps, in abundance (ante- and post-class., and very rare): positum in doliis, Varr. R. R. 3, 15, 2 ; Prud. Apoth. 717 ; 739 .

cŭmŭlātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from cumulo.

cŭmŭlo.opening: v. a. , to form into a heap, to accumulate, heap , or pile up (class.). In gen. Prop. (mostly post-Aug.; esp. in Curt. and Tac.): materiem, Lucr. 1, 989 : nubila, id. 6, 191 ; 6, 518 : stipites, Curt. 6, 6 : harenas,…

cŭmŭlus.opening: Sanscr. çva, to swell; Gr. κυέω, κύω; cf. κῦμα , a heap , as coming to a point, a pile, a mass piled up (class.; esp. freq. in the signif. II.): in hoc immenso aliarum super alias acervatarum legum cumulo, Liv. 3, 34, 6…

cūnābŭla.opening: cunae , a cradle . Prop., Cic. Div. 1, 36, 79 .—Of the resting-place of young animals, Verg. G. 4, 66 ; Plin. 10, 33, 51, § 99 .— Meton. The cradle , i. e. the earliest abode, dwellingplace : Jovis parvi, Prop. 3 (4),…

cūnae.opening: ( , , Prud. Dipt. 112 ), , a cradle . Prop.: tune etiam cubitare solitu's in cunis puer? Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 81 : opus est cunis, incunabulis, id. Truc. 5, 13 ; Cic. Sen. 23, 83 ; id. Tusc. 1, 39, 93 ; Quint. 1, 1, 21 ;…

cunctābundus.opening: ( ), , adj. cunctor , lingering, loitering, delaying (very rare): (milites) cunctabundosque et resistentes egressos castris esse, Liv. 6, 7, 2 : nusquam cunctabundus nisi cum in senatu loqueretur, Tac. A. 1, 7 : verba,…

cunctāmen.opening: ( ), , cunctor , a delaying, hesitating , Paul. Nol. 24, 416 .

cunctātĭo.opening: ( ), , cunctor , a delaying, lingering , in a good or (more freq.) in a bad sense, a tarrying, delay, hesitation, doubt (subject., while mora is object.; freq. and in good prose): danda brevis cogitationi mora ... in…

cunctātor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who acts with hesitation or tardiness, a delayer, loiterer, lingerer (not in Cic.); in a bad sense, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 10, 3 : cunctato ex acerrimo bellatore factus, Liv. 6, 23, 5 .—In a good sense,…

Cunctātor.opening: a surname of the dictator Q. Fabius Maximus (prob. retained as a title of honor, from the reproach of his master of horse; v. 1. cunctator); cf. Liv. 30, 26, 9 ; 28, 40, 6 ; Quint. 8, 2, 11 , and cunctor.

cunctātrix.opening: cunctator , one who hesitates, acts deliberately (late Lat.): lenta virtus omnis et diuturna cunctatrix, Ambros. Ep. 67, 5 .

cunctātus.opening: , formerly assumed as P. a. of cunctor; in comp. , Plin. Ep. 2, 16, 4 ; Suet. Caes. 60 ; Tac. A. 1, 71 ; but in all these passages recent edd. read cunctantior, cunctantius; v. , P. a. and adv.

cunctĭcĭnus.opening: adj. cunctuscano , prop. sounding all together; hence, concordant, harmonious (opp.simplex), Mart. Cap. 9, § 905 .

daucum.opening: ( ), , , also , , , Scrib. Comp. 167 ; 170 ; 177 = δαῦκον , a plant of the parsnip or carrot kind , much used in medicine, Plin. 19, 5, 27, § 89 : probatissimus in Creta, id. 25, 9, 64, § 110 al. ; Cels. 5, 23, 3 al. In…

Daulis.opening: Δαυλίς , a city of Phocis , situated on an eminence, and celebrated as the scene of the fable of Tereus, Progne, and Philomela, Liv. 32, 18 ; Stat. Theb. 7, 344 .— A district in Phocis, on the frontier of Doris , =…

Daunus.opening: Δαῦνος , a fabulous king over a part of Apulia (whence it obtained the appellation Daunia ), father (or ancestor) of Turnus, and father-in-law of Diomedes , Verg. A. 10, 616 ; 688 ; 12, 22 al. ; Hor. Od. 3, 30, 11 ; 4,…

dautia.opening: = lautia, Paul. ex Fest. p. 68, 10 Müll.

Dāvīd.opening: , or vīdis ( gen. David, Aus. Ephem. 3, 84 : Davidis, Juvenc. 1, 151 ; acc. -vīda, Juvenc. 2, 577 : David, Vulg. 2 Reg. 23, 16 ), the second king of the Jews, and principal author of the Book of Psalms , Tert. adv. Jud.…

Dāvus.opening: ( ), , , a name given to Roman slaves , freq. in the comedies of Plaut. and Ter.; cf. also Hor. S. 1, 10, 40 ; 2, 5, 91 ; id. A. P. 114 ; Pers. 5, 161 ; 168 al. —Prov.: Davus sum, non Oedipus, Ter. Andr. 1, 2, 24 .

dē.opening: prep. perh. for ded; cf. Oscan dat, old abl. of pronom. stem da; cf. also Lith. praep. da, as far as; and the suffixes, old case-forms, -dam, -dem, -dum, -do, with the locative -de; v. Ribbeck, Beitr. z. L. v. d. Lat.…

dĕa.opening: ( dat. and abl. plur. : diis, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 7 ; Ins. Orell. 2076: deabus, Cn. Gell. ap. Charis. p. 39 P.; Aug. C. D. 7, 24 ; 3, 3 ; Apul. M. 4, p. 156: dis deabusque, Cic. Rab. Perd. 2, 5 ; id. fragm. ap. Prisc. p.…

dĕ-ăcĭnātus.opening: adj. acinus , cleared from the grapes : dolia, Cato R. R. 26 Schneid.

dĕactĭo.opening: = peractio, a finishing , Paul. ex Fest. p. 74, 11 Müll.

dĕalbātĭo.opening: dealbo , a whitewashing , Aug. Civ. D. 3, 14 .

dĕalbātor.opening: dealbo , who whitens over, a whitewasher, a pargeter, plasterer , Cod. Just. 10, 64, 1 .

dĕ-albo.opening: v. a. albus , to whiten over, to whitewash, to parget, plaster (good prose, but rare): columnas, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 55 fin. (twice): parietes, Pall. 1, 24, 1 ; Suet. Gall. 9 ; Vitr. 7, 4 .—Prov.: duo parietes de eadem…

dĕambŭlācrum.opening: deambulo , a place to walk in, a promenade, walk , Mamert. Grat. act. ad Julian. 9 ; Vulg. 3 Reg. 7, 2 .

dĕambŭlātĭo.opening: [id.), a walking abroad, promenading , Ter. Heaut. 4, 6, 2 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 141 ; Vulg. Ezech. 12, 4 .

dĕambŭlātōrĭum.opening: id. , a gallery for walking , Capitol. Gord. 3, 32 .

dĕ-ambŭlo.opening: v. n. , to walk abroad, walk much, to take a walk, to promenade (rare): aegrotus saliat decies et deambulet, Cato R. R. 127 fin. ; 156, 4 : eamus deambulatum, id. ap. Cic. de Or. 2, 63, 256 ; so in the supine , * Ter.…

dĕ-ămo.opening: v. a. , to be desperately in love with, to love dearly or passionately (ante-class.), "vehementius amare," Non. 97, 21 (cf. depereo ). Prop.: illa, quam tuus gnatus annos multos deamat, deperit, Plaut. Epid. 2, 2, 35 ;…

dĕ-argento.opening: v. a. argentum . * To deprive of money (anteclass.): depeculassere aliqua sperans me atque deargentassere, Lucil. ap. Non. 97, 8 . — To silver over, to plate with silver (late Lat.): idola deargentata et deaurata, Hier.…

dĕ-argūmentor.opening: v. dep. n. , to decide finally (late Lat.): super aliqua re, Claud. Mamert. de Statu An. 2, 7 .

dĕ-armo.opening: v. a. Aliquem, to disarm (except in particip., late Lat. for armis spoliare): dearmatus exercitus, Liv. 4 . 10, 7.— Aliquid, to deprive of power, blunt : pharetram expilet, sagittas dearmet, App. M. 5, p. 172, 25 .

dĕ-artŭo.opening: v. a. artus; cf. artuatus and artuatim . Lit. , to dismember, to rend limb by limb; hence, trop., to ruin : "quasi per artus concidere," Non. 95, 17 (only in the foll. passages): fallaciis opes, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 14 :…

dĕ-ascĭo.opening: v. a. 1, ascio , to hew or cut with an axe, to smoothe . Lit. (late Lat.): deasciato stipiti, wrought, smoothed , Prud. στεφ . 10, 381.— To rub out, efface : hunc titulum, Murat. Inscr. 1203, 9.— Trop. : aliquem, to…

dĕ-auro.opening: v. a. , to gild, to gild over (late Lat. for inaurare): cassidas et tegerent argento et deanrarent, Cod. Theod. 10, 22, 1; Tert. Idol. 8 : columnas, Vulg. Exod. 36, 36 : vestitus, id. Psa. 44, 9 : SIGNVM DEAVRATVM,…

dēbacchātĭo.opening: debacchor , passionate raving, fury : libidinis, Salv. Gub. D. 7 init.

dē-bacchor.opening: v. dep. n. , to rave like the Bacchantes, to rage without control, revel wildly (rare): si satis jam debacchatus es, leno, Ter. Ad. 2, 1, 30 sq. ; Hier. in Ies. 11, 37, 26 .— Poet. , of inanimate things, to rage : qua…

dē-bātŭo.opening: v. a. , to beat or thrust severely (obsc.), Petr. 69, 3 .

dēbellātor.opening: debello , a conqueror, subduer (rare; mostly poet. ): ferarum, * Verg. A. 7, 651 ; * Stat. Th. 9, 545 : Vespasianus Judaeorum debellator, Tert. Apol. 5 : durus, Vulg. Sap. 18, 15 .

dēbellātrix.opening: debellator , a conqueress, she that conquers (late Lat.).— Prop.: Phrygiac Graecia, Tert. Apol. 25 . — Trop. : pudoris et famae libido, Lact. 1, 9 .

dē-bello.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dē-bello.opening: v. n. and a. (not ante-Aug.; esp. freq. in Livy). Neutr., to bring a war to an end, to finish a war . So rare in the act. form: Aulius cum Ferentanis uno secundo proelio debellavit, Liv. 9, 16 ; cf. id. Epit. 33 ; id.…

dēbĕo.opening: ( , Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 24 infra , cf. Ritschl, Opusc. Phil. 2, 590), , v. a. de-habeo , (lit., to have or keep from some one : "qui pecuniam dissolvit, statim non habet id quod reddidit, qui autem debet , aes retinet…

dē-bĭbo.opening: v. a. , to drink of : flumen, Sol. 7, 27 .

dēbĭlis.opening: (old shortened form debil , v. Ritschl, Opusc. Phil. 2, 331), , adj. de-habilis; cf. Dig. 49, 16, 4, § 12: lit. unmanageable, wanting in flexibility or activity; hence , lame, disabled, crippled, infirm, debilitated,…

dēbĭlĭtas.opening: debilis , lameness , debility, infirmity, weakness (good prose). Lit. : linguae, Cic. Pis. 1 : membrorum, Liv. 33, 2 : pedis, Labeo ap. Gell. 4, 2, 4 : pedum, Tac. H. 1, 9 : aliqua corporis, * Suet. Calig. 26 fin. et…

dēbĭlĭtātĭo.opening: id. , a laming, maiming; weakness (rare). Lit. : praemium debilitationis consecutus, i. e. of mutilation of nose and ears, App. M. 2, p. 128, 15 .— Trop. : animi, * Cic. Pis. 36, 88 .

dēbĭlĭto.opening: v. a. debilis , to lame, cripple, maim; to debilitate, unnerve, disable, weaken (freq. and class.). Lit. Of personal objects: gladiatores, qui debilitati fuerint, Gai. Inst. 3, § 146 : contusi ac debilitati inter saxa…
