dēbĭtĭo.opening: debeo , an owing, indebtedness (extremely rare): pecuniae et gratiae, Cic. Planc. 28, 68 ; cf. Gell. 1, 4, 2 sq. : torquetur debitione dotis, Cic. Att. 14, 13, 5 .— Transf. , the debt , Ambros. de Tobia, 7, 25.

dēbĭtor.opening: id. , a debtor; cf.: nexus, obaeratus. Lit. (quite class.), Cic. Off. 2, 22, 78 ; id. Flacc. 20, 48 ; id. Pis. 35, 86 ; Caes. B. C. 3, 1 ; 3, 20 ; Quint. 3, 6, 84 ; * Juv. 16, 40 et saep.: aeris, * Hor. S. 1, 3, 86 .—…

dēbĭtrix.opening: debitor , a female debtor (post-class.). Lit. : mulier, Dig. 16, 1, 24 : fisci, ib. 49, 14, 47 .— Trop. : omnium delictorum debitrix anima est, the guilty cause, Tert. Anim. 35 .

dē-blătĕro.opening: v. a. , to prate of a thing, to babble, blab out (ante and post-class.): versuum multa milia, Gell. 9, 15, 10 ; id. 1, 2, 6 .—With acc. and inf. , Plaut. Aul. 2, 3, 1 ; Lucil. ap. Non. 96, 10 .

dē-būcĭno.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to trumpet forth (eccl. Lat.), trop., Tert. virg. vel. 13.

dē-căchinno.opening: v. a. , to deride, laugh to scorn (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Apol. 47 .

dĕcăchordum.opening: , = δεκάχορδον , a musical instrument of ten strings (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Psa. 91, 4 .

dĕcăchordus.opening: adj. , = δεκάχορδος , ten-stringed (late Lat.): cithara, Fulg. Myth. 1, 14 al.

dēcăcūmĭnātĭo.opening: decacumino , a lopping, cutting off the top : cupressi, piceae, cedri, Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 236 .

dē-căcūmĭno.opening: v. a. , to cut the top off, to top and lop (t. t. of agriculture): pampinum, Col. 4, 7, 3 : ulmum, id. 5, 6, 12 .

dē-călantĭco.opening: v. a. calantica , to deprive of one's hood, to plunder one: decalanticare, eburno speculo depeculassere, Lucil. ap. Non. 97, 9 dub.

dēcalco.opening: to plaster with lime, to whitewash = albo, κονιῶ , Gloss. Vet.

dēcălĕfăcĭo.opening: to warm thoroughly , ἐκθερμαίνω , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

dēcălesco.opening: to become warm , ἐκθερμαίνομαι , Gloss. Cyrill.

dēcălĭcātor.opening: de-calix , a hard drinker , καταπότης , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

dēcalvātio.opening: decalvo , the making bald , Hieron. Ep. 122, 1.

dē-calvo.opening: v. a. (calvus], to make bald, to remove the hair (late Lat.): locum corporis, Veg. A. V. 2, 48, 3 : Sampson a muliere decalvatus, shorn, Hier. adv. Jov. 1, 23 : pueros David decalvavit, Vulg. 1 Par. 19, 4 ; 1 Cor. 11, 6.

dĕcānĭa.opening: decanus , divisions of the zodiac , Manil. 4, 298 .

dĕcānĭcum.opening: id. , a building belonging to the church , Cod. Theod. 16, 5, 30 .

dē-căno.opening: v. a. , to celebrate by singing : Cererem, Prob. Cath. 1492 P.

dēcantātĭo.opening: decanto , talkativeness , as transl. of ἀδολεσχία , Hier. Ep. 106 , no. 49.

dē-canto.opening: v. a. (in the class. per. freq. in Cic.; elsewh. rare). To sing a thing off, to repeat in a singing manner (v. cano and canto). Usually with the secondary idea of something trite, worn out, absurd; to repeat often, to…

dĕcānus.opening: decem . A chief of ten, one set over ten persons (late Lat.). Over soldiers, Veg. Mil. 2, 8 .— Over monks, a dean , Hier. Ep. 22 , no. 35.— The chief of the corpse-bearers , Cod. Just. 1, 2, 4 ; 9 .— As a judge, Vulg.…

dĕcā^prōti.opening: , = δεκάπρωτοι , the ten chief men , magistrates in the municipia and colonies (pure Lat. decem primi), Dig. 50, 4, 3, § 10 ; ib. 18, § 26 .

dĕcā^prōtīa.opening: , = δεκαπρωτεία , the office and dignity of the decaproti, Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 26 .

dĕcargўrum.opening: a large silver coin ( = majorina), Cod. Theod. 9, 23, 1 .

dēcarmĭno.opening: v. a. de-carmen , to make prose of verse, to disarrange the order of the words in a verse: sed hic ordo nobis verborum faciendus est, ut versus hujus decarminata contextio ipsa se magis exponere videatur, Cassiod. in…

dē-carno.opening: v. a. 2, caro , to take off the flesh (late Lat.), Veg. A. V. 2, 27, 2 ; 2, 42, 1 ; 3, 6, 1 ; Apic. 7, 9 .

dĕcas.opening: , = δεκάς , a decade , Tert. de Praescr. 49 al. ; Mart. Cap. 7, § 734 .

dĕcastўlos.opening: adj. , = δεκάστυλος , having ten columns, decastyle , Vitr. 3, 1 fin.

dē-caulesco.opening: v. n. caulis , to form a stem, run to stalk : raphanus antequam decaulescat, Plin. 19, 7, 36, § 122 .

Dĕcĕbălus.opening: , = Δεκέβαλος , a Dacian king, subdued by Trajan , Tac. Agr. 41 ; Suet. Dom. 6 .

dē-cēdo.opening: ( inf. sync. decesse, Ter. Heaut. prol. 32 ; Cic. Fam. 7, 1, 2 ; Neue Formenl. 2, 536. The part. perf. decessus perh. only Rutil. Nam. 1, 313 ), v. n. , to go away, depart, withdraw . (For syn. cf.: linquo, relinquo,…

Dĕcĕlēa.opening: or , , , Δεκέλεια , a demos in Attica , 120 stadia from the Boeotian frontier , Nep. Alcib. 4, 7 ; Frontin. Strat. 1, 3, 9.

dē-cello.opening: v. a. , = declino, to turn aside, deviate , Lucr. 2, 219 Lachm. ex conj. (better depellere, with the MSS. v. Munro ad loc.).

dĕcem.opening: (DEKEM, Corp. Inscr. Lat. 1, 844 al.—The best MSS. and editt. vacillate often between the word and its sign X), num. [Sanscr. and Zend, daçan, Gr. δέκα , Old H. Germ. zëhan, Germ. zehn, Eng. ten], ten . Prop.: decem…

Dĕcember.opening: decem and -ber, = fer, Sanscr. bhar, to carry, bear: cf. Septem-ber, etc. , the tenth month of the Roman year , reckoned from March, and consequently our twelfth, December (containing, as now, 31 days): "dehinc quintus…

dĕcem-jŭgis.opening: jugum .— Lit. , adj., ten-yoked; hence (with currus understood), a ten-horse chariot (very rare), Suet. Ner. 24 ; Inscr. ap. Buleng. de Circo, 55.

dĕcem-mestris.opening: adj. mensis; cf.: bimestris, trimestris , of ten months : annus, Censorin. 11; 20.

dĕcem-mŏdĭus.opening: adj., containing ten modii (very rare): corbulae, Col. 12, 50, 8 .— Subst. : , , (al. decimodiae, sc. corbulae), baskets holding each ten modii , id. 12, 18, 2 .

dĕcem-pĕda.opening: pes , a ten-foot measuring rod , Cic. Mil. 27, 74 ; id. Phil. 14, 4, 10 ; id. Ac. 2, 41, 126 ; * Hor. Od. 2, 15, 14 al.

dĕcempĕdālis.opening: adj. decem-pes , ten feet long : spatium, Cod. 11, 42, 6.

dĕcempĕdātor.opening: decempeda , a land-measurer, land-surveyor , Cic. Phil. 13, 18, 37 .

dĕcem-plex.opening: adj. plico , tenfold , Varr. L. L. 10, § 43 Müll: numerus hostium, Nep. Milt. 5 .

dĕcemplĭcātus.opening: adj. decem-plex , multiplied by ten, ten times over , Varr. L. L. 6, § 38 Müll.

dĕcem-rēmis.opening: adj. remus; cf.: biremis, triremis , lit. ten-oared , i. e. having ten banks of oars : sc. navis, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 208 .

decem-scalmus.opening: adj. scalmus , lit. ten-thowled , i. e. having ten oars : actuariola, Cic. Att. 16, 3, 6 ; Orell, N. cr.

dĕcemvĭrālis.opening: adj. decemviri , decemviral, of or belonging to the decem viri : leges, i. e. of the Twelve Tables, Liv. 3, 57 fin. ; Gell. 20, 1, 3 : potestas, Liv. 3, 55 ; Tac. A. 1, 1 : annus, Cic. Rep. 2, 37 invidia, id. Brut. 14,…

dĕcemvĭrātus.opening: decemviri , the decemvirate, the rank or office of a decemvir; with regard to the decemv. agr. divid., Cic. Agr. 2, 22, 60 ; with regard to the decemv. legib. scrib., Liv. 4, 15 al.

dĕcem-vĭri.opening: (in MSS. and old edd. often Xviri), um or ōrum ( gen. -virum, Cic. Agr. 2, 15, 39 ; 2, 21, 56 ; id. Rep. 2, 36, 61 ; Varr. L. L. 9, § 85 Müll.; Liv. 27, 8 ; 40, 12 : -virorum only in Liv., where it is very freq.), vir ,…

dĕcennālis.opening: adj. decem-annus , of ten years, decennial (late Lat.; cf. decennis): bellum, i. e. Caesar's in Gaul, Amm. 15, 12, 6 ; of the Trojan war, Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 48 .— Subst. : DECENNALIA (ium, ), a festival celebrated…

dĕcennis.opening: adj. id. , of ten years (post-Aug.): bellum, of the Greeks before Troy, Quint. 8, 4, 22 ; also proelium, Petr. 89, 2, 8 : obsidio (Veiorum), Flor. 1, 12, 8 : equae, ten years old, Plin. 8, 44, 69 ; cf.: decenni major…

dĕcennĭum.opening: decennis . A period of ten years (post-class.), App. de Deo. Socr. p. 52, 7 al. — i. q. decennalia, Trebell. Gallien. 7 fin.

dĕcennŏvālis.opening: adj. decem novem , of nineteen years : cyclus, Cassiod., comp. pasch.

Dĕcennŏvĭum.opening: decem-novem , the Pomptine Marshes (19,000 feet in length), Cassiod. Var. 2, 32 sq. ; Inscr. Grut. 152, 8 .

dĕcentĭa.opening: decens , comeliness, decency : colorum et figurarum (with venustas), Cic. N. D. 2, 58 ; id. de Or. 3, 52, 200 .

Dĕcentĭus.opening: a general of Magnentius , Amm. 15, 6, 4 ; 16, 12, 5 ; Eutr. 10, 7 .— , , adj., pertaining to Decentius.—Subst. : , , , his adherents , Amm. 18, 9, 3 .

dēceptio.opening: decipio , a deceiving, deception (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 4 fin. al.; Cod. 11, 47, 6; Vulg. 1 . Macc. 16, 17.— Deceitfulness : vitae, Vulg. Sap. 14, 21 : divitiarum, id. Marc. 4, 19 .

dēceptor.opening: id. , a deceiver (late Lat. for fraudator), Sen. Thyest. 140 ; Lact. de Ira, 4, 8; August. Serm. 362, 18 .

dēceptōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , deceitful, deceptive (late Lat.), Aug. Doctr. Christ. 2, 23 .

dēceptrix.opening: deceptor , she that deceives : perniciosa adulatio, Lact. Epit. 6 fin.

dēceptus.opening: decipio , deception (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 6 : deceptui facilis, id. Anim. 18 .

dĕcēris.opening: , = δεκήρης (sc. ναῦς ), a ten-oared ship , i. e. a ship having ten banks of oars : Liburnicas, Suet. Calig. 37 (acc. to a conject. of Turneb. Adv. 22, 30; lect. vulg. de cedris).

dēcermĭna.opening: decerpo , leaves and boughs plucked off; decermina dicuntur quae decerpuntur purgandi causa, Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 7 Müll.; hence Trop. : Fortunae, i. e. beggars , qs. the refuse of Fortune , App. M. 1, p. 104, 29 .

dē-cerno.opening: (the syncop. forms decreram, etc., decrerim, etc., decresse are freq. in Cicero and Liv., also Plaut. Curc. 5, 3, 25 ; Ter. Hec. 1, 2, 73 ; 2, 1, 15 , but not in Caes., where is only decreverat, B. G. 4, 17; 5, 5 fin. ;…

dē-cerpo.opening: v. a. carpo , to pluck off, to tear, pull , or break off, to crop, gather (class.; most freq. in the poets.—Constr., usually aliquid ex aliqua re; less freq. aliquid de aliqua re). Lit. : acina de uvis decerpito, Cato…

dēcerptor.opening: decerpo , one who plucks or excerpts . Only Trop. , one who extracts or quotes : auctori tribui quod decerptori debui, August. c. Sec. Jul. 1, 16.

dēcertātĭo.opening: decerto , the decision of a dispute, a decisive conflict or contest : rerum omnium, Cic. Phil. 11, 9, 21 ; cf. Cod. Theod. 7, 20, 2, § 2 .

dēcertātor.opening: id. , he who goes through a decisive contest, a champion : veritatis, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 3, 16 and 34.

dē-certo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dē-certo.opening: v. n. and a. , to go through a decisive contest, to fight it out (but certare, to fight , without reference to the result. But the difference was not strictly observed. Thus Caesar uses often —15 times— decertare , but…

dē-cervīcātus.opening: adj. cervix , decollated, beheaded : cadavera, Sid. Ep. 3, 3 med.

dēcessĭo.opening: decedo , a going away, departure (opp. accessio—good prose). Lit. In gen.: is mecum saepe de tua mansione aut decessione communicat, Cic. Fam. 4, 4 fin. — Esp. The withdrawal, retirement of a magistrate from the…

dēcessor.opening: decedo, no. I. B. 2 , one who retires from a province he has governed; hence, with reference to his successor, a retiring officer (rare): successori decessor invidit, Cic. Scaur. Fragm. § 33, p. 187 ed. Beier; so Tac.…

dēcessus.opening: decedo , a going away, departure (opp. accessus—good prose). In gen.: post Dionysii decessum, Nep. Tim. 2, 3 .— Esp. The withdrawal, retirement of a magistrate from the province he has governed (in Cic. oftener…

dĕcet.opening: v. impers . [Sanscr. dacas, fame; Gr. δοκέω , to seem, think; Lat. decus, dignus]. It is seemly, comely, becoming,; it beseems, behooves, is fitting, suitable, proper (for syn. v. debeo init. ): decere quasi aptum esse…

Dĕcetia.opening: a town of the Aedui in Gallia Celtica, now Decize , on the Loire, in the Départ. de la Nièvre, Caes. B. G. 7, 33, 2 .

dēcharmĭdo.opening: v. a. de-Charmides , to un-Charmidize , i. e. to destroy one's identity as Charmides, also (with allusion to etym. of Charmides, "Son of joy," from χάρμα ) to end his happiness: rursum te decharmida, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2,…

Dĕcĭānus.opening: a Roman surname , Cic. Rab. perd. 9, 24; id. Fl. 32, 77 ; Tac. A. 14, 32 .

Deciātes.opening: a people of Liguria , Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 35 ; Flor. 2, 3 fin. : oppidum Deciatum, Mela, 2, 5, 3.

Dē^cĭdĭus.opening: a Roman proper name , esp. L. Decidius Saxa, a military officer who served under Caesar , Caes. B. C. 1, 66 ; Cic. Phil. 8, 3, 9 al.

dē-cĭdo.opening: v. n. cado , to fall off, fall down (class.). Lit. In gen.: decido de lecto praeceps, Plaut. Cas. 5, 2, 48 ; so, anguis decidit de tegulis, Ter. Ph. 4, 4, 26 : poma ex arboribus decidunt, Cic. de Sen. 19 fin. ; cf.: e…

dē-cīdo.opening: v. a. caedo , to cut off. Lit. (rare in ante-Aug. per.; more freq. abscīdo; not in Caes.): taleas oleaginas tripedaneas, Cato R. R. 45 : collum, Plaut. Merc. 2, 2, 37 : aures, Tac. A. 12, 14 : virgam arbori, id. G. 10 :…

dēcĭdŭus.opening: adj. 1. decĭdo , falling down or off, deciduous (chiefly in Pliny: folia, Laber. ap. Non. 100, 10 ; Plin. 18, 25, 60, § 226 ; 16, 24, 38, § 92 (where Freund assumes decīdua, cut off , cf. Cato R. R. 5, 7 , but without…

dĕcĭēs.opening: or , num. adv. [decem], ten times . Prop.: columbae decies anno pariunt, quaedam et undecies, Plin. 10, 53, 74, § 147 : decies seni, Ov. F. 3, 163 : HS. decies centena milia, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 10 Zumpt. More commonly…

dĕcĭma.opening: , v. decimus, no. I. B. and II. B.

dĕcĭmānus.opening: or (v. decimus), , adj. decimus , of or belonging to the tenth part. Prop. Of tithes , as a tax: ager, that pays tithes, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 6 ; cf.: frumentum, i. e. a tithe of the produce, id. ib. 2, 3, 5 fin. and 81:…

dĕcĭmārĭus.opening: adj., pertaining to tithes : leges, Cod. 8, 58.— Paying tithes, subject to tithes , Ambros. in Psa. 128 , Serm. 8, 4 al.

dĕcĭmātĭo.opening: decimo , the taking of a tenth . A tithing : omnis, Vulg. Tobiae, 1, 7 .— A selecting by lot of every tenth man for punishment, decimation , Capitol. Macr. 12 .— A tenth : adhuc in ea decimatio, Vulg. Isa. 6, 13 .

dĕcĭmātrus.opening: a holiday of the Falisci, ten days after the Ides , Fest. p. 257, 6 Müll.

dĕcĭmo.opening: or , , v. a. decimus . To select by lot every tenth man for punishment, to decimate (postAug., although the practice itself occurs as early as 283 A. U. C.; v. Liv. 2, 59 fin. ), Suet. Galb. 12 : cohortes, id. Aug. 24 :…

dĕcĭmus.opening: or (the latter form prevailed in the later law lang.; hence, decumanus), , adj. decem with superl. ending , the tenth . Prop.: mensis, Plaut. Am. 1, 2, 19 ; cf. Ter. Ad. 3, 4, 29 : legio, Caes. B. G. 1, 40 ; cf. ib. 41…

Dĕcĭmus.opening: proper names . Decimus, a Roman praenomen , abbrev. D. In the gens Claudia it was given only to patricians; but among the Junii and Laelii to plebeians also; cf. Varr. L. L. 9, § 61 Müll.—Hence, , , adj., named for…

dēcĭnĕrātus.opening: adj. de-cinis , wholly turned to ashes (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Valent. 32 .

dē-cĭnĕresco.opening: v. n. , to be wholly reduced to ashes (late Lat.): ut nullo igni decinerescat, Tert. Apol. 48 fin.

dē-cĭpĭo.opening: v. a. capio , primarily signifies to catch away, catch up, seize an animal while running, fleeing, etc. (whence decipula, a snare, trap); but occurs only in the trop. sense (acc. to capio, no. II. B.), to catch,…

dēcĭpŭla.opening: , and , , decipio , a snare, gin, trap. Lit. (late Lat.): plena avibus, Vulg. Jerem. 5, 27 ; Job 18, 10.— Trop. (ante- and post-class.). Fem. , Sid. Ep. 8, 10 med. ; Mart. Cap. 4, § 423 ; Vulg. Job 18, 10 .— Neutr. ,…

dē-circĭno.opening: v. a. , to make of a circular form, to round off (only in Manil.): arcum, Manil. 1, 296 : orbem, id. 3, 352 .

dēcīsĭo.opening: 2. decīdo . (Acc. to decīdo, no. II. B.) A diminishing : luminis, App. de Mundo, p. 71, 4.—Far more freq., and in good prose.— (Acc. to decīdo, no. II. A.) A decision, settlement, agreement : nostra de aequitate, Cic.…

dēcĭtans.opening: P. a. de-cĭto , causing to glide down , App. M. 2, p. 116, 4 .

Dĕcĭus.opening: , a. An ancient Italian praenomen : Decius Magius, Liv. 23, 7, 10 ; Vell. 2, 16, 2 al. — The name of an eminent plebeian gens at Rome . Its bestknown members were the two Decii (P. Decius Mus, father and son), who, as…

dēclāmātĭo.opening: declamo . Exercise in oratorical delivery, exercise or practice in speaking, declamation (class.; most freq. in Quint.): cum sit declamatio forensium actionum meditatio, etc., Quint. 4, 2, 29 ; cf. id. 2, 10, 4 ; 12 et…

dēclāmātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. declamatio , a little exercise in speaking, a short declamation (very rare), Gell. 6, 8, 4 ; Sid. Ep. 1, 4 .

dēclāmātor.opening: declamo , one who practises set speaking, a rhetorician, declaimer (diff. from orator , a practical speaker, Quint. 10, 2, 21 ): non enim declamatorem aliquem de ludo aut rabulam de foro, sed doctissimum et…

dēclāmātōrĭus.opening: adj. declamator , of or belonging to the exercise of speaking, declamatory, rhetorical (good prose): opus, Cic. de Or. 1, 16 fin. : illo genere duci et delectari, id. Q. Fr. 3, 3 fin. ; ef.: genus dicendi, Quint. 2, 10,…

dēclāmĭto.opening: v. , freq. and a. [declamo], to practise rhetorical delivery or declamation, to declaim (good prose; most frequent in Cic.). In a good sense. Absol. : commentabar declamitans (sic enim nunc loquuntur), saepe cum M.…

dē-clāmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dē-clāmo.opening: v. n. and a. — Rhetor. t. t., to exercise one's self in rhetorical delivery, to practise speaking, to declaim . For syn. cf.: dictito, concionor, pronuntio, palam dico, praedico, recito, declamito. (Class., most freq.…

dēclārātĭo.opening: declaro , a making clear or evident, a disclosure, exposition, declaration (very rare): animi tui, Cic. Fam. 10, 5, 2 : amoris tui? id. ib. 15, 21, 3 : sub eadem declaratione, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 30 fin. ; Vulg. Ps.…

dēclārātīvus.opening: adj. id. , serving for explanation, explanatory (postclass.): pars, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 30 and 33; Mart. Cap. 4, § 341 .— Adv. : , by way of explanation , Mart. Cap. 4, § 393 .

dēclārātor.opening: id. , one who declares or makes known, an announcer : ut honoribus nostris in campo declarator exsisteres, Plin. Pan. 92, 3 .

dē-clāro.opening: v. a. , to make clear, plain, evident (by disclosing, uncovering), to show, manifest, declare , etc., ἀποφαίνω (class.; most freq. in the trop. sense). For syn. cf.: monstro, demonstro, probo, confirmo, ostendo,…

dēclīnābĭlis.opening: adj. declino , that can be (grammatically) inflected , Prisc. p. 670 P.

dēclīnātĭo.opening: id. , a bending from a thing, a bending aside; an oblique inclination or direction (good prose). Lit. : lanceam exigua corporis declinatione vitare, Curt. 9, 7 fin. ; cf.: quot ego tuas petitiones parva quadam…

dēclīnātus.opening: id. , variation, inflection of words (cf. the prec. art. II. B. 2), Varr. L. L. 9, § 34 ; 51 ; 53 . But in Cic. Fin. 5, 7, 17 , the best reading is: declinatum dolorem, v. Madvig ad h. l.).

dēclīnis.opening: adj. id. , turning aside (perh. only in the two foll. places): declinia juga, Stat. Th. 5, 297 (quae declinarent et fugerent, Schol.). So of the retreating motion of the sea in ebb and flood: undae, ebbing, Luc. 4, 427…

dē-clīno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
dē-clīno.opening: v. a. and n. CLINO = κλίνω , orig. to bend from the straight path; to turn aside or away (freq. and class.). Lit. Act. : ego modo declinavi paullum me extra viam, Plaut. Aul. 4, 8, 11 ; cf.: sese rectā regione viai,…

dē-clīvis.opening: ( nom. n. declivum, Cassiod. in Psal. 16, 5 ; neutr. plur. once heterocl. decliva, Ov. M. 2, 206 ; also declivia, id. ib. 1, 39 et saep.; cf. acclivis and aplustre), adj. clivus , inclining downwards, sloping (for syn.…

dēclīvĭtas.opening: declivis , a sloping place, declivity , Caes. B. G. 7, 85, 4 .

dēcoctĭo.opening: decoquo (postclass.), a boiling down . Prop. Abstr.: lentisci hoc modo, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 165 .— Concret., a decoction , App. Herb. 77 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 3, 17 .— Trop. , of an association, a decoction, mixture…

dēcoctor.opening: decoquo, no. I. B. , one who has squandered his own or another's property, a ruined spendthrift, bankrupt , Cic. Phil. 2, 18 ; id. Cat. 2, 3 ; Catull. 41, 4: pecuniae publicae, Cod. Theod. 12, 1, 117 al. : bonorum…

dēcoctum.opening: , v. decoquo, no. II. A. b.

dēcoctus.opening: decoquo , a boiling down, seething : gemmae mellis decoctu nitescunt, Plin. 37, 12, 74, § 195 .

dēcollātĭo.opening: a beheading , Paul. Sent. 5, 17, 3 : τραχηλοκοπία, κεφαλῆς ἀποτομή , Vet. Gloss. ( = capitis amputatio, Dig. 48, 19, 28 ), from

dē-collo.opening: v. a. collum . * To take off from the neck : ex collo deponere, Non. 97, 25 : in tuo collo est: decolles cave, Caecil. ib.— Trop. , to deprive, rob of a thing: quibus fructibus me decollavi, Lucil. ap. Diom. p. 361 ,…

dē-cōlo.opening: ( old fut. perf. decolassit = decolaverit, Plaut. Cas. 2, 4, 28 ), , v. n. colum; lit., to trickle from or through; hence trop. , to come to naught, to fail (ante-class.): si spes decolabit, Plaut. Gapt. 3, 1, 37 ; cf.…

dē-cŏlor.opening: ( acc. plur. heterocl. decoloros, Prud. στεφ . 1, 113), adj., deprived of it's natural color, discolored, defaced, faded , etc. ( poet. , and in post-Aug. prose): decolorem sanguinem omnem exsorbuit, Cic. poet. Tusc. 2,…

dēcŏlōrātē.opening: adv. decoloro , degenerately, Comp. : quanto decoloratius vivat peccatrix anima, August. de Duab. Anim. 2, 2 .

dēcŏlōrātĭo.opening: decoloro , a discoloring : quaedam ex aliqua contagione, Cic. Div. 2, 27, 58 .

dē-cŏlōro.opening: v. a. , to deprive of its natural color, to discolor, stain, deface, soil , etc. Prop.: " decoloratur id cujus color vitiatur, non mutatur," Sen. Q. N. 2, 41 : quod mare Dauniae Non decoloravere caedes, * Hor. Od. 2, 1,…

dēcompŏsĭtus.opening: de-compono , adj., formed or derived from a compound word , = παρασύνδετος , Prisc. 664 P. al.

dē-concĭlĭo.opening: v. a. , to deprive of, take away : nihil deconciliares illi, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fest. p. 217, 28 .

dē-condo.opening: v. a. , to secrete by burying: alios in ventrem immensae beluae, Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 10 .

dē-contor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. , to hesitate, to be at a loss (perhaps only in Appuleius): unde potissimum caperet exordium, decontatur, App. M. 10, p. 239 ; id. ib. 7 , p. 198.

dē-cŏquo.opening: v. a. To boil away, boil down, diminish by boiling . Lit. : usque quo ad tertiam partem decoxeris, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 26 ; so acetum ad quartas, ad tertias, Col. 12, 34 ; Plin. 22, 25, 69, § 140 : in dimidiam partem,…

dĕcor.opening: deceo , what is seemly, becoming; comeliness, elegance, grace, beauty, ornament ( poet. word; in prose perh. not before the Aug. per.; esp. freq. in Quint.; v. decus). In gen.: Mobilibusque decor naturis dandus et…

dĕcŏrāmen.opening: decoro , ornament, decoration (in post-Aug. poetry): vittaque, majorum decoramen, Sil. 16, 269 : fluvii decoramina villae, Aus. Idyll. 10, 320 .

dĕcŏrāmentum.opening: id. , ornament, decoration (late Lat.): matronalia, Tert. Cult. femin. 12: canteriorum, Arn. adv. gent. 5.

dĕcōrē.opening: adv., suitably, properly; elegantly, beautifully , etc.; v. decorus fin.

dē-cŏrĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. corium , to deprive of the skin or outer covering; to skin, to peel (post-class., and very rare): Tert. Anim. 33 : amygdala decoriata, Pall. Jan. 15, 12 .

dĕcŏris.opening: , or , adj. decus , ornamented, adorned, elegant, beautiful (only in the follg. passages; hence nom. dub.; cf.: dedecor and indecoris ): magnam domum decoremque Ditem vexarant, Naev. ap. Prisc. p. 699 P.: equis et armis…

dĕcŏro.opening: v. a. decus , to decorate, adorn, embellish, grace, beautify (class, and freq.). Lit. , with abl. : Larem corona nostrum decorari volo, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 1 : oppidum ex pecunia sua locis communibus monumentisque, Cic.…

dĕcŏrōsus.opening: adj. decus , elegant, beautiful , Ambros. de Tob. 7 .

dēcortĭcātĭo.opening: decortico , a barking, peeling : angusta, Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 236 .

dē-cortĭco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. cortex , to deprive of the bark: to bark, to peel (rare), Plin. 16, 39, 74, § 188 : abietem, id. 16, 41, 80, § 221 : ficum, Vulg. Joel 1, 7 .

dĕcōrus.opening: adj. decor , Gr. εὐπρεπής . Becoming, fitting, seemly, proper, suitable, decorous (class.). With dat. : QVAE QVOIQVE DIVO DECORAE GRATAEQVE SINT HOSTIAE PROVIDENTO, Cic. Leg. 2, 8, 20 : color albus praecipue decorus deo…

dēcrēmentum.opening: decresco , a diminution, decrease (post-class. for deminutio): rerum atque hominum, Gell. 3, 10, 11 : lunae, App. M. 11, p. 257 .

dē-crĕmo.opening: v. a. , to burn up, consume by fire , Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 2 .

dē-crĕpĭtus.opening: adj. crepo (lit., noiseless; applied to old people, who creep about like shadows), very old, decrepit (mostly ante-class.): vetulus, decrepitus senex, Plaut. Merc. 2, 2, 43 ; so, senex, id. ib. 20 ; id. Asin. 5, 2, 13 ;…

dēcrescentĭa.opening: decresco , a decreasing, waning : quotidiana lunae, Vitr. 9, 4 fin. (for which, just before, deminutio).

dē-cresco.opening: v. n. Orig., to grow less, grow shorter, decrease, wane (as the moon, bodies of water, the length of the day, etc.): ostreae cum luna pariter crescunt pariterque decrescunt, * Cic. Div. 2, 14, 33 : crescunt loca…

dēcrētālis.opening: adj. decerno , belonging to or depending on a decree, decretal (post-class.): successio bonorum, Dig. 38, 9, 1 : pagina, Sid. Ep. 7, 9 .

dēcrētĭo.opening: id. , i. q. decretum, a decision, decree , Mart. Cap. poët. 1, p. 12.

dēcrētōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , belonging to a decision, decisive (post-Aug.): non accedit ad decretorium stilum, i. e. to a definitive sentence, Sen. Clem. 1, 14 : intrepidus horam illam decretoriam (viz., the hour of death) prospice, id.…

dēcrētum.opening: a decree, ordinance, principle , etc., v. decerno fin.

dēcrētus.opening: , um. Part. , from decerno.— Part. , from decresco.

dē-crusto.opening: v. a. , to peel off, split off, disintegrate : cum saxa frigus decrustaret, et aquas in crustam verteret, Ven. Vit. Germ. 77.

dē-cŭbo.opening: v. n. , to lie away from, out of , e. g. one's bed: de eo lecto non decubat, Fap. Pictor ap. Gell. 10, 15, 14 .

dē-culco.opening: v. a. , to tread down, trample upon (post-Aug. and rare): bacas in qualo pedibus, Plin. 17, 10, 11, § 61 : aspros molares, Stat. Th. 1, 362 ; Tert. Apol. 46 .

dē-culpātus.opening: adj. culpo , faulty, censurable : verbum, Gell. 19, 10, 10 .

dĕcŭmātes.opening: adj. decimus , belonging to tithes, tithe- : agri, subject to tithes or tribute, tithe-land , Tac. G. 29 fin. , v. Orell. ad h. 1.

dē-cumbo.opening: v. n. To lie down , sc. in bed or on a couch, to recline at table, to lie ill, be confined by sickness (good prose), Cato R. R. 156, 4 : super lectum, Suet. Ner. 48 : in aureo lecto, id. Caes. 49 : hospes me ad cenam…

dĕcuncis.opening: decem-uncia , a measure or weight of ten unciae , Rhem. Fann. de Ponder. 46.—Also , Prisc. de Ponder. p. 1348 P.

dĕcŭplus.opening: adj. decem-plus , tenfold : verbum, Vulg. Dan. 1, 20 .

dĕcŭrĭa.opening: decem, after the analogy of centuria, from centum , a division consisting of ten, a company of ten, a tithing: decuria, decade , Gr. δεκάς (cf. Eng. dozen). Thus Romulus, acc. to Dion. Hal. 2, 7, p. 82 d, formed out of…

dĕcŭrĭālis.opening: adj. decuria , of or belonging to a decuria : leges, Cod. Just. 11, 13, 2 ; hence subst., a member of a decuria (mostly post-class.): numerus, Tert. Anim. 37 : DECVRIALIVM GERVLORVM DISPENSATOR, Inscr. Orell. 874 ; 976…

dĕcŭrĭātim.opening: adv. id.; cf. centuriatim , by decuriae , v. Charis. p. 165 P.

dĕcŭrĭātĭo.opening: 1. decurio , a dividing into decuriae : tribulium, descriptio populi, etc., Cic. Planc. 18, 45 .

dĕcŭrĭātus.opening: id. , a dividing into decuriae : ubi (milites) ad decuriatum aut centuriatum convenissent, Liv. 22, 38 .

dĕcŭrĭo.opening: (also DECURES decuriones, Paul. ex Fest. p. 71, 22 , and 75, 9 Müll.; and DECVRIONVS, the same, ib. 49, 16 ), id. , the head or chief of a decuria, a decurion . The name was first given by Romulus to the head of the…

dĕcŭrĭōnālis.opening: adj. 2. decurio , belonging to a decurion , βουλευτικός , Gloss. Philox.; Inscr. Grut. 469, 4 .

dĕcŭrĭōnātus.opening: id. , the office and dignity of a decurion; of cavalry, Cato ap. Fest. p. 201, 28 M.; in the municipia, Traj. ap. Plin. Ep. 10, 114 ; Dig. 50, 2, 2 sq. ; Inscr. Orell. 164 al.

dē-curro.opening: , cŭcurri or curri (cf.: decucurrit, Caes. B. G. 2, 21 ; Tac. A. 2, 7 ; Suet. Ner. 11 : decucurrerunt, Caes. B. G. 2, 19, 7 ; Petr. 64, 3 : decucurrerat, Liv. 1, 12 : decucurrisse, id. 25, 17 ; also, decurrerunt, id.…

dēcursĭo.opening: decurro , a running or flowing down (less freq. than decursus; not in Cic.). In gen.: aquae, Arn. 2, p. 84 .— In partic., milit. t. t., a manœuvre, military exercise, evolution, a descent, hostile attack , Brutus ap.…

dēcursōrĭus.opening: , um., adj., pertaining to the race-course : termini, Innoc. rei agr. p. 223 Goes.

dēcursus.opening: decurro , a running down, downward course, descent; declivity (class.). Lit. In gen.: montibus ex altis magnus decursus aquaï, Lucr. 1, 284 ; 5, 264 ; 944 ; Ov. M. 15, 266 : rapidus (amnium), Verg. A. 12, 523 : navium,…

dēcurtātio.opening: decurto , a mutilation : caudae, Mar. Victor. 2511 P.

dē-curto.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1 (only in the part. praes. and perf. ), v. a. , to cut off, curtail, mutilate . Lit. : radices, Plin. 25, 5, 21, § 53 : amicum undique decurtatum, cum aures illi nasumque abscidisset, in cavea diu…

dē-curvātus.opening: adj., bent, curved back : pars aratri, Non. 80, 20 .

dĕcussātim.opening: adv. decusso , in the form of a Roman ten (X), crosswise , Vitr. 1, 6 ; Col. 12, 56, 1 .

dĕcussātĭo.opening: id. , an intersecting of two lines crosswise, decussation , Vitr. 1, 6 ; 10, 11 .

dēcussĭo.opening: decutio , a shaking off, rejection , trop.: amputatio et decussio redundantioris nitoris, Tert. Cult. fem. 9.

dĕcussis.grammar: is i, a mutilated form used by the Agrimensores m.
dĕcussis.opening: (also , , p. 231, 243, and 265, ed. Goes.), decem-as . The number ten : ex singularibus rebus, quae μονάδες apud Graecos dicuntur perficitur decussis, Vitr. 3, 1 (cf. the art. as, no. I.).—Hence, * decussis sexis, or in…

dĕcusso.opening: v. a. decussis, no. I. , to divide crosswise , in the form of an X, to decussate , * Cic. Univ. 7 med. ; Col. 3, 13, 12 ; 4, 17, 6 al.

dē-cŭtĭo.opening: v. a. quatio , to shake off, strike or beat off, cast off (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; not in Caes. or Cic.). Lit. : decussa Cydonia ramo, Prop. 3, 13 (4, 12), 27: lilia, Ov. F. 2, 707 : summa papaverum capita…

dēcŭtĭo.opening: v. a. de-cutis , to deprive of skin, to flay , Tert. ad Nat. 1, 14 .

dē-damno.opening: v. a. (to release from condemnation, i. e.), to absolve, acquit : aliquem, sceleris manifestum, Tert. Pudic. 15 .

dē-dĕcet.opening: v. impers. (very rarely pers., v. infra , II.), it is unseemly, unsuitable, unbecoming : decere quasi aptum esse consentaneumque tempori et personae, etc.... contraque item dedecere, Cic. Or. 22, 74 .— Prop. (class.;…

dē-dĕcor.opening: adj., unseemly, unbecoming, shameful, vile (rare): dedecorem amplexi vitam, Stat. Th. 11, 760 : alga, Aus. Ep. 9, 5 : dedecores inultique caedebantur, Sall. Hist. 3, 91 (ap. Prisc. p. 699 P.).

dēdĕcŏrāmentum.opening: dedecoro , disgrace, dishonor , Gracch. ap. Isid. Orig. 2, 21, 4 (with inhonestamentum and flagitium).

dē-dĕcŏrātĭo.opening: id. , disgrace, dishonor (late Lat.), Tert. Cor. mil. 14; id. Anim. 34 .

dēdĕcŏrātor.opening: id. , one who dishonors; a reviler, blasphemer : deorum, Tert. Apol. 14 .

dē-dĕcŏro.opening: v. a. , to disgrace, dishonor, bring to shame (class.): mores, quibus boni se dedecorant, Plaut. Trin. 2, 2, 23 : me flagitiis suis, id. Bacch. 3, 3, 95 ; cf.: se flagitiis, Sall. J. 85, 42 ; * Suet. Ner. 36 ; Ter. Hec.…

dē-dĕcŏrōsus.opening: adj., disgraceful, dishonorable (post-Aug., and very rare): nex, Aur. Vict. Epit. 39 fin.—Comp. , Hier. in Jes. 16, 58, 10 .— Adv. : , disgracefully : vixi, turpius peream, Nero ap. Aur. Vict. Epit. 5 fin.

dē-dĕcōrus.opening: adj., disgraceful, dishonorable, shameful (very rare), Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 73 : majoribus suis, Tac. A. 3, 32 ; id. ib. 12, 47 .

dē-dĕcus.opening: disgrace, dishonor, infamy, shame (for syn. cf.: offensio, contumelia, infamia, ignominia, turpitudo, obscoenitas, injuria—freq. and class.). In gen.: eos dolores atque carnificinas per dedecus atque maximam contumeliam…

dēdĭcātĭo.opening: dedico , dedication, consecration : aedis, Liv. 2, 27 : theatri, Plin. 7, 48, 49, § 158 ; Suet. Claud. 21 : pontis, id. Calig. 32 : domus Dei, Vulg. 1 Esdr. 6, 16: statuae, id. Dan. 3, 2 al.

dēdĭcātīvus.opening: adj. dedico in the later philosoph. lang. = affirmativus, affirmative (opp. abdicativus): propositio, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 31, 23 al. — Adv. : , affirmatively : concludere, Mart. Cap. 4, § 409 .

dēdĭcātor.opening: id. , one who dedicates; hence, a founder, author (eccles. Lat.): damnationis nostrae, Tert. Apol. 5 ; id. Car. Christ. 17 .

dē-dĭco.opening: (in the tmesis : data deque dicata, Lucil. ap. Non. 287, 28 ), v. a. , to give out tidings, a notice , etc.; hence, to affirm, declare, announce any thing (cf. de in denuncio and depromo). In gen. (so only ante- and…

dēdignātĭo.opening: dedignor , a disdaining, refusal (post-Aug., and rare): tacita, Quint. 1, 2, 31 : parendi, Plin. Pan. 18, 1 .

dē-digno.opening: v. a. , collat. form of dedignor: tumulos aut ossibus urnas dedignant animae, Dracont. Carm. 9, 28 (Duhn).

dē-dignor.opening: v. a. dep. , to reject as unworthy, to disdain, scorn, refuse (most freq. in Ov.; perh. not ante-Aug.). With two accs. : quos ego sim toties jam dedignata maritos, * Verg. A. 4, 536 ; so, aliquem maritum, Ov. H. 16, 195…

dē-disco.opening: v. a. , to unlearn, to forget , sc. what one has learned (rare, but class.). With acc. : qui, quod didicit, id dediscit, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 56 ; cf.: multa oportet discat atque dediscat, Cic. Quint. 17 fin. ; so, haec…

dēdĭtīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. deditio , belonging to a surrender or capitulation; and subst. , , , one who has surrendered or capitulated, a captive : quicquid deinde patiemur, dediticii vestri passuri, Liv. 7, 31 ; cf. Gai. Inst. 1, 14…

dēdĭtim.opening: adv., by surrender; acc. to Diom. p. 402 P. [dedo].

dēdĭtĭo.opening: dedo, no. I. B. , a (military) giving up, a surrender, capitulation (freq. in the historians).—With subj. gen. : deditio sui, Curt. 5, 1, 18 .— Plur. : deditiones cohortium, Tac. H. 3, 70 . —With gen. obj. : ipsius…

dē-do.opening: ( infin. pass. parag. : dedier, Liv. 1, 32 ), , v. a. , lit., to give away, give up from one's self; hence, with respect to the term. ad quem, to give up any thing to one, to surrender, deliver, consign, yield (stronger…

dē-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. , to cause one to unlearn something, to unteach, teach the opposite of (rare, but class.). With double acc. : aliquem geometriam, Cic. Fin. 1, 6, 20 : regnorum gaudia temet, Stat. Th. 2, 409 .—* With acc. pers.…

dēdŏlentĭa.opening: the abandonment of grief, ceasing to lament , ἀπαλγησία , Vet. Gloss.

dē-dŏlĕo.opening: v. n. , to give over grieving, grieve no more (rare), Ov. F. 3, 480 ; id. R. Am. 294 .

dē-dŏlo.opening: v. a. , to hew away, to hew smooth, to hew : partes putres pedamentorum, Col. 4, 26, 1 : ridicas, id. 11, 2, 12 : arborem, Plin. 16, 39, 74, § 188 : vasculum crystallo dedolatum, smoothed, inlaid, App. M. 6, p. 178 :…

dē-dūco.opening: ( imper. : deduc, Cic. Rep. 1, 21, 34 ; old form, deduce, Ter. Eun. 3, 3, 32 ), 3, v. a. , to lead or bring away, to lead, fetch, bring or draw down (for syn. cf.: duco, comitor, prosequor, persequor, stipo, sequor,…

dēductus.opening: deduco , a drawing or dragging down (rare): ponderis, App. M. 1, p. 109, 28 (in Cic. Off. 2, 4, 14 , the true reading is: ductus aquarum).

dēductĭo.opening: deduco , a leading away, leading on , in accordance with the different acceptations of the primitive word. Lit. In gen.: rivorum a fonte, a leading or conducting off , Cic. Top. 8, 33 ; cf.: Albanae aquae, id. Div. 1,…

dēductīvus.opening: adj. deduco , derivative : nomina, Pomp. Comm. art. Donat. 19, 4, p. 202 K.

dēductor.opening: id. . One who brings; a guide, teacher (late Lat.): alicujus, Tert. Apol. 21 : veritatis, Tert. Cor. mil. 4.— (Acc. to deduco, no. 1. B. 5.) One who accompanies or attends on a candidate for office, an attendant , Q.…

dēductōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or for drawing off or draining (post-class.): medicamenta, aperient, purgative, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 19 : cuniculus (in stabulis), Veg. Vet. 1, 56 . Also subst. : , , , a drain : liquoris, Pall. Nov. 7, 21 .

dēdux.opening: adj. id. . Derived , descended , Symm. Ep. 8, 68 .— = conditor, on a coin ap. Eckhel. IV. p. 347.

dĕ-ēbrĭātus.opening: adj., made drunk, inebriated , Cassiod. Complex. 1 ; ad Thessal. 5 al.

dĕ-ĕo.opening: , very doubtful; defended by Gronov. ad Stat. Th. 2, 551 ; cf.: ullis ad signa deeuntibus, Sall. Fragm. in Mai. Auct. Class. 1, p. 418 (dub.: ex redeuntibus corruptum, Dietsch, Sall. Hist. 3, 67, 2 ).

dĕ-erro.opening: (in the poets dissyllabic, Lucr. 1, 711 ; Verg. E. 7, 7 al. ), āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. , to wander away, stray, go astray, go the wrong way, lose one's way (rare, but class.). Lit. : deerrare a patre, Plaut. Men. 5, 9, 54…

dēfaecābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. defaeco , that may be easily cleansed : cisterna, Sid. Ep. 1, 5 .

dēfaecātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a cleansing, purifying : carnis, Tert. Anim. 27 .

dē-faeco.opening: ( , or ; cf. Ritschl ad Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 2 ), , v. a. faex , to cleanse from dregs; to refine, purify, defecate, clarify (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : vinum, Col. 12, 33 ; Plin. 18, 26, 63, § 232 : vindemiam,…

dē-fāmātus.opening: adj. fama , dishonored, infamous (post-class.): homo turpitudine pristinae vitae defamatissimus, Gell. 18, 3, 3 ; cf. id. 14, 2, 10 : vocabula, id. 9, 2 fin.

dēfāmis.opening: adj. de-fama , shameful : mors, App. M. 9, p. 224 fin.

dē-fānātus.opening: adj. fanum , profaned, desecrated, unholy (late Lat.): spatiola, Arn. 4, p. 153 ( Inscr. Orell. 4352 dub.; Gervasio reads: DE EA NATIS).

dē-fărīnātus.opening: adj. farina , pulverized, reduced to flour : semen, Tert. adv. Valent. 31 .

dēfătīgātĭo.opening: or , , defatigo . Act., a wearying, tiring out, fatiguing , Hirt. B. G. 8, 27, 4 ; Cic. Sen. 23, 86 ; id. de Or. 3, 44 ; id. N. D. 2, 23, 59 .— Pass., weariness, fatigue, exhaustion , Caes. B. G. 3, 19, 3 ; Auct. Her.…

dē-fătīgo.opening: or , , v. a. , to weary out, tire a person; to fatigue; to exhaust . (For syn. cf.: fatigo, fessus, lassus, langueo, languidus, defessus. —Freq. and class.) Lit. Act. : cum crebro integri defessis succederent nostrosque…

dēfectĭo.opening: deficio . Defection, desertion, rebellion, revolt . Lit. : rebellio facta post deditionem, defectio datis obsidibus, Caes. B. G. 3, 10 ; 5, 26 ; 6, 3, 4 ; Liv. 7, 42 ; 23, 12 : Ampsivariorum a tergo, in the rear (of…

dēfectīvus.opening: adj. [deficio, no. III.), imperfect, defective (post-class.): et abortiva genitura, Tert. adv. Val. 14 : febris, intermittent fever, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 10 .— In gramm.: nomina, verba, some of whose forms are wanting,…

dēfector.opening: deficio, no. I. , one who revolts from another; a revolter, rebel (post-Aug.): parata in defectores ultione, Tac. A. 1, 48 ; 12, 50 fin. ; id. H. 3, 12 ; Suet. Ner. 43 ; Just. 16, 1, 13 al. : patris sui defectores, Tac.…

dēfectrix.opening: adj. acc. to deficio, no. III. , defective, imperfect : virtus, Tert. adv. Val. 38 .

dēfectus.opening: deficio . (For defectio, no. I.) Defection, revolt : magno animo defectum eorum tulit, Curt. 7, 19, 39 Mützell.: legionum, Capitol. Macr. 8 .— ( = defectio, no. III.) A failing, failure, lack, disappearance (freq. in…

dē-fendo.opening: ( infin. pass. parag. : defendier, Verg. A. 8, 493 : Juv. 15, 157 .— Part. gen. plur. sync. : defendentum, Verg. A. 11, 886 ), , v. a. arch.: FENDO; cf. Sanscr. han (ghan), to smite; Gr. θείνω; hence, also offendo,…

dē-fēnĕro.opening: v. a. , to involve in debt , Ambros. de Tobia 9 .—Hence, P. a. : , , overwhelmed by debt, exhausted by usury (post-class.): plurimis creditoribus defeneratus, App. Mag. p. 322, 21 ; Ambros. Ep. 7, 1 .

dēfensātrix.opening: id. , she who defends , Prob. p. 1452 P. (in Cicero, defenstrix, q. v.), Ambros. Hexaem. 6, 9, 69 .

dēfensĭbĭlis.opening: adj. id. , easily defended : murus, Cassiod. de Anim. 2 .— , adv. : , defensibly , Cassiod. in Psa. 79, 12 .

dēfensĭo.opening: defendo, no. II. , a defending, defence . Prop.: Remis cum spe defensionis studium propugnandi accessit, Caes. B. G. 2, 7, 2 .—With gen. subj. : urbium, id. ib. 7, 23, 5 ; id. B. C. 2, 7 fin. : ad istam omnem orationem…

dēfensĭto.opening: v. a. freq. [defenso], to defend often, to practise defending (perh, only in the foll. passages): haec non acrius accusavit in senectute, quam antea defensitaverat, Cic. Ac. 2, 22 ; cf. ib. 2, 45, 139 : causas, id.…

dēfenso.opening: v. a. intens. [defendo]. * To fend off diligently, ward off : metus, Stat. S. 5, 2, 105 .— To defend diligently, protect (rare; mostly ante-class. and poet. , not in Cic. or Caes.): moenia, Plaut. Rud. 3, 3, 30 ; Sall.…

dēfensor.opening: , rar. id. . One who fends, wards, averts , or keeps off : necis, Cic. Mil. 22, 58 : periculi, id. Mur. 2 .— A defender, protector . In gen. (for syn. cf.: tutor, praeses, vindex, cognitor, curator, patronus, advocatus,…

dēfensōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to defence (late Lat.): judicia bonorum, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 14 al.

dēfenstrix.opening: defensor , she who defends , Cic. ap. Prisc. p. 1120 P.

dē-fĕro.opening: v. a. , to bear or bring away a thing from a place; to bear, carry, bring down . Lit. In gen. Without stating the terminus (not very freq.): roseam Auroram per oras Aetheris, Lucr. 5, 656 ; 5, 273 ; 6, 639 : Rhodanus…

Dēfĕrunda.opening: , perh. a goddess that presided over the bringing of offerings , Inscr. Fratr. Arval. ap. Orell. I. p. 390.

dē-fervĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to seethe or cause to boil .— Prop.: brassicam bene, Cato R. R. 157, 9 : aquam in aëno, Vitr. 8, 5 : radicem in vino, Plin. 23, 7, 64, § 129 .—* Transf. : aër defervefactus in pulmone, heated , Varr. ap. Lact.…

dē-fervĕo.opening: v. n. , to boil thoroughly; of wine, to ferment completely , Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 85 ; of lime and water, to effervesce, Vitr. 7, 2, 1 .— Trop. , to subside : indignatio, Vulg. Esth. 2, 1 .

dē-fervesco.opening: (defervi, Ter. Ad. 1, 2, 72 ; Cic. Clu. 39, 108 ; id. Or. 30, 107 ; Cato R. R. 96, 1 ; Plin. Ep. 9, 16, 2 al. : deferbui, Cic. Cael. 18, 43 ; 31, 77 ; Col. 12, 20, 2 et saep.), , v. n. (post-Aug.), to cease boiling,…

dē-fĕtiscor.opening: (in MSS. sometimes defatiscor), fessus, 3, v. dep. n. , to become tired or wearied; to grow weary, faint; to be exhausted . (For syn. v. defatigo. As a verb. fin. ante-class. and rare, but class. and freq. in the part.…

dēfĭcĭentĭa.opening: the wanting, want (late Lat.), Paul. Nol. 23, 8 .

dē-fĭcĭo.opening: ( perf. subj. : defexit, an old formula in Liv. 1, 24 fin. , see below, no. III. fin. In the pass., besides the regular form deficior, ante- and postclass., once in Verg., Propert., and Livy, like fīo, eri: defit, Enn.…

dē-fīgo.opening: v. a. , to fasten down or in; and with especial reference to the terminus, to drive, fix , or fasten into (class.). — Lit. : in campo Martio crucem ad civium supplicium defigi et constitui jubes, Cic. Rab. perd. 4; so,…

dēfĭgūrātus.opening: adj. In gramm., declined, derived : nomina, Prisc. p. 638 P.

dē-fingo.opening: v. a. , to form, to put in shape, to fashion (very rare; prob. belonging properly to the vulgar lang.; hence in Hor., by way of sarcasm): panem, Cato R. R. 74 and 121.—Sarcast. of coarse poetic description: dum Defingit…

dēfīnĭenter.opening: adv. definio , distinctly : agnoscere, etc., August. in Joan. Tr. 14, 8 .

dēfīnĭo.opening: v. a. To bound, to set bounds to; to limit, terminate, define (for syn. v. decerno—freq. in Cic.). Lit. : ejus fundi extremam partem oleae directo ordine definiunt, Cic. Caecin. 8, 22 ; cf. id. Rep. 2, 6 : orbes caeli…

dēfīnītĭo.opening: definio . * A bounding, a boundary : AREA INTRA HANC DEFINITIONEM CIPPORVM CLAVSA VERVBVS, Inscr. Orell. 736 .— A limiting, prescribing, defining; a definition, explanation (freq. only in Cicero; cf. definio): ut…

dēfīnītīvus.opening: adj. definio . Definitive, explanatory . So in the rhet. lang. of Cicero: constitutio, Inv. 2, 17; cf. ib. 1, 13 : causa, id. Top. 24 fin. And in the later jurid. Lat.: sententia, a decisive, definitive sentence, Cod.…

dēfīnītor.opening: definio, no. I. B. 1 , one who determines, settles, appoints , (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 10 .

dēfīnītus.opening: Part. and P. a. of definio.

dēfīŏcŭlus.opening: humorously compounded from defit and oculus , who lacks an eye, one-eyed , Mart. 12, 59, 9 .

dēfixĭo.opening: enchantment , νεκρομαντίαι, κατάδεσμοι , Gloss. Lat. Gr. [defigo, no. II. B. 2, b.].

dēflā^grātĭo.opening: deflagro , a burning up, consuming by fire, conflagration (perhaps only in Cic.). Prop.: futura aliquando caeli atque terrarum, Cic. Div. 1, 49, 111 ; cf.: terrarum omnium, id. Fin. 3, 19 fin. — Trop. , destruction ,…

dēflā^gro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dēflā^gro.opening: v. n. and a. To burn down, to be consumed by fire (freq. only in Cic.; cf. conflagro). Neutr . Lit. : qua nocte natus esset Alexander, eadem Dianae Ephesiae templum deflagravisse, Cic. N. D. 2, 27 fin. ; id. Div. 1, 17…

dē-flammo.opening: v. a. , to deprive of flame, to put out, extinguish : taedam, Ap. M. 5, p. 172, 26.

dē-flecto.grammar: xi, xum, 3 v. a. and n.
dē-flecto.opening: v. a. and n. Act., to bend downwards or aside, to turn aside or in another direction . Lit. : ramum olivae, Col. 5, 11, 14 ; cf.: palmitem, id. 4, 26, 3 ; Catull. 62, 51; Plin. 17, 23, 35, § 204 : tela (Venus), Verg. A.…

dē-flĕo.grammar: ēvi, ētum, 2 v. a. and n.
dē-flĕo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. To weep over a person or thing; to lament, deplore, bewail (for syn. cf.: deploro, ejulo, ploro, lacrimo, lamentor, fleo —class.): te cinefactum deflevimus, Lucr. 3, 907 : Numam, Ov. M. 15, 487 :…

dēflētĭo.opening: defleo, no. II. , a violent weeping (late Lat.), Juvenc. 4, 122 .

dēflexĭe.opening: deflecto , a turning or bending aside (late Lat.). Lit. : certa meatus solis, Macr. Sat. 1, 17 .— Trop. : cupiditatum, Naz. Pan. Const. 5.

dēflexus.opening: deflecto , a bending, turning aside (post-class.), in the trop. sense: humani animi ab odio ad gratiam deflexus, Val. Max. 4, 2 ; cf. id. 7, 3 : a virtute, Ambros. in Psa. 1, § 23 .

dē-flo.opening: v. a. To blow off or away , Varr. R. R. 1, 64 .— To blow off, to cleanse by blowing , Plin. 28, 2, 5, § 27 . — To blab , Ambros. Ep. 47, 2 .

dē-floccātus.opening: adj. floccus , shorn of locks, bald : senes, Plaut. Ep. 5, 1, 10 .

dēflōrātĭo.opening: defloro , a plucking of flowers .— Transf. , Tert. adv. Valent. 12 .— Trop. , Cassiod. 12 : virginitatis, a deflouring, Ambros. Ep. 64 .

dēflōrĕo.opening: v. n. , to shed its blossoms (very rare): vitis pejus defloret, Col. 5, 6, 36 .

dē-flōresco.opening: v. n. , to drop its blossoms; to fade, wither . Lit. : omne frumentum ... deflorescit, Col. 2, 11 fin. ; so in praes. , id. 2, 10, 19 ; Plin. 18, 29, 69, § 286 : cum (faba) defloruit, exiguas (aquas) desiderat, id. 18,…

dēflōro.opening: de-flos , v. a. , lit. to deprive of flowers , Dracont. 1, 588 .— Transf. : fulgores solis, Amm. 20, 11, § 28 : deflorato virginitatis pudore, Ambros. de Jacob. 2, 7, 32 .

dē-flŭo.opening: v. n. To flow down . Lit. : quod sanguen defluxerat, Cato ap. Gell. 3, 7, 19 ; cf.: sanguis a renibus, Plin. 24, 18, 105, § 169 : defluit lapidosus rivus, Ov. F. 3, 273 : flamma ex Aetna monte, Liv. Fragm. 1, 116 :…

dēflŭus.opening: adj. defluo , flowing down; or transf., moving downwards, going or falling down (post-Aug.). In gen.: gradus, Stat. Th. 9, 325 : caesaries, long and flowing , Prud. στεφ . 13, 30: splendor ab alto, Stat. S. 1, 3, 53 .—…

dēflŭvĭum.opening: id. (perh. only in Plin.). A flowing down, flowing off , Plin. 18, 29, 69, § 281 : defluvia fontanea, Sol. 4, 4 .— A falling off or out : capilli, = alopecia, Plin. 28, 11, 46, § 163 ; 29, 6, 34, § 108 ; cf. capitis,…

dēfluxĭo.opening: id. , a flowing off, discharge (lat. Lat.): seminis, Firm. Math. 3, 7; ventris, Coel. Aur. Acut. 2, 18.— Absol. = διάῤῥοια , diarrhoea , id. ib. 3, 22 .

dēfluxus.opening: id. , a flowing or running off : in terras, App. de Deo Socr. p. 47 .

dē-fŏdĭo.opening: v. a. To dig downwards or deep; to dig up, to dig (rare): scrobem in limine stabuli, Col. 7, 5, 17 : specus, Verg. G. 3, 376 : domos, id. Cul. 273 : terram, Hor. S. 1, 1, 42 : locum in altitudinem pedum quinque, Plin.…

dē-foedo.opening: v. a. , to defile (late Lat.): noli defoedare coronam meam, Fulg. Serm. 69 .

dēfōmĭtātum.grammar: a fomitibus succisum, quibus confoveri erat solitum lignum

dēfŏrīs.opening: adv., from outside, outside : inclusit eum Dominus deforis, Vulg. Gen. 7, 16 : quod deforis est calicis, id. Matt. 23, 25 ; id. Luc. 11, 40 .

dēformātĭo.opening: 2. deformo , a deforming, disfiguring, defacing : tantae majestatis, Liv. 9, 5 fin. : manus, Cod. Theod. 7, 13, 4 ; 15, 1, 19 .

dē-formis.opening: ( abl. plur. : deformīs dentibus, Apul. Met. 10, p. 249, 9), adj. forma; cf. 2. deformo . Departing , either physically or (more freq.) morally, from the right shape, quality , etc.; misshapen, deformed, unsightly,…

dēformĭtas.opening: deformis, no. I. , deformity, ugliness (good prose). Lit. (physically): quae si in deformitate corporis habet aliquid offensionis, quanta illa depravatio et foeditas animi debet videri? Cic. Off. 3, 29, 105 ; id. de Or.…

dēformĭter.opening: adv., inelegantly, disgracefully , etc.; v. deformis, no. I. fin.

dē-formo.opening: v. a. forma; cf. deformis , to bring out of shape; to deform, disfigure; to spoil, mar (class.). Lit. : deformatus corpore, fractus animo, Cic. Att. 2, 21, 3 sq. ; cf.: aerumnis deformatus, Sall. J. 14, 7 : vultum…

dēfraudātĭo.opening: defraudo .— Lit. , a defrauding .— Trop. , deficiency , Tert. Anim. 43 .

dēfraudātor.opening: id. , he who defrauds, a defrauder , Gai. Inst. 4, 65 .

dēfraudātrix.opening: defraudator , she who defrauds , Tert. Jejun. 16 .

dē-fraudo.opening: or (cf. frustra and the compounds of claudo), āvi, ātum (old fut. perf. defraudassis = defraudaveris, Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 58 ), 1, v. a. , to defraud, overreach, cheat (ante-class. and late; in Cic. twice, in proverb.…

dē-frĕmo.opening: v. n. , to ceaseraging or roaring, to abate (post-class.): cum primus ille impetus defremuisset, Plin. Ep. 9, 13, 4 ; Sid. Ep. 9, 9 ; 1, 5 fin. : sensim ira, id. ib. 4, 12 .

dē-frēnātus.opening: adj. freno , unbridled, unrestrained : cursu, Ov. M. 1, 282 .

dēfrĭcātio.opening: defrico , a rubbing , Coel. Aur. Acut. 1, 11 fin. ; 2, 18; 19 al.

dē-frĭco.opening: (the former Catull. 37, 20; Col. 11, 2, 70 ; Plin. 28, 12, 50, § 188 ; the latter in Col. 6, 13, 1 ; 7, 5, 8 ; Sen. Ep. 87, 10 ), 1, v. a. , to rub off, rub down; to rub hard, to rub (rare; mostly technical; not in Cic.…

dē-frīgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to cool off, grow cold (very rare): coctura, Col. 12, 20, 4 ; 12, 21, 1 .

dē-fringo.opening: v. a. , to break off; to break to pieces (rare but class.). Lit. : amphoram defracto collo puram impleto, Cato R. R. 88 : plantas, Varr. R. R. 1, 40, 4 ; cf. Verg. G. 2, 300 : ramum arboris, Cic. Caecin. 21, 60 :…

dē-frūgo.opening: v. a. fruges , to rob of corn : segetem ne defruges, to sow too little grain , Orac. Vet. ap. Plin. 18, 24, 55, § 200 ; cf. Cato R. R. 5, 4 (Schneid. defrudet ).

dē-frŭor.opening: v. dep. , to use up, consume by enjoying : auctumnitate, Symm. Ep. 3, 23 ; cf.: defrui dicebant antiqui ut deamare, deperire , significantes omnem fructum percipere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 70, 14 Müll.

dē-frusto.opening: v. a. , to divide into pieces, to dismember (postclass.): tunicam, Amm. 31, 2 : Mesopotamiam, id. 20, 2 al.

dēfrŭtārĭus.opening: adj. defrutum , belonging to or for defrutum (only in Col.): vasa, Col. 12, 19, 3 ; 6 .—Also absol. : , id. 12, 20, 2 : cella, id. 1, 6, 9 .

dēfrŭto.opening: v. a. id. , to boil down into defrutum: quicquid vini, Cato R. R. 24, 2 : vinum, Col. 2, 22, 4 .

dēfrŭtum.opening: i, n. (perh. for defervitum, sc. mustum), must boiled down (acc. to Varr. and Col., to one third; acc. to Plin., only to one half), Varr. ap. Non. 551, 24 ; Col. 12, 20 sq. ; Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 80 ; Pall. Oct. 18 ;…

dēfŭga.opening: defugio , a runaway, deserter (late Lat.), Cod. Theod. 12, 19, 3 ; Prud. στεφ . 1, 42.

dē-fŭgĭo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. With acc., to run away from; to flee, shun, avoid : fugiendo devitare (class.): aditum alicujus sermonemque, Caes. B. G. 6, 13, 7 : proelium, id. B. C. 1, 82, 2 : patriam, Cic. Rep. 2, 19, 34 (dub.):…

dē-fŭgo.opening: v. a. , to drive away, remove : capillos, Theod. Prisc. 1, 4 .

dē-fulgŭro.opening: v. a. , to flash forth : clipeus ignem, Aus. Per. Iliad. 5 .

dēfunctĭo.opening: defungor (eccl. Lat.). Execution, performance : cordis, Salvian. Gub. Dei, p. 28.— Death , Vulg. Sir. 1, 13 .

dēfunctōrĭus.opening: adj. defungor , quickly despatched; slight, cursory (post-Aug.; for class. negligens, levis): apodixis, Petr. 132, 10 : ictus, id. 136, 5 .— Adv. : , slightly, cursorily : agere causam, Sen. Contr. 5, 31 fin. : petere…

dē-fundo.opening: v. a. , to pour down, pour out (in the ante-Aug. per. very rare; not in Cic. and Caes.). In gen.: aquam, Cato R. R. 156, 5 : vinum (sc. ex dolio in amphoram), Hor. S. 2, 2, 58 : late sanguinem, Sil. 5, 453 et saep.: ovi…

dē-fungor.opening: ( infin. pass. parag. defungier, Ter. Phorm. 5, 9, 32 ), 3, v. dep. , to have done with, to acquit one's self of, to discharge an affair or an obligation (esp. an unwelcome, unpleasant one), to perform, finish (class.).…

dēfūsĭo.opening: defundo , the pouring out into vessels, Col. 3, 2, 1 .

dē-fŭtūtus.opening: adj. futuo , exhausted by sensuality : puella, Catull. 41, 1.

dē-gĕner.opening: ( abl. degeneri, Tac. A. 12, 19 ), adj. genus , that departs from its race or kind, degenerate, not genuine (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; esp. freq. in Plin. and Tac.; not in Quint. and Suet.). Lit. :…

dēgĕnĕro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dēgĕnĕro.opening: v. n. and a. [degener]. Neutr., to depart from its race or kind, to degenerate (class.). Lit. : qui a vobis nihil degenerat, Cic. Phil. 13, 15 : Pandione nata, degeneras! Ov. M. 6, 635 : pomaque degenerant succos oblita…

dē-gĕro.opening: v. a. , to carry away, carry off (rare): de vinea sarmenta, Cato R. R. 37, 5 Schneid. N. cr. : mea ornamenta ad meretrices, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 53 : aurum meum tuae amicae, id. ib. 5, 1, 41 ( Plin. 12, 27, 60, § 131 , the…

dē-glā^bro.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to smooth off, make smooth : arbores, Dig. 47, 7, 5 : corpus, Lact. 1, 21 .

dē-glūbo.opening: , no perf. , ptum, 3, v. a. , to peel off; to shell, to husk . * Lit. : granum eo folliculo, Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 2 .— Transf. To take off the skin; to skin, flay (rare): se vel vivum, Varr. ap. Non. 158, 22 ; cf. maenam,…

dē-glūtĭno.opening: v. a. , to unglue, to separate by moistening : palpebras, Plin. 25, 13, 103, § 163 .

dē-gluttĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to swallow down (post-Aug. and rare): hunc cibum, Fronto Ep. ad amic. 1, 15: virum, Avit. 4, 364; Vulg. Jon. 2, 1 ; Psa. 124, 3. Said of the earth, Num. 16, 30.— Transf. , to overwhelm, abolish : mortem,…

dēgo.opening: v. a. de-ago , to spend, pass , sc. time (for syn. cf.: ago, gero, facio—very freq. and class.). With acc. : a mane ad noctem usque in foro dego diem, Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 3 ; so, diem in laetitia, Ter. Ad. 4, 1, 6 :…

dē-grandĭnat.opening: v. impers. , it hails violently, continues to hail , or (as others interpret) ceases to hail , Ov. F. 4, 755 .

dē-grassor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. * Neutr., to rush down : deorsum degrassantur aquae, App. de Deo Socr. p. 94 . — Act. , poet. transf., to attack fiercely, to revile : primos duces, Stat. Ach. 1, 406 (cf. grassor with the acc. , id.…

dē-grăvo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to weigh or press down, to overpower (not ante-Aug.). Prop.: unda caput, Prop. 3, 7, 58 (4, 6, 58 M.); so, caput, Ov. M. 5, 352 : altam ulmum (vitis), id. Tr. 5, 3, 35 : partīs navigii,…

dē-grĕdĭor.opening: v. dep. gradior , to go down, march down, descend (never, to go away, depart, like digredior— freq. only after the Aug. period, esp. in Liv. and Tac.): de via in semitam, Plaut. Cas. 3, 5, 40 (dub.): degressus ex arce,…

dē-grūmor.opening: v. dep. a. [gruma], to level off, to straighten (only in the foll. passages): viam, Lucil. ap. Non. 63, 9 : ferrum, Enn. ib.

dēgŭlātor.opening: degulo , a glutton , App. Mag. p. 322, 32 ; Isid. 10, 80 .

dē-gŭlo.opening: v. a. , to devour, consume (ante-class. and rare): omnia, Atta ap. Charis. p. 80 (v. 11 Rib.); so Afran. ib. and ap. Non. 97, 29 (v. 17 Rib.).

degunere.opening: to taste , Paul. ex Fest. p. 71, 21 Müll.

dē-gusto.opening: v. a. , to taste , and thus diminish a thing (cf. delibo and ἀπογεύομαι —rare but class., esp. in the trop. sense). Lit. : vinum, Cato R. R. 148 : pabulum, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 15 : novas fruges aut vina, Plin. 18, 2, 2, §…

dĕ-hăbĕo.opening: v. a. , not to have, to lack (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 22 , no. 35.

dĕ-haurĭo.grammar: like clodo, codex, clostrum, plostrum hausi, haustum, 4 v. a.
dĕ-haurĭo.opening: (also written , , etc.), , v. a. —* To skim off : amurcam, Cato R. R. 66 fin. — To swal low down, to swallow (late Lat.): margarita pretiosa, Tert. Pall. 5 fin. : carnem, id. Resurr. carn. 11 fin.

dĕ-hinc.opening: (in the poets freq. monosyllabic, e. g. Verg. A. 1, 131 ; 1, 256 ; Ov. F. 6, 788 al. ; cf. App. Orth. 45 . Dissyllabic in Verg. G. 3, 167 ; id. A. 3, 464 ; 5, 722 ; id. Hor. S. 1, 3, 104 ; id. A. P. 144 ; Sil. 8, 473…

dĕ-hisco.opening: (in the inf. dehisse, v. the foll. ), ĕre, v. n. , to part, divide, go apart; to split open; to gape, to yawn (excepting once in Varr., not ante-Aug.): dehisse terram, Varr. L. L. 5, § 148 Müll.; so of the yawning…

dĕhŏnestāmentum.opening: dehonesto , that which disfigures or dishonors; a blemish, deformity, disgrace, dishonor (excepting once in Sallust, only post-Aug. for dedecus, ignominia). With gen. : corporis, Sall. Hist. Fragm. ap. Gell. 2, 27, 2 ;…

dĕhŏnestātĭo.opening: id. , disgrace, dishonor (late Lat.), Tert. Pudic. 18 .

dĕ-hŏnesto.opening: v. a. , to disgrace, disparage, dishonor (once in Liv., otherwise post-Aug.; cf. dehonestamentum): famam maculari dehonestarique, Liv. 41, 6 ; Tac. A. 16, 24 ; Suet. Claud. 30 ; cf.: proavum infami opera, Tac. A. 3, 66…

dĕ-hŏnōro.opening: v. a. , to dishonor (late Lat.), Salv. 3, p. 106 : dehonorata Babylon, Oros. 2, 2 .

dĕhortātĭo.opening: dehortor , a dissuading , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 15 fin.

dĕhortātīvus.opening: adj. id. , fit for dissuading, likely to dissuade , Prisc. p. 1020 P.; Isid. 2, 21, 21 .

dĕhortātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , dissuasive, dehortatory , Tert. Apol. 22 .

dĕ-hortor.opening: ( per tmesin de me hortatur, Enn., v. the foll. ), v. dep. a. , to advise to the contrary; to dissuade (rare but class.): res ipsa me aut invitabit aut dehortabitur, * Cic Pis. 39, 94: multa me dehortantur a vobis,…

Dēïănīra.opening: Δηϊάνειρα , daughter of Oeneus, sister of Meleager, wife of Hercules, and mother of Hyllus . She involuntarily caused the death of Hercules, by sending him the garment Nessus had given her, Ov. M. 9, 9 sq. ; Hyg. Fab.…

dĕĭcīda.opening: Deus-caedo , slayer of God : Judaeos (invidia) fecit esse deicidas, Petr. Chrysol. Serm. 172 .

dē-ĭcĭo.opening: or , , v. a. jacio , to throw or cast down; to hurl down, precipitate (very freq., and class.). Lit. In gen.: araneas de foribus et de pariete, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 31 : aliquem de ponte in Tiberim, Cic. Rosc. Am. 35,…

Dēïdămīa.opening: Δηϊδάμεια . Daughter of Lycomedes, king of Scyros, and mother of Pyrrhus by Achilles , Hyg. Fab. 97 ; Prop. 2, 9, 16 ; Ov. A. A. 1, 704 ; cf. ib. 682 .— Daughter of King Aeacides , Just. 14, 6, 3 .

dĕĭ-fĕrus.opening: adj., bearing a god in one's self , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 7, 1 fin.

dĕĭ-fĭco.opening: v. a. , to make one a god, to deify , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 7, 2 med. ; August. Civ. D. 19, 23, 4 .

dĕĭfĭcus.opening: adj. deus-facio , who makes one a god, deifies : Deus, Tert. Apol. 11 .— Consecrated, sacred , lues ( = Gr. ἡ ἱερὰ νόσος ), epilepsy , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 30, 162 .

dĕin-ceps.opening: (dissyl., Hor. S. 2, 8, 80 ; but trisyl. Prud. Cath. 7, 136 . Cf. dehinc and deinde), adj. and adv. capio. Prop., taking place next or after, v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 591; cf.: particeps, princeps . Adj. ( gen. deincipis or…

dĕindĕ.opening: , and abbrev. (cf. Prisc. p. 1008 P., and exin, proin —in both forms ei is monosyl. in the class. poets; as dissyl., Prud. Cath. 10, 100 ; id. Ditt. 1, 1 ), adv. de-inde , thereafter, thereupon (for syn. cf.: dein,…

dĕin-sŭper.opening: adv. , = desuper, from above : in murum attollitur, Sall. H. Fragm. ap. Non. 530 fin.

dĕ-intē^gro.opening: v. a. , to impair, destroy : nomen virginis (i. e. virginitatem) deintegravit, Caecil. ap. Non. 101, 24 .

dĕ-intus.opening: adv., from within : a parte interiore (late Lat.), Veg. Vet. 3, 4, p. 353 Bip.; (opp. de foris), Vulg. Luc. 11, 40 ; ib. 11, 7 .

Dēīŏnĭdes.opening: Δηϊονίδης , son of Deïone by Apollo , i. e. Miletus , Ov. M. 9, 442 .

Dēĭŏpēa.opening: Δηϊοπεία , one of Juno's nymphs , Hyg. Fab. praef.; Verg. A. 1, 72 ; id. G. 4, 343 .

Dēiŏtărus.opening: Tetrarch of Galatia, afterwards king in Armenia Minor and a part of Pontus; a contemporary of Pompey and Caesar, and of Cicero, who made on his behalf a well-known oration, Caes. B. C. 3, 4 ; Cic. Fam. 9, 12, 2 ; id.…

dĕĭpăra.opening: deus-pario , = Θεοτόκος , she who gives birth to God , of the Virgin Mary, Cod. Just. 1, 1, 6 .

Dĕīpassiānus.opening: deus-patior , a believer in the capacity of the Divine nature for suffering , Marcellin. Com. Chron. An. 512.

Dēĭphŏbē.opening: daughter of Glaucus , Verg. A. 6, 36 ; cf. Serv. in h. l.

Dēĭphŏbus.opening: Δηΐφοβος , son of Priam and Hecuba, and husband of Helen after the death of Paris , Verg. A. 2, 310 ; 6, 495 sq.; Ov. M. 12, 547 ; Prop. 3 (4), 1, 29.

dĕĭtas.opening: deus , the divine nature, deity; late Latin for divinitas, Gr. θεότης , Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 1; Prud. Apoth. 144 al.

dējectē.opening: adv., low , v. deicio, P. a. fin.

dējectĭo.opening: deicio , a throwing or casting down or out (rare). Lit. (acc. to deicio no. 1 A. and B.): imaginum, Nazar. Pan. Const. 12, 2 .— Esp. Medic. t. t. : alvi, a purging, Cels. 1, 3 ; 2, 7 al. : dejectio alone, Sen. Ep. 120,…

dējectĭuncŭla.opening: dim. dejectio no. I. , a slight purging , Scribon. Comp. 52.

dējecto.opening: v. intens. a. [deicio], to hurl down : vasa cuncta, Mattius ap. Gell. 20, 9 fin.

dējector.opening: id. , one who throws or casts down , Dig. 9, 3, 5, § 4 .

dējectus.opening: deicio , a casting or throwing down (rare; not in Cic.). In gen.: arborum, Liv. 9, 2 : gravis (Penei), fall, Ov. M. 1, 571 ; cf. fluminum, Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 18 : aquae, id. Ep. 56 ; and absol. , Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 75…

dējĕro.opening: (the later form , found in many edd., is now retained only in Gell. 1, 3, 20 ; 11, 6, 1 ), , v. n. dejuro, with shortened rad. vowel; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 203 , to take an oath, to swear (ante- and post-class.): per…

dē-jŭgis.opening: adj. jugum , sloping , = declivis: dejuge dorso, Aus. Mos. 164 .

dē-jŭgo.opening: v. a. (lit., to remove from the yoke; hence transf.), to separate, sever : nostram unanimitatem quam memoria dejugat, Pac. ap. Non. 101, 27 , and 142, 32 (Trag. v. 110 Rib.); cf. abjugo and adjugo.

dē-jungo.opening: v. a. , to unyoke cattle: IVNCTO DEIVNCTOVE IVMENTO, Inscr. ap. Grut. 1003, 2.— Part. perf. , dejunctum, dub. reading for dijunctum, Varr. L. L. 10, 3, § 45 Müll.

dējūrātĭo.opening: ( ), , dejuro , an oath (post-class.): testari sub dejuratione (al. dejeratione), Tert. Poenit. 4 : DEIERATIO ESTO APVD MAGISTRATOS, Inscr. Fratr. Arv. ap. Marin. p. 70.

dē-jŭvo.opening: v. n. , to leave off helping, to withhold assistance : deserere illum et dejuvare in rebus advorsis pudet, Plaut. Trin. 2, 2, 63 .

dē-lābor.opening: v. dep. n. , to fall, sink, slip down (freq. and class.). Lit. : signum, de caelo delapsum, Cic. Phil. 11, 10, 24 : de manibus audacissimorum civium delapsa arma, id. Off. 1, 22, 77 ; Caes. B. C. 2, 11 : sinus ab…

dē-lăbōro.opening: v. n. , to work hard, to overwork , Afran. ap. Non. 393, 15 .

dē-lăcĕro.opening: v. a. (lit., to tear in pieces ), trop., to frustrate, destroy : me meamque rem, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 14 Brix. (Fleck., dilaceravisti, v. dilacero).

dēlā^crĭmātĭo.opening: delacrimo , a watery running or weeping of the eyes (as a disease), Plin. 25, 13, 99, § 156 ; plur. 34, 11, 26, § 113.— A cessation of weeping , Scrib. 37 .

dēlā^crĭmātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , for or belonging to weeping : collyrium, Marc. Emp. 8 .

dē-lā^crĭmo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to shed tears, to weep; transf., of the vine, Col. 4, 9 fin.

dē-lambo.opening: v. a. , to lick off, to lick , Stat. Th. 2, 681 .

dē-lāmentor.opening: v. dep. a. , to lament, bewail : natam ademptam, Ov. M. 11, 331 .

dēlănĭāre.grammar: est descindere et quasi lanam trahere
dēlănĭāre.opening: , unde lacinia et lanius dicitur, qui pecus discindit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 73, 12 Müll.

dēlăpĭdo.opening: v. a. * To clear from stones : locum, Cato R. R. 46, 1 .—* To lay with stones, to pave : DELAPIDATA lapide strata, Paul. ex Fest. p. 73, 13 Müll.; cf.: DELAPIDATA, λιθόστρωτα , Gloss.

dēlapsus.opening: delabor , a falling off, descent : aquae, a flowing off, discharge, Varr. R. R. 1, 6 fin.

dēlassābĭlis.opening: adj. delasso , that can be wearied out : pectus, Manil. 4, 242 .

dē-lasso.opening: v. a. , to weary or tire out (rare and poet. for defetigare): labore delassatus, Plaut. Asin. 5, 2, 22 : loquacem Fabium, Hor. S. 1, 1, 14 .— Poet. , with a thing as obj.: delasset omnes fabulas poetarum, Mart. 10, 5…

dēlātĭo.opening: defero, no. II. B. 2. b. , an accusation, denunciation : nominis, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 20, 64 ; id. ib. 3, 7 ; id. Cluent. 8, 25 .— Absol. : cuicumque vos delationem dedissetis, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 15, 49 ; Tac. A. 4,…

dēlātor.opening: id. , an accuser, informer, denouncer (only post-Aug.; esp. freq. in Tacit. and Suet.): judices ... delatores, Quint. 9, 2, 74 ; cf. 3, 10, 3: delatorum judicium, quasi latronum, Plin. Pan. 34, 1 sq. ; 35, 1 ; Suet.…

dēlātōrĭus.opening: adj. delator , of or belonging to an informer (post-class.): curiositas, Dig. 22, 2, 6 : libelli, denunciatory writings, Cod. Theod. 10, 10, 7 .

dēlātūra.opening: defero, no. II. B. 2. b. (late Lat. for delatio), an accusation, information , Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 18 fin. ; Vulg Sirach, 38, 17.

dē-lăvo.opening: , no perf. , -lōtum, āre, v. a. , to wash off, wash clean : porcellum liquamine, Apic. 8 . 7; Theod. Prisc. 1, 4 .

dēlēbĭlis.opening: adj. deleo , that may be blotted out or destroyed : liber, Mart. 7, 84, 7 .

dēlectābĭlis.opening: adj. delecto , delectable, delightful, agreeable (post-Aug. for jucundus, amoenus): cibus, Tac. A. 12, 67 : apologi (with festivi), Gell. 2, 29 ; Vulg. Gen. 3, 6 ; Lact. 6, 4, 3 ; 7, 7, 13 .— Comp. : tibia questu, App.…

dēlectāmentum.opening: id. , a delight (very rare): pro delectamento, amusement, pastime, Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 79 : delectamenta puerorum, etc., Cic. Pis. 25, 60 : pacis, Nazar. Paneg. Const. 35 : somni, Vulg. Sap. 7, 2 .

dēlectātĭo.opening: id. , a delighting, delight, pleasure, amusement (freq. and good prose): delectatio voluptas suavitate auditus animum deleniens, etc., Cic. Tusc. 4, 9 : homo videndi et audiendi delectatione ducitur, id. Off. 1, 30 ;…

dēlectātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. delectatio , a trifling pleasure, petty delight , Gell. praef. § 23.

dēlectĭo.opening: deligo (post-class. for delectus), a choosing, choice : imperatoris, Vopisc. Aurel. 40.

dēlecto.opening: v. intens. a. [delicio]. To allure from the right path, to entice away, to seduce (only ante-class.): me Apollo ipse delectat, ductat Delphicus, Enn. ap. Non. 97, 32 (Trag. v. 390 Vahl.: delectare, illicere, attrahere,…

dēlector.opening: deligo , one who draws out, levies, recruits , Frontin. Strat. 4, 1, 3.

dēlectus.opening: or (so often in best MSS., and adopted by Halm in Quint. and Cic., Weissenb. in Liv., Dietsch in Sall., and by Brambach, etc.; but Bait. and Kay. in Cic., Dinter and Nipperdey in Caes., delectus), , 1. deligo , a…

dēlēgātĭo.opening: delego, no. II. , an assignment, substitution, delegation of one person by another. Prop.: a mancipe, Cic. Att. 12, 3, 2 ; of one thing for another: delegatione perfecta solutio, Sen. Ben. 6, 5, 2 ; cf. context.— Trop.…

dēlēgātor.opening: id. , one who makes an assignment (sc. to another person), an assignor , Cassiod. Varr. 1, 18 .

dēlēgātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , relating to an assignment : litterae, Cod. Theod. 7, 4, 22 .

dē-lēgo.opening: v. a. , to send, assign, dispatch, delegate a person to any place, person or business; to assign, confide, commit, intrust any thing to a person (for attention, care, protection, etc.); to charge a person with a…

dēlēnĭfĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. delenio-facio , soothing, caressing, captivating, flattering, enchanting (ante- and postclass.): verba, Lucil. ap. Fulg. 567, 24 : facta, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 39 : ingenium mulierum, Turp. ap. Non. 278, 2 :…

dēlēnīmentum.opening: ( ), , delenio , any thing that soothes, charms , or allures, a charm, blandishment, allurement, enticement (ante - class., and repeatedly since the Aug. period, but not in Cic. or Caes.), Afran. ap. Non. 2, 4 , and 8…

dē-lēnĭo.opening: , and in many MSS. , , v. a. , to soothe or soften down, to cajole, charm, win, captivate, entice (very freq., and class.): delenitus sum profecto ita, ut me qui sim nesciam, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 214 : dotibus deleniti,…

dēlēnītor.opening: ( ), , delenio , one who softens down, soothes, wins over : judicis, Cic. Brut. 70, 246 .

dēlēnītōrĭus.opening: ( ), , adj., pertaining to or serving for softening, soothing : aquae, Cassiod. Varr. 10, 29 .

dēlĕo.opening: ( perf. sync. delerunt, Cic. Red. in Sen. 2, 4 : delerit, Cic. Cat. 4, 9, 19 ; id. Balb. 19, 43 : delerat, id. Fam. 15, 5, 3 : delerant, id. Sest. 19, 44 ; plqpf. subj. sync. delesset, Val. Max. 3, 7 ; Liv. 27, 40, 4 ;…

dēlētīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. deleo , from which any thing has been blotted out, effaced : charta, Dig. 37, 11, 4 .

dēlētĭlis.opening: adj. id. , that wipes or blots out : spongia, Varr. ap. Non. 96, 14 .

dēlētĭo.opening: id. , an annihilating, destroying : nostri exercitus, Lucil. ap. Non. 97, 4 .

dēlētrix.opening: id. , she that annihilates or destroys : sica hujus imperii deletrix, Auct. Harusp. resp. 23, 49.

dēlētus.opening: id. , annihilation (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 24 .

dē-lēvo.opening: (or ), , v. a. , to smooth off, make smooth : plagam acutissimo ferro, Col. Arb. 6, 4 .

dēlībāmentum.opening: delibo , wine poured out to the gods, a libation , Val. Max. 2, 6, 8 .

dēlībātĭo.opening: id. , a taking away from, diminishing (post-class.): hereditatis, Dig. 30, 113 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 22 .— The first fruit, sample, representative portion : quod si delibatio sancta est, et massa, Vulg. Rom. 11, 16 .

dēlībĕrābundus.opening: adj. delibero , weighing carefully, considering, reflecting, deliberating (rare): consules velut deliberabundi capita conferunt, diu colloquuntur, Liv. 2, 45, 7 ; 1, 54, 6 .

dēlībĕrāmentum.opening: id. , a deliberation , Laber. ap. Fronto Ep. ad M. Caes. 6 .

dēlībĕrātĭo.opening: id. , a deliberation, consultation, consideration (a Ciceron. word; elsewhere very rare). In gen.: ad deliberationes eas, quas habebat domi de republica, principes civitatis adhibebat, Cic. Phil. 1, 1, 2 ; id. Off. 3,…

dēlībĕrātīvus.opening: adj. id. , relating to deliberation, deliberative (only in rhetor. lang., esp. freq. in Quint.): genus, Cic. Inv. 1, 5, 7 ; 2, 51, 155 ; Quint. 2, 4, 25 ; 8 prooem. § 6 : causa, Cic. Inv. 2, 4, 12 ; Quint. 8, 3, 11 :…

dēlībĕrātor.opening: id. , one who deliberates , Cic. Sest. 34 fin.

dēlībĕrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from delibero.

dē-lībĕro.opening: v. a. de and libro, libra; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 74, 1 Müll.: deliberare a libella, qua quid perpenditur dictum , to weigh well in one's mind, to consider maturely, deliberate respecting a thing; to take counsel,…

dē-lībo.opening: v. a. , to take off, take away a little from any thing; of food, to taste (class.). Lit. : parvam delibet ab aequore partem, Lucr. 6, 622 : aliquid membrorum, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 16 : truncum, Col. 2, 2, 26 : paululum…

dē-lī^bro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. 3. liber , to take off the rind or bark, to peel : arborem, Col. 5, 11, 10 : radicem, id. 5, 6, 9 : corticem, id. 4, 24, 6 ; 5, 11, 1 : ramum, Pall. Febr. 17, 7 . In Lucr. 3, 1088 , the true reading…

dē-lĭbŭo.opening: (dēlībūta comas, Prud. Psych. 312 ), , v. a. LIBUO = λείβω, cf. ἀλείφω , to besmear, anoint with a liquid: delibuo καταβρέχω, ἐλαιῶ, βρέχω , Gloss. Cyrill. (in the verb. finit. only late Lat.). Lit. Verb. finit. : eum…

dēlĭcātus.opening: adj. deliciae . That gives pleasure , i. e. alluring, charming, delightful; luxurious, voluptuous . Prop. (class.): in illo delicatissimo litore, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 40 : navigia, Suet. Vit. 10 : delicatior cultus, id.…

dēlĭcĭa.opening: or , , deliquo, cf. colliciae, a flowing or running off; hence , a gutter , Vitr. 6, 3 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 73, 2 Müll.

dēlĭcĭae.opening: ( sing. , , ; ante-and post-class., Plaut. Truc. 5, 29 ; id. Rud. 2, 4, 13 ; id. Poen. 1, 2, 152 ; Inscr. Grut. 1014, 5 : , , , Phaedr. 4, 1, 8 ; Verg. Copa, 26 ; Mart. 7, 50, 2 ; 13, 98, 1 ; Inscr. Orell. 680 ; 1724 ;…

dēlĭcĭāris.opening: adj. 2. delicia , pertaining to a gutter : tegulae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 73, 2 Müll.

dēlĭcĭātus.opening: adj. 2. delicia , with a gutter : tectum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 73, 2 Müll.

dē-lĭcĭo.opening: v. a. lacio, the root of deliciae and delecto , to allure one from the right way, to entice, delight : aliquem, Titin. ap. Non. 277, 17 .

dēlĭcĭŏlae.opening: dim. deliciae no. II. , a darling : nostrae, Tulliola, Cic. Att. 1, 8 fin. —Also , , : tuum, villici filius, Sen. Ep. 12, 3 .

dēlĭcĭōsus.opening: adj. deliciae , delicious, delicate (late Lat.): lassitudines, August. Contr. 10, 34 fin. : militia, Cass. Var. 7, 9: mollities, Mart. Cap. 7, § 727 ; of persons, Ambros. de Poen. 1, 9, 24 ; Sedul. prol. 8 .

dēlictor.opening: delinquo , a delinquent, offender , Cypr. Ep. 59 fin.

dēlictum.opening: delinquo , prop. a falling short of the standard of law (hence esp. a transgression against positive law; cf. peccatum, usu. against natural law; cf. also: malefactum, maleficium, facinus, flagitium, scelus, nefas,…

dēlĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [delinquo], blemished, defective : oves, Cato R. R. 2, 7 : armenta, id. ib. (cf. Wordsworth, Fragm. and Specim. p. 614 sq.).

dēlĭcus.opening: adj. delinquo , put away from the breast, weaned : porci, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 16 ; cf. delicum , ἀπογαλακτισθέν , Gloss. Vet.

dē-lĭgo.opening: v. a. (de in the sense of reduction in breadth; cf. devincire), to bind or tie together; to bind up, to bind fast (good prose): homini rostrum deliges, Plaut. Men. 1, 1, 13 : brachium superimposito penicillo, Cels. 2,…

dēlīmātor.opening: de-limo , a filer , διαῤῥινητής , Gloss. Cyrill.

dēlīmĭtātĭo.opening: a marlcing out, limiting , Auct. de limit. p. 142 Goes. From

dē-līmĭto.opening: v. a. , to mark out , Frontin. de agr. qual. p. 38 Goes.

dēlīnĕātĭo.opening: delineo , a sketch , delineation (late Lat. for forma, descriptio), Tert. adv. Val. 27 .

dē-līnĕo.opening: , also , , v. a. linea , to sketch out, to delineate : imaginem in pariete carbone, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 89 ; Tert. adv. Val. 4 ; id. Res. Carn. 20 init.

dē-lingo.opening: v. a. , to lick, lick off or up (very rare): cochleare plenum, Cels. 3, 22 fin. : leo puerum delinxit, Lampr. Diad. 5, § 6 .—Prov.: salem, i. e. to have a meagre diet, Plaut. Curc. 4, 4, 6 ; id. Pers. 3, 3, 25 .

dē-lĭno.opening: , no perf. , lĭtum, 3, v. a. , to besmear (very rare): delinendus homo est vel gypso vel argenti spuma, Cels. 3, 19 ; cf. faciem, App. M. 8, p. 214 .

dēlinquentĭa.opening: delinquo , a fault, crime, delinquency; only in Tert. Res. Carn. 46 and 47.

dē-linquo.opening: ( perf. delinquerunt, Liv. 1, 32 codd.), v. n. and a. , to fail, be wanting . Lit. , to fail, be lacking , for the usual deficere (cf. 1. deliquium, = defectus—very rare): delinquere frumentum, Cael. ap. Serv. Verg. A.…

dēlĭquātĭtūdo.opening: deliquo , a melting, dropping , cerae, Cassiod. in Psa. 67, 3 .

dē-lĭquesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to melt away, dissolve, melt (very rare). Lit. : utinam tua ista in sortiendo sors delicuerit, Plaut. Cas. 2, 6, 47 : ubi delicuit nondum prior (sc. nix), altera venit, Ov. Tr. 3, 10, 15 : Hyrie flendo…

dēlĭquio.opening: ( ), , delinquo , a failure, want , Gell. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 4, 390 : nullam causam dico quin mihi et parentum et libertatis apud te deliquio siet, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 92 (Brix, Fleck.; al. deliquium).

dēlĭquĭum.opening: deliquo , a flowing down, dropping down , Prud. Hamart. 753 .

dē-lĭquo.opening: (in the trop. signif.) , , v. a. liquo , to clear off a turbid liquid, to clarify, to strain : turbi da quae sunt deliquantur ut liquida flant, Varr. L. L. 7, § 106 Müll.; Cels. 5, 20, 5 : passum in alia vasa, Col. 12,…

dēlĭquus.opening: or , , adj. delinquo, no. I. , wanting, lacking : tibi nil domi delicuum 'st, Plaut. Cas. 2, 2, 33 .

dēlīrāmentum.opening: (in the Fronto MS. written delēr.), , deliro , nonsense, absurdity (in Plaut. and in post-Aug. prose), Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 64 ; id. Men. 5, 5, 21 ; Plin. 2, 7, 5, § 17 ; Fronto Ep. ad M. Caes. 2, 1 ; Vulg. Luc. 24, 14 .

dēlīrātĭo.opening: id. , originally, a going out of the furrow, in ploughing; hence, trop., giddiness, silliness, folly, dotage, madness (very rare): quod vocant lirare, operiente semina, unde primum appellata deliratio est, Plin. 18, 20,…

dēlīrĭtas.opening: id. , i. q. deliratio, Laber. ap. Non. 490, 21 (v. 139 Rib.).

dēlīrĭum.opening: deliro, no. II. , in medical lang., madness, delirium , Cels. 2, 8 ; 3, 18 et saep.

dē-līro.opening: v. n. de-lira, to go out of the furrow; hence , Lit. , to deviate from a straight line : nil ut deliret amussis, Aus. Idyll. 16, 11 ; cf. Plin. 18, 20, 49, § 180 .— Trop. (cf. Vel. Long. p. 2233 P.), to be crazy,…

dēlīrus.opening: adj. deliro, no. II. , silly, doting, crazy (class.): dementit deliraque fatur, Lucr. 3, 464 : delira furiosaque, id. 2, 985 ; with amens, Hor. S. 2, 3, 107 : senex, Cic. de Or. 2, 18, 75 ; Hor. S. 2, 5, 71 : anus, Cic.…

dē-lĭtĕo.opening: , false read. in Plin. 35, 1, 1, § 3 for dilatantia, v. dilato.

dē-lĭtesco.opening: v. inch. n. [latesco], to hide away, conceal one's self; to lie hid, to lurk (class.). Lit. : bestiae in cubilibus delitescunt, Cic. N. D. 2, 49 fin. ; cf.: hostes noctu in silvis delituerant, * Caes. B. G. 4, 32, 4 :…

dē-lītĭgo.opening: v. n. , to scold, rail angrily : iratusque Chremes tumido delitigat ore, Hor. A. P. 94 .

dēlĭtor.opening: deleo , an obliterator : scelerum fratris, Att. ap. Prisc. p. 873 P.

Dēlĭum.opening: Δήλιον , a small place in Boeotia, with a temple of Apollo , Cic. Div. 1, 54, 123 ; Liv. 35, 50 sq.

Delminĭum.opening: Δελμίνιον , the ancient capital of Dalmatia , Flor. 4, 12, 11 .

dē-lŏcātĭo.opening: loco , a dislocation : articulorum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 .

dē-longe.grammar: or in two words, de longe
dē-longe.opening: adv., from afar , Vulg. Ex. 20, 21 ; id. Deut. 29, 22 .

Dēlos.opening: Δῆλος , a small island in the Aegean Sea, one of the Cyclades, the birthplace of Apollo and Diana , now Dili , Mela, 2, 7, 11; Plin. 2, 87, 89, § 202 ; 4, 12, 22, § 66 ; Cic. de Imp. Pomp. 18, 55 ; Macr. S. 1, 17 ;…

dēlōtus.opening: Part. from delavo, washed , Theod. Prisc. 1, 4 .
