Delphi.opening: Δελφοί , the famous city of the oracle of Apollo in Phocis , now Kastri : Delphi sub monte Parnaso oppidum clarissimi in terris oraculi Apollinis, Plin. 4, 3, 4, § 7 ; cf. Mela, 2, 3, 4; Mann. Gr. p. 160 sq.; Plaut. Ps.…

delphīnus.grammar: i, and in the pure Greek form īnis m.
delphīnus.opening: ( poet. ) , (once also nom. , delphis, = δελφίς , Avien. Arat. 699 ; cf. Serv. Verg. G. 1, 162 ; Prisc. p. 689 P.), , = δελφίν , a dolphin . Form delphinus , Plin. 9, 8, 7, § 20 sq. ; Plin. Ep. 9, 33, 4 sq. ; Gell. 7, 8…

delta.opening: or , = δέλτα , the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, delta , Δ : non formam at vocem deltae gero Romuleum D, Aus. Idyll. de lit. monos. 14; so (but with gender undetermined) Mel. 2, 7, 14 .— Meton. , , Δέλτα , nom.…

Deltōton.opening: , i. , = Δελτωτόν , the Triangle , a constellation, Cic. Arat. 5 ; Caes. German. Arat. 239 ; Manil. 1, 352 ; Hyg. Astr. 3, 18 ; Aus. Ecl. de sign. coel. 4.

dēlūbrum.opening: de-luo, the place of expiation , a temple, shrine, sanctuary (class., esp. freq. in poets and in elevated prose; usually in the plur.; for syn. cf.: templum, aedes, fanum, cella, sacellum, sacrarium). Plur. : CONSTRVCTA…

dēluctātĭo.opening: deluctor , a wrestling, a struggle , Mart. Cap. 5, p. 139 .

dē-lucto.opening: v. n. , to wrestle, struggle (ante-class.): quibus aerumnis deluctavi, Plaut. Trin. 4, 1, 20 ; cf.: deluctavi pro deluctatus sum, Plautus in Trinummo, "cum hisce erumnis deluctavit," Non. 468, 29 .

dē-luctor.opening: v. dep. n. , to wrestle, to struggle, combat (only in Plaut.): cum Antaeo deluctari malui quam cum Amore, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 4 .

dē-lūdĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to mock, banter, make sport of : me, Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 59 .

dē-lūdo.opening: ( arch. inf. pass. deludier, Ter. And. 1, 2, 32 ), v. a. To play false, to mock, deceive, make sport of, delude . Prop. (rare, but class.), Ter. l. l. in hac re me deludier: deludi vosmet ipsos diutius a tribuno plebis…

dē-lumbis.opening: adj. lumbus , lamed in the loins, lamed (post-Aug. and very rare). Lit. : coturnix, Plin. 10, 33, 51, § 103 .— Trop. , weakened, enervated; weak, feeble : summā delumbe salivā, Pers. 1, 104 : dietio, Sid. Ep. 8, 16 .

dē-lumbo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. id. , to lame in the loins (very rare). Lit. : quadrupede delumbata, Plin. 28, 4, 7, § 36 . — Transf. to vend : radices delumbatae, Plin 19, 6, 33, § 109: lacunaria curva ad circinum delumbata, bent…

dē-lŭo.opening: v. a. , to wash out or off, to cleanse : alvum aquā mulsā, Cels. 4, 15 fin. — DELVIT, solvit, Paul. ex Fest. . 73, 16 Müll.

dēlūsĭo.opening: deludo , a deceiving, deluding : numinum, Arn. 4, p. 127 .

dēlūsor.opening: id. , a deceiver , Cassiod. comp. ad Ep. Jud. 4.

dē-lustro.opening: v. a. , to free one from an evil charm or spell, to disenchant : aliquem radice herbae asparagi, App. Herb. 84 .

dē-lŭto.opening: v. a. * To daub or plaster with clay : habitationem, Cato R. R. 128 .—* To cleanse from clay or dirt : Dict. Cretens. 3, 24 Deder.

Dēmādes.opening: Δημάδης , a famous Athenian orator who sided with Macedon, a contemporary of Demosthenes , Cic. Brut. 9, 36 ; id. Or. 26, 90 ; Quint. 2, 17, 12 sq. ; 12, 10, 49 ; Nep. Phoc. 2 .

dē-mădesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become humid or moist : Ov. Tr. 5, 4, 40 ; Scrib. Comp. 73 .

dē-măgis.opening: very much , Lucil. ap. Non. 98, 19 sq. ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 71, 9 Müll., and Gloss. Philox.: " demagis , σφοδρῶς ."

dēmandātĭo.opening: demando , a delivering with commendation, a commending (late Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 48 .

dē-mando.opening: v. a. , to give in charge, to intrust, commit, commend (not ante-Aug.; cf., on the contrary, commendo; most freq. in Suet.; not found in Quint. or Tac.): simul plures pueri unius (sc. paedagogi) curae demandabantur,…

dē-māno.opening: v. n. , to flow down : tenuis sub artus flamma demanat, Cat. 51, 9 ; Gell. 17, 11, 1 ; Porc. Latro decl. in Cat. 10, 29 ; 36 .— Transf. , to descend, be descended from : de patriarcharum genere, Ambros. in Luc. 3, 41…

Dēmărātus.opening: Δημάρατος . A Corinthian, the father of Tarquinius Priscus , Cic. Rep. 2, 19 ; id. Tusc. 5, 37 fin. ; Liv. 1, 34 .— A Spartan king, colleague of Cleomenes , Just. 2, 10, 13 ; Sen. Ben. 6, 31, 2 .— Father of Pythagoras ,…

dē-marcesco.opening: v. n. , to fade away, wither : herba ad vesperam demarcescit et decidit, Hier. in Psal. 89 .

dēmarchĭa.opening: , = δημαρχία , the office and dignity of a demarch , Inscr. Orell. 3800 sq.

dēmarchus.opening: , = δήμαρχος , lit. a ruler of the people at Athens, the president of a demos, a demarch , answering to the Roman tribune of the people , Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 6 ; Spart. Hadr. 19 ; Inscr. Orell. 3720 .

dē-mātrĭcātus.opening: adj. matrix : nisi dematricati fuerint, bled from the vena matricalis in the neck , Veg. Vet. 4, 7, 3 ; cf. id. ib. 1, 10 ; 13.

Dēmĕa.opening: , = Δημέας , a Greek proper name , Ter. Ad. 1, 2, 19 et passim.

dēmĕācŭlum.opening: demeo , a passage under ground : Proserpinae, App. M. 6, p. 174, 11 ; cf. demeaculum , καταπορεία , Gloss. Vet.

dē-mens.opening: adj., out of one's mind or senses; mad, raving; foolish (cf. amens) (class. and very freq.; for syn. cf.: amens, excors, vecors, insanus, vesanus, delirus, alienatus mente): qua perturbatione animi quae, sanus cum…

dēmensĭo.opening: demetior , a measuring : legum, Aus. Ep. 5, 11 .

dēmentĭa.opening: f [demens], the being out of one's mind; insanity, madness; folly (freq. and class.; for syn. cf.: amentia, furor, rabies, vecordia, insania, deliratio, vesania): animi affectionem lumine mentis carentem nominaverunt…

dēmentĭo.opening: v. n. id. , to be out of one's senses, to be mad, to rave (anteand post-class.): dementit deliraque fatur, * Lucr. 3, 464 : sese mea magia in amorem inductam dementire, App. Mag. p. 324, 9 : aliquis instinctu daemonis…

dēmento.opening: v. a. and n. id. . Act., to drive mad, to craze, deprive of mind : dementatus, Cassiod. Amic. 21 : ἐξιστάναι ἰδιωτικῶς , Gloss. Graec. Lat.; esp. to bewitch, delude : propter quod magiis suis dementasset eos, Vulg. Act.…

dē-mĕo.opening: v. n. , to go down, descend (post-class.); caelo, Ap. M. 10, p. 254, 12: ad Tartarum Manesque, id. ib. 6 , p. 180, 7; Mart. Cap. 2, p. 38 .

dē-mĕrĕo.opening: v. a. With acc. rei, to merit, deserve a thing (ante-and post-class., and very rare): aliquid mercedis domino, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 90 : grandem pecuniam, Gell. 1, 8, 3 : demeritae laetitiae, Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 14 .— (Since…

dē-mergo.opening: v. a. , to sink, submerge, to plunge into, to dip (class.). Lit. : candens ferrum in gelidum imbrem, Lucr. 6, 149 : pars remorum demersa liquore, id. 4, 441 ; cf.: cornix demersit caput, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 8 fin. ; and…

dēmersĭo.opening: demergo , a being sunk down, a sinking (late Lat. and rare). Prop.: urbium, Sol. 40, 5 .— Trop. : temporalis (animae), Macr. S. 1, 12 fin.

dēmersus.opening: demergo , a sinking : levia sustentatui, gravia demersui, App. Mag. p. 287, 35 .

dē-mētĭor.opening: v. a. , to measure out, to measure , as a whole (whereas dimetior is to measure the parts of a whole—very rare): ut verba verbis quasi demensa et paria respondeant, Cic. Or. 12, 38 ; so Quint. 5, 10, 124 (al. dimensis):…

dē-mĕto.opening: v. a. , to mow, reap, cut off, gather, crop, harvest (class.). Usually of fruits: tempora demetendis fructibus et percipiendis accommodata, Cic. de Sen. 19, 70 ; cf. id. N. D. 2, 62 fin. : hordeum, Cass. Hem. ap. Prisc.…

Dēmētrĭas.opening: Gr. Δημητριάς , a city in Thessaly (Pelasgiotis), newly colonized by Demetrius Poliorcetes , formerly called Pagasae, now Volo , Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 29 ; Liv. 27, 23 fin. ; 28, 5 ; 39, 23 .— Hence, , , of Demetrias :…

Dēmētrĭum.opening: Δημήτριον , a town in Phthiotis, with a temple to Demeter (Ceres) , Mel. 2, 3, 6 ; Liv. 28, 6 .— A harbor of Samothrace , Liv. 45, 6, 3 .

Dēmētrĭus.opening: Δημήτριος , the name of several Greeks, among whom the most celebrated are, Demetrius Poliorcetes, son of Antigonus, and king of Macedonia , Cic. Off. 2, 7 fin. ; Just. 15, 1 sq. ; 16, 1 sq.— Demetrius Phalereus, a…

dē-mī^gro.opening: v. n. , to migrate from, to emigrate; to depart, remove from or to a place (class.). Lit. In gen.: de oppidis, Caes. B. G. 4, 19 : ex his aedificiis, id. ib. 4, 4 : ex agris, Liv. 38, 18 fin. ; cf.: ex agris in urbem,…

dē-mĭnōro.opening: v. a. , to lessen, diminish in honor or rank (late Lat.), Tert. Anim. 33 .

dē-mĭnŭo.opening: v. a. , to lessen by taking from , i. e. to make smaller, to lessen, diminish (cf. diminuo, to break up into small parts—freq. and class.). Lit. : de mina una quinque nummos, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 10 : istum laborem tibi,…

dēmĭnūtĭo.opening: deminuo , a diminution, decrease, lessening, abatement (good prose). Lit. : accretio et deminutio luminis, Cic. Tusc. 1, 28 : civium, id. Cat. 3, 10, 24 : vectigalium, id. Agr. 1, 7, 21 : de bonis privatorum, id. Off.…

dēmĭnūtīvus.opening: adj. deminuo, no. II. B. , in the later gramm. lang., diminutive : vox, Tert. Apol. 32 : nomen, a diminutive , Don. p. 1744 P. sq.; in this sense often subst. , , , Diom. p. 312 P.; Prisc. p. 609 sq. et saep: verba (…

Dēmĭpho.opening: , Gr. Δημοφῶν , a character in the Phormio of Terence , 2, 3, 5 et saep.

dē-mīror.opening: v. dep. a. , to wonder at a person or thing, to wonder (for the most part only in the 1st pers. pres., and peculiar to the lang. of conversation). Prop. (with acc. of neut. pron. , or acc. and inf. ): haec ego vos…

dēmissē.opening: adv., low, humbly , v. demitto, P. a. fin.

dēmissīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. demitto , hanging down, flowing, long; of a garment: tunicis demissiciis, Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 24 (for which elsewh. demissis tunicis, v. demissus).

dēmissĭo.opening: id. , a letting down, sinking, lowering (very rare). Prop.: storiarum, * Caes. B. C. 2, 9, 5 : barbae, a letting grow, Macr. S. 1, 22, 4 .—In plur. : clipei aenei demissiones, Vitr. 5, 10 fin. — Trop. * (Acc. to…

dēmissus.opening: Part. and P. a. , fr. demitto.

dē-mītĭgo.opening: v. a. , to make milder; pass., to become milder, more lenient : nosmet ipsi quotidie demitigamur, Cic. Att. 1, 13, 3 .

dē-mitto.opening: v. a. , to send down; to drop; to let, sink , or bring down; to cause to hang or fall down; to lower, put down, let fall (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: picis e caelo demissum flumen, Lucr. 6, 257 ; cf.: caelo imbrem,…

dēmĭurgus.opening: , or acc. to the Dor. form , , , = δημιουργός , Dor. δᾶμιουργός . The chief magistrate in some of the Grecian states , Liv. 32, 22 ; 38, 30 ; title of a comedy of Turpilius, Cic. Fam. 9, 22, 1 ; Non. 226, 12 al. ; cf. R…

dēmo.opening: (msi), mptum (mtum), , v. a. contr. from de-emo; cf. adimo and abemito , to take off, take away, to withdraw, subtract, remove (class. and very freq.; for syn. cf.: adimo, eripio, furor, rapio, prehendo, capio, sumo,…

Dēmŏchăres.opening: an Athenian orator and historian, nephew of Demosthenes , Cic. de Or. 2, 23, 95 ; id. Brut. 83, 286 al. ; Sen. de Ira. 3, 23, 1 .

Dēmō^crĭtus.opening: Δημόκριτος . A celebrated philosopher born at Abdera, an adherent of the Eleatic school, and the originator of the atomic theory , Lucr. 3, 372 ; Cic. Tusc. 1, 11 ; id. Fin. 1, 6 ; id. Ac. 2, 17 sq. ; id. Fat. 10 et…

Dēmodŏcus.opening: a companion of Aeneas , Verg. A. 10, 413 .

dēmogrammăteus.opening: , Gr. δημογραμματεύς , a public scribe , Cod. Just. 10, 69, 4 .

Dēmŏlĕōn.opening: Δημολέων , a centaur slain by Perseus , Ov. M. 12, 356 ; 368 .

Dēmŏlĕos.opening: a Grecian chieftain before Troy, slain by Aeneas , Verg. A. 5, 260 sq. ; cf. Quint. 8, 4, 24 .

dē-mōlĭor.opening: v. dep. a. , to cast off, remove . In gen. So only once in a trop. sense: culpam de me demolibor, Plaut. Bac. 3, 1, 16 .—Far more freq., In partic., of buildings, to throw down, pull or tear down, demolish (for syn.…

dēmōlītĭo.opening: demolior, no. II. , a tearing down, demolishing (very rare). Lit. : dum ea demolitio (statuarum) fieret, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 67 ; Vitr. 10, 19 .— * Trop. : veritatis, an undermining, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 1 .

dēmōlītor.opening: id. , that which breaks down, a demolisher : corvus quem nonnulli gruem appellant (a sort of warlike engine), Vitr. 10, 19 .

dēmonstrābĭlis.opening: adj. demonstro , demonstrable , App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 37 .

dēmonstrātĭo.opening: id. , a showing or pointing out , as with the finger, an indication, description, designation . In gen. (good prose): gestus universam rem et sententiam non demonstratione sed significatione declarans, Cic. de Or. 3, 59…

dēmonstrātīvē.opening: adv., demonstratively , v. the foll. art. fin.

dēmonstrātīvus.opening: adj. demonstro , pointing out, designating . In gen. (very rarely): digitus, the indexfinger, forefinger, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 21 .— In rhetor., demonstrative , = ἐγκωμιαστικόν : genus (orationis), a branch of…

dēmonstrātor.opening: id. , one who points out or indicates; an indicator, exhibiter (very rare): uniuscujusque sepeliendi, * Cic. de Or. 2, 86, 353 : hujus rationis, Col. 3, 10, 20 : medicinarum Aesculapius, Tert. Apol. 23 .

dēmonstrātōrĭus.opening: adj. demonstrator , pointing out, indicating : digitus, the index-finger, Isid. 11, 1, 70 .

dē-monstro.opening: ( arch. inf. pass. : demonstrarier, Ter. Ph. 2, 1, 76 ), v. a. , to point out , as with the finger; to indicate, designate, show (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen. (cf.: indico, significo, ostendo): ubi habitet (mihi)…

Dēmŏphĭlus.opening: Δημόφιλος , a Greek comic poet , Plaut. As. prol. 10 .

Dēmŏphŏon.opening: Δημοφόων . A son of Theseus and Phaedra, a lover of Phyllis, and one of those who fought before Troy , Ov. H. 2 ; id. R. Am. 597 ; Verg. Cul. 130 ; Just. 2, 6, 15 ; Prop. 2, 24, 44 (3, 19, 28 M.); cf. Hyg. Fab. 59 and…

dēmŏrātĭo.opening: demoror , a lingering, abiding, remaining : in vini demorationibus, Vulg. Prov. 12, 11 .

dē-mordĕo.opening: , no perf. , morsum, 2, v. a. , to bite off (very rare): aliquid, Plin. 28, 4, 11 : ungues, Pers. 1, 106 .

dē-mŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. n. , to die off, to die, depart, decease (i. e. from an office, out of a circle of associates, etc., cf. Fabri ad Liv. 23, 21, 7 . In the class. per. only in the perf. or part. perf.; not found in Caes. and the…

dēmŏror.opening: v. dep. n. and a. Neutr., to loiter, linger, tarry, delay (very rare): me hic demoratam tam diu, Plaut. Rud. 2, 4, 27 : ille nihil demoratus exsurgit, Tac. A. 15, 69 : quamdiu legationis causa ibi demorantur, Dig. 5, 1,…

dē-morsĭto.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. int. a. [demordeo], to bite off (only in Apuleius): ora mortuorum, Ap. M. 2, p. 124: rosas, id. ib. 3 , p. 140.

dēmos.opening: , = δῆμος , orig. a tract of land, demos (pure Lat. pagus); hence, the inhabitants of a demos, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 69 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 5 Müll.

Dēmosthĕnes.opening: ( gen. i, Cic. Opt. Gen. 5, 14 ), , Δημοσθένης , the most celebrated of the Grecian orators , Cic. de Or. 1, 13 ; 20 ; id. Brut. 9 ; Prop. 3 (4), 21, 27 ; Quint. 10, 1, 76 ; 12, 10, 23 sq.; Juv. 10, 114 et saep.—Hence,…

dē-mŏvĕo.opening: (often confounded in MSS. and edd. with di-moveo, q. v.), mōvi, mōtum, 2, v. a. , to move or turn away; to put away, remove (freq. and good prose). Lit. : demoveri et depelli de loco necesse est eum qui deiciatur ...…

demptĭo.opening: demo , a taking away (very rare): demptio aut additio literarum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 6 Müll.: damnum a demptione, id. ib. 5 , § 176.

dē-mūgītus.opening: Part. [mugio], filled with bellowing, lowing : paludes, Ov. M. 11, 376 .

dē-mulcātus.opening: Part. [mulco], beaten, cudgelled soundly : aliquis asperis verberibus, Mart. Cap. 8, § 807 .

dē-mulcĕo.opening: v. a. , to stroke down, to stroke caressingly (rare). Prop.: caput tibi, Ter. Heaut. 4, 5, 14 : dorsum, Liv. 9, 16 fin. : aures, Lact. de Ira, 7, 9: crura, Gell. 5, 14, 12 .— Trop. , to soften, allure : aures omnium…

dēmum.opening: (also demus, like prorsus, quorsus, rursus, deorsus, Liv. Andr. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 70, 8 Müll.; Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 51 Ritschl and Brix), adv. a sup. form from de, downmost; cf.: sub, summus , used to give prominence…

dē-mūneror.opening: v. dep. , to fee, reward : demunerarier ancillas, Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 59 (dub. Umpf. and Fleck. munerarier).

dē-murmŭro.opening: v. a. , to mutter over : carmen, Ov. M. 14, 58 .

dē-mussātus.opening: Part. [musso], borne silently (post-class. and rare): contumelia, Ap. M. 3, p. 140, 26: injuriis omnibus demussatis, Amm. 30, 1, 15 .

dēmūtābĭlis.opening: adj. demuto , changeable (eccl. Lat.), Prud. Apoth. 344 ; Tert. Anim. 2, 1 .

dēmūtātĭo.opening: id. , a changing, change (very rare, and critically certain only in late Lat.): demutatio morum, Cic. Rep. 2, 4, 7 dub.: carnis, Tert. Res. carn. 55; id. adv. Marc. 4, 1 ; 5, 10 fin.

dēmūtātor.opening: id. , a changer, transmuter : ossium, Tert. Res. carn. 32.

dē-mŭtĭlo.opening: v. a. , to lop off : cacumina virgarum, Col. Arb. 11, 2 .

dē-mūto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
dē-mūto.opening: v. a. and n. Act., to change, alter , and sometimes to alter for the worse, to make worse (repeatedly in Plaut. and in post-Aug. prose; otherwise rare; not in the Ciceronian period): voces demutat, Cato ap. Macr. S. 2,…

dē-muttĭo.opening: v. n. , to speak very softly , Isid. 10, 76 .

dēnārismus.opening: denarius , a sort of tax , Cod. Theod. 12, 1, 107 and 123.

dēnārĭus.opening: adj. deni , containing ten . In gen.: numerus digitorum, Vitr. 3, 1 : fistula, ten inches in circumference, Plin. 31, 6, 31, § 58 ; Vitr. 8, 7 : DENARIAE caerimoniae dicebantur et TRICENARIAE, quibus sacra adituris…

dē-narro.opening: v. a. , to tell, relate, recount, narrate (very rare; in the class. per. only once in Hor.): haec adeo ego illi jam denarrabo, Ter. Ph. 5, 7, 51 : matri denarrat, ut, etc., Hor. S. 2, 3, 315 : puer, quid ipse matri…

dē-nascor.opening: v. dep. , to perish, die (ante-class. and rare), opp. nasci, Varr. L. L. 5, § 70 Müll.; 21; Cass. Hem. ap. Non. 101, 29 ( = decrescere, Non.).

dē-nāso.opening: v. a. nasus , to deprive of the nose : os, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 72 .

dē-năto.opening: v. n. , to swim down : Tusco alveo, Hor. Od. 3, 7, 28 .

dendrăchātes.opening: , = δενδραχάτης (tree-agate), a species of agate , Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 139 .

dendrŏīdes.opening: , = δενδροειδής , a kind of tithymalus, Plin. 26, 8, 45, § 71 .

dendrŏphŏrus.opening: , = δενδροφόρος (tree-bearer). An epithet of Sylvanus : SILVANO DENDROPHORO SACRVM, Inscr. Orell. 1602 .—Hence, A college of priests who carried about branches of trees in procession, in honor of a divinity , Inscr.…

dē-nĕgo.opening: v. a. To deny a thing, to say it is not so (very rare): datum denegant, quod datum est, Plaut. Men. 4, 2, 12 : objecta, Tac. A. 15, 57 .—Far more freq. and class. (cf., on the contrary, abnego).— To reject, refuse, deny…

dēni.opening: ( gen. plur. , denum, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 49 fin. ; Col. 2, 10, 26 al. : denorum, Liv. 43, 5 fin. ), num. distrib. [decem], ten each, ten at a time, by tens . Prop.: uxores habent deni duodenique inter se communes, Caes.…

dē-nĭcālis.opening: (in MSS. also written ), , adj. nex , purifying from death; feriae or dies, a funeral solemnity among the Romans for the purification of the family of the deceased : nec vero tam denicales, quae a nece appellatae sunt,…

dēnī^grātĭo.opening: denigro , a blackening : capillorum, Theod. Prisc. 1, 1 .

dē-nī^gro.opening: v. a. , to blacken utterly, dye or color very black (very rare; in the Ciceron. per. not at all). Lit. : terram (amurca), Varr. R. R. 1, 55 fin. : lanam, Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 109 : capillum, id. 23, 5, 53, § 99 : faciem…

dēnĭque.opening: adv. etym. dub.; perh. dēnĭ, locative of de, and que . Orig. denoting succession in time, and thereupon, and then, in the sequel . In gen. (rare—for syn. cf.: tum, demum, tandem, postremo): omnes negabant ... denique…

dēnixē.opening: adv. , = enixe, q. v., Plaut. Trin. 3, 11, 26 Brix.

dēnōmĭnātĭo.opening: denomino , rhetor. t. t., the substitution of the name of an object for that of another to which it has some relation, as the name of the cause for that of the effect, of the property for that of the substance , etc.; a…

dēnōmĭnātīvus.opening: adj., pertaining to derivation, formed by derivation, derived : nomina, Prisc. p. 619 P.— Adv. : , by derivation : dicere aliquid, Mart. Cap. 4, § 381 .

dē-nōmĭno.opening: v. a. , to name, to designate specifically, to denominate (not ante-Aug.; most freq. in Quint.): hinc (sc. ab Lamo) Lamiae denominati, * Hor. Od. 3, 17, 3 ; cf. Auct. Her. 4, 32 ; Quint. 1, 5, 71 : multa sunt et Graece…

dē-normo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. norma , to disfigure, to make irregular or crooked (very rare): angulus, qui nunc denormat agellum, Hor. S. 2, 6, 9 : linea denormata, Auct. de Lim. p. 252 Goes.

dēnŏtātĭo.opening: denoto , a marking or pointing out (late Lat.): omnium denotatione damnatus. Quint. Decl. 19, 3 ; Tert. Cult. fem. 13; Vulg. Sir. 5, 17 .

dēnŏtātus.opening: id. , a marking or pointing out; only denotatui, Tert. Pall. 4 med.

dē-nŏto.opening: v. a. Lit. , to mark, set a mark on , with chalk, color, etc.: pedes venalium creta, Plin. 35, 17, 58, § 199 : lineam conspicuo colore, Col. 3, 15 .— Transf. To mark out, point out, specify, indicate, denote, designate…

dens.opening: ( gen. plur. usually dentium, but dentum is approved by Varr. L. L. 7, 38, 67 ), root in Sanscr. dantas, Gr. ὀδούς, Goth. tunthus, Germ. Zahn, and Engl. tooth; cf. edo, Engl. eat , a tooth. Prop.: cui auro dentes juncti…

densābĭlis.opening: adj. denso , binding, astringent (late Lat.): cibus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 7 : vaporatio, ib. 3, 3 .

densātīvus.opening: adj. id. , binding, astringent (late Lat.): virtutis esse, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37 .

densē.opening: adv., thickly, frequently , etc. v. densus fin.

Denselētae.opening: a tribe of Northern Thrace , Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 40 ; Cic. Pis. 34, 84 ; the same called Dentheleti, Liv. 39, 53 ; 40, 22 .

densĭtas.opening: densus , thickness, density (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : limus spissatur et in densitatem coit, Plin. 35, 15, 51, § 178 : chartae, id. 13, 12, 24, § 78 : umoris, id. 11, 3, 2, § 6 ; Vulg. Isa. 9, 18 al. — Trop. :…

denso.opening: (less freq.) , no perf. , ētum, 2 (cf. Prisc. p. 837 P.; Charis. p. 233 ib. The MSS. often confound the two forms; densare appears to be critically certain in Liv. and Quint.; densere act. only denset, Verg. A. 11, 650…

densus.opening: adj. kindred with δασύς, δαυλός (i. e. δασυλός); cf. Lat. dumus, old form dusmus, and dumetum , thick, dense , i. e. consisting of parts crowded together. opp. to rarus (on the contrary, crassus, thick , is opp. to…

dentāle.opening: , and , (only the plural class.; sing. post-class.), dens, no. I. B. , the share-beam , to which the vomer or ploughshare was attached. Prop., plur. , Verg. G. 1, 172 ; Col. 2, 2, 24 .— Sing. : genus vomerum toto…

dentānĕus.opening: adj., threatening : dentanea (fulgura) quae speciem periculi sine periculo adferunt, Sen. N. Q. 2, 49, 1 fin.

dentārĭus.opening: adj. dens , pertaining to the teeth (in the later medic. lang.): herba, i. e. that cures the toothache , Ap. Herb. 4, 8, 66.

dentarpăga.opening: vox hibr. from dens and ἅρπαξ , an instrument for drawing teeth , Varr. ap. Non. 99, 24 .

dentātus.opening: adj. dens . Toothed, having teeth . Lit. : quosdam et cum dentibus nasci, sicut M. Curium, qui ob id Dentatus cognominatus est, Plin. 7, 16, 15, § 68 : male dentata (puella), Ov. R. Am. 339 ; Mart. 1, 73 .— Pregn.:…

Denter.opening: id. , the surname of M. Livius (consul 452 A. U. C.), Liv. 10, 1 and 9.

Denthēlēthi.opening: Δανθηλῆται , = Denseletae q. v., Liv. 39, 53, 12 al.

Denthelĭăthēs.opening: adj. Δενθάλιοι, a city of the Peloponnesus , Denthelian, belonging to Denthalii : ager, Tac. A. 4, 43 .

dentĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. denticulus , furnished with small teeth, denticulated (post-Aug.): falces, Col. 2, 20, 3 : forfices, Plin. 9, 31, 51, § 97 : conchae, id. 9, 33, 52, § 102 : olus, id. 26, 15, 93, § 164 .

dentĭcŭlus.opening: dim. dens , a little tooth (not ante-Aug.). Lit. , Pall. 1, 28, 6 ; Ap. Mag. p. 278, 9.— Meton. An agricultural implement with teeth , Pall. Jun. 2, 4 .— In archit., a modillion , dental , a small ornament between the…

dentĭdūcum.opening: (sc. instrumentum) [dens-duco], an instrument for drawing teeth , as transl. of the Gr. ὀδονταγωγόν , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4 fin. (in Varro, dentarpaga q. v.).

dentĭfrangĭbŭlus.opening: , and , , dens-frango , a tooth-breaker , a comic word in Plautus. * Masc., one who knocks out teeth , Plaut. Bac. 4, 2, 23 .— * N. pl. (sc. instrumenta), the fist , id. ib. 14 .

dentĭfrĭcĭum.opening: dens - frico , tooth-powder, dentifrice , Plin. 28, 11, 49, § 178 sq. ; 29, 3, 11, § 46 al. ; Scrib. Comp. 59 et saep.

dentĭlĕgus.opening: , i. dens-lego , one who picks up his teeth , sc. after they have been knocked out; a tooth-gatherer , a comic word: dentilegos omnis mortalis faciam, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 18 .

dentĭo.opening: 1. dentio , a teething, dentition , Plin. Val. 1, 4, 2 .

dentiscalpĭum.opening: dens-scalpo , a tooth-pick , Mart. 7, 53 ; 14, 22 in lemm .

dentītĭo.opening: 1. dentio , a teething, dentition , of children, etc., Plin. 28, 19, 78, § 257 sq. ; 30, 15, 47, § 135 sq. al.; Veg. a. v. 3, 25, 1.

dentix.opening: ( , Isid. Orig. 12, 6, 23 ), , dens , a sort of sea-fish; plur. Col. 8, 16, 8 .

dē-nūbo.opening: v. n. , to marry off (sc. from the paternal home; cf. deduco), to marry (rare; perhaps not ante-Aug.). Prop.: nec Caenis in ullos Denupsit thalamos, Ov. M. 12, 196 ; Ap. M. 9, p. 231, 29; 5, p. 166, 6: Claro fratri…

dē-nūdātĭo.opening: a laying bare, uncovering , Vulg. Sir. 11 . 29. From

dē-nūdo.opening: v. a. , to lay bare, make naked, denude . i. q., nudo, to uncover (rare but class.). Lit. : denudatis ossibus, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 44, 106 : ne Verres denudetur a pectore, ne cicatrices populus Romanus aspiciat, Cic.…

dēnuntĭātĭo.opening: ( ), , denuntio , an indication, intimation, announcement, declaration . With gen. obj. = significatio: quae est enim ista a deis profecta significatio et quasi denuntiatio calamitatum? Cic. Div. 2, 25, 54 : belli, id.…

dēnuntĭātīvus.opening: adj. id. , monitory, indicatory , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 67 .

dēnuntĭātor.opening: denuntio , under the emperors (since the second century of the Christian era), a police officer, police inspector , Inscr. Orell. 5 ; 2544 and 3216.

dē-nuntĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. Orig. t. t. in the lang. of pub. law, relig., and jurispr., to give an official intimation, to make an official announcement or declaration of one's intentions (by means of a messenger, herald, etc.); to…

dēnŭō.opening: adv. contr. from dē nŏvo, which never occurs; v. Ruhnk. Ter. And. prol. 26; Oud. App. M. 3, p. 225.; cf.: Fr. de nouveau , anew, afresh, again (most freq. in Plaut. and Ter.; elsewh. rare; not in Caes. or the Aug.…

dĕ-occo.opening: v. a. , to harrow in , Plin. 18, 15, 37, § 137 .

Dēōīs.opening: Δηωΐς , the daughter of Deo ( Δηώ , Ceres), i. e. Proserpine , Ov. M. 6, 114 ; Aus. Ep. 4, 50 .

Dēōĭus.opening: adj., belonging or sacred to Deo ( Δηώ , Ceres): quercus, Ov. M. 8, 761 .

dĕ-ŏnĕro.opening: v. a. , to unload, disburden (very rare). Lit. : machinae deoneratae, Amm. 24, 6, 4 ; Arn. 6, p. 202 .— Trop. : ex illius invidia deonerare aliquid et in te traicere, * Cic. Div. in Caecil. 14, 46 : foeditate corpora…

dĕ-ŏpĕrio.opening: v. a. , to uncover, disclose (late Lat.), Ambros. de Excid. Fr. sui Sat. 2, 80.

dĕ-opto.opening: v. a. , to choose out, select : deoptandi potestas, Hyg. Fab. 191 .

dĕorsum.opening: (dissyll. per synaeresin , Lucr. 1, 362 ; 2, 205 al. ; cf. , on the contrary, trisyll., id. 2, 202 .—Also , , Cic. N. D. 1, 25, 69 ; Ap. M. 8, p. 207, 18; id. ib. 9 , p. 236, 40; id. de Deo Socr. p. 47, 35 ; id. Flor.…

dĕ-oscŭlor.opening: v. dep. a. , to kiss warmly, affectionately (very rare). Prop.: vix reprimo labra, Ob istam rem quin te deosculer, etc., Plaut. Cas. 2, 8, 17 sq. : Casinam, id. ib. 31 : tuos oculos, id. ib. 1, 1, 48 : Scipionis…

dēpactus.opening: , um. Part. , from depaciscor.— Part. , from depango.

dēpālātĭo.opening: 1. depalo . A bounding with palings, a paling off , Inscr. Orell. 3689 .— Dierum, a marking of hours by the shadows of small uprights on a dial , Vitr. 9, 7, 1 .

dēpālātor.opening: id. , one who marks out the bounds; hence, trop., a founder : disciplinae divinae (coupled with architectus), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 6 .

dē-palmo.opening: v. a. palma , to strike with the open hand, to box on the ear , Labeo ap. Gell. 20, 1, 13 .

dē-pālo.opening: v. a. , to mark off or bound with palings (late Lat.). Prop.: jugera agri..ita uti depalatum est, Inscr. Orell. 3688 .— Transf. , to found, establish : quodammodo mundum, Tert. adv. Herm. 29 : civitatem, id. Apol. 10 ;…

dē-pălo.opening: v. a. palam , to disclose, reveal : adulterium Veneris (Sol), Fulg. Myth. 2, 10 ; 3, 6 .

dē-pango.opening: , no perf. , pactum, 3, v. a. , to drive down, drive in, fix into the ground (rare). Lit. : malleolum, Col. 3, 16, 1 ; cf. id. 3, 21, 11 ; Plin. 16, 26, 46, § 110 : quercus et olea in scrobe depactae, id. 24, 1, 1, § 1…

dē-parcus.opening: adj., excessively sparing, niggardly : sordidos ac deparcos esse (putabat), Suet. Ner. 30 .

dē-pasco.opening: v. a. , and , , v. depon., to feed down, feed off . Lit. Of the shepherd: si d. saepius voles, etc., Col. 2, 10, 31 : glandem immisso pecore depasco, Dig. 10, 4, 9 : saltus, Ov. F. 5, 283 : luxuriem segetum, Verg. G. 1,…

dē-păvītus.opening: Part. [pavio], beaten down, trampled down , trop., Sol. 2 .

dēpĕciscor.opening: , -pectus, or , , v. dep. a. [de-paciscor], to bargain for, agree upon; and absol., to make an agreement . Lit. (repeatedly in Cic., elsewh. rare): ipse tria praedia sibi depectus est, Cic. Rosc. Am. 39 fin. : cum illo…

dēpectĭo.opening: depeciscor , a bargain, contract, agreement (late Lat.), Cod. Theod. 2, 10, 1 .

dē-pecto.opening: , no perf. , xum, ĕre, v. a. , to comb off, comb down, to comb (very rare): crines buxo, Ov. F. 6, 229 ; cf. jubas, id. A. A. 1, 630 : Liber depexus crinibus, id. F. 3, 465 : ars depectendi digerendique lini, Plin. 19,…

dēpĕcūlātor.opening: depeculor , a plunderer, embezzler : aerarii, Cic. Verr. 1, 1, 2 ; id. de Or. 3, 27, 106 ; id. Pis. 40, 96 .

dēpĕcūlātus.opening: (depeculor], a plundering : depeculatus a pecore dicitur. Qui enim populum fraudat, peculatus poena tenetur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 75, 11 Müll.: depeculatu ( dat. ) me meis esse habitum, Plaut. Ep. 3, 4, 83 Jacob. (dub. al.…

dē-pĕcūlor.opening: (and old Act. fut. infin. depeculassere, Lucil. ap. Non. 97, 9 ; cf. Neue, Form. 2, 421, and v. infra ), 1, v. dep. a. [peculium], to despoil, pillage, rifle, plunder, embezzle (very rare). Prop.: Apollonium omni…

dē-pello.opening: v. a. , to drive out, drive away, remove, expel; to drive, thrust , or cast down (class. and very freq.). Lit. In gen.: demoveri et depelli de loco, Cic. Caecin. 17, 49 ; cf.: anseres de Falerno, id. Phil. 5, 11 : eum…

dē-pendĕo.opening: v. a. , to hang from or on, to hang down (not freq. till the Aug. period; not in Cic. and Caes.—for syn. cf.: pendeo, impendeo). Lit. : (anellus) unus ex uno, Lucr. 6, 915 ; cf.: sordidus ex umeris nodo dependet…

dē-pendo.grammar: di, sum, 3 v. a. and n.
dē-pendo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. (orig., to weigh out; hence), to pay (rare but class.). Lit. : mi abjurare certius est quam dependere, Cic. Att. 1, 8 fin. ; Col. 5, 1, 8 ; Just. 22, 8, 8 ; Dig. 12, 6, 42 al. : dependendum tibi est,…

dēpendŭlus.opening: adj. dependeo , hanging down (an Apuleian word): crines cervice, Ap. M. 2, p. 119: alii statuis, id. ib. 3 , p. 130, 14.

dē-pennātus.opening: adj. penna , winged , trop.: depennato orationis eloquio, Varr. ap. Fulg. 561, 12 .

dēpensĭo.opening: dependo , the expenditure, outlay : theatralis, Cod. Theod. 6, 4, 29 ; lustralis auri, ib. 13, 1, 11 .

dē-perdo.opening: v a. To destroy, ruin (so only in the part. perf. , and rare): sator inopia deperditus, i. e. impoverished, Phaedr. 1, 14, 1 : ut est deperditus Io, i. e. desperately in love, Prop. 2, 30, 29 (3, 28, 29 M.); cf. amore,…

dē-pĕrĕo.opening: ( fut. deperiet for -ibit, Vulg. Eccl. 31, 7 ), 4, v. n. , to go to ruin, perish, die; to be lost, undone . In gen. (class.): neque adaugescit quicquam neque deperit inde (sc. de materia), Lucr. 2, 296 : tempestate…

dē-pĕtīgo.opening: petigo , a leprosy, scab , spread over the whole body (v. de, no. II. 2. c.), Cato R. R. 157 fin. ; cf.: scabies deque petigo, Lucil. ap. Non. 160, 18 .

dēpictĭo.opening: depingo , a description, delineation , Boeth. Geom. 1, p. 1210 al.— Rhet. t. t., a characterization , = characterismus, Auct. Carm. de Fig. 148, p. 68 Halm.

dē-pĭlis.opening: adj. 1. pilus , without hair (very rare): genae, Ap. M. 7, p. 191: pueri (with glabri), Varr. ap. Non. 530, 25 .

dē-pĭlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. id. , to pull out the hair, pluck out the feathers . Prop. (ante-class. and post-Aug., and rare): depilari magis quam amiciri, Tert. Pall. 4 : perdicem, Apic. 6, 3 ; Mart. 9, 28 : struthiocamelum,…

dē-pingo.opening: ( perf. syncop. depinxti, Plaut. Poen. 5, 2, 154 ), v. a. To depict, portray, paint, draw, represent by painting (rare but class.). Lit. : tabellas obscenas, Prop. 2, 6, 27 : pugnam Marathoniam, Nep. Milt. 6, 3 :…

dē-pinnātus.opening: adj., feathered, winged , only trop.: orationis eloquium, Varr. Sat. Menip. 58, 1 .

dē-plāco.opening: v. a. , to appease, propitiate : aliquem sibi hostiis, Mythogr. Vatic. 1, 231, p. 71 ed. Bod.; Fulg. Myth. 3, 6 dub.

dē-plango.opening: v. a. , to express grief by beating the breast; to bewail, lament ( poet. and very rare): Cadmeida palmis Deplanxere domum, Ov. M. 4, 546 ; 14, 580 ; Sen. Herc. Oet. 1852 : antiqua peccata, Hier. Jes. 1, 1, 1 .

dē-plāno.opening: v. a. , to level off, to make level or even (post-class.): montes, Lact. 4, 12, 18 : vulnus, Veg. A. V. 3 . 19.

dē-planto.opening: v. a. To take off a twig or shoot . Prop., Varr. R. R. 1, 40, 4 : virgulas de cytiso, id. ib. 1, 43 .— Transf. , to break off : ramum, Col. 2, 2, 26 .— = demitto, to set in the ground, to plant , Plin. 17, 16, 26, § 121…

dē-plĕo.opening: v. a. , to empty out, to draw off (very rare): oleum, Cato R. R. 64 fin. ; Col. 12, 50, 8 , and 10: sanguinem, to let blood, to bleed, Plin. 18, 16, 43, § 148 ; for which, d. animal, Veg. A. V. 1, 13, 4 .— Poet. , to…

dē-plexus.opening: adj. plector , clasping, grasping any thing, Lucr. 5, 1321 .

dēplōrābundus.opening: adj. deploro , weeping bitterly , Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 38 (also ap. Non. 509, 7 ).

dē-plōrātĭo.opening: id. , a lamenting, bewailing , id. Sen. Consol. ad Marc. 9 ; Ep. 74 med. ; Tert. Apol. 1 .

dē-plōro.grammar: āvi, ātum v. n. and a.
dē-plōro.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr., to weep bitterly, to moan, wail, lament, complain . Prop. (repeatedly in Cic.; elsewh. not so used): afflictus et jacens et lamentabili voce deplorans, Cic. Tusc. 2, 13 fin. : de suis incommodis,…

dē-plūmis.opening: adj. pluma , without feathers, featherless : nudae atque deplumes (hirundines), Plin. 10, 24, 34, § 70 .

dē-plŭo.opening: v. n. , to rain down ( poet. and very rare): multus in terras deplueretque lapis, Tib. 2, 5, 72 ; (in Prop. 2, 20, 8 (3, 13, 8 M.), the true reading is defluit; so Col. 10, 206 poet. ): depluta terra, drenched , Boëth.…

dē-pŏlĭo.opening: , no perf. , ītum, 4, v. a. , to smooth off, polish off (very rare). Prop.: aliquid cote, Plin. 36, 25, 63, § 188 . —Comic.: dorsum meum virgis, to cudgel, Plaut. Ep. 1, 1, 85 .— Trop. : DEPOLITUM perfectum, quia omnes…

dēpŏlītĭo.opening: depolio, no. II., a careful smoothing or finishing; hence, concr. , a perfection, finished or perfect thing : agri depolitiones, Varr. ap. Non. 66, 29 ; cf. the preced. art.

dēpompātĭo.opening: depompo . Lit. , a depriving of ornament; hence, a dishonoring : Christianorum, Hier. adv. Rufin. 31 .

dē-pompo.opening: v. a. Lit. , to deprive of ornament; hence, to dishonor , Hier. in Nahum. c. 3.

dē-pondĕro.opening: v. n. , to press down by its weight, to weigh down , Petr. Fragm. 26, 3 .

dēpōnens.opening: P. a. , v. the foll. art. fin.

dē-pōno.opening: ( perf. deposivi, Plaut. Curc. 4, 3, 4 : deposivit, id. Most. 2, 1, 35 ; Catull. 34, 8; inf. perf. deposisse, Verg. Cat. 8, 16 ; part. sync. depostus, Lucil. ap. Non. 279, 19 , v. pono), v. a. , to lay away, to put or…

dēpontāni.grammar: senes appellabantur, qui sexagenarii de ponte deiciebantur
dēpontāni.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 75, 7 Müll.; v. sexagenarius.

dēponto.opening: v. a. de-pons , to throw from a bridge , Varr. Sat. Menip. 82, 17 .

dēpŏpŭlātĭo.opening: depopulor , a laying waste, marauding, pillaging (several times in Cic.; elsewh. rare), Cic. Pis. 17, 40 ; Cic. Verr. 1, 4, 12 ; id. Rep. 2, 14 ; Liv. 43, 23 : Thracum, Cic. Font. 22, 44 : Tiberini fluminis igniumque,…

dēpŏpŭlātor.opening: id. , one who lays waste, a marauder, spoiler, pillager : fori, Cic. Dom. 5, 13 ; Caecil. ap. Non. 118, 33 (v. 191 Rib.); Vulg. Isa. 21, 2 .

dēpŏpŭlātrix.opening: depopulator , she who spoils, destroys : generis humani (luxuries), Cassiod. Var. 11, 3 med.

dē-pŏpŭlor.opening: v. dep. a. , to lay waste, ravage, plunder, pillage (class.). Prop.: ut Ambiorigis fines depopularentur, Caes. B. G. 6, 42 fin. ; cf.: ad fines depopulandos, id. ib. 7, 64, 6 ; Hirt. B. G. 8, 24, 4 ; Liv. 10, 12 al. :…

dēportātĭo.opening: deporto (rare), a carrying or conveying away, a transportation . In gen., Cato R. R. 144, 3 .— In partic., a perpetual banishment, transportation, deportation, exile , Dig. 48, 13, 3 ; 48, 22, 6 al. ; cf. deporto, no.…

dēportātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , belonging to removal or transportation : personale vel deportatorium onus, Cod. 12, 47, 1.

dē-porto.opening: ( arch. inf. pass. deportarier, Ter. Ph. 5, 7, 85 ), v. a. , to carry or convey down; to carry off, to convey away (freq. and good prose). In gen.: de fundo tigna et oleam ne deportato, Cato R. R. 144, 3 : arma…

dē-posco.opening: v. a. , to demand, require, request earnestly (freq. and class.). In gen.: unum ab omnibus sociis et civibus ad id bellum imperatorem deposci atque expeti, Cic. de Imp. Pomp. 2, 5 ; cf. id. 15, 44 : id non modo non…

dēpŏsĭtārĭus.opening: depono, no. I. B.; prop. pertaining to a deposit; hence , in jurid. Lat., One who receives a deposit, a trustee, depositary , Dig. 16, 3, 1, § 36 ; 16, 3, 7, § 2 (twice).— One who makes a deposit, a depositor , Dig. 16,…

dēpŏsĭtĭo.opening: depono (post-Aug.; most freq. in jurid. Lat.). Lit. , a laying down, putting off . A depositing for safe-keeping, Dig. 16, 3, 1 ; 5 ; 17 .— A pulling or tearing down : aedificii, Dig. 4, 2, 9, § 2 .— A depositing in the…

dēpŏsĭtīvus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a deposit : pecuniae, given in deposit, Cassiod. Var. 6, 8 .

dēpŏsĭtor.opening: id. (post-Aug. and very rare). One who deposits a thing for safe-keeping, a depositor , Dig. 16, 3, 1, § 37 .— One who disowns or disclaims : patris natique, Prud. Apoth. 179 .

dēpostŭlātor.opening: depostulo , one who demands a person, sc. for punishment, torture, etc.: Christianorum, Tert. Apol. 35 ; cf. ib. 50 fin.

dē-postŭlo.opening: v. a. , to demand, require earnestly ( = the class. deposco): auxilia sibi, Auct. B. Hisp. 1 fin.

dēpraedātĭo.opening: depraedor , a plundering (late Lat.), Cod. 2, 6, 5; Lact. Epit. 11 ; Vulg. Judith, 10, 12 .

dēpraedātor.opening: id. , a plunderer (late Lat.), Aug. Ep. 199 .

dē-praedor.opening: v. dep. a. ( act. collat. form depraedaverunt, Ambros. de Fide, 2, 3), to plunder, pillage, ravage (postclass.; for praedor, depopulor): agros, Just. 24, 6, 3 ; Ap. M. 8, p. 215; Vulg. Job, 24, 9 ; id. Isa. 33, 1 .—In…

dēpraesentĭārum.opening: adv. formed after the analogy of impraesentiarum , at present, now (only in the foll. passages), Petr. 58, 3 ; 74, 17 .

dē-prandis.opening: adj. prandeo , fasting : leo, Naev. ap. Fest. p. 182, 24 Müll.

dēprāvātē.opening: adv., perversely, wrongly : neque depravate judicare neque corrupte, Cic. Fin. 1, 21, 71 .

dēprāvātĭo.opening: depravo , a perverting, distorting, corrupting, vitiating (freq. in Cic.; elsewh. rare). Lit. : distortio et depravatio quaedam (membrorum), Cic. Fin. 5, 12, 35 ; cf.: pedum, manuum, articulorum omnium depravationes,…

dē-prāvo.opening: v. a. pravus , to pervert, distort, disfigure (opp. dirigere, corrigere; good prose). Lit. : depravata corrigere crura, Varr. L. L. 9, § 11 Müll.; cf. opp. corrigere, Cic. Fin. 1, 6 ; id. Div. 2, 46 : (oculi) uni…

dēprĕcābĭlis.opening: adj. deprecor , that may be entreated, exorable (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Psa. 90, 13 .

dēprĕcābundus.opening: adj. id. , earnestly entreating : deprecabundus et genibus principis accidens, Tac. A. 15, 53 .

dēprĕcānĕus.opening: adj. id. , exorable : fulmina, quae speciem periculi sine periculo afferunt, Caecinna ap. Sen. Q. N. 2, 49 (dub.—al. dentanea).

dēprĕcātĭo.opening: id. , a warding off or averting by prayer; a deprecating, deprecation . Prop. In gen.: periculi. Cic. Rab. perd. 9, 26: venia deprecationis, Quint. prooem. § 2.— Esp., in relig. lang., an imprecation : defigi diris…

dēprĕcātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. deprecatio , a little deprecation, a trifling plea for pardon , Salv. adv. Avar. 3, 2 .

dēprĕcātīvus.opening: adj. deprecor , deprecative : qualitas, Mart. Cap. 5, § 457 : venia, Fortun. Art. Rhet. 1, 16 : sententiae, Isid. 2, 21, 18 .

dēprĕcātor.opening: id. , one who averts by praying; an interceder, intercessor : hujus periculi, Cic. Balb. 18 : miseriarum, id. Fl. 1 : causae suae, Tac. H. 3, 31 : non solum sui deprecator, sed etiam accusator mei, Cic. Att. 11, 8, 2 ;…

dēprĕcātōrĭus.opening: adj. deprecator , deprecatory : verba, Vulg. 1 Macc. 10, 24 .

dēprĕcātrix.opening: deprecator , a female intercessor (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 12 .

dē-prĕcor.opening: v. dep. a. To avert, ward off (from one's self or others) by earnest prayer; to deprecate; also to pray, to intercede for the averting of any evil, or to obtain pardon for any transgression (cf. Gell. 6, 16, 3 ). In…

dē-prĕhendo.opening: or (v. prehendo; cf. Quint. 9, 4, 59 ), , v. a. To take or snatch away , esp. any thing which is in motion; to seize upon, catch (freq. and class.—For syn. cf.: invenio, reperio, nanciscor; offendo, aperio, patefacio,…

dēprĕhensĭo.opening: deprehendo, no. II. , a catching, seizing, surprising; a discovery (very rare): deprehensione fieri manifestum furem, Dig. 47, 2, 7 ; cf. ib. 23, 2, 43, § 12 : manifesta veneni, * Cic. Clu. 18, 50 .

dēprensa.opening: deprehendo , a species of military punishment, more severe than castigatio, but milder than ignominia, Paul. ex Fest. p. 71, 15 Müll.

dēpressĭo.opening: deprimo , a pressing or sinking down, a depression (not ante-Aug., and very rare), Macr. S. 1, 20 : fundamentorum ad solidum, Vitr. 1, 3, 2 : Socratica nasi, i. e. flat nose (opp. curva erectio), Macr. S. 7, 3, § 11 .

dēpressus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from deprimo.

dēprĕtĭātor.opening: ( ), , depretio , one who depreciates, a depreciator : operum, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 29 .

dēprĕtĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. pretium , to lower the price of, to undervalue, to depreciate (post-class.). Prop.: vetera corpora depretiata sunt, Dig. 9, 2, 22 ; cf. Gai. Inst. 3, § 212 : vilescit pretio depretiatus homo, Paul. Nol.…

dē-prĭmo.opening: v. a. premo , to press down, weigh down, sink down, to depress (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: vis venti nubem deprimit, Lucr. 6, 432 : qui (Critolaus) tantum propendere illam lancem putet, ut terram et maria…

dē-proelĭor.opening: v. n. , only in Part., warring violently : ventos aequore fervido Deproeliantes, Hor. Od. 1, 9, 11 .

dē-prōmo.opening: (-msi), promptum (-mtum), 3, v. a. , to draw out, draw forth; to bring, to fetch from anywhere, esp. out of any place (rare but class.).—Constr., usu. abl. w. ex or de of things, with a of persons; poet. and late Lat.…

dē-prŏpĕro.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr., to make great haste, to hasten : cito introite, et cito deproperate, Plaut. Cas. 3, 6, 17 .— Act., to hasten or accelerate greatly, to prepare hastily (very rare): coronas, * Hor. Od. 2, 7, 24 :…

dē-prŏpĕrus.opening: adj. , = de-properans, making great haste, hastening , Cod. Th. 7, 1, 13 (cf. Cod. 12, 36, 12).

dē-prŏpĭtĭo.opening: v. a. , = ἐξιλάσκομαι , to propitiate, reconcile , Vulg. Interp. ap. Aug. Quest. in Hept. 2, 133 .

depso.opening: v. a. , = δεψέω , to knead . Prop.: id ubi excoxeris, depsito bene, Cato, R. R. 90 ; cf. id. ib. 76 : lu tum, id. ib. 40, 4 : coria, to dress, to curry, id. ib. 135 : tibi fortasse alius molit et depsit, Varr. ap. Non.…

depstīcĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. depso , kneaded : panis, Cato R. R. 74 .

dēpūbes.opening: not of full age : porcus lactens qui prohibitus sit pubes fieri, Paul. ex Fest. p. 71, 23 Müll.

dē-pŭdesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become shameless (post-class. and rare): infamiā, Ap. M. 10, p. 253.—With gen. : non depudesco infelicitatis meae, am not ashamed , Hier. ad Eustoch.

dēpŭdet.opening: v. impers. * To be greatly ashamed : cum eum non depuderet mare infestare, Vell. 2, 73 fin. — Not to be ashamed, to become shameless (perh. not ante-Aug.; very rare): depuduit, Ov. H. 4, 155 : assiduis conviciis…

dē-pŭdīco.opening: v. a. pudicus , to violate, dishonor : stupro, Laber. ap. Gell. 16, 7 .

dē-pūgis.opening: ( ), , adj. pyga , without buttocks , or thin-buttocked , ἄπυγος , Hor. S. 1, 2, 93 .

dēpugnātĭo.opening: depugno , a violent fighting, eager contest (ante- and postclass.). Prop., Cato ap. Non. 204, 32 ; Veg. Mil. 3, 30 et saep.— Transf. Of debate: forensium certaminum depugnationes, Firm. Math. 4 praef.— A defacing :…

dē-pugno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dē-pugno.opening: v. n. and a. To fight eagerly, fight out; to contend, combat violently . Prop. (freq. and class.): collatis signis, Plaut. Cas. 2, 5, 44 ; cf. Liv. 34, 46 : acie instructā, * Caes, B. G. 7, 28: multi depugnant…

dēpulpo.opening: to grow lean , άποσαρκῶ , Gloss. Lat. Gr. [de-pulpa].

dēpulsĭo.opening: depello . A driving off, driving away, repelling, warding off . In gen.: depulsio mali, Cic. Fin. 2, 13, 41 : doloris, id. ib. 5, 7, 17 : servitutis, id. Phil. 8, 4, 12 .— Esp. in rhetor., a defence against a charge,…

dēpulso.opening: v. int. a. [id.], to thrust away, push aside : cubitis depulsa de via, Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 13 .

dēpulsor.opening: id. , one who drives away, removes, repels (rare): dominatus, * Cic. Phil. 2, 11, 27 : malorum, Lact. 2, 14, 13 : alius vel servator honorum vel malorum depulsor, Boëth. Cons. Phil. 4, 6.—In inscriptions, an epithet of…

dēpulsōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , serving to avert , sc. evil: sacra, Plin. 28, 2, 3, § 11 ; Amm. 25, 2, 4 .

dē-pungo.opening: v. a. (to prick down, i. e.), to mark off, to designate : ubi sistam, Pers. 6, 79 .

dēpurgātĭo.opening: depurgo , a cleansing by purgatives : ventris, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4 ; id. ib. 3, 21 .

dēpurgātīvus.opening: adj. id. , purifying, purgative , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 16 .

dē-purgo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to clean out, cleanse (rare): prata, Cato R. R. 50, 1 : acina, id. ib. 112, 2 : terram ab herba, id. 151 : caules lactucae, Col. 12, 9, 1 : sordes, id. 9, 14, 13 : pisces, Plaut. Stich. 2,…

dē-pŭto.opening: v. a. In agriculture, to cut off, prune : vineam, Cato R. R. 49, 1 ; 50, 1 : arbores, Col. 11, 2, 32 : palmites falce, id. 4, 7, 1 : malleolum, id. 3, 10, 19 .— Poet. : umbras (i. e. ramos), Ov. de Nuce, 63.— Ante- and…

dē-pŭvĭo.opening: v. a. from pavio; cf. contubernium, from taberna , to strike, beat : palmis misellam depuvit me, Lucil. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 70, 3 Müll.

dē-questus.opening: Part. [queror], having deeply deplored, bitterly complained of (in post-Aug. poetry): secum dequesta labores, Val. Fl. 5, 448 : imbres, Stat. Th. 1, 404 ; cf. talia, id. 11, 627 .

dē-rādo.opening: v. a. , to rub or scrape off, to smooth off, shave off (anteclass. and post-Aug.): de virga lauri deradito, Cato R. R. 121 : atramentum scalpro, Cels. 8, 4 ; 5, 26, 35 ; cf. ceram, Gell. 17, 9, 17 ; and: nomen urbis ex…

Derbē.opening: , = Δέρβη , a fortified city of Lycaonia, residence of Cicero's friend, the tyrant Antipater; a place of refuge for Christians under persecution , now Divlé, Vulg. Act. 14, 6 ; 16, 1 .—Hence, , , or , , , an inhabitant…

Derbīces.opening: ( Δέρβικες ), a people of Asia, near the mouth of the Oxus, on the Caspian Sea , Mel. 3, 5, 4 ; Curt. 3, 2, 7 ; Plin. 6, 16, 18, § 48 .

derbĭōsus.opening: adj., scabby ( = impetiginosus): oculi, Theod. Prisc. 1, 10 .

dercĕa.opening: a plant, called also herba Apollinaris, a species of the solanum, Ap. Herb. 22.

Dercĕtis.opening: , and , , , Δερκίτις and Δερκετώ , a Syrian goddess, called also Atargatis, supposed to be the same with the Greek Aphrodite , Ov. M. 4, 45 ; Hyg. Fab. 223 ; Plin. 5, 23, 19, § 81 .

dērĕlictĭo.opening: derelinquo , an abandoning; trop., a disregarding, neglecting : communis utilitatis, Cic. Off. 3, 6, 30 .

dērĕlictor.opening: derelinquo , one who abandons (late Lat.): legis, Hier. in Psa. 88 .

dērĕlictus.opening: derelinquo , an abandoning; trop., a neglecting, neglect : aliquid habere derelictui, Gell. 4, 12, 2 .

dē-rĕlinquo.opening: v. a. In the class. lang., to forsake wholly, to abandon, desert (good prose): cf.: Ti. Gracchum a Q. Tuberone derelictum videbamus, Cic. Lael. 11, 37 : ut aratores agros latos ac fertiles desererent totasque arationes…

dē-rĕpentĕ.opening: adv. (qs. departing from the regular course of time), suddenly, on a sudden (mostly ante-class—for syn. cf.: desubito, subito, repente, statim, continuo, confestim, actutum, extemplo, etc.): derepente contulit sese in…

dē-rēpo.opening: v. n. , to crawl down, sneak down (very rare): derepit ad cubile setosae suis, Phaedr. 2, 4, 12 : ad hominum fana, Varr. ap. Non. 544, 29 ; Ap. M. 4, p. 145.—* With acc. : ursi arborem aversi derepunt, Plin. 8, 36, 54,…

dē-rīdĕo.opening: v. a. , to laugh at, laugh to scorn; to scoff at, deride (class.). With acc. : omnes istos deridete atque contemnite, Cic. de Or. 3, 14, 54 ; so with contemnere, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 92 fin. : te, Hor. S. 2, 3, 53 : derisus…

dērīdĭcŭlus.opening: adj. derideo , very laughable, ridiculous (not in Cic. and Caes.): is deridiculu 'st omnibus, Plaut. Mil. 2, 1, 14 : pueri, Gell. 13, 30, 9 : versus, id. 12, 2, 3 : quod est deridiculum, Varr. R. R. 1, 18, 5 ; so Liv.…

dē-rĭgeo.opening: v. a. , to remove hardness, to soften , Commod. 73, 8 .

dē-rĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. (occurring only in the perf. ), to become stiff or rigid; to curdle (a poet. word): formidine sanguis deriguit, Verg. A. 3, 260 : deriguere oculi, were fixed, id. ib. 7, 447 ; so, oculi, Ov. M. 14, 754 :…

dē-rĭpĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. rapio , to tear off, tear away, snatch away, remove violently; to pull down (class., esp. freq. in poets). Lit. constr., with abl. with or without a prep. , or rarely with dat. : aliquem de ara, Plaut. Rud.…

dērīsĭo.opening: derideo , a laughing to scorn, mockery, derision (late Lat. for irrisio, illusio), Arn. 7, p. 239 ; Lact. 4, 18 .

dērīsor.opening: id. , a mocker, scoffer, satirical person (rare; not in Cic.): ut tu semper eris derisor, Hor. S. 2, 6, 54 ; id. A. P. 433 ; Quint. 3, 8, 51 : Anubis derisor populi, Juv. 6, 534 ; Vulg. Prov. 9, 7 al. Applied to a…

dērīsōrĭus.opening: adj. derisor , serving for laughter, ridiculous : condiciones, Dig. 28, 7, 14 .

dērīsus.opening: derideo , mockery, scorn, derision (perh. not ante-Aug.): facile ad derisum stulta levitas ducitur, Phaedr. 5, 7, 3 ; Sen. Contr. 4 prooem.; Quint. 6, 3, 7 ; Tac. Agr. 39 ; esp.: in derisum facere, to mock, put to…

dērīvāmentum.opening: derivo , a derivation , Sen. Ep. ad Paul. 14 .

dērīvātĭo.opening: derivo , a leading off, turning off, turning away . Lit. : derivationes fluminum, * Cic. Off. 2, 4, 14 : sollemnis (sc. lacus Albani), Liv. 5, 15 (cf. shortly before, priusquam ex lacu Albano aqua emissa foret).— Trop.…

dērīvātīvus.opening: adj. id. , in the later grammat. lang., derivative : nomina, Prisc. p. 593 P.: species verborum, id. p. 824 ib. et saep.

dē-rīvo.opening: v. a. rivus , to lead, turn , or draw off a liquid, from or to a place. Prop.: de fluvio aquam, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 12 sq. : aqua ex flumine derivata, * Caes. B. G. 7, 72, 3 : flumen, Hirt. ib. 8, 40, 3 ; Liv. 5, 15, 12…

dērŏgātĭo.opening: derogo , a partial abrogation of a law, a derogation : tertium est (genus) de legum derogationibus, etc., Cic. Cornel. I. Frag. 11 ; Auct. Her. 2, 10, 15 .

dērŏgātor.opening: id. , a detractor, depreciator (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 3, 13 .

dērŏgātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , belonging to a derogation or partial repeal, derogatory : edictum, Dig. 25, 4, 2 .

dē-rŏgĭto.opening: v. intens. a. , to ask urgently , Plaut. As. 2, 2, 60 (dub.).

dē-rŏgo.opening: v. a. , jurid. t. t., to repeal a part of a law, to restrict or modify it. Prop.: huic legi nec obrogari fas est, neque derogari ex hac aliquid licet, neque tota abrogari potest, Cic. Rep. 3, 22 ; cf.: de lege aliquid…

dē-rōsus.opening: Part. [derodo, not in use], gnawed away, nibbled : clipeos a muribus, * Cic. Div. 1, 44, 99 : vitis a cochleis, Plin. 11, 37, 62, § 164 : ficus a locustis, id. 17, 25, 38, § 241 .

Dertōna.opening: a city in Liguria , now Tortona , Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 49 ; Brut. ap. Cic. Fam. 11, 10, 5 ; Vell. 1, 15 .

dē-runcĭno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. runcina , to plane off; hence, in the lang. of comedy, to deceive, cheat; to shave (only in the foll. passages): militem, Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 6 : ego deruncinatus, deartuatus sum miser, id. Capt. 3,…

dē-rŭo.opening: v. a. and n. (a very rare word). Act., to throw or cast down . Lit. : hiems immensam vim aquarum ruptis nubibus deruat, Sen. Q. N. 3, 27 .— Trop. , to take away, detract : cumulum de laudibus alicujus, * Cic. Att. 16,…

dē-ruptus.opening: Part. [derumpo, not in use], broken; hence, like abruptus, of localities, precipitous, steep (not before Lucret.): dextra pars (maceriae) in aliquantum altitudinis, Liv. 42, 15 ; so, saxa, Lucr. 6, 539 : ripae, Liv. 37,…

dē-sā^cro.opening: (also written desecro; cf. consecro), , v. a. (post-Aug. and rare for the class. consecro), to consecrate, dedicate . Prop.: quercum Triviae, Stat. Th. 9, 586 .— (Acc. to consecro, no. I. B.) Of persons, to deify ,…

dē-saevĭo.opening: (the pluperfect subj. contr. desaevisset, Suet. Ner. 29 ), , v. n. To rave furiously, to rage (not anteAug., and very rare): toto Aeneas desaevit in aequore, Verg. A. 10, 569 : pelago hiems, id. ib. 4, 52 : omnes in…

dē-salto.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to dance through, to represent by dancing (very rare): desaltato cantico abiit, Suet. Calig. 54 fin. : fabulosas antiquitatum libidines, Cypr. de Spectac. med.

dē-scendo.opening: ( perf. redupl. : descendidit, Valer. Antias ap. Gell. 7, 4 fin. ; and, descendiderant, Laber. ib.; perf. : desciderunt, Inscr. Frat. Arv. 13 Henzen.), v. n. , to come down; and of inanimate subjects, to fall, sink…

dēscensĭo.opening: descendo (postAug.), a going down, descending . Prop.: balinearum, into the bath, Plin. 20, 17, 69, § 178 : Tiberina, the sail down the Tiber, Cic. Fin. 5, 24, 70 : grando in descensione saltus, upon the thickets, Vulg.…

dēscensōrĭus.opening: adj. descendo , descending, coming downwards : motus, Ambros. de Spir. Sanc. 1, 10, 118 .

dēscensus.opening: descendo , a descent (rare; not in Cic. and Caes.). In gen.: qua illi descensus erat, Sall. C. 57, 3 .— Concr., a descending way, a descent : difficilis et praeruptus, Hirt. B. G. 8, 40, 4 and 5; cf.: facilis descensus…

dē-scindo.opening: v. a. , to divide : Sacerdotes clusi succincti libellis acceptis carmen descindentes tripodaverunt, i. e. marking, in singing, the pauses and measure , Inscr. Frat. Arv. 41. (Henz.; cf.: carmina divides, Hor. Od. 1, 15,…

dē-scisco.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 3 v. n.
dē-scisco.opening: v. n. , orig. a publicist's t. t. to free one's self from a connection with any one, to withdraw, leave, revolt from , = sciscendo deficere; and with an indication of the terminus, to desert to, go over to any one…

dē-scŏbīno.opening: v. a. scobina , to file or scrape off (ante- and postclass., and very rare): supercilia, Varr. ap. Non. 492, 11 ; id. ib. 99, 28 ; Arn. 6, p. 200 .

dē-scrībo.opening: (in MSS. and edd. often confounded with discribo, q. v.), , v. a. To copy off, transcribe any thing from an original (freq. in Cic.; elsewh. rare): scripsit Balbus ad me, se a te (i. e. e tuo exemplo) quintum de Finibus…

dēscriptĭo.opening: (in MSS. and edd. often confounded with discriptio, v. infra ), describo (freq. in Cic.), a marking out, delineation, copy, transcript : in concreto. Lit. (rare): eadem caeli descriptio, Cic. Rep. 6, 22 ; cf. id. ib. 1,…

dēscriptĭuncŭla.opening: dim. descriptio , a short description, delineation : celebres subtexere, Sen. Suas. 2, 10 .

dēscriptīvus.opening: adj., containing an exact description : definitio, Boëth. defin. p. 65: loci communes, Fortun. Art. Rhet. 3, 20 .

dēscriptor.opening: describo , a describer, delineator : morum, Lact. 5, 9, 19 : descriptores gentium, ethnographers, Amm. 23, 6, 1 .

dēscriptus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from describo.

dē-scrŏbo.opening: v. a. scrobs , to set, enchase (late Lat.): gemmas auro, Tert. Res. carn. 7.

dē-sculpo.opening: v. a. , to carve out, to copy by carving or graving (late Lat.): simulacrum ligno, Tert. ad Nat. 1, 12 .

dēsĕcātĭo.opening: a cutting off : ramorum, Cassiod. in Psa. 130 : unus ensis, sed duas desecationes habet, edges, id. ib. 149, 7 . From

dē-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut off, cut away (class.): vitem, Varr. R. R. 1, 41, 3 : partes ex toto, Cic. Univ. 7 : uvas a vite, Col. 12, 43, 1 : segetes et prata, id. 11, 1, 8 : spicas fascibus, Liv. 42, 64 : particulam undique, *…

dēsectĭo.opening: deseco , a cutting off : stramentorum, Col. 6, 3, 1 .

dē-sĕnesco.opening: v. n. , to diminish by age, to die away : ira belli desenuit, Sall. ap. Prisc. p. 887 P. (Hist. 1, 93 Dietsch).

dēseps.opening: adj. de - sapio , out of one's mind, insane , Schol. Juv. 10, 233 .

dē-sĕro.opening: v. a. Lit. , to undo or sever one's connection with another; hence, with esp. reference to the latter, to leave, forsake, abandon, desert, give up (cf. derelinquere; more restricted in signif. than relinquere, which…

dē-serpo.opening: v. n. , to creep down (post-Aug. and very rare): genis lanugo, Stat. Th. 6, 586 ; cf. Ap. Mag. p. 315.

dēsertĭo.opening: 2. desero , a forsaking, deserting (rare; perh. not ante-Aug.).— Milit. t. t. (acc. to 2. desero, no. I. B.), desertion : peccatum desertionis, Dig. 49, 16, 3, § 6 ; 5, § 2 al.

dēsertor.opening: id. , one who forsakes, abandons, deserts any one.— Prop. In gen.: amicorum (opp. conservator inimicorum), Cic. Att. 8, 9, 3 : communis utilitatis aut salutis, id. Fin. 3, 19, 64 .—Esp. freq., Milit. t. t. , a runaway,…

dēsertrix.opening: desertor , she that forsakes, neglects : divinae legis, Tert. de hab. mulier. 1.

dēsertus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from desero.

dē-servĭo.opening: v. n. , to serve zealously, be devoted to, subject to (rare, but class.): valetudini tuae, dum mihi deservis, servisti non satis, Cic. Fam. 16, 18 : cuivis, id. Off. 1, 30, 109 : amicis, id. Sull. 9 : grammatico soli…

dēses.opening: ( nom. sing. appears not to occur), adj. desideo , inactive, indolent, idle (syn.: iners, segnis, piger, ignavus, socors, tardus—rare, perh. not ante-Aug., nor in Aug. poets). Prop.: sedemus desides domi, Liv. 3, 68 ;…

dē-sicco.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to dry up, to desiccate (ante- and post-class.): vasa, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 30 ; Ser. Samm. 48, 900 .

dē-sĭdĕo.opening: v. n. sedeo , to remain or continue sitting, to sit long; and with the accessory idea of inactivity, to sit idle, to remain inactive (rare; not in Cic.). In gen.: tam diu Ibi desidere neque redire filium, Plaut. Bac. 2,…

dēsīdĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. desidero , desirable (rare): desiderabilia (anteponantur) iis, quibus facile carere possis, Cic. Top. 18, 69 ; id. Fin. 1, 16, 53 : velut suis vitiis, Liv. 24, 5 : princeps, Tac. H. 2, 76 : terra, Vulg. Psa. 105,…

dēsīdĕranter.opening: adv., eagerly , v. , P. a. 1 fin.

dēsīdĕrātĭo.opening: desidero , a desiring, longing for any thing; a missing (rare): voluptatum, * Cic. de Sen. 14, 47 ; plur. Vitr. 8 praef. fin. — The question to be examined : relinquetur desideratio, quid, etc., Vitr. 2, 6, 4 .

dēsīdĕrātīvus.opening: adj. id. , in the late gram. lang. desiderative : verba (e. g. esurio, coenaturio, etc.), Aug. p. 2006 P.

dēsīdĕrĭum.opening: desidero , a longing, ardent desire or wish , properly for something once possessed; grief, regret for the absence or loss of any thing (for syn. cf.: optio, optatio, cupido, cupiditas, studium, appetitio,…

dē-sīdĕro.opening: v. a. etym. dub.; cf. considero , to long for, greatly wish for, to desire something not possessed (freq. and class.—for syn. cf.: opto, requiro, expeto, appeto, affecto, cupio, concupisco, aveo, gestio, capto, volo).…

dēsĭdĭa.opening: desideo , a sitting long, remaining in a place. Prop. (rare), Prop. 1, 15, 6 .— A sitting idle, idleness, inactivity, slothfulness (class.; for syn. cf.: inertia, languor, otium, pax, feriae, justitium, dies fasti,…

dēsīdĭa.opening: desido , a subsiding, retiring (an Appuleian word): maris, Ap. de Mundo, p. 73, 28: sanguinis, id. Dogm. Plat. p. 17, 15 .

dēsĭdĭōsus.opening: adv. desidia , qs. full of idleness, i. e. slothful, indolent, lazy (for syn. cf.: piger, segnis, iners, deses, ignavus, socors, lentus, tardus, otiosus). Prop. (rare): qui in oppido sederent quam qui rura colerent,…

dē-sīdo.opening: (de-sīdi, Cic. l. l. infra, Lampr id. Alex. Sev. 39, 7 ), , v. n. , v. consido. —Of inanimate things, esp. of places, to sink, fall , or settle down . Prop.: tantos terrae motus factos esse, ut multa oppida corruerint,…

dēsīdŭō.opening: adv. , "dicitur diuturne," a long time , Varr. ap. Fulg. p. 565, 2 .

dēsignātĭo.opening: or (the latter form better in sense II. Brambach s. v. Lex Jul. Munic. ap. Corp. Inscr. Lat. p. 206), , id. . A marking out, describing, designating : cellarum, Vitr. 5, 5 : undarum, id. 5, 3 : quadrata, id. 3, 1, 3 . —…

dēsignātor.opening: or (the latter form freq. in inscrr., and preferred by Brambach; so Keller, ad Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 5 ; Corp. Inscr. Lat. pp. 597, 768), , id. , one who regulates or arranges; a regulator .—As a t. t., An officer whose duty…

dē-signo.opening: or (the latter form preferred by Brambach in sense II. B. 2. infra; so Keller, ad Hor. Ep. 1, 5, 16 ; cf. Roby, L. G. 2, p. 384), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. , to mark out, trace out (freq. in the Aug. per.); to describe,…

Dĕsĭlāüs.opening: Δεσίλαος , a Grecian painter , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 75 (dub. Jan. Ctesilaus).

dē-sĭlĭo.opening: (desului, Plaut. Rud. prol. 75 : desilivi, Col. 6, 24, 3 : desilii, id. 8, 5, 14 ; Curt. 4, 12, 3 al. ), , v. n. salio , to leap down . Prop. (class.). Constr. with abl. of the place whence, after de, ex , poet. and in…

dē-sĭno.opening: (rarely īvi, Sol. 35, 4 , v. Neue, Form. II. 404; also, sync. perf. : desit, Mart. 6, 26, 3 : desisse, Cic. Fam. 9, 24, 2 ; Suet. Ner. 33 ; 46 ; Gell. 15, 16, 2 : desissem, Catull. 36, 5 al.: DESI, dissyl., Inscr.…

dēsĭŏcŭlus.opening: desino-oculus , one who has lost an eye , Mart. 12, 59, 9 .

dēsĭpĭentĭa.opening: desipio , want of understanding, foolishness , Lucr. 3, 499 .

dē-sĭpĭo.opening: ( perf. desipui, Lact. 2, 4 , 4), v. a. and n. sapio . * Act., to render insipid (late Lat. and rare), Tert. Pudic. 13 . — Neutr., to be void of understanding, to be silly, foolish; to act foolishly (class.): summos…

dē-sisto.opening: ( perf. destitĕrunt, Lucr. 4, 975 ), v. a. and n. (for syn. v. desino init. ). Act., to set down : in scopulo puellam, Ap. M. 4, p. 157 ( Anthol. Lat. 3, 174, 1 ).— Neutr . To stand off from a thing, to stand apart :…

dēsĭtus.opening: desino , a ceasing : spiritus, Jul. Valer. rer. gest. Alex. M. 3, 87.

dē-sĭtus.opening: Part. [1. sero], sown or planted deep : semina, Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 6 .

dēsōlātĭo.opening: desolo , a desolating, desolation (eccl. Lat.). Abstr.: in sua desolatione, Vulg. Baruch, 4, 33 ; Salv. Gub. Dei , 6, p. 214: templi, Hilar. in Psa. 58, 7 al.— Concr., a desert , Vulg. Jer. 7, 34 ; id. 44, 22 .

dēsōlātor.opening: desolo , a waster, one who makes lonely or desolate , Aug. Serm. 115 , no. 5; Hieron. in Amos, III. ad 7, 4 sq.

dēsōlātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , that makes lonely or desolate (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Psa. 120, 4 ; Hier. Ep. 18 , no. 14.

dē-sōlo.opening: v. a. , to leave alone, to forsake, abandon, desert (not anteAug., perh. first used by Verg.; most freq. in the part. perf. ). Verb finit. : desolavimus agros, Verg. A. 11, 367 : agros profugiendo, Col. 1, 3, 11 :…

dē-sorbĕo.opening: v. a. , to swallow down : vortex, Tert. Idol. 24 al. ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 804 .

dēspectātĭo.opening: despecto , a looking down, a prospect , Vitr. 2, 8 med. dub. (al. disparationes).

dēspectātor.opening: id. , one who looks down; trop., a despiser : divinarum sententiarum, Tert. ad Uxor. 8 .

dēspectĭo.opening: despicio , a looking down upon; trop., a despising, contempt : humanarum opinionum, Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 288, 24 : effundit despectionem super principes, Vulg. Job, 12, 21 al.

dēspecto.opening: v. intens. a. [id.], to look down upon any thing from a height (perh. not ante-Aug.). Prop.: ex alto terras, Ov. M. 4, 624 ; so, terras, Verg. A. 1, 396 : humum, Ov. M. 2, 710 : aquas, id. ib. 15, 699 : flammas, Verg.…

dēspector.opening: despicio, no. II. , a despiser , Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 23 .

dēspectrix.opening: despector , she that despises, a despiser : mundi (virtus), Tert. Anim. 23 .

dēspectus.opening: despicio . A looking down upon; hence, a view or prospect from an elevated place (repeatedly in Caes.; elsewh. rare; not in Cic.): erat ex oppido Alesia despectus in campum, Caes. B. G. 7, 79, 3 : in mare, id. ib. 3, 14…

dēspērābĭlis.opening: adj. despero , incurable, desperate : plaga mea, Vulg. Jer. 15, 18 .

dēspēranter.opening: adv., desperately, hopelessly , v. despero fin., no. 1.

dēspērātē.opening: adv., hopelessly , etc., v. despero, P. a., no. 2. fin.

dēspērātĭo.opening: despero , hopelessness, despair : desperatio est aegritudo sine ulla rerum exspectatione meliorum, Cic. Tusc. 4, 8, 18 . Prop. (good prose and very freq.). With gen. : omnium rerum amissio et desperatio recuperandi,…

dēspērātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from despero.

dē-sperno.opening: v. a. , to despise greatly, disdain : opes, Col. poët. 10, 298.

dē-spēro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dē-spēro.opening: v. n. and a. , to be hopeless; to have no hope of, to despair of, to give up (freq. and class.).—Constr. most freq. with de , the acc. , or acc. and inf.; less freq. with the dat. or absol. With de (in Cic. rarely): de…

dēspĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. despicor , contemptible, despicable (post-class.): homo, Amm. 26, 8, 5 ; Ambros. in Psa. 28, § 3 al. — Comp. , Sid. Ep. 2, 10 .

dēspĭcātĭo.opening: id. , contempt. —Plur. : despicationes adversantur voluptatibus, i. e. sentiments of contempt, Cic. Fin. 1, 20, 67 .

dēspĭcātus.opening: despicor , contempt (very rare, only in dat. ): aliquem habere despicatui, to despise , * Plaut. Men. 4, 3, 19 : si quis despicatui ducitur, is despised , * Cic. Fl. 27, 65 .

dēspĭcĭentĭa.opening: despicio , a despising, contempt (very rare; perh. only in Cic.): in omnium rerum humanarum contemptione ac despicientia, Cic. Tusc. 1, 40 : rerum externarum, id. Off. 1, 20 : animi, id. ib. 2, 11 : in contemnendis…

dē-spĭcĭo.opening: ( inf. perf. despexe, Plaut. Mil. 2, 6, 72 ), v. n. and a. To look down upon any thing (for syn. cf.: contemno, sperno, aspernor). Lit. (mestly poet. ). Neutr. : ad te per impluvium tuum, Plaut. Mil. 2, 6, 72 ; 2, 3, 16…

dēspĭcor.opening: v. dep. a. [despicio, no. I. B.), to despise, disdain (very rare): aliquem, Q. Pompeius ap. Prisc. p. 793 P.; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 23 .—Hence, , , in a pass. sense, despised : vir me habet despicatam, Plaut. Cas. 2, 2,…

dēspĭcus.opening: adj. id. , despised, disdained , Naev. ap. Non. 155, 26 (R ib. Fragm. Com. v. 25 ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 307 ).

dē-splendesco.opening: v. n. inch. , to cease to shine, to lose its brightness , Paul. Nol. Ep. 39 fin.

dēspŏlĭātĭo.opening: despolio , a robbing, despoiling , Tert. Res. Carn. 7 ; of a fine , Cod. Theod. 9, 17, 6 .

dēspŏlĭātor.opening: id. , a robber, plunderer , Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 18 ; Cod. Theod. 16, 2, 28 .

dē-spŏlĭo.opening: v. a. (also dep. : quos despoliatur, with depopulatur, Afran. ap. Non. 480, 13 ), to rob, plunder, despoil (rare, but good prose).—Constr., aliquem (aliquid) aliqua re : ne se armis despoliaret, * Caes. B. G. 2, 31, 4 :…

dē-spondĕo.opening: ( perf. despopondisse, Plaut. Trin. 3, 1, 2 ; plqpf. despoponderas, id. Truc. 4, 3, 51 ; with despondi, id. Aul. 2, 3, 4 : despondisse, id. Trin. 5, 2, 9 et saep.), v. a. , to promise to give, to promise, pledge . Lit.…

dēsponsātĭo.opening: desponso , a betrothing, betrothal , Tert. Verg. vel. 11; Vulg. Cant. 3, 11 .

dēsponsĭo.opening: despondeo , a despairing, desponding , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 18, 176 : animi, id. ib. 2, 32, 167 .

dē-sponso.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to betroth (post-Aug.), Suet. Caes. 1 ; id. Claud. 27 ; Aur. Vict. Orig. 13 : viro justo, Ambros. in Luc. 10, 21 ; Vulg. Matt. 1, 18 .

dēsponsor.opening: despondeo , one who betroths , acc. to Varr. L. L. 6, § 69 Müll.

dēspūmātĭo.opening: despumo , a skimming off , Tert. Carn. Chr. 19 .

dē-spūmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
dē-spūmo.opening: v. a. and n. (perh. not ante-Aug.). Act. To skim off, to skim . Prop.: undam aeni foliis, Verg. G. 1, 296 : carnem, Plin. 9, 38, 62, § 133 : mel Atticum, Col. 12, 38, 5 : aquam salsam, Pall. Febr. 25, 10 .— Transf. , to…

dē-spŭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to spit out, to spit . Prop., Liv. 5, 40 ; Naev. ap. Gell. 2, 19, 6 ; esp. as a religious observance for averting a disease, etc.; so, act. morbos, Plin. 28, 4, 7, § 35 : tenerum ignem, Claud. rapt. Pros.…

dēspūtum.opening: id. , spittle (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 20, 195 .

dē-squāmo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to scale off, to scale . Prop.: pisces, Plaut. Aul. 2, 9, 1 .— Transf. To peel off, to rub, scour, clean off : corticem, Plin. 23, 7, 70, § 134 : corpus (vitis), id. 17, 24, 37, § 227 :…

dē-sterno.opening: v. a. , to free from its covering (stratum), to unsaddle, ungird : camelos, Vulg. Gen. 24, 32 .

dē-sterto.opening: v. n. , to cease snoring; poet. , to cease dreaming , Pers. 6, 10 .

dēstĭco.opening: v. n. , to squeak , of the noise made by the shrew-mouse, Auct. Carm. Philom. 62.

dēstillātĭo.opening: destillo , a dripping down, distilling; in medic. lang., a rheum, catarrh, running , Cels. 1, 2 ; 4, 2 ; Plin. 20, 17, 71, § 183 ; 22, 25, 68, § 139 et saep.: jecoris, an abscess, Amm. 14, 11, 24 .

dē-stillo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
dē-stillo.opening: (or ), , v. a. and n. , to drip or trickle down, to distil (not in Cic.). Prop.: lentum destillat ab inguine virus, * Verg. G. 3, 281 ; cf.: ex athere, Sen. Q. N. 2, 12 : de capite in nares humor (from a cold), Cels. 4,…

dē-stĭmŭlo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to goad on, to stimulate (late Lat.), trop.: exercendi stili amore, Symm. Ep. 4, 26 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 27, 23 .

dēstĭna.opening: destino , a support, stay, prop (late Lat.): caeli, Arn. 2, p. 92 ; probably also Vitr. 5, 12, 3 .

dēstĭnātē.opening: adv., resolutely, obstinately , etc.; v. destino fin.

dēstĭnātĭo.opening: destino , a setting fast, establishing; a resolution, determination, purpose, design (perh. not ante-Aug.): depascitur segetes destinatione ante determinata in diem, Plin. 8, 25, 39, § 95 : porticum ex destinatione M.…

dēstĭnātor.opening: he who determines, designs : praevius, Ennod. 2, 6 .

dēstĭnātus.opening: , see the foll. art., P. a.

dē-stĭno.opening: v. a. obs. stanare; a particip. stem from root STA, v. sto; and cf.: dono, digno, etc., Corss. 2, 416 , to make fast, make firm, bind (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense—for syn. cf.: decerno, scisco, statuo, jubeo,…

dēstĭtor.opening: desisto , he who desists, withdraws from a thing , Julian. Epit. nov. c. 51, § 192.

dē-stĭtŭo.opening: v. a. statuo . To set down; to set, place anywhere (ante-class. and freq. in Liv.; elsewh. rare): destituit omnes servos ad mensam ante se, Caecil. ap. Non. 280, 3 : navem in alto ancoris, Naev. ib.: palum in foro, C.…

dēstĭtūtĭo.opening: destituo , a forsaking, deserting; deceiving, a failure, disappointment (very rare), Cin. Clu. 26, 71; id. Quint. 5, 20 ; Suet. Dom. 14 .— A putting away, abandoning : peccati, Vulg. Heb. 9, 26 .

dēstĭtūtor.opening: id. , one who forsakes, disappoints , or deceives , Tert. ad Nat. 2, 18 ; Auct. Priap. 83, 14 .

dē-strangŭlo.opening: v. a. , to choke, strangle; only trop., to destroy : rem publicam, Pore. Latro decl. in Cat. 24 .

dēstrictárĭum.opening: destringo , the place in the baths where the body was rubbed down , Corp. Inscr. Lat. 1251.

dēstrictīvus.opening: adj. destringo , dissolving, loosening , opp. constrictivus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 29 .

dē-stringo.opening: v. a. To strip off . Lit. (class.), of the leaves of plants: avenam, Cato R. R. 37, 5 : oleam, Col. 11, 2, 83 : bacam myrti, id. 12, 38, 7 : frondem, Quint. 12, 6, 2 : ramos, Luc. 4, 317 al. —Of rubbing the body in the…

dēstructĭbĭlis.opening: adj. destruo , destructible : omnia, Lact. de Ira D. fin. (al. destructilia).

dēstructĭlis.opening: adj. id. , destructible : aedes, Prud. στεφ . 10, 357; Lact. de Ira Dei, 23, § 28.

dēstructĭo.opening: id. , a pulling down, destruction . Prop.: murorum, Suet. Galb. 12 : munitionum, Vulg. 2 Cor. 10, 4 .— Trop. : sententiarum (opp. confirmatio), a refuting, refutation, Quint. 10, 5, 12 : appetentiae, disturbance, Cael.…

dēstructīvus.opening: adj. id. , destructive : adjutorium, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 84 .

dēstructor.opening: id. , one who pulls down, a destroyer : rerum, opp. aedificator, Tert. Apol. 46 : Trojae, Cass. Var. 14, 15; Hier. Ep. 112, 10 fin.

dē-strŭo.opening: v. a. , to pull or tear down any thing built (opp. construo— for syn. cf.: demolior, diruo). Prop. (rare but class.): navem, aedificium idem destruit facillime, qui construxit, Cic. de Sen. 20, 72 ; so, templum prope…

dē-sub.opening: praep. c. abl., below, beneath (late Lat.; cf. desuper): desub Alpibus, id est, desub ipsis Italiae faucibus, Flor. 2, 3, 2 : desub oculo, Veg. Vet. 2, 19 : desub rivo, Innocent. de Cas. liter. p. 226 ed. Goes.: desub…

dē-sŭbĭtō.opening: (by many written separately, de subito), adv., on a sudden, suddenly (except once in Cic., only ante-class.), Plaut. Bac. 1, 1, 46 ; id. Capt. prol. 62 ; id. Most. 2, 1, 63 ; id. Stich. 5, 4, 39 ; Lucil., Enn., Naev.,…

dē-sūbŭlo.opening: v. a. subula , to bore in deeply : perforare, Non. 99, 30 ; trop.: viam, Varr. ap. Non. 99, 32 .

dē-sūdasco.opening: v. n. , to sweat greatly.—Impers. pass. : ubi damnis desudascitur, Plaut. Bac. 1, 1, 33 .

dēsūdātĭo.opening: desudo , a violent sweating (late Lat.). Prop.: nimia corporis, Firm. Math. 3, 1.— Trop. , exertion, painstaking; coupled with cura, Mart. Cap. 6, § 577 .

dē-sūdo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dē-sūdo.opening: v. n. and a. (mostly post-Aug.). Neutr., to sweat greatly . Lit. , Cels. 6, 6, 29 ; Stat. Th. 3, 277 .— Trop. , to exert or fatigue one's self : in his (sc. exercitationibus ingenii) desudans atque elaborans, * Cic. de…

dēsŭē-făcĭo.opening: v. a. desueo , to disuse, disaccustom, bring out of use (very rare): catuli (a matre) minutatim desuefiunt, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 12 : multitudo desuefacta a contionibus, * Cic. Clu. 40, 110 ; cf. Tert. Pall. 4 .

dē-sŭesco.grammar: sŭēvi, sŭētum, 3 v. a. and n.
dē-sŭesco.opening: v. a. and n. (mostly poet. , or in post-Aug. prose; in Cic. and Caes. not at all; cf., however, desuefacio). Act., to disuse, to lay aside a custom or habit, to disaccustom, to put out of use : desuevi, ne quo ad cenam…

dēsŭētūdo.opening: desuesco , discontinuance of a practice or habit, disuse, desuetude : armorum, Liv. 1, 19 : bellandi, Fronto, princ. hist. p. 3, 7: desuetudine tardi, Ov. M. 14, 436 ; so absol. , id. Tr. 5, 7, 57 ; Dig. 1, 3, 32 al.

dē-sūgo.opening: , no perf. , ctum, 3, v. a. , to suck from any thing, to suck in (late Lat.), Pall. 1, 9, 4 ; 1, 37, 2 .

dē-sulco.opening: v. a. , to furrow through, to plough up , Avien. Perieg. 1137 .

dēsulto.opening: v. intens. n. [desilio], to leap down : mari, into the sea, Tert. Anim. 32 .

dēsultor.opening: id. , a leaper, vaulter , the technical designation of a sort of riders, who, in the circus-games, leaped from one horse to another without stopping. Prop., Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 15 ; Liv. 23, 29 ; 44, 9 ; Manil. 5, 85 .—…

dēsultōrĭus.opening: adj. desultor . Of or belonging to a vaulter (desultor): equi, Suet. Caes. 39 : levitas, Mart. Cap. 1, § 88 .— Subst. : , , , Cic. Mur. 27, 57 .— Desultory, superficial , Ap. M. 1, p. 102, 14.

dēsultrix.opening: adj. id. , inconstant (late Lat.): virtus, Tert. adv. Val. 38 .

dēsultūra.opening: desilio , a leaping or jumping down from a horse; comic, opp. insultura, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 9 .

dē-sum.opening: (ee in deest, deesse, deerit, etc., in the poets per synaeresin as one syll., Lucr. 1, 44 ; Cat. 64, 151 ; Verg. G. 2, 233 ; id. A. 7, 262 ; 10, 378 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 12, 24 ; Ov. M. 15, 354 et saep.; praes. subj. , desiet,…

dē-sūmo.opening: (msi), , v. a. Lit. , to take for one's self from a multitude or mass; hence, to pick out, choose, select (syn. deligere); to take upon one's self, undertake (rare, and perh. not ante-Aug.— syn. suscipere): sibi…

dē-sŭo.opening: v. a. , to fasten : cupam imbricibus ferreis, Cato R. R. 21, 3 .

dē-sŭper.opening: adv., from above, from overhead (repeatedly in the historians and poets; not in Cic.): qui in phalangas insilirent et desuper vulnerarent, Caes. B. G. 1, 52, 5 (a false reading in Caes. B. C. 1, 79, 2 ; but v. Lachm. ad…

dē-supernē.opening: adv., from above , Vitr. 10 . 16, 10 (dub. v. Lachm. ad Lucr. 6, 511 ).

dē-surgo.opening: v. n. , to rise from any place; to rise (extremely rare). Prop.: certa desurgere parte, * Lucr. 5, 703 : cenă, * Hor. S. 2, 2, 77 .— Transf. , to go to stool , Scrib. Comp. 140 and 142; Plin. 28, 14, 59, § 211 .

dēsurrectĭo.opening: desurgo , a going to stool , Scrib. Comp. 37 ; 142 .

dē-sursum.opening: adv. ( = desuper), from above , Tert. de Praescr. 46 al. : descendens, Vulg. Jacob, 3, 15 al.

dētectĭo.opening: detego , an uncovering; trop., revealing : creatoris, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 36 fin.

dētector.opening: id. , an uncoverer; trop., revealer (eccl. Lat.): creatoris, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 36 med. : conscientiae, id. adv. Val. 3 .

dē-tĕgo.opening: v. a. , to uncover, expose, lay bare (freq. in the Aug. per.). Lit. : ventus detexit villam, unroofed, Plaut. Rud. 1, 1, 3 : aedem Junonis ad partem dimidiam, Liv. 42, 3 : regiam Caci, Verg. A. 8, 241 : juga montium…

dē-tendo.opening: , no perf. , sum, 3, v. a. , to unstretch, relax a thing strained (very rare): tabernacula, to strike the tents , * Caes. B. C. 3, 85, 3 ; Liv. 41, 3, 1 .

dētentātor.opening: detento , one who holds or keeps back something, a detainer , Cod. 7, 39, 7; 11, 59, 2.

dētentĭo.opening: detineo , a keeping back, detaining , Dig. 4, 6, 15 ; 25, 1, 5 ; Vulg. Sirach, 24, 16 .

dētento.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. intens. a. [id.], to hold or keep back, to detain (late Lat.), Ven. Carm. 11, 21: servos, Cod. Th. 7, 13, 16 al.

dētentor.opening: id. , one who holds or keeps back, a detainer : possessionis alienae, Cod. 8, 4, 10.

dētentus.opening: detineo , a holding or keeping back , Tert. adv. Val. 32 .

dē-tĕpesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to cease to be lukewarm, to grow cool , Sid. Ep. 5, 17 .

dē-tergĕo.opening: (also post-class.: detergis, Claud. Cons. Mall. Theod. 191 : detergunt, id. ap. Eutr. 2, 375 : detergantur, Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 21 ; Ap. Mag. 59, p. 312, 26; Sen. Ep. 47, 4 , v. tergeo), v. a. To wipe off, wipe away…

dētĕrĭae.opening: lean , Paul. ex Fest. p. 73, 5 Müll.
