dētĕrĭor.opening: adj. comp. ( sup. deterrimus, a um) [from an obs. adj. deter , from de , down; hence, lower, inferior, worse], worse, poorer, meaner (freq. and class.—for syn. cf.: malus, injustus, improbus; pravus, nequam, corruptus,…

dētĕrĭōro.opening: v. a. deterior , to make worse, to deteriorate (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. de Statu an. 1, 3 al.

dētermĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. determino , that has an end, finite : materia, Tert. adv. Herm. 41 .

dētermĭnātĭo.opening: id. , a boundary, conclusion, end : extrema ora et d. mundi, Cic. N. D. 2, 40, 101 : exitus et determinatio orationis, id. Inv. 1, 52, 98 .

dētermĭnātor.opening: id. , one who prescribes or determines : disciplinae, Tert. Pudic. 11 .

dē-termĭno.opening: v. a. , to enclose within boundaries, to bound; to limit, prescribe, determine (rare but class.). Prop.: regiones, limites, confinia, Plaut. Poen. prol. 49 : augur regiones ab oriente ad occasum determinavit, Liv. 1, 18…

dē-tĕro.opening: v. a. , to rub away, to wear away, to wear out (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Caes.). Prop.: strataque jam volgi pedibus detrita viarum saxea, Lucr. 1, 315 : a catena collum detritum cani, Phaedr.…

dē-terrĕo.opening: v. a. To frighten from any thing; to deter, discourage from, prevent, hinder (class.).—Constr. (Aliquem) ab aliqua re : homines adolescentes a dicendi studio, Cic. de Or. 1, 25, 117 : sanos homines a scribendo, id.…

dētersĭō.opening: detergeo , a cleansing : mitissima, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 203 .

dētestābĭlis.opening: adj. detestor , execrable, abominable, detestable (good prose): omen, Cic. Phil. 11, 5, 11 ; cf.: exsecratus populo Romano, detestabilis, etc., id. ib. 2, 26 fin. : nihil esse tam detestabile tamque pestiferum quam…

dētestātĭo.opening: id. . In relig. lang. Execration, cursing, detestation , Liv. 10, 38 ; Hor. Epod. 5, 89 ; Sen. Ep. 117 med. ; Gell. 2, 6, 3 ; Vulg. Dan. 9, 11 . — A keeping off, averting , Plin. 15, 30, 40, § 135 : scelerum, Cic. Dom.…

dē-testātĭo.opening: 2. testis , the removal of the testes, castration , Ap. M. 7, p. 198, 7.

dētestātor.opening: detestor, no. I. , one who execrates, a curser (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 27 al.

dētesto.opening: v. a. act. collat. form of detestor , to execrate (very rare): detestabant, Amm. 26, 6, 17 ; v. also detestor fin.

dē-testor.opening: v. dep. a. In relig. lang. To curse while calling a deity to witness , i. e. to execrate, abominate (for syn. cf.: abominari, adversari, abhorrere, horrere, devovere, execrari): cum (te) viderunt, tamquam auspicium…

dē-texo.opening: v. a. , to weave off, to finish or make by weaving, to weave, plait (mostly poet. ). Lit. : inter decem annos unam togam, Titin. ap. Non. 406, 19 ; cf.: ad detexundam telam, Plaut. Ps. 1, 4, 7 : vestimentum, Dig. 32, 1,…

dē-tĭnĕo.opening: v. a. teneo , to hold off, keep back, detain . Lit. (class.): nos de nostro negotio, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 190 : aliquem ab aliquo incepto studioque, Sall. C. 4, 2 : aliquem apud villam, Plaut. Cist. 2, 1, 13 : so,…

dē-tondĕo.opening: (detotonderat, Varr. ap. Prisc. p. 868 P.; opp. detondit, Enn. ib.: detonderis, Cato R. R. 96, 1 ; Col. 7, 4, 7 ), v. a. , to shear off, cut off, to clip, shear . Prop.: oves, Cato R. R. 96, 1 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 28 ;…

dē-tŏno.opening: v. n. To thunder down, to thunder . Prop.: hic (sc. Juppiter) ubi detonuit, Ov. Tr. 2, 35 .— Trop. , to thunder forth, express in thundertones, to storm (freq. in Florus): captis superioribus jugis in subjectos…

dētonsĭo.opening: detondeo , a shearing off : capitis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 3 .

dētonso.opening: v. intens. a. [detondeo], to shear off : capillum, Fab. Pict. ap. Gell. 10, 15, 11 .

dē-torno.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to turn off with a lathe, to turn (very rare). Prop.: anulos, Plin. 13, 9, 18, § 62 .— Trop. : sententiam, Gell. 9, 8, 4 .

dē-torquĕo.opening: (detorsum, v. infra no. 1. A. 2.), , v. a. and n. Act., to turn or bend aside, to turn off, turn away (class.). In gen. Lit. : ponticulum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 59 : cornua (antennarum), Verg. A. 5, 832 : habenas, id. ib.…

dē-torrĕo.opening: v. a. , to scorch, to burn (late Lat.): me flamma, Sid. Ep. 1, 7 .

dētractĭo.opening: detraho , a drawing off, taking away, withdrawal . In gen. (good prose): alieni, opp. appetitio, Cic. Off. 3, 6, 30 : doloris, id. ib. 3, 33, 118 : loci, departure from, id. Att. 12, 35 : sanguinis, Cels. 4, 4 ; Quint.…

dētractor.opening: detraho, no. II. B. , a disparager, detractor : sui, Tac. A. 11, 11 fin. (for which, detrectator laudum suarum, Liv. 34, 15 fin. ): abominatio hominum detractor, Vulg. Prov. 24, 9 al.

dētractōrius.opening: adj. detractor , disparaging, slanderous.—Plur. as subst. : inflammat linguae mobilitas ... ad detractoria, (Pseud.) August. ad Frat. Erem. 3 .

dētractus.opening: detraho , a taking away, rejection : syllabae (opp. adjectio), Sen. Suas. 7 fin.

dē-trăho.opening: ( inf. perf. sync. detraxe, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 15 ), v. a. , to draw or take off, draw away, draw or take down; to pull down; to take away, remove, withdraw (class. and very freq.). Lit. In gen. With acc. and de or ex…

dētrectātĭo.opening: ( ), , detrecto , a declining, refusing (very rare, and perh. not ante-Aug.): militiae, Liv. 3, 69 : heredis, Plin. 18, 6, 7, § 37 : fidei, Tert. Pat. 3 : sine detrectatione, Liv. 7, 28 .

dētrectātor.opening: ( ), , id. . * One who declines or refuses : ministerii, Petr. 117, 11 .— A diminisher, disparager : laudum suarum, Liv. 34, 15, 9 : honorum, Aus. Idyll. 2, 51 .

dē-trecto.opening: (in the best MSS. also ), , v. a. Orig., to decline, refuse, reject any thing; and hence, to decline, refuse to do any thing (not in Cic.—for syn. cf.: nego, infitias eo, infitior, diffiteor, denego, recuso, abnuo,…

dētrīmentōsus.opening: adj. detrimentum , hurtful, detrimental : ab hoste discedere detrimentosum esse existimabat, Caes. B. G. 7, 33 .

dētrīmentum.opening: detero , a rubbing off . * Lit. : limae tenuantis, Ap. M. 6, p. 175, 25.— Transf. , loss, damage, detriment . In gen. (class.; cf. for syn.: damnum, jactura, incommodum, dispendium): emolumenta et detrimenta (quae…

dētrītus.opening: detero , a rubbing away : detrimentum a detritu, Varr. L. L. 5, 36, § 176 Müll.

dē-trĭumpho.opening: v. a. , to triumph over, to conquer (late Lat.): daemones, Tert. Apol. 27 al.

dē-trūdo.opening: v. a. , to thrust, drive , or force away; to thrust down, push down (class.). Lit. In gen.: neminem statui detrusum, qui non adhibita vi manu demotus et actus praeceps intellegatur, Cic. Caecin. 17, 49 : qui advorsum…

dētruncātĭo.opening: detrunco , a lopping off (rare): ramorum, Plin. 24, 9, 37, § 57 ; so absol. , id. 17, 24, 37, § 237 .

dē-trunco.opening: v. a. , to lop or cut off (rare, and perh. not ante-Aug.). Prop.: arbores, Liv. 21, 37 : superiorem partem, Col. 5, 6, 13 : alam regi apium, Plin. 11, 17, 17, § 54 : caput, Ov. M. 8, 770 al. — Transf. to the body from…

dētrūsĭo.opening: detrudo , a thrusting down (late Lat.): in lacum, Hier. Isai. 8, 24, 22 al.

dē-tŭmesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to cease swelling, to settle down, subside (postAug. and very rare): stagna lacusque sonori detumuere, Stat. Th. 3, 259 : animi maris, id. ib. 5, 468 .— Trop. : odia, Petr. 109, 5 : colla superbarum…

dē-tundo.opening: , no perf. , sum, 3, v. a. , to beat, bruise (very rare; perh. only in the foll. passages): guberna, Lucil. ap. Non. 490, 32 (dub. Gerl. detondete): digitos pedum ad lapides, Ap. M. 2, p. 128, 39.

dē-turbo.opening: v. a. , to drive, thrust , or cast down, to throw or beat down , sc. in a violent, tumultuous manner (freq. and class.; orig. perh. peculiar to milit. lang.). Lit. : aliquem de pugnaculis, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 63 : nostros…

dē-turpo.opening: v. a. , to disfigure (postAug. and very rare): comatos occipitio raso, Suet. Calig. 35 : poma rugis. Plin. 15, 16, 18, § 59 : caput suum, Vulg. 1 Cor. 11, 4 sq.

Deucălĭon.opening: Δευκαλίων , son of Prometheus, king of Phthia, in Thessaly, and husband of Pyrrha . He is famous on account of the deluge sent in his days by Jupiter, and as the progenitor of a new race of men, Ov. M. 1, 318 sq. ; Hyg.…

dĕ-unx.opening: uncia , eleven twelfths , Varr. L. L. 5, § 172 Müll.: jugeri, Col. 5, 1, 12 : heres ex deunce, Cic. Caecin. 6 fin. : avidi deunces, i. e. eleven per cent., Pers. 5, 150 : potare deunces, i. e. eleven measures (cyathos),…

dĕ-ūro.opening: v. a. , to burn up, consume (freq. in the historians; elsewh. rare; not in Cic.). Prop.: pluteos turrium, * Caes. B. G. 7, 25 : vicum, Liv. 10, 4 ; cf.: agros vicosque (with depopulari), id. 39, 2 : partem Circi, Tac.…

dĕus.opening: ( voc. sing. deus, Vulg. Psa. 22, 3 al. ; but, dee, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 29 ; Prud. Hamart. 931 ; cf. Prob. Inst. Art. 532, p. 340 . The nom. plur. is di and dei; dii is freq. in MSS., but prob. indicates only the length…

deutĕrĭus.opening: adj. , = δευτέριος , secondary (pure Lat. secundarius): vina ( = lora), Plin. 14, 10, 12, § 86 .

deutĕrŏnŏmĭum.opening: , = δευτερονόμιον . A copy of the law , Vulg. Deut. 17, 18 ; id. Josue, 8, 32.— The fifth book of Moses, Deuteronomy , Lact. 4, 17, 6 al.

dĕ-ūtor.opening: v. dep. , to use wrongfully, abuse; with abl. : victo, Nep. Eum. 11, 3 .

dē-văgor.opening: v. dep. n. , to wander, to stray from (post-class.): a venditionibus, Cod. Th. 1, 10, 5.— Trop. , to deviate, digress : a venditionibus ulterius, Justin. de Conc. Dig. 1.

dēvastātor.opening: he who devastates , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 6, 45 .

dē-vasto.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to lay waste, devastate (rare, and perh. not anteAug.): fines, Liv. 4, 59 : Marsos, id. 22, 9 : agmina ferro, Ov. M. 13, 255 .— Trop. : fortitudinem, Vulg. Isa. 23, 14 : ecclesiam, id. Act.…

dē-vecto.opening: v. intens. a. , to carry away : ligatum, Sedul. 5, 345 .

dē-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to carry down, to carry, convey, take away . Prop. (class.; most freq. in the histt.): has (carinas) carris junctis devehit noctu milia passuum a castris XXII., Caes. B. C. 1, 54, 3 : legionem equis, id. B. G.…

dē-vello.opening: , ( perf. devolsit, Cat. 63, 5 ), 3, v. a. , to pluck down, to pull or tear off (very rare; not in Cic. and Caes.): pennas, Plaut, Poen. 4, 2, 50; cf.: plumam anseribus, Fronto Ep. ad Verr. 1 fin. : plantas de matrum…

dē-vēlo.opening: v. a. , to unveil, uncover : ora sorori, Ov. M. 6, 604 .

dē-vĕnĕror.opening: v. dep. a. , to reverence, worship (very rare). Prop.: deos prece, Ov. H. 2, 18 .— Transf. : somnia ter sanctā deveneranda molā, i. e. to avert by prayers, Tib. 1, 5, 14 .

dē-vĕnĭo.opening: v. n. ; orig., to come from somewhere; hence, with predominant reference to the term. ad quem (cf. de, no. II. B.), to go to, arrive at, reach (class.). Lit. : quomodo ad hunc devenerim In servitutem ab eo, etc., Plaut.…

dē-vĕnusto.opening: v. a. , to disfigure, deform (late Lat.): pulchritudinis insignia, Gell. 12, 1, 8 al.

dē-verbĕro.opening: v. a. , to thrash or cudgel soundly (very rare): homines deverberasse usque ad necem, Ter. Ph. 2, 2, 13 : servum, Lact. 2, 7, 20 (al. diverb.).

dēvergentĭa.opening: devergo , an inclining downwards, a sloping : d. et convexiones mundi, Gell. 14, 1, 8 .

dē-vergo.opening: v. n. , to incline downwards, to sink , Ap. de Deo Socr. p. 46; Tert. Exhort. Cast. 2 .

Dēverra.opening: deverro , the goddess of sweeping, that presided over the threshold of a house where a woman lay in child-bed, to protect her against Sylvanus , acc. to Varr. ap. Aug. Civ. D. 6, 9 ; cf. Voss. ad Verg. Ecl. 10, 24 .

dē-verro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to sweep away, sweep out (very rare): devorare omnia ac deverrere, Lucil. ap. Non. 420, 7 ; Varr. ap. Aug. Civ. D. 6, 9 ; Col. 7, 4, 5 .

dēversĭto.opening: v. intens. n. [deverto], to put up at an inn; trop.: ad verborum venustates, to dwell upon, Gell. 17, 20, 6 .

dēversĭtor.opening: deversor , one who puts up at an inn, a guest , Petr. 79, 6 , and 95, 1.

dē-versor.opening: deverto , one who lodges anywhere, an inmate, guest : caupo cum quibusdam deversoribus illum consequitur, Cic. Inv. 2, 4, 15 (MSS. diversoribus, which Kayser restores).

dēversōrĭŏlum.opening: dim. deversorium , a small lodging-place , Cic. Fam. 12, 20 ; Att. 14, 8 ( Suet. Caes. 72 dub.).

dēversōrĭus.opening: ( , Auct. Her. 4, 51, 64 ; Sen. Ep. 108, 6 ; Curt. 7, 2, 22 ), adj. 2. deversor , belonging to an inn or lodging-place, fit to lodge in : taberna, a lodging-place, lodging, inn, Plaut. Men. 2, 3, 81 ; id. Truc. 3, 2, 29…

dēversus.opening: , i. e. deorsum versus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 71, 1 Müll.

dēvertĭcŭlum.opening: (many MSS. and some edd. , old form ), , deverto . A by-road, by-path, side-way . Prop.: quae deverticula flexionesque quaesivisti? Cic. Pis. 22, 53 ; Ter. Eun. 4, 2, 7 ; Curt. 3, 13, 9 ; Suet. Ner. 48 ; Plin. 31, 3,…

dē-verto.grammar: ti, sum 3 v. a. and n.
dē-verto.opening: or , (in MSS. often confounded with diverto), , v. a. and n. Act. To turn away, turn aside any thing: comites suo hortatu, Luc. 6, 317 : acies, id. 2, 470 : ventura fata suo cursu, id. 6, 591 ; cf. Aur. Vict. Caes. 38…

dē-vescor.opening: v. dep. a. , to eat up, devour , poet. : animas, Stat. Th. 1, 604 .

dē-vestĭo.opening: v. a. , to undress (a word used by Ap.): se, Ap. M. 3, p. 138, 24 al.

dēvestīvus.opening: adj., undressed : genitura, Tert. adv. Val. 14 .

dēvexĭtas.opening: devexus , a declivity, a sloping : loci, Plin. Ep. 8, 8, 3 : litoris, id. 2, 65, 65, § 165 .

dēvexus.opening: adj. deveho , of places, inclining downwards, sloping, shelving, steep (class.—for syn. v. declivis). Lit. : lucus Vestae, qui a Palatii radice in novam viam devexus est, Cic. Div. 1, 45 ; cf. Liv. 44, 35 : mundus in…

dēvĭātor.opening: devio , one who leaves the way, a forsaker : puritatis (Pseud.), August. ad Frat. Erem. 29 .

dēvictĭo.opening: devinco , a conquering : mortis, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 108 .

dē-vĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to lose one's vigor , Tert. Anim, 27 .

dē-vincĭo.opening: ( perf. sync. devinxti, Plaut. As. 5, 1, 21 ), v. a. , to bind fast, tie up (class.; esp. freq. in trop. signif.). Lit. : servum, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 92 ; cf. leonem, Plin. 8, 16, 21, § 54 : Dircam ad taurum, Plaut. Ps.…

dē-vinco.opening: v. a. , to conquer completely, overcome, subdue . Prop. (class.; for syn. cf.: vinco, supero, fundo, fugo, profligo, subigo, subicio, domo): Galliam Germaniamque, Caes. B. C. 3, 87 ; id. B. G. 7, 34 ; Hirt. ib. 8, 46 :…

dēvinctĭo.opening: devincio , a binding, ensnaring : magicae, enchantments, Tert. Spect. 2 .

dēvinctus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from devincio.

dē-vĭo.opening: v. n. , to turn from the straight road, to go aside, to deviate (late Lat.; for de via declinare or devertere). Prop., Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 22 ; Aug. Doctr. Christ. 3, 36 fin. — Trop. , Macr. S. 5, 15 ; Symm. Ep. 9, 121…

dē-virgĭno.opening: v. a. , to deprive of virginity, to deflour . Prop., Petr. 25, 1 ; Dig. 1, 18, 21 : juvenculam, Vulg. Sirach, 20, 2 .— Transf. in the pass. , of young persons, to quit the period of youth , Varr. ap. Non. 458, 26 .

dēvītātĭo.opening: devito , an avoiding : legionum, Cic. Att. 16, 2, 4 .

dē-vīto.opening: v. a. , to avoid, go out of the way of, shun (rare but class.): illos fluctus, Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 79 ; cf.: procellam temporis, Cic. Verr. 1, 3, 8 : malum, Ter. And. 3, 5, 5 : letum, Lucr. 3, 1092 : dolorem, Cic. Tusc.…

dē-vĭus.opening: adj. via , lying off the high-road; out of the way, devious (class.; for syn. cf.: avius, invius). Lit. : iter, a by-way, Cic. Att. 4, 3, 4 ; 14, 10, 1 (cf. avius); Suet. Galb. 20 : oppidum, Cic. Pis. 36 fin. : saltus,…

dē-vŏco.opening: v. a. , to call off, call away; also to call down .—With abl. of the place whence after de, ab, ex , rarely without a prep. ; and with reference to the term. ad quem (cf. de, no. II. B.), to call, to fetch by calling to…

dē-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly down or away (very rare). Lit. To fly down : devolant angues jubati deorsum in impluvium, Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 56 : Iris per caelum, Verg. A. 4, 702 : sibi de caelo devolaturam in sinum victoriam, Liv. 7, 12,…

dē-volvo.opening: v. a. , to roll or tumble down (class.). Lit. : saxa in musculum, Caes. B. C. 2, 11, 1 , and 2; cf. saxa (amnis), Quint. 12, 10, 61 : auratas trabes, Verg. A. 2, 449 : tonitrua, i. e. to imitate it (by rolling down…

dē-vŏmo.opening: v. a. , to vomit forth , Caecil. ap. Gell. 2, 23, 13 .

dēvŏrābĭlis.opening: adj. devoro , that can be devoured : tegmen, Alcim. Ep. 77 .

dēvŏrātĭo.opening: id. , a devouring : carnis, Tert. Res. carn. 54.—With gen. subject. : piscis, Vulg. Tobiae, 12, 3 ; id. Ezech. 34, 5 .

dēvŏrātor.opening: id. , a devourer (late Lat.), Tert. Res. carn. 32; Vulg. Sap. 12, 5 ; id. Luc. 7, 35 .

dēvŏrātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , devouring : crimina devoratoria salutis, destructive to, Tert. Idol. 1 .—As subst. : , , , the devouring maw : mortis, Ambros. Ep. 4, 5 fin.

dēvŏrātrix.opening: devorator , she that devours : puerorum, Porphyr. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 13, 10 : hominum, Vulg. Ezech. 36, 13 .

dē-vŏro.opening: v. a. , to swallow, swallow down, gulp down, devour (class.; esp. freq. in transf. signif.—for syn. cf.: edo, comedo, vescor, pascor, mando). Lit. , of the physical act: id quod devoratur, Cic. N. D. 2, 54, 135 : ovum…

dēvortĭum.opening: deverto , a by-way, by-road : itinerum, Tac. Agr. 19, 5 Halm (Ritter, divortia).

dēvōtāmentum.opening: devoveo , a cursing, anathema , Tert. adv. Gnost. 2 .

dēvōtātio.opening: id. , a making of vows, consecration , Vulg. 3 Reg. 8, 38 ; August. 4 Quaest. in Hept. 40.

dēvōtē.opening: adv., devotedly, faithfully , v. devoveo, P. a. fin.

dēvōtĭo.opening: devoveo . A devoting, consecrating . Prop.: Deciorum devotiones, the devoting of themselves, Cic. N. D. 3, 6, 15 ; cf. vitae, id. Rab. Post. 1 fin. ; capitis, id. Dom. 57 ; a vow , Vulg. Act. 23, 1 . — Transf. , fealty,…

dē-vōto.opening: v. intens. a. [id.]. To dedicate, devote (rare): et me dicabo atque animam devotabo hostibus, Att. ap. Non. 98, 13 (but Cic. Par. 1, 2, 12 , read devota vita); and, To bewitch, enchant : sortes, Plaut. Cas. 2, 6, 36 :…

dēvōtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from devoveo.

dē-vŏvĕo.opening: v. a. To vow, devote (usually to a deity). Prop. (class.): Marti ea, quae bello ceperint, Caes. B. G. 6, 17, 3 ; so, Dianae pulcherrimum, Cic. Off. 3, 25, 95 : gnatam pro muta agna, Hor. S. 2, 3, 219 et saep.; esp.…

Dexămĕnus.opening: the name of a centaur; i. q. Eurytion, Ov. Ib. 406 .

Dexippus.opening: Δέξιππος , a Greek proper name , Cic. Fam. 14, 3, 3 .

Dexĭus.opening: a Roman proper name , Cic. Fam. 7, 23, 4 .

Dexo.opening: Δεξων , a Greek proper name , Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 42 al.

dextans.opening: contr. from de and sextans: as dempto sextante, Varr. L. L. 5, § 172 Müll. , ten twelfths of any thing (mostly post-Aug.; Cic. writes instead: pars dimidia et tertia, Fam. 13, 29, 4; cf.: remissis senio et trientibus,…

dextella.opening: dim. dextra , a little right hand : Quintus filius illius, ut scribis, est dextella, Cic. Att. 14, 20, 5 .

dexter.opening: , and more freq. tra, trum ( dat. plur. fem. : dextrabus manibus, Liv. Andron. ap. Non. 493, 20 .— Comp. dextĕrĭor; sup. dextĭmus), adj. dex-ter, root dek-, Gr. δέκομαι, whence δάκτυλος, digitus; cf. Germ. Finger, from…

dextĕra.opening: or , , (as in most langg.; cf. Gr. δεξιά , Germ. die Rechte, etc.; sc. manus), the right hand (freq. a sign of greeting, of fidelity; a symbol of strength, courage, etc.). Prop.: cedo sis dexteram, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2,…

dextrā.opening: praep. [orig. dextrā, abl. of preceding], on the right of (post-Aug.); with acc. : dextra sinistraque januam, Gell. 16, 5, 3 : dextra viam stratam, Liv. 8, 15, 8 : dextra ac sinistra aquilonem, Vitr. 1, 6, 10 ; id. 6,…

dextĕre.opening: and , adv., dexterously, skilfully : dextre obeundo officia, Liv. 1, 34 fin.—Comp. : nemo dexterius fortunā est usus, Hor. S. 1, 9, 45 .

dextĕrĭtas.opening: dexter, II. . Dexterity, aptness, readiness in doing good offices (rare and not ante-Aug.): tanta inerat comitas Scipioni atque ad omnia naturalis ingenii dexteritas, Liv. 28, 18, 6 ; 37, 7, 15 ; Gell. 13, 16, 1 al. —*…

dextrāle.opening: id. , a bracelet (late Lat.), Cypr. Habit. Verg. med. ; Vulg. Exod. 35, 22 al.

dextrālĭŏlum.opening: dim. dextrale , a little bracelet , Vulg. Judith, 10, 3 .

dextrātĭo.opening: dexter , a movement towards the right side (a religious ceremonial), Sol. 45, 15 .

dextrātus.opening: adj. id. , lying to the right (late Lat.): ager, pars, Auct. de Limit. p. 298 Goes.

dextrŏchĕrĭum.opening: vox hibrida, from dexter and χείρ , a bracelet (late Lat.), Capitol. Max. 6, 8 ; 27, 8 : gemmatum, Schol. Juv. 9, 50 .

dextrorsum.opening: or , or uncontracted (or ), adv. dexter-versus , towards the right side, to the right , Att. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 22, 44 : ille sinistrorsum hic dextrorsum abit, Hor. S. 2, 3, 50 : dextrorsus pergere, Liv. 6, 31, 5 :…

Dīa.opening: Δῖα . The old name of the island of Naxos, Ov. M. 3, 690 ; 8, 174 . — A city in the Chersonesus Taurica, Plin. 4, 12, 26, § 86 .— An island near Crete , now Standia , id. 4, 12, 20, § 61 .— A woman's name . The mother…

dĭăartўmătōn.opening: , = διὰ ἀρτυμάτων , a kind of salve , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 116 .

dĭăbā^thrārĭus.opening: diabathrum , the maker of a sort of slipper, a shoemaker , Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 39 .

dĭăbā^thrum.opening: , = διάβαθρον , a sort of slipper , Naev. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 53 Müll. (v. 60 Rib.); cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 74, 9 Müll.

dĭăbētes.opening: , = διαβήτης , a siphon; called also sipho, Col. 3, 10, 2 .

Dĭā^blintes.opening: a people in Gallia Lugdunensis, near the present Mayenne, in the Department de la Sarthe , Caes. B. G. 3, 9 fin. ; called also , Plin. 4, 18, 32, § 107 .

dĭăbŏle.opening: , = διαβολή , a rhet. t. t., false accusation, slander (pure Lat. criminatio), Jul. Rufin. de Fig. p. 209 Ruhnk.

dĭăbŏlĭcus.opening: adj. , = διαβολικός , devilish, diabolical , Paul. Nol. 29, 11 : viri, Vulg. 3 Reg. 21, 13 .

dĭăbŏlus.opening: , = διάβολος , a devil , Tert. Anim. 35 ; Vulg. 3 Reg. 21, 13 .—Esp., the devil , Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 10 ; Vulg. 1 Johan. 3, 8 al. et saep. With long a , in Paul. Nol. 26, 528 .

dĭăcĕcaumĕne.opening: , = διακεκαυμένη , sc. γῆ , the torrid zone , Sol. 32, 37 ; cf. Hygin. Astr. 1, 8.

dĭăchĕton.opening: a small plant in Rhodes; called also crysisceptrum, Plin. 24, 13, 69, § 112 (Jan. diaxylon).

dĭăchȳlōn.opening: = διὰ χυλῶν , a sort of medicine , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 18 ; 2, 29 al.

dĭăchўton.opening: (sc. vinum), = διαχυτόν , a sort of sweet wine , Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 84 .

dĭăcōdīōn.opening: , = διὰ κωδειῶν , a sort of medicine prepared from poppy-juice , Plin. 20, 18, 76, § 200 ; 20, 19, 79, § 207 sq.; Isid. Or. 4, 9, 9 al.

dĭācŏnātus.opening: (and , , , Sever. Sulp. vita Mart. 5 al. ) [diaconus], the office of deacon, deaconship , Hier. Ep. 22, 12 al.

dĭācŏnĭcus.opening: adj. diaconus , belonging to a deaconship : loca, Cod. Th. 16, 5, 30.— Subst. : , , , a place for storing the vessets of the altar , Cod. Theod. 16, 5, 10 .

dĭācŏnus.opening: (collat. form in plur. : diacones, Vulg. Tim. 3, 8 ; 12 : diaconibus, id. Phil. 1, 1 ), , = διάκονος , in eccl. Lat., a servant or minister of the church, a deacon , Tert. Praescr. 3 ; Cod. Just. 1, 3, 6 et saep. — , ,…

dĭăcŏpe.opening: , = διακοπή , gram. t. t., a tmesis , Charis. p. 246 P.

dĭăcŏpus.opening: , = διάκοπος , an opening or sluice in a dam for leading off the water, Dig. 47, 11, 10 .

dĭădēma.opening: (diadēma, , , Pompon. ap. Prisc. p. 679 P. [Com. v. 163 Rib.]; Ap. M. 10, p. 253, 10), = διάδημα , a royal head-dress, a diadem (for syn. cf.: infula, vitta, redimiculum), Cic. Phil. 2, 34, 85 ; 3, 5, 12 ; Quint. 9, 3,…

dĭădēmālis.opening: adj. diadema , pertaining to or wearing a diadem : frons, Diacont. 2, 31.

dĭădēmātus.opening: adj. id. , adorned with a diadem : Apollo, Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 79 . —Hence,

Dĭădēmātus.opening: a Roman surname , Cic. Post. Red. ad Quir. 3, 6 .

dĭădŏchos.opening: , = διάδοχος , a jewel resembling the beryl , Plin. 37, 10, 57, § 157 .

dĭădŏta.opening: , = διαδότης a distributor (pure Lat.: divisor, diribitor), Cod. Th. 7, 4, 28.

dĭădūmĕnus.opening: adj. , = διαδούμενος , wearing a diadem : juvenis, Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 55 : statua, Sen. Ep. 65, 5 .— Antoninus Diadumenus, a Roman emperor, son and successor of Macrinus; cf. Lampr. Anton. Diadum. 4 .

dĭaerĕsis.opening: , = διαίρεσις . In gram., the dividing of one syllable into two , as aquaï for aquae, Serv. ad Verg. A. 7, 464 .— In rhet., a figure, pure Lat. distributio, distribution , Jul. Rufin. 21, p. 242 .

dĭaeta.opening: ( or , Lampr. Heliog. 29 fin. ; 30 ; and in many MSS. in the foll. passages; cf. the letter D), , , = δίαιτα . A mode of living prescribed by a physician, diet : sola diaeta curari, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 12, 146 .— Trop.…

dĭaetarchus.opening: , = διαίταρχος , one who has the care of apartments, a valetde-chambre , Inscr. Orell. 2912 .—Called also † , , , ib. 2913 . And v. the foll. art.

dĭaetārĭus.opening: diaeta, no. II. , a valet-de-chambre , Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 42 , ib. 4, 9, 1 .

dĭaetēta.opening: , = διαιτητής , an umpire (pure Lat. arbiter), Cod. 2, 13, 27 al.

dĭaetētĭcus.opening: adj. , = διαιτητικός , belonging to diet : libri, curatio, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 12, 145 .— Subst. , , , , physicians who cure by diet (opp. chirurgi), Scrib. Comp. 200 (cf. Cic. Att. 4, 3, 3 ).

dĭaglaucĭum.opening: or , , , a salve made from the herb glaucium, Plin. 27, 10, 59, § 83 ; Scrib. Comp. 22 .

dĭăgōnālis.opening: adj. [from διαγώνιος and the Lat. ending alis), diagonal : linea, Vitr. 9, 1 ; 6, 5 .—And subst. , , , : diagonii linea, id. 6, 4 .

Dĭăgondas.opening: , = Διαγόνδας , a Theban lawgiver , Cic. Leg. 2, 15, 37 .

dĭăgōnĭŏs.opening: , = διαγώνιος , adj., diagonal : linea, Vitr. 6, 3, 3 : structura, id. 6, 8, 7 al.

Dĭăgŏras.opening: Διαγόρας . An atheistic philosopher and poet of Melos, a contemporary of Pindar , Cic. N. D. 1, 1 ; 1, 23 ; 42 ; 3, 37; Val. Max. 1, 2 .— One of the most famous athletes in the Olympic games, a native of Rhodes , Cic.…

dĭagramma.opening: , = διάγραμμα , in music, the scale, gamut , Vitr. 5, 4 .

dĭagrydĭum.opening: , = διαγρύδιον , the juice of the plant scammonea, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 12 al.

dĭăĭtĕon.opening: = διὰ ἰτεῶν , a salve made of the juice of the willow , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13 .

dĭălectĭca.opening: , and , , and , , v. dialecticus, no. II.

dĭălectĭcē.opening: adv., dialectically , v. the foll. no. I.

dĭălectĭcus.opening: adj. , = διαλεκτικός , belonging to disputation, dialectical . Adj. : captiones, Cic. Fin. 2, 6, 17 : disputationes, Quint. 5, 14, 27 : pars, id. 12, 2, 13 et saep.: sapientiae professor, Plin. 7, 53, 54, § 180 .— Adv.…

dĭălectos.opening: or , , , = διάλεκτος , a dialect , Suet. Tib. 56 .

dĭălĕpĭdos.opening: = διὰ λεπίδος , an unguent made with the scales that fly from metal in hammering , Marc. Emp. 9 ; Inscr. Orell. 4233 al.

dĭăleucos.opening: adj. , = διάλευκος , intermixed with white, whitish : crocum, Plin. 21, 6, 17, § 33 .

dĭălĭbănum.opening: , = διὰ λιβάνων or λιβάνου , a salve made with frankincense , Marc. Emp. 9 .

dĭālĭon.opening: , = διάλιον or διήλιον , the plant heliotropium, Ap. Herb. 49.

Dĭālis.opening: adj. from Dis, in Diespiter = Juppiter . Of or belonging to Jupiter : flamen, the priest of Jove (instituted by Numa, and the most distinguished of the flamines), Varr. L. L. 5, § 84 ; 6, § 16 Müll.; Fabius Pictor and…

dĭălŏgismos.opening: , = διαλογισμός , rhet. t. t., a consideration , Jul. Rufin. de Fig. 20, p. 211 sq.

dĭălŏgista.opening: , = διαλογιστής , an able disputant , Vulc. Gallic. Av id. Cass. 3 .

dĭălŏgus.opening: , = διάλογος , a (philosophical) conversation, a dialogue (for syn. cf.: colloquium, contio, contentio, oratio), Cic. Or. 44 fin. ; id. Brut. 60 fin. ; Quint. 5, 14, 27 ; 6, 3, 44 al. (written as Greek, Cic. Att. 5, 5 ;…

dĭălutense.opening: a sort of purple mussel found half in the mud [lutum; acc. to others, = διάλυτος , dissolutus], Plin. 9, 37, 6, § 131 Sillig.

dĭălўsis.opening: , = διάλυσις , rhet. t. t., a separation , Rutil. Lup. 1, 15, p. 52 .

dĭălўton.opening: , = διάλυτον , rhet. t. t., i. q. dialysis, Jul. Rufin. de Fig. 18, p. 240 .

dĭămastīgōsis.opening: , = διαμαστίγωσις , a severe scourging , Tert. ad Mart. 4 .

dĭămĕlĭlōtōn.opening: = διὰ μελιλώτων , a salve made of meliloton , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 3 al.

dĭămĕlĭtōn.opening: = διὰ μελίτων , a salve made of honey , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

dĭămē^tros.opening: , = διάμετρος , a diameter , Col. 5, 2, 7 ; Vitr. 10, 14 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 20 sq. al.— Adj., central : radiatio, Firm. Math. 4, 1 med.

dĭămetrum.opening: (that is wanting to the measure), the wantage, loss , Cod. Theod. 13, 5, 38 .

dĭămĭsўos.opening: = διὰ μίσυος , a salve made of misy (vitriolic earth), Marc. Emp. 9 .

dĭămŏrōn.opening: , = διὰ μόρων , a medicament composed of the juice of black mulberries and honey , Pall. Sept. 16 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 3, 18 .

Dĭāna.opening: (in inscrr. also, DEANA, Orell. 1453; 1462; 1546. Also written , Varr. R. R. 1, 37, 3 ; cf. Nigid. ap. Macr. S. 1, 9 . The i measured long, Cinna ap. Suet. Gramm. 11 ; Verg. A. 1, 499 ; Hor. C. 1, 21, 1 ; cf. Diom. p.…

dĭănœa.opening: , = διάνοια , rhet. t. t., by which a fact is exhibited instead of a conception , Jul. Rufin. de Fig. 18, p. 210 .

dĭănŏme.opening: , = διανομή , distribution of money (in canvassing for office), Plin. Ep. 10, 117 fin. ; ib. 118 .

dĭăpantōn.opening: = διὰ πάντων , universally : CORONATO, Inscr. Orell. 2627 sq.

dĭăpasma.opening: , = διάπασμα , a scented powder for sprinkling on any thing , Plin. 13, 2, 3, § 19 ; 21, 19, 73, § 125 ; Mart. 1, 88, 5 .

dĭăpāsōn.opening: = διὰ πασῶν (sc. χορδῶν ), in music, the whole octave , Vitr. 5, 4, 8 ; Plaut. 2, 22, 20 ; Mart. Cap. 9, § 944 ; so too, = διὰ πέντε , a fifth , Mart. Cap. 9, § 934 al. ; = διατεσσάρων , a fourth , id. 2, § 107 ; Vitr.…

dĭăpentĕ.opening: = διὰ πέντε , V. diapason.— A medicine made of five ingredients , Veg. 2, 36, 1 .

dĭăphŏra.opening: , = διαφορά , rhet. t. t., distinction (repetition of the same word in different meanings), Rutil. Lup. 12, p. 43 .

dĭăphŏrēsis.opening: , = διαφόρησις , in the later medic. lang., A sweat , Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 14.— Meton. , an exhaustion , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 15 .

dĭăphŏrētĭcus.opening: adj. , = διαφορητικός , promoting perspiration, sudorific, diaphoretic : solutio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 17 .

dĭaphragma.opening: , = διάφραγμα , the diaphragm, midriff , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 12 (in Cels. 2, 7 , written as Greek).

Dĭăpontĭus.opening: , = διαπόντιος , beyond seas , a feigned name in Plautus.

dĭăpŏrēsis.opening: , = διαπόρησις , rhet. t. t., a doubting, perplexity , Aquil. Rom. 10, p. 151: est addubitatio, Mart. Cap. 5, § 523 .

dĭapsalma.opening: , = διάψαλμα , a pause in music, Hier. Ep. 28 .

dĭapsōrĭcum.opening: , = διὰ ψωρικῶν , an eye-salve , Marc. Emp. 9 .

dĭārĭum.opening: dies . A daily allowance of food or pay (so only in the plur. ), Cic. Att. 8, 14 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 40 ; Sen. Contr. 4, 27 fin. ; cf. Charis. p. 21 P.— * A diary, journal : diarium, quam Graeci ἐφημερίδα vocant, Asel.…

dĭăsostes.opening: , = διασώστης , a sort of policemen , Julian. Epit. nov. 123, § 532 and 537.

dĭaspermatōn.opening: , = διὰ σπερμάτων , a drug made from seeds , Isid. Or. 4, 9, 9 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 116 .

dĭastēma.opening: (short ĕ, Sid. Carm. 15, 64 ), , , = διάστημα , space between, distance, interval (late Lat.). In gen., Sid. Ep. 8, 11 med. — Esp., in music, an interval , Mart. Cap. 9, § 948 ; Censor. 13 .

dĭastēmătĭcus.opening: adj. , = διαστηματικός , having pauses, intervals : vox (opp. continua), Mart. Cap. 9, § 937 .

dĭastŏle.opening: , = διαστολή , in gram., The diastole , Diom. p. 470 P. al.— The comma , Donat. p. 1742 P.

dĭastŏleus.opening: , = διαστολεύς , an auditor of accounts , Cod. 4, 69, 4.

dĭastȳlos.opening: adj. , = διάστυλος , having columns far apart, diastyle : species aedium, Vitr. 3, 3, 1 sq.

dĭăsyrtĭcus.opening: adj. , = διασυρτικός , mocking, reviling : Spart. Carac. 10 : praedicatio, Hier. adv. Ruf. 1 , no. 1.— Adv. : , mockingly , Serv. Verg. A. 2, 193 .

dĭătessărōn.opening: = διὰ τεσσάρων , v. diapason.— A medicine made of four ingredients , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 18, 112 ; Plin. Val. 3, 22 .

dĭăthўra.opening: , = διάθυρα , an enclosure before the door of a Greek house (called, in Roman houses, prothyra), Vitr. 6, 10 .

dĭătoichon.opening: , = διάτοιχον , a sort of brick-work , Plin. 36, 22, 51, § 172 ex conj., v. Sillig. ad h. 1.

dĭătŏnĭcus.opening: adj. , = διατονικός , diatonic , in music: modulatio, Mart. Cap. 9, § 959; § 963.— Neutr. as subst. : , , a kind of masonry filled in with rubble , Plin. 36, 22, 51, § 172 .

dĭătŏnus.opening: adj. , = διάτονος (extended). In architecture: lateres, band-stones, which run through the thickness of a wall and bind it together, Vitr. 2, 8, 7 .— In music: , , the natural or diatonic series of notes without breaks…

dĭā^trētārĭus.opening: diatretus , one who does perforated or filigree work, a turner, carver , Cod. Theod. 13, 4, 2 al.

dĭā^trētus.opening: adj. , = διάτρητος , pierced with holes, filigree, carved, embossed : calix, Dig. 9, 2, 27, § 29 .— Subst. : , , , pierced work, filigree-work , Mart. 12, 70, 9 .

dĭā^trĭba.opening: , = διατριβή , a learned discussion .— Transf. , a school , Gell. 1, 26 ; 17, 20, 4 al.

dĭā^trĭtaeus.opening: adj. , = διατριταῖος , of the space of three days : tempus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3, 35 ; cf. the foll.

dĭā^trĭtus.opening: , = διάτριτος , the return of a fever on the third day , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1 (twice); 1, 3, 57 al.

dĭătўpōsis.opening: , = διατύπωσις , rhet. t. t., a description, representation , Mart. Cap. 5, § 524 al.

dĭaulos.opening: , = δίαυλος , a double course (in which the runner, after reaching the goal, ran the same distance back), Vitr. 5, 11 ; Hyg. Fab. 173 .

dĭăzeugmĕnon.opening: , = διαζεύγμενον , in rhet., a separation, disjunction , Mart. Cap. 5, § 536 .

dĭăzeuxis.opening: , = διάζευξις , rhet. t. t., = diaeresis, a separation , Prob. p. 1438 P.

dĭăzōma.opening: , = διάζωμα , a space between the seats in a theatre , Vitr. 5, 6, 7 ; cf. balteus, no. 2. d.

dī-bālo.opening: v. a. , to bleat abroad , i. e. to make common or contemptible by clamor; to injure , Caecil. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 103 Müll. (Rib. Com. v. 249).

dĭbăphus.grammar: a, um, or us, um adj.
dĭbăphus.opening: adj. , = δίβαφος , double dyed (once with scarlet and then with purple): purpura, Plin. 9, 39, 63, § 137 ; 21, 8, 22, § 45 .—Because the Roman magistrates wore garments striped with purple, Trop. : , ( = ἡ δίβαφος , sc.…

dībrăchys.opening: = δίβραχυς , a metrical foot consisting of two short syllables, a dibrach , Diom. p. 471 P.; Mar. Victor. p. 2486 ib. (pure Lat. bibrevis).

dī-būcĭno.opening: v. a. , to trumpet forth , acc. to Vel. Long. p. 2227 P.; Cassiod. p. 2294 ib.

dĭca.opening: , = δίκη , law t. t., a lawsuit, judicial process, action . Usually in the phrase dicam scribere (alicui) = δίκην γράφειν τινί , to bring an action against any one, Plaut. Aul. 4, 10, 30 ; Ter. Ph. 1, 2, 77 ; 2, 2, 15 ;…

dĭcābŭla.opening: and , , dicax , chatter, idle talk (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 8, § 809 ; Tert. adv. Val. 20 .

dĭcācĭtas.opening: id. , biting wit, raillery, banter (for syn. cf.: sal, facetiae, cavillatio, lepos, urbanitas): dicacitas sine dubio a dicendo, quod est omni generi commune, ducta est; proprie tamen significat sermonem cum risu aliquos…

dĭcācŭlus.opening: adj. id. . * Talkative, loquacious : amatrix, Plaut. As. 3, 1, 8 .— Facetious, witty (perh. only in Appul.): puella (with lepida), Ap. M. 2, p. 118, 2: sermo, id. ib. 3, 135, 9 .— Adv. : , keenly, satirically,…

Dĭcaearchī^a.opening: the old name of Puteoli, now Puzzuolo , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 61 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 4 Müll.—Also called , , Petr. 120, 68 ; and: Dicarchi moenia, Stat. Silv. 2, 2, 96 .— Derivv. , the inhabitants of that city.—Gen.…

Dĭcaearchus.opening: Δικαίαρχος . The founder of Dicaearchia , Stat. Silv. 2, 2, 96 .— A pupil of Aristotle, a famous philosopher and geographer , Cic. Tusc. 1, 10 ; 31 fin. ; id. Off. 2, 5 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 16 al.

dĭcaeŏlŏgia.opening: , = δικαιολογία , a rhet. t. t., a plea, defence , Rutil. Lup. 3, p. 81 .

dĭcātĭo.opening: 1. dico, no. II. B. 1. . A formal declaration of intention to become a citizen , Cic. Balb. 11 (v. the passage in its connection).— = praedicatio, a praising . Prop., Cod. Theod. 9, 3, 2 . — As a title: tua dicatio,…

dĭcax.opening: adj. 1. dico , talking sharply, satirical, sarcastic, acute, witty (class.): Demosthenes non tam dicax fuit quam facetus. Est autem illud acrioris ingenii, hoc majoris artis, Cic. Or. 26, 90 ; cf. Quint. 6, 3, 21 ; so…

dĭchalcum.opening: , = δίχαλκον , a small coin, the fourth (acc. to others, the fifth) part of an obolus , Vitr. 3, 1 ; cf. Plin. 21, 34, 109, § 185 .

dĭchōneutus.opening: adj. , = δισ-χώνευτος , recast, adulterated : aes, Cod. Theod. 11, 21, 1 .

dĭchŏrēus.opening: , = διχορεῖος , a double trochee , Cic. Or. 63, 212 sq.

dĭchŏtŏmos.opening: adj. , = διχότομος , cut in two, halved (pure Lat. dimidiatus), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 ; Firm. Math. 4 praef.

dī^chrŏnus.opening: adj. , = δίχρονος , of two quantities, common (pure Lat. anceps): vocales, Victor. p. 1966 P. al.; Mart. Cap. 9, § 982 .

dīcĭmōnĭum.opening: 2. dīco , speaking, oratory , an antiquated word acc. to Varr. L. L. 6, § 61 ex conj. Müll.

dĭcĭo.opening: (less correctly, ; occurs only in the gen., dat., acc. , and abl. sing. , and in plur. once, Prud. Psych. 221 ; so Hemsterhuis, Orat. p. 7.—Georges rejects the dat. sing. , but v. infra ; cf. Neue, Formenl. 1, 514 sq.),…

dicis.opening: gen. [v. 2. dico], in the phrase dicis causa or gratia, orig. a jurid. t. t., meaning for the sake of judicial form; hence, in gen., for form's sake, for the sake of appearance , λόγου χάριν : ut illis aliquid…

dĭco.opening: (dixe for dixisse, Val. Ant. ap. Arn. 5, 1 ; DICASSIT dixerit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 75, 15 ; rather = dicaverit), v. a. orig. the same word with 2. dīco; cf. the meaning of abdĭco and abdīco, of indĭco and indīco, dedĭco,…

dīco.opening: ( praes. DEICO, Inscr. Orell. 4848 ; imp. usu. dic; cf. duc, fac, fer, from duco, etc., DEICVNTO, and perf. DEIXSERINT, P. C. de Therm. ib. 3673 ; imp. dice, Naev. ap. Fest. p. 298, 29 Müll.; Plaut. Capt. 2, 2, 109 ;…

dicrŏtum.opening: (sc. navigium), = δίκροτος (two-oared), a galley with two banks of oars , Cic. Att. 5, 11, 4 ; 16, 4 fin. —Also called , , (sc. navis), Auct. B. Alex. 47, 2.

dictābŏlārĭum.opening: dicto , i. q. dicterium, a satirical saying , plur., Laber. ap. Fronto de Or. 1.

dictāmen.opening: dicto , late Lat. for dictum, praescriptum, praeceptum.

dictamnum.opening: , or , , v. Dicte, no. II. B.

dictāta.opening: lessons, exercises , etc., v. dicto fin.

dictātĭo.opening: dicto , a dictating, dictation (late Lat.), Dig. 29, 1, 4 al.

dictātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. dictatio , a short dictation , Hier. adv. Vigil. 3 .

dictātor.opening: dicto, qs. a commander . A dictator , the chief magistrate in several Italian states, elected by the Romans in seasons of emergency for six months, and armed with absolute authority; formerly called Magister populi, and…

dictātōrĭus.opening: adj. dictator , of or belonging to a dictator; dictatorial : gladius, Cic. Clu. 44, 123 : majestas, Liv. 4, 14 ; 8, 30 : fulmen, id. 6, 39 : invidia, id. 22, 26 ; cf. animadversio, Vell. 2, 68 fin. : juvenis, i. e. the…

dictātrix.opening: id. , a dictatress , comic., Plaut. Pers. 5, 1, 18 .

dictātūra.opening: id. . The office of a dictator, dictatorship , Cic. Phil. 1, 1 fin. ; id. Off. 3, 31, 112 ; * Caes. B. C. 3, 2 ; Liv. 6, 39 ; 7, 3 fin. ; Quint. 3, 8, 53 ; Suet. Caes. 76 ; id. Aug. 52 et saep.—* The work of dictating…

Dictē.opening: Δίκτη , a mountain in the eastern part of Crete (now Sethia ), in a cave of which Jupiter, acc. to fable, was concealed from Saturn , Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 164 .— Derivv., , , adj., Dictaean , among poets for Cretan :…

dictērĭum.opening: , = δεικτήριον , a witty saying, a bon-mot (pure Lat. dictum). — Plur. , Pompcn. ap. Macr. S. 2, 1, 14 ; Varr. ap. Non. 101, 3 : dicteria dicere in omnes, Mart. 6, 44, 3 .

dictĭcŏs.opening: adj. , = δεικτικός . Gen., pointing : digitus quem Graeci dicticon vocant, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 21 .— Esp., rhet. t. t., demonstrative : enthymema, Jul. Vict. Art. Rhet. 11.

dictĭo.opening: 2. dico , a saying, speaking, uttering, delivery . In gen. (Good prose, for the most part only in jurid. and rhetor. lang.) Sententiae, Cic. Inv. 2, 4 : testimonii, i. e. the right of giving testimony , * Ter. Ph. 2, 1,…

dictĭōsus.opening: adj. dictum , perhaps facetious, satirical , Varr. L. L. 6, § 61 Müll.

dictĭto.opening: v. intens. a. [dicto], to say often or emphatically; to declare, maintain, assert repeatedly (good prose). In gen.: non, obsecro, es, quem semper te esse dictitasti, Ter. Ph. 5, 1, 16 .; cf. Liv. 3, 20 ; 9, 18 : qui ita…

dicto.opening: v. freq. a. 2. dico , to say often; to pronounce, declare , or assert repeatedly . In gen. (very rare): rogarem te, ut diceres pro me tu idem, qui illis orationem dictavisses, Cic. Fin. 4, 22 fin. : mercemur servum qui…

dictor.opening: 2. dico , one who says something, a speaker (late Lat.), Aug. Doctr. Chr. 4, 19 al.

dictŭrĭo.opening: v. desid. a., to long to say or tell (late Lat.): fortiter a se facta semper dicturiunt, Macr. S. 7, 2, 7 ; 2, 3, 16 .

dictus.opening: 2. dico , a saying, speech , Aur. Vict. epit. 14.

Dictynna.opening: Δίκτυννα . The nymph Britomartis, so called because, when pursued by Minos , she sprang into a net ( δίκτυον ; cf. Callim. Hymn. Dian. 189 sq.), Verg. Cir. 304 .— An appellation of Diana , Ov. M. 2, 441 ; 5, 619 ; id.…

Dictys.opening: Δίκτυς . A mariner changed by Bacchus into a dolphin , Ov. M. 3, 615 .— A centaur, slain at the wedding of Pirithoüs , Ov. M. 12, 334 sq. — A fisherman on the island of Seriphos, who saved Perseus from drowning , Stat.…

dĭdascălĭcus.opening: adj. , = διδασκαλικός , pertaining to instruction, didactic (ante- and post-class.): opusculum, Aus. Ep. 17 .— Subst. : , , , the title of a work by Attius , in Gell. 3, 11, 4 al. ; cf. Madvig Opuscc. Acadd. prior. pp.…

Dīdĭus.opening: the name of a Roman plebeian gens; so T. Didius, consul in the year 656 a. u. c., Cic. Planc. 25, 61 ; Ov. F. 6, 568 al. ; Didius Julianus, emperor of Rome in the year 193 A. D., whose life is written by Spartianus.—…

dī-do.opening: (also written ; v. the foll. ), didĭdi, didĭtum, 3, v. a. , to give out, spread abroad, disseminate, distribute (anteclass. and poet. ; esp. in Lucr.; once in Tac.). Lit. : numquam ego argentum ... disdidi, Cato ap.…

Dīdō.opening: Διδώ , the celebrated foundress of Carthage, daughter of the Tyrian king Belus, wife of Sichaeus, and sister of Pygmalion; called also Elisa or Elissa.—Nom. Dido, Verg. A. 1, 299 ; 340 ; 360 et saep.; Ov. Am. 2, 18, 25…

dī^drāchmon.opening: , and , , , = διδραχμον , a double drachma , Tert. Praescr. 11 ; Vulg. Matt. 17, 23 al.

dī-dūco.opening: v. a. , to draw apart; to part, split, separate, sever, sunder, divide (class.). Lit. In gen.: ventus eas (sc. nubes) leviter diducit, Lucr. 6, 215 : cum compresserat digitos pugnumque fecerat ... cum autem diduxerat et…

dīductĭo.opening: diduco , an expanding, separating (very rare; perh. only in Seneca): ostendit intentionem spiritus velocitas ejus et diductio, Sen. Q. N. 2, 8, 2 : in diductione rerum, in dividing, separating the elements, id. ib. 3,…

Dĭdўmae.opening: A group of islands on the coast of Troas , Plin. 5, 31, 38, § 138 .— Islands on the coast of Lycia , Plin. 5, 31, 35, § 131 . (In Ov. M. 7, 469 , the better reading is Didyme.)

Dĭdўmaeus.opening: adj. of Didyma, a city of Ionia : oraculum Didymaei Apollinis, Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 112 ; cf. ib. 6, 16, 18, § 49 ; Macr. Sat. 1, 17, 64 , and v. Didyme, no. III.

Dĭdўmāon.opening: the name of a skilful artificer , Verg. A. 5, 359 .

Dĭdўmē.opening: An island near Sicily , Plin. 3, 9, 14, § 94 ; Mel. 2, 7, 18 ; Ov. F. 4, 475 .— An island in the Aegaean Sea , Ov. M. 7, 469 .— A city in Ionia (also called , Δίδυμα ), in the Milesian territory, now Jeronda or Joran,…

dĭĕchī^dnōn.opening: δἰ ἐχιδνῶν , a medicine , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2 sub fin.

dĭēcŭla.opening: dim. dies , the short space of a day, one little day, a little while , Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 88 ; Ter. And. 4, 2, 27 ; Cic. Att. 5, 21, 13 ; and repeatedly in Ap.; so Met. 1, p. 106; ib. 6, 179 .

di-ērectus.opening: (in Plaut. always trisyllabic), a , P. a. erigo , qs. stretched out and raised on high, i. e. crucified (only in Plautus and Varro; not in Terence), an abusive expression, like the English Go and be hanged! gallowsbird…

dĭes.opening: (dīes, Liv. Andron. Fragm. Odys. 7 ), ēi (ēī, Verg. A. 4, 156 ; Hor. S. 1, 8, 35 et saep.; dissyl.: di-ei, Ter. Eun. 4, 7, 31 ; also gen. dies, die, and dii—dies, as in acies, facies, pernicies, etc., Enn. ap. Gell. 9,…

dĭĕsis.opening: , = δίεσις . In ancient music, A quarter-tone , Vitr. 5, 4 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 1 fin. — The first audible tone of an instrument , Vitr. 5, 3 .

Dĭespĭter.opening: Dies, Sanscr. Divas, L. divus; cf. ho-dier-nus, and πατήρ, pater; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 233; 2, 458 , another name for Juppiter , Varr. L. L. 5, § 66 and 9, § 75 and 77 Müll.; Plaut. Capt. 4, 4, 1 ; id. Poen. 3, 4, 29;…

dĭĕtēris.opening: , = διετηρίς , a period of two years , Censor. 18, 2 .

dĭezeugmĕnon.opening: , = διεζευγμένον , rhet. t. t. (pure Lat. disjunctum), a separation of equal circumstances , Aquil. Rom. de Fig. 43, p. 187.— Plur. , musical t. t., = τετράχορδα διεζευγμένα , two tetrachords, forming a scale , Vitr. 5,…

diffāmātĭo.opening: diffamo , a publishing, promulgation (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. D. 3, 31 .

diffāmĭa.opening: dis-fama , defamation (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. D. 3, 31 al.

dif-fāmo.opening: v. a. fama , to spread abroad by an ill report; to publish, divulge . Prop. (rare and not anteAug.): vulgat adulterium diffamatumque parenti Indicat, Ov. M. 4, 236 ; cf. prava, Tac. A. 14, 22 : nomen pessimum super…

diffarrĕātĭo.opening: an ancient form of Roman divorce (cf.: remancipatio, divortium, repudium): genus sacrificii, quo inter virum et mulierem fiebat dissolutio. Dicta diffarreatio , quia fiebat farreo libo adhibito, Paul. ex Fest. p. 74, 13…

diffensus.opening: Part. [dis- FENDO = ferio, trudo], deferred, protracted : dilatus, XII. Tab. ap. Fest. p. 273, 26 Müll. (for which others read diffisus; cf. Dig. 2, 11, 2, § 3 , and v. diffindo, II. B.).

diffĕrentĭa.opening: differo , a difference, diversity (cf.: discrepantia, distantia, discrimen, diversitas, variatio—good prose, esp. freq. in Quint.). With gen. : honesti et decori, Cic. Off. 1, 27, 94 : naturarum, id. ib. 1, 31, 112 :…

diffĕrĭtas.opening: id. (ante- and postclass.; v. the preceding art.), a difference, Lucr. 4, 636 ; Arn. 2, p. 54 ; 7 , p. 233.

dif-fĕro.opening: ( inf. differrier, Lucr. 1, 1088 . In tmesi : disque tulissent, Plaut. Trin. 4, 1, 14 ), v. a. and n. Act., to carry different ways; to spread abroad, scatter, disperse, separate (cf.: reicere, proferre, procrastinare,…

dif-fertus.opening: Part. [farcio, kept asunder, stretched out by stuffing, i. e.], stuffed full, filled, crowded (cf.: plenus, refertus, confertus—rare but class.; not in Cicero): plena lictorum provincia, differta exactoribus, * Caes. B.…

dif-fībŭlo.opening: v. a. , to unclasp, unbuckle : chlamydem, Stat. Th. 6, 570 : vincula, Sid. Ep. 3, 3 .

diffĭcĭlē.opening: adv., with difficulty; v. foll. art. fin., no. α .

dif-fĭcĭlis.opening: (old form difficul, like facul, famul, simul, etc., Varr. ap. Non. 111, 25 ), adj. facilis; hence, far from easy to do, to accomplish, to bear, etc.; v. facilis , hard, difficult, troublesome (very freq. and class.). In…

diffĭcĭlĭter.opening: adv., with difficulty; v. difficilis fin., no. γ .

diffĭcultas.opening: ( gen. plur. difficultatium, Liv. 9, 31, 14 ; Gell. 14, 2, 3 ), difficilis , difficulty, trouble, distress, poverty, want. In gen. (freq. in good prose in sing. and plur. With gen. : ineundi consilii, Cic. Rep. 1, 34 :…

diffĭculter.opening: adv., with difficulty; v. difficilis fin., no. β .

diffīdentĭa.opening: diffido , want of confidence, mistrust, distrust, diffidence (class.).—Without gen. : fidentiae contrarium est diffidentia, Cic. Inv. 2, 54, 165 ; cf. id. Tusc. 4, 37, 80 ; so Quint. 5, 7, 1 ; 8 prooem. § 27; 9, 2, 72;…

dif-fīdo.opening: (post-class. perf. diffidi), 3, v. n. , to distrust; to be diffident or distrustful, to despair (freq. and class.). With dat. (so most freq.): eum potius (corrupisse), qui sibi aliqua ratione diffideret, quam eum, qui…

dif-findo.opening: (also diffīsum), 3, v. a. , to cleave asunder, to divide (rare but class.). Lit. : vitem mediam per medullam, Cato R. R. 41, 2 : malos, Enn. ap. Non. 114, 7 (Ann. v. 389 ed. Vahl., where the read. is, as in Non.,…

dif-fingo.opening: v. a. , to form differently, to remodel, to make anew (very rare; perh. only in the foll. passages). Prop.: ferrum incude, Hor. C. 1, 35, 39 .— Trop. : neque diffinget infectumque reddet, Quod fugiens semel hora vexit,…

diffissĭo.opening: diffindo, no. II. B. , the putting off or deferring of business to the following day : in dierum diffissionibus comperendinationibusque, Gell. 14, 2, 1 .

dif-fĭtĕor.opening: v. dep. a. [fateor], to disavow, to deny (very rare; perh. only in the foll. passages—for syn. v. denego init. ): numquam diffitebor multa me simulasse invitum, Planc. in Cic. Fam. 10, 8, 4 ; so with acc. and inf. ,…

difflātus.opening: difflo , a blowing in an opposite direction : ventorum, Amm. 15, 11, 18 .

dif-flētus.opening: Part. [fleo], wept out, drained with weeping (post-class. and very rare): oculi, App. M. 1, p. 104 ; cf.: cognita clade uxor totos efflevit oculos, Pseudo uint. Decl. 6, 4 .

dif-flo.opening: v. a. , to blow apart, disperse by blowing : flatu disturbare, Non. 97, 10 (ante- and post-class.): pars difflatur vento, Lucil. ap. Non. 97, 12 : legiones spiritu, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 17 : nubila (nimbi), Aus. Ephem.…

dif-flŭo.opening: v. n. , to flow in different directions, to flow away (class.; repeatedly in Lucr.—cf.: laxo, rescindo, solvo). Lit. : diffluere humorem cernis, Lucr. 3, 436 ; cf.: ut nos quasi extra ripas diffluentes coerceret, Cic.…

difflŭus.opening: adj. diffluo , flowing asunder, overflowing , Matius ap. Macr. S. 2, 16, 5 .

dif-flŭvĭo.opening: v. a. fluvius; cf. quadrifluvium (qs. to part into two streams, i. e.), to divide, to split : vitem, Col. Arb. 7, 5 ; cf. Schneid. ad Pall. 12, 15, 3, p. 207 sq.

diffluxĭo.opening: diffluo , a flowing off, discharge , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 18 .

diffors.opening: , -rtis, adj. dis-fors : oratio, a kind of defence, by which the act charged is admitted, but justified , Jul. Victor, Art. Rhet. 3, 3; 5.

dif-fringo.opening: ( ), no perf. , fractum, 3, v. a. , to break in pieces, to shatter (very rare): crura, Plaut. As. 2, 4, 68 : axem, Suet. Caes. 37 : gubernaculum, id. Aug. 17 : basin Colossici Apollinis, Vitr. 10, 6 .

dif-fŭgĭo.opening: v. n. , to fly asunder, flee in different directions, to disperse, scatter (class.): diffugiebat enim varium genus omne ferarum, Lucr. 5, 1337 sq. ; 3, 256 ; cf. id. 1, 762 sq. : vox una diffugit in multas aures, id. 4,…

diffŭgĭum.opening: diffugio , a fleeing in different directions, a dispersion : proximorum diffugia, Tac. H. 1, 39 fin.

dif-fŭgo.opening: v. a. , to put to flight, scatter : nebulis diffugatis, August. in Psa. 41, 10 : episcopos, Marcel. Com. Chron. An. 484.

dif-fulgŭro.opening: v. a. , to scatter lightning around , Sid. Carm. 11, 20 .

dif-fulmĭno.opening: v. a. , to scatter a multitude, qs. by lightning, Sil. 5, 276 .

dif-fūmĭgo.opening: v. a. , to fumigate , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

diffundĭto.opening: v. freq. a. diffundo , to pour out, scatter, spread (very rare; perh. only post-class.): pretium per domos, Amm. 18, 5, 6 : aliquid ex sese, id. 21, 1, 11 : ubique sese diffunditans, id. 16, 12 : amoris vi diffunditari…

dif-fundo.opening: v. a. , to spread by pouring, to pour out, pour forth (very freq. and class.). Lit. : (glacies) liquefacta se diffunderet, Cic. N. D. 2, 10 : sanguis per venas in omne corpus diffunditur, id. ib. 2, 55, 138 : (unda)…

diffūsĭo.opening: diffundo . The spreading out, extending : maris, Mart. Cap. 6, § 661 .— Cheerfulness : animi, Sen. Vit. Beat. 5, 1 .

diffūsor.opening: id. no. I. 1. , a drawer-off of liquids: OLEARIVS, Inscr. Orell. 4077 .

dif-fŭtūtus.opening: adj. futuo , exhausted by indulgence : mentula, Cat. 29, 14 .

dĭgămĭa.opening: , = διγαμία , a marrying twice , Tert. Monog. 6 al.

dī-gĕro.opening: v. a. , to force apart, separate, divide, distribute (cf.: dispono, distribuo, divido, dispenso, ordino, compono). Lit. Ingen. (so mostly post-Aug.): (insulae) interdum discordantibus ventis digeruntur (opp. junctae…

dīgestĭbĭlis.opening: adj. digero, I. B. 1. , pertaining to digestion (late Lat.): cibus, i. e. digestible, easy of digestion, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5, 159 : oxygarum, i. e. promoting digestion, Apic. 1, 34 .

dīgestĭlis.opening: adj. id. , promoting digestion (late Lat.): meatus, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 6, 3 .

dīgestīvus.opening: adj. id. I. B. 1. , pertaining to digestion, digestive : vis, Macer, Carm. 1, 18.

dīgestōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , promoting digestion (late Lat.): medicamentum, Plin. Val. 2, 8 : embamma, Marc. Empir. 20.

dīgestus.opening: digero , a distributing : sanctarum opum, i. e. management of the imperial treasury, Stat. S. 3, 3, 86 .

dĭgĭtālis.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the finger : gracilitas, Plin. 14, 3, 4, § 40 : crassitudo, id. 22, 20, 23, § 48 ; cf. Varr. R. R. 1, 55, 1 Schneid. and Gesn. (al. digitabulis).

dĭgĭtātus.opening: adj. id. , having fingers or toes : aves, Plin. 11, 47, 107, § 256 .

dĭgĭtŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a little finger , Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 15 ; id. Bacch. 4, 4, 24 ; Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 53 ; Varr. ap. Non. 135, 24 : aniculae collum digitulis duobus oblidere, Cic. Scaur. Fragm. § 10 al.— Transf. , of the parrot's…

dignanter.opening: adv., courteously , etc., v. dignor fin.

dignē.opening: adv., worthily, fitly, becomingly , v. dignus fin.

dignĭtōsus.opening: adj. dignitas , dignified, respectable , ἀξιωματικός , Gloss. Philox.: homo, Petr. 57, 10 .

dīgressĭo.opening: digredior , a parting, separating; a going away, departing, departure . * Lit. (in this signif. more freq. digressus): congressio, tum vero digressio nostra, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 3, 4 .—More freq., Trop. , a going aside,…

dīgressīvus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to digression, digressive : relatio, Cassiod. Inst. Div. litt. 4.

dī-jŭgo.opening: ( ), no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to separate : aliquem ab aliquo (with dijunxit), Arn. 5, p. 162 .

dīlābĭdus.opening: adj. dilabor , that soon goes to pieces : vestes, Plin. 8, 55, 81, § 219 .

dĭmăchaerus.opening: adj. , = διμάχαιρος , fighting with two swords : gladiator, Inscr. Orell. 2584 .

dī-mădesco.opening: v. inch. , to melt away : nives, Luc. 6, 479 .

dī-māno.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to flow different ways, to spread abroad (very rare): meus hic forensis labor dimanavit ad existimationem hominum paulo latius, Cic. Cael. 3, 6 .
