dīnŭmĕrātĭo.opening: id. , a counting over, reckoning up, enumeration . In gen. (very rare): noctium ac dierum, Cic. Rep. 3, 2 fin. ; cf. (dierum), Paul. Sent. 5, 33 : (personarum), Dig. 38, 10, 10, § 16 ; Vulg. 2 Par. 2, 17 .— Esp., as a…

dīnŭmĕrātor.opening: id. , a reckoner, calculator : syllabarum, Aug. in Psa. 55, 10 .

dī-nŭmĕro.opening: v. a. , to count over, reckon up, enumerate . In gen. (class.): stellas, Cic. Off. 1, 43, 154 : annos, id. Rep. 2, 15 ; cf. horas, Plin. 2, 73, 75, § 185 : tempora, * Verg. A. 6, 691 : noctes, Ov. M. 11, 574 al. :…

dĭ-nummĭum.opening: vox hibr., from δίς and nummus , a tax of two nummi, Cod. Theod. 14, 27, 2 .

dĭo.opening: or , , , = Δίων . A brother-in-law of the elder Dionysius, of Syracuse, the pupil and friend of Plato . His life was written by Nepos and Plutarch; cf. also Cic Tusc. 5, 35; id. de Or. 3, 34 ; Jornand. 2, 92 .— An…

dĭōbŏlāris.opening: adj. vox hibr., διώβολον, with ending -aris , that costs or is worth two oboli: scorta, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 58 ; cf. id. Fragm. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 64 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 74, 6 Müll.: anus, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 64 .—Hence,…

Dĭŏchăres.opening: a freedman of Caesar , Cic. Att. 11, 6, 7 .—Hence, , , adj., of Diochares : litterae, id. ib. 13, 45, 1 .

Dĭoclētĭānus.opening: , C. Aurelius Valerius, a Roman emperor from 284-305 A. D., Aurel. Vict. Caes. 38 ; id. Epit. 39 ; Eutrop. 9, 13 sq.; before his accession to the throne named Diocles, Aur. Vict. Ep. 39 .

Dĭŏdōrus.opening: , = Διόδωρος . A Peripatetic philosopher, a pupil of Critolaüs , Cic. Fin. 5, 5 ; id. Ac. 2, 24 ; id. Tusc. 5 , 30 sq.— A famous dialectician , Cic. Fat. 6 ; Plin. 7, 53, 54, § 180 .— Siculus, a well-known historian of…

Dĭŏdŏtus.opening: , = Διόδοτος , a Stoic, and teacher of Cicero , Cic. Brut. 90 ; id. Fam. 9, 4 ; id. Att. 2, 20 ; id. Ac. 2, 36 ; id. Tusc. 5, 39 et saep.; Tac. Or. 30 .

dĭœcēsis.opening: , = διοίκησις . A governor's jurisdiction, a district , Cic. Fam. 3, 8, 4 ( ib. 13, 53 and 67, written as Greek); Cod. Theod. 7, 6, 3 ; Amm. 17, 7, 6 .— In eccl. Lat., a bishop's jurisdiction, a diocese , Sid. Ep. 7, 6…

dĭœcētes.opening: , = διοικητής , an overseer of the revenue, royal treasurer , Cic. Rab. Post. 8, 22 ; 10, 28 .

Dĭŏgĕnes.opening: , = Διογένης . Apolloniates, a celebrated Ionian philosopher, pupil of Anaximenes , Cic. N. D. 1, 12, 29 .— The well-known Cynic philosopher of Sinope , Cic. Tusc. 1, 43, 104 ; id. N. D. 3, 34 ; id. Mur. 36 et saep.— A…

dĭōgmītae.opening: , = ΔΙΩΓΜΙΤΑΙ [from διωγμός , pursuit], a sort of lightarmed frontier troops kept for the pursuit of robbers , Amm. 27, 9 ; Capitol. Anton. Philos. 21 .

Dĭŏmēdes.opening: , = Διομήδης . A son of Tydeus, king of Aetolia, and Deipyle, the successor of Adrastus in Argos; a famous hero at the siege of Troy, after which he went to Apulia, where he founded Argyripa ( Arpi ), Ov. M. 13, 100 sq.…

Dĭōnē.opening: ( , , Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 59 ), , = Διώνη . The mother of Venus , Cic. l. l.; Hyg. praef.; Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 433 .—Hence, , , adj., of Dione : vestis, the garment worked by Dione for her daughter , Claud. Epith. Pall.…

dĭōnўmus.opening: adj. , = διώνυμος , with a double name , Prisc. 580 P.

Dĭŏnȳsia.opening: a noted dancer , Cic. Rosc. Com. 8 ; Gell. 1, 5 .

Dĭŏnȳsĭus.opening: , = Διονύσιος , the name of several celebrated Greeks; esp., The elder Dionysius, tyrant of Syracuse , Nep. Dio, 1 ; id. Reg. 2 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 20 sq. ; id. N. D. 3, 33 sq. al.— His son, likewise tyrant of Syracuse ,…

dĭŏnȳsŏnymphas.opening: , = διονυσονυμφάς , a plant , i. q. casignete, q. v., Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 165 .

Dĭŏnȳsŏpŏlītae.opening: the inhabitants of Dionysopolis, a city of Magna Phrygia , Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 2, § 4 ; Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 106 ; id. 4, 10, 17, § 44 .

Dĭŏnȳsus.opening: or , , , = Διόνυσος , the Greek name of Bacchus (not in the Aug. poets), Cic. N. D. 3, 21 ; 23 ; Att. ap. Macr. S. 6, 5 ; Plaut. Stich. 5, 2, 13 ; Aus. Epigr. 30 .— Derivv., , , adj., of or pertaining to Bacchus; , , ,…

dĭŏpĕtes.opening: , = διοπετής (falling from heaven): rana, a sort of frog, rainfrog , called also, calamites, Plin. 32, 7, 24, § 70 ; 32, 10, 50, § 139 .

Dĭŏphănes.opening: , = Διοφάνης . Of Mitylenae, teacher of Tib. Gracchus , Cic. Brut. 27, 104 .— Of Nicaea, a Latin author on husbandry , Varr. R. R. 1, 1, 8 al.

dĭoptra.opening: , = δίοπτρα , an optical instrument to measure the height of places, Vitr. 8, 6 ; for measuring the sun's shadow, Plin. 2, 69, 69, § 176 .

Dĭōryctos.opening: , = διωρυκτός [ διῶρυξ ], a trench or canal, in Acarnania, between Leucadia and the continent , Plin. 4, 1, 2, § 5 .

dĭōryx.opening: , = διῶρυξ , a canal : manu factus amnis, ex Nili alveo dioryge adductus, Mel. 3, 8 fin.

Dĭos bălănus.opening: , = Διὸς βάλανος , a kind of chestnut , perh. the large sweet chestnut , Plin. 15, 23, 25, § 93 .

Dĭos pneuma.opening: , = Διὸς πνεῦμα , a species of rosemary , App. Herb. 79 .

Dĭospўros.opening: , = Διόσπυρος , a plant , otherwise called lithospermon, stonecrop , Plin. 27, 11, 74, § 98 .

dĭōta.opening: , = διώτη , a two-handled vessel, a wine-jar , Hor. C. 1, 9, 8 .

Dĭŏvis.opening: or , , collat. form of Jovis, old nom. for later Juppiter, q. v.; cf. Diespiter , the old Italian name for Juppiter , acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, § 66 Müll.; Gell. 5, 12, 1 and 6; Inscr. in Bullet. del Inst. 1846 .

Dīphĭlus.opening: , = Δίφιλος . A celebrated Greek comic writer of Sinope, imitated by Plautus , Plaut. Cas. prol. 32 ; id. Rud. prol. 32 ; Ter. Ad. prol. 6 ; Vell. 1, 16, 3 . — An architect employed by Quintus Cicero , Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1,…

diphrўges.opening: , = διφρυγές, τό , a kind of slag formed in furnaces when copper is melted , Plin. 34, 13, 37, § 135 ; Cels. 5, 7, 22 ; Scrib. Comp. 227 and 247.

diphthongus.opening: , = δίφθογγος , a diphthong , Mart. Cap. 3, § 277 ; Prisc. p. 561 P. al.

dĭphўes.opening: , = διφυής , a precious stone, otherwise unknown , Plin. 37, 10, 57, § 157 .

dī^plangīum.opening: , = διπλαγγεῖον , a double vessel (pure Lat. duplex vas), Theod. Prisc. 1, 19 (cf. Scrib. Comp. 73 ).

dī^plăsĭus.opening: adj. , = διπλάσιος , twofold, duplicate : ex ratione diplasia, hoc est duplici, Mart. Cap. 9, § 934 .

diplinthĭus.opening: adj. , = διπλίνθιος , two bricks thick : parietes, Vitr. 2, 8, 17 .

dī^plŏïs.opening: , = διπλοΐς , a double robe to be wrapped around the body, a cloak, mantle , Sulpic. Sever. Hist. Sacr. 1, 35, 7; Vulg. Psa. 108, 28 ; id. Baruch, 5, 2; Acro on Hor. Ep. 1, 17, 25 ; Nov. ap. Non. 316, 5 .

dī^plōma.opening: ( dat. and abl. plur. regul. diplomatibus, Tac. H. 2, 65 ; Plin. Ep. 10, 122 ; Suet. Aug. 50 ; Murat. Inscr. 885, 4), , = δίπλωμα , a letter folded double , viz., A state letter of recommendation given to persons…

diplōmārĭus.opening: diploma , one who carried out the imperial letters of recommendation , Inscr. Orell. 2917 .

dipsăcos.opening: , = δίψακος , the plant teasel , Dipsacus fullonum, Linn.; Plin. 27, 9, 47, § 71 .

dipsas.opening: , = διψάς , a kind of serpent whose bite causes violent thirst , the Coluber Vipera, Linn.; Plin. 23, 8, 80, § 152 ; Mart. 3, 44, 7 ; Luc. 9, 610 ; 718 ; Sil. 3, 313 ; Vulg. Deut. 8, 15 .

Dipsas.opening: a name given to an old bawd , Ov. Am. 1, 8, 2 .

diptĕros.opening: adj. , = δίπτερος , with two wings : aedes, Vitr. 3, 1, 7 praef.

diptōta.opening: , = δίπτωτα . In the later gramm., nouns that have only two cases, diptotes , Diomed. p. 288 P. et saep.; cf.: diptotos forma, Ars Consent. p. 2033 fin. ib.

diptўcha.opening: , = δίπτυχα . A writing-tablet of two leaves (late Lat.), Cod. Theod. 15, 9, 1 ; Symm. Ep. 2, 80 al. — The double shell of the oyster, Ambros. Hexaem. 5, 8 .

Dĭpўlon.opening: , = Δίπυλον , a gate at Athens that closed the Ceramicus, and through which one passed in going to the Academy , Cic. Fin. 5, 1, 1 ; Liv. 31, 24, 8 .

dĭpўros.opening: adj. , = δίπυρος , twice burned , Phaëthon, Mart. 4, 47, 2 .

dī-rādo.opening: v. a. , to scratch slightly : tergum piscis, Cassiod. Varr. 11, 40 .

Dīrae.opening: the Furies , v. dirus, I. B. 2.

Dircē.opening: ( acc. Dircam, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 65 ), , = Δίρκη . A fountain N. W. of Thebes, in Boeotia , Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 25 ; Ov. M. 2, 239 ; Stat. Th. 1, 38 .— Meton. , poet. , the region lying around this fountain , Stat. Th. 2,…

Dircenna.opening: a fountain in Spain, near Bilbilis , Mart. 1, 50, 17 .

dircĭon.opening: a plant also known as Apollinaris herba, a kind of solanum , Ap. Herb. 23.

dīrectā.opening: (sc. viā), perpendicularly , see dirigo, P. a. fin. c.

dīrectārĭus.opening: dirigo , one who secretly enters a house in order to steal, a sneak-thief, burglar (very rare), Dig. 47, 11, 7 ; Paul. Sent. 5, 4 .

dīrectē.opening: adv., directly, straight , etc., v. dirigo, P. a. fin. a.

dīrectĭangŭlus.opening: adj. directus-angulus , right-angled, rectangular , Mart. Cap. 6, § 712 .

dīrectim.opening: adv., directly, straightway , etc., v. dirigo, P. a. fin. d.

dīrectĭo.opening: dirigo (a very rare word). A making straight or even, a levelling : plana coagmentorum, Vitr. 7, 3, 5 sq. — Concr., a straight line , App. de Mundo, p. 57.— Trop. A directing, aiming , towards any thing: quaedam…

dīrectĭtūde.opening: directus , rightness, correctness : aeterna, Cassiod. in Psa. 101, 30 .

dīrecto.opening: adv., directly, in a straight line , v. dirigo, P. a. fin. b.

dīrectōrĭus.opening: adj. dirigo , that directs or sends in any direction, directory : litterae, Cod. Theod. 14, 15, 3, § 1 .

dīrectūra.opening: id. , a making straight, even, a levelling , Vitr. 7, 3, 5 .

dīrectus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from dirigo.

dĭremptĭo.opening: dirimo , a separation : aequitatis, Val. Max. 4, 7, 1 .

dīreptĭo.opening: diripio , a plundering, pillaging (rare, but good prose): urbs relicta direptioni et incendiis, Cic. Fam. 4, 1, 2 ; cf. urbis, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 52 ; * Caes. B. C. 2, 12 : oppidi (with expugnatio), Suet. Claud. 21 :…

dīreptor.opening: id. , a plunderer (very rare; cf.: fur, praedo, raptor), Cic. Phil. 3, 11, 27 ; id. Cat. 2, 9 fin. ; Tac. H. 3, 33 .

dĭrĭbĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. dishabeo, like dirimo, from dis-emo, to keep apart, hence , pub. law t. t., to lay apart, separate, divide, sort , the tablets or ballots taken out of the ballot-box, in order to determine who has…

dĭrĭbĭtĭo.opening: diribeo , a separating or sorting of the tablets taken from the ballot-box , Cic. Planc. 6, 14 ; Symm. Laud. in Patr. 3, p. 40 ed. Mai.

dĭrĭbĭtor.opening: id. , the separater or sorter of the ballots used in voting , Cic. Pis. 15, 36 ; id. post Red. in Sen. 11, 28 ; Aus. Grat. Act. 5 .— Transf. , in gen., a distributor , App. M. 2, 32, p. 137 ed. Oud.; Amm. 18, 5, 6 .

dĭrĭbĭtōrĭum.opening: (sc. aedificium; in Dio Cass. 55, 8: τὸ δειριβιτώριον ) [id.], the building in which the ballots were sorted (v. diribeo), Suet. Claud. 18 ; Plin. 6, 40, 76, § 201 ; 36, 15, 24, § 102 Sillig. N. cr.

dī-rĭgo.opening: or (the latter form preferred by Roby, L. G. 2, p. 387; cf. Rib. Proleg. ad Verg. p. 401 sq.; so Liv. 21, 19, 1 ; 21, 47, 8 ; 22, 28 Weissenb.; id. 22, 47, 2 Drak.; Lach. ad Lucr. 4, 609 ; Tac. A. 6, 40 Ritter; acc. to…

dĭrĭmo.opening: ( perf. dirempsi, cited as error, Charis. 220 P.), , v. a. disĕmo, like diribeo, from dis-habeo , to take apart; to part, separate, divide (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense—cf.: findo, scindo, divello, separo,…

dī-rĭpĭo.opening: v. a. rapio , to tear asunder, tear in pieces (class.). In gen. (rarely): Pentheum diripuisse aiunt Bacchas, Plaut. Merc. 2, 4, 1 : Hippolytum (equi), Ov. A. A. 1, 338 ; id. F. 5, 310 : nec opinantes (leae), Lucr. 5,…

dīrĭtas.opening: dirus (rare but class.), lit. fearfulness, viz., Of fate, fatal mischief, misfortune : si qua invecta diritas casu foret, Cic. Poët. Tusc. 3, 14: totius diei, Suet. Ner. 8 ; cf. ominis, Gell. 4, 9, 10 .— Of character,…

dī-rumpo.opening: or , , v. a. , to break or dash to pieces; to break, burst asunder (rare but class.). Lit. : tabulā caput, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 37 : ne medius disrumpar miser, id. Curc. 2, 1, 7 : cum se in nubem induerint (venti)…

dī-rŭo.opening: v. a. , to tear asunder, overthrow, demolish, destroy (class. —cf.: deleo, diluo, exstinguo, everto, demolior). Prop.: maceriam, Ter. Ad. 5, 7, 10 : urbem, Cic. Inv. 1, 40, 73 ; id. Q. Fr. 1, 1, 8, § 25 ; Suet. Caes. 54…

dīruptĭo.opening: dirumpo , a tearing asunder, tearing to pieces : magnorum corporum, Sen. Q. N. 2, 15 .

dīrus.opening: adj. Sanscr. root dī, to flee; Gr. δέος, δείδω, δεινός , fearful, awful (for syn. cf.: saevus, atrox, ferox, crudelis, trux, furens, furiosus, immitis). Orig. belonging to the lang. of augurs; of fate, ill-omened,…

dīs.opening: neutr. dite (mostly poet. ; in prose very rare before the Aug. per.): dis quidem esses, Ter. Ad. 5, 1, 8 : dite solum, Val. Fl. 2, 296 : hujus ditis aedes, Ter. Ad. 4, 2, 42 ; so, ditis domus, Hor. Epod. 2, 65 : diti…

Dīs.opening: ( nom. Dītis, Petr. Poët. 120, 76; Quint. 1, 6, 34 ; cf. Serv. Verg. A. 6, 273 ; the nom. Dis very rare in the poets; Aus. Idyl. 12 : de deis, 3), cf.: dīus, divus, deus , orig. denoting godhead, deity , in general, and…

dĭs.opening: Sanscr. dva, two: dvis, twice; Gr. δίς (δϝις); cf.: bis, bini, dubius, duo; also Sanscr. vi- (for dvi-) = dis- , occurs before vowels only in dishiasco; it stands unchanged before c, p, q, t, s , and di; loses its s…

dis-calcĕātus.opening: adj., unshod, barefooted , Suet. Ner. 51 ; Vulg. Deut. 25, 10 al.

dis-căpēdĭno.opening: v. a. capedo , manus, to hold the hands apart , App. Flor. 3, p. 141 .

dis-căvĕo.opening: v. n. , to be on one's guard against, keep away from, beware of : malo, Plaut. Men. 2, 1, 24 .

dis-cēdo.opening: ( perf. sync. discesti, Plaut. As. 2, 1, 3 ), v. n. (With the notion of dis predominating.) To part asunder, divide, separate (rare but class.; cf.: linquo, relinquo, desero, desum, destituo, deficio). Lit. : cum terra…

discentĭa.opening: disco , a learning (late Lat.), Tert. Anim. 23 and 24.

disceptātĭo.opening: discepto , a dispute, disputation, debate, discussion, disquisition . In gen. (good prose in sing. and plur.; cf. for syn.: controversia, concertatio, altercatio, contentio, jurgium, rixa, disputatio): cum quibus omnis…

disceptātor.opening: discepto , an umpire, arbitrator, judge : disceptator id est rei sententiaeque moderator, Cic. Part. Or. 3, 10 : IVRIS DISCEPTATOR, QVI PRIVATA IVDICET IVDICARIVE IVBEAT, PRAETOR ESTO, id. Leg. 3, 3, 8 : nec vero…

disceptātrix.opening: disceptator , a female umpire, arbitrator, judge (very rare): dialectica veri et falsi quasi disceptatrix et judex, * Cic. Ac. 2, 28, 91 ; Lampr. Commod. 5 .

discepto.opening: v. a. dis and capio . Jurid. t. t. (lit., to seize hold of and separate; hence, to stop the dispute), to decide, determine, judge a controversy, = dijudicare (cf.: dissero, disputo; good prose, but rare): res juste…

discernenter.opening: adv., with a distinction , etc.; v. discerno, P. a. fin.

discernĭbĭlis.opening: adj. discerno , that may be distinguished, discernible : similitudo, Aug. Enchir. 90 .

discernĭcŭlum.opening: id. . * The bodkin in a woman's head-dress, which parted the hair, a hair-bodkin , Lucil. ap. Non. 35, 31 ; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 129 .—* Trop. , a difference : coloris, Gell. 17, 15, 4 ; Ambros. Apol. Dav. Alt. 4, 26 .

dis-cerno.opening: v. a. , to separate, set apart. Lit. , to separate, part, divide (freq. since the Aug. per.): equas, ne inter se pugnare possint, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 10 : ordines (preceded by senatus a populo secretus ), Liv. 34, 54 :…

dis-cerpo.opening: v. a. carpo , to pluck or tear in pieces, to rend, to mangle (class.). Lit. : animus nec secerni nec dividi nec discerpi nec distrahi potest, Cic. Tusc. 1, 29, 71 ; cf. id. N. D. 1, 11, 27 : inter orgia Bacchi…

discerptĭo.opening: discerpo , a tearing in pieces, rending : discerptiones eorum, Vulg. 4 Esdr. 12, 32: juris humani, Liv. 41, 24, 10 Madvig. (al. dissertio).

discessĭo.opening: discedo . (Very rarely), a separation of married persons, Ter. And. 3, 3, 36 ; of the people into parties (with seditio), Gell. 2, 12 : stellarum et discessiones et coetus, separations and conjunctions, id. 14, 1, 8 ;…

discessus.opening: discedo . A going asunder, separation, opening (very rare): caeli, i. e. lightning, Cic. Div. 2, 28, 60 : est interitus quasi discessus et secretio ac diremptus earum partium, quae ante interitum junctione aliqua…

discĕus.opening: , = δίσκος (a quoit), a sort of comet shaped like a quoit , Plin. 2, 25, 22, § 89 .

discĭdĭum.opening: discindo . A tearing asunder, dividing, parting (freq. in Lucr., elsewh. rare): partibus ejus (sc. corporis) discidium parere et nexus exsolvere, Lucr. 1, 220 ; cf. id. 249 ; 452 ; 2, 120 ; 3, 839 al.: nubis, id. 6, 293…

dis-cīdo.opening: v. a. caedo , to cut in pieces (very rare; perh. only in the foll. passages): aliquod in multas partīs ferro, Lucr. 3, 659 ; id. 669 .

dī-scindo.opening: v. a. , to tear or cleave asunder, to cut asunder, divide, rend, tear (class.—for syn. cf.: findo, scindo, dirimo, divello, separo, secerno). Lit. : salicem Graecam discindito, Cato R. R. 40, 2 : vestem, Ter. Ad. 1, 2,…

dis-cingo.opening: v. a. , to ungird, deprive of the girdle . Lit. : discinctā tunicā fugiendum est, Hor. S. 1, 2, 132 ; Vell. 2, 41 fin. ; cf.: tunicati et discincti, Suet. Aug. 100 : jam discingitur armis, Sil. 8, 34 .—As a milit.…

discī^plīna.opening: (also uncontr. DISCIPVLINA, Num. Hadr. ap. Eckh. D. N. V. 6, p. 503; the Cod. palimps. Cic. Rep. 2, 19 , prima manu has likewise DISCIPVLINA: so, discipulina, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 75 Lorenz; id. As. 1, 3, 49 Fleck.; cf.…

discī^plīnābĭlis.opening: adj. disciplina , to be learned by teaching , Cassiod. Var. 4, 33 ; Isid. 2, 24, 9 .—Hence, adv. : , in an instructive manner , Cassiod. in Psalt. praef. 4; id. in Psa. 150, 4 .

discī^plīnātus.opening: adj. id. , instructed, disciplined (late Lat.), Vulg. Jacob. 3, 13 al. ; Alcim. Avit. 4, 46 : disciplinatior, Tert. Fug. in persec. 1, fin.

discī^plīnōsus.opening: adj. id. , docile : gladiator, Cato ap. Non. 463, 5 ; cf. Gell. 4, 9, 12 .

discĭpŭlātus.opening: discipulus , the condition of a disciple, discipleship , Tert. Praescr. Haeret. 22 ; Cassiod. Var. 5, 40 .

discĭpŭlus.opening: disco, and root of puer, pupilla; cf. Sanscr., putras, son; Gr. πῶλος; Engl., foal , a learner, scholar, pupil, disciple . In gen., Plaut. Bacch. 1, 2, 44 sq. ; Cic. Div. 1, 3, 6 ; 1, 23, 46 ; id. N. D. 3, 7 et saep.—…

discissĭo.opening: discindo , a separation, division (late Lat., v. the class. discidium), Aug. Ep. 261 al.

discissūra.opening: id. , a rending asunder, a rent (late Lat.): corporis, Ambros. Serm. 13 .

dis-clūdo.opening: v. a. claudo (rare but classical; already obsolete in the time of Macrobius, v. Macr. S. 6, 4 ). To shut up separately, to keep separate; orig. belonging to household lang.: dispares disclusos habere pisces, Varr. R. R.…

disclūsĭo.opening: discludo , a separation : loci, App. de Deo Socr. init.

disco.opening: ( part. fut. : sic disciturum, etc., App. ap. Prisc. p. 887 P.), v. a. from the root da-, Gr. δεδαώς, δαῆναι; dak-, cf. doceo, doctus, Gr. διδάσκω , to learn, to learn to know, to become acquainted with , etc. (for syn.…

discŏbīno.opening: v. a. dis-scobina , to file away, to scratch, destroy by scratching : simulacra, Arn. 6, 14 .

discŏbŏlus.opening: , = δισκοβόλος , the thrower of the discus or quoit , a famous piece of sculpture by Myron, Quint. 2, 13, 10 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 57 ; also by Naucydes, Plin. ib. § 80; and a painting by Tauriscus, id. 35, 11, 40, § 144…

discŏï_des.opening: adj. , = δισκοειδής , quoit-shaped : figura, Theod. Prisc. 4, 2 .

discŏlĭus.opening: pes = δισκολιός , a verse consisting of an iambus, pyrrhichius, and trochaeus , Atil. Fortun. p. 2687 P.

dis-cŏlor.opening: ( abl. -ori, Flor. 1, 16, 7 ; Curt. 3, 3, 26 —post-class. form of the fem. discolora, in the signif. of II. A.: lana, Prud. στεφ . 10, 302: serta, Symm. Laud. in Val. 2, 1 ed. Mai.: venustas, Mart. Cap. 4 init. ; and…

discŏlōrĭus.opening: and , , v. the preced. art. init.

dis-concinnus.opening: adj., unsuitable, ill-matched : oculos (opp. concinnos), Fronto de Or. 2.

dis-condūco.opening: v. n. , not to be profitable or conducive, to be injurious, prejudicial : nil disconducit huic rei, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 85 .

dis-convĕnĭentĭa.opening: disconvenio , want of agreement, inconsistency (opp. convenientia), Tert. Test. An. 6 .

dis-convĕnĭo.opening: v. n. , to disagree; to be inharmonious, inconsistent (very rare): aestuat et vitae disconvenit ordine toto, Hor. Ep. 1, 1, 99 .— Impers. : eo disconvenit inter Meque et te, Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 19 : disconveniens deo, Lact.…

dis-cŏŏpĕrĭo.opening: v. a. , to uncover, disclose, lay bare, expose (eccl. Lat.): caput, Vulg. Lev. 21, 10 : turpitudinem, id. ib. 18, 7 : verecundiora patris, id. Ezech. 22, 10 .— Transf. , to put off, take off, remove a covering: pallium,…

discŏphŏrus.opening: , = δισκοφόρος , one who carries a dish (discus, II.), a dishbearer , Hier. in Daniel, praef.

dis-cŏquo.opening: v. a. , to boil to pieces, to boil thoroughly (post-Aug.), Cels. 6, 9 ; Plin. 22, 25, 70, § 142 ; 32, 7, 26, § 81 ; 23, 6, 60, § 113 ; Vulg. Ezech. 24, 5 al.

discordābĭlis.opening: adj. discordo , disagreeing, discordant : ingenio haud discordabili, Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 42 .

discordĭa.opening: discors , disunion, disagreement, dissension, variance, discord (class.), Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 66 ; Ter. Hec. 4, 4, 71 ; Cic. Tusc. 4, 9, 21 ; id. Lael. 7, 24 ; id. Off. 1, 25, 85 ; id. Mur. 39, 83 ; Sall. C. 5, 2 ; Liv.…

discordĭālis.opening: , false reading in Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 142 , instead of discordiam, v. Sillig, ad h. l.

discordĭōsus.opening: adj. discordia , full of discord, prone to discord (very rare; cf. discors and v. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 369): volgus seditiosum atque discordiosum, * Sall. J. 66, 2 : domus, Sid. Ep. 6, 2 .— , adv. : , in a spirit of…

discordĭtas.opening: discors , disunion, discord , Pac. ap. Non. 97, 1 .

discordĭum.opening: discors , discord, dissension.—Plur. : publica discordia, Calp. Ecl. 1, 57 .

discordo.opening: v. n. id. , to be at variance, to differ, to quarrel (rare but class.). Lit. : discordare inter se, Ter. And. 3, 3, 43 : cupiditates in animis dissident atque discordant, Cic. Fin. 1, 13, 44 : animus a se ipse dissidens…

discŏrĭātĭo.opening: dis-corium , a flaying, removal of the skin , Soran. qu. Med. 245 (cf. discorio, ἀποδέρω , Gloss.).

dis-cors.opening: ( nom. f. discordis, Pompon. ap. Prisc. p. 726 Com., v. 164 Rib.), adj. cor , discordant, disagreeing, inharmonious, at variance; opp. concors (class.). Prop. Of persons: homines non contentione, non ambitione…

discrēbĭlis.opening: adj. discerno , that can be discerned, discernible : vox, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 3, 42 Mai.

dis-crēdo.opening: v. a. , to be incredulous towards, not to believe (late Lat.), Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 3, 58 Mai.; Commod. praef. 3, al.

discrĕpābĭlis.opening: adj. discrepo , irreconcilable, discrepant , Cassiod. in Psa. 100, 1 .

discrĕpans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from discrepo.

discrĕpantĭa.opening: discrepo , discordance, dissimilarity, discrepancy (a Ciceron. word): rerum et verborum, Cic. Fin. 3, 12 fin. : scripti et voluntatis, id. Top. 25 fin. : nulla, id. Off. 1, 31, 111 .

discrĕpātĭo.opening: id. , a discrepancy, dispute : inter consules fuit, Liv. 10, 18, 7 ; cf. Drak. ad Liv. 21, 31, 8 .

discrĕpĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to disagree wholly, to be altogether different (a Lucretian word): res longe, Lucr. 6, 1105 ; id. 2, 1018 : inter se (with disjunctum), id. 3, 803 .

dis-crĕpo.opening: v. n. , to differ in sound, to sound differently, discordantly, not to harmonize (for syn. cf.: differo, disto, intersum). Lit. (rare; perh. only in Cic.): ut in fidibus aut tibiis, quamvis paulum discrepent, tamen id a…

dis-cresco.opening: v. n. , to grow broad, grow out , Lact. de Mort. Pers. 33, 10 .

discrētĭo.opening: discerno (postclass.). A separation : cum vis aliqua utrumque (corpus et animam) discreverit, quae discretio mors vocetur, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, 17 ; Lact. 7, 12, 4 .— A difference, distinction : sine discretione,…

discrētīvus.opening: adj. id. , serving to distinguish , Prisc. p. 1021 ; 1061 al. P.— Adv. : , by way of distinction , Donat. ad Ter. Eun. 1, 2, 43 .

discrētor.opening: id. , he who discerns or judges, a discerner : cogitationum deus, Vulg. Hebr. 4, 12 al.

discrētōrĭum.opening: , = διάφραγμα , the diaphragm , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 12, 143 .

dī-scrībo.opening: v. a. , to distribute, divide among several persons, apportion, assign : (class.) quodne (argentum) ego discripsi porro illis quibus debui? Ter. Phorm. 5, 8, 30 : quorum ipsorum bona, quantacumque erant, statim suis…

discrīmen.opening: contr. from discerimen à discerno; cf. crimen from cerno , lit., that which separates or divides two things from each other (for syn. cf.: differentia, discrepantia, diversitas, distantia); hence, Lit. , an intervening…

discrīmĭnālis.opening: adj. discrimino , that serves to divide or part (late Lat.): acus, a pin or bodkin that parts the hair, a hair-pin , Hier. Ruf. 3, 42 .—Also, subst. : , , , a head-dress , Vulg. lsa. 3, 20.

discrīmĭnātim.opening: adv. id. , with a difference or distinction (very rare), Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 7 .

discrīmĭnātĭo.opening: id. , rhet. t. t., = παραδιαστολή , the contrasting of opposite thoughts , Rufin. Schem. lex. § 20.

discrīmĭnātor.opening: id. , one who distinguishes or discriminates (late Lat) = distinctor, Aug. ap. Joann. 20, 12.

discrīmĭnātrix.opening: discriminator , she who distinguishes (late Lat.): fandi ac nefandi, Nazar. Pan. ad Const. 7 .

discrīmĭno.opening: v. a. discrimen , to divide, part, separate (very rare; cf. divido, dispertio): aliquid, Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 4 : Etruriam discriminat Cassia, * Cic. Phil. 12, 9 : late agros, Verg. A. 11, 144 : crinem, Vulg. Jud. 10, 3…

discrīmĭnōsĭus.opening: adv. comp. [id.], more decisively , Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 2, 24 .

dīscriptio.opening: discribo , a division, distribution, apportionment : civitatis, Cic. Sest. 65, 137 : populi, id. Planc. 18, 45 : privatarum possessionum, id. Off. 1, 7, 21 ; id. Tusc. 4, 1, 1 ; 5, 24, 68 ; id. Rep. 1, 46, 70 ; id. N.…

discrŭcĭātus.opening: violent torture, torment , Prud. Ham. 836 . From

dis-crŭcĭo.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. a. , to torture violently, to torment (repeatedly in Plaut. and Cic.; elsewh. rare). Physically: aliquem discruciatum necare, Cic. Phil. 13, 18, 37 ; Amm. 27, 12, 3 .—More freq., Mentally, with…

discŭbĭtĭo.opening: discumbo , a place for lying down, a couch , Inscr. Orell. 2106 .

discŭbĭtus.opening: id. , a reclining at table , Val. Max. 2, 1, 9 .— Transf. , a place at table : amare primos discubitus, Vulg. Luc. 20, 46 al.

dis-culcĭo.opening: v. a. calceo , to unshoe, remove the shoe from , Diom. 374 P.

dis-cumbo.opening: v. n. , to lie down . More freq., to recline at table for the purpose of eating (cf. accumbo—so esp. freq. since the Aug. per.): discubuimus omnes praeter illam, Cic. Att. 5, 1, 4 ; Lucr. 3, 912 ; Quint. 11, 2, 13 ;…

dis-cŭnĕātus.opening: adj., wedged apart, kept asunder as by a wedge : conchae, Plin. 9, 30, 48, § 90 .

dis-cŭpĭo.opening: v. n. (in famil. lang. for vehementer cupio), to desire greatly, to long for : discupio dicere, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 87 : te videre, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 15, 2 : se vendere, Cat. 106, 2 .

dis-curro.opening: ( perf. discucurri, Liv. 25, 25, 9 ; Sen. Contr. 4, 2 ; Suet. Calig. 32 : discurrisse, Curt. 4, 15, 5 ; oftener curri, Liv. 34, 37 ; 3, 7, 32 ; Sen. Ep. 90, 36 ; Curt. 4, 15, 10 al. ), , v. n. To run different ways, to…

discursātĭo.opening: discurso , a running hither and thither, a running about (post-Aug. and rare): officiosa per urbem, Sen. Brev. Vit. 3 : magna, Front. Strat. 1, 5 fin. : animalium, Lact. Opif. D. 3 .

discursātor.opening: id. , one who runs hither and thither, one who runs about (late Lat.): pedites et leves, Amm. 16, 12, 21 ; cf. hostis, id. 29, 5, 7 ; 14, 2, 6 .

discursim.opening: adv. discurro , by running or going about , Macr. S. 7, 1, 1 (dub.); Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 1, 51 .

discursĭo.opening: id. , a running different ways, scattering (late Lat.): discursiones predatoriae, scattered raids for plunder, foragings, Amm. 15, 4, 11 .— A hasty passing through : discursione rapidā maturabant, Amm. 31, 9, 2 .

discurso.grammar: āre v. freq. a. and n.
discurso.opening: v. freq. a. and n. id. . Neutr., to run about, hasten up and down (post - Aug. and rare): multum in agendo discursantem, salientem, etc.... non agere dixit (Domitius Afer) sed satagere, Quint. 6, 3, 54 ; cf. id. 11, 3,…

discursor.opening: id. , one who runs about , (Pseud.) Augustin. ad Frat. Erem. Serm. 5.

discursus.opening: discurro . A running to and fro, a running about (mostly post-class.): magno clamore discursuque passim fugae se mandant, Hirt. B. G. 8, 29, 2 ; Liv. 25, 25 ; Quint. 1, 12, 10 ; Plin. Ep. 1, 9, 7 ; Ov. F. 2, 223 ; Juv.…

discus.opening: , = δίσκος . A quoit , an implement for exercise in ancient gymnastics, Stat. Th. 6, 646 sq. ; Prop. 3, 14, 10 (4, 13, 10 M.); Hor. C. 1, 8, 11 ; id. S. 2, 2, 13 ; id. A. P. 380 ; Ov. M. 10, 177 al. — Prov.: qui discum…

Discus.opening: the name of a freedman , Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 60 .

discussē.opening: adv., minutely, accurately , etc., v. discutio fin.

discussĭo.opening: discutio (very rare). A shaking , Sen. Q. N. 6, 19, 2 .— An examination, discussion . In gen. (late Lat. for disputatio, quaestio): sequitur illa discussio, quid sit, etc., Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 16, 8 ; Tert. Pudic. 11…

discussor.opening: id. , an examiner (late Lat.). In gen., Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 21, 8 .— In partic., in the later period of the empire, one who revised the accounts of the public revenue in the provinces, an auditor , Gr. λογοθέτης , Cod.…

discussōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , discutient, dissolving : vis, Plin. 30, 8, 22, § 75 .

discussus.opening: discutio , a dashing, agitating : (lupus) si haesit in hamo, tumultuoso discussu laxat volnera, Plin. 32, 2, 5, § 13 .

dis-cŭtĭo.opening: v. a. quatio , to strike asunder, dash to pieces, shatter , etc. In gen.: dentes, Lucil. ap. Non. 455, 18 : deum delubra, Lucr. 6, 418 ; cf.: columna rostrata tota ad imum fulmine discussa est, Liv. 42, 20 : ne saxa ex…

disdĭăpāsōn.opening: , = δὶς διὰ πασῶν , a double octave in music, Mart. Cap. 9, § 950 ; Vitr. 5, 4, 9 al. ; cf. diapason.

dĭsertē.opening: adv., clearly , etc., v. dissero, P. a. fin. .

dĭsertim.opening: adv., clearly, expressly , etc., v. dissero, P. a. fin. .

dĭsertĭōnes.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 8 ; cf. Müll. ad h. l.

dĭsertĭtūdo.opening: disertus , eloquence (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 50 , no. 5; Vulg. Isa. 33, 19 .

dis-glūtĭno.opening: v. a. , to disjoin, disunite (late Lat.): conjuncta (with dissuere), Hier. Ep. 66 , no. 12.

dis-grĕgo.opening: v. a. , to separate, divide (opp. congrego; late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 3, § 289 ; 9, § 913 .

disgrĕgus.opening: adj. disgrego , different, unlike (with dispar), Mart. Cap. 9, § 892 .

dis-hĭasco.opening: v. n. , to gape open, to chink, chap , Cato R. R. 12 .

dīs-ĭcĭo.opening: (or , Lucr. 3, 639 ; less correctly, ), , v. a. jacio , to throw asunder; to drive asunder; to scatter, disperse (freq. in poets and historians, esp. since the Aug. per.; not in Cic., Plaut., or Ter.). In gen.: partibus…

disjecto.opening: v. freq. a. disicio , to hurl hither and thither, to scatter, disperse : disjectare solet magnum mare transtra, cavernas, etc., Lucr. 2, 553 ; id. ib. 562 ; 3, 501: conspiratas gentes, Amm. 16, 3 ; cf. id. 19, 7 .

disjectus.opening: disicio , a casting asunder, scattering , Lucr. 3, 928 .

disjunctē.opening: adv., separately, distinctly , etc., v. disjungo, P. a. fin. a.

disjunctim.opening: adv., separately , etc., v. disjungo, P. a. fin. b.

disjunctĭo.opening: or , , disjungo , a separation (a Ciceron. word). In gen.: in tanta disjunctione meorum, tanta acerbitate, Cic. Sest. 21, 47 ; cf. (amicorum), with alienatio, id. Lael. 21 : animorum disjunctio dissensionem facit, i. e.…

disjunctīvus.opening: or , , adj. id. , placed in opposition, opposed to each other (post-class.). In philos. lang.: proloquium, i. q. disjunctio (II. A.), Gell. 5, 11, 9 ; cf. ib. § 8.— In gram. lang., disjunctive, expressed with…

disjunctus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from disjungo.

dis-jungo.opening: or , , v. a. , to disjoin, disunite, separate , opp. to conjungo (freq. and class.). Lit. Esp., to unyoke draught cattle: asinum, bovem ab opere, Varr. R. R. 2, 6, 4 ; Col. 2, 3, 1 ; Plin. 18, 27, 67, § 251 : bovem…

disjurgĭum.opening: dis-jurgium , a difference, quarrel , Inscr. Orell. 3023 ; 4777 .

dismōtum.opening: , v. dimoveo init. † † , , adj. , = δίσωμος , holding two bodies : VAS, a sarcophagus for two persons, Inscr. Orell. 4548 .

dispālesco.opening: v. inch. n. [dispalor], to spread about, be noised abroad , Plaut. Bacch. 4, 9, 123 .

dis-pālor.opening: v. dep. n. , to wander about, to straggle, stray (very rare). Prop.: dispalati ab signis, Sisenn. ap. Non. 101, 6 ; id. ib. 7 ; Nep. Lys. 1, 2 ; id. Hann. 5, 2 ; Amm. 15, 3 ; 31, 2 .—* Trop. : multitudo in varias artes…

dis-pando.opening: or , no perf. , sum; also, in colloq. lang., , (in Plaut., v. the foll. ), v. a. , to stretch out, spread out, to extend, expand (very rare). Prop.: dispennite hominem divorsum et distennite, Plaut. Mil. 5, 14 :…

dis-par.opening: adj., unlike, dissimilar, different, unequal (freq. and class.; cf.: impar, dissimilis, absimilis). Absol. : dispares mores disparia studia sequentur, quorum dissimilitudo dissociat amicitias, Cic. Lael. 20, 74 : cf.…

dispărasco.opening: v. n. dispar , to be unlike , Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 3, 9 med. dub.

dispărātĭo.opening: disparo , a separation : procreationis, i. e. a delivery, Vitr. 2, 9 : brevis, Amm. 21, 12, 8 .

dis-părĭlis.opening: adj., dissimilar, different (very rare): pabulum, Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 4 : formae, id. L. L. 9, § 40 Müll.: aspiratio terrarum, * Cic. Div. 1, 36, 79 : vites, Col. 3, 2, 17 : ictus errantium siderum, Plin. 2, 45, 45, §…

dispărĭlĭtas.opening: disparilis , dissimilarity, difference (ante- and post-class. and very rare): vocis, Varr. L. L. 10, § 36 Müll.: rerum, Gell. praef. § 3: collationis, id. 7, 3, 47 .

dispărĭlĭter.opening: adv., differently, dissimilarly , v. disparilis fin.

dis-păro.opening: v. a. , to part, separate, divide (rare but class.). In gen.: Juppiter nos per gentes alium alia disparat, Plaut. Rud. prol. 10 : (Servius Tullius) seniores a junioribus divisit, eosque ita disparavit, ut, etc., Cic.…

dispartĭbĭlis.opening: adj. dispartio , divisible; coupled with demutabilis (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Hermog. 39 .

dispatens.opening: P. a. dis-pateo , opening in different directions : latibula sibi parant in plures exitus dispatentia, Lact. 3, 10, 3 .

dispectĭo.opening: dispicio , a viewing, considering : tituli, Tert. Res Carn. 19 .

dispecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to consider, contemplate, examine : momenta, Arn. 1, p. 13 .

dispector.opening: id. , one who considers, examines, a searcher (eccl. Lat.): cordis Deus, Tert. Anim. 15 : alienarum sententiarum, id. ad Uxor. 2, 8 .

dispectus.opening: dispicio , regard, consideration, examination , Sen. de Ira, 2, 9, 2; id. Ep. 94 med.

dis-pello.opening: v. a. , to drive asunder, to scatter, disperse (rare but class.). Lit. : dispulsa suo de coetu materiaï Copia, Lucr. 1, 1017 : pecudes dispulsae, Cic. Att. 7, 7, 7 : ater quos aequore turbo Dispulerat, Verg. A. 1, 512 ;…

dispendĭōsus.opening: adj. dispendium , hurtful, prejudicial (post-Aug. and very rare): cunctatio, Col. 2, 20, 1 : occasiones, Cod. Theod. 11, 2, 4 al.

dispendĭum.opening: dispendo (opp compendium, v. 3, dis, II.), expense, cost, loss (mostly ante- and post-class.; cf.: impensa, impendium, sumptus; also: noxa, damnum, detrimentum, jactura, incommodum). Lit. : dispendium ideo, quod in…

dispensātĭo.opening: dispenso . Economical management, charge, direction, superintendence . Lit. : aerarii, Cic. Vatin. 15, 36 .— Transf. : annonae, Liv. 10, 11 ; cf. id. 4, 12 fin. : est autem in eximendis favis necessaria dispensatio,…

dispensātīvus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to management or administratorship : philosophia, Isid. Orig. 2, 24, 16 .— Adv. : , in the manner of an administrator, in substitution , Hier. Ep. 112, 14 .

dispensātor.opening: id. , a household superintendent, a manager, steward; as manager of the imperial treasury, a cashier, treasurer , διοικητής ; usually the most trustworthy slaves, but under the emperors sometimes ingenui (v. Orell. on…

dispensātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , relating to management or control (late Lat.), Hier. in Ies. 14, 53, 12 .

dispensātrix.opening: dispensator , she that dispenses, a female steward , Hier. Quaest. Hebr. in Paralip. 8 ; Inscr. Murat. 968, 9 .

dis-penso.opening: v. freq. a. Orig. of money, to distribute by weight, to disburse, pay out (for syn. cf.: partior, impertio, distribuo, divido): ducentos nummos (sc. inter milites), Plaut. Bacch. 4, 9, 47 .— In gen., to manage, regulate…

dis-percŭtĭo.opening: v. a. , to dash out : cerebrum, Plaut. Cas. 3, 5, 18 .

dis-perdo.opening: v. a. , to destroy, spoil, ruin (rare but class.): bibe, es, disperde rem, Plaut. Cas. 2, 3, 32 ; cf. id. Trin. 2, 2, 58 : ut a majoribus nostris possessiones relictas disperdat et dissipet, * Cic. Agr. 1, 1, 2 :…

dis-pĕrĕo.opening: v. n. , to go completely to ruin, to be lost or undone, to perish (rare; mostly ante-class.): quin prius disperibit faxo, quam unam calcem civerit, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 86 : fructus dispereunt, Varr. R. R. 1, 11, 1 ; cf.…

di-spergo.opening: , in late Lat. and sometimes in MSS. of the older authors written (cf. aspergo and conspergo), si, sum, 3, v. a. , to scatter on all sides, to scatter about, disperse (freq. and class., esp. in the part. perf. ). Lit. :…

di-sperno.opening: v. a. , to despise : jussa, Juvenc. 2, 257 .

dispersĭo.opening: dispergo , a scattering, dispersion . In gen. Act. : exercitus, Isid. 18, 2, 7 : populi, gentis, Tert. adv. Jud. 13 : gentium, Vulg. Johan. 7, 35 . — Pass. : pascentium equorum, Veg. Mil. 3, 8 .— Transf. Destruction :…

dis-pertĭo.opening: (in many MSS. also , Liv. 3, 10, 9 ; Nep. Eum. 2 ), īvi or ii, ītum, 4 ( arch. inf. pass. : dispertirier, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 26 ), v. a. partio , to distribute, divide (class.). Lit. : dispertiti viri, dispertiti ordines,…

dispertītĭo.opening: dispertio , a division, destruction : urbis, Cic. Phil. 3, 12, 30 fin. (where disperditio is a false reading, but v. dispersio); Tert. adv. Herm. 31 .

dis-pesco.opening: (pescui, acc. to Prisc. p. 885 P.), , v. a. commonly referred to pasco; lit., to take from the pasture (pecus a pastione deducere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 11), but more probably from root pac-, παγ- of Gr. πήγνυμι, to…

di-spĭcĭo.grammar: spexi, spectum, 3 v. n. and a.
di-spĭcĭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to see through all parts (cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. vol. 2, p. 236 and 237), to see with an effort, to open wide the eyes in order to see, to look through, to see; to glance, to gaze; and actively, to descry,…

dis-plāno.opening: v. a. , to level away, to level : rutro caput, Varr. ap. Non. 18, 25 .

dis-plĭcātus.opening: Part. [plico], scattered, dispersed : apes, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 7 .

displĭcentĭa.opening: displiceo , dissatisfaction, discontent : sui (with taedium), Sen. Tranq. An. 2, 8 .— Med. t. t., indisposition : corporis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 6, 86 ; 5, 10, 96 .

dis-plĭcĕo.opening: (displicitus est, Gell. 1, 21, 4 ), , v. n. placeo , to displease (opp. placeo and complaceo, v. 3. dis, II. —rare but class.): quodne vobis placeat, displiceat mihi? Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 19 ; so opp. placere, id. Men. 4,…

dis-plĭco.opening: v. a. , to scatter , Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 7 .

dis-plōdo.opening: , no perf. , ōsum, 3, v. a. , to spread out, dilate, extend (for the most part only ante- and post-class., and in the part. perf.; in class. prose not at all): pedibus magnis, et altis, qui ingredienti ei displodantur,…

displŭvĭāta.opening: (cava aedium) sunt, in quibus deliquiae arcam sustinentes stillicidia reiciunt, i. e. of which the rain-water runs off on both sides of the walls , Vitr. 6, 3 .

di-spŏlĭo.opening: v. a. , to plunder, spoil utterly : templum lunae Ephesiae, Treb. Poll. Gallien. 6, 2; also as var. lect. for despolio, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 20, § 43 , v. Zumpt ad h. l.

di-spondēus.opening: , = δισπόνδειος , a double spondee ¯¯¯¯, Diomed. p. 476 P.; Don. p. 1739 ib. et saep.

dis-pōno.opening: (contr. dispostum, Lucr. 1, 52 ; 2, 644 ), 3, v. a. , to place here and there, to set in different places, to distribute regularly, to dispose, arrange (cf. dispenso, II.—freq. and class.). Lit. In gen., to set in…

dispŏsĭtĭo.opening: dispono . A regular disposition, arrangement , in oratory, Cic. Inv. 1, 7, 9 ; id. de Or. 2, 42, 179 ; Auct. Her. 1, 2, 3 ; 3, 10, 18 ; Quint. 3, 3, 1 sq. et saep.; in arch., Vitr. 1, 2 ; in painting, Plin. 35, 10, 36,…

dispŏsĭtor.opening: id. , a disposer, arranger : mundi deus, Sen. Q. N. 5, 18, 4 : rerum naturae (of the Λογος ), Lact. 4, 9, 2 .

dispŏsĭtūra.opening: id. , a disposition, arrangement , perh. only Lucr. 1, 1027 ; 5, 192 .

dispŏsĭtus.opening: id. , a disposition, arrangement : dispositu civilium rerum peritus, Tac. H. 2, 5 .

dis-pŭdet.opening: v. impers. , to be greatly ashamed (perh. only in foll. passages): alia memorare dispudet, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 77 ; id. Most. 5, 2, 44 ; Ter. Eun. 5, 1, 16 .—With genit. : non vos tot calumniarum tandem dispudet? App.…

dis-pulvĕro.opening: v. a. , to reduce to powder, pulverize : saxa, etc., Naev. ap. Non. 95, 28 (Com. Fragm. v. 57 Rib.).

dispunctĭo.opening: dispungo , a settling up, balancing of accounts (late Lat.). Lit. : concedenda creditoribus (with recognitio), Dig. 42, 5, 15 .— Trop. , an investigation, examination, a testing : boni et mali operis, Tert. adv. Marc.…

dispunctor.opening: id. , an examiner, investigator : meritorum (with judex), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 17 .

dis-pungo.opening: v. a. In postAug. mercant. lang., to check off the debits and credits of an account; hence, to examine, revise, settle, balance an account: dispungere est conferre accepta et data, Dig. 50, 16, 56 . Lit. : rationes…

dispŭtābĭlis.opening: adj. disputo , that may be disputed, disputable : omnis res in utramque partem, Sen. Ep. 88, 43 .

dispŭtātĭo.opening: id. . * A computing, calculating, considering (cf.: commentatio, dissertatio): venire in disputationem, Col. 5, 1 fin. —Far more freq., An arguing, reasoning, disputing; and concr., an argument, debate, dispute (cf.:…

dispŭtātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. disputatio , a short discussion, trivial dispute , Sen. Ep. 117 med. ; Gell. 1, 3 fin.

dispŭtātīvus.opening: adj. disputo , pertaining to a dispute : intentiones, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 9, 19 .— Adv. : , in the way of discussion or dispute : dicere aliquid, ib. 5, 42 .

dispŭtātor.opening: id. , a disputer, disputant (rare): subtilis, * Cic. Off. 1, 1, 3 : suae artis unumquemque et auctorem et disputatorem optimum esse, Val. Max. 8, 12 init.

dispŭtātōrĭe.opening: adv. disputator , in the manner of disputants , Sid. Ep. 9, 9 .

dispŭtātrix.opening: id. , a female disputant, one given to disputation : etiam virtus erit, Quint. 2, 20, 7 ; as the Lat. equivalent of διαλεκτική (sc. τέχνη ), the art of disputing , id. 12, 2, 13 .

dis-pŭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
dis-pŭto.opening: v. n. and a. Orig. in mercant. lang., to cast or reckon up, to calculate a sum by going over its items; to estimate, compute : ubi disputata est ratio cum argentario, Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 55 .— Transf. beyond the mercant.…

dis-quīro.opening: v. a. quaero , to inquire diligently , to investigate , Hor. S. 2, 2, 7 ; Claud. Laud. Stil. 1, 239 ; Lampr id. Alex. Sev. 16, 2 ; Vulg. 2 Macc. 2, 31 .

disquīsītĭo.opening: disquiro , a (judicial) inquiry , investigation : in magnis disquisitionibus repentinisque periculis, * Cic. Sull. 28, 79 ; Liv. 8, 23 ; 26, 31 ; Tac. A. 3, 60 ; 5, 11 ; Suet. Caes. 15 ; id. Ner. 2 .

dis-rāro.opening: or , , v. a. In econom. lang., to thin out , to make thin by cutting, Col. 4, 32, 4 ; 5, 6, 36 .— Transf. Of nutriment, to thin , dilute , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 15, 152 .— Of the body, to cause to perspire excessively ,…

dissaepīmentum.opening: ( ), , dissaepio , that which separates , a partition , Fest. p. 166, 12 Müll.

dis-saepĭo.opening: (less correctly ), , v. a. , to part off by a boundary, to separate , divide (very rare). Lit. : aër dissaepit colles, atque aëra montes, Lucr. 1, 998 ; cf. parietibus, Varr. L. L. 5, § 162 Müll.: vix ea limitibus…

dissaeptĭo.opening: dissaepio , a partition , Vitr. 2, 8, 20 .— Transf. : velut dissaeptio juris humani, Liv. 41, 24, 10 Hertz (dub. Madv. discerptio; Weissenb. dissertio).

dissaeptum.opening: id. , a barrier , partition : saxea domorum, Lucr. 6, 951 ; so too of the diaphragm: quod ventrem et cetera intestina secernit, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, § 77 .

dis-sĕco.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to cut asunder , cut in pieces , cut up , dissect (post-Aug.; esp. freq. in Pliny the elder— cf.: seco, meto, findo, scindo): unionem, Plin. 9, 35, 58, § 121 : pectus, id. 11, 37, 70, § 185 : caput…

dissēmĭnātĭo.opening: dissemino , a scattering of seed , a sowing , disseminating (post-class.): evangelii, Tert. Fuga in Persec. 6 .—In plur. : malevolorum, App. M. 11 fin.

dissēmĭnātor.opening: id. , one who spreads abroad : incontinentiae, Ambros. in Psa. 36, 49 .

dis-sēmĭno.opening: v. a. — Lit. , to scatter seed, to sow; hence, trop., to spread abroad , disseminate (rare, but good prose); coupled with spargere, Cic. Arch. 12, 30 ; cf. id. Planc. 23, 56 : malum latius opinione, id. Cat. 4, 3 fin. :…

dissensĭo.opening: dissentio , difference of opinion , disagreement , dissension , discord (good prose): inter homines de jure, Cic. de Or. 1, 56, 238 ; cf. id. Leg. 2, 13, 32 : animorum disjunctio dissensionem facit, id. Agr. 2, 6 :…

dissensus.opening: dissentio , dissension , disagreement , discord ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose), Verg. A. 11, 455 ; Stat. Th. 10, 558 ; Dig. 17, 2, 65, § 3 ; 46, 3, 80 .

dissentānĕus.opening: adj. id. , disagreeing , contrary , dissentaneous (opp. consentaneus, Cic. Part. Or. 2, 7 ; cf. Nigid. ap. Non. 100, 7 .

dis-sentĭo.opening: v. n. (opp. consentio), to differ in sentiment , to dissent , disagree (freq. and class.).—Constr. usually ab aliquo; less freq. inter se , cum aliquo , the dat. or absol : soles nonnumquam hac de re a me in…

dissēpărātĭo.opening: disseparo , a parting , separation (late Lat.), Auct. Decl. in Catil. 31.

dis-sēpăro.opening: v. a. , to part , divide (late Lat.), Nazar. Paneg. Const. 2 : acus quae capillos a medio, fronte disseparat, Non. 282, 19 .

dissĕrēnasco.opening: v. inch. n. impers. [dissereno], to clear up , grow clear : cum undique disserenāsset, Liv. 39, 46, 4 .

dis-sĕrēno.opening: v. impers. and a. Impers. , to be clear , as if by dispersing the clouds: si cacumina (montium) pura flent, disserenabit, Plin. 18, 35, 82, § 356 .— In late Lat., act. , to make clear. —Only trop., to clear away :…

dis-sĕro.opening: ( part. perf. disserta, first in Hier. in Isa. 4, 11 ; class. form dĭsertus, as a P. a. , is very freq.; v. under P. a. ), , v. a. — Lit. , to set forth in order, arrange distinctly; hence, to examine , argue , discuss;…

dis-serpo.opening: v. n. , to creep about , to spread imperceptibly : late disserpunt tremores, Lucr. 6, 547 .

dissertātĭo.opening: disserto , a spoken dissertation , discourse , disquisition (not a written treatise; cf. disputatio; late Lat.), Gell. 1, 2, 6 ; 10, 4, 1 ; 14, 3, 5 (in Plin. 10, 68, 87, § 190 , the true reading is edissertatio) al.

dissertĭo.opening: 2. dissero , destruction , abolition : cur exsecrabilis ista nobis solis velut dissertio juris humani est? Liv. 41, 24, 10 (dub., this not being the etym. sense of the word; al. dissaeptio, discerptio).— The explanation…

disserto.opening: v. freq. a. dissero , to discuss , argue , debate a thing; or to dispute , converse , treat respecting a thing (ante-class. and post-Aug., esp. in Tac.): quid ego cum illo dissertem amplius? Cato ap. Paul. ex Fest. p.…

dis-sĭdĕo.opening: v. n. sedeo , to sit apart , to be remote from , to be divided , separated. Lit. (only poet. and very rare): quantum Hypanis dissidet Eridano, Prop. 1, 12, 4 : sceptris nostris, * Verg. A. 7, 370 : ab omni dissidet…

dissidium.opening: , q. v., and cf. Madv. ad Cic. Fin. Exc. II. p. 812 sq.

dissignātĭo.opening: , another form for designatio, q. v., Tab. Heracl. p. 53 al.

dis-sĭlĭo.opening: v. n. salio , to leap or burst asunder , to fly apart. Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): duo de concursu corpora lata si cita dissiliant, Lucr. 1, 385 ; cf. id. 1, 391 ; 2, 87 : dissiliunt ferventi saxa vapore, id.…

dis-sĭmĭlis.opening: adj. , unlike , dissimilar , different (as the opp. of similis and consimilis, v. 3. dis, II.; cf.: dispar, impar, absimilis; very freq. and class.).—Constr. with the gen. , dat. , with atque , et , inter se , or absol.…

dissĭmĭlĭtūdo.opening: dissimilis , unlikeness , difference , dissimilitude (very freq. in sing. and plur. ); sing. , Cic. Lael. 20, 74 ; id. de Or. 1, 59, 252 ; id. Fin. 5, 7, 19 ; id. Leg. 1, 10, 30 ; Quint. 5, 2, 3 ; 9, 3, 92 et saep.;…

dissĭmŭlāmentum.opening: dissimulo , a dissembling , pretence (post-class.), App. Flor. no. 3, p. 341, 21; id. Mag. p. 329, 9 .

dissĭmŭlanter.opening: adv. , dissemblingly , secretly , etc., v. dissimulo fin.

dissĭmŭlantĭa.opening: dissimulo , a dissembling : coupled with ironia, Cic. de Or. 2, 67, 270 .

dissĭmŭlātĭo.opening: id. , a dissembling , concealing , disguising , dissimulation (good prose). In gen., Cic. Off. 3, 15 ; id. de Or. 2, 67 ; Quint. 6, 3, 85 ; Tac. A. 11, 26 : veste servili in dissimulationem sui compositus, id. ib. 13,…

dissĭmŭlātor.opening: id. , a dissembler , concealer , Sall. C. 5, 4 ; Quint. 2, 2, 5 ; Tac. H. 2, 56 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 9, 9 al.

dissĭmŭlo.opening: v. a. dissimilis , to feign that a thing is not that which it is; to dissemble , disguise; to hide , conceal , keep secret (cf.: fingo, simulo, confingo, comminiscor—very freq. and class.). With acc. : nihil fingam,…

dissĭpābĭlis.opening: adj. dissipo , that may be scattered or dispersed : ignis et aër, Cic. N. D. 3, 12, 31 .

dissĭpātĭo.opening: id. , a scattering , dispersing (a Ciceronian word). * In gen.: hic error ac dissipatio civium, Cic. Rep. 2, 4, 7 .— Pregn., destruction , annihilation : interitus et dissipatio corporum, Cic. N. D. 1, 25, 71 : praedae,…

dissĭpātor.opening: id. , a disperser , destroyer , Prud. Psych. 34 praef.

dissĭpātrix.opening: dissipator , she who scatters or destroys : vitiorum, August. Serm. 30 .

dis-sĭpo.opening: , acc. to many MSS., , ( part. perf. in the tmesis : disque supatis, Lucr. 1, 651 ), , v. a. SUPO = jacio, v. the art. † supat; hence, i. q. disicio , to spread abroad , scatter , disperse (very freq. and class., esp.…

dis-sĭtus.opening: adj. , lying apart , remote (an Appuleian word), opp. assitus, App. Flor. init. p. 340: femora, i. q. divaricata, id. M. 7, p. 198, 13 .

dissŏcĭābĭlis.opening: adj. dissocio . * Act. , separating , dividing : Oceanus, Hor. C. 1, 3, 22 .— Pass. , that cannot be united , irreconcilable , incompatible : olim res miscere, Tac. Agr. 3 : corpus, Claud. in Ruf. 2, 238 .

dissŏcĭālis.opening: adj. id. , irreconcilable , repugnant : humanis animal dissociale cibis (of the Jews who separate themselves in respect to food), Rutil. Itin. 1, 384 .

dissŏcĭātĭo.opening: id. , a separation (post-Aug.), Plin. 6, 1, 1, § 2 ; 7, 13, 11, § 57 ; Tac. A. 16, 34 .

dis-sŏcĭo.opening: v. a. , to separate from fellowship , to disjoin , disunite. Lit. (almost exclusively poet. ): artas partis, Lucr. 5, 355 ; cf.: dissociata locis concordi pace ligavit, Ov. M. 1, 25 : montes opaca valle, * Hor. Ep. 1,…

dissŏlūbĭlis.opening: adj. dissolvo , that may be dissolved , dissoluble : mortale omne animal et dissolubile et dividuum sit necesse est, Cic. N. D. 3, 12, 29 : coagmentatio, id. ib. 1, 8, 20 ; Lact. 2, 8, 39 ; 4, 8, 10 .— Comp. :…

dissŏlūte.opening: adv. , loosely , disconnectedly; laxly , negligently , carelessly; v. dissolvo, P. a. fin.

dissŏlūtĭo.opening: dissolvo , a dissolving , destroying , breaking up , dissolution (good prose). Lit. : navigii, Tac. A. 14, 5 : naturae (mors), Cic. Leg. 1, 11 ; id. Fin. 5, 11, 31 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 31 : stomachi, i. e. looseness, Plin.…

dissŏlūtor.opening: id. , a destroyer (late Lat.): sepulcrorum, Cod. Th. 3, 16, 1; Cod. Just. 5, 17, 8 .

dissŏlūtrix.opening: dissolutor , she who destroys , a destroyer : corporis (mors), Tert. Anim. 42 .

dissŏlūtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from dissolvo.

dis-solvo.opening: v. a. , to loosen asunder , to unloose , disunite , separate , dissolve , destroy (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: facilius est apta dissolvere quam dissipata conectere, Cic. Or. 71, 235 : opus ipsa suum eadem quae…

dissŏnanter.opening: adv. dissono , inharmoniously , inconsistently , August. Genes. ad Lit. 4, 33 .

dissŏnantĭa.opening: id. , dissonance , discrepancy (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. de Stat. An. 2, 21 .

dis-sŏno.opening: v. n. , to disagree in sound , to be dissonant , opp. consono (very rare; not ante-Aug.). Lit. : dissonantes loci, that produce discordant sounds, Vitr. 5, 8, 1 .— Trop. , to disagree , to differ : an universa hujus…

dis-sŏnus.opening: adj. , opp. consonus, dissonant , discordant , confused (not anteAug.; nor in Verg., Ov., or Hor.). Lit. : chorus canentium dissonum quiddam canere, Col. 12, 2, 4 ; so, clamores, Liv. 4, 28 ; Plin. Ep. 3, 20, 4 : voces…

dis-sors.opening: adj. (opp. consors), of a different fate , separate , apart , not shared : ab omni milite dissors Gloria, undivided, unshared, Ov. Am. 2, 12, 11 : dissortemque utero fetum tulit, id. M. 8, 133 (Heins.; al. discordem, v.…

dis-suādĕo.opening: v. a. —A pub. law t. t., to advise against , dissuade , oppose by argument , resist a proposition. Prop. (class.). With acc. : quis enim umquam tam secunda contione legem agrariam suasit, quam ego dissuasi? Cic. Agr. 2,…

dissuāsĭo.opening: dissuadeo , an advising to the contrary; a dissuasion (very rare): rogationis ejus, * Cic. Clu. 51, 140 ; so opp. suasio, Auct. Her. 1, 2 .—In plur. , Sen. Ep. 94, 39 .

dissuāsor.opening: id. , one who advises to the contrary , an opposer (very rare), Cic. de Or. 2, 65, 261 ; Liv. 2, 41 ; Luc. 4, 248 al.

dis-suāvĭor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. a. , to kiss ardently : tuos oculos, Q. Cic. in Cic. Fam. 16, 27 fin.

dis-suesco.opening: v. n. , to disuse , to become disused or unaccustomed to (late Lat.), Alcim. Avit. 4, 46 .

dis-suētūdo.opening: a becoming unaccustomed , disusing , Ambros. de Cain et Abel. 2, 6, 22.

dissulcus.grammar: porcus dicitur, cum in cervice setas dividit

dissulto.opening: v. freq. n. [dissilio], to leap apart , to fly in pieces , burst asunder ( poet. , and in post-Aug. prose): dissultant ripae, Verg. A. 8, 240 : tanti crepitus, id. ib. 12, 923 : ferrum utrimque, Plin. 37, 4, 15, § 57 :…

dis-sŭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. — Lit. , to unstitich , to rip open; hence, in gen., to open , to dissolve by degrees (a rare word). Lit. : sinum, Ov. F. 1, 408 : malas, to open the mouth wide, Pers. 3, 59 : habebit vestimenta…

dis-tābesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to consume or melt away (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : distabescit sal, Cato R. R. 24 ; so, jecur in coquendo, Fest. S. V. MONSTRA, p. 157, 14 Müll.: suspirium in aqua, Veg. Vet. 1, 11, 13 .— Trop. : in…

dis-taedet.opening: , † tisum (acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 18 ), 2, v. impers. , to be very tired of , disgusted with , to loathe (very rare): haud quod tui me neque domi distaedeat, Plaut. Am. 1, 3, 5 : me cum hoc ipso distaedet loqui,…

distantĭa.opening: disto , distance , remoteness. Lit. : a longissimis distantiae suae (sc. Veneris) finibus, Plin. 2, 15, 12, § 61 — Transf. , a separation , opening : oris hiscens, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 5, 50 . — Trop. , difference ,…

dis-tectus.opening: adj. dis and tego , uncovered , Alcim. Avit. 4, 408 .

di-stĕgus.opening: adj. δίστεγος , of two stories , having two apartments : armarium, Inscr. Orell. 4549 .— Subst. : , , (sc. armarium), Inscr. Grut. 292, 1 al.

dis-tendo.opening: (and vulg. ), (in late Lat. also distensus, Coripp. Joann. 7, 324; but in Auct. B. Alex. 45, 2, the right reading is dispersis), , v. a. , to stretch asunder , stretch out , extend (not freq. till after the Aug. per.;…

distentĭo.opening: distendo , a stretching out , distention (very rare), Cels. 2, 4 ; 8, 4 ; Scrib. Comp. 89 .— Trop. , fullness , i. e. occupation , Vulg. Eccl. 8, 16 .

distentus.opening: distendo , a swelling out , distention : subflatae cutis distentu, Plin. 8, 38, 57, § 138 .

distermĭnātĭo.opening: a separation , division , Simplic. p. 83 Goes.

distermĭnātor.opening: distermino , a separator , divider : axis disterminator mundi, App. de Mundo, p. 57.

dis-termĭno.opening: v. a. , to separate by a boundary , to divide , limit , part (rare; mostly post-Aug.): quas (sterlas) intervallum binas disterminat unum, Cic. Arat. 94 : Hispanias Galliasque Pyrenaei montes, Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 30 :…

distermĭnus.opening: adj. dis-terminus , separated , divided : Tartessos latis distermina terris, Sil. 5, 399 .— Act. , separating , parting. —As subst. : , , (sc. linea), the diameter , diagonal , Mart. Cap. 6, § 714 .

di-sterno.opening: v. a. , to spread out : lectum, i. e. to make, prepare, App. M. 10, p. 256, 7 .— Impers. : extra limen pueris distratum fuerat, id. ib. 2 , p. 121, 25.

dis-tĕro.opening: v. a. , to bruise or grind to pieces. * Lit. : caseum in mortario, Cato R. R. 75 .—* Trop. : aliquem clunibus basiisque, Petr. 24, 4 .

dis-texo.opening: v. a. , to unravel , ravel out , Sid. C. 15, 161 .

distĭchus.opening: adj. , = δίστιχος , consisting of two rows. Adj. : hordeum, Col. 2, 9, 16 .— Subst. † , , , a building with two stories or two rows of chambers , Inscr. Fabr. p. 627 , no. 234.— , , , a poem of two verses , a distich…

di-stĭmŭlo.opening: v. a. , to goad through; transf.: bona, i. e. to run through, waste, consume, Plaut. Bacch. 1, 1, 30 .

distincte.opening: adv. , distinctly , clearly; handsomely , etc., v. distinguo, P. a. fin.

distinctĭo.opening: distinguo . (Acc. to distinguo, I. B.) In gen. Subject., a distinguishing , discriminating , a distinction : harum rerum facilis est et expedita distinctio, Cic. Fin. 1, 10, 33 ; so, facilis ingenui et illiberalis…

distinctor.opening: id. , one who distinguishes (late Lat.): justorum injustorumque (judices), Amm. 22, 3 ; 18, 1, 2 ; Aug. in Joann. 20, 12 .

distinctus.opening: distinguo , a distinguishing , distinction; object., a difference (post-Aug. and very rare): distinctu pinnarum, * Tac. A. 6, 28 ; cf. Stat. S. 1, 5, 41 .

dis-tĭnĕo.opening: v. a. teneo . To keep asunder , to separate , divide. Lit. : tigna binis utrimque fibulis ab extrema parte distinebantur, Caes. B. G. 4, 17, 7 ; Vitr. 3, 3 : mare, quod late terrarum distinet oras, Lucr. 5, 203 ; 5, 690…

di-stinguo.opening: v. a. root in Sanscr. tegami, to be sharp; Gr. στίζω, στίγμα; Lat. stimulus stilus, in-stigare, etc. . —Prop., to separate by points; hence, in gen., To separate , divide , part. Lit. (very rare, and almost exclusively…

di-sto.opening: ( perf. distiti, only Boëth. in Porphyr. 4, p. 89), v. n. , to stand apart , to be separate , distant (freq. and class.). Lit. (cf. absum), absol. : quantum summa labra (fossae) distabant, Caes. B. G. 7, 72, 1 ; cf. id.…

dis-torquĕo.opening: ( supine , distorsum acc. to Prisc. 871 P.), , v. a. , to turn different ways , to twist , distort (rare but class.). Prop.: os, Ter. Eun. 4, 4, 3 ; so, ora cachinno, Ov. A. A. 3, 287 : oculos, Hor. S. 1, 9, 65 : labra,…

distorsĭo.opening: distorqueo , perversion , perverse conduct , Aug. in Psa. 66, 7 .

distortĭo.opening: id. , a distorting , writhing , contortion : membrorum, Cic. Tusc. 4, 13, 29 ; cf. id. Fin. 5, 12, 35 : oris, Cels. 4, 2, 2 .

distortus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from distorqueo.

distractĭo.opening: distraho , a pulling asunder , dividing , separating. In gen. Lit. : distractio cruciatusque membrorum, Gell. 12, 5, 3 .— Transf. , a parting , dividing : humanorum animorum, Cic. N. D. 1, 11, 27 : animi corporisque,…

distractor.opening: id. I. . One who worries , a tormenter : improbus (i. e. Achilles), Anthol. Lat. 1, 93, 1 .— A retailer , Cod. Th. 11, 1, 4: argenti, i. e. a money-changer, id. Just. 8, 14, 27 ; 12, 35 al.

distractus.opening: distraho , dissolution of a contract , opp. to contractus, Just. Inst. 3, 27, § 6 .

dis-trăho.opening: v. a. To pull asunder , tear in pieces , to separate forcibly , divide (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: corpus quod dirimi distrahive non possit, Cic. N. D. 3, 12 ; cf. id. Tusc. 1, 29, 71 : exanimor, feror, differor,…

dis-trĭbŭo.opening: v. a. , to divide , distribute (class.; cf.: divido, impertio, dispenso, participo, communico). Lit. : argentum, Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 17 : partiendum sibi ac latius distribuendum exercitum putavit, Caes. B. G. 3, 10 fin. :…

distrĭbūtĭo.opening: distribuo , a division , distribution. In gen.: caeli, Cic. Div. 2, 20 : invidiae et criminum, id. Clu. 1 : utilis rerum ac partium in locos, Quint. 7, 1, 1 .—In plur. , Cic. Part. 2, 7 .— Esp. As a fig. of speech, the…

distrĭbūtīvus.opening: adj. id. , apportioning , distributive : nomina, Prisc. 1112 P.

distrĭbūtor.opening: id. , a distributer (post-class.), App. Trism. p. 92, 26 .

distrĭbūtrix.opening: distributor , she who apportions or distributes , Hier. in Didym. de Spir. Sanc. 23 fin.

districte.opening: and , advv. , v. distringo, P. a. fin. , α and β .

districtĭo.opening: distringo . Lit. , a stretching out , as a punishment, Cassiod. Var. 3, 34 ; 47 .— Trop. , a hindrance , difficulty , Ambros. de Job, 3, 4, 12; Dig. 4, 8, 16 dub.

districtīvus.opening: adj. id. . In medic., pertaining to dissolving : adjutoria, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 2, 20 ; 2, 29, 159 .

districtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from distringo.

di-stringo.opening: v. a. To draw asunder , to stretch out (very rarely): radiis rotarum districti pendent, * Verg. A. 6, 616 .— Poet. : (canum) rabies districta, i. e. showing the teeth, Lucr. 5, 1064 ; cf.: acies dentium, Amm. 14, 7, 13…

dis-trunco.opening: v. a. , to cut to pieces , cut up : ego te hic agnum faciam, et medium distruncabo, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 53 .

disturbātĭo.opening: disturbo , destruction. * Prop.: Corinthi, Cic. Off. 3, 11, 46 .— Trop. , Mythogr. Vatic. in Mai. Auct. Class. 3, p. 85 b.
