Draus.opening: or , , , the river Drave in Hungary , Plin. 3, 25, 28, § 147 ; Flor. 4, 12, 8 .

drenso.opening: v. n. , expresses the note of the swan, Auct. Philom. 23.

Drĕpăna.opening: , = Δρέπανα , a town on the western coast of Sicily , now Trapani , Cato acc. to Serv. Verg. A. 3, 707 , Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 90 ; Liv. 28, 41 ; Flor. 2, 2, 12 .—Called also , Verg. A. 3, 707 , and ( ), , Sil. 14, 269 .…

drĕpănis.opening: , = δρεπανίς , the martin , Hirundo apus, Linn.; Plin. 11, 47, 101, § 257 .

drīmўphăgĭa.opening: , = δριμυφαγία , the eating of acrid food , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 26 ; 2, 6, 93 .

drindĭo.opening: v. n. , expresses the cry of the weasel, Auct. Philom. 61.

drŏmas.opening: , = δρομάς . A dromedary , Liv. 37, 40 ; Curt. 5, 2, 5 ; Vop. Aur. 28 .—Called also , , , Hier. Vit. Malchi, 10; Vulg. Isa. 60, 6 .— , , , the name of one of Actaeon's hounds , Ov. M. 3, 217 .

drŏmo.opening: , = δρόμων (the runner). A sort of shell-fish , Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 148 .— A kind of vessel rapidly propelled by many oars , a cutter , Cod. Just. 1, 27, 2 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 1, 14 .

Drŏmō.opening: , Gr. Δρόμων , the name of a slave , Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 22 ; cf. id. Heaut. 2, 3, 34 .

drŏmos.opening: , = δρόμος . A place for running; a race-course , Grut. Inscr. 339, 2.— Esp., as nom. prop. , , , , the plain near Sparta , on which the Lacedaemonian youth exercised, Liv. 34, 27, 5 .— Dromos Achilleos, a peninsula…

drōpăcismus.opening: , = δρωπακισμός , the removal of hair by plasters of pitch , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 6, 93 .

drōpăco.opening: v. a. , to depilate , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

drōpax.opening: , = δρώπαξ , a pitchointment , depilatory , Mart. 3, 74 ; 10, 65, 8 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 36 sq.

drŏsŏlĭthus.opening: δροσόλιθος , dewstone , a precious stone now unknown , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 190 .

Drŭentĭa.opening: a tributary river of the Rhodanus , now Durance , Liv. 21, 31, 9 ; Sil. 3, 468 ; Aus. Mos. 479 .

Drŭĭdes.opening: ( , , Cic. Div. 1, 41 ; Tac. A. 14, 30 ; id. H. 4, 54 ; Suet. Claud. 25 ; Luc. 1, 451 .—Dub. form acc. Druidas, Mel. 3, 2, 3 ; Plin. 30, 1, 4, § 13 ), , the Druids , the priests and wise men of the Gauls , Caes. B. G.…

drungus.opening: a body of soldiers , a troop (late Lat.), Veg. Mil. 3, 16 ; Vop. Prob. 19 .

druppa.opening: or ( ) oliva = δρύππα (v. Lidd. and Scott under δρυπεπής ), an over-ripe , wrinkled olive , Plin. 15, 1, 2, § 6 ; and absol. , , id. 15, 7 7, § 26; 17, 24, 37, § 230; 19, 5, 26, § 78.

Drūsus.opening: a well-known Roman surname in the Livian family , first assumed by the Livius who slew the Gallic general Drausus, Suet. Tib. 3 .—Esp. M. Livius Drusus , uncle of Cato Uticensis , murdered by Q. Varius , Cic. Arch. 3, 6…

Drўădes.opening: ( dat. Graec. dryasin, Prop. 1, 20, 12 ; dub. al. adryasin; cf. ib. 32 and 34), , = Δρυάδες , wood-nymphs , dryads , Prop. 1, 20, 45 ; Verg. E. 5, 59 ; id. G. 1, 11 ; Ov. M. 3, 507 ; 6, 453 al. —In the sing. , Dryas,…

drўītis.opening: , = δρυῖτις , an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 188 .

Drȳmo.opening: , = Δρυμώ , a sea-nymph , Verg. G. 4, 336 ; Hyg. Fab. praef.

Drўŏpe.opening: , = Δρυόπη . The mother of Amphissus by Apollo , Ov. M. 9, 331 ; 364 sq.— The mother of Tarquitus by Faunus , Verg. A. 10, 551 .

drўŏphŏnon.opening: , = δρυόφονον , a sort of fern , Plin. 27, 9, 49, § 73 .

Drўops.opening: One of the Dryopes , a people of Epirus , Ov. Ib. 490 ; usu. plur. : , , the Dryopians , Plin. 4 praef. ; Verg. A. 4, 146 .— The name of a warrior , Verg. A. 10, 346 .

drўoptĕris.opening: , = δρυοπτερίς , a plant similar to the preceding , Plin. 27, 9, 48, § 72 .

dŭālis.opening: adj. duo , that contains two : numerus (nasi), i. e. the dual number, duality, Lact. Opif. D. 10, 9 .—In gram. lang.: numerus, the dual, Quint. 1, 5, 42 al.

dubenus.grammar: apud antiquos dicebatur qui nunc dominus

dŭbĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , doubtful , dubious (post-class.): fabulae, Gell. 3, 3, 3 : hoc (with inexplicabile), id. 5, 10, 15 .

Dūbis.opening: , = Δοῦβις , a river in Gallia Belgica, now Doubs , Caes. B. G. 1, 38, 4 .

dŭbĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. dubito , doubtful (very rare). Pass. , to be doubted : verum, Ov. M. 1, 223 : virtus, id. ib. 13, 21 . — Act. , feeling doubt : pectus, Prud. Apoth. 649 .

dŭbĭtanter.opening: adv. , doubtingly , v. dubito fin. A.

dŭbĭtātim.opening: adv. , hesitatingly , v. dubito fin. B.

dŭbĭtātĭo.opening: dubito . A wavering in opinion or judgment; a being uncertain , a doubting; uncertainty , doubt. Prop. In gen. (freq. and good prose). Absol. : nec tibi sollicitudinem ex dubitatione mea, nec spem ex affirmatione,…

dŭbĭtātīvus.opening: adj. dubito , doubtful (late Lat.): sensus, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 25 fin.—Adv. : , doubtfully : pronuntiare, Tert. Car. Chr. 23 fin.

dŭbĭtātor.opening: id. , a doubter (late Lat.); with gen. , Tert. adv. Haeret. 33 .

dŭbĭto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [for duhibitare, freq. from duhibeo, i. e. duohabeo (cf. habitare from habeo), to have or hold, as two, v. dubius; cf. also Gr. δοιάζω from δοιοί ; Germ. zweifeln from zwei], to vibrate from one side…

dŭbĭus.opening: adj. for duhibius, duohabeo, held as two or double, i. e. doubtful; cf. dubito, Corss. Ausspr. 2, 1027 . Moving in two directions alternately , vibrating to and fro , fluctuating (cf. ambiguus, anceps, incertus,…

dŭcālis.opening: adj. dux , of or belonging to a leader or commander (post-class.): tunicae, Valer. Imp. ap. Vop. Aurel. 13 .— Adv. : , like a leader or general : antecedere, Sid. Ep. 5, 13 .— Comp. , Sid. Ep. 8, 6 .

dŭcātor.opening: id. , a general , prince , chief (post-class.): civitatis, Tert. adv. Jud. 13 .

dŭcātrix.opening: ducator , a female leader : vitiorum iracundia, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 14 .

dŭcātus.opening: dux , military leadership , command = ἡγεμονία (post-Aug.), Suet. Tib. 19 ; Flor. 3, 21, 2 ; Just. 2, 15, 14 ; Vulg. Sirach, 7, 4 : calculis omnibus ducatum latrones ei deferunt, App. M. 7, p. 191 med. — In gen.,…

dŭcēna.opening: duceni , the office of a ducenarius, Cod. Th. 12, 1, 5.

dŭcēnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , containing two hundred , of or relating to two hundred (post-Aug.): pondera, Plin. 7, 20, 19, § 83 : procuratores, i. e. who received a salary of 200 sestertia, Suet. Claud. 24 (cf. Dio Cass. 53, 15):…

dŭcēni.opening: ( gen. ducenūm, Sen. N. Q. 3, 7, 3 ; Liv. 7, 25 ; Plin. 9, 3, 2, § 4 ), num. distr. , two hundred each , two hundred , Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 40 ; Hirt. B. G. 8, 4 ; Liv. 9, 19 ; 40, 18 ; Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 28 et saep.

dŭcentēsĭma.opening: (sc. pars) [ducenti], the two hundredth part , as a tax; one half per cent. , Tac. A. 2, 42 ; Suet. Calig. 16 .

dŭcenti.opening: ( sing. ducentum, Lucil. ap. Non. 493 fin. ; Col. 5, 3, 7 ; gen. ducentūm, Liv. 32, 37 al. ; Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 15 : ducentarum, Nep. Them. 2, 5 : -torum, Front. Aq. 7 ), num. [duo-centum], two hundred. Lit. , Plaut.…

dŭcentĭes.opening: or , adv. num. ducenti , two hundred times. Lit. , Cic. Phil. 2, 16, 40 ; Cels. 2, 14 fin. — Transf. , for many times indefinitely, Cat. 29, 15 .

dŭcĭānus.opening: adj. dux , of or belonging to a leader or commander (late Lat.): officium, Cod. Th. 15, 11, 2: apparitores, ib. 11, 25, 1 : judicium, Cod. Just. 7, 62, 38 .— Subst. : , , , a commander's servant , Cod. Th. 7, 16, 3;…

dūco.opening: ( imp. duc; but duce, Plaut. Ep. 3, 3, 18 ; id. Most. 1, 4, 11 ; id. Poen. 5, 4, 59 ; id. Rud. 2, 3, 55 ; id. Trin. 2, 2, 103 ; id. Truc. 2, 5, 26 .— Perf. sync. : duxti, Varr. ap. Non. 283, 32 ; Cat. 91, 9 ; Prop. 1,…

ductābĭlĭtas.opening: ducto , aptness to be duped , Att. ap. Non. 150, 13 .

ductārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or for drawing : funis, perh. only Vitr. 10, 2 ; 3 and 5.

ductĭlis.opening: adj. duco , that may be led , guided , or conducted (post-Aug. and rare): scena, movable, Serv. Verg. G. 3, 24 : flumen aquae riguae, i. e. a canal, Mart. 12, 31, 2 : aes, i. e. that may be hammered out thin, Plin. 34,…

ductim.opening: adv. id. , by drawing (very rare): major pars operis in vinea ductim, potius quam caesim faciendaest (for which, shortly after: ductu falcis, non ictu), Col. 4, 25, 2 : invergere in me liquores, in good draughts, Plaut.…

ductĭo.opening: id. , a leading , a leading off or away (very rare; perh. not anteAug.): aquarum, Vitr. 1, 1 ; 10, 19 : alvi, Cels. 2, 12 ; 4, 24 fin. : ut ducere quis posset eos in quos habet jus ductionis, Dig. 43, 30, 3, § 1 .

ductĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to lead , to lead with one (a Plautin. word). Prop. In gen., Plaut. Rud. 2, 7, 26 .— In partic., to lead home a wife, to marry , Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 60 .— Trop. , to deceive : ego follitim ductitabo,…

ducto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to lead or draw , conduct (very freq. in Plaut.; elsewh. perh. only in Ter., Sall., and once in Tac.; not in Cic., Caes., or the Aug. authors). Lit. In gen.: aliquem, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 158 : restim…

ductor.opening: id. , a leader , commander , chief , general (class.; a favorite word of Vergil, used by him more than 20 times; cf.: dux, imperator, princeps, praetor, praefectus, etc.): exercitus, * Cic. Tusc. 1, 37 ; Liv. 1, 28 :…

ductrix.opening: ductor , a female chief , a general : Penthesilea, Dar. Phryg. 36.

ductus.opening: duco , a leading , conducting (class.). Lit. In gen.: aquarum, Cic. Off. 2, 4, 14 ; id. Leg. 2, 1, 2 ; cf. the work of Frontinus: De aquaeductibus; in this sense also simply ductus, id. ib. 5 sq.: aequali ductu…

dūdum.opening: adv. temp. [diu-dum, it is some time since; cf. Don. Ter. And. 3, 4, 3 ; Prisc. p. 1018 P. Hence]. A short time ago , a little while ago (in Plaut. and Ter. freq., and repeatedly in Cicero's philos. writings and…

dŭella.opening: duo , a Roman weight = two sextulae, or the third part of an uncia, Rhemn. Fann. de Pond. 23; Isid. Or. 16, 25 .

dŭellis.opening: duellum = bellum , a warrior , Arn. 1, p. 10 .

Dŭellĭus.opening: (in MSS. and inscrr. also written and ), duellum = bellum; cf. Cic. Or. 45, 153; Quint. 1, 4, 15 , a Roman gens; esp., C., the famous conqueror of the Carthaginians , in honor of whom the Columna rostrata was erected ,…

dŭĭcensus.grammar: dicebatur cum altero, id est, cum filio census
dŭĭcensus.opening: , Paul. ex. Fest. p. 66, 14 Müll. [duis = bis and censeo].

dŭis.opening: verb. , v. do init. — Num. , v. bis init.

dŭītae.opening: duo , heretics who believed in two gods , Prud. Hamart. praef. 37.

dŭĭtas.opening: id. , the state of being two , duality , Dig. 50, 16, 242, § 3 ; δυάς , duitas, Gloss.

dulcăcĭdus.opening: adj. dulcis-acidus , of a sourish-sweet flavor (late Lat.): liquor, Seren. Sammon. 11, 151; 32, 607.

dulcātor.opening: dulco , a sweetener : fontis amari, Paul. Nol. Carm. 23, 237 .

dulce.opening: adv. , sweetly , pleasantly , v. dulcis, fin. .

dulcēdo.opening: dulcis , sweetness. Lit. , a sweet taste (rare): radix amara cum quadam dulcedine, Plin. 25, 6, 30, § 66 ; Vulg. Exod. 15, 25 .—Far more freq. and class., Trop. , pleasantness , agreeableness , delightfulness , charm :…

dulcesco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to become sweet , Cic. de Sen. 15, 53 ; Plin. 3, 18, 22, § 127 ; 31, 7, 41, § 70 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 17, 23 .

dulcĭārĭus.opening: adj. dulcia , of confections , making sweetmeats : vascula, to hold confections, Inscr. Orell. 114 .— Esp. of persons: pistor, a confectioner, pastry-cook, Mart. 14, 222 in lemm.; App. M. 10, p. 244, 30 .—Hence, subst.…

dulcĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [dulcis], sweetish (very rare): potio, * Cic. Tusc. 3, 19, 46 ; caseus, as a term of endearment, * Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 179 .

dulcĭfer.opening: adj. dulcis-fero , containing sweetness , sweet (very rare): ficus, Enn. ap. Charis. p. 103 P. (v. 71 Vahl.): cantharus, * Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 17 .

dulcĭfĭco.opening: v. a. dulcis-facio , to sweeten : oratio jejunium dulcificat, Petr. Chrysol. Serm. Dub. 6 .

dulcĭlŏquus.opening: adj. dulcis-loquor , sweetly speaking (late Lat. and rare): calami, Aus. Idyll. 20, 4 : ars Orphei, Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .

dulcĭ-mŏdus.opening: adj. dulcis , sweetly modulated (late Lat.): psalmi, Prud. Psych. 664 .

dulcĭnervis.opening: adj. dulcis-nervus , sweetly-stringed (late Lat.): arcus, Mart. Capt. 9, § 917 .

dulcĭŏla.opening: dim. dulcis , little sugar-cakes : mellita, App. M. 4, p. 115, 12 .

dulcĭōrĕlŏcus.opening: adj. dulcisos-loquor , speaking with a sweet mouth , an epithet of Nestor, Laev. ap. Gell. 19, 7, 13 .

dulcis.opening: adj. from gulcis, by dissimilation; cf. ten-ebrae from root tam-; root in Sanscr. gul-jam, sweetness; Gr. γλυκύς, γλυκερός, sweet , sweet (very freq.; cf.: suavis, venustus, jucundus, gratus, acceptus, amoenus, etc.).…

dulcĭsŏnōrus.opening: adj. dulcissonorus , sweetly sounding : res Serv. Centim. p. 24 Santen. (p. 467, 17 Keil).

dulcĭsŏnus.opening: adj. dulcis-sonus , sweetly sounding : murmur, Sid. Carm. 6, 5 ; Cassiod. in Psalt. praef.

dulcĭtas.opening: dulcis , sweetness , pleasantness (ante- and post-classical). Lit. : fici, App. de Mundo, 74, 34.— Trop. : conspirantis animae, Att. ap. Non. 96, 27 (Trag. v. 640 Rib.): tanta, Caecil. ap. Non. ib. (Com. v. 218 Rib.).

dulcĭtūdo.opening: dulcis , sweetness (very rare). Lit. : gustatus, qui dulcitudine praeter ceteros sensus commovetur, Cic. de Or. 3, 25, 99 .— Trop. , pleasantness , agreeableness , charm : usurarum, Dig. 42, 8, 10, § 10 : CVM QVA VIXIT…

dulco.opening: v. a. id. , to sweeten (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 5, 4 ; id. Carm. 2, 105 .

dulcor.opening: id. , sweetness (cf. the opp. amaror; late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 1 . 6; 3, 5; Vulg. Sirach, 11, 3 al.

dulcōro.opening: v. a. dulcor , to sweeten (late Lat.): amaritudinem, Hier. Ep. 22, 9 ; id. ib. 69, 9 : animam, Vulg. Prov. 27, 9 : mare mortuum et amaras aquas, Hier. ap. Psa. 76.—Hence, P. a. : , , sweetened , Plin. Val. 1, 2 al.

Dulgĭbīni.opening: ( Δουλγούμνιοι ), Ptol., a Germanic tribe on the banks of the Weser , in the present Lippe - Detmold, Paderborn, and Pyrmont, Tac. G. 34 .

dūlĭce.opening: adv. , = δουλικῶς , in the manner of a slave , servilely , Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 58 .

Dūlĭchĭum.opening: ( Δουλίχιον Hom., Δολίχαι Strab.), an island of the Ionian Sea , southeast of Ithaca , belonging to the kingdom of Ulysses , perhaps one of the Echinades, but its situation is uncertain, Mel. 2, 7, 10 ; Plin. 4, 12, 19,…

Dūlŏrestes.opening: ( ), , the title of a tragedy of Pacuvius , Prisc. 668 P. v. R ib. Trag. Rel. p. 91 sq. and 364.

dum.opening: conj. [for dium, acc. from dius; cf. diu, Corss. Ausspr. 2, 856], denotes the temporal relation of two actions to cach other, As contemporaneous, or, As in immediate succession, so that with the commencement of one…

dūmālis.opening: adj. dumus , bushy , bristly : coma, Mart. Cap. 4, § 329 .

dūmesco.opening: dumus , to be overgrown with bushes , acc. to Diom. p. 335 P.

dūmētum.opening: or (another form: DUMECTA antiqui quasi DUMICETA appellabant, quae nos dumeta , Paul. ex Fest. p. 67, 10 Müll.), , id. , thorn-bushes , thorn-hedge , thicket. Lit. , Cic. Tusc. 5, 23 ; Verg. G. 1, 15 ; Hor. C. 3, 4, 63…

dūmĭcŏla.opening: , m. [dumus-colo], that dwells in thickets , Avien. Perieg. 895 .

Dumnŏrix.opening: an Aeduan , brother of Divitiacus , Caes. B. G. 1, 3 al.

dūmōsus.grammar: like Casmena, Casmili a, um adj.
dūmōsus.opening: (also ; old form , , etc., Liv. Andron. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 67, 5 Müll.), , adj. dumus , full of thornbushes , bushy (rare): rupes, Verg. E. 1, 77 ; cf. saxa, Ov. M. 10, 535 : montes, Col. 4, 33, 5 ; colles, id. Poët.…

dumtaxat.opening: (less correctly, ; in ante-Aug. monuments perh. always written separately; often in inscriptions separated by some words: dum ... taxat; cf. also Lex ap. Fest. p. 246, 12 Müll.), adv. dum-taxo; hence, lit., as far as it…

dūmus.opening: (old form , v. dumosus), , dusmus for densimus, from densus , a thorn-bush , bramble , Cic. Tusc. 5, 23, 65 ; Verg. G. 3, 315 ; 338 ; 4, 130 ; id. A. 4, 526 et saep.

dŭŏ.opening: ( acc. masc. duo as freq. as duos; cf. ambo. Passages with duo, Att. ap. Charis. p. 101 P.; Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 4 ; 3, 2, 37 ; id. Most. 3, 2, 89 ; 147 ; 148 ; id. Ps. 1, 3, 99 ; 4, 2, 43 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 18, 5 ; 3, 1, 9 ;…

dŭŏdĕcăjŭgum.opening: vox hybr., δυόδεκα + jugum , a team of twelve animals , Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 4.

dŭōdĕcas.opening: , = δυωδεκάς , the number twelve , Tert. Praescr. 49 .

dŭŏdĕcennis.opening: adj. duodecim-annus , twelve years old , Sulpic. Sever. Dial. 1, 10; 3, 2.

dŭŏdĕcennĭum.opening: duodecennis , a period of twelve years , Cod. Th. 2, 27, 1, § 6.

dŭŏdĕcĭes.opening: (or , quadrisyl., Auct. Carm. de Phoenice, 28), adv. num. duodecim , twelve times , Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 75 ; Liv. 38, 28 .

dŭŏdĕcim.opening: card. num. [duo-decem], twelve , Plaut. Ep. 5, 2, 10 ; Cic. Rep. 2, 17 ; Caes. B. G. 1, 5, 2 et saep.—So, duodecim (and more freq. XII.) Tabulae, the laws of the Twelve Tables , Cic. Off. 1, 12 ; Quint. 5, 14, 18 ;…

dŭŏ-dĕcĭmus.opening: ord. num. , the twelfth (a common word in Caes.): legio, Caes. B. G. 2, 23, 4 ; 2, 25, 1 ; 3, 1, 1 ; 7, 62, 4; id. B. C. 3, 34, 3 .— Adv. : , for the twelfth time : consul, Capitol. Anton. Pius, 1, § 8.

dŭŏdĕcim-vir.opening: one of the twelve commissioners, Inscr. Orell. 3969 .

dŭŏdēnārĭus.opening: adj. duodeni , containing twelve : numerus, Varr. L. L. 5, § 34 Müll.

dŭŏ-dēni.opening: distr. num. , twelve each; twelve : uxores habent deni duodenique inter se communes, Caes. B. G. 5, 14, 4 : duodena describit in singulos homines jugera, Cic. Agr. 2, 31, 85 ; Liv. 5, 33 ; cf.: fossa duplex duodenūm…

dŭŏdennium.opening: the space of twelve years , Mythogr. Vat. 3, p. 163 med. (al. duodecennium).

dŭŏ-dē-quā^drāgēni.opening: distr. num. , thirty-eight each : pedum columnae, Plin. 36, 2, 2, § 6 ; and 36, 15, 24, § 114.

dŭŏ-dē-quādrāgēsĭmus.opening: ordin. num. , the thirty-eight : anno, Liv. 1, 40 .

dŭŏ-dē-quā^drāginta.opening: card. num. , thirty-eight , Cic. Tusc. 5, 20 ; Liv. 35, 40 .

dŭŏ-dē-quinquāgēni.opening: distr. num. , forty-eight each; forty-eight : diebus, Plin. 2, 8, 6, § 38 .

dŭŏ-dē-quinquāgēsĭmus.opening: ordin. num. , the forty-eighth : anno, Cic. Brut. 44 : die, Col. 9, 14, 4 .

dŭŏ-dē-quinquāginta.opening: card. num. , forty-eight , Col. 9, 14, 1 ; 12, 5, 1 (written IIL., Lex. Acil. Repet. 32 al.).

dŭŏ-dē-sexāgēsĭmus.opening: ordin. num. , the fifty-eighth : annus, Vell. 2, 53, 13 .

dŭŏ-dē-trīcēsĭmus.opening: ordin. num. , the twenty - eighth : dies, Varr. ap. Gell. 3, 10, 6 .

dŭŏ-dē-trīcĭens.opening: adv. num. , twentyeight times , Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 70 Zumpt N. cr.

dŭŏ-dē-trīginta.opening: card. num. , twentyeight , Liv. 33, 36 fin. ; Suet. Tib. 1 al.

dŭŏ-dē-vīcēni.opening: distr. num. , eighteen each : denarii, Liv. 21, 41 .

dŭŏ-dē-vīcēsĭmus.opening: (or ), , ordin. num. , the eighteenth , Cato and Varr. ap. Non. 100, 11 sq. : pars tauri, Plin. 2, 73, 75, § 184 ; Plin. Ep. 6, 20, 5 ; and, per tmesin: duo enim devicesima Olympiade, Plin. 35, 8, 34, § 55 .

dŭŏ-dē-vīginti.opening: card. num. , eighteen , Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 74 sq. ; Cic. Ac. 2, 41, 128 ; id. Rep. 2, 22 ; Caes. B. G. 2, 5 fin. ; id. B. C. 3, 71 al. ; cf. also: annis mille centum et duobus de viginti fere, etc., Eutr. 10, 9 .

dŭŏ-et-vīcēsĭmāni.opening: duoet-vicesimus , soldiers of the twenty-second legion , Tac. H. 4, 37 ; 5, 1 .

dŭŏ-et-vīcēsĭmus.opening: ordin. num. , the twenty-second : anno, Fab. Pict. ap. Gell. 5, 4 : legio, Tac. H. 1, 18 ; 1, 55 ; 4, 24 ; 4, 37; cf. the preced. art.

effector.opening: id. , an effecter , producer , author (a Ciceronian word), Cic. Univ. 5 fin. ; id. Div. 2, 26 ; id. de Or. 1, 33, 150 (quoted in Quint. 10, 3, 1 ; for which, perfector, Cic. de Or. 1, 60 fin. ).

effectōrĭus.opening: adj. effector , effectual , resistless : vis, August. Immort. Anim. 14 ; 15 ; id. Gen. ad Lit. Op. Imp. 4, 16 .

effectrix.opening: id. , she who effects , produces , causes; perh. only Cic. Fin. 2, 17, 55 ; id. Univ. 10, 32 .

effectus.opening: efficio , a doing , effecting. In gen., execution , accomplishment , performance : ad effectum consiliorum pervenire, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 8, 4 : operis, Liv. 21, 7 : ad effectum aliquid adducere, id. 33, 33, 8 ;…

ef-fēcundo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to make fruitful , to fertilize , Vop. Prob. 21 .

effēmĭnāte.opening: adv. , v. effemino, P. a. fin.

effēmĭnātĭo.opening: effemino , effeminacy (late Lat.): corporis, Firm. Math. 7, 16: animi, Hier. in Isa. 14, 52, 2 .

effēmĭnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from effemino.

ef-fēmĭno.opening: v. a. femina , to make feminine. * Lit. : effeminarunt eum (sc. aërem) Junonique tribuerunt, Cic. N. D. 2, 26, 66 .— Trop. , to make womanish , effeminate , to enervate : fortitudinis praecepta sunt, quae effeminari…

effĕrasco.opening: v. inch. n. [2. effero], to become savage , fierce , Amm. 18, 7, 5 .

effĕrāte.opening: adv. , v. 2. effero, P. a. fin.

effĕrātĭo.opening: effero , a making savage , Hier. Ep. 107, 2 .

effĕrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from 2. effero.

effĕrĭtas.opening: ( ), , efferus , an excessively wild state , wildness , degeneracy (opp. mansuetudo), Cic. Sest. 42, 91 : quas (terras) peragrans undique omnem ecferitatem expuli, id. Tusc. Poet. 2, 8, 20 fin. (al. feritatem); Lact.…

ef-fĕro.opening: v. a. ex-ferus , to make wild , savage , fierce (class.; most freq. since the Aug. per.). Physically: terram immanitate beluarum efferari, Cic. N. D. 2, 39, 99 : speciem oris, Liv. 2, 23 ; cf. vultum, Suet. Calig. 50 :…

effertus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from effarcio.

ef-fĕrus.opening: adj. , very wild , fierce , savage ( poet. and post-class.; freq. in Verg.): proles, Lucr. 2, 604 ; cf. juventus, Verg. A. 8, 6 : Dido, id. ib. 4, 642 : Chimaera, id. ib. 7, 787 : mens Caci, id. ib. 8, 205 ; cf.: vis…

effervens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from effervo.

ef-fervesco.opening: (so Cic. Cael. 31, 77 al. ; ante- and post-class. fervi, Cato R. R. 115, 1; Tac. A. 1, 74 ), 3, v. inch. n. To boil up or over , to foam up , to effervesce , ferment , to grow violent , rage (class.). Lit. : dictum…

ef-fervo.opening: ( praes. effervent, Vitr. 2, 6, 5 ), v. n. , to boil up or over ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): in agros Aetna, Verg. G. 1, 471 : quatenus in pullos animales vortier ova Cernimus alituum vermesque effervere, qs. to…

effēto.opening: ( ), , to put out of use , to abolish , Cassiod. Var. 9, 15 ante med.

ef-fētus.opening: (not effoetus), , adj. , that has brought forth young , that has laid eggs (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. (mostly in Col.): cum effetae loca genitalia tumebunt, Col. 7, 7, 4 ; 7, 12, 11 ; 9, 1, 7 .— Poet. :…

effĭcācĭa.opening: efficax , efficacy , efficiency , virtue (post-Aug.), Plin. 11, 5, 4, § 12 ; Amm. 14, 8, 5 ; 16, 12, 25 ; Vulg. Sirach, 9, 4 ; Lact. de Ira D. 10, 37 .

effĭcācĭtas.opening: id. , efficacy , efficiency , power; perh. only Cic. Tusc. 4, 13, 31 ; Q. Cic. Petit. Cons. 3, 10 .

effĭcācĭter.opening: adv. , efficaciously , effectually , v. efficax fin.

effĭcax.opening: adj. efficio , efficacious , effectual , powerful , efficient (mostly postAug.; not in Cic. and Caes; but cf. efficacitas): nosti Marcellum, quam tardus et parum efficax sit, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 10, 3 ; cf.: ultor…

effĭcĭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from efficio.

effĭcĭentĭa.opening: efficio , efficient power , efficiency , influence (rare; mostly in philos. lang.), Cic. N. D. 2, 37, 95 ; id. Fat. 9, 19 : spiritalis, Hil. in Psa. 131, 24: inenarrabilis, id. Trin. 3, 18 ; Lact. Opif. D. 19, 7 .

ef-fĭcĭo.opening: ( ), ( perf. subj. effexis, Plaut. As. 3, 5, 63 ; id. Poen. 1, 3, 19 ; inf. pass. ecfiĕri, id. Pers. 5, 1, 9 ; Lucr. 6, 761 ), v. a. , to make out , work out; hence, to bring to pass , to effect , execute , complete ,…

effictĭo.opening: effingo , rhet. t. t., a representing , portraying of corporeal peculiarities, Auct. Her. 4, 49, 63 .

effĭgĭātus.opening: effigio , a representing , portraying , App. Flor. 15, p. 350, 36 .

effĭgĭentĭa.opening: effingo , the creating , fashioning. — Transf. = the Creator , Mart. Cap. 9, § 922 .

effĭgĭes.opening: (ante-class. form nom. : effĭgĭa, Plaut. Rud. 2, 4, 7 ; Afran. ap. Non. 493, 2 ; Inscr. Orell. 7416 λ .— Nom. plur. : effigiae, Lucr. 4, 105 .— Acc. plur. : effigias, id. 4, 42 and 85), effingo, I. , an (artistic) copy…

effĭgĭo.opening: v. a. effigies , to form , fashion , portray (late Lat.): hominem (Deus), Prud. Cath. 10, 4 : aliquem imaginibus, Sid. Ep. 6, 12 ; Amm. 14, 6, 9 .

effĭgūrātĭo.opening: , rhet. t. t., = προσωποποιΐα , a representation , Rufin. de Schem. p. 275 .

ef-findo.opening: v. a. , to divide , cleave : fluctus rectos, Manil. 4, 283 .

ef-fingo.opening: v. a. , orig., to work out by pressing = fingendo exprimere, ἐκμάσσειν (v. fingo).—Hence, To form , fashion (artistically—class.; most freq. in the trop. sense; cf.: formo, informo, conformo, fingo, reddo, instituo,…

ef-firmo.opening: v. a. , to strengthen , encourage , Att. ap. Non. 256, 18 .

efflāgĭtātĭo.opening: efflagito , an urgent demand , pressing request (very rare), * Cic. Fam. 5, 19, 2 ; Plancus, ib. 10, 24, 6 .

efflāgĭtātus.opening: id. , an earnest or urgent request : coactu atque efflagitatu meo, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 29 .

ef-flāgĭto.opening: v. a. , to demand or ask urgently , to request earnestly (class.; for syn. cf.: posco, flagito, exigo, obsecro, etc.): epistolam, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 11 : libros, Quint. Ep. ad Tryph. § 3: judicio rum desiderio tribunicia…

ef-flammans.opening: adj. flammo , emitting flames , flaming , blazing : stellae, Mart. Cap. 2, § 207 .

ef-flĕo.opening: v. a. , to weep out , exhaust by weeping : oculos, Quint. decl. 6, 4.

efflicto.opening: v. freq. a. effligo , to strike dead , Plaut. Stich. 4, 2, 26 .

ef-flīgo.opening: v. a. , to strike dead , to kill , destroy (very rare): qui filium misit ad effligendum Pompeium, Cic. Att. 9, 19, 2 : nisi pedatu tertio omnis efflixero (with obtruncavero and occidero), Plaut. Cist. 2, 1, 50 ; cf.:…

ef-flo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ef-flo.opening: v. a. and n. , to blow or breathe out (mostly poet. and post-Aug. prose). Act. In gen.: (Sol) suos efflavit ignes, Lucr. 5, 652 ; cf.: ignes Aetnaeos faucibus, Verg. A. 7, 786 : ignes ore et naribus, Ov. M. 2, 85 :…

ef-flōrĕo.opening: v. n. , to bloom or blossom forth , Tert. Jud. Dom. 209 ; Vulg. Psa. 102, 14 al.

ef-flōresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to bloom or blossom. Lit. (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Sirach, 51, 19 ; id. Isa. 18, 5 .— Trop. (repeatedly in Cic.), to bloom , spring up , flourish (in youth, beauty, etc.): ex rerum cognitione efflorescat et…

efflŭesco.opening: v. inch. [effluo], to revel , riot : sumptuosis conviviis, Ambros. de Off. M. 2, 21, 109 .

ef-flŭo.opening: v. n. (and very rarely a. ), to flow or run out , to flow forth (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense). Lit. : facit effluere imbres, Lucr. 6, 512 : una cum sanguine vita, Cic. Tusc. 2, 24 fin. : umor e cavis populi…

efflŭus.opening: adj. effluo , flowing out (late Lat.): ignis, Avien. Progn. Arat. 1717 : amnis in pontum cadit, id. Perieg. 1162 .

efflŭvĭum.opening: id. , a flowing out , an outlet (post-Aug. and very rare): umoris e corpore, Plin. 7, 51, 52, § 171 : lacus, Tac. A. 12, 57 : cerebri effluvio exspirare, Vell. 2, 120 fin. , v. Kritz. ad h. l.

ef-fōco.opening: v. a. faux , to suffocate , smother. — Trop. : bonis suis effocantur, Sen. Brev. Vit. 2, 3 dub. (al. offoco).

ef-fŏdĭo.opening: , also and (cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, 767, 769), fōdi, fossum, 3 ( inf. pass. : ecfodiri, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 44 ; 2, 4, 21 ), v. a. , to dig out , dig up (class.): nec ferrum, aes, argentum, aurum effoderetur, Cic. Off. 2, 3…

ef-for.opening: v. dep. a. ( defect. In use only: effor, Cav. ap. Diom. p. 375 P.: effaris, App. M. 7, 25, p. 199, 6 : effatur, Verg. A. 10, 523 al. : effamini, Arn. 7, 41 : effantur, App. Mund. prooem. p. 56, 22: effabor, Lucr. 5, 104…

ef-fŏro.opening: v. a. , to bore through , perforate : truncum, Col. 9, 1, 3 .

effossĭo.opening: effodio , a digging out; in the plur. : laboriosae, Cod. Just. 11, 6, 3 .

ef-fŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to refresh : carnem, Veg. 4, 28, 2 dub.

effractārĭus.opening: effractor , a house-breaker , burglar , Sen. Ep. 68, 4 .

effractor.opening: effringo , a housebreaker , burglar (jurid. Lat.), Dig. 1, 15, 3 ; 47, 17, 1 ; Sid. Ep. 9, 7 .

effractūra.opening: id. , house-breaking , burglary (jurid. Lat.): effracturae fiunt plerumque in insulis in horreisque, Dig. 1, 15, 3, § 2 ; 38, 2, 48 .

effrēnāte.opening: adv. , unrestrainedly , violently , v. effreno, P. a. fin.

effrēnātĭo.opening: effreno , unbridled impetuosity : impotentis animi, Cic. Phil. 5, 8, 22 .

effrēnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from effreno.

ef-frēno.opening: or , no perf. , , v. a. , to unbridle , let loose (very rare).— Poet. transf.: Vulturnum Effrenat, Sil. 9, 496 .—Far more freq., , , P. a. Unbridled , without a rein : equi, Liv. 40, 40, 5 : equi velut effrenati passim…

ef-frēnus.opening: (also effrenis mula, Plin. 8, 44, 69, § 171 ; Sen. de Ira, 3, 15, 2), adj. ex-frenum , free from the bridle , unbridled (not ante Aug., and mostly poet. for effrenatus; cf. also: infrenus, infrenatus). Lit. : equus,…

ef-frĭco.opening: ( Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 12 ), , v. a. , to rub off or out (post-Aug. and very rare). Lit. : sordium enormem illuviem operose, App. M. 1, p. 105, 9 : calices, id. ib. 4 , p. 145, 31: spicas decerptas, Tert. l. l.— Trop. :…

ef-fringo.grammar: frēgi, fractum, 3 v. a. and n.
ef-fringo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to break off , to break open : effringere quam aperire putant robustius, Quint. 2, 12, 1 (class.): cardines foribus, Plaut. Am. 4, 2, 6 ; id. As. 2, 3, 8 ; more freq.: fores, id. Stich. 2, 2, 3 ; id.…

ef-frondesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to put forth leaves , be covered with foliage , Vop. Prob. 19, 3 .

ef-frons.opening: adj. (putting forth the forehead, i. e. trop.), barefaced , shameless : consilium, Vop. Num. 13 .

ef-frŭtĭco.opening: v. a. and n. (late Lat.). * Act. , to put forth , produce , transf. , Tert. Anim. 27 fin. —* Neutr. , to shoot or grow forth , Tert. ad Nat. 1, 5 .

effŭgātĭo.opening: effugo , a putting to flight : dolorum, [Hilar.] Anon. in Job, 3, p. 238.

effŭgĭa.grammar: vocari veteri more solet hostia, quae ad aras adducta est immolanda, si casu effugeret

ef-fŭgĭo.opening: ( inf. pass. effugiri, Pseud. Syr. Sent. 815 Rib.), , v. n. and a. (class. and freq., esp. in the active sense). Neutr. , to flee away; or, with reference to the result, to escape : effugias ex urbe inanis, Plaut. Trin.…

effŭgĭum.opening: effugio , a flecing away , flight (rarely, but class.; cf.: perfugium, refugium, asylum): effugiumque fugae prolatet copia semper, Lucr. 1, 983 : effugium praecludere eunti, id. 3, 523 ; cf. id. 1, 974 : dare effugium…

effŭgĭus.opening: adj. effugio , escaping : hostia, Serv. Verg. A. 2, 140 .

ef-fŭgo.opening: v. a. , to put to flight (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 18 , no. 19; Vulg. Sirach, 30, 20 ; id. 1 Macc. 1, 56 .

ef-fultus.opening: Part. [fulcio], propped up , supported ( poet. and in post-class. prose): effultus stratis velleribus, Verg. A. 7, 94 ; cf. id. ib. 8, 368 ; Stat. S. 3, 1, 5 ; App. M. 2, p. 123 .

ef-fūmĭgātus.opening: Part. [fumigo], smoked out , driven out by smoke : coluber, Tert. ad Mart. 1 .

ef-fūmo.opening: v. n. , to emit smoke , to smoke : moles, Auct. Aetn. 497 .

ef-fundo.opening: (or ), , v. a. , to pour out , pour forth , shed , spread abroad (class.; esp. freq. in the transf. and trop. signif.). Lit. : vinum in barathrum (i. e. ventrem), Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 28 ; cf. Cic. Pis. 10 : aquam oblatam…

effūsĭo.opening: effundo , a pouring out , pouring forth , shedding (a Ciceron. word). Lit. : atramenti, Cic. N. D. 2, 49, 127 : aquae liquor et effusio, i. e. its property of pouring forth, fluidity, id. ib. 2, 10, 26 : sanguinis,…

effūsor.opening: id. , a prodigal , waster , Aug. Serm. de Divers. 27 fin.

effūsōrĭe.opening: adv. effusus, effundo , i. q. effuse, 1., far and wide , dispersedly , Amm. 31, 16 fin.

effūsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from effundo.

effūtīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. effutio , prattling , unmeaning , inarticulate: euax verbum nihil significat, sed effuticium naturaliter est, a mere natural utterance or sound , Varr. L. L. 7, § 92 Müll.

ef-fūtĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. FVTIO, acc. to Prisc. p. 631 P. , to blab out , babble forth , to prate , chatter , utter (class.): multa ore, Lucr. 5, 910 ; so, aliquid, Cic. N. D. 1, 30, 84 ; * Hor. A. P. 231 ; Gell. 5, 1 ; cf.:…

ef-fŭtŭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to waste in debauchery : ecfututa latera, Cat. 6, 13 : aurum, Poëta ap. Suet. Caes. 51 fin.

Egesta.opening: the Greek name of Segesta (sc. Ἔγεστα ), Fest. p. 340, 5 Müll.

eglecopala.opening: , a Gallic name for blue marl , Plin. 17, 8, 4, § 46 .

Egnātĭa.opening: A city and harbor on the coast of Appulia , now Torre d' Agnazzo or Monopoli , Plin. 2, 107, 111, § 240 ; the same called Gnatia, Hor. S. 1, 5, 97 sq. ; Mel. 2, 4, 7 ; Inscr. in Avellino Bull. Arch. Ottobre, 1845.— The…

Egnātĭus.opening: a Roman proper name. L. Egn. Rufus, friend of Cicero , Cic. Fam. 13, 43 sq. ; id. Att. 7, 18, 4 al. — M. Egn. Rufus, the name of an edile , 733 A. U. C., who set on foot a conspiracy against Augustus , Suet. Aug. 19 ;…

Egnātŭlēĭus.opening: , L., a quaestor who deserted with the legio Martia from Antony to Octavius , Cic. Phil. 3, 3, 7 .

ei.opening: interj. , oh! etc., Plaut. Cas. 3, 6, 7 ; Ter. And. 1, 1, 46 , v. hei.

ellĕbŏrīne.opening: ( ), , , = ἑλλεβορίνη , a kind of hellebore , Plin. 13, 20, 35, § 114 ; id. 27, 9, 52, § 76 .

ellĕbŏrismus.opening: , = ἑλλεβορισμός , a purgative made from hellebore : destillandus etiam elleborismus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 108 .

ellĕbŏro.opening: ( ) (no perf. nor sup. ), , v. a. elleborus , to purify with hellebore , Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 77 .

ellĕbŏrōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , in need of hellebore (i. e.), out of his senses: Gr. Quaeso, sanun es? Tr. Sum elleborosus. Gr. Ut ego cerritus, Plaut. Rud. 4, 3, 67 .

ellĕbŏrus.opening: ( ), , , and ( ), , , hellebore , in pure Lat. veratrum, a plant much used by the ancients as a remedy for mental diseases, epilepsy, etc.; the best grew on the island of Anticyra, in the Aegean Sea, Pl. 25, 5, 21; id.…

ellipsis.opening: ( ), , , = ἔλλειψις , in rhet. lang., an ellipsis (pure Lat. detractio), Quint. 8, 6, 21 ; cf. id. 1, 5, 40 ; Schol. Juv. 1, 89 .

ellychnĭum.opening: , = ἐλλύχνιον , a lamp-wick , Plin. 23, 4, 41, § 84 ; 28, 11, 47, § 168 ; Vitr. 8, 1 ; Stat. S. 4, 9, 29 .

Elpēnor.opening: , = Ἐλπήνωρ , one of the companions of Ulysses , whom Circe changed into swine , Juv. 15, 22 ; being afterwards disenchanted, he fell from a roof while drunk, and broke his neck, Ov. Tr. 3, 4, 19 ; id. M. 14, 252 ; id.…

Elusātes.opening: a Gallic tribe in Aquitania , Caes. B. G. 3, 27 ; Plin. 4, 19, 33, § 108 .

Elysii.opening: A people of Eastern Germany , between the Oder and the Vistula , Tac. G. 43 .— The Elysian Fields , v. the foll. II.

em.opening: interj. , = en (freq. in Plaut. and Ter. in best MSS.), Plaut. Merc. 2, 2, 42 ; id. Bacch. 4, 8, 29 ; id. Trin. prol. 3 (v. Brix ad loc.); id. ib. 1, 2, 148 ; id. Most. 5, 2, 58 ; id. Men. 2, 1, 26 ; id. Am. 2, 2, 146…

embaenĕtĭca.opening: , = ἐμβαινετική , an artificial appetite , Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 1, 4 Bait. (al. emetica, q. v.).

embăsĭcoetas.opening: , = ἐμβασικοίτας , i. q. cinaedus, and likewise the name of an obscenely shaped drinking - vessel; hence, in a double sense, Petr. 24, 1 and 2.

embăsis.opening: , = ἔμβασις , a bathing in any thing , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8, 18 ; 3, 17, 151 al.

embătes.opening: , = ἐμβάτης , archit. t. t., a model , Lat. modulus, Vitr. 1, 2, 4 .

emblēma.opening: ( abl. plur. emblematis, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 22 ; * Quint. 2, 4, 27 ), , = ἔμβλημα , inlaid work. Raised ornaments on vessels, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 17 ; 22 sq.; Dig. 34, 2, 32 et saep.— Tessellated work , mosaic , Lucil. ap.…

embŏla.opening: , = ἐμβολή , a putting on board , shipment (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 1, 2, 10; Novell. 163, 2.

embŏlĭārĭa.opening: embolium , an actress who performed in the interludes , Plin. 7, 48, 49, § 158 ; Inscr. Murat. 660, 4 .

embŏlĭmaeus.opening: adj. , = ἐμβολιμαῖος , inserted , intercalary (pure Lat. intercalaris): dies, Aus. Eclog. de Rat. Dier. 13 . Called also = ἐμβόλιμος , Sol. 1 .

embŏlismus.opening: adj. , = ἐμβολισμός , intercalary : dies, Sol. 1, § 42 : annus, leap-year, Isid. Orig. 6, 17, 21 sq. —As subst. : , , , the interposition , intercalation , Isid. 6, 17, 23 .

embŏlĭum.opening: , = ἐμβόλιον , something thrown in; in scenic lang., an interlude , ballet , Cic. Sest. 54, 116 (embolia pertinent ad gestus saltatorios, Schol.).

embŏlum.opening: , = ἔμβολον , the beak of a ship : aēneum, Petr. 30, 1 .

embŏlus.opening: , = ἔμβολος , in mechanics, the piston of a pump , Vitr. 10, 12 .

embrŏcha.opening: , = ἐμβροχή , a wet poultice , Theod. Prisc. 1, 33 .

emere.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 4, 18 , and 76, 1 Müll.; cf. adimo and demo.

eminatio.opening: , false read. in Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 19 : conminatio, Brix: minatio, Fleck., Ritschl.

eminor.opening: , false read. in Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 11 : minor, Fleck.

emmănes.opening: , = ἐμμανής , the plant hyoscyamus, App. Herb. 4 .

emmŏton.opening: , = ἔμμοτον , a salve spread on lint , Theod. Prisc. 1, 28 .

Empĕdŏcles.opening: ( gen. -cli, Gell. 4, 11, 9 ; acc. -clem, Cic. Ac. 1, 12, 44 ; -clen, id. ib. 2, 5, 14 al.), , = Ἐμπεδοκλῆς , a famous natural philosopher of Agrigentum , about 460 B. C., Lucr. 1, 716 sq. ; Cic. N. D. 1, 12 ; id. de…

empĕtros.opening: , = ἔμπετρος , a plant called in pure Lat. calcifraga, Plin. 27, 9, 51, § 75 .

emphănistĭcum.opening: , = ἐμφανιστικόν , a duty paid by a priest for the ordination , Julian. Ep. Nov. c. 50, § 191.

emphăsis.opening: , = ἔμφασις , a figure of rhet., emphasis , rhetorical stress (cf.: pondus, significatio), Quint. 9, 2, 64 ; 8, 2, 11 ; 8, 3, 86 al.

emphragma.opening: , = ἔμφραγμα , a stoppage , obstruction , Veg. Vet. 2, 12 and 19 (1, 40; 47 Bip.).

emphўteusis.opening: , = ἐμφύτευσις (lit., an implanting), in jurid. lang., a permanent tenure of land upon condition of cultivating it properly , and paying a stipulated rent , a sort of fee-farm or copyhold , Cod. Just. 4, 66, 1 ; Just.…

emphўteuta.opening: , = ἐμφυτεύτης , the lessee in the tenure of emphyteusis , Cod. Just. 4, 66, 1 sq. ; called also , ib. 11, 62, 1 ; the latter also adj. , of or belonging to emphyteusis : praedium, contractus, ib. 4, 66, 2 sq.

emphўteutĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἐμφυτευτικός , of or pertaining to emphyteusis : jus, contractus, etc., Cod. Just. 4, 66, 1 sq. ; cf. the preced. art.

empīrĭce.opening: ( , , Marc. de Med. 6), , = ἐμπειρική , empiricism in medicine, i. e. a system founded wholly on practice , Plin. 29, 1, 4, § 5 .—Hence, , , , an empiric , a physician whose knowledge of medicine is derived from…

emplastrātĭo.opening: emplastro , in horticult. lang., the insertion of a small piece of the bark in inoculating a tree , etc., scutcheon-grafting , budding , Col. 5, 11, 1 ; id. Arb. 26, 1 ; 11, 2, 59 ; Plin. 17, 16, 26, § 118 sq. ; Pall.…

emplastro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , in horticult. lang., to inoculate by inserting a bit of the bark with the eye , to scutcheongraft , to bud , Col. 5, 11, 10 ; 11, 2, 37 ; Pall. Mai. 6 ; id. Nov. 7, 7 .

emplastrum.opening: (or , , , Gell. 16, 7 fin. ), = ἔμπλαστρον . In medic. lang., a plaster. Prop., Cels. 5, 17 ; 19 ; Cato, R. R. 39, 2 ; Plin. 21, 4, 10, § 15 ; 34, 10, 22, § 103 et saep.—* Trop. : quid est jusjurandum? Emplastrum aeris…

et-si.opening: conj. [et, II. H.], like etiamsi, a concessive conditional particle, though , although , albeit. Prop. With indic. : gaudeo, etsi nihil scio, quod gaudeam, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 62 : etsi scio ego, Philumena, meum jus esse…

eu.opening: interj. , = εὖ , well! well done! bravo! an exclamation of joy or approbation, Plaut. Most. 1, 4, 26 ; Ter. Phorm. 3, 1, 14 ; Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 10 ; Ter. Eun. 1, 2, 74 ; Hor. A. P. 328 .—Esp.: Eu Hercle! Plaut. Men. 5,…

Euadne.opening: ( , ), , , = Εὐάδνη , wife of Capaneus , one of the " Seven before Thebes; " when her husband's body was burned , she threw herself on the pile , Prop. 3, 13, 24 (4, 12, 24 M.); 1, 15, 21; Verg. A. 6, 447 ; Ov. Tr. 4,…

Euander.opening: (Gr. nom. , Verg. A. 8, 100, 185 al. ; voc. -dre, id. ib. 11, 55 . Less correctly, ), , , = Εὔανδρος . Son of Carmenta (v. Carmentis), born at Pallantium , in Arcadia; he emigrated to Italy sixty years before the Trojan…

euax.opening: interj. only Plautine , expressive of delight at some tidings or event, hail! joy! good! Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 13 ; 4, 4, 72 ; Cassiod. 4, 4, 13 .

Euboea.opening: , = Εὔβοια , an island in the Aegean Sea , separated from Boeotia by Euripus , now Negroponte , Mel. 2, 7, 9 ; Plin. 4, 12, 21, § 63 ; Ov. M. 13, 660 al. — Derivv. , , adj. , Euboean : litus, Prop. 2, 26, 38 (3, 22, 18…

eubŏlĭon.opening: , i. q. dictamnus, the plant dittany , App. Herb. 62 .

Eubūleus.opening: one of the Anaces or Dioscuri , Cic. N. D. 3, 21, 53 .

Eubūlĭdas.opening: a Greek proper name , Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 23 al.

Euchadia.opening: a Greek proper name , Cic. Pis. 36, 89 .

euchăris.opening: adj. , = εὔχαρις , agreeable , grateful , Vulg. Sir. 6, 5 .

euchăristĭa.opening: , = εὐχαριστία . A thanksgiving , Tert. adv. Haer. 47 .— The Lord's supper in the Christian Church, the eucharist , Cypr. Ep. 10 .

euchăristĭcon.opening: , = εὐχαριστικόν , thanksgiving , Tert. Praescr. Haeret. 47 ; the name of a poem of thanks addressed by Statius to the Emperor Domitian, Stat. S. 4, 2 .

Euclīdes.opening: , = Εὐκλείδης , a Greek proper name , Euclid. A philosopher of Megara , a disciple of Socrates and founder of the Megaric sect , Cic. Ac. 2, 42, 129 ; Gell. 6, 10, 10 ; Sid. Carm. 2, 176 .— A mathematician in Alexandria…

Eudaemon.opening: , = Εὐδαίμων (fortunate), the Greek appellation of the southern part of Arabia ( Arabia Felix ), Mel. 3, 8, 6 ; Plin. 6, 27, 31, § 138 ; Sol. 33, 4 ; and of its inhabitants , Vop. Aurel. 33 ; Capitol. Macr. 12 .

Eudēmus.opening: , = Εὔδημος , a Greek proper name , Cic. Div. 1, 25, 53 .—Also a Greek physician , Tac. A. 4, 3 al.

eudiaeon.grammar: lineum filum, quod medici extremo in clysterio relinquunt
eudiaeon.opening: , per quod κλυσμός emittitur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 78, 13 Müll.

Eudoses.opening: a tribe of Germany , mentioned only by Tac. G. 40 .

Eudoxus.opening: , = Εὔδοξος , a Greek astrologer , a disciple of Plato , Cic. Div. 2, 42, 87 ; id. Rep. 1, 14 al.

Euēnus.opening: ( , also ), , , = Εὔηνος , a king of Etolia , father of Marpessa; in despair at the loss of whom he threw himself into the river Lycormas , Hyg. Fab. 242 ; Prop. 1, 2, 18 .— The river formerly called Lycormas , now the…

euergănĕus.opening: adj. εὐεργός , well-wrought , well-joined : trabes, Vitr. 5, 1, 9 .

euēthes.opening: adj. , = εὐἡθης (good-natured, hence), simple , silly (pure Lat. stultus), Amm. 22, 8, 33 .

eugălacton.opening: , = εὐγάλακτον , another name of the plant glaux , Plin. 27, 9, 58, § 82 .

Eugănĕi.opening: a people of northern Italy , Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 130 sq. ; Liv. 1, 1 . —Hence, , , adj. , of the Euganei, Euganean : gentes, Plin. 3, 20, 24, § 133 : lacus, Mart. 4, 25, 4 : agna, Juv. 8, 15 .

eugĕ.opening: ( or , Ter. And. 2, 2, 8 ), interj. , = εὖγε , an exclamation of joy, applause, admiration, etc., well done! good! bravo! (cf. eu; freq. in Plaut. and Ter., and in the Vulg.). In gen.: euge, euge, perbene, Ab saxo…

eugĕnēus.opening: or , , adj. , = εὐγενής , well-born , i. e. noble , generous; applied to wine of good quality: (vinum), Cato R. R. 6, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 25 : (uvae), Col. 3, 2, 16 .

Euhan.opening: (cf. Lach. ad Lucr. 5, 743 ; also, , Prisc. 1, 29 ; not , as in many edd.), , = Εὐάν , a surname of Bacchus , Lucr. 5, 742 ; Ov. M. 4, 15 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 804 .—Hence, , (cf. Gr. εὐάζων ), adj. , crying Euhan! an…

Euhēmĕrus.opening: , = Εὐήμερος , a Greek poet and philosopher , Cic. N. D. 1, 41, 119 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 2 ; Lact. 1, 11, 33 al.

Euhius.opening: (cf. Lach. ad Lucr. 5, 743 ; also, ; less correctly, as in some edd., ), , , a surname of Bacchus , Lucr. 5, 742 ; Cic. Fl. 25, 60 ; Hor. C. 1, 18, 9 ; 2, 11, 17 ; Col. poët. 10, 424.— Acc. Euhion, Pers. 1, 102 ; Ov. A.…

euhoe.opening: (dissyl.; also, ; less correctly, ; cf. Lach. ad Lucr. 5, 743 ), interj. , = εὐοῖ , a shout of joy at the festivals of Bacchus : euhoe Bacche, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 82 ; Ov. A. A. 1, 563 ; Cat. 64, 255 ; Verg. A. 7, 389 ;…

Eumaeus.opening: , = Εὔμαιος , the swineherd of Ulysses in Homer , Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 1 ; Hyg. Fab. 126 .

eumēces.opening: , = εὐμῆκες (very long). A kind of balsam-tree , Plin. 12, 25, 54, § 114 .— An unknown gem , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 160 .

Eumēdes.opening: , = Εὐμήδης , a Trojan herald , father of Dolon , Ov. Tr. 3, 4, 27 ; Verg. A. 12, 346 .

Eumēlus.opening: , = Εὔμηλος . A king of Patrae , Ov. M. 7, 390 .— A companion of Aeneas , Verg. A. 5, 665 .

Eumĕnes.opening: , = Εὐμένης , a famous general under Alexander the Great , and after his death governor of Cappadocia , Nep. Eum. ; Just. 13, 4 sq. ; Curt. 10, 4, 3 .

Eumĕnĭdes.opening: , = Εὐμενίδες (the benevolent, the gracious ones), a euphemistic name for the Furies , Cic. N. D. 3, 18, 46 ; Hor. C. 2, 13, 36 ; Verg. G. 1, 278 ; 4, 483 ; id. A. 4, 469 al. —In the sing. : , a Fury , Sil. 2, 559 ;…

Eumolpus.opening: , = Εὔμολπος , a fabulous Thracian singer and priest of Ceres , who brought the Eleusinian mysteries and the culture of the vine to Attica , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 199 .— His descendant of the same name , the son of Musaeus…

eunūchīnus.opening: adj. eunuchus , of or belonging to a eunuch : facies, Hier. Ep. 22, 27 .

eunūchĭon.opening: , = εὐνούχιον , a kind of lettuce that subdues amatory desires , Plin. 19, 8, 38, § 127 .

eunūchismus.opening: , = εὐνουχισμός , an unmanning , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 118 .

eunūchīzātus.opening: Part. [ εὐνουχιζω ], made a eunuch , mutilated , Hier. contr. Jov. 1, 7.

eunūcho.opening: v. a. eunuchus , to make a eunuch of , to unman : se, Varr. ap. Non. 106, 8 .

eunūchus.opening: , = εὐνοῦχος , a eunuch. Prop., Cic. Or. 70, 232 ; Mart. 3, 82 ; Juv. 6, 366 ; 378 ; 12, 35 ; Vulg. Gen. 37, 36 et saep.— (Sc. fabula.) Fem. , the name of one of Terence's comedies.

euōnўmos.opening: , = εὔωνυμος (of good, prosperous name), name of a tree ( spindle-tree ) in Lesbos , Plin. 13, 22, 38, § 118 .

Eupălium.opening: , = Εὐπάλιον , a city of western Locris , Liv. 28, 8 .—The same called , Plin. 4, 3, 4, § 7 .

Eupător.opening: , = Εὐπάτωρ , a surname of Mithridates , king of Pontus , Plin. 33, 12, 54, § 151 .

eupătŏrĭa.opening: , = εὐπατορία , a plant , called also agrimonia, agrimony , Plin. 25, 6, 29, § 56 .

eupĕlĭos.opening: , = εὐπέλιος , a plant , called also daphnoides, App. Herb. 58 ; see the foll. art.

eupĕtălos.opening: , = εὐπέταλος , an unknown precious stone , perh. the opal , Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 161 .

Euphorbus.opening: , = Εὔφορβος . Son of Panthus , a brave Trojan , whose soul Pythagoras asserted had descended to himself , through the process of transmigration , Ov. M. 15, 161 ; Gell. 4, 11 fin. — A celebrated Greek physician , after…

Euphŏrĭo.opening: and , , , = Εὐφορίων , a grammarian and poet , born at Chalcis , in Euboea , who flourished in the time of Ptolemy Euergetes , Varr. R. R. 41, 9 ; Cic. Div. 2, 64, 132 ; id. Tusc. 3, 19, 45 ; Quint. 10, 1, 56 ; Suet.…

Euphrānor.opening: , = Εὐφράνωρ . A celebrated painter and sculptor , a contemporary of Praxiteles , Quint. 12, 10, 6 ; 12 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 50 ; 35, 11, 40, § 128 ; Juv. 3, 217 .— An architect , Vitr. 7, 14 .

Euphrātes.opening: (in Inscr. also EVFRATES), , , = Εὐφράτης , A wellknown river in Syria , which rises in Armenia , and , after its junction with the Tigris , empties into the Persian Gulf , now Frat , Mel. 1, 11, 2 ; 3, 8, 5 ; Plin. 5,…

euphrŏne.opening: , = εὐφρόνη (the propitious), euphemism for night : ut euethen Graeci dicimus stultum, et noctem euphronen, et furias Eumenidas, Amm. 22, 8, 33 ; cf. Lidd. and Scott, s. v. εὐφρόνη .

Euphrŏsўne.opening: , = Εὐφροσύνη , one of the graces , Sen. Ben. 1, 3, 6 .

euphrŏsўnum.opening: or , , , = εὐφρόσυνον , a plant , called also buglossos, Plin. 25, 8, 40, § 81 .

euplŏcămus.opening: , = εὐπλόκαμος , having beautiful locks , Lucil. ap. Non. 35, 31 .

Eupŏlĕmus.opening: , = Εὐπόλεμος , a Greek proper name , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 22 .

Eupŏlis.opening: , = Εὔπολις , a celebrated comic poet in Athens , contemporary with Aristophanes , Hor. S. 1, 4, 1 ; Vell. 1, 16 ; Quint. 1, 10, 18 ; 10, 1, 66 ; 12, 10, 65 al. ; acc. Eupolin, Hor. S. 2, 3, 12 : Eupolidem, Pers. 1, 124…

euptĕron.opening: , = εὔπτερον , a plant , called also polytrichon, App. Herb. 51 .

eurĭnus.opening: , = εὔρινος : ventus, an east wind, Col. 11, 2, 14 .

eurĭpĭce.opening: , = εὐριπική , a kind of rush , Plin. 21, 18, 71, § 119 .

Eurīpĭdes.opening: , = Εὐριπίδης , a celebrated Athenian tragic poet , Quint. 10, 1, 67 sq. ; Gell. 15, 20 ; dat. Euripidae, id. 7, 3 med. ; Cic. Tusc. 1, 26 fin. ; 1, 48 ; 3, 14 et saep.—Hence, , , adj. , of Euripides : carmen, Cic.…

eurīpus.opening: ( ), , , = εὔριπος , a narrow channel , strait. Prop. In gen., Cic. Mur. 17 ; Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 99 ; 2, 97, 100, § 219 .— In partic.: , , , = Εὔριπος , the channel between Boeotia and Euboea , now Egripo , Mel. 2, 7, 9…

eurŏ-ăquĭlo.opening: the northeast wind , Vulg. Act. Apost. 27, 14 ; cf. the foll. two articles.

eurŏ-auster.grammar: dictus, quod ex una parte habeat Eurum, ab altera Austrum

eurŏ-nŏtus.opening: , = εὐρόνοτος , the south-southeast wind , that which is between eurus and notus , Col. 11, 2, 42 ; Plin. 2, 47, 46, § 120 ; Vitr. 1, 6 .

Eurōpa.opening: , and , , , = Εὐρώπη . Daughter of the Phoenician king Agenor , sister of Cadmus , and mother of Sarpedon and Minos by Jupiter , who , under the form of a bull , carried her off to Crete , Ov. M. 2, 836 sq. ; Hyg. Fab.…

Eurōtas.opening: , = Εὐρώτας , the principal river of Laconia , on the banks of which Sparta stood , now Basilipotamo , Mel. 2, 3, 9 ; Plin. 4, 5, 8, § 16 ; Cic. Inv. 2, 21, 96 ; id. Tusc. 5, 34, 98 ; Ov. M. 2, 247 ; id. Am. 2, 17, 32…

eurōtĭas.opening: , = εὐρωτίας , an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 161 .

eurōus.opening: adj. eurus; cf.: arctous, Lesbous , eastern , orient : fluctus, Verg. A. 3, 533 .

eurus.opening: , = εὖρος , the southeast wind (pure Lat. Vulturnus), Col. 11, 2, 65 ; 5, 5, 15 ; Sen. Q. N. 5, 16 ; Plin. 2, 47, 46, § 119 ; Gell. 2, 22, 7 sq. ; Vitr. 1, 6 ; Hor. C 1, 28, 25; 2, 16, 24 al.—In plur. , Verg. G. 2, 339…

Eurўālus.opening: , = Εὐρύηλος , a hill near Syracuse , Liv. 25, 25 .

Eurўălus.opening: , = Εὐρύαλος . A friend of Nisus , Verg. A. 5, 294 ; 9, 179 sq.; Ov. Tr. 1, 5, 23 .— A king of Thessaly , Ov. Ib. 289 .

Eurўdămas.opening: , = εὐρυδάμας (the wide-ruling), a surname of Hector , Ov. H. 329 .

Eurўdĭca.opening: , = Εὐρυδίκη , the name of a slave of Rhea Sylvia ; Euridica, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 20 .

Eurўdĭce.opening: , = Εὐρυδίκη . The wife of Orpheus , who died of the bite of a serpent. Orpheus obtained from Pluto permission to bring her back from the Lower World , under promise that he would not look back at her on the way. But ,…

Eurўlŏchus.opening: , = Εὐρύλοχος , the only one of the companions of Ulysses who withstood Circe's magic cup , Ov. M. 14, 252 ; 287 .

Eurўmĕdon.opening: , = Εὐρυμέδων . A river of Pamphylia , Liv. 33, 41 ; 37, 23 ; Mel. 1, 14, 1 ; Avien. Descr. Orb. 1015 .— An Athenian general in the Peloponnesian war , Just. 4, 4, 11 ; 4, 5, 7 .— A son of Faunus , Stat. Th. 11, 32 .

Eurўmĕnae.opening: , = Εὐρυμεναί , a city of Thessaly , Liv. 39, 25 al. ; Val. Fl. 2, 14 .

Eurўmus.opening: , = Εὔρυμος , a seer , father of the seer Telemus , Hyg. Fab. 125 and 128.—Whence, , , , the surname of Telemus , Ov. M. 13, 771 .

Eurўnŏme.opening: , = Εὐρυνόμη , daughter of Oceanus and Tethys , mother of Leucothoë , Ov. M. 4, 210 sq.

Eurўpўlus.opening: , = Εὐρύπυλος . Son of Hercules and king of the island of Cos , Ov. M. 7, 363 .—Hence, , , , adj. , Eurypylan , poet. i. q. Coan : textura, Prop. 4 (5), 5, 23. — Son of Euaemon of Thessaly , and leader of a body of…

Eurysthĕnes.opening: , = Εὐρυσθένης , son of Aristodemus , king of Sparta , brother of Procles , Nep. Ages. 1, 2 ; Cic. Div. 2, 43, 191 .

Eurystheus.opening: ( ), , , = Εὐρυσθεύς , son of Sthenelus and grandson of Perseus , a king of Mycenae , who , at the command of Juno , imposed upon Hercules his famous twelve labors , Cic. Tusc. 2, 8, 20 ; Ov. H. 9, 7 ; 45 ; id. M. 9,…

eurythmĭa.opening: , = εὐρυθμία , in architect., beautiful arrangement , proportion , harmony of the parts, Vitr. 1, 2 ; 6, 2 .

Eurўtus.opening: , = Εὔρυτος . King of Oechalia and father of Iole , Ov. M. 9, 356 .—Whence Iole is called , , , Ov. M. 9, 395 ; id. H. 9, 133 .— A centaur , Ov. M. 12, 220 .—Also called , , , Ov. A. A. 1, 593 (cf. Hom. Od. 21, 285).—…

euschēmē.opening: adv. , = εὐσχήμως , becomingly , gracefully , handsomely , Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 58 ; id. Trin. 3, 1, 24 .

eusĕbes.opening: , = εὐσεβές , an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 161 .

Eusĕbes.opening: , = Εὐσεβής , a surname of Ariobarzanes , Cic. Fam. 15, 2 .

Eusĕbĭus.opening: a Latin rhetorician , Rufin. p. 191 Bait.

eustŏmăchus.opening: adj. , = εὐστό μαχος , good for digesting , Gargil. 1, 3; Theod. Prisc. 7 .

eustȳlos.opening: adj. , = εὔστυλος , with pillars evenly arranged , Vitr. 3, 2 .

Euterpe.opening: , = Εὐτέρπη , the muse of music , Hor. C. 1, 1, 33 ; Aus. Idyll. 20, 4 .

euthalos.opening: a kind of laurel , also called daphnoides, Plin. 15, 30, 39, § 132 (al. eupetalos).

euthīa.opening: , = εὐθεῖα , a straight line , Mart. Cap. 9, § 958 .

Eutrăpĕlus.opening: , = Εὐτράπελος (witty), a surname given to P. Volumnius , a friend of Marc Antony , Cic. Att. 15, 8, 1 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 31 al.

Eutrŏpĭus.opening: , Flavius, a Roman historian in the middle of the fourth century of the Christian era , contemporary with the Emperor Julian , and author of a Breviarium Historiae Romanae, Amm. 29, 1, 36 ; Greg. Naz. Ep. 137 sq.; Symm.…

Euxīnus.opening: adj. , = Εὔξεινος (hospitable), an epithet of the Black Sea. Usually connected with Pontus. In Ovid also freq.: Euxinum mare, Ov. Tr. 4, 8, 42 ; 4, 10, 97 ; 5, 10, 2 ; id. Pont. 4, 6, 46 ; cf. aequor, id. Tr. 5, 2, 63 :…

euzōmon.opening: , = εὔζωμον , a sort of cabbage (pure Lat. eruca), Plin. 20, 13, 49, § 126 .
