ex-ăbundo.opening: to abound exceedingly (late Lat.): immensarum divitiarum copiis, Salv. adv. Avar. 4, 6 .

exăcerbātĭo.opening: exacerbo , an exasperation , Rufin. de Schem. 11, p. 274 : peccatorum, i. e. because of , Salv. Gub. Dei , 4, 7.— Esp., of the stirring of divine anger by the Jews in the wilderness, the provocation , Vulg. Hebr. 3, 8 ;…

exăcerbātrix.opening: id. , she who exasperates , Salv. Gub. Dei , 3, 9.

ex-ăcerbesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become exasperated , irritated , angry : quis est tam mitis quin exacerbescat, App. Mag. p. 327, 28 .

ex-ăcerbo.opening: v. a. (not anteAug.). To exasperate , irritate , provoke , make angry; to grieve , afflict : ut recenti aliqua ira exacerbarentur animi, Liv. 2, 35 fin. ; 46 ; 6, 18 ; 8, 33; Suet. Tib. 62 ; 75 ; Plin. Ep. 8, 5, 2 ;…

ex-ăcervans.opening: Part. [acervo], heaping up exceedingly : tela, Amm. 23, 5, 3 .

ex-ăcesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become sour (rare): ficus, Col. 12, 17, 1 .

exăcon.opening: ( ), , , the Gallic name of the herb centaureum ( centaury ), Plin. 25, 6, 31, § 68 .

exacte.opening: adv. , exactly , precisely , accurately , v. exigo, P. a. fin.

exactĭo.opening: exigo . * A driving out , expelling : (regum), Cic. de Or. 1, 9, 37 (perh. only on account of the preceding exactis regibus).— A demanding , exacting , requisition. In gen.: in exhibendis operariis, Lact. Mort. Pers. 7,…

exactor.opening: id.; cf. also exactio . * A driver-out , expeller : regum (Junii Valeriique), Liv. 9, 17, 11 .— A demander , exactor (cf.: redemptor, manceps, magister; also: publicanus, portitor). In gen.: operis, i. e. an overseer ,…

exactrix.opening: exactor , she who demands : rescriptorum, Aug. Ep. 135 .

exactus.opening: exigo , a sending off or away : mercis, i. e. disposal, sale, Quint. Decl. 12, 19 .

ex-ăcŭo.opening: v. a. , to make very sharp , to sharpen , make pointed (class.). Lit. : ferramenta cote, Plin. 28, 4, 12, § 47 ; 34, 14, 41, § 146 : ridicas, Col. 11, 2, 12 : vallos furcasque bicornes, Verg. G. 1, 264 : spicula, id.…

exăcūtĭo.opening: exacuo , a sharpening , pointing : calami, Plin. 17, 14, 24, § 106 .

ex-adversum.opening: ( ) and ( ), adv. and praep. Lit. from opposite; hence, over against , opposite , vis-a\-vis. Adv. : apud ipsum lacum est pistrilla, et exadversum fabrica, Ter. Ad. 4, 2, 44 : video exadvorsum Pistoclerum, Plaut. Bacch.…

ex-advŏcātus.opening: one who has been an advocate , an ex-advocate , Aug. Civ. D. 22, 8 .

ex-aedĭfĭcātĭo.opening: exaedifico , a building , erecting , completion of an edifice; trop. of an oration: ipsa autem exaedificatio posita est in rebus et verbis, Cic. de Or. 2, 15, 63 ; Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 4, § 15.

ex-aedĭfĭco.opening: v. a. To finish building , to build up , erect , construct (rare but class.). Lit. : oppidum, * Caes. B. C. 1, 15, 2 ; cf. Liv. 30, 1 fin. : Capitolium (with efficere), Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 19 : domos et villas, Sall. C.…

exaequātĭo.opening: exaequo , an equalling. * Lit. , a levelling : agrorum, Serv. Verg. G. 1, 95 ; concr., a level, a plane, Vitr. 5, 12, 4 .— Trop. , a levelling , an equality : hanc ipsam exaequationem non fero (cf., shortly before:…

ex-aequo.opening: v. a. To make even or level with any thing. Lit. (very rarely): inferior pars (ex transtillis) sub aqua exaequanda, etc., Vitr. 5, 12, 3 : tumulos tumulis exaequabant, Auct. B. Hisp. 5 fin. — Transf. : aurum auro…

exaerĕsĭmus.opening: adj. , = ἐξαιρέσιμος , that may be omitted , taken out : quod suos dies mensisque congruere volunt ... non numquam eximant unum aliquem diem ex mense: quos illi exairesimos dies nominant, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 52 . § 129.

exaestŭātĭo.opening: exaestuo , a boiling up , a fermentation (post-class.). Lit. , Sol. 5, 17 .— Trop. : animi, Non. 464, 10 .

ex-aestŭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ex-aestŭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to boil up , foam up , ferment (not freq. till after the Aug. period; in Cic. and Caes. not at all). Neut. Lit. In gen.: exaestuat mare, Liv. 26, 42 fin. ; Curt. 6, 4 : fretum, id. 4, 2 : unda ima…

exaggĕrātĭo.opening: exaggero , a heaping or raising up. * Lit. concr., in plur. , Just. 2, 1 fin. (al. aggerationes).— Trop. , elevation , exaltation (very seldom); amplitudinem et quasi quandam exaggerationem quam altissimam animi, * Cic.…

exaggĕrātor.opening: id. , one who increases , an enlarger : famae, Hier. Ep. 22, 8 ; id. ad Eustoch. 28 .

ex-aggĕro.opening: v. a. , to raise a mound , dam , or dike; to heap up (class.; cf.: acervo, coacervo, cumulo, aggero). Lit. : aggesta humo planitiem, Curt. 6, 5 : terram, Plin. 19, 8, 41, § 139 : clivum super capita columnarum, id. 36,…

exăgĭtātĭo.opening: exagito , a disturbance (late Lat.): mentis, Acr. ad Hor. S. 2, 3, 208 .

exăgĭtātor.opening: exagito, II. B. 1. , one who severely blames , a censurer : omnium rhetorum, Cic. Or. 13, 42 .

ex-ăgĭto.opening: v. freq. a. , to drive out of its position or place; to stir up , rouse up , disturb. Lit. (very seldom): ut quicquid faecis subsederit exagitet, et in summum reducat, Col. 12, 19, 4 : vis (venti) exagitata foras…

exăgĭum.opening: ex-ago; cf. examen, II. , a weighing , weight; a balance (late Lat.), Theod. et Val. Nov. 25 ; Inscr. Orell. 3166 ; cf. Ἐξάγιοϝ pensatio; ἐξαγιάζω examino, Gloss. Philox.

exăgōgă.opening: , = ἐξαγωγή (pure Lat. evectio), an exportation of goods, export , Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 17 ; id. Truc. 4, 2, 6 : bonorum exagogae, id. ib. 2, 7, 2 ; cf.: Exagogen evectionem, Paul. ex Fest. p. 80, 15 Müll.

ex-ălăpo.opening: v. a. , to box on the ears : exalapandus et flagellandus, August. in Psa. 49, 6 .

ex-albesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become white. Lit. (very rarely), Gell. 12, 1, 12 .—More freq., Trop. , to grow white , turn pale from fright, etc., Enn. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 58, 218 ; and in Fin. 5, 11, 31; Cic. Ac. 2, 15, 48 ; id. de…

ex-albĭdus.opening: adj. , whitish , white (repeatedly in Pliny): rami (arboris), Plin. 12, 17, 39, § 78 : folia urticae, id. 24, 19, 112, § 172 : vina, id. 23, 1, 22, § 40 .

ex-albo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. albus , to make white , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 10 ; 4, 8 .

ex-alburnātus.opening: adj. alburnum , deprived of the alburnum : robur, Plin. 16, 40, 76, § 204 .

exaltātĭo.opening: exalto . Exaltation , elevation (eccl. Lat.): ab exaltatione tua dispersae sunt gentes, Vulg. Isa. 33, 3 . — Trop. , pride , haughtiness : non congruit professoribus humilitatis, Tert. Cult. Fem. 3 ; cf. oculorum, Vulg.…

exaltātīve.opening: adv. id. , in an exalted state , under inspiration : propheta se convertit, Cassiod. in Psa. 9, 33 .

ex-alto.opening: v. a. altus (postAug.; mostly eccl. Lat.). To raise , elevate , exalt : deus alia exaltat, alia submittit, Sen. Q. N. 3 prooem.: TERMINOS VETVSTATE COLLAPSOS, Inscr. Fabr. p. 748 , no. 555: solium, Vulg. Isa. 14, 13 .—…

ex-ălūmĭnātus.opening: adj. alumen , of the color of alum : uniones, Plin. 9, 35, 56, § 113 .

ex-ămārĭco.opening: v. a. , to imbitter exceedingly : doloribus [Hilar.] Anon. in Job, 2, p. 137.

ex-ambĭo.grammar: ii, ītum, 4 v. n. and a.
ex-ambĭo.opening: v. n. and a. (late Lat.). Neut. , to go round asking , soliciting : ad Martyras, Cypr. Ep. 20 .— Act. , to ask , solicit a person: viros, mulierculas, Mamert. Grat. Act. ad Julian. 19 : suffragium tui favoris, Symm. Ep.…

ex-āmen.opening: for ex-agmen, from ex and ago; cf. contamino and contagies, flamen and flagrare . A multitude issuing forth or flying out , a swarm. Primarily and class. of a swarm of bees: res rusticae laetae sunt tum pecudum pastu,…

exāmĭnātē.opening: adv. , carefully , considerately , v. examino, P. a. fin.

exāmĭnātĭo.opening: examino . Lit. , i. q. libratio, an equipoise , equilibrium , Vitr. 10, 8 .— Trop. , a weighing , examination (post-class.), Dig. 3, 5, 8 ; 47, 14, 1 fin.

exāmĭnātor.opening: id. . * Lit. , a weigher , Cassiod. Var. 6, 18 fin. — Trop. , an examiner (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 9 ; Aug. contr. Cresc. 3, 73.

exāmĭnātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , belonging to an examination : martyria fidei, Tert. adv. Gnost. 7 .

exāmĭnātrix.opening: id. , she that tests or tries : tentatio, August. Sanct. Virg. 46 .

exāmĭnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from examino.

exāmĭno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
exāmĭno.opening: v. n. and a. [examen]. * (acc. to examen, I.).— Neut. , to form swarms , to swarm : examinant alvi, Col. 9, 14, 5 .— (acc. to examen, II.). Lit. Act. , to weigh (class.): (aër) tamquam paribus examinatus ponderibus,…

ex-amplexor.opening: v. dep. a. , to clasp , embrace , Auct. Her. 4, 52 fin.

ex-ămurco.opening: v. a. amurca .Prop., to cleanse from dregs. — Transf. , to deprive of moisture , to dry , App. M. 4, p. 149, 14 .

ex-ămussim.opening: adv. amussis, by the rule, i. e. , exactly , precisely , perfectly (= ad amussim, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 26 ; Gell. 1, 4, 1 ; 20, 1, 34 ); cf. Sisenn. ap. Charis. p. 178 ; Non. 9, 6 sq. ; p. 80, 19 Müll. (ante- and…

ex-ancillātus.opening: Part. [ancillor], serving like a slave : anima falsis dis, Tert. Apol. 17 fin.

ex-anclo.opening: (less accurately -antlo), , v. a. (an archaic word; mostly ante-class.; cf. Quint. 1, 6, 40 ), to draw or bring out as a servant. Lit. In gen.: clavum, Pac. ap. Non. 29, 2, 7 .— In partic., to draw out a liquid =…

ex-ănĭmābĭlĭter.opening: adv. exanimo , half dead with fear or horror, Nov. ap. Non. 376, 12 .

ex-ănĭmālis.opening: adj. pass. (perh. only in Plaut.), lifeless , dead : ni illum exanimalem faxo, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 8, 7 .— Act. , deadly : curae exanimales, id. Rud. 1, 4, 2 .

exănĭmātĭo.opening: exanimo . A depriving of breath , suffocating : volvarum, i. e. hysterical passion, Plin. 32, 3, 13, § 28 (for which suffocatio, id. 20, 5, 15, § 30 , and strangulatus, id. 26, 15, 90, § 153 ).— Trop. , terror , fright…

ex-ănĭmis.opening: , and , (cf. Wagner ad Verg. A. 4, 8 ; the latter form common in the plur. , of which the former has only exanimes, nom. and acc. ), adj. anima , lifeless , dead (mostly postAug.; not in Cic. and Caes.; cf.: inanimis,…

ex-ănĭmo.opening: v. a. To deprive of air or wind. Lit. : folles, i. e. to press together , so as to force out the air , Auct. Aetnae, 560.— Transf. (in pass. ), to be out of breath , weakened , exhausted : simul fore ut duplicato cursu…

exanthēma.opening: , = ἐξάνθημα , an eruption on the skin , exanthema , Marc. Emp. 19 (in Cels. 5, 28, 15 , written as Greek).

ex-ăpĕrĭo.opening: v. a. , to open wide , throw open (very rare): exapertae repente delubri fores, et audita major humana vox, Tac. H. 5, 13 : implicatissimam nodositatem, to undo, unloose, Aug. Conf. 10 .

ex-ăpŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. , to be in utter perplexity : nec aporiati exaporiantur, Ruf. Aquil. Orig. in Cant. p. 305 .

ex-apto.opening: v. a. , to fit , adjust : Deo coronas, App. M. 11, p. 271, 19 .

ex-aptus.opening: adj. , fastened (very rare): exaptum pendere onus ingens, Lucil. ap. Non. 235, 7 ; cf.: ex quo orbe pendeant exapta catenis tintinabula, Varr. ap. Plin. 36, 13, 19, § 92 ; so Fronto Fer. Als. p. 213 Mai.

ex-ăquesco.opening: v. n. , to turn to water : mundus tum exignescere, tum exaquescere videtur, Censor. 18, 11 .

exărātĭo.opening: exaro (late Lat.). * A ploughing up , Mart. Cap. 6, § 637 .— * Transf. , a writing , composition , Sid. Carm. 9, 335 .

exarchus.opening: , = ἔξαρχος , a superintendent , overseer : monasteriorum, Just. Nov. 133, 4 .

ex-ardĕo.opening: v. a. (eccl. Lat.). Prop., to burn : ignis, Vulg. Sir. 16, 7 ; cf. ib. 28, 14 ; 27 .— Trop. , of the feelings, to be inflamed , blaze out : in brevi ira, Vulg. Psa. 2, 13 : in desideriis suis, id. Rom. 1, 27 .

ex-ardesco.opening: v. inch. n. , qs. to blaze out, i. e. to kindle , take fire (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense and in Cic.; cf.: ardeo, ferveo, caleo, flagro, candeo, uro, etc., incendor, inflammor, etc.). Lit. : nulla materies tam…

ex-ārĕfīo.opening: v. pass. [arefacio], to dry up , become completely dry : fucus marinus, Plin. 26, 10, 66, § 103 .

ex-āresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to dry up , become completely dry (rare, but class.). Lit. : vestimenta uvida, Plaut. Rud. 2, 7, 20 : frumentum, Varr. R. R. 1, 32 : silva omnis radicitus, Suet. Galb. 1 : amnes, Cic. Pis. 33, 82 ; id.…

ex-ārĭdus.opening: adj. , dried up , quite dry. — Trop. : status Judaeorum (with emortuus), Tert. Res. Carn. 30 .

ex-armātĭo.opening: exarmo , a weakening , lessening : fluxurarum, Cypr. Sing. Cler. 39 .

ex-armo.opening: v. a. , to deprive of arms , to disarm (post-Aug.). Lit. : cohortes, Tac. H. 2, 76 fin. : dextras, Luc. 5, 356 : Medos, id. 8, 387 ; Col. 7, 3, 5 ; cf. Lampr. Hel. 21 .— Transf. Navem, i. e. to unrig , dismantle , Sen.…

ex-ăro.opening: v. a. , to plough or dig up (class.). Lit. : radices, Cato. R. R. 61; id. ap. Plin. 17, 18, 30, § 127 ; Plin. 18, 6, 8, § 46 : sepulcra, Cic. Leg. 2, 23, 58 : terminos (with deicere), Dig. 10, 1, 4, § 4 : deum, puerum,…

ex-artĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. , inarticulate , irregular : sonus tinnitusque, Tert. ad Nat. 1, 8 .

ex-ascĭātus.opening: Part. [ascio], hewn out; hence, in gen., properly prepared : opus, Plaut. As. 2, 2, 93 .

exaspĕrātĭo.opening: exaspero , a roughness , Scrib. Comp. 222 ; Veg. Vet. 5, 61, 1 .— Bitterness , exasperation , Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 16 ; Macr. S. 7, 12, 38 .

exaspĕrātrix.opening: id. , she who irritates or exasperates , Vulg. Ezech. 2, 8 .

ex-aspĕro.opening: v. a. , to make rough , to roughen (not ante-Aug.). Lit. : fauces, Cels. 1, 3 ; cf.: summam cutem, id. 3, 27 : arterias, Plin. 22, 23, 48, § 100 : corpus, id. 31, 6, 34, § 67 : tussim, id. 23, 4, 51, § 97 : faucium…

exauctōrĭtas.opening: exauctoro , a discharge from military service , Cod. Th. 8, 5, 35.

ex-auctōro.opening: v. a. Milit. t. t. , to discharge from service (after sixteen years of service, before the end of the usual term of twenty years, i. e. before the regular missio; see missio. This discharge was either an honorable one…

exaudībĭlis.opening: adj. exaudio , that may be heard or listened to , Aug. Sol. 1, 1 .— Giving ear to requests , listening , Schol. Juv. 13, 248 .

ex-audĭo.grammar: īvi or ii, ītum, 4 v. a.
ex-audĭo.opening: v. a. To hear or perceive clearly (class.): Nec satis exaudiebam, nec sermonis fallebar tamen, Quae loquerentur, Plaut. Epid. 2, 2, 55 ; cf. id. Merc. 4, 3, 8 ; id. Men. 3, 2, 13 ; id. Trin. 3, 3, 25 : cum aliquantulum…

exaudītĭo.opening: exaudio, II. B. , a hearkening to , granting : oratio exauditione dei dignior, Aug. Civ. D. 21, 24 ; Vulg. 2 Chron. 33, 19.

exaudītor.opening: id. , one who hearkens to , grants , Vulg. Sirach, 35, 19 .

ex-augĕo.opening: v. a. , to increase exceedingly (rare): amplius, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 193 Müll. (Ann. v. 270 ed. Vahlen): benefacta majorum tuorum exauge, Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 9 ; ib. 32 : opinionem, Ter. Heaut. 2, 2, 3 .

exaugŭrātĭo.opening: exauguro , a desecrating , profaning : omnium sacellorum exaugurationes, Liv. 1, 55, 3 .

ex-augŭro.opening: v. a. , to apply to profane uses a thing which has been consecrated , to desecrate , profane (very rare): fana, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. NEQVITVM, p. 162, 32 Müll.; cf. Liv. 1, 55 : vestalem, Gell. 6, 7, 14 : sacerdotes,…

ex-auspĭco.opening: v. n. , to take an augury from any thing: ex vinculis, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 108 .

ex-ballisto.opening: v. a. ballista , a comically formed word, to put an end to , to finish or conquer with the ballista: Ballionem exballistabo lepide, Plaut. Ps. 2, 1, 10 .

exbĭbo.opening: , = ebibo, to drink out , drink up : neque illic calidum exbibit in prandium, Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 19 (Ritschl, bibit).

exbŏla.opening: , = ἐκβολή , a kind of missile , weapon , Naev. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 108 (Com. Rel. p. 24 Rib.).

exbures.opening: , sive exburae , quae exbiberunt, quasi epotae , Paul. ex Fest. p. 79, 11 Müll.

excaecātor.opening: excaeco , one who blinds , Aug. Serm. 43 ex Homil. 50.

ex-caeco.opening: v. a. , to blind , make blind (rare). Lit. : num ergo is excaecat nos aut orbat sensibus? etc., * Cic. Ac. 2, 23, 74 ; Plin. 20, 18, 76, § 200 ; Flor. 2, 20, 5 .— Transf. To deprive a plant of the eyes or buds , Col.…

ex-calcĕo.opening: ( ), , v. a. (the deponent form, v. below), to take off the shoes. In gen.: petiit, ut sibi pedes praeberet excalciandos, Suet. Vit. 2 .—More freq. with a personal object and in the part. perf. : excalciatus cursitare,…

excaldātĭo.opening: excaldo , a washing or bathing in warm water (late Lat.), Capitol. Albin. 5 al.

ex-caldo.opening: v. a. caldus , to wash or bathe in warm water (late Lat.), Marc. Empir. 26; Apic. 4, 2 al.

ex-călesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become warm , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 med.

ex-calfăcĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to warm , to heat (post-Aug.; esp. freq. in Pliny the Elder): excalfacit, Plin. 21, 20, 82, § 139 ; 21, 21, 89, § 155 : excalfieri, id. 24, 7, 28, § 42 ; Scrib. Comp. 158 : lacus sole excalfactus,…

excalfactōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , warming , heating (a Plinian word), Plin. 21, 18, 72, § 120 ; 24, 11, 64, § 105 ; 25, 13, 95, § 152 .

ex-candĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to heat , inflame (perh. only in the foll. passages), trop.: excande me fecerunt cupiditate ( tmesis ), Varr. R. R. 3, 4, 1 : annonam macelli, i. e. to enhance, raise, id. ib. 3, 2, 16 ; cf. exardesco and…

ex-candĕo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to make bright , whiten : cutem, Schol. Juv. 2, 107 .— Neut. , to gleam , glisten , be bright : lapides, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 3, 22 .

excandescentĭa.opening: excandesco , nascent anger , passionateness , irascibility , Cic. Tusc. 4, 9, 21 ; cf. App. Dogm. Plat. 1 fin.

excandesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow hot , to take fire , kindle , to glow (class.). Lit. : cum bitumen et sulphur additum est, excandescet, Cato R. R. 95 ; Col. 7, 5, 16 . — Trop. , to glow , to burn , esp. with anger: haec nullam…

excantātor.opening: excanto , a charmer , one who removes by enchantment : venatorum morsuum, Hier. in Joel Prol.

ex-canto.opening: (excantassit = excantaverit, Tab. XII. ap. Sen. Q. N. 4, 7, 2 ), , v. a. , to charm out or forth , to bring out by enchantment (not in Cic. or Caes.), Varr. ap. Non. 102, 11 ; Lucil. and Plaut. ib.; * Prop. 3, 3, 49 (4,…

ex-carnĭfĭco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to cut or tear any one to pieces (a rare word). Lit. : aliquem, Cic. N. D. 3, 33 fin. ; Suet. Vit. 17 ; Sen. Ep. 24 .— Trop. , to torment , torture : aliquem, Ter. Heaut. 4, 6, 9 : excarnificatus…

ex-castrātus.opening: Part. [castro], emasculated. Lit. , Gell. 9, 9, 10 .— Transf. , shelled , husked : sinapi, Scrib. Comp. 9 .

ex-caudĭco.opening: ( ), , v. a. [caudex), to weed out , root up = exstirpare. Prop., Lex ap. Front. Aquaed. 129 .— Transf. , to dig round , i. q. ablaqueare: ablaqueandae sunt vites, quod Itali excodicare appellant, Pall. Jan. 1 .— Trop.…

excăvātĭo.opening: excavo , a hollowing out : lapidis, Sen. Q. N. 4, 3, 3 .

ex-căvo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to hollow out. Lit. : trullam, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 27 fin. : cavernam sibi rostro, Plin. 9, 27, 43, § 82 : ripas, id. 10, 33, 49, § 95 : terram, id. 33 prooem.: lapides excavant aquae, Vulg. Job, 14,…

ex-cēdo.opening: ( subj. perf. sync. excessis, Ter. And. 4, 4, 21 ), v. n. and a. Neut. , to go out , go forth or away , to depart , retire , withdraw (freq. and class.; cf.: discedo, deficio, destituo, desero, linquo, relinquo). Lit.…

excellens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from excello.

excellenter.opening: adv. , excellently; v. , P. a. 1. fin.

excellentia.opening: excello, P. a. 1. , superiority , excellence , perfection ( abstr. and rel. ): magna cum excellentia praestantiaque animantium reliquarum, Cic. Off. 1, 28 ; cf. id. ib. 1, 27 fin. : animi excellentia magnitudoque, id.…

ex-cello.opening: (also acc. to the 2d conj., praes. indic. excellet, Aem. Mac. ap. Diom. p. 371 P., and subj. excelleat, Cic. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 838 and 896 P.), v. a. and n. cello . Act. , to raise up , elevate; only: recellere…

excelsĭtas.opening: excelsus , loftiness , height. Lit. : montium, Plin. 2, 64, 64, § 160 : harundinis, id. 16, 36, 66, § 167 : lilii, id. 21, 5, 11, § 23 .— Trop. : excelsitas animi et magnitudo, Cic. Off. 3, 5, 24 .

excensĭo.opening: escendo , a climbing , ascent , Curt. 9, 4, 4 ; Liv. 44, 10, 11 (Madvig al. escensio).

exceptācŭlum.opening: excepto , a receptacle : maliloquii, Tert. Spect. 2 med.

exceptīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. excipio , caught up , intercepted : alica, Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 115 .

exceptĭo.opening: id. , an exception , restriction , limitation [good prose and very freq., esp. in Cic.). In gen.: consiliorum, voluntatum sine ulla exceptione communitas, Cic. Lael. 17 ; so, sine (ulla) or cum exceptione, id. Fam. 6,…

exceptĭuncŭla.opening: dim. exceptio , a small limitation or exception , Sen. Ep. 20, 5 .

excepto.opening: v. freq. a. excipio , to take out , to take up , catch (very rare): barbatulos nullos exceptans de piscina, * Cic. Par. 5, 2, 38 ; so, aliquem, * Caes. B. G. 7, 47 fin. : (equae) exceptant leves auras, catch up. , i. e.…

exceptor.opening: id. , one who catches up any thing said, i. e. who writes it down, an amanuensis , short-hand writer , scribe (post-Aug.). In gen., Dig. 19, 2, 19 fin. ; Firm. 3, 6 med. and 12.— Esp., in the later period of the empire,…

exceptōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , serviceable for receiving (post-Aug.): quali, Dig. 33, 7, 8 ; cf. subst. : exceptorium excipulum, conceptaculum, ἐκδοχεῖον , Gloss.— Subst. : , , , a receptacle , reservoir; plur. , Vulg. Sir. 39, 22 .

ex-cĕrē^bro.opening: cerebrum , to deprive of brains , i. q. to make senseless : canem, Vulg. Isa. 66, 3 .— Part. : , , deprived of brains , i. q. rendered senseless , stupefied : excerebratus es novo vino, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 11 .

ex-cerno.opening: v. a. , to sift out , to separate (perh. not ante-Aug.). In gen.: furfures a farina, Col. 8, 4, 1 : frumenta, i. e. to cleanse, id. 2, 20, 5 ; cf.: caementa cribris, Vitr. 7, 6 : ex captorum numero excretos Saguntinos…

ex-cerpo.opening: v. a. carpo , to pick or take out. * Lit. : semina pomis, Hor. S. 2, 3, 272 .— Trop. (class.). To pick out , choose , select , gather : non solum ex malis eligere minima oportere, sed etiam excerpere ex ipsis, si quid…

excerptĭo.opening: excerpo, II. A. , an extract selected from a composition, an excerpt , Gell. 17, 21, 1 .

ex-cervīcātĭo.opening: cervicatus , obstinacy , stubbornness , Hier. in Naum, 3; cf. cervicositas.

excessĭo.opening: excedo , departure , death : ante excessionis diem, Hier. Orig. in Jerem. Hom. 13 fin. ; Lutat. Schol. ad Stat. Th. 4, 599 .

excessus.opening: excedo, I. A. 2. and B. 2. . A departure. In gen.: excessus ejus, Vell. 1, 15, 1 .—Esp., a departure from life: in his esse et excessum e vita et in vita mansionem, Cic. Fin. 3, 18, 60 ; Val. Max. 9, 13 prooem.; Sen.…

excē^tra.opening: perh. corrupted from ἔχιδνα , a snake , serpent (very rare). Prop., Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 3 sq. ; * Cic. poet. Tusc. 2, 9, 22.— Transf. , a reproachful epithet for a bad, intriguing woman, Plaut. Cas. 3, 5, 19 ; id. Ps. 1,…

excĭdĭo.opening: exscindo, v. 1. excidium , a destroying , destruction : oppidi, Plaut. Curc. 4, 3, 2 ; cf.: excidionem urbis a caedendo dictam manifestum est, Paul. ex Fest. p. 80, 9 Müll.

excĭdĭum.opening: excĭdo , a going down , setting : solis, Prud. Apoth. 694 .

ex-cĭdo.opening: v. n. cado , to fall out or down , to fall from (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense). Lit. In gen.: quod (animal) cum ex utero elapsum excidit, Cic. N. D. 2, 51, 128 : sol excidisse mihi e mundo videtur, id. Att. 9,…

ex-cīdo.opening: v. a. caedo , to cut out or off , to hew out , to cut or hew down (class.). Lit. : lapides e terra, Cic. Off. 2, 3 fin. : omnes arbores longe lateque, Caes. B. C. 2, 15, 1 ; cf.: excisa enim est arbor, non evulsa, Cic.…

ex-cĭo.opening: (long and short equally freq.; cf. excĭtus, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 20, 40 ; Lucr. 4, 1207 ; Cat. 61, 11 ; 63, 42 ; 64, 56 ; Verg. A. 4, 301 ; 7, 376 ; 12, 445 ; Ov. M. 2, 779 al. : excītus, Lucr. 4, 1215 ; Verg. A. 3,…

ex-cĭpĭo.opening: v. a. capio . (With the notion of the ex predominating.) To take or draw out. Lit. (rarely): aliquem e mari, to draw out , fish out , Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 293, 26 (Rep. 4, 8, 8 Baiter): vidulum (e mari), Plaut. Rud. 4,…

excĭpŭla.opening: (sc. vasa), excipio , vessels for receiving liquids , receivers , receptacles , Plin. 25, 7, 38, § 78 : in excipulis ejus fluminis, i. e. cavities, basins, id. 9, 22, 38, § 75 .

excĭpŭum.grammar: quod excipitur, ut prae cipuum quod ante capitur

excīsātus.opening: adj. excisus, from excīdo , cut out or off : excisatis auribus, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Non. 108, 17 .

excīsĭo.opening: excido , a cutting out , excision. Prop.: plagae, Pall. 3, 30 .— Plur. concr. , the parts cut out , Vitr. 10, 12, 1 .— A destroying , Cic. Dom. 58 ; id. Harusp. Resp. 2, 3 .

excīsōrĭus.opening: adj. excido , that serves for cutting out : scalper, Cels. 8, 3, § 15 .

excīsūra.opening: ex-cīdo , the cutting out , Edic. Diocl. 7, no. 42.

excĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. excito , inciting , animating : modulatio (with jucunda), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5 fin.

excĭtātē.opening: adv. , v. excito, P. a. fin.

excĭtātĭo.opening: excito , a rousing up , wakening (post-class.), Arn. 7, 237 .

excĭtātor.opening: id. , one who rouses or animates (post-class.): mentium, Prud. Cath. 1, 3 .

excĭtātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from excito.

excĭto.opening: v. freq. a. excio , to call out or forth , to bring or send out , to wake or rouse up (freq. and class.; cf.: provoco, evoco; irrito, lacesso, invito). Lit. : unde (Acherunte) animae excitantur obscura umbra, Poëta ap.…

excītus.opening: , false reading in App. M. 6, p. 184 fin. , for exitu.

exclāmātĭo.opening: exclamo , a loud calling or crying out (very rare). In gen.: acuta atque attenuata nimis, Auct. Her. 3, 12, 21 : acutas vocis exclamationes vitare debemus, id. ib. ; Quint. 11, 3, 179 ; Vulg. Sirach, 35, 13 .— In…

ex-clāmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ex-clāmo.opening: v. n. and a. Neut. , to call or cry aloud , to call or cry out , to exclaim : cum exclamasset Laelius, Cic. Rep. 6, 12 fin. : in stadio cursores exclamant quam maxime possunt, id. Tusc. 2, 23, 56 ; cf. Plaut. Most. 2,…

ex-clāro.opening: v. a. , to light up , illumine (opp. obscurare), Vitr. 1, 2, 7 .

ex-clūdo.opening: ( perf. sync. exclusti for exclusisti, Ter. Eun. 1, 2, 18 ) [cludo, claudo], to shut out , exclude; to cut off , remove , separate from any thing (class.). Lit. In gen.: aliquem a portu et perfugio, Cic. Fam. 5, 15, 3 :…

exclūsĭo.opening: excludo , a shutting out , exclusion (very rare; not in Cic.): de exclusione verbum nullum, Ter. Eun. 1, 2, 8 : ventorum, Vitr. 1, 6 : exceptio est quasi quaedam exclusio, etc., Dig. 44, 1, 2 .

exclūsor.opening: excludo, I. B. , one who shuts or drives out : daemoniorum, Aug. Serm. 37, 2 ; id. de Verb. Dom. 2 .— Esp., a maker of silver vessels : qui de confusione massae noverunt formam vasis exprimere, Aug. in Psa. 67, § 39 ;…

exclūsōrĭus.opening: adj. excludo , exclusory (post-class.): exceptio, replicatio, Dig. 44, 1, 2, § 2 .

exclūsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from excludo.

excoctĭo.opening: excoquo , a boiling or baking thoroughly (post-class.): calcis, a burning, Cod. Just. 12, 16, 3 : panis, a baking, ib. 12, 39, 1 .

excōgĭtātĭo.opening: excogito , a thinking out , a contriving , devising , inventing (syn. inventio): quid? illa vis quae tandem est, quae investigat occulta, quae inventio atque excogitatio dicitur? Cic. Tusc. 1, 25, 61 : excogitationem…

excōgĭtātor.opening: id. , a contriver , inventor (post-class.): verborum et nominum, Arn. 3, 119 .

excōgĭtātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from excogito.

excogitatus.opening: , false reading in Gell. 5, 10 fin. , instead of excogitatae.

ex-cōgĭto.opening: v. a. , to find out by thinking , to contrive , devise , invent (freq. and class.; cf.: comminiscor, simulo, confingo, fingo, etc.): quid enim mali aut sceleris fingi aut excogitari potest, quod non ille conceperit?…

ex-cŏlo.opening: v. a. , to work carefully , to tend , cultivate. Lit. (very rare, and mostly post-Aug.): vineas, Plin. 14, 4, 5, § 48 ; cf. rura, Claud. ap. Eutr. 2, 196 : victum hominum (boves), Plin. 8, 47, 72, § 187 : lanas rudes,…

ex-cōlo.opening: v. a. , to strain out (post-class.): acetum, Pall. Jun. 8, 1 : culicem, Vulg. Matt. 23, 24 .

ex-cŏmĕdo.opening: v. a. , to eat up , consume , App. Herb. 8 .

excommūnĭcātĭo.opening: excommunico , ban of the Church , excommunication , Aug. de Fide, 3 et saep.

ex-commūnĭco.opening: v. a. (lit., to put out of the community; hence, in eccl. Lat.), to lay under the ban of the Church , to excommunicate , Hier. adv. Ruf. 2, 18 : aliquem excommunicatum habere, Hilar. Op. Hist. Fragm. 11, 4.

ex-condo.opening: v. a. , to form , exhibit (post-class.): aliquem, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 18 .

ex-congrŭus.opening: adj. , not agreeing , not harmonious : laus, Symm. Or. pro Syn. 5 ed. Mai.

ex-consŭlāris.opening: one who has been a consul , an ex-consul , Inscr. Grut. 151, 6 .

ex-cŏquo.opening: v. a. , to boil out , melt out , dry up. Lit. : usque coquito, dum dimidium excoquas, i. e. you boil away, Cato, R. R. 107, 2 : mustum ad dimidium, Col. 12, 19, 1 : testudinem vino, to boil thoroughly, Plin. 32, 4, 14,…

ex-cŏrĭo.opening: v. a. corium , to strip of its skin or covering , to skin , strip , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 10, 30 ; Vulg. Micah, 3, 3 .— In mal. part., App. M. 10, p. 717 Oud. dub.; cf. Hildebr. ed. min. p. 137, note 3.

ex-cornis.opening: adj. cornu , without horns : bestia, Tert. Pall. 5 .

ex-cors.opening: adj. cor, the heart, as the seat of intelligence; v. cor , without intelligence , without understanding , senseless , silly , stupid (class.; cf.: amens, demens, vecors, insanus, vesanus, delirus): aliis cor ipsum…

excrēmentum.opening: excresco , an elevation , prominence : humilior inter excrementa costarum spina, Sid. Ep. 1, 2 .— Transf. , of numbers which increase regularly in series: sic decem milia ceteraque excrementa, Mart. Cap. 7, § 734 .

ex-crĕmo.opening: v. a. , to burn (postclass.), Tert. Cult. Fem. 6 .

ex-cresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow out or forth , to grow up , rise up (not ante-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: quae si satis excreverint (palmae), Col. 4, 21, 3 : abies, larix, palma in longitudinem, Plin. 16, 30, 54, § 125 : lactucae ad…

excrētus.opening: grown up; P. a. , from excresco.

excrŭcĭābĭlis.opening: adj. excrucio . * Pass. , deserving of torture : anus, Plaut. Cist. 4, 1, 1 .—* Act. , tormenting , torturing : exitium, Prud. στεφ . 3, 114.

excrŭcĭātĭo.opening: id. , torment , torture , = cruciatus (late Lat.), Aug. Tract. in Joann. 27 fin.

excrŭcĭātor.opening: id. , a tormentor : cordis, corporis, August. cont. Gaudent. 1, 21.

excrŭcĭātus.opening: id. , torment , torture , = cruciatus (post-class.): duri corporis, Prud. στεφ . 14, 19.

ex-crŭcĭo.opening: (archaic inf. praes. excruciarier, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 4 ), v. a. , to torment greatly , to torture , rack , plague (class.). Physically: perii! excruciabit me herus, Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 45 : servos fame vinculisque, Caes.…

excŭbātĭo.opening: excubo , a watching , keeping watch. * Lit. : ab excubatione desistere, Dig. 49, 16, 3, § 6 .—* Trop. : perpetua pro dignitate et salute amicorum, Val. Max. 4, 7, 7 .

excŭbĭae.opening: id. , a lying out of the house. In gen., Plaut. Cas. prol. 54 .—Far more freq. and class., In partic., a lying out on guard , a watching , keeping watch (cf.: custodia, vigiliae, insomnia): si haec arma, si Capitolinae…

excŭbĭtor.opening: excubo , one who keeps guard , a watchman , guard , sentinel : haec eadem (castella) noctu excubitoribus ac firmis praesidiis tenebantur, Caes. B. G. 7, 69 fin. : tribunus excubitor, the captain of the guard, Suet.…

excŭbĭtōrĭum.opening: id. , a post where guards were stationed , P. Victor. de Reg. Urb. Rom. sub fin.

excŭbĭtus.opening: id. , a watching , keeping watch : in excubitu, Auct. B. Hisp. 6, 4.

ex-cŭbo.opening: v. n. , to lie or sleep out of doors. In gen. (rare but class.): moniti Lacedaemonii, ut urbem et tecta linquerent armatique in agro excubarent, Cic. Div. 1, 50, 112 : apes noctu deprehensae in expeditione excubant…

ex-cūdo.opening: v. a. , to strike , beat or hammer out. Lit. : silici scintillam, Verg. A. 1, 174 : ignem, Plin. 16, 40, 77, § 208 .— Transf. , to hatch out : pullos ex ovis, Cic. N. D. 2, 52, 129 ; cf. Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 2 ; 10 ; 13 :…

exculcātor.opening: exculco , milit. t. t., a skirmisher , scout , Veg. Mil. 2, 15 .

ex-culco.opening: calco , to tread or beat out (very rare; not in Cic.). Lit. : ex dominis meis pugnis furfures, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 30 .—* Transf. , to tread down , to stamp firm or close : singuli ab infimo solo pedes terra…

excultor.opening: 1. excolo , a cultivator , rearer (post-class.): florum, Tert. Monog. 16 : tyrannicae crudelitatis, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 2, 22 .

ex-cŭnĕātus.opening: adj. cuneus , crowded out of the seats in the theatre; that can not get a seat , App. Flor. p. 353, 37 .

ex-cūrātus.opening: Part. [curo], carefully attended to , taken good care of : lepide excuratus incessisti, Plaut. Cas. 3, 6, 6 : victus, carefully provided, exquisite, choice, id. Ps. 5, 1, 8 .

ex-cūrĭo.opening: v. a. curia , io eject from the curia or from the senate (anteclass.), Varr. ap. Non. 36, 30 ; 465, 27 ex conject.

ex-curro.opening: ( Plaut. Most. 2, 1, 12 ; Liv. 1, 15 et saep.; less freq. curri, Liv. 25, 30 ), , v. n. and a. Neut. , to run out or forth , to hasten forwards. Lit. : cum se excucurrisse illuc frustra sciverit, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 125…

ex-cursātĭo.opening: curso , a sally , onset : crebrae, Val. Max. 2, 3, 3 .

ex-cursātor.opening: id. . In milit. lang., a skirmisher , scout , Amm. 24, 1, 1 .

excursĭo.opening: excurro , a running out or forth. Lit. In gen.: status (oratoris) erectus et celsus: excursio moderata eaque rara, a stepping forwards, Cic. Or. 18, 59 ; so, nec vultu nec manu nec excursionibus nimius, Quint. 1, 11, 3…

excurso.opening: v. n. freq. of excurro , to break forth repeatedly , to make frequent sallies or incursions : ubi plures innumeris videt excursare latebris, Stat. Th. 2, 550 .

excursor.opening: excurro, I. A. b. . A skirmisher , scout , spy : paratissimus pro nobis, Val. Max. 7, 3, 7 : istius excursor et emissarius, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 8, § 22 .— Transf. : excursores venti habentur, qui directo spiritu proflant,…

excursus.opening: excurro , a running out or forth (rare; not in Cic.; cf. excursio). Lit. : excursusque breves tentant (apes), excursions, Verg. G. 4, 194 : avium, Sol. 20, 3 ; cf. the outflow of water, Plin. Ep. 4, 30, 8 .— In partic.,…

excūsābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. excuso , that may be excused , excusable (very rare; not in Cic.): delicti pars, Ov. P. 1, 7, 41 .— Comp. : error, Val. Max. 8, 11, 4 .— Adv. : , excusably , Alcim. Avit. Homil. Fragm. 2 .— Comp. :…

excūsābundus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , excusing himself , App. Mag. p. 324, 14 .

excūsāmentum.opening: id. , an excuse : admissi, Mart. Cap. 8, § 807 .

excūsātē.opening: ( ), adv. , without blame; v. excuso, P. a. fin.

excūsātĭo.opening: ( ), , excuso , an excusing , excuse (freq. and class.); constr. with obj. or subj. gen. , absol. , with cur , quominus , etc. With gen. obj. : peccati, Cic. Lael. 11, 37 : intermissionis litterarum, id. Fam. 16, 25 :…

excūsātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. of excusatio , a trifling excuse , Salv. adv. Avar. 5, 2 .

excūsātor.opening: ( ), , excuso , one who excuses (late Lat.): deorum, Aug. Civ. D. 3, 20 : tuus, id. Serm. 3, 3 al.

excūsātus.opening: ( ), , Part. and P. a. , from excuso.

ex-cūso.opening: ( ), , v. a. causa; cf. accuso, from ad-causa; qs. to release from a charge, to free from blame; hence , to excuse a person or thing. Lit. With a personal object, aliquem alicui: Atticae meae velim me ita excuses, ut…

excūsor.opening: excudo , a coppersmith , a smith , the Gr. χαλκευτής , Quint. 2, 21, 10 .

excusse.opening: adv. , v. excutio, P. a. fin.

excussĭo.opening: excutio , a shaking down : oleae, Vulg. Isa. 17, 6 .

excussōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , that serves for shaking out : cribra e lino, bolting-sieves, Plin. 18, 11, 28, § 108 .

excussus.opening: excutio , a beating out , beating , Prud. στεφ . 5, 226.

ex-cŭtĭo.opening: (archaic perf. subj. excussit, for excusserit, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 2, 16 ), v. a. quatio , to shake out or off , to cast out , drive out , to send forth (class., esp. in the trop. sense). Lit. In gen.: posse ex his…

Exdemeticus.opening: the title of a satire by Varro , Gell. 19, 8, 17 .

ex-dorsŭo.opening: or , , v. a. dorsum; lit., to deprive of the back; hence, in partic. , of fishes, to take out the backbone , to bone (ante- and post-class.): congrum, muraenam exdorsua, quantum potes, Plaut. Aul. 2, 9, 2 : pisces (with…

ex-dŭumvĭr.opening: one who has been a duumvir , August. Ep. 88 .

exĕbĕnus.opening: , = ἐξέβενος , a precious stone of a shining white , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 159 .

ex-ĕdo.opening: (exessum, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 5 ), 3 (archaic praes. subj. exedint, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 32 . Post-class. form of the praes. ind. exedit, for exest, Sen. Q. N. 4, 2, 10 ; Seren. Sammon. 7), v. a. , to eat up , devour ,…

exĕdra.opening: , = ἐξέδρα , a hall furnished with seats , a hall for conversing or disputing in. Prop.: exedrae spatiosae, habentes sedes, in quibus philosophi, rhetores, reliquique ... sedentes disputare possint, Vitr. 5, 11, 2 ; 7,…

exĕdrĭum.opening: , = ἐξέδριον , a sitting-room , parlor , Cic. Fam. 7, 23, 3 .

ex-ēdūrātus.opening: Part. [edurus], deprived of hardness : exuviae (with mollitae and evigoratae), Tert. Pall. 4 .

exēgētĭce.opening: , = ἐξηγητική , the art of interpretation , exegesis , Diom. 2, p. 421 P.

exemplar.opening: , (exemplare, is, Lucr. 2, 124 , v. Lachm. ad h. l.), exemplum . A transcript , copy. Prop.: tibi earum (litterarum) exemplar misi, Asin. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 31, 6 ; Cic. Att. 4, 5, 1 : liber in exemplaria transcriptus…

exemplāris.opening: adj. exemplum . That serves as a pattern or example , exemplary (late Lat.): virtutes, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 8, 5 .— Subst. : , , (i. e. libri), copies (for the usual exemplaria), Tac. H. 4, 25 ; Fronto Ep. ad Anton. 2,…

exemplārĭum.opening: exemplar , post-class for exemplar (cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. p. 82 ). A copy : binae tabulae testamenti eodem tempore exemplarii causa scriptae, Dig. 31, 47 ; Hier. adv. Helv. 8 .— A model , pattern , original , Arn. 6, 198…

exemplātus.opening: adj. exemplum , copied , transcribed : libellus, Sid. Ep. 4, 16 .

exemplo.opening: v. a. id. , to adduce as an example , August. Ep. 149 .

exemplum.opening: eximo , orig., what is taken out as a sample (cf. eximius, from eximo), a sample. Prop. (cf. exemplar, specimen): purpurae, tritici, Auct. Her. 4, 6, 9 .—Hence, Transf. An imitation , image , portrait taken from…

exemptĭlis.opening: adj. eximo , that may be taken out , removable (post-Aug. and very rare): perticae, Col. 8, 11, 4 : margarita, lapides, Dig. 34, 2, 25, § 11 .

exemptĭo.opening: id. . In gen., a taking out , removing (not in Cic. or Caes.): alvi (apiarii), Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 34 ; cf. favorum, Col. 3, 18, 5 : cretae, Dig. 19, 5, 16 .— In jurid. Lat., a detention of a person summoned before…

exemptor.opening: id. , one who takes out any thing, esp. stone , a quarryman , Plin. 36, 15, 24, § 125 .

exemptus.opening: eximo , a taking out or away : cuneorum (opp. adjectus), Vitr. 9, 8, 6 .

exĕnĭa.opening: collat. form of xenia, with e prosth.; cf. xenium; v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 286 fin. : munera non solum pecunia est, ... non solum exenia sunt, August. in Psa. 25 ; Enarr. 2, 13; P. Diac. Vit. Greg. 24.

ex-ĕo.opening: (rarely īvi, Gell. 12, 12, 3 ; Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 50 ; perf. exit, for exiit, id. Ps. 2, 4, 40 ; Verg. A. 2, 497 ), ĭtum, īre ( fut. exibo, but exies, exiet, Sen. Ep. 113, 20 ; id. Apocol. 3, 1 al. ; exiet for exibit,…

ex-ercĕo.opening: v. a. arceo , to drive on , keep busy , keep at work; to oversee , superintend; with an inanimate object, to work , work at , employ one's self about a thing. Lit. (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose): quod in opere…

exercĭbĭlis.opening: adj. exerceo , practicable : regula, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 3, 8, 151 .

exercĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. exsarcio ; only trop., to make up for , earn : sumptum suom, Ter. Heaut. 1, 1, 91 .

exercĭtāmentum.opening: exercito , exercise : corporum, App. Flor. p. 351, 39 .

exercĭtātē.opening: adv. , v. exercito, P. a. fin.

exercĭtātĭo.opening: exercito . A moving , agitating , setting in motion : per aëris exercitationem (aqua) percolata tempestatibus liquescendo pervenit ad terram, Vitr. 8, 2, 1 .— Exercise , practice : corpora nostra motu atque…

exercĭtātor.opening: id. , an exerciser , trainer (post-Aug.), Plin. 23, 7, 63, § 121 : agilitatis, id. 35, 11, 40, § 136 : EQVITVM, Inscr. Orell. 3498 sq. ; cf. ib. 3413 .

exercĭtātōrĭus.opening: adj. exercitator , diligent , active : labores, August. Epist. 26, 2 .

exercĭtātrix.opening: id. , that which exercises the body, gymnastics : duas partes civilitatis corpori assignet (Plato), medicinam et quam interpretantur exercitatricem, Quint. 2, 15, 25 .

exercĭtātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from exercito.

exercĭte.opening: adv. , v. exerceo, P. a. fin.

exercĭtĭo.opening: exerceo , practice , exercise , management , administration (anteand post-class., for the class. exercitatio): inertia plus detrimenti facit quam exercitio, Cato ap. Gell. 11, 2, 6 : navium, Dig. 14, 1, 1, § 20 :…

exercĭtĭum.opening: id. , exercise (postAug.; not in Cic. and Caes.): frequentibus exercitiis praeparare milites ad proelia, Sall. Fragm. ap. Veg. Mil. 1, 9 fin. : equitum, Tac. A. 2, 55 ; cf. Vell. 2, 109 : aliarum quoque rerum vel studio…

exercĭto.opening: v. freq. a. exerceo, II. , to exercise diligently or frequently , practise (in the verb. finit. rare, but very freq. and class. as P. a. ): Achilles ibi se ac suos cursu exercitavisse memoratur, Mel. 2, 1, 5 : corpus…

exercĭtor.opening: exerceo, II. , an exerciser , trainer (ante- and post-class.) Prop.: huic Gurgulio'st exercitor, is hunc hominem cursuram docet, Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 9 ; 2, 1, 4 , Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 14 med. — Transf. , one who…

exercĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. exercitor (post-class.). Of or belonging to exercise : jacula, Tert. Poenit. 12 .— Of or belonging to trade or business : actio, Dig. 14 tit. 1; ib. 1, 7 .

exercĭtŭālis.opening: adj. 2. exercitus , belonging to an army (late Lat.): vir, Cassiod. Var. 11, 1 : libri, i. e. books of military divination, Amm. 23, 5, 10 .

exercĭtus.opening: ( gen. sing. exerciti, Naev. ap. Charis. p. 103 P.; Att. Trag. Fragm. 150, 311 ( Rib. p. 155, 177 ); Varr. ap. Non. 485, 16 sq. EXERCITVIS, acc. to Non. ib. 11 , without example. EXERCITVVS, Inscr. Orell. 4922 .— Dat. :…

ex-erro.opening: v. n. , to wander away (post-Aug. and very rare). Lit. : dexterque exerrat Arion (equus), Stat. Th. 6, 444 ; Anthol. Lat. 5, 172, 1 ; 6, 17, 22 .— Trop. , to deviate , err : a via veritatis, Cypr. Ep. 1, 12 ; Vulg. Sap.…

exēsor.opening: exedo , that which eats away any thing: murorum (aestus), i. e. an underminer, Lucr. 4, 220 ; 6, 926 .

exesto.opening: , extra esto. Sic enim lictor in quibusdam sacris clamitabat: HOSTIS, VINCTVS, MVLIER, VIRGO EXESTO; scilicet interesse prohibebatur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 82, 8 Müll.

ex-fībŭlo.opening: v. a. , to unclasp , loosen : ilia, Prud. Psych. 633 .

exfīlo.opening: v. a. ex-filum , to deprive of threads , unravel : sericum, Cassiod. in Psa. 38, 13 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 83 .

exfir.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 79, 13 Mull. N. cr.

ex-fŏlĭo.opening: v. a. folium , to strip of leaves : rosas, Apic. 4, 2, § 129 .

ex-fornĭcātus.opening: Part. [-fornicor], having committed fornication , Vulg. Ep. Jud. 7 .

ex-fundātus.opening: Part. [fundus], razed to the ground : oppidum, Cael. Antipater ap. Non. 108, 10 .

exfuti.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 81, 10 Müll. N. cr.

ex-fŭtūtus.opening: Part. [futuo], worn out by debauchery , Cat. 6, 13 ; cf. effutuo.

exhālātĭo.opening: exhalo , an exhalation , vapor (class.): exhalationes terrae, Cic. Tusc. 1, 19, 43 ; Sen. Q. N. 2, 10 ; Plin. 31, 3, 27, § 44 ; Pall. 1, 7, 4 .

ex-hālo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ex-hālo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to breathe out , exhale , evaporate (class.): exhalantque lacus nebulam, Lucr. 5, 463 : nebulam, fumos, Verg. G. 2, 217 ; Ov. M. 11, 597 : caliginem, Plin. 2, 42, 42, § 111 : mortiferum spiritum, id.…

ex-hărēno.opening: v. a. harena , to cleanse from sand : aes, Plin. 33, 3, 20, § 65 .

ex-haurĭo.opening: v. a. ( fut. part. act. exhausurus, Sen. Ep. 51, 6 ), to draw out , to empty by drawing , to exhaust (class., esp. in the transf. and trop. senses). Lit. , of liquids: cum alii malos scandant, alii per foros cursent,…

ex-herbo.opening: v. a. herba , to free from grass or woods : locum, Col. 11, 3, 11 : salicem, id. 4, 31, 2 .

exhērēdātor.opening: exheredo , a disinheriter , Cassiod. de Amic. 9, § 5 .

exhērēdĭto.opening: (for the class. exheredo), to disinherit (late Lat.), Salv. Contra Avar. 3, p. 113 .

exhērēdo.opening: v. a. exheres , to disinherit. Prop.: fratrem exheredans te faciebat heredem, Cic. Phil. 2, 16, 41 : aliquem, id. Clu. 48, 135 ; id. Rosc. Am. 18, 52 ; Auct. Her. 4, 23, 33 ; Quint. 5, 13, 32 ; 7, 4, 20 : liberos bonis,…

ex-hēres.opening: adj. , disinherited.— Subst. , a disinherited person : paternorum bonorum exheres filius, Cic. de Or. 1, 38, 175 ; Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 77 ; Quint. 5, 10, 107 ; 7, 1, 42 sq. al.—Comically: nive exheredem fecero vitae…

ex-hĭbĕo.opening: ( , v. Brix. ad Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 37 ), , v. a. habeo; lit., to hold out, reach out; hence , To hold forth , tender , present; to deliver , give up , produce (class.; syn.: praebeo, porrigo, praesto, tribuo, ministro,…

exhĭbĭtĭo.opening: exhibeo (postclass.). A handing out , giving up , producing , delivering : tabularum testamenti, Dig. 29, 3, 2 fin. : chirographi, Gell. 14, 2, 7 .— (Acc. to exhibeo, I. B. 2.) Sustenance , maintenance , Dig. 26, 2, 26…

exhĭbĭtor.opening: id. , one who presents or gives , a giver (post-class.): ludorum, Arn. 7, 297 : convivii, Non. 281, 20 .

exhĭbĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. exhibitor , relating to handing over or giving up (jurid. Lat.): interdictum, Dig. 43, 5, 3 ; cf. ib. 43, 29, 3 .

exhĭlărātĭo.opening: exhilaro , a gladdening , rejoicing (late Lat.): voluntatis, Aug. de Gen. ad lit. 8, 8.

ex-hĭlăro.opening: v. a. , to gladden , cheer , to make merry or joyous , to rejoice , delight , exhilarate. Prop. (rare but class.): miraris tam exhilaratam esse servitutem nostram? Cic. Fam. 9, 26, 1 ; Mart. 8, 50, 6 ; Col. 6, 24, 2 .—…

ex-hinc.opening: adv. , hereupon , after this , then (post-class. and very rare, for exinde, exin), App. M. 11, p. 269, 19 .

exhŏnōrātio.opening: exhonoro , a dishonoring , Aug. Civ. D. 5, 18, 2 .

ex-hŏnōro.opening: v. a. , to dishonor (late Lat.): Aug. Tract. in Joann. 36, 4 ; id. Ep. 118, 3 ; Vulg. Sirach, 10, 16 : pauperem, despise , id. Job, 2, 6.

ex-horrĕo.opening: v. a. , to tremble or shudder exceedingly at any thing, to be terrified at , to dread (very rare): aestus, Col. pöet. 10, 154: mortem sic quisquam exhorruit, ut, etc., Juv. 8, 196 .

exhorresco.opening: v. inch. n. and a. [exhorreo]. Neutr. , to tremble or shudder exceedingly , to be terrified (class.): non possum non exhorrescere, si quid intra cutem subest vulneris, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 18, 3 : in quo igitur…

exhortātĭo.opening: exhortor , an exhorting , exhortation , encouraging (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.): quae tua exhortatione excepi, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 7, 1 ; Quint. 12, 2, 6 : strepere cuncta clamoribus et tumultu et exhortatione…

exhortātīvus.opening: adj. id. , belonging to exhortation or encouragement , exhortative : status (a transl. of the Gr. προτρεπτικὴ παρορμητικὴ στάσις ), Quint. 3, 6, 47; Macr. de Diff. 16, 4 ; Isid. 2, 21, 20 ; 25 .

exhortātor.opening: id. , an exhorter , encourager (post-class.): omnium tolerantiarum, Tert. de Fuga in Persec. fin.

exhortātōrĭus.opening: adj. exhortator , belonging to or containing exhortation , hortatory (late Lat.): epistula, Hier. Ep. 2, 1 ; Aug. Ep. 209 .

ex-hortor.opening: v. dep. a. ( act. : exhortavit, Petr. 76, 10 ; pass. : exhortantur, August. Ep. 228 : exhortatus est, App. de Deo Soc. 1, 7 ), to exhort , encourage ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Prop.: trepidosque obitumque…

ex-hūmōro.opening: v. a. humor , to free from (injurious) humors , Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 1, 12 .

exhȳ^drĭae.opening: (venti) = ἐξυδρίαι ἄνεμοι , winds accompanied by rain , App. de Mundo, p. 62, 3.

ex-ignesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become ignited , turn to fire : mundus tum exignescere, tum exaquescere videtur, Censor. de Die Nat. 18 .

ex-ĭgo.opening: v. a. ago , to drive out or forth , to thrust out , to take or turn out. Lit. In gen.: reges ex civitate, to expel, Cic. de Or. 2, 48, 199 : hostem e campo, Liv. 3, 61, 8 : exigor patria, Naev. ap. Non. 291, 4 : aliquem…

exĭgŭē.opening: adv. , briefly , sparingly , v. exiguus fin.

exĭgŭĭtas.opening: exiguus , scantiness in measure or number, smallness , littleness , shortness , scarcity (class.). With gen. : cum paucitatem militum ex castrorum exiguitate cognoscerent, Caes. B. G. 4, 30, 1 : pellium, id. ib. 4, 1…

exĭgŭus.opening: adj. exigo, II. B. 5.; cf. contiguus, from contingo; lit., weighed, exact; hence opp. to abundant, beyond measure; cf.: parvus, pusillus, minutus , scanty in measure or number, small , little , petty , short , poor ,…

exīlis.opening: adj. ex and ile, ilia; hence, without entrails, i. e. thin, lank, Corss. Ausspr. 2, 1003 , small , thin , slender , lank , meagre , poor , feeble (class.; syn.: tenuis, gracilis, macer): exile et exiguum et vietum cor,…

exīlĭtas.opening: exilis , thinness , meagreness , weakness , poorness (class.): aculei apum, Plin. 11, 2, 1, § 3 : foliorum, id. 24, 19, 118, § 178 : soli, Col. 18, 16, 6 : femineae vocis, Quint. 1, 11, 1 ; cf. id. 11, 3, 19 : quarundam…

exĭmĭĕtas.opening: eximius , excellence , eminence (late Lat.), Symm. Ep. 3, 3 ; Aug. Ep. 32, 231 ; 237 .

exĭmĭus.opening: adj. eximo . Taken out from the mass, i. e. excepted , exempt (rare but class. = exemptus, exceptus): eximium neminem habere, Ter. Hec. 1, 1, 9 : neque esset veri simile, cum omnibus Siculis faceret injurias, te illi…

ex-ĭmo.opening: v. a. emo; cf. adimo and demo , to take out , take away , remove (class.; syn.: demo, adimo, eripio, furor, etc.). Lit. In gen. (with de , ex , or simple abl. ; rare with dat. ): eximito (acina) de dolio, Cato R. R.…

ex-ĭnānĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
ex-ĭnānĭo.opening: v. a. , to empty , make empty (rare but class.): Siciliam provinciam C. Verres per triennium depopulatus esse, Siculorum civitates vastasse, domos exinanisse, fana spoliasse dicitur, to make desolate, Cic. Div. in…

exĭnānītĭo.opening: exinanio , an emptying , evacuation (post-Aug.): alvi, Plin. 13, 22, 38, § 118 : florescendi, i. e. an exhausting, enfeebling, id. 17, 2, 2, § 12 .

ex-indē.opening: , and apocopated (like dein, proin, from deinde, proinde; cf. also: dein etiam saepe et exin pro deinde et exinde dicimus, Cic. Or. 45, 154 ; also , , istim; acc. to the best MSS. in Enn. ap. Fest. p. 356, 4 ; Plaut.…

exinfulabat.opening: = exserebat: infulas enim sacerdotum filamenta vocabant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 81, 18 Müll.

exintĕro.opening: ( , ), , v. a. ἐξεντεριζω . Prop., to disembowel , draw (ante- and post-class.), Plin. 30, 5, 14, § 42 ; 30, 10, 27, § 88 ; 32, 8, 29, § 92 : porcum, Petr. 54, 3 : hydram, Hyg. Fab. 30 : exinteratus lepus, Just. 1, 5…

existĭmābĭlis.opening: adj. existimo , supposable , probable , likely (late Latin), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 5 ; 35 ; 3, 17 fin.

existĭmātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a judging , judgment , opinion , supposition (class.; in sing. and plur. equally common). Prop.: re et existimatione jam, lege et pronuntiatione nondum condemnato, Cic. Clu. 20, 56 . non est tibi his solis…

existĭmātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a judge of any thing, a critic (rare but class.): ut existimatores videamur loqui, non magistri, Cic. Or. 31, 112 : doctus et intellegens, id. Brut. 93, 320 ; cf.: intellegens dicendi. id. ib. 54, 200 :…

ex-istĭmo.opening: or , , v. a. aestimo . = aestimo, to value , estimate , reckon , esteem , with gen. of value (rare): satin abiit neque quod dixi flocci existumat? Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 73 : dum ne ob malefacta peream, parvi existumo, id.…

exĭtĭābĭlis.opening: adj. exitium , destructive , fatal , deadly (rare but class.): exitiabilem illi faciam diem, Plaut. Ep. 4, 2, 36 : bellum suis civibus, * Cic. Att. 10, 4, 3 ; so, bellum, Eutr. 9, 7 : tyrannus, Liv. 29, 17, 19 : clades,…

exĭtĭālis.opening: adj. id. , destructive , fatal , deadly (rare but class.): exitus exitiales habere, * Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 6, § 12 : donum, Verg. A. 2, 31 : scelus, id. ib. 6, 511 : animalia venenata magis exitialia, si, etc., Plin. 10,…

exĭtĭo.opening: exeo , a going or coming out (ante-class. and late Lat.): ex utero, Plaut. Truc. 2, 6, 30 : a Deo, Hilar. Trin. 6, 31.

exĭtĭōsus.opening: adj. exitium , destructive , pernicious , deadly (rare but class.): conjuratio, Cic. Cat. 4, 3, 6 : quibus a servis caedem fieri senatus et bonorum rei publicae exitiosum fuisset, id. Planc. 36, 87 ; cf.: quod exitiosum…

exĭtĭum.opening: ( gen. plur. exitium, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 31, 67 , and Or. 46, 155), exeo . Lit. , a going out , egress (ante-class.): exitium antiqui ponebant pro exitu; nunc exitium pessimum exitum dicimus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 81, 6…

exĭtus.opening: exeo , a going out or forth , egress , departure (class., esp. in the trop. signif.). Lit. : reditum mihi gloriosum injuria tua dedit, non exitum calamitosum, Cic. Par. 4, 29 : omni exitu et pabulatione interclusi,…

ex-jūro.opening: v. a. , to swear solemnly , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Non. 105, 22 . (The line, Plaut. Am. 3, 3, 18 , found in some edd. is spurious.)

ex-lex.opening: adj. , beyond the law , bound by no law , lawless (only nom. and acc.; rare but class.): postremo quaero, parebis legibus an non? anne exlex solus vives? Varr. ap. Non. 10, 19 ; cf. Lucil. ib. 22 ; Liv 9, 34, 8 Drak. N.…

ex-mucco.opening: , in mal. part., Inscr. Pompeii in Bullet. Napol. I. p. 68, b.

ex-obrŭtus.opening: Part. [obruo], scraped out , cleared out : dolium, App. M. 9, p. 219, 34, p. 194 Bip.

ex-obsē^cro.opening: v. n. , to entreat earnestly : supplicabo, exobsecrabo, ut, etc., Plaut. As. 1, 3, 93 .

ex-occŭpo.opening: v. a. , to discharge of employment , free from occupation : sensus, Petr. Chrysol. Serm. 65 init.

exŏchădĭum.opening: , = ἐξοχάδιον , external piles , Marc. Emp. 31 .—Called also , , , = ἐξοχάς , Aug. Ep. 149 .

exōcoetus.opening: , = ἐξώκοιτος , a fish that sleeps on the shore , Plin. 9, 19, 34, § 76 .

ex-ŏcŭlo.opening: v. a. oculus , to deprive of the eyes or sight (ante- and postclass.): ni ei caput exoculassitis, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 26 : caecam et prorsus exoculatam esse fortunam, eyeless, sightless, App. M. 7, p. 188, 24 ; id. ib.…

exŏdĭārĭus.opening: exodium , a player in the exodium, Inscr. Orell. 2591 (of the year A.D. 167); Amm. 28, 4, 33 ; cf. Schol. Juv. 3, 175 .

exŏdĭum.opening: , = ἐξόδιον . Prop., a piece of a comic description ( a kind of dramatized satura ), for the most part attached to the Atellanae, but given , under the emperors , as a separate performance after tragedies , Liv. 7, 2,…

exŏdōrātus.opening: adj. ex-odor , deprived of its smell , Tert. Pall. 4 .

Exŏdus.opening: , = Ἔξοδος (a going out), the name of the second book of Moses (so called from its narrative of the departure from Egypt), Tert. adv. Jud. 11 et saep.

ex-ŏlesco.opening: v. inch. n. To grow out , to attain its full size , grow up. In gen., so only in the part. perf. , , grown up , full grown , mature : exoletus qui excessit olescendi id est crescendi modum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 5, 7 Müll.;…

exōmĭdes.opening: Fest. p. 81 Müll.; cf. Gell. 7, 12, 3 (= ἐξωμίς ).

exŏmŏlŏgēsis.opening: , = ἐξομολόγησις , a confession (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Poen. 9 ; id. de Orat. 7 al.

exŏnĕrātĭo.opening: exonero , an unloading , lightening , discharge (post-class.): mercedis, Dig. 19, 2, 15, § 7 .

exŏnĕrātor.opening: id. , an unloader , discharger , Inscr. Grut. 1117, 5 .

ex-ŏnĕro.opening: v. a. , to free from a burden , to disburden , unload , discharge (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; in Cic. and Caes. not at all). Lit. : navem, Plaut. Stich. 4, 1, 26 ; Auct. Afr. 8, 1; cf.: navigia jactu, Sen.…

exŏnўchŏn.opening: , = ἐξόνυχον , a plant , the lithospermon , Plin. 27, 11, 74, § 98 .

ex-ŏpīnisso.opening: v. n. , to think : viderint alii quid de hoc exopinissent, Petr. 62 fin.

exoptābĭlis.opening: adj. exopto , desirable , desired (rare): nuntius, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 67 : tempus, Sil. 11, 387 : amico, Lucil. Sat. 26, 5 .

exoptātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from exopto.

ex-opto.opening: v. a. , to wish or desire greatly , to long for a thing (class.). With acc. : quae majori parti pulcherrima videntur, ea maxime exoptant, Cic. Off. 1, 32, 118 : Samnitium adventum, Liv. 9, 25, 5 : illum exoptavit…

exōrābĭlis.opening: adj. exoro . Pass. , easily entreated or moved , exorable (class.), Plaut. Stich. 1, 2, 26 : si implacabiles iracundiae sunt, summa est acerbitas: sin autem exorabiles, summa levitas, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 1, 13 fin. : in…

exōrābŭla.opening: id. , means of entreating or convincing , enticements , arguments (ante- and post-class.): quotque exoretur exorabulis, Plaut. Truc. 1, 1, 6 : judicantium, App. Flor. p. 360 .

exōrātĭo.opening: id. , a moving by entreaty , effectual entreaty , Vulg. Sir. 16, 12 : manium paternorum, an appeasing, Quint. Decl. 8 .

exōrātīvus.opening: adj. id. , prayerful : dicere nescio quid exorativum, Cassiod. in Psa. 17, 32 .

exōrātor.opening: id. , one who obtains by entreaty , a successful suppliant , Ter. Hec. prol. alt. 2.

exōrātrix.opening: exorator , she who obtains by entreaty , Salvian Gub. D. p. 93 Rittersh.

ex-orbātus.opening: adj. ex-orbo , utterly orphaned , bereaved , Rénier, Inscr. Afr. 3981.

exorbĭtātĭo.opening: exorbito , a deviation , transgression (post-class.): disciplinae, Tert. Idol. 14 .

exorbĭtātor.opening: id. , a deviator from any thing, a transgressor (post-class.): exorbitator et destructor Judaïsmi, Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 6 fin.

ex-orbĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ex-orbĭto.opening: v. n. and a. [orbita] (post-class.). Neutr. , to go out of the track , to deviate. Lit. : exorbitantes boves, qui vehiculum trahebant, Aug. Civ. D. 22, 8 med. : stellis exorbitare a praestitutis itineribus non licet,…

exorcismus.opening: , = ἐξορκισμός , an exorcism (post - class.): exorcismis fugare daemones, Tert. Cor. Mil. 11 .

exorcista.opening: , = ἐξορκιστής , an exorcist (post-class.), Cod. Just. 1, 3, 6 ; Firm. Math. 3, 5; 9 fin. ; Vulg. Act. 19, 13 al.

exorcīzo.opening: v. a. , = ἐξορκίζω , to drive away evil spirits by adjuration , to exorcise (post-class.), Dig. 50, 13, 1, § 3 ; Aug. Civ. D. 10, 22 .

ex-ordĭor.opening: v. dep. a. , to begin a web , to lay the warp , to weave (class.). Lit. : funem longum pedes LXXII., Cato R. R. 135, 4 ; cf. trop.: neque exordiri primum, unde occipias, habes, Neque detexundam ad telam certos terminos,…

exordĭum.opening: exordior, I. . Prop., the beginning , the warp of a web (rare): non possum togam praetextam sperare, cum exordium pullum videam, Quint. 5, 10, 71 .— Transf. , in gen., a beginning , commencement (the usual meaning;…

ex-ŏrĭor.opening: ( part. fut. act. exorturus, Aug. Civ. D. 17, 14 fin. —The praes. indic. and imperf. subj. acc. to the third conj. : exoritur, Lucr. 1, 23 ; Verg. A. 2, 313 ; Ov. F. 4, 904 al. : exoreretur, Lucr. 2, 507 ; cf. id. 1,…

exormiston.opening: , = ἐξορμιστόν , a fish , perh. a kind of muraena, Cassiod. Var. 12, 14 .

exornātĭo.opening: exorno , an adorning , decorating , embellishing. Lit. : quae ad lavationem, quae ad exornationem pertinerent, to the toilet , Col. (Cic. Oecon.?) 12, 3, 2.— Trop. , of speech, embellishment. In gen.: ipsa inventa…

exornātor.opening: id. , an adorner , embellisher. — Trop. , of speech: ceteri non exornatores rerum, sed tantummodo narratores fuerunt, Cic. de Or. 2, 12, 54 .

exornātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from exorno.

ex-orno.opening: v. a. , to fit out , equip , furnish , supply with any thing. In gen. (rare; not in Cic.): nullae magis res duae plus negoti habent (sc. quam navis et mulier) forte si occeperis exornare, to give them an outfit, Plaut.…

ex-ōro.opening: (archaic inf. praes. pass. exorarier, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 167 ), v. a. , to move , prevail upon , persuade by entreaty; to gain or obtain by entreaty (class.): quem ego, ut mentiatur, inducere possum; ut pejeret, exorare…

exorsus.opening: exordior , a beginning , commencement : orationis, Cic. de Imp. Pomp. 4, 11 .

exortīvus.opening: adj. 2. exortus . Of or belonging to the rising of the heavenly bodies, ascendant (post-Aug.): mensura, Plin. 7, 49, 50, § 160 .— Transf. , towards the sunrise , eastern : pars, Plin. 18, 34, 77, § 338 : Oceanus, id.…

exortus.opening: exorior , a coming forth , rising : solis, Auct. Her. 3, 22, 36 ; Suet. Aug. 5 ; Plin. 12, 11, 23, § 40 : cum ab occasu solis ad exortus intenderent iter, Liv. 21, 30, 4 : stellarum, id. 2, 15, 12 : aequinoctiales,…

exoscŭlātĭo.opening: exosculor , a fond or mutual kissing : columbarum, billing, Plin. 10, 34, 52, § 104 ; 10, 12, 15, § 33 .

ex-oscŭlor.opening: v. dep. a. , to kiss eagerly , kiss fondly (post-Aug.). Lit. : multum ac diu exosculatus adolescentem, Plin. Ep. 5, 17, 4 : aliquem, Suet. Vit. 7 fin. : collum uxoris, id. Calig. 33 : manus cum fletu, id. Oth. 12 ; Tac.…

exossis.opening: , and , , adj. ex-ŏs , without bones , boneless (post-class.). Lit. : cum sit (lepus marinus) cetera exossis, App. Mag. p. 300, 13 .— Transf. Pliant , limber , supple , yielding : exossis plane et enervis, App. Mag. p.…

exosso.opening: v. a. id. , to deprive of the bones , to bone : mirum ni hic me quasi muraenam exossare cogitat, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 163 : congrum, Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 24 ; cf.: congrum, muraenam exdorsua ... exossata fac sient, Plaut. Aul. 2,…

exōstra.opening: , = ἐξώστρα . A machine in the theatre , by which the back part of the stage was turned towards the spectators; transf. of any thing public : quibuscum jam in exostra helluatur, Cic. Prov. Cons. 6, 14 .— A hanging…

ex-ōsus.opening: Part. [odi]. Act. , hating exceedingly , detesting ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): si nondum exosus ad unum Trojanos, Verg. A. 5, 687 : pugnas, id. ib. 12, 818 : bella, id. ib. 12, 517 : terras, Ov. M. 7, 524 : arma,…

exōtĕrĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἐξωτερικός , external , exoteric : libri (opp. acroatici), Gell. 20, 5, 2 (in Cic. Fin. 5, 5 , written as Greek).

exōtĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἐξωτικός , foreign , exotic (ante- and post-class.). Adj. : unguenta, Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 41 : vinum, Gell. 13, 5, 5 : jus (piscium), App. M. 10, p. 246, 28 : pulvis, id. Mag. p. 278, 4 : sermo, id. Met. 1 init.…

ex-pallesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow or turn very pale (perh. occurring only in the perf. ): viden' ut expalluit! Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 32 ; Ov. M. 6, 602 ; Plin. Ep. 1, 5, 13 ; Luc. 1, 539 al. : erubuisse, expalluisse, titubasse ...…

ex-pallĭātus.opening: adj. pallium , robbed of his cloak : Plaut. Cas. 5, 3, 6 .

ex-pallĭdus.opening: adj. , exceedingly pale or wan (post-Aug. and very rare): colore, Suet. Calig. 50 (al. pallido): corpus frigidum et expallidum, Tert. Res. Carn. 57 .

ex-palmo.opening: v. a. , to slap , box , strike , ῥαπίζω , ex-palmo, Gloss.: manibus, August. in Psa. 56, 13 .

expalpo.opening: v. a. , and , , v. dep. a. , to obtain by coaxing or flattery (ante-class.): exora, blandire, expalpa, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 144 : si quid expalpare possim ab illo, Pompon. ap. Non. 104, 12 : nunc servus argentum a patre…

ex-pando.grammar: pandi, pansum or passum 3 v. a.
ex-pando.opening: (the former, Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 228 ; 9, 33, 52, § 103 ; 31, 6, 37, § 70 ; the latter, Caecil. ap. Gell. 15, 15, 2 ; but in Tac. H. 5, 13 , very dub., the more prob. reading being exapertae, v. Orell. ad h. l.), , v.…

expansĭo.opening: expando , a spreading out , expansion (late Lat.): corporis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 139 .

ex-păpillātus.opening: adj. papilla , bared to the breast : expapillato brachio, Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 44 (quasi usque ad papillam renudato, Non. 103, 4 ); v. Ritschl ad h. l.

ex-partus.opening: adj. pario , of female animals, past bearing : pecudes, Varr. R. R, 2, 5, 7, p. 181 Bip.

expatare.grammar: in locum patentem se dare, sive in spatium se conferre
expatare.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 80, 5 Müll. N. cr.

ex-pā^trĭcĭus.opening: one who has ceased to be a patrician , an ex-patrician , Cod. Just. 3, 24, 3 .

ex-pā^tro.opening: v. a. , to finish , bring to an end , to squander in voluptuousness , Cat. 29, 17 .

ex-pausātus.opening: Part. [pausa], rested , refreshed (late Lat.): jumentum, Veg. Vet. 5, 38 .

ex-păvĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to terrify , frighten , make afraid (post-Aug. and very rare): mugitu tauri equi expavefacti, Hyg. Fab. 47 (in Sen. Ep. 85, 41 , read expavescentia).

ex-păvĕo.opening: v. a. , to be sorely afraid of any thing: hanc audaciam stili nostri, Stat. S. 3 praef. ; Mart. Cap. 1, § 84 .

ex-păvesco.opening: v. inch. n. and a. , to be or become greatly terrified , to be very much afraid; to be greatly frightened at or afraid of , to fear greatly (perh. not anteAug.). Absol. : expavescentibus repente, Plin. 23, 1, 24, § 49…

ex-păvĭdus.opening: adj. , terrified greatly : pecuniae magnitudine ictus expavidusque, Gell. 1, 8, 6 .

ex-pectŏro.opening: v. a. pectus , to drive from the breast; to expel , banish from the mind (ante-class.): tum pavor sapientiam omnem mi exanimato expectorat, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 4, 8, 19 (Trag. Fragm. ed. R ib. p. 17 ): pavorem hunc meum…

ex-pĕcūlĭātus.opening: adj. peculium , stripped of property : servi, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 21 .

ex-pĕdĭo.opening: (archaic fut. expedibo, Enn., Pac., Att., and Pompon. ap. Non. 505, 15 sq. ; 477, 2 ; Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 36 ), v. a. pes , orig., to free the feet , i. e. from a snare; hence, in gen., to extricate , disengage , let…

expĕdītē.opening: adv. , v. expedio, P. a. fin.

expĕdītĭo.opening: expedio . Milit. t. t. , an enterprise against the enemy , an expedition , campaign : tripartito milites equitesque in expeditionem misit, * Caes. B. G. 5, 10, 1 ; cf.: in expeditionem exercitum educere, * Cic. Div. 1,…

expĕdītĭōnālis.opening: adj. expeditio, I. , of or belonging to a military expedition (post-class.): usus, Spart. Nigr. 10 : res, Amm. 31, 16, 5 : portus, Cod. Th. 8, 10, 11.

expĕdītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from expedio.

expējūro.opening: v. n. , to swear falsely , perjure one's self : expejurabant, execrabant se ac suos, Afran. ap. Non. 473, 24 (R ib. Com. Fragm. p. 188 ).

ex-pello.opening: v. a. , to drive out or away , thrust out or away , to eject , expel (class.). Lit. : haec tanta virtus ex hac urbe expelletur, exterminabitur, proicietur? Cic. Mil. 37, 101 : me ex re publica, id. Fam. 6, 6, 2 :…

ex-pendo.opening: v. a. , to weigh out , weigh. Lit. In gen. (very rare): aliquem, Plaut. As. 2, 2, 34 : ut jam expendantur, non numerentur pecuniae, Cic. Phil. 2, 38, 97 : bacam, nucem, Cels. 5, 19, 12 .—With abl. of that against which…

expensa.opening: (sc. pecunia) [expendo], a disbursement , expense (post-class.): neque tempus neque finem expensarum habet, Dig. 27, 10, 1 : non indecores aeraria lassant expensae, Claud. II. Cons. Stil. 145 .

expensĭo.opening: expendo , an expense , expenditure (post-class.), Cod. Th. 6, 4, 24; Symm. Ep. 5, 74 .

expenso.opening: v. freq. a. id. . To pay out , pay (ante- and post-class.): argentum accepto, expenso, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 31 : nummos, Dig. 40, 5, 41, § 10 .—* To equalize , distribute equally : dies intercalares intercalationibus…

expergē-făcĭo.opening: v. a. expergo , to awaken , rouse. Lit. : expergefactus e somno, Suet. Calig. 6 ; 38 ; id. Aug. 94 : repente, id. Claud. 8 ; Vulg. Gen. 41, 4 al. — Transf. , in gen., to arouse , stir up , excite : si forte…

expergēfactĭo.opening: expergefacio , an awakening , rousing : a somno, Aug. de Vera Relig. 50 .

expergĭfĭco.opening: v. a. expergificus , to awaken , arouse , excite : ingenium, Gell. 17, 12, 1 .

expergĭfĭcus.opening: adj. expergofacio , that awakens or excites : carmen, App. Flor. p. 349, 21 .

expergiscor.opening: (archaic inf. praes. expergiscier, Plaut. As. 2, 1, 1 ), v. dep. (act. form in the imperf. subj. expergisceret, Pompon. ap. Non. 473, 6 ), expergo , to be awakened , to awake (class.). Lit. : si dormis, expergiscere.…

expergĭtē.opening: adv. , v. expergo, P. a. fin.

expergo.opening: v. a. , to awaken , rouse up (cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 80 Müll.; ante- and post-class.). Lit. : omnes vocis expergit sono, Santra ap. Non. 104, 16 (Com. 4 R ib. p. 228 ): expergite pectora tarda sopore, Att. ib.: nec…

expĕrĭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from experior.

expĕrĭentĭa.opening: experior , a trial , proof , experiment (class.). Prop.: experientiā tentare quaedam, Varr. R. R. 1, 18, 8 ; Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 18, 3 : patrimonii amplificandi, Cic. Rab. Post. 16, 43 : belli, Vell. 2, 78, 2 :…

expĕrīmentum.opening: id. , a proof , test , trial , experiment (mostly post-Aug.; cf.: documentum periculum): nimirum hoc maximum est experimentum, cum constet aegritudinem vetustate tolli, etc., * Cic. Tusc. 3, 30, 74 : Metello…

ex-pĕrĭor.opening: ( act. experiero, Varr. L. L. 8, 9, 24 dub.), 4, v. dep. a. [ex- and root per-; Sanscr. par-, pi-parmi, conduct; Gr. περάω , pass through; πόρος , passage; πεῖρα , experience; Lat. porta, portus, peritus, periculum;…

expĕrītos.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 79, 15 Müll.; cf.: experitus non peritus, id est extra peritiam positus, Placid. p. 461 .
